title: Three route-entry premises corrected during take-up

data.head: ## Three route-entry premises corrected during take-up

body:
The entry's mechanism was written from the prior session's reading; grounding it against the live tooling
(evidence: `.andromeda/runs/2026-08-08T19-29-55-phase/advisory-evidence.md`) corrected three points. The
**intent is unchanged** — only the route to it.

1. **RUSTSEC-2026-0190 is `anyhow`, not `crossbeam-epoch`,** and it is an `unsound` advisory: `cargo audit`
   reports it as an allowed warning (exit 0) while `cargo deny` denies it. It is invisible to an audit-only
   check — a live instance of the 2026-06-23 session learning that both tools must run.

2. **crossbeam-epoch is not in the Tauri tree.** It enters only via `assert_fs` → globwalk → ignore →
   crossbeam-deque — a **dev-dependency**, never compiled into the release binary. Severity in context is
   test-fixture-only; it is fixed anyway because the gate denies it.

3. **quick-xml needs no Tauri bump.** `tauri-utils` is already at its latest (2.9.3); the semver-major
   0.39 → 0.41 jump is absorbed inside `plist`, whose caret-compatible 1.9.0 → 1.10.0 minor bump
   `tauri-utils` already accepts. `cargo update -p quick-xml` alone moves nothing — **plist is the lever**.

Consequence: this is a **lock-only** change. No `Cargo.toml` dependency edit is required, no `deny.toml`
exception is added, and the Tauri version is untouched. These advisories are actionable-with-fixes, so
`deny.toml` remains the wrong instrument for them (it is reserved for the unmaintained-transitive /
non-actionable class).
**In scope**
- `Cargo.lock` — the three `cargo update -p {plist,crossbeam-epoch,anyhow}` bumps.

- Re-proving the full gate: workspace build, `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci` (428 baseline),
  `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --doc`, `scripts/agent-run.sh run`,
  `cargo audit`, `cargo deny check advisories bans sources licenses`.

- Any **compile or test breakage caused by these bumps** — quick-xml 0.41 is a major bump consumed by
  `tauri-build`'s build script (Info.plist handling), so `conductor-tauri` compilation is the real risk
  surface and must be exercised, not assumed.

- Resolving the RUSTSEC-2024-0429 (glib 0.18.5, unsound) open item below, so the gate cannot come back
  red on a latent fifth error.
**Out of scope**
- Any `Cargo.toml` version-floor edit, unless the P4 review explicitly elects one (see Decisions).
- New `deny.toml` entries — none of these four qualifies.

- A Tauri minor/patch bump (2.11.3 → 2.11.5 exists) — unnecessary for the gate, and a GUI-tree change
  with its own verification cost. Only pull it in if a bump above forces it.
- The 17 `unmaintained` + remaining `unsound` warnings already justified in `deny.toml` — untouched.
- The `npm audit --omit=dev` frontend gate — a separate tree, not advisory-decayed here.
- The stale `rmcp = "1.7.0"` workspace-dependency entry (see Decisions) — flagged, not assumed in.

- **`Cargo.lock`** — the committed, un-drifted lock is itself the contract (`security.md` §Dependencies:
  it is what makes the audit deterministic).

- **CI** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) — the existing separate `cargo audit` + `cargo deny check` steps are
  the gate being restored; no new step is expected.

- **No engine, seam, scenario, report-envelope, or GUI model change.** Zero Rust source change is the
  expected outcome; any source edit would be bump-forced fallout, and is a signal to re-examine scope.

1. **Lock-only, or also raise the manifest floors?** `anyhow = "1.0.102"` in `[workspace.dependencies]`
   would keep naming a version with a known unsound advisory even after the lock moves. Raising it to
   `1.0.103`+ encodes the security floor durably; leaving it relies on the committed lock alone.

2. **The orphan `rmcp = "1.7.0"`.** It sits in `[workspace.dependencies]`, no member references it, and it
   is **absent from `Cargo.lock`** — while the architecture records rmcp as removed on 2026-06-27. It is
   dead manifest cruft contradicting a documented decision, and a zero-risk one-line deletion, but it is
   dependency *hygiene*, not advisory remediation. Include or leave to a later chunk.

`cargo audit` lists RUSTSEC-2024-0429 (glib 0.18.5, `unsound`) which did **not** appear among cargo-deny's
four errors and is **not** in `deny.toml`'s ignore list. Establish why before declaring the gate green.

_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-08-08-sut-capability-manifest · **Version:** conductor-0.2.0 · **Generated:** 2026-08-08T11:22:08Z
- **Epoch:** 1 — Foundation: re-aim at the SUT (keystone) · **Capability:** `verification-matrix.json#v2-01`

Conductor's accepted Pulse-capability set is a compile-time constant. `pid_format` in
`crates/conductor-core/src/scenario.rs:23-34` validates a P-ID with `(1..=60).contains(&n)` and rejects
anything else with `"expected P-NNN with NNN in 001..=060"`, so a scenario naming any capability Pulse
shipped in its v0.3.0 (the ledger now reaches P-082) fails garde validation at load. Every downstream proof
this version plans is aimed at a stale target until that constant stops being the source of truth. This is
the keystone chunk of the keystone epoch.

This chunk replaces the constant with a **versioned, committed, runtime-parsed manifest** at
`contracts/pulse-capabilities.toml`, loaded and bounds-checked by a new `conductor-core` module that mirrors
the shipped `ContractManifest` loader (per arch §Established Decisions [Module Boundaries] + §Stack; the
in-repo precedent is `crates/conductor-verify/src/manifest.rs`). The intent's requirement is that **a Pulse
release becomes a data update, not a code change** — so the deliverable is judged by whether bumping Pulse's
capability set requires editing only the TOML artifact.

Failure handling follows the **two-tier split the same precedent already demonstrates** (operator-decided at
P4): the *loader* returns a typed `conductor-core` harness fault — read/parse/bounds failure is
`Result::Err`, never a verdict, never a panic, never a silent widen back to `1..=60` (per arch §Conventions
Error handling + security-plan §Input Validation + §Anti-Patterns Universal); the `Blocked` **ReportState**
with its named precondition stays the *gate/run* surface's job, where the identity fields a blocked row
requires (`run_id`/`seed`/`scenario`/`p_ids`/`slo_tier`) actually exist. This chunk builds only the loader
tier. The classification universe (`coverage.rs`) and the drift check are explicitly **not** here.

1. **Author the manifest artifact** `contracts/pulse-capabilities.toml` — a Pulse version/date stamp plus the
   accepted capability id set covering Pulse's current ledger (P-001..P-082). Committed and git-tracked,
   deterministically ordered (no globbing, no filesystem-order construction) per arch §Cross-cutting Patterns
   (Determinism discipline). Parsed with the already-present `toml` dep — **no new dependency**.

2. **Add `crates/conductor-core/src/capability_manifest.rs`** mirroring `ContractManifest`'s shape: a
   `#[derive(Deserialize)]` struct, a `default_path()` returning the workspace-relative
   `contracts/pulse-capabilities.toml`, a `load(&Path)` that reads → parses → runs a private `validate()`,
   and a typed harness-fault return. `validate()` bounds-checks the set: non-empty, every id well-formed
   `P-NNN`, no duplicates, no garbage entries (per security-plan §Input Validation).

3. **Keep error text path-free.** The read failure carries only `e.kind()`, never the `io::Error` `Display`
   — copy the normative comment at `manifest.rs:42` (*"never the path itself — io::Error's Display leaks
   it"*). The parse failure goes through `sanitize_error`, as `Scenario::from_toml_str` already does.

4. **Re-source `pid_format`** so the accepted set comes from the manifest instead of `(1..=60)`, and its
   rejection message names the manifest rather than a hardcoded range. **`Scenario::from_toml_str(&str)`
   keeps its signature** — see Implementation notes for why this is a hard constraint, not a preference.

5. **Provide an injectable path for tests** so a test can validate against a fixture capability set without
   writing into `contracts/` and without process-global mutable state (per test-plan §11 § Test Data).
6. **Register the module** in `crates/conductor-core/src/lib.rs`.

7. **Decide the `CoreError` surface** — reuse `Config(String)` or add one manifest variant. A distinct
   variant is what lets the cli edge emit a manifest-specific `hint:` line alongside the existing
   missing-contract-manifest hint at `crates/conductor-cli/src/main.rs:59`; either is acceptable, but the
   operator-facing `error:`/`hint:` pair must be sanitized per design-system §Surface: cli §Component
   Patterns 5.

8. **Re-key the superseded tests** in `scenario.rs`: `malformed_or_out_of_range_p_ids_are_rejected` currently
   asserts `"P-061"` MUST fail (it must now pass, since Pulse shipped it) and `boundary_p_ids_are_accepted`
   pins `P-001`/`P-009`/`P-060`. Re-key both to the manifest-sourced set rather than deleting the coverage;
   keep an out-of-manifest id in the reject list so the negative case survives.

9. **Emit one structured boundary line** at load per obs-plan §6 (boundary-call wrappers): `info` on success,
   `error` on the unrecoverable case. Every logged field must be in `conductor-core::redact`'s allowlist or
   folded into `message`/`count` — a `manifest_path`/`manifest_version`/`capability_count` field would be
   silently dropped by the processor stage. No new span name (manifest load is not one of obs-plan §4's
   seven must-trace paths).

- `contracts/pulse-capabilities.toml` — the versioned SUT capability manifest: Pulse version/date stamp +
  the accepted capability id set. Sibling of the existing `contracts/mcp-contract.toml`.

- `crates/conductor-core/src/capability_manifest.rs` — loader + private validator + its `#[cfg(test)]`
  module (the 4-test shape from `manifest.rs:74-114`).

- `crates/conductor-core/src/scenario.rs` — `pid_format` (`:23-34`) sources its accepted set from the
  manifest; rejection message names the manifest; test cases `malformed_or_out_of_range_p_ids_are_rejected`
  and `boundary_p_ids_are_accepted` re-keyed. Preserve the existing garde field-level pattern (garde 0.22.1
  has no container-level `custom` — see the normative comment at `scenario.rs:115`).
- `crates/conductor-core/src/lib.rs` — module registration.
- `crates/conductor-core/src/error.rs` — optionally one `CoreError` variant (step 7).

- `crates/conductor-core/src/coverage.rs` and its `matrix_has_exactly_sixty_capabilities` (`:141`) /

**Epoch:** 1 — Foundation: re-aim at the SUT (keystone)
**Version:** conductor-0.2.0
**Capability:** `verification-matrix.json#v2-01`
**Carried annotations:** none (no `PREREQ:` / `CARRY:` on the entry)

Conductor is a harness whose whole purpose is proving a live Pulse. Over a 41-day pause Pulse shipped 22 new
capabilities (P-061..P-082) and Conductor cannot so much as *name* them: the accepted capability set is a
**compile-time constant**, so a scenario keyed to anything above P-060 fails validation at load. Every
downstream proof in this version is aimed at a stale target until that constant stops being the source of
truth. This is the keystone chunk of the keystone epoch — nothing in Epochs 2–6 is worth running before it.

**OBSERVED (intent §4 F1):** `crates/conductor-core/src/scenario.rs:23-33` validates `P-NNN` with
`(1..=60).contains(&n)` and returns `"expected P-NNN with NNN in 001..=060"`; the unit test at `:195` asserts
`"P-061"` MUST be rejected. Pulse's ledger now reaches P-082.

**EXPECT (intent §4 F1):** the accepted capability set tracks the SUT instead of a compile-time constant —
sourced from a versioned SUT capability artifact under `refs/`, so **a Pulse release is a data update, not a
code change**. Widening the constant to `001..=082` is named in the intent as the *minimum* and is explicitly
**not the answer**: it re-freezes the same defect one version later. Take it only as a declared interim, never
as the deliverable.

1. **A versioned SUT capability artifact** at `contracts/pulse-capabilities.toml` enumerating Pulse's current
   capability set. _(Amended at P5 validation-1 — the scope originally said `.andromeda/refs/`, following the
   intent's "under `refs/`" wording. Planning surfaced that `.andromeda/refs/` holds only Pulse-authored
   planning documents, none parsed at runtime, and is absent from arch's directory tree, whereas `contracts/`
   is arch's registered runtime-read config root already holding the sibling `mcp-contract.toml`. Operator
   decision at P4: `contracts/`. This avoids an arch §Occupied Resources + directory-tree amendment.)_

2. **`conductor-core` sources the accepted P-ID set from that artifact** rather than from the hardcoded
   `(1..=60)` range in the scenario-model validator, so scenario validation accepts exactly the SUT's real
   capability set.

3. **A validated load boundary.** The manifest is a new on-disk parsed input at a trust boundary: it is
   validated at load, and a malformed / absent / unparseable manifest surfaces a **named precondition** rather
   than being silently downgraded, silently widened, or panicking.

4. **The superseded unit test** at `scenario.rs:195` — which encodes the old bound by asserting `"P-061"` must
   be rejected — is replaced by tests keyed to the manifest-sourced set.

- **NOT the drift check** (`v2-02`, the next chunk) — this chunk makes the set data-sourced; failing loudly when
  Pulse advances past what Conductor knows is separate.

- **NOT the coverage classification** of P-061..P-082 into auto / drive+observe / static-only /
  not-Conductor's (`v2-03`), and NOT the out-of-scope rendering treatment.
- **NOT new scenarios** for the in-lane capabilities P-067 / P-072 / P-079 (`v2-04`).

- **NOT any live-Pulse work** — no MCP read-back, no emission, no preflight change. This chunk is offline and
  fully CI-verifiable.

- **Conductor does not fix or modify Pulse** (version non-goal); the artifact is Conductor's own record of the
  SUT's claimed surface, not a change to the SUT.
- **`conductor-core`** — the scenario model's P-ID validation (garde surface); the source of the accepted set.

- **`contracts/`** — a new versioned capability artifact alongside `mcp-contract.toml` (runtime-read config
  data, not a spec source).

- **Scope law** — "no scenario without a P-ID" is preserved and strengthened: the P-ID space stays the SUT's
  (`P-NNN`), never Conductor's own (`v2-NN`).
- **Verdict/error wall** — the load failure path must land on the correct side of the wall (see open question).
- **Determinism** — sourcing the set from a committed artifact must not introduce run-to-run variance.

1. **Which side of the verdict/error wall does a malformed manifest land on?** → **RESOLVED: two-tier**
   (operator decision at P4). The *loader* returns a typed `conductor-core` harness fault (`Result::Err`) —
   matching both in-repo precedents (`Scenario::from_toml_str` → `CoreError::Config`, and
   `ContractManifest::load` → `VerifyError::Manifest`, documented "never a verification verdict"). The
   route line's "malformed reporting blocked" is satisfied at the *gate/run* surface, which already renders
   `[BLOCKED]` + a named precondition. Decisive structural argument (arch extract): a `Blocked` row requires
   `run_id`/`seed`/`scenario`/`p_ids`/`slo_tier`, none of which exist at manifest-load time. This chunk builds
   only the loader tier.

2. **Does the accepted-set source also feed `coverage.rs`?** → **RESOLVED: no — `v2-03` owns it.** Research
   found `coverage.rs` is a `static COVERAGE: [CapabilityRow; 60]` of `&'static str`, documented "no runtime
   IO" (`coverage.rs:46`), so manifest-sourcing it is a *representation change*, not a re-point. `coverage.rs`
   and its two "exactly sixty" tests stay green and untouched here; the plan carries an explicit
   do-not-modify guard.

3. **Manifest path handle.** → **RESOLVED: no override handle.** The manifest resolves from `default_path()`
   exactly as `ContractManifest` does. If /implement finds cause to add one it must be `CONDUCTOR_*`-namespaced,
   resolved through the existing `conductor_core::config_path::resolve_under` at the **cli edge**, carry
   traversal-rejection tests, and be registered in arch §Occupied Resources at wrap — never added quietly.

_(Also settled at P4, not originally a scope question: `Scenario::from_toml_str(&str)` **keeps its signature**.
The code-graph reported 1 production caller; a grep cross-check found 5 across 4 crates, so threading a
manifest parameter would turn a contained validator change into a four-crate ripple.)_

title: Definition of done for this chunk

data.head: ## Definition of done for this chunk

body:
A scenario naming any capability present in the manifest validates at load; one absent from it is rejected with
a message that names the manifest rather than a hardcoded range; a malformed or absent manifest produces the
named precondition instead of a silent pass or a panic; and adding a future Pulse release requires editing only
the artifact, with no Rust source change. Workspace lint + tests green, `Cargo.lock` un-drifted.

_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-08-09-current-sut-coverage-classification · **Version:** conductor-0.2.0 · **Generated:** 2026-08-09T13:47Z

Conductor's coverage classification stops at `P-060` while the accepted capability set — data, since
`2026-08-08-sut-capability-manifest` — reaches `P-082`. `conductor_core::check_sut_drift` already gates that
difference against a pinned residual ledger (`KNOWN_UNCLASSIFIED`, 22 ids). This chunk closes the gap for good:
**every capability the manifest accepts carries exactly one classification, with zero unclassified entries**, and
the "not Conductor's to verify" boundary becomes a recorded decision rather than an absence.

Three things follow. First, a **fourth `CoverageMode` variant** — `not-conductors` — distinct from `static-only`
(which means *no dynamic telemetry dimension*; the new one means *outside Conductor's remit by standing
non-goal*). It is a classification axis only: `Verdict` and `ReportState` stay closed, no seventh lamp, and no row
renders as `Blocked` or `Fail` for being out of remit (per architecture.md §Standard Contracts, a11y-plan §6
State-naming crosswalk, design-system.md §Anti-Patterns / Rejected Defaults). Second, **the 22 new rows**,
classified per intent §4 F2 + §5 boundary with titles and categories sourced verbatim from Pulse's own
`andromeda-pulse-0.3.0/requirements.md` and `verification-matrix.json`. Third, **`KNOWN_UNCLASSIFIED` empties** —
the anti-rot mechanism working as designed, since the drift check fails on a pinned-but-now-classified id.

Two decisions were taken by the operator at P4. **Representation:** the classification stays **code-native** —
`static COVERAGE` widens in Rust and `contracts/pulse-capabilities.toml` stays ids-only. This preserves the
documented no-runtime-IO property, keeps `coverage_matrix() -> &'static [CapabilityRow]` so no consumer signature
moves, and keeps `check_sut_drift` a genuine two-source comparison instead of a self-check (per architecture.md
§Established Decisions [Accepted Capability Set]; the alternative would have widened a validated input boundary
per security-plan.md §Input Validation). **Lane modes:** `auto` = P-073/P-074/P-079, `drive+observe` =
P-067/P-072/P-075 — P-075 aggregates the four delegated timing budgets and three of those four (P-025, P-027,
P-037) are already `drive+observe` in the shipped table, so classifying the aggregate as `auto` would contradict
its own members.

The chunk introduces the classification and keeps every existing surface correct; the **visual treatment** of
not-Conductor's rows (distinct in the matrix, the footer roll-up and the CLI table) is the next working entry,
_Out-of-scope classification treatment_, and is deliberately not designed here.

1. **Add the fourth variant** in `crates/conductor-core/src/coverage.rs`: `CoverageMode::NotConductors`, serde
   `rename = "not-conductors"`, matching `label()` arm, appended to `ALL` (which fixes render/tally order).
   Document the variant against `static-only` so the distinction is on the record. The wire spelling drops the
   apostrophe from the requirement's prose "not-Conductor's" — it is parsed by a CLI column, a TOML/JSON wire and
   a TS union, and it joins the existing lowercase family (`auto` / `drive+observe` / `static-only`).

2. **Widen the table** to the full accepted set using the existing `const fn row(...)`. Titles and categories come
   verbatim from research.md §"The 22 new capabilities"; the category for `P-061`..`P-078` is Pulse's v0.3.0 theme
   heading, and `P-079`..`P-082` — minted mid-build as operator-surfaced caps — carry `operator-surfaced`.
   Classification:
   - **auto (3)** — `P-073` deterministic L4 mode · `P-074` Tier1 incident-path reliability · `P-079`
     constellation severity live-wiring (workspace-key single-sourcing).
   - **drive+observe (3)** — `P-067` live-only service truth · `P-072` Investigate actions functional · `P-075`
     Conductor e2e + delegated-timing verification.
   - **not-conductors (16)** — `P-061`..`P-066`, `P-068`..`P-071`, `P-080`..`P-082` (Pulse's UI/visual set, its
     webview suite's to verify) · `P-076` (Pulse's own integration e2e) · `P-077` (demo injector) · `P-078`
     (agent-headful self-verify harness) — Pulse's own tooling.

3. **Empty the residual ledger** in `crates/conductor-core/src/drift.rs`: `KNOWN_UNCLASSIFIED = &[]`, and update
   its doc comment (it names this chunk as retirement owner). `committed_artifacts_match_the_known_gap` then
   degenerates to the plain zero-drift assertion its own doc anticipates. Keep
   `a_known_gap_entry_that_is_now_classified_is_drift` on its **synthetic** fixture — it must not reference the
   now-empty constant, or it stops testing pin-rot.

4. **Make the count assertions manifest-relative** — no literal `60`, `82`, or `1..=N` survives (per test-plan §1
   Scenario-catalog entity, §4). Derive every expected set by loading `contracts/pulse-capabilities.toml`:
   - `coverage.rs` — replace the two exactly-sixty tests with (a) set-equality against the manifest's accepted
     ids, (b) no-duplicates + ascending order. Contiguity then follows from the manifest rather than a literal.
   - `report/coverage.rs` — the footer golden splits in two so format stays locked without becoming tautological:
     an **exact-string** `assert_eq!` on `summary_line(&synthetic_rows)` (a module-private fn, directly testable)
     locks the format, and the real render is asserted manifest-relative on totals.
   - `cli/render.rs`, `cli/tests/cli_smoke.rs`, `tauri/commands.rs` — iterate the accepted set / compare against
     `coverage_matrix().len()` instead of `1..=60` / `P-060` / `Some(60)`. Rename the four `…sixty…` test fns.

5. **Extend the artifact-hygiene leak list** in `report/coverage.rs` with the new variant's Rust identifier, so
   the rendered Markdown is proven never to carry it (per obs-plan.md §11 Logs / PII Scrubbing).

6. **Update the webview mirror** in `CoverageMatrix.tsx`: add the wire spelling to the `CoverageMode` union
   (`:6`) **and to `tally()` (`:16-19`)** — `tally()` hardcodes three `by(…)` calls and would otherwise
   silently under-count the summary line (a11y-plan §4, SC 4.1.3). No new token, no lamp change, no glyph.

7. **Reconcile the doc/help sites** the widening makes false — the 8 in-code sites from research.md (note
   `cli/cli.rs:49` is clap **help text**, user-visible), and the 6 spec sites: `architecture.md:33`,
   `design-system.md:7` + `:257`, `layout-templates.md:121` + `:177` + `:222`. Follow the 2026-08-08 precedent:
   make them **manifest-relative** ("the manifest's accepted set"), never substitute a new literal `82`.

8. **Fix the wireframe sample caption** at `layout-templates.md:222`, in the same amendment pass. It is a
   sample, but it bakes **two coupled stale-derived facts** — `step 60/60 done` and a per-state tally
   (`55 Pass · 1 Calib · 1 Fail · 1 Manual · 1 Residual · 1 Blocked`) that itself sums to 60 — so leaving it
   recreates exactly the `:37`-vs-`:121` self-contradiction this chunk eliminates. Illustrative status is not an
   exemption: a baked count in a sample is the same class of stale derived fact. The invariant to restore is
   **internal coherence** — the caption's per-state counts must sum to its own step denominator, and that
   denominator must name the manifest's accepted set rather than a bare literal. Follow the form the same sweep
   already established one screen earlier at `:37` (`COVERAGE (manifest set) 82 loaded`), which keeps a
   concrete-looking sample while tagging the total as manifest-derived; the exact spelling is /implement's call
   so long as the sum and the denominator agree.
- None.

- `crates/conductor-core/src/coverage.rs` — the variant (+`ALL`, `label`, serde rename), 22 rows, the two count
  tests, module + field + fn docs (`:3-4`, `:49`, `:59`). **Impact:** `CoverageMode` @ 158 refs, 147 of them in
  this file; `coverage_matrix` @ 15 refs across 7 files.

- `crates/conductor-core/src/drift.rs` — `KNOWN_UNCLASSIFIED` → `[]` + doc. **Impact:** `KNOWN_UNCLASSIFIED` @ 2
  refs only (`drift.rs`, `lib.rs` re-export) — negligible blast radius.

- `crates/conductor-report/src/coverage.rs` — footer golden split, row-count assertion, leak list, module doc
  `:3`. **Impact:** `CoverageMode` @ `coverage.rs:34`, `:63`, `:65`, `:100`.

- `crates/conductor-cli/src/render.rs` — `for n in 1..=60` @ `:290`, test fn name `:288`, doc `:77`. **Impact:**
  the single out-of-core `CoverageMode` use is `r.mode.label()` @ `render.rs:167` — no new arm needed there.
- `crates/conductor-cli/src/cli.rs` — clap help text `:49` (user-visible).
- `crates/conductor-cli/src/commands/coverage.rs` — module doc `:1`.
- `crates/conductor-cli/tests/cli_smoke.rs` — `:189` fn name, `:195` `P-001`/`P-060` stdout assertion.

- `crates/conductor-tauri/src/commands.rs` — `Some(60)` @ `:327`, fn name `:317`, doc `:117`. **Impact:**
  `coverage_matrix` @ `commands.rs:124-125` + the `generate_handler!` registration @ `main.rs:23`; this crate
  never names `CoverageMode` (0 of the 158 refs) — the variant reaches the webview as a serde string.
- `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/src/components/CoverageMatrix.tsx` — union `:6`, `tally()` `:16-19`.

- `.andromeda/architecture.md` `:33` · `.andromeda/design-system.md` `:7`, `:257` ·
  `.andromeda/layout-templates.md` `:121`, `:177`, `:222` (the wireframe sample caption — both its step
  denominator and the per-state tally that sums to it).

**Do not touch:** `crates/conductor-cli/src/render.rs:42` (`Lamp::Blocked => 60` is an xterm-256 ANSI color
code, not a capability count).

```bash
cargo nextest run -p conductor-core
cargo nextest run -p conductor-report -p conductor-cli -p conductor-tauri
npm --prefix crates/conductor-tauri/ui run build
cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci
cargo test --workspace --doc
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo audit
cargo deny check
bash scripts/agent-run.sh run
```

`npm run build` must precede any workspace cargo command that compiles `conductor-tauri` — `generate_context!`
resolves `ui/dist` at compile time and a bare `cargo build` does not run `beforeBuildCommand` (frontend rules,
2026-06-24). `agent-run.sh run` wires this as its `ensure_frontend` step.

**ui-smoke — recorded skip, not a silent pass.** The webview a11y/contrast harness
(`@crabnebula/tauri-driver` + axe-core + colorjs.io) is display-gated to Linux+xvfb with a live Pulse and is not
part of the always-on gate (frontend rules, 2026-06-27). This chunk's frontend delta is a two-line mirror update
in `CoverageMatrix.tsx` with no token, lamp or DOM-structure change; `npm run build`'s `tsc --noEmit` is its
typecheck gate. The real-webview sweep remains the Epoch-5 _Desktop a11y sweep_ entry.
Each verifiable; traces to the extracts' contributions. Links `verification-matrix.json#v2-03`.

- (arch/v2-03) Every id `contracts/pulse-capabilities.toml` accepts resolves to exactly one `CoverageMode`, with
  zero unclassified entries and no id classified that the manifest does not accept — asserted by set equality
  against the loaded manifest, not a literal count (per architecture.md §Established Decisions [Accepted
  Capability Set]; verification-matrix.json#v2-03).

- (arch/v2-03) The not-Conductor's set is **explicitly enumerated** as 16 classified rows — Pulse's UI/visual set
  plus its own tooling — never implied by absence, and no capability is expressed as `Blocked`, `ManualCheck` or
  a missing row (per architecture.md §Standard Contracts, §Cross-cutting Patterns Scope law;
  verification-matrix.json#v2-03).

- (arch) `Verdict` and `ReportState` are byte-identical to their §Standard Contracts spellings; the new mode
  appears only on the coverage axis and never in a run-report envelope's `verdict`/`state` (per architecture.md
  §Standard Contracts, §Conventions Error handling).

- (arch) `coverage_matrix()` keeps its `&'static [CapabilityRow]` signature and its no-runtime-IO property;
  `conductor-core` gains no new dependency edge (per architecture.md §Established Decisions [Module Boundaries]).

- (tests) `conductor_core::check_sut_drift` passes against the committed artifacts with `KNOWN_UNCLASSIFIED == []`,
  and an injected unclassified id still returns `Err` — assertion strength preserved, not loosened (per
  test-plan.md §4; security-plan.md §Security Anti-Patterns § Universal).

- (tests) No coverage or classification assertion names a literal capability count or P-ID range anywhere in the
  workspace; all seven previously-literal sites derive their expected set from the manifest (per test-plan.md §1
  Scenario-catalog entity, §4).

- (tests) The fourth variant has an exact-string serde-wire golden and a `label()` assertion at unit level, and
  `summary_line`'s format stays locked by an exact-string golden over synthetic rows (per test-plan.md §4
  conductor-report bullet).

- (obs) The rendered `coverage-matrix.md` and the CLI coverage table contain no Rust identifier for the new
  variant and none of `CoverageMode`/`CapabilityRow`/`coverage_matrix`/host-path tokens —
  `no_host_paths_or_struct_names_leak` extended with the new identifier and green (per obs-plan.md §11 Logs /
  PII Scrubbing).

- (obs) No new span name, no span added to `coverage_matrix()` or `check_sut_drift`, and no new log field (per
  obs-plan.md §11 Spans, §11 Telemetry Strategy).

- (a11y) The fourth mode renders as visible DOM text in the matrix Mode cell and as text in the CLI table — never
  color-only or glyph-only; `tally()` counts all four modes and its per-mode counts sum to `rows.length` (per
  a11y-plan.md §11 Visual SC 1.4.1, §4 SC 4.1.3).

- (a11y) The six-lamp set in `lamp.rs` / `lamp.ts` is unchanged: no seventh lamp, no not-Conductor's →
  `Blocked`/`Fail` projection (per a11y-plan.md §6 State-naming crosswalk).

- (design) The change introduces zero new hex, ANSI or palette entries, and the widened matrix stays a dense
  single-row-per-P-ID list — no card/tile grid (per design-system.md §Surface: desktop-webview / Tokens,
  §Component Patterns 3).

- (layouts) The CLI coverage table still renders exactly its 4 columns and the run/SLO table its 6, every state
  cell keeps its `[PASS]`/`[HOLD]`/`[FAIL]`/`[BLOCKED]` prefix, and no surface gains a column, lamp or card (per
  layout-templates.md §cli content block 1, §desktop content block 1).

- (docs) `architecture.md:33`, `design-system.md:7`/`:257`, `layout-templates.md:121`/`:177` and the eight
  in-code doc/help sites name the manifest's accepted set rather than any literal — de-hardcoded, not
  re-substituted with `82` (per architecture.md §Established Decisions [Accepted Capability Set]).

- (layouts/docs) The `layout-templates.md:222` sample caption is internally coherent after the change: its
  per-state counts sum to its own step denominator, and that denominator names the manifest's accepted set —
  no reader can derive a stale total from the sample, and no `60`-summing tally survives anywhere in the file

  Wireframe / suite run; §Wireframe — Run console (idle) header strip).

- (security) `cargo audit` exits 0, `cargo deny check` is ok across all four classes, `Cargo.lock` is un-drifted,

- (tests) `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci` returns 0 with zero retries, `cargo test --workspace

  Contracts, §Cross-cutting Patterns Scope law · security-plan.md §Input Validation, §Error Handling,
  §Dependency Security, §Data Protection · test-plan.md §1, §4, §6, §9, §10 · obs-plan.md §4, §6, §11 ·

- Research files inspected: `crates/conductor-core/src/{coverage,drift,capability_manifest}.rs` ·
  `crates/conductor-report/src/coverage.rs` · `crates/conductor-cli/src/render.rs` ·
  `crates/conductor-tauri/src/commands.rs` · `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/src/components/CoverageMatrix.tsx` ·
  `andromeda-pulse-0.3.0/requirements.md` · `andromeda-pulse-0.3.0/verification-matrix.json`.

- **Expected tallies after the change** (useful as a self-check, but assert them manifest-relatively, never as
  literals): 82 total = 43 auto · 16 drive+observe · 7 static-only · 16 not-conductors. The existing 60 rows keep
  their classification unchanged — this chunk adds rows and a variant, it does not re-classify P-001..P-060.

- **Order matters.** Emptying `KNOWN_UNCLASSIFIED` before the 22 rows land makes `check_sut_drift` fail with "22
  accepted but unclassified"; adding the rows before emptying it fails with "22 already classified — shrink the
  known gap". Both directions are the gate working correctly. Land the rows and the empty pin in one change.

- **`P-075` is Conductor's own deliverable but classified `drive+observe`.** Its verification lands in Epoch 4

- **`layout-templates.md:222` is IN scope** (operator decision at P5, overriding the layouts extract's
  "may stay"). Its rationale generalizes: a baked count inside an illustrative sample is the same stale-derived-fact
  class as a baked count in prose, and the file is already open for `:121`/`:177` in this amendment pass. Watch the
  coupling — the caption's tally and its step denominator must be fixed **together** or the sample becomes
  internally inconsistent, which is worse than the stale total it replaces.

**Chunk:** Current-SUT coverage classification — every manifest capability classified across four modes incl. the recorded not-Conductor's boundary, retiring the KNOWN_UNCLASSIFIED residual ledger (conductor-core, v2-03)

data.head: ## Graph impact (from the code-graph query — row counts are the run-dir trace's `rows` field)

body: - **`CoverageMode`** — **158 refs**: 147 inside `conductor-core/src/coverage.rs` itself (the 60 row literals + tests), 3 `drift.rs`, 1 `lib.rs` (re-export), **6 `conductor-report/src/coverage.rs`**, **1 `conductor-cli/src/render.rs`** (`r.mode.label()` @ `render.rs:167`). Only two out-of-core consumer files.

- **`coverage_matrix`** — **15 refs** across 7 files: `conductor-cli/src/render.rs` (2), `conductor-report/src/coverage.rs` (3), `conductor-tauri/src/commands.rs` (2 — one is core's, one the command's own same-named fn), `conductor-tauri/src/main.rs` (1, the `generate_handler!` registration), plus core-internal (`coverage.rs` 4, `drift.rs` 2, `lib.rs` 1).
- **`CapabilityRow`** — **40 refs**: core 23, report 11, cli 4, tauri 2.
- **`KNOWN_UNCLASSIFIED`** — **2 refs only** (`drift.rs` definition, `lib.rs` re-export). Emptying it has essentially zero blast radius.

- **`conductor-core` crate edges** — **6 rows, all INBOUND, zero outbound**: `conductor-cli`, `conductor-report`, `conductor-run`, `conductor-tauri`, `conductor-timeline`, `conductor-verify` → `conductor-core`. Adding a variant is a downstream-only fan-out; core gains no edge.

- **`conductor-tauri` does NOT reference `CoverageMode`** (0 rows in the 158) — it moves `CapabilityRow` through serde, so the fourth variant reaches the webview as a *string*. The binding site is the TS union at `CoverageMatrix.tsx:6`, not Rust.

- **Wire-spelling single-truth** (`coverage.rs:36-42` + `:180-192`): `label()` returns exactly the serde `rename`, asserted by `mode_label_matches_serde_wire` + a JSON round-trip. Every renderer prints `label()` / the serialized string — so one new `#[serde(rename)]` propagates to Markdown, CLI and webview without a per-surface string.

- **Fixed-order tally over `CoverageMode::ALL`** (`conductor-report/src/coverage.rs:62-69`, mirrored in `CoverageMatrix.tsx:16-19`): the footer/summary iterates `ALL`, so a 4th variant auto-appears in the Markdown summary line — but the **TS `tally()` hardcodes its three `by(…)` calls** and will silently under-count until edited.
- **Pure-function render** (`conductor-report/src/coverage.rs:24-38`): no clock, no IO ⇒ exact-string golden-testable; `write` is an atomic `.tmp`→rename overwrite.

- **Manifest boundary shape** (`capability_manifest.rs:36-82`): one `load` → one private `validate`; read faults carry `e.kind()` only, parse faults go through `sanitize_error`. Any schema extension extends `validate`, never a second parse path.

- **Artifact-hygiene leak test** (`conductor-report/src/coverage.rs:107-115`): asserts the rendered Markdown contains none of `CoverageMatrix` / `CapabilityRow` / `CoverageMode` / `coverage_matrix` / host-path prefixes. A new variant's Rust identifier must be added to that list.
- **Rust identifier ≠ rendered string**: the leak test above means the fourth variant's *identifier* must never appear in output; only its `label()` does.
- **`const fn row(...)`** (`coverage.rs:64-71`) is the table's constructor — new rows use it verbatim.
- **Manual span, not the attribute** on the Tauri command (`commands.rs:123`) — already correct; the row-count change needs no instrumentation change.

- **Category vocabulary**: existing rows use the v0.2.0 audit's category names ("Hard Signal Detection", "Privacy & Trust", …). Pulse v0.3.0's equivalents are its 5 theme headings (Window & shell hygiene · State honesty & legibility · AI-debug climax · External verification · Test gap & housekeeping).

title: Boundaries — what this chunk is NOT

data.head: ## Boundaries — what this chunk is NOT

body:
- **Not the live proof.** This chunk authors the CATALOG. `v2-04`'s acceptance ("each drive a live Pulse and
  yield a non-blocked verdict via MCP read-back, with journal and `runs.db` evidence per scenario") cannot
  pass here: the faithful per-phase dispatcher (`v2-08`), real per-check read-back extraction (`v2-09`) and
  a live `ready: true` preflight (`v2-10`) are all Epoch-2 entries, and `execute_scenario` still grades every
  check against the literal `"incidents-listed"` (`conductor-run/src/lib.rs:216`). This chunk therefore
  **partially advances `v2-04`** and leaves it `chunk: null` per the verification-matrix multi-chunk rule,
  citing it in provenance rather than claiming it.

- **Not a Pulse fix.** Intent §5 states the new non-goal explicitly: Conductor does not fix Pulse. F10's
  workspace-key divergence has a Pulse-side remedy; Conductor records the requirement, detects the
  condition and fails loudly. Authoring the P-079 scenario is the *record*, not the fix. The detection
  itself ("Workspace-key divergence probe") is a separate Epoch-2 entry.

- **Not UI automation.** The standing non-goal holds: visual claims are operator-checklist items, which is
  precisely why P-067 and P-072 are `DriveObserve` and not `Auto`.

- **Not P-073 / P-074.** They stay in `UNBACKED_AUTO`; they are owned by the Epoch-2 "Pulse run contract"
  and Epoch-3 "fingerprint-storm live proof" entries. Only `P-079` leaves the pin here.
- **No new crate, no new seam, no dependency delta** expected.

- **Marker:** 2026-08-09-interpretation-correctness-posture · **Version:** conductor-0.2.0 · **Generated:** 2026-08-09T18:06:03Z

Pulse's deterministic L4 mode (`ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC=true`) replaces the Llama-3.2-3B inference
with a canned `L4Output`, which is what makes every live leg conductor-0.2.0 plans reproducible. The cost,
named in intent §4 **F3**, is that those legs exercise the plumbing and never the interpretation — while
Pulse's own positioning memo calls interpretation-correctness *"the single most important test in all of
Pulse"*. This chunk makes that boundary a **recorded, enforced decision** rather than an accident.

`v2-05` admits two branches and the operator chose **Branch B — a recorded deferral**, because Branch A is
not buildable inside this chunk's boundaries: a real-model leg must *assert the top hypothesis*, but
`execute_scenario` grades every `ExpectedCheck` against the literal placeholder `"incidents-listed"`
(`conductor-run/src/lib.rs:216`), and real per-check read-back extraction is `v2-09` in Epoch 2, which this
chunk's scope excludes. A real-model leg is also non-deterministic by construction and so could never enter
the zero-retry CI set (per test-plan §10 + arch §CI/CD).

The deferral is made **load-bearing** rather than narrated by the finding P3 surfaced: **eleven
`CoverageMode::Auto` capabilities have no verifying scenario at all** — `P-031`, `P-033`, `P-034`, `P-039`,
`P-041`, `P-042`, `P-043`, `P-044`, `P-073`, `P-074`, `P-079` — and **no gate in the repo can see this**.
`check_sut_drift` compares classification↔manifest, never classification↔scenarios, so Conductor currently
claims "auto-verified" for 43 capabilities while 11 of those claims have nothing behind them. Four of the
eleven (`P-031`/`P-033`/`P-034`/`P-044`) are exactly the diagnostic-quality cluster F3 says deterministic L4
bypasses. So this chunk ships a `check_sut_drift` **sibling** that holds the unbacked-`Auto` set to an exact
pinned ledger, carries the interpretation deferral (and its named owner, a **conductor-0.3.0 entry**) in that
pin's doc comment, and surfaces the count on the three coverage roll-ups so a reader of a green artifact can
see what the green does not cover. Per the 2026-08-09 sut-drift-check pattern: the gate is green immediately
and can only shrink under compulsion.

1. **Add the `CoreError` variant.** Extend `crates/conductor-core/src/error.rs` with a fourth thiserror
   variant for unbacked coverage — a harness fault carrying a named reason, distinct from
   `CoreError::SutDrift` (that asks "did Pulse's ledger advance past our classification?"; this asks "does
   our own `Auto` claim have anything behind it?"). Message is identity-only: capability ids and counts, never
   a filesystem path and never an internal type name (security-plan §Error Handling).

3. **Add `check_scenario_backing` to `drift.rs`,** shaped exactly like `check_sut_drift` (`drift.rs:47`) — a
   pure set comparison over `BTreeSet<&str>`, no runtime IO inside the function, the caller supplying the
   scenario-claimed ids. It takes the classification rows, the P-IDs claimed by the committed catalog, and the
   pinned ledger; returns `Ok(())` iff the unbacked-`Auto` set equals the pin **exactly**. Three drift
   conditions, each named separately in the message (mirror `drift_message`, `drift.rs:70`):
   - an `Auto` row with no scenario and not pinned → a new unbacked claim;
   - a pinned id that *does* have a scenario → pin rot, shrink the ledger;
   - a pinned id no longer classified `Auto` → the pin lost its backing (reclassified or retired).
   Only `Auto` rows participate: `DriveObserve` is operator-confirmed by definition, `StaticOnly` and
   `NotConductors` are deliberately not Conductor's to drive (`coverage.rs:16-36`).

4. **Export both** from `crates/conductor-core/src/lib.rs:37`, beside the existing
   `pub use drift::{KNOWN_UNCLASSIFIED, check_sut_drift};`.

5. **Assert the gate over the committed artifacts.** `check_sut_drift` has **no production call site** — it is
   live via the in-crate test `committed_artifacts_match_the_known_gap` (`drift.rs:138`), which is the release
   gate because `cargo nextest` is. Mirror that exactly: a test that loads the real
   `contracts/pulse-capabilities.toml`, walks the real `scenarios/` catalog via
   `conductor_core::list_scenarios` (its `ScenarioSummary` already carries `p_ids`,
   `scenario_catalog.rs:23`), and asserts `check_scenario_backing` is green against `UNBACKED_AUTO`. Add unit
   tests for each of the three drift conditions plus an empty-pin pass, mirroring `drift.rs:145-177`, and an
   identity-only message test mirroring `drift.rs:178`.

6. **Surface the count on the three coverage roll-ups — reading the pin, not the filesystem.** This is the
   architectural move that keeps the change small: the gate proves `UNBACKED_AUTO` equals reality, so the
   roll-ups may cite `UNBACKED_AUTO.len()` with **no IO and no signature change**, preserving
   `CapabilityRow`'s documented "no allocation and no runtime IO" property (`coverage.rs:59`).
   - `crates/conductor-report/src/coverage.rs:76` (`summary_line`) — qualify the auto term, e.g.
     `43 auto (11 unbacked)`. It is a **qualifier on an existing summand, never a fifth summand**: the
     per-mode counts must still sum to the row denominator (layout-templates §Component — Footer).
   - `crates/conductor-cli/src/render.rs:92` (`coverage_summary`) — the identical fact, adapted not forked.
   - The webview coverage header strip — same fact. Source it through a minimal read-only
     `#[tauri::command]` beside `coverage_matrix` (`crates/conductor-tauri/src/commands.rs:121`), following
     the shipped "command returns the core type, never re-author in TS" pattern. **Do not mirror the pin in
     TypeScript.**
   - Every number stays derived; no literal counts anywhere (the 2026-08-08/08-09 de-hardcoding rule).

7. **Resolve the folded-in `cargo audit` PREREQ.** Re-run it. If green, the deferral closes — note the heal.
   If it still fails on `duplicate advisory ID: RUSTSEC-2026-0244`, **raise the cargo-audit floor** in
   `.andromeda/security-plan.md` §Dependency Security to the fixed release. Explicitly **not** a `deny.toml`
   entry and **not** a CI edit (`.claude/rules/security.md` 2026-08-09). Note that security-plan is a spec
   master — see Implementation notes; the floor raise is recorded as an Expected amendment, not edited here.
- _(none)_ — every change extends an existing module.
- `crates/conductor-core/src/error.rs` — add the unbacked-coverage `CoreError` variant (identity-only message).

- `crates/conductor-core/src/drift.rs` — add `UNBACKED_AUTO` (the pin + the deferral record in its doc
  comment) and `check_scenario_backing` (+ its tests); preserve the existing `BTreeSet` three-condition shape
  and the identity-only `drift_message` discipline.
- `crates/conductor-core/src/lib.rs` — extend the `pub use drift::{…}` re-export at line 37.

- `crates/conductor-report/src/coverage.rs` — qualify the auto term in `summary_line` (line 76); update the
  exact-string roll-up goldens at `:107`/`:133` and keep `summary_counts_sum_to_the_row_count` (`:159`) green.
- `crates/conductor-cli/src/render.rs` — the same qualifier in `coverage_summary` (line 92).

- `crates/conductor-tauri/src/commands.rs` — a minimal read-only command exposing the unbacked ids/count
  beside `coverage_matrix` (line 121).

- `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/src/components/CoverageMatrix.tsx` (+ its CSS if a class is needed) — render the
  qualifier in the header strip; **sweep the stale `CoverageMatrix.css:1` comment "all 60 capabilities"**

data.head: ## Measured facts this chunk must reckon with

body: Computed over `coverage.rs` (82 rows: 43 Auto / 16 DriveObserve / 7 StaticOnly / 16 NotConductors — matching the shipped roll-up) versus the 40 distinct P-IDs claimed across `scenarios/*.toml`:

**11 `Auto`-classified capabilities have no scenario at all:**
`P-031` Report Structure · **`P-033` Ranked Hypothesis Generation** · `P-034` Suggested Investigation Steps · `P-039` MCP Delivery When Configured · `P-041` Persistent Incident Corpus · `P-042` Cross-Session Continuity · `P-043` Project-Scoped Memory · `P-044` Retrieval-Augmented Interpretation · `P-073` Deterministic env-gated L4 mode · `P-074` Tier1 incident-path reliability under load · `P-079` Constellation severity live-wiring.

So P-033 is **not a singular anomaly** — it is one of eleven `Auto` claims with nothing behind them, and no gate in the repo can see this (`check_sut_drift` compares classification↔manifest, not classification↔scenarios). Three of the eleven (`P-073`/`P-074`/`P-079`) are already routed to named future entries; the interpretation cluster (`P-031`/`P-033`/`P-034`/`P-044`) is precisely the diagnostic-quality set F3 says deterministic L4 bypasses.
Depends on the branch chosen at P4. Candidates, none yet committed:
- `scenarios/` — a new P-033 TOML (Branch A, or a declare-only Branch-B artifact).
- `.claude/rules/verification-harness.md` — the `:47` open-decision entry, which this chunk closes either way (a wrap-owned Session-Additions edit).
- `crates/conductor-core/src/coverage.rs` — only if the posture reclassifies P-033 (a `check_sut_drift`-governed edit).
- `crates/conductor-core/src/drift.rs` — only if the posture becomes a live gate over the Auto-without-scenario set.

1. **Branch A is not buildable inside this chunk's boundaries.** A real-model leg must *assert the top hypothesis*, but `execute_scenario` grades every check against the literal `"incidents-listed"` (`conductor-run/src/lib.rs:216`); real per-check extraction is `v2-09` in Epoch 2, which this chunk's scope explicitly excludes. Building it here means pulling Epoch-2 work forward. → P4 decision.

2. **Should the posture be a live gate or a recorded decision?** The research surfaces a concrete gate candidate (Auto-classified rows with no verifying scenario — currently 11, invisible to every existing check), which would make the posture load-bearing in the way `check_sut_drift` is. → P4 decision.
3. **Does the deferral name P-033 alone or the whole interpretation cluster?** The honest scope is `P-031`/`P-033`/`P-034`/`P-044`. → P4 decision.

**Working-route entry (Epoch 1 — Foundation: re-aim at the SUT):**
> Interpretation-correctness posture — one real-model leg with a known root cause and asserted top
> hypothesis, or a recorded deferral naming its owner
**Version:** conductor-0.2.0 · **Capability:** `v2-05` (method `manual`, status `planned`)

Pulse now ships a deterministic L4 mode (`ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC=true`): a canned `L4Output`
replaces the Llama-3.2-3B inference so the incident pipeline becomes reproducible. Every live leg
conductor-0.2.0 plans (Epochs 2–4) depends on that mode. The consequence intent §4 **F3** names:

> with `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC=true` the canned `L4Output` replaces the model, so every live leg
> 0.2.0 plans exercises **the plumbing and never the interpretation** — while Pulse's own positioning memo
> names interpretation-correctness ("inject a known root cause, verify the top hypothesis identifies it")
> *"the single most important test in all of Pulse"*.

So a fully green Conductor run under deterministic L4 proves that telemetry flows, cues fire, incidents
form, read-back works and SLOs hold — and proves **nothing** about whether Pulse's explanation is right.
This chunk makes that boundary a **recorded decision** rather than an accident.
The recorded posture, in exactly one of the two forms `v2-05`'s acceptance admits:

- **Branch A — a real-model correctness leg.** Deterministic mode OFF, a *known* root cause injected, the
  **top hypothesis asserted to identify it**, and the leg passes. This is the P-033 (Ranked Hypothesis
  Generation) path.

- **Branch B — a recorded deferral.** The gap is deferred **with a named owner**, together with the
  explicit statement that **"Conductor green" does not mean interpretation is trustworthy**.

Absence of both is a `v2-05` failure. Which branch is taken is an **operator decision at plan time**

**Marker:** `2026-08-09-out-of-scope-classification-treatment`
**Version:** conductor-0.2.0 · Epoch 1 — Foundation: re-aim at the SUT
**Working entry:** _Out-of-scope classification treatment — not-Conductor's rows distinct in coverage matrix,
footer roll-up and CLI table, never Blocked or Fail_

The SUT capability manifest accepts 82 capabilities; 16 of them are **not Conductor's to verify** — Pulse's
UI/visual set and its own tooling, outside Conductor's remit by standing non-goal. That boundary is now a
recorded decision in code, but on every rendered surface an out-of-scope row still reads like any other row.
This chunk makes the out-of-scope classification **visually distinct** wherever coverage is rendered, and
guarantees it never reads as a **failure** (`Fail`) or as a **never-measured verdict** (`Blocked`) — the two
states an undifferentiated row is most likely to be mistaken for.

The classification is a statement about *remit*, not about *outcome*. A reader scanning the matrix must be
able to tell, without counting or cross-referencing, that these rows were never in play.
Carried forward from `2026-08-09-current-sut-coverage-classification`:

- `CoverageMode::NotConductors` exists in `conductor-core/src/coverage.rs` with the stable wire spelling
  `not-conductors` (serde rename + `label()`, pinned by `not_conductors_wire_spelling_is_stable`).

- **Marker:** 2026-08-09-sut-drift-check · **Version:** conductor-0.2.0 · **Generated:** 2026-08-09T12:15Z

`2026-08-08-sut-capability-manifest` made the *accepted* capability set data — `contracts/pulse-capabilities.toml`,
82 ids at `sut_version = "v0.3.0"` — so a scenario may name anything Pulse actually ships. Nothing, however,
asserts that Conductor has *reckoned with* those ids: `coverage_matrix()` is still a `static [CapabilityRow; 60]`
over `P-001..P-060` (`crates/conductor-core/src/coverage.rs:60,73`). Manifest and classification disagree by 22
ids and no gate says so. That is the exact failure the version exists to end — 22 Pulse capabilities went
unnoticed across a 41-day pause because nothing in the repo could notice.

This chunk builds the detector: an offline, deterministic comparison of the shipped `CapabilityManifest` against
the shipped coverage classification that returns a **harness fault** naming the offending ids. The accepted set
enters only through `CapabilityManifest::load` / `accepts` (the chunk's CARRY) — no second parse, no re-derived
id universe, no hardcoded range as the reference (per architecture.md §Established Decisions [Accepted Capability
Set] + security-plan.md §Input Validation). Drift is `Result::Err`, never a `Verdict`/`ReportState`, upholding
the verdict/error wall (per architecture.md §Conventions "Error handling" + test-plan.md §3).

**The gate is live and green from day one, via a pinned known-gap ledger** (operator decision, P4). A plain
zero-drift assertion would fail on the committed tree and block this chunk's own wrap, so `check` compares the
*observed* gap against an explicit pinned list of the 22 ids Conductor knowingly has not classified yet. Today
that matches exactly → `Ok`. The moment Pulse's ledger advances (a manifest id outside the pin), or the pin rots
(a pinned id that has since been classified), or a classified row loses its manifest backing, the check fails
naming the ids. The next chunk (`v2-03`, *Current-SUT coverage classification*) empties the pin and the check
degenerates to the plain zero-drift assertion it was always meant to be. The surface is the **core unit tier
only** (operator decision, P4) — matching `verification-matrix.json#v2-02`'s declared `method: unit`, enforced in
CI through the existing `agent-run run` dogfood step, and leaving operator-facing surfacing to the Epoch-6
*Coverage completeness gate* entry that already owns it. No cli output constraint binds this chunk.

1. **Add the `SutDrift` harness-fault variant** to `CoreError` in `crates/conductor-core/src/error.rs`. The enum
   is `#[non_exhaustive]` and its doc explicitly anticipates later chunks extending the surface (`error.rs:12`),
   so this is the sanctioned extension point — do **not** overload `Config` ("scenario config error: …" is the
   wrong label for a SUT-drift condition). Message prefix should name the condition, not a struct.

2. **Create `crates/conductor-core/src/drift.rs`** holding the comparison. Confirmed name-free: the P3 graph
   existence query for `%drift%` returned 0 rows across the workspace.

3. **Model the two directions.** Compute, from the manifest's `capabilities` and the classification's `p_id`s:
   - `unclassified` — manifest ids with no classification row (the acceptance's named direction);
   - `retired` — classification rows with no manifest entry (a capability Pulse dropped). Not required by
     `v2-02`'s acceptance, but it is one extra set difference and it reports nothing today (the classification is
     a subset of the manifest), so it is a free latent guard rather than added risk.

2. **Surface.** Test-only (`conductor-core` unit tier), or additionally reachable from the harness — extending the existing `conductor coverage` verb vs a `preflight`-style exit-code gate? This decides whether the design/layouts cli constraints bind at all.

3. **Direction of the comparison.** `v2-02`'s acceptance names one direction (manifest ids the classification lacks). Should the check also report the reverse (classification rows absent from the manifest — a capability Pulse *retired*)? Not required by the acceptance; cheap to include.

**Working entry (verbatim):**
> SUT-drift check — loud failure when Pulse's ledger advances past the capability set Conductor knows
> `CARRY:` the accepted set now ships as `contracts/pulse-capabilities.toml`
> (`sut_version`/`captured_at`/`capabilities[]`) with `CapabilityManifest::load` + `accepts` — build the drift
> check over THAT, don't re-source it.

**Version:** conductor-0.2.0 · **Epoch:** 1 — Foundation: re-aim at the SUT
**Capability:** `verification-matrix.json#v2-02` (intent §Theme 1 · F1, second clause)

`2026-08-08-sut-capability-manifest` made the *accepted* set data (`contracts/pulse-capabilities.toml`,
82 ids, `sut_version = "v0.3.0"`), so a scenario may now name any id Pulse actually ships. But nothing
asserts that Conductor has *reckoned with* those ids. The coverage classification
(`crates/conductor-core/src/coverage.rs`) is still a `static [CapabilityRow; 60]` over `P-001..P-060`,
with tests that assert exactly-sixty and contiguity. So today the manifest knows 82 capabilities and the
classification knows 60 — a 22-id blind spot (`P-061..P-082`) that no gate reports.

That is precisely the failure mode the version exists to end: 22 new Pulse capabilities went unnoticed
across a 41-day pause because nothing in the repo could notice. Widening a number does not fix it; a
*check* does.

A drift check over the two artifacts that already exist — the shipped `CapabilityManifest` and the
shipped coverage classification — that fails loudly, naming the unknown ids, when the manifest carries
capabilities the classification does not cover, and passes when the two are in sync.

Per the CARRY: the accepted set is **read through `CapabilityManifest::load` / `accepts`**. This chunk
does not re-source, re-parse, duplicate, or re-derive the accepted set, and does not introduce a second
place where "which P-IDs exist" is written down.

The check's failure output is the deliverable as much as the boolean: it must name the drifted ids (and
the manifest's `sut_version` / `captured_at`, which exist to make the message actionable), so an operator
reading a red gate knows which Pulse release moved and what is owed — not merely that a count mismatched.

Amended at P4: the comparison also reports the **reverse** direction — a classified row with no manifest
entry, i.e. a capability Pulse retired. `v2-02`'s acceptance does not require it, and it reports nothing
today (the classification is a subset of the manifest), but it is one extra set difference and therefore
a free latent guard rather than added risk.

- **Does NOT classify anything.** Extending the classification to the current SUT set is the next
  chunk (*Current-SUT coverage classification*, `v2-03`), which carries its own CARRY about `coverage.rs`
  being `&'static str` rows with "no runtime IO" and its two exactly-sixty tests. This chunk builds the
  detector; that chunk makes it green. **RESOLVED at P4 (operator decision) — amended here, per
  validation.md's intent-incomplete rule:** the scope originally framed this as a two-way choice (hard
  gate red until `v2-03`, vs a non-gating signal). Planning surfaced a third and better option, which was
  chosen: the check is **live and gating from day one against a pinned known-gap ledger** holding today's
  22 unclassified ids. It is green on the committed tree, and fails the moment a manifest id appears
  outside the pin (a Pulse release), a pinned id gets classified (pin rot), or a classified row loses its
  manifest backing. `v2-03` empties the pin and the check becomes the plain zero-drift assertion. The pin
  is a *residual ledger*, never a second source of the accepted set.

- **Does NOT query a live Pulse.** `v2-02`'s method is `unit`; the manifest is the recorded SUT proxy and
  the check is an offline artifact-vs-artifact assertion. Detecting that Pulse's *live* ledger moved past
  the manifest is a different (live-path) concern and is not in this chunk.

- **Does NOT edit the manifest** — `contracts/pulse-capabilities.toml` stays as shipped; re-aiming at a
  newer Pulse remains a manifest edit, and this check is what makes such an edit impossible to make
  silently.

- **Does NOT touch scenario validation.** `Scenario::from_toml_str_with` / `check_capabilities` /
  `pid_format` are unchanged; this is a coverage-universe check, not a membership check.
- **No new crate edge.** Both artifacts live in `conductor-core`.
| Surface | Involvement |
| `crates/conductor-core/src/capability_manifest.rs` | consumed (`load` / `accepts` / `default_path`) — read-only |
| `crates/conductor-core/src/coverage.rs` | consumed (`coverage_matrix()`) — the classified universe |

| `crates/conductor-core/src/error.rs` | modified — a new `SutDrift` variant on the `#[non_exhaustive]` `CoreError` (its documented extension point); a drift failure must respect the verdict/error wall, never a `Verdict`/`ReportState` |

| CLI / agent-run surface | **RESOLVED at P4: not touched.** The check lands in the core unit tier only, matching `v2-02`'s declared `method: unit`; CI enforcement rides the existing `agent-run run` dogfood step, and operator-facing surfacing stays with the Epoch-6 *Coverage completeness gate* entry that already owns it |
| `contracts/pulse-capabilities.toml` | read-only input; never rewritten by the check |

title: Invariants this chunk must not break

data.head: ## Invariants this chunk must not break

body:
- The accepted set is DATA (manifest), never a compile-time constant — the check must not reintroduce a
  hardcoded id range or a second hardcoded count.
- Verdict/error wall: a drift condition is a harness-side failure, not a scenario `Blocked`/`Fail`.

- Artifact hygiene: the failure message names capability ids and manifest metadata — never absolute host
  paths or internal struct names.
- Determinism: the check reads committed artifacts only; same tree ⇒ same result.

_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-08-09-sut-load-envelope · **Version:** conductor-0.2.0 · **Generated:** 2026-08-09T21:20:00Z

Pulse's DuckDB append path stalls after ~10 minutes of sustained 10k/s storm: ingest keeps receiving while
`duckdb.append` stops, so `viz.query.traces` returns 0 rows and no new incidents form until restart (intent
§Theme 1 F4). Conductor's whole method is sustained shaped load, so the harness can induce that stall itself —
and today nothing distinguishes "Pulse is broken" from "we drove Pulse outside its proven-good region." A long
storm run would report the SUT for a fault the harness caused. This chunk closes that attribution hole from
both ends: it **records the envelope where scenario authors meet it and asserts the catalog against it**
(`v2-06`), and it **classifies an over-envelope run as environment-suspect rather than Fail** (`v2-07`).
Two P4 decisions shape the build, both operator-confirmed.

**The envelope is asserted on its derivable axis, with the un-derivable axis recorded rather than faked.**
Research established that the committed scenario model carries no rate or occurrence-count field at all
(`phase_spec.rs` — `PhaseSpec{name, gap_ms, emission}`, `EmissionSpec{signal}`), so the storm-rate half of the
envelope simply is not derivable from committed data; `fingerprint-storm.toml` records in-file that the driver
infers per-phase counts from *phase names*. A duration-only bound would also be actively wrong: `activity-floor`
runs 3900s but fifty of its sixty-five minutes are deliberate quiet gaps, and the SUT stalls on sustained
throughput, not elapsed time. So the envelope artifact carries **both** terms with their provenance, the gate
asserts the derivable one (total scenario duration), and the two predominantly-quiet scenarios are **exact-set
pinned exemptions carrying their reason** — the project's own established move for a gate that must go live
before the work making it green exists (`.claude/rules/testing.md` 2026-08-09; the `KNOWN_UNCLASSIFIED` /
`UNBACKED_AUTO` ledgers at `drift.rs:38,61`). The rate axis is named as owed to Epoch 2's *Faithful emission
dispatcher*, which is what will make it derivable. This keeps the chunk inside its scope boundary — it must not
pre-build Epoch 2 — while making the un-assertable axis visible instead of silently absent.

**`environment-suspect` is a run-level qualifier, not a sixth `ReportState`.** The code-graph puts 204
`ReportState` references across 16 files in 6 crates, plus the webview `LAMP_META` mirror; arch is explicit that
widening `state ∈ {Pass, Fail, ManualCheck, KnownResidual, Blocked}` is an architecture amendment with lockstep
fan-out (per architecture.md §Standard Contracts). Five of seven distillers independently landed on the
qualifier: obs cites the `(N unbacked)` precedent for a qualifier riding alongside a closed set, layouts and
a11y both cite the out-of-scope Mode-cell precedent where a reused token deliberately did *not* become a
seventh lamp state, and tests calls it "the cheaper binding" because it leaves the polled envelope fields
intact. The qualifier therefore scopes to the **run**, leaves `RunRecord`'s eleven fields and the `runs` table's
eleven columns provably untouched, and never alters any per-check `state`.

1. **Commit the envelope artifact** — `contracts/pulse-load-envelope.toml`, mirroring
   `contracts/pulse-capabilities.toml`'s shape: `sut_version` · `captured_at` · a `provenance` string naming
   intent §Theme 1 F4 as the transcribed SUT record (nothing in `.andromeda/refs/` carries the stall — the
   artifact must say plainly it is transcribed, not Conductor-measured) · an `[envelope]` table with the
   sustained-rate term, the sustained-storm-duration term, and the derivable `max_scenario_duration_ms` proxy ·
   an `[[exempt]]` array of `{scenario, reason}`.

2. **Load + validate it** in a new `crates/conductor-core/src/load_envelope.rs`, following the
   `CapabilityManifest` precedent exactly (per security-plan §Input Validation): a fixed `default_path()`
   resolved through the shipped `config_path::resolve_under` guard with **no `CONDUCTOR_*` override handle**,
   `load()` returning a named `CoreError` on absent/malformed/unparseable, and read faults carrying `e.kind()`
   only — never the path. Bounds-check at load: non-empty version/date/provenance, positive terms, no duplicate
   exemption scenario.

3. **Add the gate** `check_load_envelope(&LoadEnvelope, &[Scenario]) -> Result<()>` in the same module, built on
   the `drift.rs:79-136` template: pure `BTreeSet` set-algebra over committed artifacts, failing on three
   disjoint conditions — a scenario over the duration term and not exempt; an exemption whose scenario is now
   inside the envelope (**ledger rot**); an exemption naming no scenario in the catalog (**lost subject**). The
   message is identity-only (scenario names + the envelope's `sut_version`/`captured_at`), never a path, never
   an internal type name (per `drift.rs:100-101`).

4. **Surface the constraint where scenarios are authored** — the envelope terms and the exemption discipline
   land in the scenario-authoring surface, not only in `.andromeda/`. Name the SET/terms, never a fresh literal
   that re-stales (the standing derived-count discipline; four separate amendments cited in the layouts
   extract).

5. **Classify the run** in `conductor-run`: at run composition, evaluate the resolved scenario against the
   envelope and produce a run-scoped value — in-envelope, or environment-suspect carrying its breach cause. This
   is a **typed value on the `Ok` path**, never `Result::Err` (the verdict/error wall); only a malformed/absent
   envelope artifact is `Err`. It must not touch any per-check `verdict` or `state`.

6. **Persist it run-level** — a NEW `run_envelope` table in `crates/conductor-report/src/db.rs`
   (`run_id` PK · classification · cause), created by the same additive `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` bootstrap.
   A separate table, not a column on `runs`: the existing eleven-column table and its `(run_id, scenario)` PK
   stay byte-identical, which is what makes "`state ∈ {…}` provably unchanged" checkable. Bound parameters only.

7. **Render it on all three surfaces**, outside the lamp column, reusing the recessive `KnownResidual` register
   with no new token (per design-system §Color Palette + layout-templates §Component — Primary content block 1
   Mode bullet): the Markdown report header banner naming the breach cause; the CLI summary caption with an
   always-rendered ASCII text label that survives `NO_COLOR`/piping; and a run-level banner in the existing
   webview RunReport view with a DOM text label (never color-alone). Never `--status-fail`, never
   `--count-blocked` (it shares its hex with `--text-muted` and would read as `Blocked`), motionless.

8. **Wire the gate into the test suite** as a static assertion over the committed catalog, beside the existing
   `check_sut_drift` / `check_scenario_backing` gates.

9. **Discharge the folded PREREQ** — re-run `cargo audit` (fifth consecutive check) and **observe**
   `cargo deny check` green. No floor raise, no `deny.toml` ignore, no CI edit. Close the deferral only if the
   advisory database now parses.

- `crates/conductor-core/src/lib.rs` — module declaration + re-exports (the `capability_manifest` / `drift` pattern).
- `crates/conductor-core/src/error.rs` — a named `CoreError` variant for the envelope fault (the `SutDrift` / `UnbackedCoverage` precedent).
- `crates/conductor-run/src/lib.rs` — evaluate the envelope at run composition; carry the run-scoped classification (`ReportState` @ `conductor-run/src/lib.rs`, 9 refs — read only, not widened).
- `crates/conductor-report/src/db.rs` — the additive `run_envelope` table + bound-parameter insert/read; the `runs` table untouched.
- `crates/conductor-report/src/report.rs` — the run-level banner in the Markdown report header (`ReportState` @ 24 refs here — rendering only, set unchanged).
- `crates/conductor-cli/src/render.rs` — the CLI summary caption + ASCII label (`ReportState` @ 12 refs — rendering only).

`npm run a11y` (wdio + axe-core + colorjs.io) is the chunk's standing UI gate — this chunk adds a webview
render surface, so its frontend-meaningful half is required. It is **display-gated to Linux+xvfb**; on the
Windows dev host it records a skip, never a silent pass. The `v2-07` report/`runs.db` evidence is produced by
the `-p conductor-report -p conductor-run` integration leg (TempDir + `open_in_memory`), not by a live
65-minute run.

- (tests) `cargo nextest run -p conductor-core` passes with the new envelope gate: it fails when a committed
  `scenarios/*.toml` exceeds the envelope's duration term and is not exempt, is expressed over the **set** of
  catalog entries (no literal scenario count, no P-ID range), and its fault message names identity without host
  paths or internal struct names (per test-plan §6 Selector strategy + §11 Test Data). — `verification-matrix.json#v2-06`

- (tests) The exemption ledger is held to **exact-set equality in both directions** — an exemption whose
  scenario is now inside the envelope fails as ledger rot, and an exemption naming no catalog scenario fails as
  a lost subject — so it can only shrink under compulsion (per test-plan §4 static-assertion bullet). — `verification-matrix.json#v2-06`

- (arch) An envelope breach is returned as a typed value on the `Ok` path; only a malformed / absent /
  unparseable envelope artifact produces `Result::Err` with a named `CoreError`. No breach path returns `Err`,
  no artifact fault returns a report state (per architecture.md §Error Handling + §Established Decisions
  [Accepted Capability Set]).

- (arch) `state ∈ {Pass, Fail, ManualCheck, KnownResidual, Blocked}` is **provably unchanged**: `ReportState`
  gains no variant, `RunRecord` keeps exactly its eleven fields in declaration order, and the `runs` table keeps
  its eleven columns and `(run_id, scenario)` PK — the qualifier lands in the additive `run_envelope` table
  (per architecture.md §Standard Contracts + §Conventions Data model conventions). — `verification-matrix.json#v2-07`

- (tests) Integration: an over-envelope run yields an environment-suspect classification **distinct from
  `Fail`**, exits **0** (a reported state is never a non-zero exit), and its Markdown report names the envelope
  breach as the cause (per test-plan §3 exit-code semantics + §11 E2E). — `verification-matrix.json#v2-07`

- (arch) Load-time assertion lives in `conductor-core`, report/index round-trip in `conductor-report`,
  realized-run classification in `conductor-run`; no new cross-seam dependency edge appears in any `Cargo.toml`
  (per architecture.md §Established Decisions [Module Boundaries]).

- (security) The envelope artifact is validated at load, resolved through `resolve_under` from a fixed path with
  **no new `CONDUCTOR_*` handle**, and its error variants stringify without any path component (per
  security-plan §Input Validation).

- (security) The environment-suspect report and `run_envelope` row carry no absolute host path and no internal
  struct/field name, and every new SQL write uses rusqlite bound parameters — no `format!`-built SQL in the
  storage seam (per security-plan §Error Handling + §Input Validation).

- (security) `cargo audit` re-run with its output recorded verbatim AND `cargo deny check advisories bans
  licenses sources` **observed** green; `git diff` shows zero changes to `deny.toml` and `.github/workflows/`,
  and no floor raise; `Cargo.lock` un-drifted with no new dependency (per security-plan §Dependency Security).

- (design) The classification binds existing tokens **by name** on every surface — zero new hex, zero new ANSI
  entries, zero raw ms/px — and is visually distinct from both `Fail` red and the empty/"no result yet" state
  (per design-system §Surface: cli Tokens + §Anti-Patterns → Rejected Defaults).

- (layouts) The qualifier renders **outside the lamp column** on all three surfaces, never in `status-fail` /
  ANSI 203 and never reusing `--count-blocked`; the results/SLO table stays 6 columns and the coverage matrix
  stays 4 (per layout-templates §Component — Primary content block 1 Mode bullet + §cli IA notes → Command model).

- (layouts/design) Color is never the only channel: an always-rendered ASCII text label on the CLI surviving
  `NO_COLOR=1` and piping, text/emphasis in the Markdown artifact, and a DOM text label in the webview (per
  layout-templates §cli IA notes → Pipe discipline + design-system §Iconography).

- (obs) The breach cause is emitted in **structured** fields registered in the `conductor-core::redact`
  field-name allowlist — proven present in the emitted artifact, not silently dropped — with no absolute host
  path, logged at `warn` (per obs-plan §11 PII Scrubbing + §6 Log levels).

- (obs) No metric instrument, histogram, meter provider, or OTel SDK init is added for the envelope terms; they
  are asserted as JSON-field comparisons. Any new span conforms to `{module}.{operation}` within the bounded
  span-name set (per obs-plan §5 + §4 Span naming convention).

- (a11y) The webview banner carries a DOM text label + glyph supplement covered by the not-color-alone
  assertion, is announced via `status`/`aria-live` as its own state and never as `Fail`, verdict-first lamp
  precedence still resolves a single lamp per row, and the run-report path shows zero WCAG AA violations under
  the axe run — **or** the display-gate skip is recorded (per a11y-plan §6 State color tokens + §3 Screen
  reader test pattern).

- (tests) `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci` green with `retries = 0`, `cargo test --workspace --doc`
  and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean (per test-plan §10).

- Research files inspected: `crates/conductor-core/src/phase_spec.rs`, `crates/conductor-core/src/drift.rs`,

- **The exemptions are a debt, not an excuse.** `activity-floor` (3900s; 10+10+30 min of deliberate quiet) and

A duration-only assertion would produce a false positive on the one scenario whose whole point is idleness. The envelope predicate needs the rate axis to be honest — and the model cannot express it (`phase_spec.rs` has no count/rate field). **This is the plan's central decision, and it is upstream of the `ReportState` fork.**
