- **Marker:** 2026-09-06-halo-hue-budget-re-driven · **Version:** conductor-0.2.0 · **Generated:** 2026-09-06T19:40Z

- **Revised:** 2026-09-07 at the P5 review — five operator findings applied; finding #1 changed what the
  chunk can claim (see §Goal).

Re-drive `halo-hue-encoding` so it produces a stimulus of its own — an error stream sustained through Pulse's
incident formation — and grade what the delegated `metric.constellation.hue_update_ms` observable actually
measures. The prior chunk measured 35 581 ms and 36 705 ms against a 2 000 ms budget and proved the cause
structural: the observable reports staleness, and the scenario drove nothing, so both samples were the
preflight canary's (`v2-20` PREMISE-CORRECTION; `delegated_timing_harvest.rs:325-337`).

**Three terms of the fire site govern the design, and the third was found at this plan's review — it changes
the deliverable.** Research established the first two at SUT HEAD `83d4060`: the effect emits the **slowest**
changed dot's staleness and *that* dot's tier (`ConstellationCanvas.tsx:117-155`), and `visibleDots` drops any
service quiet longer than `LIVE_RECENCY_WINDOW_NANOS = 60 s` (`constellation-types.ts:27`). The third is
**quantization**: `ServiceRegistryEntry.last_seen_unix_nano` has **no ingest-path writer**. A sweep
(`grep -rn "last_seen_unix_nano\s*=[^=]" crates/ pulse-app/src` → 4 hits: `registry.rs:257` restart transition,
`registry.rs:336` tick, plus unrelated `buffer/src/drain.rs:492` and `corpus/src/contract.rs:546`) leaves the
steady-state writer as `registry.tick_all`, which sets the field to the **tick's** `now` and only when
`snapshot.current_quiet_duration_seconds == 0` — integer-truncated seconds since the floor's last observe
(`activity_floor.rs:142-149`). The tick is `DEFAULT_LIFECYCLE_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL = Duration::from_secs(15)`
(`lifecycle/mod.rs:52`), passed unchanged at `main.rs:1489` with no env override.

Therefore `hue_update_ms ≈ t_sample − t_last_refreshing_tick`, distributed U(0, 15 s) at a randomly-timed
flip — **independent of the dispatch rate**, with roughly 13 % of flips landing under 2 s by coincidence.
**The ≤2 s bound is unmeasurable through this leaf while `last_seen` is lifecycle-tick-quantized**, and a
pass asserted against 2 000 ms would pin a tick coincidence as attainment. The chunk therefore ships the
**mechanism pin plus the measured value**, and no pass arm, until the SUT changes the writer. The SUT-side fix
(the registry copying the floor's `last_observed_unix_nanos`, or the fire site reading span arrival) is a
Pulse intake item, not this chunk's work (scope §2).

Attribution rides neither service identity (the leaf's allowlist is exactly `["duration_ms","severity_tier"]`
under the SUT's own "Aggregate-only: no service identifier", `observability.rs:986-990`) nor `severity_tier`
(a dot's tier is incident-derived, `registry.rs:59-65`, and incidents form only from Autonomous cues,
`coordinator.rs:395`, so the scenario must reach the same band the canary does). It is **temporal**, and the
canary is separated by construction: preflight readiness *requires* a fresh canary incident
(`canary.rs:1-7` — "asserts an incident opened AFTER that storm's emission instant"), so the canary's tier
flip and its hue sample land **before `scenario.run` starts**, and its dot leaves `visibleDots` 60 s after the
storm — before its incident auto-resolves. The chunk also discharges the scenario's unreachable declared tier
(CARRY §3.2) and the `ReadBack::AutoResolved` re-proof (CARRY §3.3).

1. **Re-shape `scenarios/halo-hue-encoding.toml`'s two phases so the scenario drives its own Autonomous
   incident and keeps emitting through formation — at 2 dispatches per second.** Phase 1 `healthy-baseline`:
   `gap_ms = 30000` with a `[phases.emission]` block `kind = "plain"`, `occurrences = 60`. Phase 2
   `error-pressure`: `gap_ms = 150000` with `kind = "exception"`, `occurrences = 300`,
   `variants = ["identical"]` — the committed idiom at
   `scenarios/constellation-severity-live-wiring.toml:38-48`. Phase 1 makes the `conductor` service a live
   constellation dot (registering it in `hueTierRef` at `tier = null`) before any incident exists, and
   separates the subject's flip from the canary's by ≥ 28 s.

   **What the sustained stream buys is liveness, not freshness** — it keeps the dot inside `visibleDots` and
   lets the 15 s tick refresh `last_seen`; **no rate reaches the 2 s bound** (§Goal). **The 2/s rate is
   chosen over 1/s to make every tick refresh BY CONSTRUCTION, which is what step 6's mechanism pin needs.**
   A tick refreshes only when `current_quiet_duration_seconds == 0`, i.e. a span arrived < 1 s before it
   (`registry.rs:336`; `activity_floor.rs:142-149`). At 1/s a jitter beat puts a 1 000–1 050 ms-old span at
   some ticks (`jitter_ms = 50`), that tick skips the refresh, and the following flip's sample then offsets
   to the tick *before* — ~15 s past step 6's ~1 100 ms tolerance, failing the pin spuriously in roughly
   1–5 % of runs. At 2/s the max span age at any tick is ~525 ms (500 ms interval + half the 50 ms jitter),
   so `quiet` is 0 at every tick and the beat cannot arise. (The alternative — keep 1/s and let the pin accept
   an offset to the preceding tick OR the one before it, `k × 15 s` — is rejected in §Constraints as the
   weaker letter: it widens the assertion instead of removing the cause.) 2/s also reaches the 10 identical
   fingerprints of `DEFAULT_AUTONOMOUS_THRESHOLD` (`storm.rs:65`, `:80`) about 5 s into phase 2.

2. **Re-tier `slo_tier` from `"<5s"` to `"<90s"`** in the same file, and rewrite the trailing `# the fast
   tier` comment to state that the value is the closest honest bucket for a whole-run latency that exceeds
   every tier by construction (`<90s` is the largest of the closed set, `scenario.rs:52-73`). This discharges
   CARRY §3.2 — the declared tier was already unreachable against the scenario's own 6 000 ms of gaps
   (measured `latency_ms` 6081 / 6080). Follows the `2026-08-18-error-baseline-spike-live-proof` precedent.

3. **Keep the scenario DECLARE-ONLY: do not add an `[[expected]]` block, and keep the existing
   `[[checklist]]` row.** The hue duration reaches no MCP read-back surface, so an `[[expected]]` check
   cannot carry it and `budget_ms` would grade Conductor's own round-trip instead (per test-plan §6;
   obs-plan §4). `Scenario::check_checklist` (`scenario.rs:160`) is therefore never tripped. Update the
   `[[checklist]]` `induced` text, which currently states the scenario "declares no emission of its own" —
   that sentence becomes false at step 1.

4. **Rewrite the scenario's header block** to replace the `BUDGET DISPROVED` narrative with the re-driven
   design and **all three** fire-site terms: slowest-changed-dot-wins, the 60 s live-recency ceiling, and the
   **15 s lifecycle-tick quantization of `last_seen`** with its citations (`registry.rs:336`,
   `activity_floor.rs:142-149`, `lifecycle/mod.rs:52`). State plainly that the ≤2 s bound is unmeasurable
   through this leaf until the SUT changes the writer, and that the sustained stream buys liveness rather
   than freshness. Keep the `DELEGATED TIMING` / `SURFACE CORRECTION` paragraphs that remain true.

5. **Add a scenario-attributing selection helper to
   `crates/conductor-run/tests/delegated_timing_harvest.rs`, leaving `grade()` untouched.** `grade()` folds
   with `f64::max` (`:114-130`) and is correct for the other three bounds. The helper takes its phase
   boundaries from the leg's **frozen per-leg self-obs capture** `runs/live-suite/{label}.jsonl` — *not*
   `runs/<run_id>.jsonl`, which carries no phase data — whose lines carry `timestamp_ms` and comprise
   `conductor_timeline::scheduler` / `timeline.execute` / `span_event new|close` (`phase_count`,
   `emission_count`), one `conductor_emit::client` / `emit.batch` / `new` per dispatch, and
   `conductor_run::execute` / `scenario.run` / `new|close`. **Phase-2 start** = `timeline.execute` new plus
   the phase-1 gap, or equivalently the first `emit.batch` of phase 2. The selection window opens at
   **phase-2 START** and closes at the leg's read-back. The helper ALSO reads the `triage.lifecycle.tick`
   lines from the same Pulse-side capture (allowlisted at `observability.rs:1653`) so step 6 can pin the
   mechanism. Pulse-side hue lines carry their own `timestamp` on the same host clock (skew measured 45 ms
   on 2026-09-06). Absence of any in-window sample grades `Err`, never a satisfied budget (the module's own
   `ABSENCE IS NEVER A PASS` rule, `:22`).

6. **Replace `p025_hue_update_is_measured_over_budget_by_a_staleness_mechanism` (`:337`) with a
   MECHANISM PIN plus the measured value — and no pass arm against 2 000 ms.** The test asserts that each
   in-window sample's `duration_ms` equals its offset to the **preceding `triage.lifecycle.tick`** within the
   poll + IPC tolerance (~1 100 ms), and records the measured value. This is what makes the quantization a
   verified property of the observable rather than a story about it. The doc comment carries the retired
   test's mechanism paragraph forward and extends it with all three terms, naming the quantization as the
   reason no ≤2 s assertion may be written here until the SUT changes the writer.

7. **Add the hue leg to the `--live` suite in both shells, ordered FIRST.** In `scripts/agent-run.sh`
   `live_suite()` (`:91-136`) insert a `live_leg h halo-hue-encoding` call after the preconditions probe and
   before `live_leg b1`, with a budget covering the scenario's ~180 s of phases plus the preflight budget
   (`live_leg_budget_sec 180` = 405 s against a ~235–320 s leg); mirror it in `scripts/agent-run.ps1`. Update
   the composition comment at `:107` and the `--live` banner text at `:202-205`. Ordering first is
   load-bearing: the subject's own incident idles from phase-2 end and auto-resolves ≤ 150 s later, well
   before leg A's read-back ~350 s further on, so the hue leg cannot perturb leg A's empty-active-set
   precondition.

8. **Record the stretched bootstrap posture as a BOOT-WIDE property of the operator's launch.**
   `Thresholds::from_env()` runs once at boot (`main.rs:472`), so
   `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_BASELINE_BOOTSTRAP_SECONDS=86399` (accepted: strictly `< 86_400`) governs the **whole
   suite** — it is not "leg A's firing form". Document it as: *boot-wide; load-bearing for leg A (it disarms
   the silence evaluator that would otherwise raise incidents during leg A's own silent phase), inert for the
   hue leg (the storm path consults no baseline — the `BootstrapState` gate sits only inside
   `evaluate_service_went_silent`, `emitter.rs:186`)*. No Conductor code sets it and no `CONDUCTOR_*` handle
   is added; it rides the operator's `pulse-app` launch, and the SUT's own `warn_bootstrap_window` line with
   `reason = "env_override"` is what the light gate reads to confirm which posture booted. Put this in the
   suite banner text beside the existing stop-form lines.

9. **Update `scenarios/auto-resolve-idle-window.toml`'s header (`:28-32`)** — CARRY §3.3. Replace the stale
   MARGIN model with both measured causes and the posture that resolves them: past the bootstrap hour the arm
   is unreachable at any window length; inside it the window must clear 150 s from the LAST preflight
   incident; and under the boot-wide stretched window the silence evaluator is disarmed for the whole suite.
   Keep the `gap_ms = 200000` value (research did not falsify it) and keep the harvest literals.

10. **Run the live suite and commit its captures.** Freeze each leg's Conductor-side and Pulse-side captures
    into `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-09-06-halo-hue-budget-re-driven/evidence/`, host-path-free (per
    security-plan §Error Handling; obs-plan §9). Record for each leg: the SUT's booted bootstrap posture line,
    the in-window hue observations **with their preceding tick offsets**, leg A's `ReadBack` arm, and the
    scenario's envelope row.
- `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-09-06-halo-hue-budget-re-driven/evidence/` — the leg captures + a verdict note.

- `crates/conductor-run/tests/delegated_timing_harvest.rs` — new window-selection + tick-reading helper; the
  P-025 test at `:337` replaced by the mechanism pin. `bounds()`, `observations()`, `grade()` and the other
  three bounds' tests unchanged.
- `scenarios/auto-resolve-idle-window.toml` — header `:28-32` only; `gap_ms` unchanged.

- `scripts/agent-run.sh` + `scripts/agent-run.ps1` — the new `h` leg in `live_suite()`, ordered first, plus
  the composition comment and banner text (incl. the boot-wide posture note). Both shells move together
  (test-plan §3 parity).

**No caller threading is required** — this chunk changes no signature. The graph query
(`research.md` §Graph impact, `rows: 72`) confirms each symbol in the boundary has a single production
caller: `phase_rate_exceeds` → `phase_breach` @ `load_envelope.rs:209`, `max_spans_per_dispatch` →
`phase_breach` @ `:211`, `check_checklist` → `from_toml_str` @ `scenario.rs:160`. **Crate-local companions
checked and clear:** no committed stream golden pins this scenario — `crates/conductor-run/tests/snapshots/`
holds `dispatch_wire__error_baseline_stream_seed_424242`, `dispatch_wire__storm_stream_seed_4317017` and
`dispatch_wire__storm_stream_seed_7`, and `dispatch_wire.rs` loads only `fingerprint-storm.toml` (`:102`) and
`error-baseline-spike.toml` (`:498`) (basis: `ls crates/conductor-run/tests/snapshots/` + `grep -n` on that
file). The static catalog gate `check_load_envelope` already covers the re-shaped phases.

```bash
# unit + the re-aimed harvest assertion
cargo nextest run -p conductor-run
cargo nextest run -p conductor-core          # the catalog load-envelope gate over the re-shaped scenario
cargo test -p conductor-run                  # runner-portability arm (test-plan §4)
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

# workspace gate
cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci

# harness smoke — REQUIRED because scripts/agent-run.{sh,ps1} are in the modify-set (a boot-path
# touchpoint). Asserts the 5-command surface still parses and reads disk artifacts after the --live
# edit. NOT the live leg's gate: a bare status verb cannot tell this run from a prior run's residue,
# which is why the leg below is asserted on its own printed verdicts instead.
bash scripts/agent-run.sh status

# supply-chain merge gate — green required even at zero dependency delta (security-plan
# §Dependency Security). Step 0 reads the LOCAL advisory-db copy's currency BEFORE any red is
# classified external (the corrected 2026-09-05 rule; untracked residue there produced 51 false
# re-pins). Expect NO output from the probe, then exit 0 from both runners.
git -C "${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/advisory-db" status --porcelain
cargo audit
cargo deny check advisories bans licenses sources

# --- LIVE LEG (operator-gated; never a CI gate — test-plan §9) --------------------------------
# 1. NON-PRIMING liveness probe FIRST — an absent Pulse must read as a failed precondition, never
#    as a failed run. This probe does not prime incident state (unlike `boot`).
PATH="$PULSE_BIN:$PATH" cargo run -q -p conductor-cli -- preconditions
# 2. The suite. The OPERATOR launches pulse-app with deterministic L4 + MCP + a FRESH data dir and
#    the BOOT-WIDE bootstrap posture (Thresholds::from_env() runs once at boot, main.rs:472):
#      ANDROMEDA_PULSE_BASELINE_BOOTSTRAP_SECONDS=86399
#    load-bearing for leg A, inert for the hue leg. Confirm from the SUT's own warn_bootstrap_window
#    line with reason="env_override" — not from Conductor, which never sets it.
#    Assert the PRINTED per-leg verdicts, not the exit code: `run --live` exits 0 over a [BLOCKED]
#    row by design (only Lamp::Fail exits non-zero).
PATH="$PULSE_BIN:$PATH" ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MCP_ENABLED=true ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC=true \
  ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR="$LEG_DIR" bash scripts/agent-run.sh run --live
# 3. STOP FORM — the wdio arm self-terminates via onComplete -> tauriDriver.kill(); after an
#    interrupted run: taskkill /F /IM msedgedriver.exe /IM conductor-tauri.exe (+ the node CLI).
#    pulse-app is NOT stopped by the harness — the operator started it and stops it.
```

  only at 15 s lifecycle ticks (§Goal), so a sample under 2 s is a tick coincidence (~13 % of flips), not
  attainment. No pass arm until the SUT changes the writer.

- **Raising the dispatch rate to make `last_seen` FRESH — REJECTED, it cannot.** The value is written by the
  tick, not by ingest, so no rate reaches the 2 s bound. (2/s is nonetheless CHOSEN in step 1 for a different
  reason: it makes every tick refresh by construction, which the mechanism pin depends on.)

  would absorb the jitter beat into the assertion rather than removing its cause, and a pin that accepts an
  offset to "the preceding tick or the one before it" no longer distinguishes a refreshed tick from a skipped
  one — which is precisely the property under test.

title: THE HEADLINE FINDING — the fire site's arithmetic decides the design, and two of its three terms were unrecorded

data.head: ## THE HEADLINE FINDING — the fire site's arithmetic decides the design, and two of its three terms were unrecorded

body:
The CONTEXT's mechanism is **verified at HEAD** and is **sharper than any Conductor artifact states**. Fire site:
`andromeda-pulse pulse-app/ui/src/widget/ConstellationCanvas.tsx:117-155` (HEAD `83d4060`), a `useEffect` keyed `[dots, items]`:

```
const elapsedMs = nowMs - item.last_seen_unix_nano / 1_000_000;   // :141  — STALENESS, as recorded
if (elapsedMs > slowestMs) { slowestMs = elapsedMs; slowestTier = tier ?? "none"; }   // :142-145
...
void recordConstellationHueLatency({ duration_ms: slowestMs, severity_tier: slowestTier });   // :152
```
Three terms, only the first of which was known:
1. **Staleness, confirmed** — `now − last_seen`, exactly as the CONTEXT and the scenario header state. ✓

2. **SLOWEST-WINS, previously unrecorded.** The effect loops EVERY dot whose tier changed in that render pass and emits the **maximum** staleness, with `severity_tier` naming *that* dot's tier — not the scenario's. So if the scenario's dot and the canary's dot change tier in the SAME pass, the emitted sample is the canary's, and its `severity_tier` is reported. A `changed === 0` pass emits nothing.

3. **A 60-SECOND CEILING, previously unrecorded.** `visibleDots` filters on `isServiceLive` — `now − last_seen <= LIVE_RECENCY_WINDOW_NANOS`, and `LIVE_RECENCY_WINDOW_NANOS = 60 * 1_000_000_000` (`constellation-types.ts:27`, mirroring the Rust FSM's `ACTIVE_TO_QUIET_THRESHOLD_SECONDS`). A service quiet longer than 60 s is not a dot at all, so **no `hue_update_ms` sample can exceed ~60 000 ms.** The measured 35 581 / 36 705 ms sit inside that ceiling, which corroborates the staleness reading rather than a slow render.

**What this makes the design target, quantified:** the budget is met iff, at the instant the scenario's dot changes tier, that service's `last_seen` is under 2 000 ms old — i.e. **the scenario's dispatch interval must be well under 2 s and emission must still be running when the tier flips.**

body:
- **`scenarios/halo-hue-encoding.toml` declares ZERO `[phases.emission]` blocks.** Two phases,
  `healthy-baseline` and `error-pressure`, each carrying `gap_ms = 3000` and nothing else. Basis:

- **Its declared tier is already violated by its own phase data.** `slo_tier = "<5s"` (the header calls it
  "the fast tier") against 3000 + 3000 = 6000 ms of `gap_ms`. Basis: whole-file read. CARRY 1's premise
  verified.

- **It declares one `[[checklist]]` row and no `[[expected]]` check** — declare-only, so nothing grades it
  today (`verdict: null`). Basis: whole-file read. `Scenario::check_checklist` forbids a `[[checklist]]`
  beside a non-empty `expected`, so adding a graded check and keeping the checklist row is a load-path
  conflict this chunk must resolve deliberately, not incidentally. `[inferred]`

- **The harvest test pins the DISPROOF, not a pass.** `crates/conductor-run/tests/delegated_timing_harvest.rs:337`
  is `p025_hue_update_is_measured_over_budget_by_a_staleness_mechanism`, and `:36` states it exists
  "never as a pass". Basis: grep + the file's own module doc. Re-driving the scenario puts this test's
  subject in play.

- **P-025 is classified `CoverageMode::DriveObserve`** (`crates/conductor-core/src/coverage.rs:239`), not
  `Auto` — so it does not participate in the `UNBACKED_AUTO` backing ledger
  (`crates/conductor-core/src/drift.rs:61`), and this chunk changes no coverage classification. Basis:
  direct read of both files. `[inferred]`

- **The load envelope's asserted terms are `max_sustained_storm_ms = 600000` and
  `max_sustained_rate_spans_per_s = 10000`**, with `max_scenario_duration_ms = 600000` recorded but not
  asserted, and the `[[exempt]]` ledger **empty** and held at exact-set equality in both directions. Basis:
  `contracts/pulse-load-envelope.toml:21-47`. A sustained emitting window is exactly what this chunk adds,
  so both asserted terms are live constraints on the new shape — and the rate term now counts **wire
  records** via `EmissionSpec::max_spans_per_dispatch()` (shipped by `2026-09-06-coverage-completeness-gate`),
  not dispatches. `[inferred]`

- **The service-identity split does NOT settle attribution for this observable.**
  `[premise-corrected: the hue leaf's allowlist is exactly `["duration_ms", "severity_tier"]` and the
  SUT's own comment at `pulse-app/src/observability.rs:986-990` reads "Aggregate-only: no service
  identifier" — so `conductor` vs `conductor-canary` cannot discriminate a hue sample.]** The
  `CANARY_SERVICE_NAME` / `DEFAULT_SERVICE_NAME` split is real (architecture §Occupied Resources) and
  still governs Pulse's per-service sample counts and EWMAs; it simply reaches no field on THIS line.
  Attribution must ride what the line carries — the `severity_tier` VALUE and sample order — or be
  designed out by ensuring the scenario's dot is the only one changing tier. Worse: the fire site emits
  the **slowest** changed dot's staleness and that dot's tier, so a same-pass canary change would
  *report the canary*. See `research.md` §THE HEADLINE FINDING and Open question 1.

  SUT's. This chunk changes only what Conductor drives and how it grades.

- **No `[[expected]]` check bound to a Pulse-internal duration.** `budget_ms` / `effective_deadline_ms`
  grade `read_back_observed_at − journal_emitted_at` — Conductor's own MCP round-trip — so binding a
  Pulse-internal render/hue duration to it is a category error, recorded as such in `v2-20`'s
  PREMISE-CORRECTION and in the scenario header. The delegated bound stays graded at the **harvest tier**.

- **No claim on the VISUAL hue.** P-025's rendered hue remains operator-checklist (`DriveObserve`); only
  the delegated timing observable is in play.
- **No new automation stack, no new dependency, no widening of the trust boundary.**

- **No retroactive un-verification of `v2-20`.** P-025 was excluded from that cap by operator ruling on

title: 5. Definition of done (scope-level; the plan sharpens these)

data.head: ## 5. Definition of done (scope-level; the plan sharpens these)

body:
1. `halo-hue-encoding` drives an error-shaped stream that reaches a severity tier change **of its own** and
   is still emitting when that change fires — attribution provable, not assumed.

2. The delegated `hue_update_ms` observable is graded at its **real measured value** on a live leg, and the
   MECHANISM that governs it is pinned. **Amended at the P5 review (2026-09-07) — intent-incomplete:** the
   ≤2 s bound is **unmeasurable through this leaf**, because `ServiceRegistryEntry.last_seen_unix_nano` has
   no ingest-path writer and is refreshed only by the 15 s lifecycle tick (`registry.rs:336` gated on
   `current_quiet_duration_seconds == 0`, integer-truncated at `activity_floor.rs:142-149`;
   `DEFAULT_LIFECYCLE_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL = 15 s` at `lifecycle/mod.rs:52`, wired unchanged at
   `main.rs:1489`). So `hue_update_ms ≈ t_sample − t_last_refreshing_tick`, U(0, 15 s) and independent of
   dispatch rate — a sub-2 s sample is a tick coincidence (~13 % of flips), never attainment. The
   deliverable is therefore the mechanism pin plus the measured value, with **no pass arm** against 2 000 ms
   until the SUT changes the writer. That SUT-side fix is a Pulse intake item, not this chunk's work (§2).

3. The scenario's `slo_tier` is re-tiered to the re-driven shape, and the new shape passes the load
   envelope's asserted terms without an exemption.

4. The `AutoResolved` observable is re-proven on a fresh data dir under a **stated** bootstrap posture, or
   the attempt's measurement is recorded with which of causes (a)/(b) it hit.
5. The plan states, explicitly, whether the proof leans on `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_BASELINE_BOOTSTRAP_SECONDS`.

_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-09-06-operator-gated-live-suite · **Version:** conductor-0.2.0 · **Generated:** 2026-09-06T07:11:20Z

- **Revision:** re-synthesised twice at P5 review (2026-09-06), promotion intact.
  **Round 1** — four verified findings: observable 1's arm unreachable as planned, the leg ORDER (including
  B2's expected exit-0 `[BLOCKED]` row under `set -euo pipefail`), the truncating self-obs sink, and the
  wall-clock budget. **Round 2** — three corrections: the AutoResolved arm's reachability is PER-SCENARIO
  (`ack-cooldown` reaches it live; the review's own round-1 universal was retracted), the `conductor coverage`
  gate proved nothing and was replaced with the catalog-reading unit tests, and the harvest pins its lines as
  LITERALS rather than reading `evidence/`. Plus the `env -u` wrap that makes the scenario-load check
  non-priming, and B2's deterministic-L4 premise.

Give Conductor ONE named, re-runnable, operator-gated invocation that fires the live-Pulse proof legs in a single
correct shape and lands a durable evidence record — so a live proof stops being a hand-assembled paste of env
blocks whose partial forms fail silently as a ~0s `[BLOCKED]` indistinguishable from a genuine SUT-side gate
failure (research.md §Conventions; verification-harness 2026-08-20/2026-08-22). Today that surface is scattered
across **six firing-form families / eight invocations** with different env blocks, orderings and evidence
destinations. The suite composes them behind `agent-run run --live`, shipped at identical semantics in both
shells, and it is **never a CI gate** (per test-plan §9 + architecture.md §Established Decisions [CI/CD], one
rule with two homes).

Second, it buys behavioural coverage the mutation tier structurally cannot. Three `conductor-run` survivors are
accepted-deliberate because no hermetic test can reach their sites — a fixed `http://127.0.0.1:4317` endpoint
const, a crate-private `Preflight`, a `PATH`-resolved sidecar absent on a hermetic host (all three re-derived at
HEAD, research.md §Scope premise closure) — but their OBSERVABLES are live-path facts a driven run can assert
from persisted records. Landing them does **not** retire the tier acceptances: the mutants stay
accepted-deliberate and test-plan §12's roster is untouched by this chunk.

The chunk claims **no capability**. Each of the six pooled matrix entries is owned by a different route entry
(see §Implementation notes); nothing here makes any of them fully verifiable.

1. **Add the `--live` stage flag to `agent-run run`, in `scripts/agent-run.sh`.** It is a STAGE FLAG under the
   existing `run` verb beside `--unit` / `--integration` / `--e2e`, never a sixth command — the 5-command
   discipline forbids a sixth without a test-plan amendment (per test-plan §3; verification-harness "Do not add
   a 6th command"). It must not be reachable from `run` with no flag, so a bare `agent-run run` (the CI gate)
   never fires a live leg.

2. **Make the leading arm the shipped `conductor preconditions` probe, not a new one.** `--live` invokes the
   existing verb first and short-circuits on a genuinely unmet subject, printing the `[PRECONDITION]` unmet arm
   — one line per unmet subject naming its statement and candidate causes, host-path-free (per layout-templates
   §Surface: cli `conductor preconditions [--json]`; design-system §Surface: cli / Tokens). It is the correct
   probe because it is non-mutating and **fires no canary**, so it primes none of the state the legs then
   collide with. Do not mint a second precondition report shape and do not add a seventh bracket label.

3. **Refuse on a partial env rather than proceeding.** A short-circuit exits non-zero with the named subjects;
   it never degrades to a silent `[BLOCKED]` row and never writes a run record. Conductor must NOT materialize
   a missing handle: `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_*` are READ-only to Conductor (per architecture.md §Occupied Resources —
   Environment variables). Distinguish the two classes explicitly — an absent HOST-TOOL handle
   (`CONDUCTOR_MSEDGEDRIVER`, `CONDUCTOR_NVDA`) SKIPS its own leg at exit 0 with a fetch recipe naming the
   handle, never its value (per a11y-plan §3 / §9), while an incomplete live-Pulse env REFUSES the suite.

4. **Add the purpose-built silent scenario `scenarios/auto-resolve-idle-window.toml`.** The mechanism observable
   1 depends on is **measured, not derived**: `observe` (`crates/conductor-verify/src/extract.rs:76`) calls
   `query_incident_list(None)` with **no filter** and returns `EmptyCorpus` only when `incident_ids` is empty,
   while the run's own preflight canary incident stays open until Pulse auto-resolves it (120s idle + a 30s
   tick — Pulse's `DEFAULT_INCIDENT_AUTO_RESOLVE_WINDOW_SECS = 120`,
   `andromeda-pulse crates/triage/src/incident/persistence.rs:42`). The live proof is leg E of 2026-08-21,
   pinned at `crates/conductor-run/tests/severity_harvest.rs:505-513`: an `ack-cooldown` run (370s of phases,
   **no emission tables at all**) emits no incident-forming stimulus, so the only incident is the preflight
   canary's, it auto-resolves 120s + a tick later, the 370s scenario outlasts it, and read-back finds an empty
   active list → `AutoResolved`.
   **So reuse is REACHABLE, and the bound is per-scenario, not universal:** the SHORT declare-only scenarios
   (2–75s of phases) read back well inside the canary incident's idle window and yield `Graded` →
   `manual_record` → `ManualCheck`, never `AutoResolved`; `ack-cooldown` at 370s does reach it. The new
   scenario is chosen over reusing `ack-cooldown` for two reasons, neither of them reachability: **wall clock**
   (165s roughly halves leg A against 370s) and **declared intent** (a scenario whose stated purpose is the
   idle window, rather than one whose P-023 cool-down semantics are incidental to this use). The new scenario
   is ONE silent phase long enough for the
   canary's own incident to auto-resolve before read-back: `p_ids = ["P-022"]` (Pulse's auto-resolution
   capability, already classified and already backed by `incident-auto-resolution`), `slo_tier = "<90s"`, zero
   `[[expected]]` blocks (declare-only), and a single phase with `gap_ms = 165000` and
   `[phases.emission] kind = "plain", occurrences = 0` — the exact silence-window shape
   `scenarios/incident-auto-resolution.toml`'s `wait-auto-resolve` phase already uses. A phase declaring no
   occurrences emits nothing, so the load-envelope's two sustained terms (judged per EMITTING phase) do not
   bind it.
   **The file MUST carry a `LOAD ENVELOPE` header comment**, or
   `load_envelope::tests::every_committed_scenario_points_authors_at_the_envelope`
   (`crates/conductor-core/src/load_envelope.rs:525-536`) fails: it asserts every committed scenario's text
   contains that literal string as an author-facing pointer to the envelope contract. Copy the two-line header
   the existing scenarios open with.

5. **Compose the legs in this order — it is load-bearing, and each leg's outcome is predicted.**
   - **B1 — a short declare-only leg** (`degraded-mode-report`, 2 phases × 3000ms ≈ 6s). Its canary forms an
     incident, the gate reaches ready (observable 3's ABSENT arm), and read-back finds that incident still open
     → `Graded` → `manual_record` → a row carrying `latency_ms`. **This leg is observable 2's subject.**
   - **B2 — fired IMMEDIATELY after B1**, inside the 120s window while B1's canary incident is still open. B2's
     own canary dedupes against it on the `(kind, scope, scope_id)` tuple (Pulse's dedupe path calls
     `observe_reemission`, `inference_runtime.rs:815`), no fresh incident forms, and the gate goes
     **not-ready-but-connected** — the only state that reaches `canary.rs:59`. **This leg is observable 3's
     PRESENT arm.** Its row is `Blocked`.
     **`ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC=true` is LOAD-BEARING here, not just for reproducibility.** Under
     deterministic L4 the canary incident forms in ~2s (the 2026-09-04 boot measured 47s = 45s warm-up + ~2s),
     so B2's storm lands ~57s after B1's — comfortably inside the 120s window. With the real model, formation
     took ~110s (`lifecycle_live.rs` header), which would push B2's storm outside the window and silently cost
     observable 3's present arm. An env without this flag does not just make the leg slow; it makes it wrong.
   - **Quiet window ≥150s**, counted from B2's storm (≥120s idle + the 30s resolver tick).
   - **A — the silent scenario** from step 4. Its canary forms a fresh incident and the gate reaches ready
     (observable 3's ABSENT arm again); the 165s silent phase then outlasts the canary incident's idle timeout,
     so read-back finds an EMPTY active set → `EmptyCorpus` + declare-only → `AutoResolved` → `KnownResidual`
     plus the `declare-only read-back empty: no active incident outlived the emission window` self-obs line.
     **This leg is observable 1's subject.**
   - **The driven a11y arm** (`npm run a11y:driven`). No extra quiet window is needed: A's own canary incident
     has already resolved by A's read-back.
   - **CRITICAL — B2 exiting 0 with a `[BLOCKED]` row is the EXPECTED outcome, not a failure.**
     `exit_code` (`crates/conductor-cli/src/commands/mod.rs:28-34`) returns non-zero only on `Lamp::Fail`;
     every other reported state exits 0. `scripts/agent-run.sh:18` sets `set -euo pipefail`, so a non-zero B2
     would **abort the whole suite**. The assertion failure to guard is the inverse: a READY gate on B2 means
     the dedupe did not happen and observable 3's present arm was never produced.

6. **Mirror the whole flag in `scripts/agent-run.ps1` at identical semantics.** Both shells ship every verb at
   parity (per test-plan §3; layout-templates §Surface: cli). PowerShell operators cannot fall back to `bash` —
   it resolves to the WSL relay and dies with `execvpe(/bin/bash) failed` (verification-harness 2026-08-22 (a)).

7. **Freeze each leg's self-obs BEFORE the next leg runs — the sink truncates.**
   `logs/agent-latest.jsonl` is opened with `.truncate(true)` (`crates/conductor-core/src/obs.rs:108-111`, its
   doc at `:59`), so every `--agent-mode` invocation WIPES the previous leg's lines. Grading "what the legs left
   on disk" at the end would see only the last leg. After EACH leg, copy `logs/agent-latest.jsonl` into the
   chunk's `evidence/` under that leg's name — the harvest tier's frozen-lines precedent — and grade the copies.
   A per-leg `CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR` does **not** solve this: `agent_log_path` (`crates/conductor-cli/src/paths.rs:87-88`)
   resolves the logs dir as `runs_dir.parent()/logs`, so `runs/leg-a` and `runs/leg-b` both land in `runs/logs`.
   The per-run `runs/<run_id>.jsonl` journals and `runs.db` rows are per-run and DO survive.

8. **Add `crates/conductor-run/tests/live_suite.rs` behind the existing `live-pulse` feature.** It PRINTS its
   observations rather than asserting pinned expectations — the capture is the deliverable — exactly as
   `lifecycle_live.rs:30` states for its own pair. Reuse the feature already declared (`live-pulse = []`,
   `crates/conductor-run/Cargo.toml`); declaring no dependency keeps `Cargo.lock` byte-unchanged and the target
   off every default `nextest` / `clippy` / release path (per test-plan §9). Its module header carries the full
   one-paste firing form, as `lifecycle_live.rs` does.

9. **The artifacts come from the CLI, never from an in-process test.** `logs/agent-latest.jsonl` is written only
   when `conductor-cli`'s `main` selects the file sink — `obs_sink(agent_mode)` at
   `crates/conductor-cli/src/main.rs:26,44-45`, where `agent_mode = --agent-mode flag || CONDUCTOR_AGENT_MODE
   env-set`. A test target driving `conductor_run::{preflight, drive_run}` in-process installs its own
   subscriber and produces NO such file. So the graded half reads the frozen per-leg copies from step 7 and the
   per-run journals; it must not try to mint them. Equally, `boot` writes no run artifacts at all
   (verification-harness 2026-08-16), so the producing leg is a SCENARIO leg or nothing.

10. **Capture observable 1 — the `AutoResolved` degraded route — from leg A's persisted records.** Read the
    envelope's `state` from `runs/<run_id>.jsonl` with a typed parse that DISCRIMINATES the envelope line from
    the nine-key `CheckRecord` line (a file-wide parse-to-envelope is a false negative on any run emitting check
    rows, per test-plan §3 Log format → Agent parsing). **There is no `degraded` field to read**: `RunRecord`'s
    eleven fields carry none and `degraded_mode_response` occurs nowhere under `crates/`. The discriminator is
    the state mapping — `manual_record` (`execute.rs:245-266`) sets
    `state: state_for(observation, ReportState::ManualCheck)` and `state_for` (`:233-235`) returns
    `KnownResidual` iff `observation.degraded`, so on a declare-only scenario `state == KnownResidual` ⟺
    `degraded == true`. Pair it with leg A's frozen `declare-only read-back empty: no active incident outlived
    the emission window` line (`execute.rs:92-94`), which fires only on the `AutoResolved` arm and is what
    separates that route from the degraded-read-back route B1 takes.

11. **Capture observable 2 — the manual-path latency subtraction — as a BOUNDED equality, from leg B1.** Assert
    `|latency_ms − 1000·(read_back_observed_at − journal_emitted_at in whole seconds)| < 1000` against the
    persisted envelope. It cannot be an exact equality: `conductor_core::obs::now_rfc3339` (`obs.rs:212-219`)
    formats from `d.as_secs()`, so both instants are second-truncated while `latency_ms` is millisecond-grained
    from `now_ms()` (per architecture.md §Standard Contracts — Timestamp formats + §Conventions — Data model
    conventions). The bound still discriminates `execute.rs:136:25`'s `-` → `+` / `/` mutants, whose outputs
    miss by far more than one second. State it as a subtraction, never a sum or quotient (per obs-plan §5).

12. **Capture observable 3 — the readiness-gate self-obs line — on BOTH arms, from the frozen per-leg copies.**
    Assert `preflight blocked: readiness gate not satisfied` PRESENT in leg B2's copy and ABSENT in leg B1's and
    leg A's; both arms are required, because the mutant deletes the `!` in the guard (`canary.rs:58:8`) and an
    inverted guard passes a one-arm assertion. Key on the EXACT string: `canary.rs` carries three other
    `preflight blocked:` lines (`:49` and `:79` "MCP read-back path unreachable", `:189` canary-emission
    failure), and the connect arms return EARLY, so a prefix match would conflate them.

13. **Add `crates/conductor-run/tests/live_suite_harvest.rs` as the graded half — with the per-leg lines pinned
    as LITERALS in the test file.** The harvest tier never reads a path at grading time: `severity_harvest.rs`
    holds its captures as inline raw-string literals (`leg_a_lines()` at `:261-279`,
    `leg_e_auto_resolved_arm_line()` at `:509`), and this target must follow that. A default-suite test cannot
    read `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/…/evidence/` anyway — that is a version-workspace path outside the crate. So
    `evidence/` holds the FULL per-leg copies as the human-readable record, and the harvest pins the specific
    lines it grades. This half runs in the DEFAULT test suite (no feature gate) so the grading is a standing
    gate, while the live capture that produced it is not.

14. **Write the evidence record under `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-09-06-operator-gated-live-suite/evidence/`.**
    It holds the per-leg frozen self-obs copies (step 7) plus a record of WHAT was measured, on WHICH leg, and
    against WHICH SUT HEAD, and a **process census taken before and after, per subject**, as a table with a
    final state of `terminated` or `left running: {why} + who stops it` — `pulse-app: left running — operator
    stops it`; a leg never kills what it did not start (verification-harness 2026-09-02). Host-path-free and
    free of internal seam-crate struct names.

15. **Size the suite's wall-clock wrapper above the real budget.** Each preflight pays a 45s warm-up
    (`contracts/pulse-run-contract.toml:26-27` `warmup_ms = 45000`) and a not-ready gate pays the 90s poll floor
    (`:30` `min_canary_poll_seconds = 90`; `canary_poll` at `canary.rs:262-274`). Budget: B1 ~60s · B2 ~135s ·
    quiet window 150s · A ~200s · the a11y arm ~3–4 min ⇒ **~12–15 minutes total**. The wrapper both shells
    apply must exceed that; the existing `boot` budget (`warmup_ms/1000 + poll + margin`) is far too small.

16. **Name the STOP form beside the firing form** in both the module header and the evidence record: the wdio
    arm self-terminates via `onComplete` → `tauriDriver.kill()`; the interrupted-run manual stop is
    `taskkill /F /IM msedgedriver.exe /IM conductor-tauri.exe` plus the node CLI.
- `scenarios/auto-resolve-idle-window.toml` — the purpose-built declare-only silent scenario (leg A's subject).
- `crates/conductor-run/tests/live_suite.rs` — the `live-pulse`-gated live driver; prints its captures.
- `crates/conductor-run/tests/live_suite_harvest.rs` — the ungated graded half over frozen committed lines.
- `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-09-06-operator-gated-live-suite/evidence/` — per-leg frozen self-obs + census.

- `scripts/agent-run.sh` — add the `--live` stage arm to the `run` verb's `case` (beside `--unit` /

```bash
PATH=/d/dev/projects/andromeda-pulse/target/release:$PATH \
ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR=<the live pulse-app's data dir> \
```

| `conductor-run/src/lib.rs:518` — `Observation.degraded` on the `ReadBack::AutoResolved` arm | `crates/conductor-run/src/execute.rs:91-96` (arm opens `:91`; `Observation { degraded: true, .. }` at `:95`) | `execute.rs:95:27` |

Verified-as-written (no correction needed): test-plan **§6** does carry the driven arm's full firing form including the
quiet window; test-plan **§9** does carry the live-leg CI ban; the disposition ledger does carry **classes B and C**; and
the SUT dedupe coordinate holds byte-exact — `andromeda-pulse pulse-app/src/inference_runtime.rs:811` at HEAD `83d4060`
is `.find(|inc| inc.kind == kind && inc.scope == scope && inc.scope_id == scope_id)`, re-read this session.

- **Mechanism, marker text kept verbatim — VERIFIED at P3:** the driven a11y arm's live precondition is
  SELF-COLLIDING — `conductor preflight` fires its own canary storm, and Pulse dedupes a new incident against any
  OPEN one on the same `(kind, scope, scope_id)` tuple (*as measured at
  `andromeda-pulse pulse-app/src/inference_runtime.rs:811`, HEAD `83d4060`*), so a second canary inside the ~120s
  idle + 30s resolver window forms no FRESH incident and preflight blocks. The `measured at` marker set the depth:
  the evidence pointer was spot-checked still-true at HEAD (the line reads
  `.find(|inc| inc.kind == kind && inc.scope == scope && inc.scope_id == scope_id)`).
- The RELIABLE shape is the quiet window, already recorded as part of the leg's firing form (test-plan §6).

- **An undecided design fork this entry MAY weigh — `not decided` in the entry's own words:** a PER-RUN CANARY
  IDENTITY, salting the canary's `scope_id` so the preflight tuple and the driven-run tuple differ by construction,
  removing the collision instead of waiting it out. Weighable here because this entry's stated job is a re-runnable
  live-Pulse proof invocation. **Not resolvable at P1** — it goes to P4 as a fork, not a lean.
- Either way the suite stays **never a CI gate**, and test-plan §9's live-leg ban is unchanged.

Three `conductor-run` mutation survivors are accepted-deliberate at the TIER because no hermetic test can reach their
sites, but their OBSERVABLES are live-path facts a driven run can assert **from persisted records** — so the coverage
is owned here rather than parked inside an accepted class. Assert, on a live-Pulse driven run:

1. `Observation.degraded == true` on a declare-only scenario whose read-back finds an empty active set (the
   `ReadBack::AutoResolved` arm — re-aimed to `execute.rs:91-96`).

2. the persisted `latency_ms` equals `read_back_observed_at − journal_emitted_at` on the manual path (re-aimed to
   `execute.rs:136`) — **a subtraction, not a sum or quotient**.

3. the `preflight blocked: readiness gate not satisfied` self-obs line appears on a NOT-ready gate and is absent on a
   ready one (re-aimed to `canary.rs:58-59`), which needs a connected sidecar and therefore a live leg.

- **Mechanism, marker text kept verbatim — VERIFIED at P3:** each is unreachable from a unit test *for a measured
  reason* — a fixed `http://127.0.0.1:4317` endpoint const contended under `--jobs 2`; a crate-private `Preflight`;
  a spawned `andromeda-pulse-mcp` absent on a hermetic host. All three re-derived at HEAD:
  `DEFAULT_OTLP_ENDPOINT = "http://127.0.0.1:4317"` (`conductor-emit/src/client.rs:23`); `Preflight`'s `client` and
  `ready` are `pub(crate)` (`canary.rs:32-33`) under a doc comment stating they are never `pub`; the sidecar is a
  fixed program NAME resolved through the inherited `PATH`.

- `[added at P3]` **The persisted proxy for observable 1 exists, but not as a `degraded` field.** `RunRecord`'s
  eleven fields carry no `degraded` key and `degraded_mode_response` appears NOWHERE in `crates/` (0 hits) — so
  obs-plan's "envelope extras like `degraded_mode_response`" has no implementation. What DOES discriminate is the
  declare-only state mapping: `manual_record` sets `state: state_for(observation, ReportState::ManualCheck)` and
  `state_for` returns `KnownResidual` iff `observation.degraded`, so on a declare-only scenario
  `state == KnownResidual` ⟺ `degraded == true`. Which ROUTE produced it is separated by the self-obs line
  `declare-only read-back empty: no active incident outlived the emission window` (`execute.rs:92-94`), which
  fires only on the `AutoResolved` arm.

- `[added at P3]` **Observable 2 cannot be asserted as an exact equality from persisted records.**
  `now_rfc3339` (`conductor-core/src/obs.rs:212-219`) truncates to `as_secs()`, so both envelope instants are
  whole-second while `latency_ms` is millisecond-grained from `now_ms()`. The assertion is a BOUNDED one
  (|`latency_ms` − 1000·Δsecs| < 1000), and it still kills `execute.rs:136:25`'s `-` → `+` / `/` mutants, whose
  outputs miss by far more than a second.

- **Landing these does NOT retire the tier acceptances:** the mutants stay accepted-deliberate (a live leg is never a
  CI gate, test-plan §9), and this CARRY buys the behavioural coverage the accepted class cannot. Test-plan §12's
  roster is unchanged by this chunk.

Give Conductor ONE named, re-runnable, operator-gated invocation that fires the live-Pulse proof legs in a single
correct shape and lands a durable evidence record — so a live proof stops being a hand-assembled paste of env blocks
whose partial forms fail silently, and so the three CARRY-2 observables get asserted from persisted records for the
first time. It is never a CI gate and never becomes one.

- **[premise-corrected: SIX families / eight invocations, not "at least four" — measured at P3]** The live-proof
  surface today is scattered across SIX firing-form families with different env blocks, orderings and evidence
  destinations: (1) `agent-run boot`; (2) `agent-run run` plus its CONDITIONAL `SCENARIO=<name|P-ID> [SEED=<n>]`
  scenario leg — the only leg that rewrites `logs/agent-latest.jsonl`; (3) `agent-run run --e2e` → `npm run a11y`;
  (4) `cargo test -p conductor-run --features live-pulse --test lifecycle_live` (the one feature-gated live driver,
  whose own header already documents a full one-paste env block and the two pacing facts); (5) `npm run a11y:driven`;
  (6) the three `sr*` suites `npm run a11y:sr` / `a11y:sr-empty` / `a11y:sr-error`. Both harness shells ship each
  verb at identical semantics.

- Outcome: one entry point that composes the legs in the correct order with the quiet window honoured, refuses to run
  a partial env rather than degrading to a silent `[BLOCKED]`, and is invocable repeatedly without hand-editing.

- **Boundary — the invocation's SHAPE is not fixed by the entry** (a P4 decision, **narrowed at P3**): test-plan
  §9's sanctioned live-leg SET has exactly four members — `workflow_dispatch`, `scripts/agent-run.sh`, a
  cargo-feature-gated test file invoked directly, and an npm-script wdio suite. A NEW `conductor-cli` verb is not a
  member as written, and the harness's 5-command discipline forbids a 6th `agent-run` command without a test-plan
  amendment — so the live-set-compatible options are a STAGE FLAG on an existing `agent-run` verb, a
  `live-pulse`-gated test target, or both. Whichever is chosen must not put a live leg on any default
  `nextest` / `clippy` / release path.

- **Precedent to follow — VERIFIED at P3:** the harvest tier (`crates/conductor-run/tests/*_harvest.rs`, **nine
  targets** confirmed) already grades live claims against COMMITTED frozen leg lines sliced from
  `{data_dir}/logs/agent-latest.jsonl.<date>` by a pre-leg line count, and `lifecycle_live.rs:30` states the split
  in its own words — it "PRINTS its observation rather than asserting a pinned expectation: the capture is the
  deliverable, and the grading lives in `lifecycle_harvest.rs` over the frozen lines." The capture/grade split is
  the existing shape; this chunk reuses it rather than minting a second evidence convention.

- Outcome: a re-run produces an evidence artifact under this chunk's `evidence/` that records WHAT was measured, on
  WHICH arm, and against WHICH SUT HEAD — host-path-free per the artifact-hygiene invariant.

title: W4 — the CARRY-1 fork, weighed and recorded

data.head: ### W4 — the CARRY-1 fork, weighed and recorded

body:
- The per-run canary identity option is either adopted (with its `scope_id` salting shipped) or explicitly declined
  in favour of the recorded quiet-window shape — **decided at P4 with the operator, never silently**. Whichever way,
  the decision and its basis are recorded.

- **RESOLVED at P4 (operator-decided): DECLINED.** The quiet window is kept as the recorded reliable shape, and
  shipped canary behaviour is unchanged. Basis: test-plan §6 already records the quiet window as the firing form,
  and research added the fact that the dedupe collision is the cheapest lever for producing observable 3's
  negative arm — a CONNECTED client with an UNSATISFIED gate, the only state that reaches `canary.rs:59`.

Two justified divergences the plan surfaced; the intent was incomplete, so scope is amended to the better
understanding rather than the plan re-worked.

- **The `sr*` screen-reader suites are NOT composed by `--live`.** W1's "composes the legs" did not enumerate
  which. They are excluded because they are a screen-reader proof rather than a live-Pulse proof (only the `sr`
  subject uses live Pulse at all) and they need `CONDUCTOR_NVDA` plus a fifth `CONDUCTOR_SCENARIOS_DIR` handle.
  They keep their own npm invocations. The driven a11y arm IS composed, because CARRY 1 is specifically about
  its live precondition.

- **The suite fires THREE scenario legs, not one.** B1 (short declare-only — observable 2's subject, and
  observable 3's absent arm), B2 (fired deliberately INSIDE the quiet window so its canary dedupes and the gate
  goes not-ready-but-connected — observable 3's present arm), and A (the silent scenario — observable 1's
  subject). The scope named the observables but not the leg count they imply.

- **A purpose-built scenario is a DELIVERABLE, not just a subject.** `scenarios/auto-resolve-idle-window.toml`
  (one silent phase, `gap_ms = 165000`, `occurrences = 0`, `p_ids = ["P-022"]`, plus the mandatory
  `LOAD ENVELOPE` header comment) is authored for observable 1's subject. The mechanism: `observe`
  (`crates/conductor-verify/src/extract.rs:76`) calls `query_incident_list(None)` with no filter and returns
  `EmptyCorpus` only when the active set is empty, while the run's own preflight canary incident stays open for
  120s idle + a 30s tick.
  **[premise-corrected at P5 round 2: reachability is PER-SCENARIO, not a property of the family.** An earlier
  draft of this bullet said the arm is "unreachable with every committed declare-only scenario" — false.
  `ack-cooldown` (370s of phases, no emission tables) DOES reach it, proven live at leg E on 2026-08-21 and
  pinned at `crates/conductor-run/tests/severity_harvest.rs:505-513`. Only the SHORT declare-only scenarios
  (2–75s) are unreachable. The new scenario is therefore chosen on wall clock (165s roughly halves leg A) and
  declared intent, never on reachability.]**

- **Each leg's self-obs must be FROZEN before the next leg runs.** `logs/agent-latest.jsonl` is opened
  `.truncate(true)` (`conductor-core/src/obs.rs:108-111`), so a single end-of-suite read would see only the last
  leg; and a per-leg `CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR` does not separate them, because `agent_log_path` resolves the logs dir
  as `runs_dir.parent()/logs` (`conductor-cli/src/paths.rs:87-88`).

- **The suite's wall-clock budget is ~12–15 minutes**, not the ~150s per leg the scope's quiet-window framing
  implied: each preflight pays a 45s warm-up and a not-ready gate pays the 90s poll floor
  (`contracts/pulse-run-contract.toml:26-27,30`).

title: Boundaries (what this chunk does NOT do)

data.head: ## Boundaries (what this chunk does NOT do)

body: - **Never a CI gate.** test-plan §9's live-leg ban and arch's CI/CD note stand; no CI workflow gains a live stage.

- **Does not retire the accepted-deliberate mutation classes B and C** (CARRY 2 says so in its own words); test-plan
  §12's roster is not edited by this chunk.
- **No PULSE UI automation** (scope law). Driving Conductor's own webview stays in scope.

- **No new inbound listener.** The `:4317` port-occupier and the dev-only `4444`/`4445` driver ports remain the whole
  deliberate-bind set.

- **Does not manage the Pulse process.** Launching `pulse-app` stays the operator's act; the suite may REFUSE to run
  when preconditions are unmet, but it never starts or stops the SUT.
- Claims no capability by itself; whether any pooled matrix entry becomes fully verifiable here is decided at P5.

_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-09-06-run-report-envelope-conformance-gate · **Version:** conductor-0.2.0 · **Generated:** 2026-09-06T12:15Z

The per-run journal `runs/<run_id>.jsonl` is the agent-parseable ground truth every SLO measurement reads, and
it is the one governed artifact with no conformance gate: obs-plan §9 states in writing that the run-report
envelope "gets its own (not-yet-built) conformance gate", while the shipped gate at `ci.yml:112-160` covers
only the self-obs stream. This chunk builds that gate — every journal row asserted schema-complete against its
declared shape and free of absolute host paths, red on violation.

Two facts measured at P3 shape it. First, **the gate is a regression guard, not a bug hunt**: across the 71
journals on this host the rows are 74 envelopes + 1 check record, with zero non-conformant rows, zero
unparseable lines and zero host-path hits — so a first run is expected GREEN on real artifacts, exactly the
`2026-06-27-obs-ci-conformance-gate` precedent (PASS-on-real + FAIL-on-a-removed-field). Its value is that
host-path freedom currently holds by upstream convention across ~6 producers with nothing asserting it —
`conductor-report` contains no `redact_value` call at all, so obs-plan §11's application site (b) is
unimplemented and the property is one careless field away from breaking silently.

Second, **the gate's central requirement is already violated by a shipped reader**. `read_run_journal`
(`run_journal.rs:39`) parses every line as `RunRecord`, so a run that emitted per-check records fails the read
outright — measured, not reasoned: `conductor report 2026-08-21T18-53-35-135` exits 1 with `missing field
\`seed\``, while an envelope-only control renders at exit 0. Two production callers are affected (`conductor
report`, the Tauri `run_report`). test-plan §3's amendment (d) predicted this hazard in writing at the very
chunk that introduced the second shape; the spec was corrected and the code was not. Fixing it is the gate's
own rule applied once, at the one place that provably breaks it — and it lets the reader and the gate share a
single discrimination rule rather than two.

The CARRY from `2026-08-21-per-check-latency-measurement` rides with it: the harness `cleanup` verb deletes
from `runs` alone, leaving orphans in `run_check` and `run_envelope`. P3 measured why that has never been
caught — **`sqlite3` is absent from this host entirely and CI never installs it**, and both shells guard their
DB arm on `command -v sqlite3` / `Get-Command sqlite3`, so the delete has never executed anywhere we can
observe. Operator-decided at P4: the teardown moves **into the binary**, where test-plan §3:162's prescribed
form (`DELETE … WHERE run_id = ?1`, "rusqlite bound parameters") is expressible at all — which the `sqlite3`
CLI cannot do. Cleanup becomes portable, testable, host-dependency-free, and the string-interpolation tension
the CARRY records disappears rather than doubling.

1. **Add a journal-line classifier to `conductor-core/src/run_journal.rs`.** One function classifies a single
   journal line into exactly one registered shape — an envelope (`RunRecord`), a per-check record
   (`CheckRecord`), or an error naming the line as conforming to neither. Discrimination is by typed parse,
   sound because the two shapes have disjoint REQUIRED (non-`Option`) keys — an envelope needs `seed` /
   `p_ids` / `slo_tier` / `scenario` / `state` / `run_id`, a check record needs `check_index` / `kind` /
   `deadline_ms`, and neither line can supply the other's (arch §Standard Contracts; obs-plan §3). Attempt the
   envelope shape first, then the check shape; report the ORIGINAL envelope parse error when neither matches,
   since the envelope is the dominant shape and its error names the missing field.
   **The typed parse settles SHAPE and the closed enum sets — it does NOT settle key presence.** Measured on
   serde 1.0.229 with four controls: a derived `Deserialize` accepts an ABSENT `Option` field as `None`
   without any `#[serde(default)]`, so the envelope's five `Option` keys (`journal_emitted_at`,
   `read_back_observed_at`, `verdict`, `latency_ms`, `fingerprints`) and the check record's `budget_ms` all
   deserialize cleanly when simply missing. Presence is therefore a SEPARATE assertion, owned by step 5.

2. **Make `read_run_journal` tolerate the second shape.** It keeps returning `Vec<RunRecord>` — its two
   production callers want the scenario grain — but now classifies each line and skips check records instead
   of failing on them. A line matching NEITHER shape stays a hard error, so genuinely malformed rows still
   surface. Re-export the classifier from `conductor-core/src/lib.rs` beside `read_run_journal` (`:63`) so the
   gate asserts through the same rule the reader uses (obs-plan §11 single-location ownership, applied to
   shape discrimination as well as redaction).

3. **Pin the reader regression in `run_journal.rs`'s own unit tests.** A journal carrying an envelope line
   followed by a check line reads back the envelope rows and does not error; a line conforming to neither
   shape still errors with a message naming the missing field. This is the assertion whose absence let the
   defect stand.

4. **Seed a per-check record into the fixture subject** — `crates/conductor-run/tests/envelope_fixture.rs`,
   `seed_into` at `:134`, currently passes `&[]` as `persist`'s `checks` argument. Pass one `CheckRecord`
   consistent with the fixture's lamps subject. This is the ONLY way to obtain a `run_check` row and a
   `CheckRecord` journal line without a live Pulse, and it goes through the production writer, which is what
   test-plan §7 requires (a hand-populated `runs.db` is banned). **Ordering:** unreachable before step 2,
   because `envelope_fixture.rs:115` re-reads the persisted journal through `read_run_journal`.

5. **Build the conformance gate** as `crates/conductor-run/tests/journal_conformance.rs`. Over two subjects —
   the committed `tests/fixtures/lamps-journal.jsonl`, and a journal produced in-test through
   `conductor_run::persist` carrying BOTH shapes — assert four properties per line:
   (a) **shape** — it classifies as exactly one registered shape via step 1's classifier;
   (b) **key presence** — a `serde_json::Value` key-set check, independent of the typed parse because the
   typed parse cannot see an absent `Option` key: the object's key set must be a SUPERSET of the shape's full
   name list (all eleven envelope names, or all nine check names). Extra keys are ALLOWED — obs-plan §3 keeps
   the per-scenario extension point open, which is the same reason `deny_unknown_fields` is rejected below.
   This is what makes "a Blocked row's five measurement fields are PRESENT and null, never absent" (arch
   §Standard Contracts; security-plan §Error Handling) an assertion rather than a hope; the writer already
   emits explicit nulls (`RunRecord::blocked` sets `None`, and no field carries `skip_serializing_if`), so the
   property is real today and the check guards agent parsers against a future `skip_serializing_if`;
   (c) **closed sets** — `verdict` and `state` fall in their closed sets, with the crosswalk's governed
   co-occurrences accepted (a11y-plan §6);
   (d) **host-path freedom** — every string-valued field survives `conductor_core::redact_value` unchanged.

6. **Add the gate's negative arms** in the same file, because a gate never exercised against a violation is
   not known to fail. THREE arms, and the middle one is the reason step 5(b) exists at all:
   (i) a row with a REQUIRED key removed (e.g. `seed`) — caught by the typed parse;
   (ii) a row with an **`Option` key removed** (e.g. `latency_ms`) — caught ONLY by the key-set check, since
   the typed parse accepts it as `None` (measured, step 1). An arm that removes a required key would never
   exercise the presence check, so this arm is not optional;
   (iii) a row carrying an injected absolute host path — caught by the redaction predicate.
   Construct all three by mutating a serialized record in-test — never by committing a malformed fixture.

7. **Add `RunsDb::delete_run` to `crates/conductor-report/src/db.rs`** — the storage seam owns the SQL. Three
   `DELETE … WHERE run_id = ?1` statements over `runs`, `run_check` and `run_envelope` with rusqlite BOUND
   parameters, applied in one transaction so teardown is all-or-nothing, and idempotent (deleting nothing is
   success). Follow the file's existing raw-SQL, no-migration idiom (arch §Established Decisions [ORM]).

8. **Unit-test `delete_run` in `db.rs`** against a DB carrying rows in all three tables: every table returns
   `count(*) = 0` afterwards, and a second call is a no-op. This is the count-zero verification test-plan
   §3:164 has always specified and nothing ever implemented.

9. **Add the `cleanup` verb to `conductor-cli`** — a `Cleanup { run_id }` variant on `Commands`
   (`cli.rs:20-60`), a `commands/cleanup.rs` handler, and its registration + dispatch in `commands/mod.rs`
   (which today declares `coverage`/`preconditions`/`preflight`/`report`/`run`/`suite`). It resolves the runs
   dir through the existing CLI path edge so `CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR` + `resolve_under` apply unchanged, calls
   `RunsDb::delete_run`, and prints one confirmation line in the shipped `render` style — no new colour, no
   new bracket label (design-system §Surface: cli / Tokens).

10. **Point both shells at the verb.** In `scripts/agent-run.sh` (`:232-234`) and `scripts/agent-run.ps1`
    (`:253-255`), replace the `sqlite3`-guarded block with the binary invocation each file already uses for
    every other verb (`"$CARGO" run -q -p conductor-cli --bin conductor -- cleanup "$id"` / the pwsh array
    form). Keep each shell's existing run-id guard (`valid_run_id` `:60`/`:230`; `Test-RunId` `:58`/`:249`),
    keep the `rm -f` on the two named artifacts, and keep idempotency. The agent-run verb count stays five and
    both shells stay at identical semantics (layout-templates §Surface: cli — Primary screens).

11. **Add a CI journal-conformance step** to `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, beside the obs gate. Its producer
    already exists — the obs gate's `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR: 'pulse;injection'` step (`:118-124`) yields a
    Blocked envelope at exit 0 and writes `runs/<run_id>.jsonl` as a side effect nothing currently asserts.
    **Mechanism: the step RUNS THE RUST GATE over that journal — it does not re-implement it in `jq`.** A `jq`
    re-listing of the key names would be a THIRD copy of the schema (the Rust structs · obs-plan §3/§6 · the
    YAML), and the chunk's whole posture is single-sourcing. So `journal_conformance.rs` reads
    `CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR` when set and asserts over the journals it finds there (falling back to its fixture +
    in-test subjects when unset, so an ordinary suite run is unchanged), and the CI step invokes that test
    target with the handle pointed at the producer's output. `CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR` is an EXISTING handle — no
    new handle and no fourth handle class. The host-path half MAY mirror the obs gate's anchor set in YAML as
    the pre-existing exception noted below, but the key lists live in exactly one place.

- `crates/conductor-run/tests/journal_conformance.rs` — the conformance gate: positive arms over the committed
  fixture and a `persist`-produced mixed-shape journal, plus the three negative arms. Additionally reads
  `CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR` when set and asserts over every journal it finds there — the mechanism by which the CI
  step (step 11) reuses this gate instead of re-listing the schema in `jq`. Unset, it asserts over its own
  subjects only, so an ordinary suite run is unchanged.
- `crates/conductor-cli/src/commands/cleanup.rs` — the `cleanup` verb handler.

- `crates/conductor-core/src/run_journal.rs` — the line classifier; `read_run_journal` skips check records and
  still errors on a line matching neither shape; the regression unit tests.
- `crates/conductor-core/src/lib.rs` — re-export the classifier beside `read_run_journal` (`:63`).

- `crates/conductor-report/src/db.rs` — `RunsDb::delete_run` (three bound-parameter deletes in a transaction)
  plus its count-zero unit test.
- `crates/conductor-cli/src/cli.rs` — the `Cleanup { run_id }` variant on `Commands`.
- `crates/conductor-cli/src/commands/mod.rs` — declare the `cleanup` module and dispatch the new variant.

- `crates/conductor-run/tests/envelope_fixture.rs` — `seed_into` (`:134`) passes one `CheckRecord` to
  `persist` instead of `&[]`.
- `scripts/agent-run.sh` — `cleanup` (`:232-234`) calls the binary instead of `sqlite3`.
- `scripts/agent-run.ps1` — the same, at identical semantics (`:253-255`).
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — the journal-conformance step beside the obs gate.

```bash
# 1. Unit + integration: the classifier, the reader regression, the gate, delete_run, the fixture round-trip.
cargo nextest run -p conductor-core -p conductor-report -p conductor-run -p conductor-cli --profile ci

# 2. Full workspace suite + doctests — conductor-core is a source delta every crate sees.
cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci
cargo test --workspace --doc

# 3. Lint gate.
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

# 4. CARRY end-to-end on the BASH shell, against a subject seeded through the production writer
#    (test-plan §7 bans a hand-populated runs.db). runs/ is gitignored, so the probe dir never enters the
```

title: A LIVE PRODUCTION DEFECT, measured not reasoned

data.head: ## A LIVE PRODUCTION DEFECT, measured not reasoned

body: `conductor_core::read_run_journal` (`run_journal.rs:39`) parses **every** journal line as `RunRecord`, so any run that emitted a per-check record makes the whole read fail. Probed with the prebuilt `target/debug/conductor.exe`:
| Subject | Result |
| `report 2026-08-21T18-53-35-135` (has a check row) | **exit 1** — `error: scenario config error: parse journal line: missing field \`seed\` at line 1 column 218` |
| `report 2026-09-06T09-11-09-325` (envelope-only) | exit 0, the 6-column table renders |

It has **two production callers** — `conductor-cli/src/commands/report.rs:17` (the `conductor report` verb) and `conductor-tauri/src/commands.rs:206` (the `run_report` Tauri command) — so both the CLI report and the webview run-report view fail outright on such a run. Latent since `2026-08-21-per-check-latency-measurement` introduced the second shape. test-plan §3's amendment (d) from that very chunk predicted it in writing ("a file-wide parse-to-envelope is a false negative on any run emitting check rows"); the correction was applied to the SPEC and the reader was never changed. Secondary: the error is mis-classified as `scenario config error` (`CoreError::Config`) for a journal parse.

**Why it belongs to this chunk:** the gate's central requirement is that the two shapes be discriminated, and the shipped reader is the one place that provably does not. A gate certifying rows that two shipped commands cannot read would be the contradiction the chunk exists to remove — and the discrimination rule is single-sourced if the reader and the gate share it.

- Bind the host-path notion to `conductor_core::redact_value` and assert `redact_value(s) == s` per string field — `is_host_path_token` is private (`redact.rs:120`) and must not be duplicated (obs-plan §11 single-location ownership).
- Typed parse over `serde_json::Value` key-set comparison — arch §Stack (Serialization) and the existing readers' idiom; no new dependency (`serde_json` is already a `conductor-run` dev-dep).

- Gate code lands in existing crates only, minting no new cross-seam edge (arch §Module boundaries): the classifier in `conductor-core` beside `read_run_journal`, the gate test in `conductor-run/tests/`.
- `assert_fs::TempDir` + `CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR` for a producer that writes run artifacts (test-plan §3 Per-test isolation).

- Both harness shells stay at identical semantics (layout-templates §Surface: cli); each added `DELETE` sits behind the existing run-id gate — `valid_run_id` (`agent-run.sh:60`, applied `:230`) / `Test-RunId` (`agent-run.ps1:58`, applied `:249`).

- `crates/conductor-run/tests/journal_conformance.rs` — the conformance gate: over the committed fixture AND a journal produced in-test through `conductor_run::persist`, assert every line classifies as exactly one registered shape, that both shapes' key sets are complete by typed parse, that a Blocked row's five measurement fields are present-and-null (not absent), that `verdict`/`state` sit in their closed sets, and that every string field survives `redact_value` unchanged. Plus the negative arms: a row with a removed field, and a row with an injected absolute host path, each must FAIL.

- `crates/conductor-core/src/run_journal.rs` — add the line classifier (a line is an envelope, a check record, or an error) and make `read_run_journal` return envelope rows while tolerating check rows; a line matching neither shape stays a hard error. Export the classifier so the gate asserts through the same rule the reader uses.
- `crates/conductor-core/src/lib.rs` — re-export the new classifier item beside `read_run_journal` (`:63`), so `conductor-run`'s test can reach it.
- `scripts/agent-run.sh` — `cleanup` (`:233`): add `DELETE FROM run_check` and `DELETE FROM run_envelope`, both behind the existing `valid_run_id` gate.
- `scripts/agent-run.ps1` — `cleanup` (`:254`): the same two deletes, behind the existing `Test-RunId` gate, at identical semantics.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — a journal-conformance assertion step over the run journal the existing obs producer (`:118-124`) already writes, beside the obs gate.

- `crates/conductor-run/tests/envelope_fixture.rs` — extend the seeded subject so a `run_check` row and a `CheckRecord` journal line exist for the cleanup count-zero verification and the discrimination arm to bite. **[provisional — see open question 1]**

1. Whether the cleanup count-zero verification needs a seeded `run_check` row of its own, or whether asserting `count(*) = 0` on an already-empty table is verification enough → blocks: implementation-scope (decides whether `envelope_fixture.rs` is touched). A zero that was always zero proves nothing about the delete, so the honest form seeds a row first; the cheaper form does not.

2. Whether the CI step should assert over the produced journal alone or also re-run the Rust gate → blocks: plan-decision. Leaning: the Rust test is the gate (build-failing everywhere, binds to `redact_value`); the CI step adds coverage of a REAL produced artifact the fixture cannot stand in for.
Every `[inferred]` bullet in `scope.md` was re-read against the findings above; `scope.md` has been amended accordingly.

- **VERIFIED** (tag dropped): both-row-shape coverage · build-failing enforcement (home now settled) · "not a schema change" · "not the Markdown report / `runs.db`" · "no live Pulse" · "no new `CONDUCTOR_*` handle".

- **`[premise-corrected]`**: the host-path binding. Scope said the gate mirrors `conductor-core::redact::is_host_path_token`; that function is **private** (`redact.rs:120`) and only `redact_value` / `sanitize_error` are `pub`. The predicate becomes `redact_value(s) == s`, which reuses the same single source without widening the API.

- **Scope gained a section it was missing** (intent-incomplete, not a defect): the `read_run_journal` production defect above. Scope's open question 3 asked whether the two shapes are discriminable *at all*; the answer is yes at the type level and **no at the shipped reader**, which scope had no bullet for.

- The a11y extract's question — whether the new `run_envelope` delete can strand the routine arm's seeded subject — is **answered NO**: `wdio.conf.ts:90-93` `seedFixtureRuns()` does `rmSync(target, {recursive:true, force:true})` then re-creates and re-seeds per session, so the arm cannot inherit a deleted row.

**Working entry (verbatim):** _Run-report envelope conformance gate — every run journal row
schema-complete and host-path-free, build failing on violation_

**One-line goal:** the run journal (`runs/<run_id>.jsonl`) gets the conformance gate the self-obs
stream has had since Epoch 10 — every row asserted schema-complete against its declared shape and
free of absolute host paths, failing the build on violation.

_Amended at P3 (scope premise closure). Verified `[inferred]` tags dropped; one bullet carries
`[premise-corrected]`; one section is new (intent-incomplete — planning surfaced what the scope
missed). Evidence: `research.md`._

- **A conformance gate over `runs/<run_id>.jsonl`.** obs-plan §9 `:535` already reserves it in
  writing — the log conformance gate validates the self-obs base-line schema "NOT the Section-6
  run-report ENVELOPE …, which is the scenario-RESULT record in `runs/<run_id>.jsonl` and gets its
  own (not-yet-built) conformance gate." This chunk builds that gate.

- **Schema-completeness over BOTH row shapes the journal carries.** obs-plan §3 establishes that the
  report seam writes two line shapes onto one journal — the eleven-field Run-report envelope and the
  nine-key per-check `CheckRecord`. "Every row" covers both, and the gate must DISCRIMINATE them
  rather than assert one shape over all lines. VERIFIED at HEAD: neither shape can deserialize as
  the other (disjoint required keys) and neither carries `#[serde(default)]`, so **a typed parse is
  simultaneously the discriminator and the key-presence check**.

- **Host-path-freedom over the same rows,** bound to the single source in `conductor-core::redact`.
  `[premise-corrected: is_host_path_token is PRIVATE (redact.rs:120); only redact_value and
  sanitize_error are pub, so the predicate is redact_value(s) == s — same source, no API widening]`

- **Build-failing enforcement**, settled at P3: a Rust test in the default nextest suite (red on
  every dev machine and in CI, and able to call `redact_value` directly), plus a CI step over the
  run journal the existing obs producer already writes — a REAL produced artifact a fixture cannot
  stand in for.

on this host for the first time and removes the undeclared host dependency. The `agent-run`
5-command count is untouched.

- **Not the self-obs stream.** `logs/agent-latest.jsonl` already has its gate (`ci.yml:112-160`);
