data.head: ## Baseline — measured this session, on the build branch

body:
**CI run 34209940695**, head `a71e6bf` (`build/conductor-0.2.0`; `origin` and `HEAD` now agree — the
operator's push has happened, so this is a build-branch run, not a probe ref).
| Job | Result |
| Rust gate (build · test · lint · supply-chain · coverage) | ✓ success (09:25:52 → 09:33:13Z) |
| Frontend gate (npm audit · build) | ✓ success (09:25:51 → 09:26:48Z) |
| A11y gate (routine arm · axe · contrast · violation JSON) | ✗ failure (09:25:50 → 09:37:36Z, 11 m 46 s) |
Read from the job log itself, not inherited:

- `09:26:37.132Z` — `[precondition] CONDUCTOR_MSEDGEDRIVER: resolved` — **the SR chunk's driver-handle fix
  holds on the build branch.** The `EDGEWEBDRIVER`-in-the-step-shell resolution works.
- `09:34:06.926Z` — `Execution of 1 workers started` (≈8 min of npm install + release build precede it).

- `09:35:08.923Z` — `[0-0] WARN webdriver: WebDriverError: session not created: DevToolsActivePort file
  doesn't exist when running "http://127.0.0.1:4444/session" with method "POST"`

- `09:36:09.055Z` — `Spec Files: 0 passed, 1 failed, 1 total (100% completed) in 00:02:01`, the spec
  `FAILED in wry` after `(1 retries)`; then `error: wdio exited 1` → `Process completed with exit code 1`.

Two properties of that log worth carrying into the work: **the decisive line is logged at `WARN`, not
`ERROR`** (the standing corpus rule about severity-as-proxy applies to any sweep of these logs), and
**wdio's full RED output now reaches the job log** — the second SR-chunk fix, also holding.

This run supersedes the four probe-ref runs as the citable baseline; those proved the two fixes on probe
branches and are evidence about the fixes, not about the current build-branch state.

**Standing premise, MEASURED:** on the hosted `windows-2025` runner **a WebView2-mode session never exposes
`DevToolsActivePort`** — through `@crabnebula/tauri-driver` and direct at `msedgedriver` alike, as measured
at run 34162118841, and now reproduced on the build branch at run 34209940695.
**The cause beyond that statement is UNMEASURED.** Do not inherit a mechanism for it.
**Excluded by measurement** (all of them, at the prior chunk):
- runtime absence — WebView2 Evergreen Runtime present;

- version mismatch — msedgedriver = Runtime = Edge, all `151.0.4129.101`, self-consistent (this dev host
  runs 152, so the runner is one major behind, but internally consistent);

data.head: ## Premises — closed at P3 against research (`research.md`)

body:
- **VERIFIED — The hypotheses are independently testable and orderable.** Research derived the order from
  the driver's real surfaces: **H2 is cheapest by a wide margin** (one added key on `appEnv`, no dependency
  and no spawn-form change), H4 is an operator/infrastructure fact, H1 is a governed-spawn-form change
  requiring escalation, and H3 is demoted on a falsified premise. A **fifth** option surfaced that the entry
  never named — `tauri-plugin-automation` + `@crabnebula/test-runner-backend`, the bridge README's other
  Windows path — inside the one stack but adding a runtime plugin to the shipped app.

- **NARROWED — the official `tauri-driver` crate is not "drop-in" (hypothesis 1).** Its availability and CLI
  parity remain unverified (no network read taken), but the swap is now known to change the spawn PROGRAM
  from a repo-derived resolved constant (`require.resolve('@crabnebula/tauri-driver/cli.js')`) to a
  `PATH`-resolved installed binary — a **sixth governed spawn form** under security-plan rule (b), which that
  plan's history classifies as boundary widening: escalate, never routine.

- `[premise-corrected: operator dev-host measurement at the P5 review — msedgedriver in webview2 mode puts the
  app's profile in its OWN %TEMP%\scoped_dir<pid>_<rand>\EBWebView\ and does so even with
  WEBVIEW2_USER_DATA_FOLDER exported to the driver, leaving the inherited dir empty]` **Hypothesis 2 is
  RETIRED as a remedy: the handle is not a lever on the driver path.** The P3 reading — that the env chain
  makes the handle "one added key on `appEnv`" — was right about propagation and wrong about effect: the
  chain propagates and **the driver overwrites at the end of it**. The loader does honour the handle on a
  BARE launch (`<dir>\EBWebView\DevToolsActivePort` in 1 s), which is precisely why it looked like a lever.
  My P3 probe measured that *tauri-driver* neither sets nor overrides a user-data folder — true, and
  irrelevant, because the overriding writer is **msedgedriver**, which I never probed. The chunk therefore
  ships no remedy and becomes diagnose-only.

- `[premise-corrected: test-plan.md:307 records msedgedriver 151 driving WebView2 Runtime 152 GREEN on the
  dev host across three sr* sessions and the routine --e2e re-run; the runner's driver, Runtime and Edge are
  all 151.0.4129.101, self-consistent]` **The version axis points the WRONG WAY and hypothesis 3 is demoted.**
  The failing side (the runner) has no version skew at all; the passing side (this dev host) has a cross-major
  one. Steerability was never the question — causality was, and the measurement contradicts it.

- **UNVERIFIED, and correctly so — a self-hosted Windows runner (hypothesis 4).** An infrastructure fact about
  the operator's environment, not a code fact. Additionally, whether test-plan §10's "never a runner to pin
  to" reaches a hosted-runner *capability gap* is a plan-decision P4 must state rather than assume.

- **VERIFIED — a `deferred` disposition is reachable without a green job.** The matrix contract's §Status
  lifecycle names terminal-for-done as `verified` **or** operator `deferred` with the reason in `notes`.

- **VERIFIED — the ~8-minute pre-spec build is the probe cycle's floor.** Run 34209940695: job start
  09:25:50Z → workers 09:34:06.926Z = 8 m 16 s, whole job 11 m 46 s. The plan's step count must respect it.

Vary the **WebView2 runtime major** on the hosted `windows-2025` runner and re-observe probe (a). This is
the one variable every passing case shares and the single failing case lacks: passing = {runtime
152.0.4191.x × driver 151, 2026-09-02 morning} ∪ {runtime 152.0.4191.x × driver 152.0.4191.53, since
2026-09-02 14:45}; failing = {runtime 151.0.4129.101 × driver 151.0.4129.101} on the runner. The prior
chunk established, with **no driver in the picture at all**, that the runner's runtime never opens its
remote-debugging endpoint — so every driver-layer hypothesis is retired and the runtime is the variable
that was never varied.

The work is one new gate step in the `a11y` job that installs the signed Evergreen bootstrapper with its
Authenticode signature checked **before** it executes, plus one line that stages an existing but
uncaptured liveness witness. Per security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Universal the signature check is a
terminal gate, never an advisory line; per arch §Occupied Resources (`CONDUCTOR_A11Y_STRICT`), test-plan §9
(E2E webview row), obs-plan §11 (CI) and a11y-plan §11 (Anti-Patterns → CI) no gate step may gain
`continue-on-error` — research confirmed that boundary is a **preserve**, not a change: the three existing
`continue-on-error` sites are the two diagnostics and the diag upload, none on a gate path.

This chunk is a **probe, and both outcomes complete it**. If the endpoint opens on 152+, the runtime major
was the cause. If it still never opens, the runtime-major hypothesis is **falsified** and that is a real
measurement to record with its mechanism — per this project's standing rule a disproved premise is
recorded, never hidden and never quietly relaxed. The remaining unmeasured candidates (no interactive
desktop session on a hosted runner; a Session-0 / service-account restriction on the WebView2 browser
process; an image policy on remote debugging) then become the surviving set.

1. **Add the runtime-install gate step to the `a11y` job** in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, positioned
   immediately after the `actions/setup-node@v4` step and **before** the step named
   `WebView2 driver + runtime versions (diagnostic)`. Name it
   `Install WebView2 Evergreen runtime 152+ (gate)`, `shell: pwsh`. It carries **no**
   `continue-on-error` and **no** `if:` condition. *(Anchored by step name per test-plan §9 Matrix builds
   and a11y-plan §3 Configuration — this insertion shifts every later line, so a coordinate anchor would
   be stale on arrival.)*

2. **Print the pre-install runtime version inside that step**, read from the same EdgeUpdate registry
   client key the `WebView2 driver + runtime versions (diagnostic)` step already reads. Emit it as a
   single greppable line in the established `[diag]`-style label shape (version string only — a version
   is outside the host-path ban per security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Logging).

3. **Fetch the Evergreen bootstrapper over HTTPS** from the official Microsoft `go.microsoft.com`
   Evergreen link, with TLS verification intact. No `-SkipCertificateCheck`, no plaintext `http://`
   (security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Data Protection). Write it to a path under `$env:RUNNER_TEMP`
   resolved in the **step shell** (`$env:NAME`), never through a `${{ env.* }}` expression — arch
   §Occupied Resources (`EDGEWEBDRIVER`) records that the expression context holds only
   workflow/job/step declarations and yielded an empty base when misused.

4. **Gate on the signature BEFORE executing the bootstrapper.** Evaluate
   `Get-AuthenticodeSignature` on the downloaded file and require both a `Valid` status and a Microsoft
   signer. Any other result prints one host-path-free line naming the handle and its state — the
   `[precondition] <NAME>: <state>` idiom already used at the routine arm — and `exit 1`. No
   `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` may wrap the signature evaluation. This is the never-silently-downgrade
   discipline (security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Universal): a warning that proceeds is the exact
   banned shape.

5. **Execute the bootstrapper as a fixed program with a fixed silent-install argv** — the program path as
   the command and each switch as a separate argument. Never an interpolated shell string, never
   `Invoke-Expression` (security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Code Patterns rule (b)). The install must
   be silent and non-interactive: the agent-driven path is never blocked on a prompt (layout-templates
   §Surface: cli — IA notes, Headless invariant).

6. **Print the post-install runtime version from the same registry key, then assert the major is ≥ 152**,
   failing the step non-zero when it is not. Assert **the major, not that the version changed** — an
   assert-on-change would false-red on a host already at 152+ while an assert-on-major correctly catches
   the case that actually wastes the push: a silent no-op leaving the runner at 151, under which probe (a)
   would measure nothing yet read as a falsified hypothesis.

7. **Stage the existing liveness witness.** In the step named `WebView2 session isolation (diagnostic)`,
   add `runs/logs/conductor-tauri.jsonl` to the `foreach` that stages files into
   `$env:RUNNER_TEMP/session-diag`. The file is written unconditionally by the Tauri backend
   (`crates/conductor-tauri/src/main.rs:48`, sibling of the runs dir) and the step already sets
   `CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR: runs/e2e-fixture`, so probe (a)'s bare launch produces it — but the current
   staging block copies only `app.stderr.txt`, `msedgedriver.log` and a Crashpad dir. Guard the copy with
   the same `Test-Path` the existing entries use so an absent file is not an error. This yields an
   app-liveness witness **independent of `DevToolsActivePort`**, which is exactly the reading the chunk's
   verdict turns on (obs-plan §3 Log file location).

8. **Validate the step's logic on the dev host before the single budgeted push** — the download, the
   signature evaluation (both branches), the registry reads and the version-major assertion. **Do not run
   the installer locally:** this host is at 152.0.4191.66 and CI at 151.0.4129.101, so a local install
   exercises install-over-newer (a no-op) and cannot measure the CI upgrade path at all. The prior chunk's
   dev-host validation caught two PowerShell defects that would have failed silently under
   `continue-on-error` and consumed its single push; PowerShell defects are the measured risk class here,
   and steps 2–6 are entirely PowerShell.

9. **Run the mandatory Rust gates** (below) — this chunk's absorbed PREREQ closes the deferral the prior
   chunk took under the source-delta-proportional rule, so they are non-deferrable here regardless of this
   chunk's own zero compiled-source delta.

10. **Write the either-way verdict** to
    `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-09-08-webview2-runtime-152-installed-in-job/evidence/probe-verdict.md`
    after the CI run:
    which branch the run landed on, the run id, the `[diag] (a) bare-app DevToolsActivePort first seen:`
    line verbatim, and the pre/post runtime versions. Host-path-free. If the endpoint still never opens,
    the record states the runtime-major hypothesis **falsified** with its mechanism and names the
    surviving unmeasured candidates.

- `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-09-08-webview2-runtime-152-installed-in-job/evidence/probe-verdict.md` —
  the either-way probe verdict; host-path-free, run id + the decisive `[diag]` line + pre/post versions.

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — the `a11y` job only. (a) one new gate step
  `Install WebView2 Evergreen runtime 152+ (gate)` between `actions/setup-node@v4` and
  `WebView2 driver + runtime versions (diagnostic)`; (b) one guarded path added to the staging `foreach`
  inside `WebView2 session isolation (diagnostic)`. Preserve the job's `runs-on: windows-2025` explicit
  label, the existing `continue-on-error` placement, and every other step byte-unchanged.

No crate, scenario, contract, script, `wdio.conf.ts` or spec-master edit. **Caller threading: N/A** — no
symbol's signature changes and no value threads through a call chain (research §Graph impact: the change
surface lies outside both indexed planes). **Seam facts: N/A** — no dependency is added to any manifest,
so `Cargo.lock` and `package-lock.json` are byte-unchanged and the package count holds.

```bash
# --- supply-chain pin (rides every chunk; porcelain probe FIRST, per security-plan §Dependency Security) ---
git -C "${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/advisory-db" status --porcelain   # MUST print nothing; untracked residue
                                                                      # is what a fetch leaves and is read
                                                                      # BEFORE any red is called external
cargo audit                          # bare form — NEVER --deny warnings (exits 1 by construction against
                                     # the deny.toml-adjudicated allowed warnings); capture $? from the
                                     # BARE command, never through a pipe.
                                     # DISPOSITION: expected GREEN (exit 0). The RUSTSEC-2026-0244
                                     # deferral was CLOSED at 2026-09-05-audit-corrective once the red
                                     # proved to be local cache residue, not an external fault — so this
                                     # is no longer a standing-RED gate. Reads the LOCAL advisory-db
                                     # cache, whose currency the porcelain probe above establishes first;
                                     # a red is external ONLY after that probe prints nothing.
cargo deny check advisories bans licenses sources   # DISPOSITION: expected GREEN; the audit+deny overlap
                                     # is deliberate — one red for an external reason while the other is
                                     # green is the overlap doing its job

# --- mandatory Rust gates: the absorbed PREREQ closes the prior chunk's deferral ---
npm --prefix crates/conductor-tauri/ui run build   # MUST precede any workspace cargo command that compiles
                                                   # conductor-tauri: tauri-build's generate_context!
                                                   # resolves build.frontendDist at COMPILE time
cargo fmt --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci         # zero-retry ci profile; assert the printed test COUNT
                                                   # beside the verdict, not the exit alone

# --- the changed artifact itself (this chunk's only source delta is YAML) ---
python -X utf8 -c "import yaml;d=yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/ci.yml',encoding='utf-8'));print('a11y steps:',len(d['jobs']['a11y']['steps']))"
                                                                # asserts: parses, and the step count is 12
                                                                # (11 today + the new gate step)
grep -n 'continue-on-error' .github/workflows/ci.yml            # asserts: still exactly 3 hits, and READ
                                                                # them — each must sit on a diagnostic or
                                                                # the diag upload, never a gate. The count
                                                                # alone cannot tell you which.
grep -n 'http://' .github/workflows/ci.yml                      # asserts: exactly ONE hit, the pre-existing
                                                                # loopback POST to 127.0.0.1:9515. Written
                                                                # as a POSITIVE probe deliberately: the
                                                                # negative form `http://(?!127\.0\.0\.1)`
                                                                # is a PCRE lookahead, which grep -E does
                                                                # not implement — measured, it matches
                                                                # nothing and exits 0, i.e. it passes no
                                                                # matter what the new step contains.
grep -n 'SkipCertificateCheck\|Invoke-Expression' .github/workflows/ci.yml ; true
                                                                # asserts: zero hits (zero-is-healthy, so
                                                                # `; true` keeps the chain alive)
grep -n 'runs-on: windows-2025' .github/workflows/ci.yml        # asserts: the explicit label survives
```

No boot-path smoke applies: this chunk changes no binary and no harness script. A bare
`agent-run.sh status` is deliberately **not** listed — it exits 0 while proving nothing, printing the most
recent envelope on disk regardless of whether any run happened (verification-harness.md `:49`).

**The decisive measurement is not a local gate.** Probe (a) runs only in the `a11y` CI job, which cannot
execute until this workflow change is committed and pushed — the operator's act. Its firing form is the
job itself; there is no local invocation that reproduces it, because the subject *is* the hosted runner's
runtime. **Stop form (dev-host validation only, step 8):** the validation script starts no long-lived
process, but if any `conductor-tauri.exe` is launched during it, take a process census **before and
after** keyed on `conductor-tauri|msedgewebview2|msedgedriver|tauri-driver|node` — `msedgewebview2.exe`
must be in the pattern (its omission left six processes with no baseline at the prior chunk), and
**stopping msedgedriver does not kill the app it launched**, so the manual stop form is
`taskkill /F /IM msedgedriver.exe /IM conductor-tauri.exe` (verification-harness.md `:58`, extended
2026-09-08).

- (security) `Get-AuthenticodeSignature` is evaluated **before** the bootstrapper executes, and a
  non-`Valid` status or non-Microsoft signer exits the step non-zero; the evaluation is not wrapped in
  `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` (per security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Universal,
  never-silently-downgrade).

- (security) The bootstrapper is fetched over HTTPS with certificate verification intact and executed as a
  fixed program with a fixed argv — the added step contains no `-SkipCertificateCheck`, no plaintext
  `http://`, no `Invoke-Expression` and no shell-string command assembly (per security-plan §Security
  Anti-Patterns → Data Protection; §Security Anti-Patterns → Code Patterns rule (b)).

- (security) `cargo audit` exits 0 and `cargo deny check advisories bans licenses sources` exits 0 over a
  committed, un-drifted `Cargo.lock`; a red is adjudicated by the advisory-db `git status --porcelain`
  probe before any external classification (per security-plan §Dependency Security).

- (arch) The `a11y` job still declares `runs-on: windows-2025` explicitly, and **no gate step carries
  `continue-on-error`** — the count stays at exactly three, all on the two diagnostics and the diag upload
  (per architecture.md §Infrastructure Patterns — Build system; §Occupied Resources
  `CONDUCTOR_A11Y_STRICT`).

- (arch) Every runner-process variable the new step consumes is read in the step SHELL (`$env:NAME`),
  never via `${{ env.* }}`; the step claims no `CONDUCTOR_*` name (per architecture.md §Occupied Resources
  — `EDGEWEBDRIVER` · Environment variables).

- (tests) `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci` returns 0 (per test-plan §9 Pipeline structure →
  Unit stage).

- (tests) `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` return 0 (per
  test-plan §9 Pipeline structure → Lint stage).

- (obs) **[structural — asserted locally]** The steps `A11y violation-JSON conformance gate` (with
  `CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR: runs/a11y`) and `Upload a11y violation record` are still present, still after the
  routine arm, and byte-unchanged — no artifact and no gate lost or reordered out of effect. Proved by the
  YAML parse + step-name greps in `## Test Commands`, **not** by producing `runs/a11y/<run_id>.jsonl`,
  whose only producer is the CI job (per obs-plan §9 CI Integration).

- (obs) **[CI-produced — no local producer, by construction]** The pre- and post-install runtime versions
  and the `[diag] (a)` verdict are readable from the job log by grep alone, and no absolute runner path is
  carried into the committed evidence (per obs-plan §2 Agent-readable invariants; §11 PII Scrubbing).

- (a11y) The routine arm is unchanged apart from the preceding install — same job name, `windows-2025`,
  `agent-run run --e2e`, conformance gate and violation upload (per a11y-plan §9 CI Integration).

- (a11y) **[CI-produced — no local producer, by construction]** The probe's outcome is recorded either
  way: endpoint-opens, or the runtime-major hypothesis **falsified with its mechanism** and the surviving
  unmeasured candidates named — a11y-plan §11 → Strategy's "CI proof of the routine Operable pair is still
  OWED" stays true rather than being retired (per a11y-plan §11 Anti-Patterns → Strategy; §12 Decisions
  Log).

**Why three criteria carry no listed producer** (the P5 check-4 resolution, recorded rather than papered
over): the two marked **[CI-produced]** assert content of the `a11y` job's run log and the evidence record
derived from it. That job cannot execute until this workflow change is committed and **pushed** — the
operator's act — so no local invocation can produce them, and inventing one would be a proxy that proves
something else. They are verified at wrap against the named run id. Every other criterion is provable by a
listed command; the obs upload/conformance criterion was **reworded** from asserting the artifact to
asserting the steps, which is what a local command can actually establish.

- (layouts) The install introduces no interactive prompt or elevation gate into the headless CI path, and
  a signature refusal prints a host-path-free sanitized line and stops the step — the refuse class, not
  the skip class (per layout-templates §Surface: cli — IA notes, Headless invariant; §cli Primary screens
  refuse-vs-skip).
**No capability is claimed by this chunk.** See `## Implementation notes` → *v2-24 disposition*.

  test-runner-backend) are **retired on evidence, do not revisit** — both are driver-layer and the fault is
  measured upstream of every driver. `H2` (`WEBVIEW2_USER_DATA_FOLDER`) is doubly retired. `H3` as
  driver-skew is rejected (runner driver = runtime = Edge, all `151.0.4129.101`, self-consistent).

- **No self-hosted runner.** `H4` is **route-forward ONLY** — none exists for this project
  (operator-confirmed 2026-09-08) and the repo is public.

title: Premises this chunk itself introduces — closed at P3

data.head: ## Premises this chunk itself introduces — closed at P3

body:
- **VERIFIED** The versions-diagnostic registry read is the right post-install observable. The step
  "WebView2 driver + runtime versions (diagnostic)" reads the EdgeUpdate client key and prints a version
  string only; it returned `151.0.4129.101` on run 34234558853, so the observable demonstrably works and
  is host-path-free.

- **VERIFIED** No other `a11y`-job step depends on the runtime being 151. No step pins a runtime version;
  the only version-sensitive handle is the image-shipped driver (`EDGEWEBDRIVER`), and a11y-plan §1/§3
  already record runtime 152 × driver 151 as a **measured-working pair** (2026-09-02), so installing 152+
  over the image's 151 driver is not a new unsupported combination.

- **VERIFIED (and it is the load-bearing one)** `CONDUCTOR_A11Y_STRICT: '1'` is already set on the routine
  arm, and `continue-on-error` appears at exactly three sites — the two diagnostics and the
  session-diag upload — none of them on a gate path. The chunk's "no gate step gains `continue-on-error`"
  boundary is therefore a *preserve*, not a *change*.

- **VERIFIED — and it confirms the security extract's premise** The `a11y` job performs **no non-loopback
  fetch today**; the only `Invoke-WebRequest` in the whole workflow targets `http://127.0.0.1:9515/session`.
  The bootstrapper download is genuinely the project's **first non-loopback egress in a job step**, which
  is what makes the rule-(b) governed-form question (below) real rather than hypothetical.

- **[inferred — NOT closable in this repo; the plan must MEASURE it, not assume it]** The Evergreen
  bootstrapper installs *latest* and has no version selector, so "152+" is whatever latest is. The half
  that matters is the **no-op risk**: if the install silently declines because a per-machine runtime is
  already present at 151, the probe measures nothing and would read as a falsified hypothesis. This is
  why the pre/post version print is a plan step and not a nicety.

- **[inferred — runner-only, dev-host validation is the mitigation]** The install succeeds on
  `windows-2025` without an interactive session or elevation prompt, and `Get-AuthenticodeSignature`
  returns `Valid` with a Microsoft signer on that image. Neither is verifiable from this host; the
  prior chunk's precedent (dev-host validation caught two probe defects before its single budgeted
  push) applies directly.

- **Marker:** 2026-09-09-port-occupier-test-hygiene · **Version:** conductor-0.2.0 · **Generated:** 2026-09-09T18:05Z

`crates/conductor-faults/tests/port_occupier.rs` violates the runner-portability contract that `test-plan`
§4 states and `architecture.md` §Established Decisions [Module Boundaries] makes possible: every crate green
under plain `cargo test -p <crate>` as well as under nextest. Measured at HEAD in P3: exit **101**, 6 of 7
integration tests passing.

The cause is not a diffuse race. The file holds **seven** `#[test]` fns in ONE binary. **Five** of the six
siblings construct a `PortOccupier` — `:12`, `:24`, `:34` (which calls `occupy` twice, the second
deliberately failing to a typed error, so it contributes one successful bind), `:43`, `:53` — while
`default_target_is_the_otlp_ingest_port` (`:62`) constructs nothing and merely asserts the constant. The
seventh, the witness, installs the process-global `init_observability` subscriber and constructs one
occupier **of its own** before reading the lines the subscriber writes. Under libtest's shared process every
one of those spans lands in that single sink — P3 measured **13 `fault.port_occupier` records in a 14-line
log, six `new` records carrying six distinct ephemeral ports** (the five siblings plus the witness's own) —
and the test's record finder takes the **first match**, which returned a sibling's port (60254). The failing
assertion is `the bound port survives the allowlist`. Under nextest's process-per-test there is exactly one
such record, which is why that runner has always been green.

`test-plan` §11 → Integration already names both the defect and its remedy, on a measured case in another
crate (`2026-08-20-verifier-self-hardening`): *"the remedy is a test binary of its own … never serializing
the file … which hides the shared-state defect rather than removing it."* The repo already applies it three
times — `conductor-run/tests/canary_obs_witness.rs:23`, `conductor-verify/tests/readback_shape_witness.rs:26`,
`conductor-timeline/tests/obs_span.rs:15`, each holding exactly one test fn (all three `#[tokio::test]`, not
plain `#[test]`). `port_occupier.rs` is the sole violator of a convention with three in-tree precedents. So this chunk applies the established remedy rather
than inventing one, and the assertion moves **byte-identically** — which is what preserves its power to fail
if `port` ever leaves `redact::ALLOWLISTED_FIELDS` (obs-plan §4; `"port"` confirmed present at
`redact.rs:51`).

The chunk's second half is non-optional and equally the point: the wrap gate that surfaced this
short-circuited at crate 4 of 8, leaving four crates unmeasured. P3 measured all four — every one exits 0 —
so the route entry's warning that a fix "may simply advance the first red" is **measured false**. A second
hole sat beside it: that loop enumerated only the **eight** crates the formatting pass touched, while the
workspace has **nine** members, so `conductor-report` was outside the gate entirely. `test-plan` §4 states
the contract per crate, not per touched crate — and an omitted member is the same hole as a short-circuit by
another mechanism. `conductor-report` is measured green here (exit 0, 51 + 3 passed), and this chunk's sweep
therefore **derives its crate list from the workspace manifest** and measures all nine, naming every red,
so neither a short-circuit nor an omission can hide a violation again.

1. **Create `crates/conductor-faults/tests/port_occupier_span_witness.rs`.** Move
   `the_hold_is_bracketed_by_a_fault_span_on_the_emitted_lines` (currently `port_occupier.rs:68-112`,
   including its `///` doc comment) into this new file as the file's **only** `#[test]` fn. The fn body is
   carried across **unchanged** — no re-ordering, no re-wording of the assertion or its message. Bring only
   the imports it needs: `conductor_core::{ObsSink, init_observability}`, `conductor_faults::PortOccupier`,
   `serde_json::{Map, Value}`.

2. **Write the file's module doc comment** stating the isolation reason, following the shape of
   `conductor-verify/tests/readback_shape_witness.rs:1-5`: that `conductor_core::init_observability`
   installs a process-global, first-install-wins subscriber; that a per-test temp sink does not isolate it
   because concurrent siblings' `fault.port_occupier` spans land in whichever file won the install; that
   serializing the file would hide the shared state rather than remove it (`test-plan` §11); and that one
   test per binary holds under both runners.

3. **Remove the moved test from `crates/conductor-faults/tests/port_occupier.rs`**, together with the
   imports only it used — `conductor_core::{ObsSink, init_observability}` and `serde_json::{Map, Value}`.
   **Keep** `std::net::{IpAddr, Ipv4Addr, TcpListener}`, `conductor_faults::{FaultError, OTLP_INGEST_PORT,
   PortOccupier}` — the six remaining tests use them. The file's own header doc comment (`:1-3`) stays.

4. **Run the one-shot known-positive control and record its evidence.** Temporarily remove `"port"` from

title: The mechanism, re-derived at HEAD (measured, not inherited)

data.head: ## The mechanism, re-derived at HEAD (measured, not inherited)

body:
The route entry's claim carried `measured at 2026-09-09-workspace-formatting-pass-and-a-fmt-ci-gate`, so
its evidence pointer was spot-checked. It holds, and the measurement refines it to a finer grain:

- `cargo test -p conductor-faults` → **exit 101**, `6 passed; 1 failed` (unit lib target: 23/23 green).
  Byte-consistent with the entry's three measurements.
- **The failing assertion is `the bound port survives the allowlist`** (`port_occupier.rs:104-108`).

- **Why:** the test's log file holds **14 lines carrying 13 `fault.port_occupier` records** — six `new`
  records with six distinct ephemeral ports (`60250, 60251, 60252, 60253, 60254, 60255`) plus six `close`
  records. Its own occupier contributes exactly one `new`. The finder at :90-100 is
  `.find(|o| span == "fault.port_occupier" && span_event == event)` — **first match wins** — and returned
  port `60254`, which is a *sibling's* occupier. `assert_eq!` then compares a sibling's port against this
  test's own and fails.

- **Why nextest is green:** process-per-test means exactly one `new` record exists in the process, so the
  first match is trivially the right one. **Why `--test-threads=1` is green:** serial execution means no
  sibling occupier is alive while the subscriber is installed.

- So the defect is not "a race" in the loose sense — it is **first-match record selection over a shared
  process-global sink**, and it is deterministic in kind and nondeterministic only in which sibling wins.

**Corollary discovered while measuring — the failure is SILENT.** `init_observability` installs
`log_panic` as the process panic hook (`obs.rs:172`), which routes the panic through `tracing` into the
file sink. The libtest failure block therefore carries **no `---- stdout ----` section and no panic
message**, and `-- --nocapture` adds nothing. The assertion text was recoverable only from the test's own
JSONL (`%TEMP%/conductor-faults-obs-{pid}/agent-latest.jsonl`, which the test deletes on success only, so
leftovers accumulate — 5 such directories were present). A maintainer hitting this red sees a bare test
name and nothing else.
Run at HEAD, each exit code captured from the bare command before any pipe:
| Crate | `cargo test -p <crate>` | Result |
| `conductor-verify` | exit **0** | green (incl. `readback_shape_witness`) |
| `conductor-run` | exit **0** | green (22 targets) |
| `conductor-cli` | exit **0** | green |
| `conductor-tauri` | exit **0** | green |
| `conductor-report` | exit **0** | green (51 + 3 passed) — **not one of the entry's eight**; see below |

The route entry warned that "fixing the fault crate may simply advance the first red rather than turn the
loop green." **Measured false at HEAD:** `conductor-faults` is the only red.

**A second hole, found at the P5 review (operator).** The wrap gate's loop enumerated only the **eight**
crates the formatting pass touched, but the workspace has **nine** members (`cargo metadata --no-deps`), so
`conductor-report` was outside the gate entirely — the same blind spot as a short-circuit, by a different
mechanism, and `test-plan` §4 states the contract per crate rather than per touched crate. Measured green
here. The plan's sweep therefore derives its list from the manifest and covers all nine.

- **One-test-per-binary for a process-global-singleton test** (`conductor-run/tests/canary_obs_witness.rs:1`,
  `conductor-verify/tests/readback_shape_witness.rs:1`, `conductor-timeline/tests/obs_span.rs`): all three
  crates that call `init_observability` from an integration test already isolate that test in its own
  `tests/*.rs`, each holding **exactly one** test fn — all three `#[tokio::test]`
  (`canary_obs_witness.rs:23`, `readback_shape_witness.rs:26`, `obs_span.rs:15`), **not** plain `#[test]`,
  so a literal `grep -c '#\[test\]'` over them returns 0 and is the wrong probe for the property. Two state
  the rule in their own doc comments —
  `readback_shape_witness.rs:1-5` reads "alone in its own test binary… serializing the file would hide the
  shared state rather than remove it (test-plan §11). **One test per binary holds under both runners.**"
  `conductor-faults/tests/port_occupier.rs` is the **only** violator of a convention already applied three
  times in-tree.

- **The subject's own siblings are the contaminant** (`port_occupier.rs:11-66`): **five** of the six
  siblings construct a `PortOccupier` — `:12`, `:24`, `:34` (two `occupy` calls, the second deliberately
  failing to a typed error, so one successful bind), `:43`, `:53` — while `:62`
  (`default_target_is_the_otlp_ingest_port`) constructs nothing and only asserts the constant. The occupier
  emits its span at its RAII bind site inside `conductor-faults`, so any sibling running concurrently with
  the installed subscriber writes into the same file. The six `new` records are those five plus the
  witness's own occupier.

- **`close` records carry no attributes** (measured: `port=None`, `fault_type=None`), matching obs-plan §4's
  "attributes on the `new` record alone" — so `record("close")` at :109 asserts existence only and is
  unaffected by the selection defect.

- **Doc-comment the isolation reason at the top of the new file**, naming the process-global mechanism and
  test-plan §11 — the shape both `canary_obs_witness.rs:1-6` and `readback_shape_witness.rs:1-5` use.
- **Naming:** `{subject}_{aspect}_witness.rs` (`canary_obs_witness.rs`, `readback_shape_witness.rs`).

- **No manifest change needed:** `serde_json` is already a `[dev-dependencies]` entry of `conductor-faults`
  and dev-deps apply to every test target in the crate.
- Cite graph lines as `line + 1` (SCIP ranges are 0-indexed; cookbook §Reading the result).

- `crates/conductor-faults/tests/port_occupier_span_witness.rs` — the single test
  `the_hold_is_bracketed_by_a_fault_span_on_the_emitted_lines`, moved verbatim from `port_occupier.rs`,
  with the isolation-reason doc comment. Its assertion is carried across **unchanged**, which is what
  preserves its power to fail if `port` leaves the allowlist.

- `crates/conductor-faults/tests/port_occupier.rs` — remove the moved test (:68-112) and the imports it
  alone needs (`conductor_core::{ObsSink, init_observability}`, `serde_json::{Map, Value}`; `TcpListener`,
  `IpAddr`, `Ipv4Addr` stay — the six remaining tests use them). No other change.

- No `src/` file, no `Cargo.toml`, no `.config/nextest.toml`, no `ci.yml`. Zero cross-crate blast radius
  (crate-edge query above).

- **Should the moved test's temp-dir key change?** It is `conductor-faults-obs-{process::id()}`; leftovers
  accumulate because the cleanup at `:111` is skipped on panic. → blocks: `implementation-scope` (a
  cosmetic hygiene call for /implement; it does not affect the fix's correctness either way).

- **Does the new binary need a known-positive control?** `testing.md:89` requires a criterion's probe to be
  able to FAIL on the property's negation. → blocks: `plan-decision` — resolved in P4: the plan carries a
  control step (temporarily drop `"port"` from `ALLOWLISTED_FIELDS`, observe the moved test go red, revert)
  rather than asserting preservation by inspection.

title: Reading of "free of its process-global observability dependency" (val-1, intent-incomplete)

data.head: ## Reading of "free of its process-global observability dependency" (val-1, intent-incomplete)

body:
The working entry's title clause admits two readings, and P5's validation-1 resolved it as
**intent-incomplete** rather than a plan defect — recorded here because the phrase is the operator's own
wording and the choice is visible in the review:

- **(a) literal** — the test should stop depending on the process-global subscriber (e.g. a thread-local
  `with_default` subscriber instead of `init_observability`).

- **(b) adopted** — the test should be free of that dependency's *consequences*: isolated so the
  shared-process runner is green, while still asserting on what the SHIPPED `init_observability` writes.

**(b) is adopted**, on three grounds that (a) contradicts: `test-plan` §11 (`test-plan.md:538`) prescribes
*"a test binary of its own"* for this exact singleton and names no subscriber substitution; all three
in-tree applications of that remedy (`canary_obs_witness.rs`, `readback_shape_witness.rs`, `obs_span.rs`)
still call `init_observability`; and asserting against a test-constructed local subscriber would weaken the
proof — the assertion's whole point (obs-plan §4) is that the *production* subscriber's allowlist lets
`port` survive. The entry itself says it "names the cause, not a mitigation", so it does not prescribe (a).

The runner-portability contract that `test-plan` §4 + §12 state — *every crate green under
`cargo test -p <crate>` as well as under nextest* — is violated in-repo. This chunk makes it true for
`conductor-faults`, and then **measures** whether it is true for the four crates the violating gate never
reached.

The entry names the **cause, not a mitigation**, deliberately. Three remedies are pre-banned by
`test-plan` §11 and were rejected explicitly at `2026-09-06-operator-gated-live-suite`: **a retry, a runner
pin, and an in-test `sleep`**. None of them may appear in this chunk's solution.

title: The second half the entry insists on — the unmeasured four

data.head: ## The second half the entry insists on — the unmeasured four

body:
The wrap gate that surfaced this is a `for … do cargo test -p "$c" || exit 1; done` loop over the eight
crates the formatting pass touched, in the order **core · timeline · emit · faults · verify · run · cli ·
tauri**, and it **short-circuits at the fourth**. Therefore:

- **Measured green** under the shared-process runner: `conductor-core`, `conductor-timeline`,
  `conductor-emit`.
- **Unmeasured** there: `conductor-verify`, `conductor-run`, `conductor-cli`, `conductor-tauri`.

- The entry's own instruction: *fixing the fault crate may simply advance the first red rather than turn the
  loop green, and this entry should expect to **measure** the remaining four rather than assume them.*

A chunk that fixes `conductor-faults` and declares the contract satisfied would be making exactly the
unmeasured-universal claim the entry forbids.

1. **Fix `conductor-faults`** so `cargo test -p conductor-faults` (plain, parallel libtest, no
   `--test-threads=1`) exits 0 — without a retry, a runner pin, or an in-test `sleep`.

2. **Preserve the assertion's evidentiary value.** The test's stated purpose (its doc comment) is that the
   span brackets the bind *on the emitted lines*, because `fields(...)` in the macro prove nothing — the
   tracing field allowlist gates them (`obs-plan` §4). Any restructuring must keep a probe that can still
   **fail** if the `port` field stops surviving the allowlist. **VERIFIED at P3** — a finder keyed on the
   port itself would make that assertion unable to fail, which `testing.md:89` names as *not evidence*; P4
   must not resolve the race that way. `"port"` is confirmed present in `ALLOWLISTED_FIELDS`
   (`redact.rs:51`), so the assertion has a real subject.

3. **Measure the four unmeasured crates** under `cargo test -p <crate>` and record each result — green or
   red — as a fact, not an assumption.

4. **Disposition whatever the measurement finds.**
   `[premise-corrected: measured at P3 — all four crates exit 0 under plain `cargo test -p`, so no second
   red exists and the disposition fork never opens]` The route entry's warning that fixing the fault crate
   "may simply advance the first red" is measured FALSE at HEAD: `conductor-faults` is the only red of the
   eight, and fixing it turns the whole loop green. This chunk still *re-measures* all four at implement
   (a P3 measurement is not the chunk's gate), but it plans for green rather than for a fork.

5. **Keep both runners green.** `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci` must remain at its current
   green (902/902 across 55 binaries) — the fix must not trade one runner for the other.
- Changing the runner discipline itself, or `test-plan` §11's ban on retries/pins/sleeps.

- The process-global **panic-hook** race in `conductor-core/src/obs.rs` — a CARRY owned by the *Release
  build and bundle* entry (`working-route.md:133`). **RESOLVED at P3: they are NOT the same defect** (that
  CARRY is two `take_hook`/`set_hook` pairs in obs.rs's own unit tests racing each other; this chunk's is
  record selection over a shared sink), so it stays out of scope. Two facts surfaced for its owner, not
  absorbed here: its coordinates are **stale** — at HEAD the pairs are `obs.rs:535-540` and `:582-587`, not
  `:491-496`/`:532-537` — and the same panic hook makes THIS chunk's failure silent (`research.md`
  §Corollary).
- Any spec amendment. `test-plan` §4/§12 state the contract correctly; this chunk makes the repo match it.
| Surface | Nature |
| `crates/conductor-faults/tests/port_occupier.rs` | the failing test + its 6 siblings |

| `conductor_core::{init_observability, ObsSink}` | the process-global subscriber the test installs — **VERIFIED at P3: read-only for this chunk.** The remedy is test-side (one test per binary), the convention already applied in the three other crates whose integration tests call it |
| `test-plan` §4 · §12 | the runner-portability contract this satisfies |
| `test-plan` §11 | the banned-mitigation list this must not violate |
| `obs-plan` §4 | the tracing field allowlist the assertion exists to prove |
| `conductor-verify` · `-run` · `-cli` · `-tauri` test targets | measured, not assumed |
- `cargo test -p conductor-faults` exits 0 under plain parallel libtest, repeatably.
- The allowlist-survival assertion still exists and can still fail on its negation.
- Each of the four unmeasured crates has a **recorded measured result** under `cargo test -p`.
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci` still green; `cargo clippy -D warnings` still green.
- No retry, no runner pin, no in-test sleep anywhere in the delta.

title: Plan — 2026-09-09-workspace-formatting-pass-and-a-fmt-ci-gate: "Workspace formatting pass and a fmt CI gate"

data.head: # Plan — 2026-09-09-workspace-formatting-pass-and-a-fmt-ci-gate: "Workspace formatting pass and a fmt CI gate"

body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-09-09-workspace-formatting-pass-and-a-fmt-ci-gate · **Version:** conductor-0.2.0
- **Generated:** 2026-09-09T10:30Z · **Epoch:** 6b — Polish & ship

Make the workspace `cargo fmt`-clean and add the gate that keeps it so. Two halves, neither sufficient
alone: `cargo fmt --check` exits 1 at HEAD over 282 sites in 60 files spanning 8 of the 9 crates, and no
workflow — nor either `agent-run` script — runs rustfmt at all, which is the mechanism by which the tree
rotted unobserved for four days after `rustfmt.toml` landed (2026-09-05, commit `59d5b7c`).

The pass itself is mechanical and its safety is measured, not argued. Parsing the pending diff gives
+1581/−486 lines whose change classes are exactly edition-2024 import re-sorting and expression
re-wrapping, and the load-bearing property — *the pass alters no code, only its layout* — is verified as
**per-file token-multiset identity**: for each of the 60 files the multiset of identifiers, string
literals and numerals on the added side equals that on the removed side (60/60, zero exceptions; 262
distinct string literals per side, none exclusive to either). That single whole-diff invariant is what
keeps a 60-file review tractable, and it is stronger than the byte-identity check the route entry
proposed (research.md §1).

The gate lands in the existing `rust` job — CI's Rust gate, `windows-latest` — which test-plan §9's Lint
row already names as fmt's home beside clippy (`test-plan.md:455`, with the build-failure clauses at
`:477`/`:507`). That row is TARGET state deliberately left standing under the
`2026-09-06-coverage-completeness-gate` narrow ruling: this chunk makes it TRUE rather than retiring it,
and no detector proposal to retire it is to be accepted. Per arch §Established Decisions [CI/CD] the gate
inherits the existing runner model and carries no `continue-on-error` and no `if:`; per a11y-plan §3 and
test-plan §9 it is described by JOB NAME, never by `ci.yml` line coordinates.

1. **Run the pass.** Execute `cargo fmt --all` from the workspace root. Do not hand-edit any `.rs` file
   in this chunk — every byte of the source delta is rustfmt's output under the committed
   `rustfmt.toml` (`edition = "2024"`, its only key) and the pinned toolchain (`rust-toolchain.toml`,
   `channel = "1.95.0"`, rustfmt component present). No `#[rustfmt::skip]` is added anywhere: the tree
   carries zero today and research established none is needed (research.md §5).

2. **Write the formatting-only verifier** at
   `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-09-09-workspace-formatting-pass-and-a-fmt-ci-gate/verify_fmt_token_invariant.py`
   — chunk evidence, not a shipped artifact, and not under `scripts/`. Contract: take the `.rs` diff
   (working tree vs `HEAD`; when that is empty, fall back to `HEAD~1..HEAD` so the entry stays
   meaningful after the chunk commits), group hunks per file, and for each file compare the multiset of
   identifiers, string literals and numerals on the `+` side against the `-` side. **`cargo fmt --check`
   output prefixes every `+`/`-` with an ANSI colour escape and `git diff` may too — strip ANSI before
   classifying** (measured: a classifier keying on `startswith('+')` returned 0/0 against 282 real
   hunks). Print `token-multiset differences: N` as the last line; exit non-zero when `N > 0`.

3. **Add the gate step to `ci.yml`, job `rust`.** One new step named `Formatting gate (cargo fmt)`
   running `cargo fmt --all --check`, inserted **immediately after `Install toolchain
   (rust-toolchain.toml)`, becoming index 2** of that job (which grows 21 → 22 steps). Operator ruling
   at the P5 review; rationale and its honest counter are in Implementation notes. rustfmt resolves
   through the toolchain installed by the preceding step and needs nothing else — no cache restore, no
   node, no bundle, no compile. No `continue-on-error`, no `if:`, no new job, no new runner label, no
   new env handle, no `needs:` edge. The `a11y` and `frontend` jobs are byte-unchanged.

4. **Run the gates** in the `## Test Commands` order and record each reading. The coverage floor is not
   a formality here — see Implementation notes.

- `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-09-09-workspace-formatting-pass-and-a-fmt-ci-gate/verify_fmt_token_invariant.py`
  — the formatting-only verifier of step 2. Chunk evidence; nothing under `crates/` or `scripts/`
  imports or ships it.

- **60 `.rs` files** across 8 crates — rustfmt output only, never hand-edited. The list is not pinned
  here because the pass empties it; it is reproducible at implement time as the file set named by
  `cargo fmt --all --check`. Distribution measured at HEAD 2026-09-09 by parsing that output
  (`fmtstat.py`, session scratchpad): `conductor-verify` 110 sites/18 files · `conductor-run` 64/8 ·
  `conductor-emit` 51/16 · `conductor-timeline` 24/8 · `conductor-faults` 12/5 · `conductor-tauri` 10/2
  · `conductor-cli` 7/1 · `conductor-core` 4/2. `conductor-report` carries 0 and is untouched.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — one added step in job `rust` (step 3 above).

No caller threading is owed: the pass changes no symbol, signature, call site or crate edge, so the
code-graph has no impact surface (research.md §Scope — graph NOT APPLICABLE, distinct from unavailable;
both plane DBs are present and fresh). No manifest, lockfile, registry, capability or allowlist file is
implicated.

Agent-driven project: the harness smoke (`agent-run.sh status`) is listed per test-plan §3's 5-command
discipline. **No live leg** — this chunk drives no external process, no scenario and no Pulse, so no
`leg = 'live'` entry and no liveness probe exists to precede one. **No `self-verify` entry** — this is
not a UI/visual chunk: the frontend tree is untouched, `ui/dist` is unchanged, and the only
`conductor-tauri` files in the pass are `src/main.rs` and `src/pause.rs` (Rust, not webview). **No
`npm run build`** for the same reason. Nothing is deferred.

title: bash scripts/agent-run.sh status
body:
[[gate]]
run = 'bash scripts/agent-run.sh status'
role = 'smoke'

- (tests) `cargo fmt --all --check` returns 0 at post-pass HEAD (per test-plan §9 Pipeline structure,
  Lint row `:455`, and §9/§10 Build failure conditions `:477`/`:507`).

- (tests) CI's `rust` job runs `cargo fmt --all --check` as a named step with no `continue-on-error` and
  no `if:`, turning the job red on violation (per test-plan §9 Pipeline structure + §11 Quality).

- (arch) The gate's invocation covers every registered workspace member, so a tenth member added later
  cannot escape it (per architecture.md §Occupied Resources — Crate names · §Established Decisions
  [Module Boundaries]).

- (arch) No new occupied resource lands: no job, runner label, port, egress target, env handle, crate,
  `[workspace.dependencies]` entry or `Cargo.lock` delta (per architecture.md §Occupied Resources ·
  §Infrastructure Patterns — Build system).

- (security) `Cargo.lock` is byte-unchanged by the chunk, and `cargo audit` plus
  `cargo deny check advisories bans licenses sources` exit 0 (per security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns
  → Universal, §Dependency Security).

- (security) The added step is a fixed toolchain program with a fixed argv — no shell-string assembly,
  no `Invoke-Expression`, no network-fetched program — and no pre-existing gate step in `ci.yml` is
  reordered, weakened or removed (per security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Code Patterns rule (b),
  §Dependency Security CI integration).

- (design/obs/security) The source delta is formatting-only, evidenced by per-file token-multiset
  identity across every changed file (`token-multiset differences: 0`) — which is what establishes that
  no ANSI value, status-prefix literal, span name, allowlist field or garde annotation moved (per
  design-system §Surface: cli / Tokens · obs-plan §11 Spans / Traces · security-plan §Security
  Anti-Patterns → Input).

- (tests) `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --
  -D warnings` are green after the pass, with no test quarantined and no gate relaxed (per test-plan §9
  Unit + Lint rows, §10 Zero-flakiness budget, §11 Quality).

- (tests) Each of the 8 touched crates is additionally green under `cargo test -p <crate>` — the
  runner-portability gate (per test-plan §4 Framework + §12).

- (tests/obs) The `--fail-under-lines 60` coverage floor still holds after the pass (per test-plan §10
  Coverage thresholds; obs-plan §10 Build / deploy failure conditions).

- (a11y/obs) The `a11y` job is byte-unchanged, **evidenced by `a11y_sig` holding at `1a3138d5`** — the
  md5 of its `sort_keys`-normalized YAML, which covers `runs-on: windows-2025`, the 12-step list, the
  `CONDUCTOR_A11Y_STRICT: '1'` declaration and the `continue-on-error` diagnostics together — and the
  three `if: always()` uploads in `rust` still fire (per a11y-plan §9 CI Integration → Platform, §11 →
  CI; obs-plan §9 CI Integration). The step count and the repo-wide flag count do NOT prove this on
  their own; the signature is what the criterion rests on.

- (a11y) No a11y or WCAG claim is derived from this chunk, and the Lint stage owes no a11y artifact
  (per a11y-plan §9 Per-pipeline-stage a11y artifacts, Lint row `n/a` + §11 → Strategy).

**Capabilities claimed: none.** The four pooled ids were read at P4 and none is this chunk's subject —
`v2-04` (live-Pulse scenarios for P-067/P-072/P-079), `v2-21` (the matrix file's own structure),
`v2-24` (the routine a11y specs, owned by the wrap that dispositions it), `v2-27` (release binary +
Tauri bundle, which is the next route entry). No `notes` line is owed on any of them, because none was
considered-and-failed for this chunk — they are simply other work.

- Spec anchors: `architecture.md` §Established Decisions [CI/CD] · §Occupied Resources — Crate names /
  Environment variables · §Infrastructure Patterns — Build system / Directory structure ·
  §Established Decisions [Module Boundaries]; `security-plan.md` §Security Anti-Patterns → Universal /
  Input / Code Patterns rule (b) / Logging · §Dependency Security · §Input Validation;
  `test-plan.md` §3 CI stage selectors · §4 Framework · §9 Pipeline structure (Lint row `:455`) /
  Build failure conditions (`:477`) / Matrix builds · §10 Coverage thresholds + Zero-flakiness ·
  §11 Quality + CI · §12; `obs-plan.md` §1 instrumentation-scope · §9 CI Integration · §10 · §11;
  `a11y-plan.md` §1 · §3 Configuration + CI integration · §9 · §11; `design-system.md` §Surface: cli /
  Tokens · §Anti-Patterns; `layout-templates.md` §cli IA notes · §cli Component blocks 1–2.

- Research files inspected: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `Cargo.toml`, `rustfmt.toml`,
  `rust-toolchain.toml`, `.gitattributes`, `crates/conductor-report/src/journal.rs`.
- Extracts: `.andromeda/runs/2026-09-09T10-06-34-phase/{arch,security,design,layouts,tests,obs,a11y}.md`.

- **Do NOT retire or reword `test-plan.md:455`, `:477` or `:507`** — target-state descriptors this chunk
  makes true, per the `2026-09-06-coverage-completeness-gate` narrow ruling. Reject any detector
  proposal to retire them.

- **Rejected — the bare `cargo fmt --check` form** that test-plan §9's row literally names: it is
  equivalent only while `Cargo.toml` declares no `default-members`, and would silently narrow if one
  were added. `--all --check` is a strict superset and satisfies the row's intent; the divergence from
  the row's literal text is deliberate and surfaced at the P5 review rather than taken silently.

- **Rejected — folding the fmt check into `scripts/agent-run.{sh,ps1}`** (where CI's lint half actually
  runs today, via `agent-run.ps1 run`). test-plan §3 keeps the command count at five and holds
  `cargo clippy` as its own §9 stage rather than folding it into `--unit`; a fmt check is the same
  class. It ships as a workflow step, adding no harness verb and no stage selector.

- **Rejected — a separate `fmt` job.** arch §Established Decisions [CI/CD] has a new gate inherit the
  existing job model; a fourth job would add a runner and a cold cache for a check that takes seconds.

- **Do NOT hand-edit any `.rs` file.** Every source byte is rustfmt's output; a hand edit would
  invalidate the token-multiset invariant that is this chunk's whole safety argument.

- **Do NOT touch the `a11y` job or the WebView2 / driver thread.** That is a different route entry's
  subject and stays byte-unchanged here.
- **Do NOT add `#[rustfmt::skip]`** — the tree carries zero and none is needed (research.md §5).

- **Step placement: EARLY, at index 2 — operator ruling at the P5 review.** Measured from the job
  itself: at index 8 a formatting violation is reported only after the rust-cache restore,
  `install-action`, `npm ci` + the vite bundle and `cargo build --workspace --locked` — the 2026-09-08
  run took ~18 min end to end — whereas at index 2 it is seconds, and the lost signal is identical
  because the job is red before `Test + lint` either way. Artifact preservation does not constrain the
  choice: all three `rust`-job uploads carry `if: always()` (`ci.yml:109`, `:118`, `:182`). **The
  honest counter, recorded as the trade being made:** with the gate at index 8 a red push still yields
  Build and flakiness-budget results; at index 2 it yields none. That is thin on a single-operator
  repo, but it is a real loss, not a nil one. The Lint-stage identity that argued for index 8 is prose
  in two masters this chunk already amends, so it costs one clause rather than an extra amendment.

- **The coverage floor is a real risk on this chunk, not a formality.** The pass is net **+1095** lines
  (+1581/−486, derived by parsing `cargo fmt --check` with ANSI stripped — `classify2.py`, session
  scratchpad), and 30 of the 60 files are under `src/`, which the floor counts (`tests/` is excluded by
  `--ignore-filename-regex`). Expression re-wrapping turns one long line into several, and whether the
  added lines are counted as covered is not knowable without running the collection. If the floor
  drops below 60, that is a finding to record with its measurement — **not** a threshold to relax
  (test-plan §11 Quality bans lowering a bar to pass the build).

- **A `cargo test -p` red may not be this chunk's.** The *Release build and bundle* entry
  (`working-route.md:131`) carries a verified CARRY describing a process-global panic-hook race in
  `conductor-core/src/obs.rs` (two take/restore sites, `:491-496` and `:532-537`) that only manifests
  under the shared-process runner — observed red exactly once, not reproduced in 3 forced-parallel runs
  at HEAD. `obs.rs` is **not** in this pass (0 of 60 files). If the runner-portability entry goes red
  there, attribute it to that CARRY and its owning entry, not to the formatting pass.

- **The gate is line-ending invariant — tested, not assumed.** `rustfmt`'s `newline_style` defaults to
  `Auto`, and the same clean file passes `--check` at exit 0 in both LF and CRLF form (research.md §2).
  `.gitattributes` pins only `coverage-matrix.md`, so `.rs` files ride `core.autocrlf`; a CRLF checkout
  on the runner cannot redden a gate that is green locally.

- **Expected amendments (wrap):** `architecture.md` §Established Decisions [CI/CD] — the `rust` job
  gains a fmt gate step; the job set stays three, so the direction is to extend the CI enumeration, not
  to restate the job model. arch's lockstep siblings (§Stack CI/CD row, §Infrastructure Patterns Build
  system, §Infrastructure Patterns CI/CD approach, §Inherited Defaults CI/CD) move with it if they
  enumerate what CI runs.

title: Measured facts that decide the plan

data.head: ## Measured facts that decide the plan

title: 1. The pass is formatting-only, proven per-file

data.head: ### 1. The pass is formatting-only, proven per-file

body:
`cargo fmt --check` at HEAD: **exit 1, 282 sites, 60 files, 8 of 9 crates** (`conductor-report` clean).
Parsing the diff with ANSI stripped: **+1581 / −486 lines, net +1095**.

The load-bearing equality the plan needs is *the pass alters no code, only its layout*. Verified as
**per-file token-multiset identity**: for each of the 60 files, the multiset of identifiers, string
literals and numeric literals on the added side equals that on the removed side.

```
files with fmt hunks: 60
files whose per-file token multiset is IDENTICAL: 60
files with a token-multiset DIFFERENCE: 0
distinct string literals — added 262, removed 262; 0 exclusive to either side
```

This is strictly stronger than the working entry's proposed byte-identity-against-rustfmt check and it
is one whole-diff invariant rather than a 60-file reading task, so **review cost does not scale with
the file count** — which retires the entry's `~40 files` review-cost worry independently of the
count correction (60, not ~40).

Change classes, from the same parse: import re-sorting (30 `use` statements, 45 use-list items — the
edition-2024 order, types before functions) and expression re-wrapping (`bare-delimiter` 228 added vs 5
removed; `method-chain` 279 vs 40). This **verifies the working entry's EVIDENCE clause** ("ordinary
edition-2024 import ordering and line wrapping") on a firmer basis than the entry stated it.

title: 2. The gate is line-ending invariant — tested, not asserted

data.head: ### 2. The gate is line-ending invariant — tested, not asserted

body:
`rustfmt --print-config default` gives `newline_style = "Auto"`, which adapts per file. Tested directly
on a currently-clean file copied out of the tree:

```
LF   copy: rustfmt --edition 2024 --config skip_children=true --check → exit 0, 0 lines
CRLF copy: same command                                              → exit 0, 0 lines
```

So a CRLF checkout cannot make the gate red where an LF checkout is green. *(answers the arch
extract's checkout-invariance question, which `.gitattributes` alone could not)*

title: 3. `default-members` is absent → the invocation fork resolves to `--all`

data.head: ### 3. `default-members` is absent → the invocation fork resolves to `--all`

body:
`Cargo.toml` lists all nine members and declares **no `default-members` key**, which is why bare
`cargo fmt --check` and `cargo fmt --all --check` both measure 282 sites today. They are equivalent
*now* and diverge the moment a `default-members` key is added, which would silently narrow the bare
form. arch's criterion ("the invocation must cover every registered workspace member so it cannot go
blind as members are added") is therefore satisfied only by the explicit form.

title: 4. Every sensitive surface the extracts named is OUTSIDE the pass

data.head: ### 4. Every sensitive surface the extracts named is OUTSIDE the pass

body:

title: Scope — Workspace formatting pass and a fmt CI gate

data.head: # Scope — Workspace formatting pass and a fmt CI gate

body:
**Marker:** `2026-09-09-workspace-formatting-pass-and-a-fmt-ci-gate`
**Version:** conductor-0.2.0 · Epoch 6b — Polish & ship
**Working entry:** `conductor-0.2.0/working-route.md:129` (minted at the
`2026-09-08-webview2-runtime-152-installed-in-job` wrap on the operator's directive; placement
operator-chosen at that wrap's P5, ahead of *Release build and bundle*)

**Surface intent (verbatim from the entry):** the tree made `cargo fmt --check`-clean and the gate
added to CI so it cannot re-rot.
Two halves, both required — neither alone satisfies the entry:

1. **The formatting pass.** Apply the workspace's own `rustfmt.toml` across the tree so
   `cargo fmt --check` exits 0 at HEAD.

2. **The CI gate.** A fmt step in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` that runs the same check and turns the
   job red on violation, so the tree cannot silently re-rot. Today no workflow runs rustfmt at all,
   which is the mechanism by which the rot went unobserved for four days.
