title: Folded freight from the working entry

data.head: ## Folded freight from the working entry

body:
The entry carries a `CONTEXT` block (no `PREREQ:` / `CARRY:` / `BLOCKED-ON:` annotations). Its
causal-mechanism claims fold below as their own bullets, each keeping the entry's own marker text
verbatim — statedness is not measurement at HEAD, so each is `[inferred]` until P3's scope premise
closure resolves it.

- **PARTLY VERIFIED (P3) — Root cause, operator-supplied, measured pipeline-side (backlog W90):**
  "`rustfmt.toml` (edition 2024) shipped 2026-09-05 with only `commands.rs` re-sorted, and CI never
  gained a fmt step." The *shipped-2026-09-05* and *no-CI-step* halves are verified and hold (the
  latter strengthened at P3: no `fmt` token appears in `ci.yml` OR in either `agent-run` script).
  The *only-`commands.rs`-re-sorted* half stays `[inferred]` and is deliberately **not** re-derived:
  it is a claim about the 2026-09-04 commit's history, both `commands.rs` and `spawn.rs` are clean at
  HEAD either way, and it shapes no step of this chunk.

- **VERIFIED (P3) — EVIDENCE, as the entry states it:** "the invocation is NOT the cause —
  `rustfmt.toml` is `edition = "2024"` (stable, no unstable options), the toolchain is pinned
  1.95.0 with rustfmt as a component, and the diffs are ordinary edition-2024 import ordering and
  line wrapping." The three configuration facts were re-verified at promotion. The diff-content
  claim is now verified too, on a firmer basis than the entry stated it: parsing the diff (ANSI
  stripped) gives +1581/−486 lines whose change classes are exactly import re-sorting (30 `use`
  statements, 45 use-list items) and expression re-wrapping (`bare-delimiter` 228 added vs 5
  removed; `method-chain` 279 vs 40). See `research.md` §1.

- **VERIFIED, IN A STRONGER FORM (P3) — the entry's `hypothesis:` marker, kept:** "a formatting-only
  diff can be partitioned from semantic change by byte-identity against `rustfmt --config-path
  rustfmt.toml`, keeping review cheap at ~40 files — the technique is established (`2026-09-06`
  crate-root recursion) but unmeasured at this scale." Measured: the partition holds, and the
  stronger available invariant is **per-file token-multiset identity** — for each of the 60 files the
  multiset of identifiers, string literals and numerals on the added side equals the removed side
  (60/60 identical, 0 exceptions; 262 distinct string literals per side, 0 exclusive to either).
  Because that is ONE whole-diff invariant rather than a 60-file reading task, **review cost does not
  scale with the file count**, which retires the entry's review-cost worry independently of the
  count correction (60, not ~40).

- **Formatting-only.** No semantic change ships in the pass. The partition argument is the
  byte-identity technique above; anything rustfmt would not itself produce is out of scope.

- **`test-plan.md:455` is left standing, not retired.** It is a TARGET-state descriptor, and this
  chunk makes it true. This follows the `2026-09-06-coverage-completeness-gate` narrow ruling and
  the explicit guard carried through the prior chunk's wrap — no detector proposal to retire it is
  to be accepted here.

- **Rust only.** `rustfmt` governs `.rs`; no other formatter (prettier, black, the `ui/` TypeScript
  tree) enters scope. The npm side has its own gate and is untouched.

- **No behavioural CI change beyond the added gate.** The `a11y` job's open questions (the
  WebView2 endpoint, the driver-layer ECONNREFUSED) are a different thread and stay out.
- **60 `.rs` files** across 8 crates (list above) — formatting only.
- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`** — one added gate step in job `rust`.
- **`.andromeda/test-plan.md:455`** — becomes TRUE by this chunk; the row itself is not edited.

- **`verify_fmt_token_invariant.py`** in this chunk's own directory — added at validation-1 as an
  INTENT-INCOMPLETE amendment: planning surfaced that the formatting-only claim needs a *re-runnable*
  verifier, not just the one-shot P3 measurement, so the wrap light gate can re-assert it. Chunk
  evidence, not a shipped artifact — nothing under `crates/` or `scripts/` references it.

- **The `--fail-under-lines 60` coverage floor is genuinely at risk and is not a formality here.** The
  pass is net **+1095** lines (+1581/−486) with 30 of the 60 files under `src/`, which the floor counts
  (`tests/` is excluded by `--ignore-filename-regex`). Expression re-wrapping turns one long line into
  several, and whether the added lines count as covered cannot be known without running the collection.
  The working entry did not anticipate this and no extract raised it. If the floor drops below 60 that
  is a finding to record with its measurement, never a threshold to relax (test-plan §11 Quality).

- **RESOLVED — which CI job hosts the gate:** job **`rust`** ("Rust gate (build · test · lint ·
  supply-chain · coverage)", `windows-latest`, `ci.yml:16-187`). Its lint half today runs through the
  harness, not a bare cargo call: the step `Test + lint (dogfood agent-run)` invokes
  `.\scripts\agent-run.ps1 run`, and there is no standalone `cargo clippy` step. Neither `ci.yml` nor
  either `agent-run` script contains any `fmt` token, so the gate has no existing home in the
  workflow or the harness. Named by JOB, never by line, per a11y-plan §3 and test-plan §9.
  *Step ORDER within the job remains open — carried to `research.md` §Open questions as a
  plan-decision for P4.*

- **RESOLVED — the invocation form is `cargo fmt --all --check`.** `Cargo.toml` declares no
  `default-members` key, which is why the bare and `--all` forms both measure 282 sites today; they
  diverge the moment such a key is added, which would silently narrow the bare form. arch's
  member-completeness criterion is satisfied only by the explicit form. (test-plan §9's Lint row
  names the bare form; `--all --check` is a strict superset and makes the row true — surfaced at
  the P5 review as a deliberate, argued choice rather than decided silently.)

- **OPEN, by construction — whether the pass leaves `nextest`, `clippy` and the coverage floor
  green.** Unknowable before the pass runs; token-multiset identity makes regression very unlikely
  but is not a substitute for running them. All three ride the plan's Test Commands.

- **RESOLVED — no `#[rustfmt::skip]` is needed.** The tree carries **zero** today; no flagged file
  holds a snapshot assertion, a hand-aligned token table, an ANSI/status literal or a garde
  annotation; and per-file token-multiset identity holds in all 60.

- **RESOLVED — the crate-root recursion effect does not apply.** The 2026-09-06 learning describes a
  chunk whose real delta was small being widened by a crate root pulling in its module tree. Here the
  whole workspace is formatted deliberately, so the diff IS the complete intended set — nothing is
  pulled in unexpectedly.

title: Premises added at P3 (not anticipated by the working entry)

data.head: ## Premises added at P3 (not anticipated by the working entry)

body:
- **The gate is line-ending invariant — tested, not asserted.** `.gitattributes` carries exactly one
  rule (`coverage-matrix.md text eol=lf`), so `.rs` files ride `core.autocrlf` (this host: `true`);
  they measure `i/lf w/lf`. `rustfmt`'s `newline_style` defaults to `Auto`, and the same clean file
  passes `--check` at **exit 0 in both LF and CRLF form**. A CRLF checkout cannot redden the gate.

- **Every sensitive surface the seven extracts named is outside the pass.** `garde` (5 files in
  tree / 0 flagged), `info_span!` (5/0), `insta::` (4/0), `[PASS]`-class prefixes (8/0), `owo_colors`
  (1/0), `comfy_table` (1/0), `rusqlite` (3/0), `creation_flags` (1/0), and all of
  `conductor-core/src`, `conductor-cli/src`, `commands.rs`, `obs.rs`, `redact` and `conductor-report`
  (0). Every preservation constraint the design, layouts, obs, a11y and security extracts raised is
  therefore satisfied vacuously. Each zero was positive-controlled against the tree first.

- **Artifact preservation does not constrain step placement.** All three `rust`-job uploads
  (coverage `:109`, JUnit `:118`, obs self-observation `:182`) carry `if: always()`, so a fail-fast
  gate anywhere in the job cannot drop them — which dissolves the obs↔tests placement tension the
  fan-out surfaced.
- Any semantic refactor riding the formatting diff.
- Retiring or rewording `test-plan.md:455`, `:477`, `:507`.
- The `v2-24` disposition and the a11y/driver threads (owned by the wrap that dispositions `v2-24`).
- Formatting anything outside the Rust workspace.

_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-09-10-live-pulse-in-lane-scenario-round · **Version:** conductor-0.2.0 · **Generated:** 2026-09-10T11:12Z

Drive the three committed in-lane scenarios — `live-only-service-truth` (P-067),
`investigate-actions-functional` (P-072) and `constellation-severity-live-wiring` (P-079) — against a
live, operator-launched Pulse, and produce for each a **non-blocked verdict via MCP read-back with
journal and `runs.db` evidence**, which is exactly `verification-matrix.json#v2-04`'s acceptance. This
is a **round, not harness work**: research settled that no source delta is required (`research.md`
§Files to modify), so the deliverable is driven evidence plus the recorded disposition of one finding.

The round's difficulty is not the driving — it is **sequencing**. Every `conductor run` fires its own
preflight canary, and Pulse dedupes a new incident against **any open incident, not by fingerprint**
(`verification-harness.md:50`, measured). Three legs back-to-back therefore land two
`Blocked: no incident opened after the canary storm was emitted` rows — precisely the state `v2-04`
forbids. Each leg is consequently fired behind a **≥150 s quiet window** (Pulse's 120 s idle plus a full
30 s resolver tick), the same interval the shipped `live_suite()` already uses at `agent-run.sh:127`.

Grading is settled and differs per scenario, which is why each leg is planned for its own outcome rather
than one shared expectation (per arch §Standard Contracts + §Established Decisions [Read-Back Dependency
Posture]). P-067 and P-072 carry **no `[[expected]]` block**, so they route through the
operator-checklist branch to `manual_record` → `ManualCheck`, or to `KnownResidual` when the read-back is
empty or degraded — **both non-blocked**. P-079 carries a Hard `CountAtLeast ≥ 1` and grades
programmatically; its floor reads `span_refs`, which Pulse writes empty at every production incident, so
the floor is unmet and routes to `CalibrationRegion` **regardless of the declared `Hard`** — also
non-blocked, and an already-ratified treatment (see Constraints).

1. **Confirm the SUT preconditions before any leg fires.** The operator launches `pulse-app` (built with
   the `mcp-server` feature, from a cwd **outside** this repo — it writes Specta bindings relative to its
   own cwd) and supplies its data dir. Verify the sidecar binary resolves on `PATH` in **POSIX form**
   (`/d/dev/projects/andromeda-pulse/target/release:$PATH`; bash splits a Windows-form path on the
   drive-letter colon) via the `which andromeda-pulse-mcp` entry in `## Test Commands`, then run the
   non-priming `conductor preconditions` entry. Do **not** run `agent-run.sh boot` — it fires a canary the
   first leg would then dedupe against (`verification-harness.md:53(a)`).

2. **Fire leg 1 — P-067 `live-only-service-truth`** using its `## Test Commands` entry, whose `run`
   carries the 150 s quiet window ahead of the invocation. Expected outcome: a `ManualCheck` row
   (`KnownResidual` if the read-back returns an empty or degraded observation). Record the printed
   per-P-ID line and the minted `run_id`.

3. **Fire leg 2 — P-072 `investigate-actions-functional`**, same form. Its `<90s` tier is recorded on the
   envelope but **not graded** (a declare-only scenario writes zero `CheckRecord`s and `deadline_ms` lives
   only on a `CheckRecord`). Expected outcome: `ManualCheck` or `KnownResidual`.

4. **Fire leg 3 — P-079 `constellation-severity-live-wiring`**, same form. Expected outcome:
   **`CalibrationRegion` verdict with a `ManualCheck` state** (an unmet sample floor never hard-fails,
   `slo.rs:96-100`). A `Pass` here would mean `span_refs` became non-empty on Pulse's side and is a
   finding to record, not a result to assume.

5. **Assert the evidence, per scenario, from the artifacts** — not from exit codes. A leg exits 0 on a
   `Blocked` row (`exit_code` is non-zero only on `Lamp::Fail`, `verification-harness.md:60(b)`), so the
   `runs.db` and journal probe entries in `## Test Commands` are what actually gate the round: each of the
   three scenarios' newest row is non-`Blocked`, and each has a journal envelope line (selected by the
   envelope-only `seed` key, **never the file's last line** — a `CheckRecord` ends P-079's journal).

6. **Commit the evidence — `/runs/` is gitignored (`.gitignore:17`), so nothing the probes read survives
   the commit.** `v2-04`'s acceptance names journal and `runs.db` evidence per scenario; the probes prove
   it at gate time, but the artifacts are ephemeral and the version closes right after this chunk, so this
   is the last cheap moment to keep them. Copy, into
   `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-09-10-live-pulse-in-lane-scenario-round/evidence/`:
   each leg's **envelope line** verbatim as `p-067.jsonl` · `p-072.jsonl` · `p-079.jsonl` (selected by the
   envelope-only `seed` key, never the file's last line), plus `live-round-verdict.md` carrying the three
   `runs.db` row values (`run_id` · `scenario` · `verdict` · `state` · `latency_ms` · `slo_tier`), the
   three printed per-P-ID lines, and step 7's posture witness. This follows the shipped precedent at
   `2026-09-06-operator-gated-live-suite/evidence/` (per-leg `.jsonl` + a verdict summary) and
   `2026-09-07-sr-findings-fixed/evidence/`. A wrap light-gate re-run lands its own copies suffixed
   `.run2-lightgate` rather than overwriting these, per that same precedent.

7. **Record the SUT's booted posture from Pulse's own log**, not from the launch command: grep Pulse's
   `{data_dir}/logs/agent-latest.jsonl.<date>` for the TARGET `triage.baseline.bootstrap_window.override`,
   never for the emitting function name (`verification-harness.md:60(e)`). Capture it in
   `evidence/live-round-verdict.md` beside the three verdicts.

8. **Record the vacuous-`CountAtLeast` finding with its scope and a named owner** (see Constraints). It is
   a class spanning **three** committed scenarios, not a P-079 defect, and it is not this chunk's to fix.
- `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-09-10-live-pulse-in-lane-scenario-round/evidence/p-067.jsonl` — leg 1's envelope line, verbatim.
- `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-09-10-live-pulse-in-lane-scenario-round/evidence/p-072.jsonl` — leg 2's envelope line, verbatim.
- `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-09-10-live-pulse-in-lane-scenario-round/evidence/p-079.jsonl` — leg 3's envelope line, verbatim.

- `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-09-10-live-pulse-in-lane-scenario-round/evidence/live-round-verdict.md` — the three `runs.db` row values, the three printed per-P-ID lines, and the SUT's booted-posture witness line.
_Written by step 6 — the durable copy of evidence that otherwise lives only under the gitignored `/runs/`._

- (none) — the round requires no source delta. `scenarios/*.toml` are explicitly **not** touched
  (scope §Boundaries); the three spec masters that describe this mechanism are already correct
  (see Constraints) so no Expected amendment is owed.

Agent-driven project. **This chunk HAS a live leg and a boot path**, so the `role = 'smoke'` entry is a
mint-then-read `status` placed AFTER the legs — it reads the envelope those legs just minted, never a
prior run's residue (`verification-harness.md:49`). **No `self-verify` entry**: not a UI/visual chunk —
zero `ui/`, `.tsx` or webview delta. **No `build` entry**: nothing is regenerated. The supply-chain
probes are listed because the round is banked against the committed lockfile; the standing advisory
deferral was **CLOSED** at `2026-09-05-audit-corrective`, so no PREREQ re-pin is owed. **Nothing is
deferred.**

**The committed-evidence criterion has no producing gate by design.** `evidence/*.jsonl` and
`evidence/live-round-verdict.md` are authored by /implement step 6 — an authoring act like any other new
file, not a runtime artifact a command emits — so no entry carries them as `artifact`. Their existence and
non-emptiness are asserted by the `committed evidence files: 4` probe below, which the wrap light gate
re-runs.

The three live legs each carry their quiet window **inside `run`**, because the window is part of that
leg's firing form (a SUT-side dedupe precondition that emits no signal to wait on), not an in-test sleep
— the distinction test-plan §11 draws. Leg 1 carries one too, so the block is **literally re-runnable**
by the wrap light gate against a Pulse that already holds this round's last canary.

body:
- (matrix) `verification-matrix.json#v2-04` — scenarios keyed to P-067, P-072 and P-079 each drive a live
  Pulse and yield a **non-blocked** verdict via MCP read-back, with journal and `runs.db` evidence per
  scenario; evidenced by the two probe entries reading `non-blocked rows: 3` and
  `journal envelopes non-blocked: 3`.

- (arch) Each leg's evidence is the eleven-field envelope row in `runs/<run_id>.jsonl` plus its `runs.db`
  row, with **zero `run_check` rows** for the two declare-only scenarios and per-check `CheckRecord` rows
  only for P-079 (per architecture.md §Standard Contracts — Run report envelope / Per-check record).

- (tests) The evidence **survives the commit**: `evidence/p-067.jsonl`, `evidence/p-072.jsonl`,
  `evidence/p-079.jsonl` each hold their leg's envelope line verbatim, and `evidence/live-round-verdict.md`
  holds the three `runs.db` row values plus the posture witness — because `/runs/` is gitignored
  (`.gitignore:17`) and the probes' proof is otherwise ephemeral (per test-plan.md §3 Status endpoint
  shape; the committed-evidence precedent at `2026-09-06-operator-gated-live-suite/evidence/`).

- (arch) No live-Pulse leg is added to any CI job; the round stays an operator/local gate, and each leg's
  firing form resolves the sidecar on `PATH` so a `[BLOCKED]` row cannot be a `PATH` artefact
  (per architecture.md §Established Decisions [CI/CD] and §Occupied Resources — Service/process names).

- (obs) Each scenario's journal row carries all eleven envelope keys with `state` and `verdict` inside
  their closed sets and `state` ≠ `Blocked` (per obs-plan.md §6 Required fields / §3 Log format JSON schema).

- (design) P-067 and P-072 render with the `[MANUAL]` ASCII prefix — or `[RESIDUAL]` when the read-back is
  empty or degraded — and never `[FAIL]` or `[BLOCKED]`; P-079 renders its own machine-verdict lamp. No
  state collapses into another and no seventh label is minted (per design-system.md §Color Palette →
  the Verdict-vs-ReportState note).

- (layouts) The harness stage-flag set remains `--unit`/`--integration`/`--e2e`/`--live` and the five-command
  discipline is unchanged — the three legs land as gate entries, not as a new command or a sixth verb
  (per layout-templates.md §Surface: cli — Primary screens, `agent-run.{sh,ps1}` bullet).

- (security) No artifact produced by any leg — `runs/<run_id>.jsonl`, the `runs.db` row, `<run_id>.md` —
  contains an absolute host path, an internal seam-crate struct name, or an `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_*` handle
  value (per security-plan.md §Error Handling; §Security Anti-Patterns → Logging).

- (security) Each non-blocked verdict is reached with the readiness gate **intact** — no preflight arm
  relaxed, skipped or re-graded (per security-plan.md §Security Anti-Patterns → Universal).

- (tests) Every leg exits 0 on a `ManualCheck`/`KnownResidual`/`CalibrationRegion` row, and no leg's pass
  condition is read off an exit code: the `lacks [BLOCKED]` assertion and the two artifact probes carry
  the verdict (per test-plan.md §11 E2E; §3 `run` exit-code semantics).

- (a11y) The round claims **no** a11y coverage and no WCAG conformance for the CLI legs it drives; the
  not-assertable verdict for the `conductor` verb SET is left intact (per a11y-plan.md §1 A11y Scope
  Summary → `conductor-cli` entity).

  [Timing-Tolerance Model] · [CI/CD] · §Occupied Resources — Service/process names, On-disk artifacts ·
  security-plan.md §Input Validation · §Error Handling · §Security Anti-Patterns · §Dependency Security ·
  obs-plan.md §3 · §6 · §10 · test-plan.md §3 · §6 · §9 · §11 · design-system.md §Color Palette ·
  §Surface: cli · layout-templates.md §Surface: cli · a11y-plan.md §1 · §6 · §9.

- Harness rules: `.claude/rules/verification-harness.md` entries 47–55, 58, 60 (structural extraction) ·
  `.claude/rules/observability.md` (full).

- Research files inspected: `crates/conductor-run/src/execute.rs` · `crates/conductor-verify/src/{extract,slo,preflight}.rs` ·
  `crates/conductor-report/src/db.rs` · `scripts/agent-run.sh` · `scenarios/*.toml` (×3) ·
  `andromeda-pulse` `pulse-app/src/{inference_runtime,deterministic_inference}.rs` ·
  `crates/mcp-server/src/tools.rs` · `crates/triage/src/incident/persistence.rs`.

- **Do not re-author any scenario to make a verdict greener** — scope §Boundaries. The three `.toml` files
  are committed and verified; a scenario that cannot yield its claimed verdict is a recorded premise
  correction, not an edit.

- **Do not retire P-079's `CountAtLeast` check in this chunk** — rejected after measurement. The condition
  is a **class, not a P-079 defect**. **Basis, stated as the derivation** (`grep -n 'kind = "CountAtLeast"'
  scenarios/*.toml`): exactly **three** files carry a LIVE `kind = "CountAtLeast"` key, one each —
  `constellation-severity-live-wiring.toml:53` · `findings-counter-refresh.toml:49` ·
  `pulse-run-contract.toml:58`. Do **not** re-derive this with a bare token grep: `grep -c CountAtLeast`
  returns hits in **seven** files, because four (`ack-cooldown` · `error-baseline-spike` ·
  `incident-auto-resolution` · `latency-regression`) mention the token only in comments recording checks
  already retired, and `findings-counter-refresh` reads 3 (one live key plus two retirement comments).
  The precedent that this outcome is ACCEPTED rather than a defect is
  **`architecture.md:69`** (a ~10 KB single line; the clause sits at offset ~5712, inside the
  `KnownResidual`-routes paragraph): "`findings-counter-refresh` carries one `[[expected]]` and still
  landed `KnownResidual`, because ITS read-back came back degraded, and its unmet `CountAtLeast` floor
  graded `CalibrationRegion` rather than failing (a sample floor never hard-fails)" — recorded as a
  measured, shipped outcome, not flagged for repair. Note the limit honestly: that clause's subject is the
  degraded-read-back ROUTE, so it establishes acceptance-in-practice, not an explicit ruling that a
  vacuous floor may stand; the MECHANISM is carried by `architecture-amendments.md:403`, and the
  retirement comments in the four sibling scenarios are the applied precedent. Retiring only P-079 would
  be inconsistent with a shipped sibling; retiring all three is beyond this chunk. **Owner:** a
  route-entry candidate raised at wrap, named in the chunk report.

- **No Expected amendment to a master is owed.** `architecture-amendments.md:403` already states the
  mechanism verbatim — "`CountAtLeast` grades `span_refs` the incident producer writes empty" (2026-08-21,
  the ground on which five severity-lifecycle scenarios were retired to declare-only) — and
  `architecture.md:69` already records the grading outcome as measured and accepted for a still-shipping
  sibling. Both were re-measured true this pass, at those exact lines. (`architecture.md:63` is the
  freshness-carrier paragraph and carries neither claim — it contains zero occurrences of
  `findings-counter-refresh`; an earlier draft of this plan mis-cited it, corrected at the P5 review.)

- **`.claude/rules/verification-harness.md:47` is stale and is a LEAF, not a master** — it states the
  deterministic-L4 fixture pins `evidence_refs` to `[]`, which Pulse retired (the fixture now populates a
  constant `det-*` triple, its own doc calling the population load-bearing). architecture.md:63,
  obs-plan.md:314-315 and test-plan.md:76/335 all already carry the corrected form, so the master tier is
  right and only the rules file lags — a cascade gap for wrap's curation, never a master amendment.
  It changes nothing here: `span_ids` is empty independently of L4 mode.

- **Rejected: `SCENARIO=<name> bash scripts/agent-run.sh run`** as the leg form. It is the documented
  artifact-producing firing form, but it also runs nextest + doctest + clippy on **every** leg — three
  full workspace suites for three scenarios.

- **Rejected: adding three legs inside `live_suite()`.** It would require a `.sh`/`.ps1` parity edit, change
  a shipped suite's leg order, and append ~3 legs plus quiet windows to an operator session already
  carrying H/B1/B2/quiet/A and the driven a11y arm under a 15-minute mocha ceiling (a11y-plan §10).

- **Never run `boot` before a leg on the same data dir** — `conductor run` fires its own preflight canary
  and boot's canary is exactly what it would dedupe against (`verification-harness.md:53(a)`; measured
  cost: two 12-minute runs).

- **Sequencing is the whole risk.** Legs fired back-to-back dedupe against the previous leg's still-open
  canary and land `Blocked`. Each entry's 150 s window is the cure and is not optional. Budget the round
  at roughly 12–15 minutes: 3 × (150 s window + ~47 s preflight + scenario) with scenario windows summing
  18 s · 35 s · 30 s (derived by summing each TOML's `gap_ms`: 3000+12000+3000, 3000+20000+12000,
  3000+15000+12000).

- **Each leg's own canary is still open at its own read-back** — every scenario window is far inside
  Pulse's 120 s auto-resolve window (`DEFAULT_INCIDENT_AUTO_RESOLVE_WINDOW_SECS = 120`,
  `andromeda-pulse crates/triage/src/incident/persistence.rs:42`, HEAD `83d4060`). So `observe()` never
  returns `EmptyCorpus`, which is what keeps P-079 off the `Blocked` route.

- **`logs/agent-latest.jsonl` truncates per invocation**, so only the last leg's self-obs survives unless
  frozen between legs. `v2-04`'s required evidence is unaffected: `runs/<run_id>.jsonl` and the `runs.db`
  row are per-run and do survive (`verification-harness.md:60(a)`). Freeze per leg only if the chunk
  evidence wants the self-obs stream.

- **A missing witness line is not evidence about the wire.** With the sidecar unreachable the preflight
  blocks before the canary gate runs, so the canary never emits at all — check the binary before drawing
  any conclusion from an absence (`verification-harness.md:48`).

- **The SUT must stay UP through the wrap.** The wrap's light gate re-runs every entry verbatim — all
  three legs, quiet windows included, another ~12–15 minutes. If `pulse-app` is stopped after /implement,
  the legs cannot fire and the round's proof degrades to the committed artifacts from step 6 alone. This
  is the operator's to hold, and it belongs in the chunk report's next-step line, not only here.

- **Expected amendments (wrap):** none to any of the seven masters (see Constraints — both relevant arch
  sites were re-measured true this pass, at `architecture-amendments.md:403` and `architecture.md:69`).

title: The load-bearing equality — MEASURED, and it decides P-079

data.head: ## The load-bearing equality — MEASURED, and it decides P-079

body:
The design needs: *does P-079's `CountAtLeast ≥ 1` yield a met floor for a live Pulse read-back?*
**No — it is structurally unsatisfiable, and every link is measured:**
| # | Site | Fact |
| 1 | Pulse `inference_runtime.rs:871` | `evidence_refs: EvidenceRefs { … span_ids: Vec::new() … }` — **hard-empty at the only production construction site** |

| 2 | Pulse, whole repo | the only other `EvidenceRefs.span_ids` writes are `markdown.rs:507` (`vec![]`) and `tools.rs:868` (`vec![[1u8;8]]`, a unit-test fixture). **Nothing mutates it after creation** |
| 3 | Pulse `tools.rs:430–439` | `span_refs` maps 1:1 from `incident.evidence_refs.span_ids` ⇒ always `[]` live |
| 4 | Conductor `extract.rs:116` | `observation.evidence_count += string_array(&slice, "span_refs").len()` ⇒ **0**, summed over every open incident |
| 5 | Conductor `extract.rs:55` | `CountAtLeast` observes `evidence_count.to_string()` ⇒ `"0"` |
| 6 | Conductor `slo.rs:53–62` | `compare` parses both sides: `0 >= 1` ⇒ **false** |
| 7 | Conductor `slo.rs:96–100` | unmet `CountAtLeast` ⇒ `ClaimClass::CalibrationRegion` **regardless of the declared class** — "sample floors never hard-fail" |

This is *stronger* than the false-green the scope anticipated. The scope feared the still-open canary
could satisfy the floor; in fact **nothing** can. It is the same shape as the five live-proof re-bases
the tests extract names (test-plan §6 Fingerprint-storm, where `Absent` passed **vacuously**), whose
prescribed remedy is: retire the ungradeable check to declare-only and move the live claim to the
**harvest tier**, applied at **both** its §6 and §1 sites.

**Correction to a harness-rule premise:** `verification-harness.md:47` states the deterministic-L4
fixture pins `evidence_refs` to `[]` (`deterministic_inference.rs:35`, measured 2026-08-16). At Pulse
HEAD `83d4060` that is **stale** — the fixture now POPULATES them (`det-span-…` / `det-template-0007` /
`det-fingerprint-…`) and its own doc comment says the population is load-bearing precisely to stop
vacuous passes. It changes nothing here: only `fingerprint_hashes` is joined from L4 output
(`grounded_fingerprint_hashes`, `inference_runtime.rs:845`), and `span_ids` is hard-empty independently
of L4 mode.

title: Open questions from scope — all four closed

data.head: ## Open questions from scope — all four closed

body:
1. **Does an empty-`expected` scenario reach MCP read-back? → YES.** `execute.rs:98` calls
   `observe(client).await` **unconditionally**; `scenario.expected.is_empty()` is merely the second
   argument to `route_read_back`, which routes the *interpretation*, not whether read-back happens.
   `v2-04`'s "via MCP read-back" mechanism clause is satisfiable for all three scenarios.
2. **Is `span_refs` populated? → NO, never, live.** See the table above.

3. **Where do ManualCheck rows come from? → `execute.rs:120–147`.** The empty-`expected` branch builds a
   `HoldPoint { step: "operator-checklist", checklist: scenario.checklist.clone() }` — **empty for all
   three** — resolves it through `resolve_hold` (headless resolver, never blocking), logs the resolution
   at `info`, and returns `manual_record(...)`: `verdict: None`, `state: state_for(observation, ManualCheck)`.
   **`state_for` (`execute.rs`) returns `KnownResidual` when `observation.degraded`, else the measured
   state.** So P-067/P-072 land `ManualCheck` on a non-empty corpus and **`KnownResidual`** on an empty
   one (the `AutoResolved` arm sets `degraded: true`) or under a degraded read-back — **both non-blocked**.

4. **Wiring fork → three `leg = 'live'` gate entries driven directly** (a decisive material lean, see
   Conventions below). Not a P4 question.

5. **Resolver tick** — `TARGET_INCIDENT_AUTO_RESOLVE_TICK = "triage.incident.auto_resolve.tick"`
   (`pulse-app/src/incident_observer.rs:29`) exists, but the **period constant was not located in Pulse
   source**. `verification-harness.md:50` states it fires every 30 s. Recorded as
   **corroborated-in-repo, not source-derived** — the directive's `hypothesis:` marker stands.

title: The sequencing constraint — the real threat to `v2-04`

data.head: ## The sequencing constraint — the real threat to `v2-04`

body:
`verification-harness.md:50` (measured, `fingerprint-storm-live-proof`): **Pulse dedupes a new incident
against any OPEN incident, and NOT by fingerprint** — the canary's `exception_type` is unique per run and
its incident still returned `created:false, deduped:true`, producing
`Blocked: no incident opened after the canary storm was emitted`. **Every `conductor run` fires its own
preflight canary** (`canary.rs`, `preflight.rs:6`), so this blocks **any back-to-back leg**.

Three legs run back-to-back therefore yield **two `Blocked` rows** — exactly what `v2-04` forbids. The
cure on one shared data dir (the only option here: `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` must EQUAL the live
`pulse-app`'s dir, so a per-leg dir of Conductor's own empties every read-back) is the **quiet window:
≥150 s = Pulse's 120 s idle + up to a full 30 s resolver tick** after the preceding canary. The shipped
`live_suite()` does exactly this (`agent-run.sh:127`).

Scenario emission windows, summed from each TOML's `gap_ms` — all far inside the 120 s window, so each
leg's own canary is **still open at its read-back** (the directive's arithmetic, confirmed):
**P-067 18 s · P-072 35 s · P-079 30 s.**

Counter-fact that bounds it (`verification-harness.md:50`, extended 2026-08-18): a scenario emitting only
benign traffic for **≥~2–3 min** outlives its canary and read-back finds an EMPTY corpus. None of these
three comes close, so that arm does not fire.

- **`live_leg` is scenario-agnostic** (`agent-run.sh:78`): `live_leg <label> <scenario> <budget>` → `timeout … conductor run "$scenario" --agent-mode`, then freezes `logs/agent-latest.jsonl` to `runs/live-suite/<label>.jsonl`. Either wiring fork reuses this shape; option B reuses the invocation without the shell.

- **Per-run artifacts survive truncation** (`verification-harness.md:60(a)`): `logs/agent-latest.jsonl` is opened `.truncate(true)` so every `--agent-mode` run wipes the prior leg's self-obs — but `runs/<run_id>.jsonl` and the `runs.db` row are **per-run and do survive**. `v2-04`'s required evidence is exactly those two, so it is intact under any wiring.

- **Zero `CheckRecord`s for declare-only** (`execute.rs:208–213`, `ScenarioOutcome::without_checks` → `checks: Vec::new()`): P-067/P-072 write no `run_check` rows and get **no SLO grading** — `deadline_ms` lives only on `CheckRecord`. Their `latency_ms`/`slo_tier` are recorded on the envelope but never asserted.
- **`[BLOCKED]` in ~0 s = sidecar resolution, not the SUT** (`verification-harness.md:54`): elapsed time is the discriminator; verify `which andromeda-pulse-mcp` before the leg.

- **Firing form** (`verification-harness.md:48/49/53/54`, re-confirmed): `PATH` in **POSIX form**
  (`/d/dev/projects/andromeda-pulse/target/release:$PATH` — bash splits a Windows-form path on the
  drive-letter colon) · `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` = **the live `pulse-app`'s dir** · `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MCP_ENABLED=true`
  in **Conductor's own** environment · `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC=true`. The sidecar must be
  **built** in the Pulse repo (`cargo build -p mcp-server --bin andromeda-pulse-mcp --features mcp-server`);
  unbuilt, the canary never emits and a missing witness is indistinguishable from a leg that never ran.

- **NEVER `boot` before `conductor run` on the same data dir** (`verification-harness.md:53(a)`) — `run`
  fires its own preflight canary and boot's canary is exactly what it would dedupe against. The leg
  invocation is `conductor run <scenario> --agent-mode` **alone**.

- **`L4_DETERMINISTIC` is load-bearing for ALL THREE legs**, and not for the reason the directive gave.
  The directive ties it to P-072's `<90s` tier — but a declare-only scenario is **never SLO-graded**
  (finding above), so that mechanism does not bind. The real one: without deterministic L4 an incident
  forms only if the 3B model surfaces it (`verification-harness.md:47`), so the **preflight canary** may
  form no incident and every leg blocks. Conclusion unchanged, mechanism corrected and widened.

- **Read the SUT's posture from Pulse's own log**, never the launch string: grep the TARGET
  `triage.baseline.bootstrap_window.override`, never the emitting fn name (`verification-harness.md:60(e)`).

- **Gate-entry format** — the current `## Test Commands` shape is a ```toml fence of `[[gate]]` tables
  (`run`/`role`/`new`/`baseline`/`expect`/`note`), per `2026-09-09-port-occupier-test-hygiene/plan.md`.
  No chunk has yet shipped a `leg = 'live'` entry (both current mentions are prose declining one), so
  this plan authors the first.

- **Wiring fork — decisive material lean: option B**, three `leg = 'live'` entries driven as
  `conductor run <scenario> --agent-mode`. Basis: it adds **no harness source delta** (so no `.sh`/`.ps1`
  parity obligation and no change to a shipped suite's leg order), the wrap light gate re-runs the
  entries **literally**, and `v2-04`'s required evidence is per-run and survives regardless. Option A
  would append ~3 legs × (scenario + 150 s quiet) to an operator session already carrying `live_suite()`'s
  H/B1/B2/quiet/A plus the a11y arm under a 15-minute mocha ceiling (a11y-plan §10). Rejected:
  `SCENARIO=<name> bash scripts/agent-run.sh run` — it is the documented artifact-producing firing form
  but also runs nextest + doctest + clippy on **every** leg (3× the full workspace suite).

- (none) — no source delta is required by the round itself. The plan's deliverable is driven evidence
  plus the recorded disposition of the P-079 finding.

title: Directive mechanism claims — folded as `[inferred]`, marker text kept verbatim

body:
Per `promotion.md`, a causal-mechanism claim in the folded freight enters scope `[inferred]`-tagged
with its marker text verbatim, measured-marked or not — statedness is not measurement at HEAD. P3's
scope premise closure re-verifies these.

- **VERIFIED (P3)** — *"READ-BACK MECHANIC, measured at HEAD"* — because `observe()` is unfiltered and
  every `conductor run` fires its own preflight canary, and Pulse auto-resolves only after a 120 s idle
  window plus a resolver tick the harness comment puts at 30 s (*"tick period not re-derived by me —
  treat as `hypothesis:`"*), **each read-back sees its own canary still open**. Confirmed by summing
  each TOML's `gap_ms`: **P-067 18 s · P-072 35 s · P-079 30 s**, all far inside the 120 s window. The
  resolver tick stays `hypothesis:` — `TARGET_INCIDENT_AUTO_RESOLVE_TICK` exists
  (`pulse-app/src/incident_observer.rs:29`) but the period constant is not in Pulse source; 30 s is
  corroborated in-repo by `verification-harness.md:50` only.

- `[premise-corrected: a declare-only scenario is NEVER SLO-graded — `ScenarioOutcome::without_checks`
  writes zero `CheckRecord`s and `deadline_ms` exists only on a `CheckRecord`, so P-072's `<90s` tier is
  recorded on the envelope and never asserted. The handle IS load-bearing, for ALL THREE legs and by a
  different mechanism: without deterministic L4 an incident forms only if the 3B model surfaces it
  (`verification-harness.md:47`), so the PREFLIGHT CANARY may form no incident and every leg blocks.]*
  The directive's conclusion — set `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC` — stands; its stated reason
  (P-072's tier) does not bind, and the true reason is broader.

title: Directive mechanism claim PARTIALLY FALSIFIED at P1 — the correction that changes the work

data.head: ### Directive mechanism claim PARTIALLY FALSIFIED at P1 — the correction that changes the work

body: The directive states the canary consequence as uniform across all three:

> With these scenarios' tiers … the canary CANNOT have resolved by read-back, so each read-back sees
> its own canary still open and the honest outcome is a graded MANUAL row. That is `ManualCheck`,
> which is NOT `Blocked` … Plan for it explicitly per scenario.

Reading the three `.toml` files in full falsifies the universal, and on a different mechanism than
the one claimed. **The scenarios do not share a grading shape:**

- **P-067 `live-only-service-truth`** — carries **no `[[expected]]` block**. Its own header states
  the path: *"empty `expected` → verdict None → Lamp::Manual, the ManualCheck / operator-checklist
  path"*. Coverage mode `drive+observe`. → **ManualCheck**, as the directive says.

- **P-072 `investigate-actions-functional`** — carries **no `[[expected]]` block**, same declared
  path, coverage mode `drive+observe`. → **ManualCheck**, as the directive says.

- **P-079 `constellation-severity-live-wiring`** — carries a **`[[expected]]` block**:
  `kind = "CountAtLeast"`, `class = "Hard"`, `expected = "1"`. Coverage mode **`auto`** — *"Conductor
  drives the storm AND asserts the reaction through MCP read-back."* → **NOT ManualCheck.** It grades
  programmatically and can Pass or Fail.
Two consequences, both scope-shaping:

1. **The manual-ness of P-067/P-072 is structural, not canary-caused.** It follows from an empty
   `expected` — a property of the committed scenarios, stated in their own headers — and would hold
   with no canary in the picture at all. The directive reaches the right verdict for these two
   through a mechanism that is not the operative one; the distinction matters because it means the
   canary's open state is *not* what makes them non-blocked.

2. **P-079 needs a genuinely different plan.**
   `[premise-corrected: the risk is not that the CANARY satisfies the floor — NOTHING can. Measured at
   Pulse HEAD `83d4060`: `Incident.evidence_refs.span_ids` is `Vec::new()` at the only production
   construction site (`pulse-app/src/inference_runtime.rs:871`) and nothing mutates it after, so
   `retrieve_telemetry_slice.span_refs` is `[]` for every live incident, `evidence_count` is always 0,
   and `0 >= 1` is false. P-079's `CountAtLeast >= 1` is STRUCTURALLY UNSATISFIABLE against a live
   Pulse — a vacuous check, not a contaminable one.]* The consequence for grading is benign and
   measured: an unmet `CountAtLeast` routes to `ClaimClass::CalibrationRegion` **regardless of the
   declared `Hard`** (`slo.rs:96-100` — "sample floors never hard-fail"), so P-079 cannot `Fail` on
   this floor and yields a non-blocked `CalibrationRegion`/`ManualCheck` row. It satisfies `v2-04`'s
   acceptance while asserting nothing about P-079's capability.

   **Disposition RESOLVED at P4 (val-1: intent-incomplete — planning found the finding was already
   ruled).** It is not a P-079 defect but an **unswept member of a ratified class**:
   `architecture-amendments.md:403` states the mechanism verbatim — "`CountAtLeast` grades `span_refs`
   the incident producer writes empty" (2026-08-21, the ground on which five severity-lifecycle
   scenarios were retired to declare-only) — and **`architecture.md:69`** (offset ~5712 in a ~10 KB line)
   records the grading outcome as measured and ACCEPTED for a still-shipping sibling
   (`findings-counter-refresh`, unmet floor → `CalibrationRegion`, "a sample floor never hard-fails"); its
   clause is about the degraded-read-back route, so it is acceptance-in-practice rather than an explicit
   ruling. (`architecture.md:63` is the freshness-carrier paragraph and carries neither claim — an earlier
   draft mis-cited it.) Exactly three committed scenarios carry a LIVE `kind = "CountAtLeast"` key —
   `constellation-severity-live-wiring.toml:53` · `findings-counter-refresh.toml:49` ·
   `pulse-run-contract.toml:58`; a bare token grep returns seven files and is the wrong basis. So
   retiring only P-079 would contradict an accepted sibling and retiring all three is beyond this chunk.
   The round therefore **drives, records and claims**, and routes the class as a finding with a named
   owner. No scenario edit, no master amendment.

This is the W73 shape the directive warns about, arriving from the opposite side: not a scenario
planned green that grades manual, but a scenario the directive planned manual that in fact grades
Hard — and whose Pass may not mean what it appears to.

1. **Does an empty-`expected` scenario reach MCP read-back? → YES.** `observe(client).await` is called
   **unconditionally** at `execute.rs:98`; `expected.is_empty()` is only the routing flag passed to
   `route_read_back`. `v2-04`'s "via MCP read-back" mechanism clause is satisfiable for all three.
2. **Is `span_refs` populated? → NO, never, live.** See the premise correction above.

3. **Where do ManualCheck rows come from? → `execute.rs:120-147`.** The empty-`expected` branch builds a
   `HoldPoint { step: "operator-checklist", checklist: … }` — empty for all three — resolves it headlessly
   and returns `manual_record`: `verdict: None`, `state: state_for(observation, ManualCheck)`. **`state_for`
   returns `KnownResidual` when `observation.degraded`**, so P-067/P-072 land `ManualCheck` on a non-empty
   corpus and `KnownResidual` on an empty one — **both non-blocked**.

4. **Wiring fork → three `leg = 'live'` gate entries** driven as `conductor run <scenario> --agent-mode`
   (decisive material lean; basis in `research.md` §Conventions). No harness source delta.
5. **Resolver tick** — see the VERIFIED bullet above; stays `hypothesis:`, and no leg depends on it.

title: Constraint discovered at P3 that the entry, the directive and this scope all missed

data.head: ## Constraint discovered at P3 that the entry, the directive and this scope all missed

body:
**Three legs cannot run back-to-back.** `verification-harness.md:50` (measured): Pulse dedupes a new
incident against **any OPEN incident, and NOT by fingerprint** — the canary's unique `exception_type`
still returned `created:false, deduped:true`, producing `Blocked: no incident opened after the canary
storm was emitted`. Every `conductor run` fires its own preflight canary, so legs 2 and 3 would each
land the exact `Blocked` row `v2-04` forbids. The cure on one shared data dir — the only option, since
`ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` must EQUAL the live `pulse-app`'s dir — is a **quiet window of ≥150 s
(120 s idle + a full 30 s resolver tick) between legs**, the same interval `live_suite()` already uses
at `agent-run.sh:127`. This is a sequencing requirement on the round, not harness work.

Per scenario: the run journal (`runs/<run_id>.jsonl`), the `runs.db` row, the Markdown run report,
and the frozen self-obs capture — with the verdict, its class (`ManualCheck` vs graded), and the
SUT's boot posture read from **Pulse's own witness line** rather than the launch command.
- **Claim `v2-04` here** — this entry's whole reason.

- **`v2-21`** (`by-construction`) is claimable at either remaining chunk; leave it to *Release build
  and bundle*, where the matrix is final, unless P5 finds a reason to take it now.

_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-09-10-release-build-and-bundle · **Version:** conductor-0.2.0 · **Generated:** 2026-09-10T18:17:43Z

Close `conductor-0.2.0`. Produce the release binary and the Tauri 2 bundle behind the standing supply-chain
gate, record a final SLO verification pass against the **shipped** artifact, and claim the version's last two
capabilities (`v2-27`, `v2-21`) so the matrix done-test flips.

The release gate is the headless binary; the bundle is convenience, not a gate (per architecture.md
§Established Decisions [Deployment]). The gate ordering is not cosmetic — `cargo audit` and `cargo deny`
green over an un-drifted `Cargo.lock` are a **precondition of** `cargo build --release`, never a follow-up
(per security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Universal; test-plan §11 → CI). Two build facts bind: the
webview bundle must exist before any cargo compile of `conductor-tauri` (`generate_context!` resolves
`build.frontendDist` at compile time), and the **`custom-protocol` feature, not the profile**, decides whether
the binary serves the embedded bundle or opens `devUrl` (per architecture.md §Infrastructure Patterns — Build
system).

The chunk also lands the two open carried defects. **CARRY A** — the process-global panic-hook race in
`conductor-core/src/obs.rs` — is fixed at the cause with one shared in-code guard, which the code-graph
bounds to exactly two tests. **CARRY C** — the SR leg's run-to-run announcement variance — is a bounded
cause investigation whose remainder routes to residuals; per a11y-plan §3/§11 the SR leg is supplemental,
never sole, so no release claim rests on it either way.

Three operator decisions were taken at the P4 review round and are binding here: the version stamp **bumps
0.1.0 → 0.2.0**; the SLO pass drives **bounded in-lane live legs** through the shipped binary; **CARRY C
stays in this chunk** as a bounded investigation.

1. **Bump the version stamp to 0.2.0, in both places at once.** Set `version = "0.2.0"` in the workspace
   `Cargo.toml` `[workspace.package]` and `"version": "0.2.0"` in
   `crates/conductor-tauri/tauri.conf.json`. All nine members inherit via `version.workspace = true`, so no
   member manifest changes. The two files must move together or the binary and the bundle disagree.
   Regenerate `Cargo.lock` by building — the nine member version fields move; that is the bump landing, not
   drift.
   *Measured basis (research.md §Scope premise closure): no spec mandates a stamp and **no test pins the
   live value** — `baseline_harvest.rs:206` is a synthetic `format!` fixture, `:369` a verbatim historical
   capture, and `canary_obs_witness.rs:70` asserts the key not the value. The stamp reaches
   `env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")` at exactly two sites: `obs.rs:51` and `conductor-verify/src/client.rs:93`.*

2. **Fix CARRY A at the cause with one shared guard.** In `crates/conductor-core/src/obs.rs`, introduce a
   single test-module-scoped guard (a `static` mutex) and have **both**
   `panic_hook_emits_one_error_line` (`:528`) and `panic_hook_redacts_host_path_in_payload` (`:575`) hold it
   across their whole `take_hook` → `set_hook` → `with_default` → `set_hook(prev)` window. Handle a poisoned
   lock so a failing test cannot cascade into a spurious second failure.
   *Both tests must still assert exactly what they pin today — one error line; host-path redaction of the
   panic payload (per security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Logging; obs-plan §10). Neither assertion may
   be merged away, stubbed or weakened.*
   *Graph-bounded (research.md §Graph impact): `log_panic` has exactly 3 call sites — production
   `install_panic_hook` @`obs.rs:172` plus these two — and `take_hook` exactly 2. Nothing outside this file
   is impacted; `file_sink_writes_redacted_json_to_the_file` @`:609` shares `build_subscriber` but never the
   hook, so it is not a third racer.*

3. **Prove CARRY A under BOTH runners.** The remedy is only demonstrated when
   `cargo nextest run -p conductor-core` (process-per-test) **and** `cargo test -p conductor-core`
   (shared-process) are both green — only the shared-process runner can expose a test that was relying on
   per-test-process isolation (per test-plan §4 runner-portability gate; §11 → Integration).

4. **Add the `v2-21` ledger gate as a committed-artifact test.** A new crate-local `--test` target asserting,
   over the active version directory: the `v2-NN` id set in `requirements.md` equals the id set in
   `verification-matrix.json`, ids are unique, and no id matches `^P-\d+$`. Follow
   `crates/conductor-report/tests/coverage_gate.rs` — `repo_root()` from `env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")` (never
   CWD-relative), an explicit non-vacuity guard, and **set equality, never a literal count** (test-plan §1's
   own signal forbids a count assertion). **Resolve the active version directory rather than baking
   `conductor-0.2.0`** — a hard-coded literal rots at 0.3.0.

5. **Run the supply-chain gate before any release build.** In order: the advisory-db currency probe, bare
   `cargo audit` (never `--deny warnings` — it exits 1 by construction against the adjudicated allowed set,
   per test-plan §12), `cargo deny check advisories bans licenses sources`, and the `--locked` un-drift
   check. A red audit is diagnosed by reading the local advisory-db clone's `git status --porcelain` FIRST,
   before any external classification (per security-plan §Dependency Security).

6. **Build the release artifacts.** `ensure_frontend` (`npm run build`) → `cargo build --release --workspace`
   → the bundle-serving GUI binary `cargo build --release -p conductor-tauri --features
   tauri/custom-protocol`. Reuse the shells' existing form (`scripts/agent-run.sh:137-138`) rather than
   inventing a second build invocation.

7. **Acquire the Tauri CLI and produce the bundle.** The CLI is a **host dev-tool floor**, not a lockfile
   dependency — `cargo install tauri-cli --locked` at the arch-registered 2.11.3 line, the same class as
   cargo-audit / cargo-deny / cargo-llvm-cov / cargo-mutants. Then produce the bundle and record what it
   emitted (installer paths, sizes) into the chunk's `evidence/`. Confirm the CLI's expected working
   directory on the first invocation and pin the exact form into the gate entry's reading.
   *Measured basis: `cargo-tauri` is not on PATH, `Cargo.toml` declares only `tauri-build` (a
   build-dependency, not the CLI), and `@tauri-apps/cli` appears **0 times** in both `ui/package.json` and
   `ui/package-lock.json` — derivation: `grep -c '@tauri-apps/cli'` on each. `architecture.md:204` states
   that only the Tauri CLI runs `beforeBuildCommand`.*

8. **Drive the final SLO verification pass through the SHIPPED release binary.** Three bounded in-lane legs,
   each invoked as `./target/release/conductor run <scenario> --agent-mode` — **never `agent-run boot`
   first**, because `conductor run` fires its own preflight canary and boot's canary leaves an open incident
   the run's canary dedupes against (verification-harness.md `:53`(a)). Each leg after the first waits a
   **150 s quiet window** (Pulse's 120 s idle + a full 30 s resolver tick) because Pulse dedupes a new
   incident against ANY open incident (`:50`). The legs, chosen for attainable tiers with real margin:

   | leg | scenario | tier | declared phases | margin |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | 1 | `live-only-service-truth` | `<20s` | 18 000 ms | 2 000 ms — **proven live** (measured 18169 ms last chunk) |
   | 2 | `exception-event-capture` | `<5s` | 2 000 ms | 3 000 ms |
   | 3 | `cross-incident-recurrence` | `<20s` | 6 000 ms | 14 000 ms |

   For each leg assert, from the run's own envelope, `latency_ms <= threshold(slo_tier)` against
   5000/20000/90000 ms (per obs-plan §10 Performance budgets — a JSON field assertion, never an instrument),
   and record journal + `runs.db` evidence per scenario into `evidence/`, committed durably because
   `/runs/` is gitignored.

9. **Record the SLO tier-declaration finding — do not fix it here.** See §Implementation notes; it extends an
   existing ledgered residual and belongs to the next version's route Phase A, not to a release chunk.

10. **CARRY C — bounded cause investigation.** Re-run the `sr` leg in its full firing form to characterize
    the variance, and pursue the cause. **This is characterization, never retry-to-green**: a11y-plan §11 SLO
    and test-plan §10 both forbid a retry policy, a runner pin and an in-test `sleep(N)` as remedies. The
    entry's own first hypothesis is already dead — `nvda_named_window: false` does **not** discriminate
    (run1 `true`/announced, run2 **`false`/announced**, run3 `false`/not-announced), so `run2` is the
    counter-example and the field is 1-of-2. Reason instead against the bind-timing axis layout-templates
    already treats as causal (mount timing relative to when the screen reader binds — §Primary content block
    1, States). Whatever is not settled is routed to residuals with its measurement; the chunk does not
    commit to a fix.
    *Two traps that have already cost live runs: the `sr*` suites **never rebuild** (only `--e2e` does), so
    an app-side change is invisible to them until an `--e2e` run intervenes (verification-harness.md `:62`);
    and `nvda-pass.json` is **cumulative per subject**, so only `subjects.live.recorded_at` tells you whether
    a row is this run's (`:63`).*

11. **Claim `v2-27` and `v2-21`** in `verification-matrix.json` with the concretized acceptances, and commit
    the evidence set.

- `crates/conductor-report/tests/matrix_ledger_gate.rs` — the `v2-21` set-equality gate (home follows the
  dependency edge and the `coverage_gate.rs` precedent; confirm at implement that this crate can reach both
  sides, else `conductor-core`).

- `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-09-10-release-build-and-bundle/evidence/` — the recorded SLO pass (journal +
  `runs.db` rows per leg), the supply-chain gate readings, the bundle manifest, and the CARRY C record.
- `Cargo.toml` — `[workspace.package] version` 0.1.0 → 0.2.0.
- `crates/conductor-tauri/tauri.conf.json` — `version` 0.1.0 → 0.2.0 (must move with the above).
- `Cargo.lock` — regenerated by the build; the nine member version fields move. Committed.

- `crates/conductor-core/src/obs.rs` — the shared guard + both tests taking it (`:528`, `:575`). No
  signature changes, no new `pub`, no `lib.rs` re-export — which is the point (per architecture.md
  §Established Decisions [Module Boundaries]).

- `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/**` — ONLY if the CARRY C investigation lands a DOM/announcement change at the
  cause; if it does, the npm arm binds (`npm audit --omit=dev` clean, `package-lock.json` committed).

The supply-chain probes lead — they gate the release build, not follow it. The live legs are operator-gated:
they need an operator-launched Pulse and the Pulse tree's release dir on `PATH`, and a missing handle means
the entry is not run rather than run empty. `pulse-app` is the OPERATOR's process to start and stop; no gate
here stops it. The `sr` leg is likewise operator-local and never a CI gate (per test-plan §9 / §11 → CI).

title: git -C "${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/advisory-db" status --porcelain
body:
[[gate]]
run = 'git -C "${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/advisory-db" status --porcelain'
role = 'probe'

body:
- (tests) `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci` returns 0, **and** `cargo test -p conductor-core`
  returns 0 — CARRY A demonstrated under both runners, with no `retries` and no serialization knob
  introduced (per test-plan §4 + §10 Zero-flakiness budget).

- (obs/security) After the CARRY A remedy both `obs.rs` tests still assert what they pin — one error line,
  and host-path redaction of the panic payload — neither merged away nor stubbed (per obs-plan §10
  Always-required SLO invariant; security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Logging).

- (security/arch) Bare `cargo audit` exits 0 and `cargo deny check advisories bans licenses sources` exits 0
  over the committed lock, recorded as run **before** the release build, with `cargo metadata --locked`
  clean (per security-plan §Dependency Security; architecture.md §Infrastructure Patterns — Build system).

- (arch) A release binary is produced by `cargo build --release --workspace`, and the bundle-serving GUI
  binary is built `--features tauri/custom-protocol` after `npm run build`; a bare `--release` build is not
  accepted as bundle-serving (per architecture.md §Infrastructure Patterns — Build system).

- (arch) A Tauri 2 bundle is produced and its emitted installer paths and sizes are recorded in the chunk's
  `evidence/` (per architecture.md §Established Decisions [Deployment] — the bundle is convenience, so its
  absence would fail `v2-27`'s acceptance but never the release gate). Claims `verification-matrix.json#v2-27`.

- (obs) The final SLO verification pass is recorded against the shipped artifact: each of the three live legs
  is non-`Blocked` and its envelope's `latency_ms <= threshold(slo_tier)` against 5000/20000/90000 ms, with
  journal + `runs.db` evidence committed per scenario (per obs-plan §10 Performance budgets / §5 Metric
  Coverage). Claims `verification-matrix.json#v2-27`.

- (tests) The `v2-21` ledger gate passes: the `v2-NN` id set in `requirements.md` equals the set in
  `verification-matrix.json`, ids are unique, and no id matches `^P-\d+$` — asserted as **set equality**, not
  a count, with a non-vacuity guard (per test-plan §1 Critical Path 6; §6 Coverage-matrix completeness gate).
  Claims `verification-matrix.json#v2-21`.

- (a11y) The routine `--e2e` arm over the shipped bundle is graded on its PRINTED verdict — the
  `[webview2 … windows]` driven-session banner and a zero `Spec Files:` failed count with the skip tally
  inside the expected-skip SET — never on the exit code alone (per a11y-plan §11 CI; layout-templates
  §Surface: cli — Primary screens).

- (a11y) The CARRY C disposition is a cause-level finding or an explicit routed deferral, introducing no
  retry, no runner pin and no soft a11y SLO for the `sr*` leg (per a11y-plan §11 SLO; test-plan §10).

- (security/obs) The release artifacts and every recorded pass artifact (`<run_id>.md`, `runs.db` rows,
  journals, the SR record) carry zero absolute host paths and zero internal seam-crate struct names (per
  security-plan §Error Handling; obs-plan §9 Log conformance check).

- (arch) The chunk lands no new workspace crate, no new port, and no new `CONDUCTOR_*` handle, and no shipped
  binary opens an inbound listener beyond the `:4317` port-occupier fault (per architecture.md §Occupied
  Resources; §Cross-cutting Patterns — Trust boundary).

- Spec anchors: architecture.md §Established Decisions [Deployment] / [Module Boundaries] · §Infrastructure
  Patterns — Build system · §Occupied Resources · §Standard Contracts — Run report envelope ·
  security-plan §Dependency Security / §Security Anti-Patterns → Universal, → Logging / §Error Handling ·
  test-plan §1 Critical Path 6 / §3 / §4 / §9 / §10 / §11 → CI, → Integration, → E2E / §12 ·
  obs-plan §3 / §5 / §9 / §10 / §11 · a11y-plan §3 / §9 / §10 / §11 · design-system §Surface: cli /
  §Typography → Loading / §Motion → Hard limits · layout-templates §Surface: cli — Primary screens /
  §Component — Hero / §Primary content block 1.

- Research files inspected: `crates/conductor-core/src/obs.rs`, `crates/conductor-run/tests/baseline_harvest.rs`,
  `crates/conductor-run/tests/canary_obs_witness.rs`, `crates/conductor-report/tests/coverage_gate.rs`,
  `crates/conductor-tauri/tauri.conf.json`, `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/package.json`, `Cargo.toml`,
  `scripts/agent-run.sh`, `.andromeda/residuals.md`, `conductor-0.2.0/requirements.md`,
  `conductor-0.2.0/verification-matrix.json`, `.claude/rules/verification-harness.md`.

- Decisive leans stated, not asked: **CARRY A's remedy is a shared in-code guard** — leaned per test-plan
  `:538`, whose "never serializing the file" is parenthetically scoped to a RUNNER knob (`--test-threads=1`
  / a profile knob), leaving an in-code guard open, while architecture.md §Module Boundaries forbids the
  public-API widening the own-test-binary route would need (the three helpers are verified private with no
  `lib.rs` re-export). **The Tauri CLI is a host dev-tool floor** — leaned per security-plan §Security
  Anti-Patterns → Code Patterns rule (b), which already places a bundler verb outside the six governed
  spawn forms, and per the existing cargo-audit / cargo-deny / cargo-llvm-cov precedent.

- **Serializing CARRY A's tests with `--test-threads=1` or a nextest profile knob — REJECTED.** test-plan
  §11 → Integration names that as hiding the shared-state defect rather than removing it.

- **Moving the two panic-hook tests into their own `tests/*.rs` binary — REJECTED.** It would require making
  `build_subscriber` and `log_panic` `pub` (an integration test binary is an external crate, so `pub(crate)`
  is insufficient), widening `conductor-core`'s public API for tests alone — architecture.md §Established
  Decisions [Module Boundaries].

- **Re-running the `sr` leg until `S3-04` announces — REJECTED.** a11y-plan §11 SLO and test-plan §10 both
  ban a retry policy; §11 → E2E bans an in-test `sleep(N)` to synchronise, a carve-out already proposed and
  refused at `2026-09-06-operator-gated-live-suite`.

- **Adding `@tauri-apps/cli` to the frontend tree — REJECTED.** It would pull the bundler CLI into
  `package-lock.json` and the npm audit arm for no gain over the established `cargo install` host-tool
  pattern.

- **Re-declaring the mis-tiered scenarios in this chunk — REJECTED.** Scenario calibration is not release
  work; the finding is recorded and routed (see below), and P-079's own residual already targets `next`.

- **Driving the composed `run --live` suite as the SLO pass — REJECTED** (operator decision at the P4
  review): test-plan records its auto-resolve leg as not run-stable even under the stretched bootstrap
  posture, so the release pass would hinge on a leg known to be conditional.

- **Promoting `cargo auditable`, release signing or an SBOM step into a gate — REJECTED.** security-plan
  §Dependency Security marks them SKIP for artifacts Conductor produces and names `cargo auditable`
  explicitly as additive and not a gate.

- **Gate ordering is load-bearing.** The supply-chain probes precede the `build` entries by contract, and the
  `build` entries precede everything that verifies their artifacts. Do not reorder.

- **The SLO tier-declaration finding — record, do not fix.** Measured this chunk over all 36 scenario TOMLs
  (derivation: summed `^gap_ms` per file against the closed tier deadlines 5000/20000/90000 ms;
  `scratchpad/tier_audit.py`, re-runnable), and validated against three independent live measurements from
  `2026-09-10-live-pulse-in-lane-scenario-round` where summed phases predicted `latency_ms` to within ~200 ms
  on every leg (18 000→18169, 35 000→35120, 30 000→30212). **17 of 36 scenarios declare a tier smaller than
  their own summed phase duration**, but the 17 are three different things and only the last two are defects:
  - **9 accepted-deliberate** — beyond every tier and correctly declaring `<90s`, the "closest honest
    bucket" posture already operator-ratified in `matrix#v2-12`'s notes ("whole-run latency … exceeds every
    tier deadline (max 90_000 ms) by construction"). Not defects; `<90s` is the largest bucket in a closed
    set.
  - **2 mis-declared, beyond every tier** — `ack-cooldown` (`<20s`, 370 000 ms) and `severity-tier-autonomous`
    (`<5s`, 120 000 ms) should carry `<90s` under that same ratified convention.
  - **6 mis-declared, where a larger tier WOULD hold** — `severity-tier-suggested` (`<20s`, 82 000 ms →
    `<90s`), `constellation-severity-live-wiring` (`<20s`, 30 000 ms → `<90s`; **already ledgered**),
    `findings-counter-refresh`, `report-render-surface`, `service-constellation-discovery` and
    `threshold-hot-reload` (each `<5s`, 6 000 ms → `<20s`).

  So the ledgered P-079 tier defect is **one member of a class of 8, seven of them unrecorded**, and the
  residual's own guess at the origin is corroborated: these tiers read as chosen under the belief that
  `latency_ms` ≈ a reaction time, which is exactly the obs-plan gloss retired last wrap. Route it, do not
  fix it here.

- **Expected amendments (wrap):** `test-plan.md` §4 — the dev-tool roster gains `tauri-cli` as a host-tool
  FLOOR beside cargo-audit / cargo-deny / cargo-llvm-cov / cargo-mutants, since this chunk makes it a
  required build tool.

body: Editor lines = the graph's 0-indexed `line` + 1.

- **`log_panic`** — exactly **3** call sites: `install_panic_hook` @`obs.rs:172` (production) and the two
  racing tests @`:536` / `:583`. No other caller anywhere.

- **`build_subscriber`** — **5** call sites: `init_observability` @`:82`, the test helper `capture` @`:435`,
  the two racing tests @`:530` / `:577`, and `file_sink_writes_redacted_json_to_the_file` @`:609`.
- **`install_panic_hook`** — **1** caller, `init_observability` @`:84`.

- **Meaning for CARRY A:** the race's blast radius is **entirely inside `obs.rs`'s `tests` module and is
  exactly the two named tests**. `file_sink_writes_redacted_json_to_the_file` shares `build_subscriber` but
  never touches the panic hook (`grep take_hook` returns exactly 2 sites, `:535`/`:582`), so it is not a
  third racer. Nothing outside `conductor-core` is impacted.

- **Take-and-restore, not first-install-wins** (`obs.rs:535-540`, `:582-587`): both tests do
  `take_hook` → `set_hook(log_panic)` → `with_default(subscriber, …)` → `set_hook(prev)`. They use a
  SCOPED subscriber (`tracing::subscriber::with_default`), never the global `init_observability`.

- **Crate-private helper set** (`obs.rs:157`, `:171`, `:175`): `build_subscriber`, `install_panic_hook` and
  `log_panic` are bare `fn` — no `pub`. `lib.rs:48` re-exports only
  `ObsSink, ServiceIdentity, init_observability, mint_run_id, now_rfc3339`. `fixed_identity` (`:424`) and
  `capture` (`:433`) live inside the `tests` module.

- **Committed-artifact gate shape** (`coverage_gate.rs:19-45`): `repo_root()` from `env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")`
  (never CWD-relative — "a cargo test binary runs with its CWD at the package root"), an explicit
  non-vacuity guard ("the gate would pass vacuously"), then SET equality — never a literal count.

- **Release build form already in the shells** (`agent-run.sh:137-138`, `:239-240`):
  `ensure_frontend` then `cargo build --release -p conductor-tauri --features tauri/custom-protocol`.

- **Version identity is compile-time derived, at two sites**: `obs.rs:51`
  `service_version: env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")` and `conductor-verify/src/client.rs:93`
  `"clientInfo": { "name": "conductor", "version": env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION") }`. A workspace stamp change
  therefore reaches every self-obs line AND the MCP `initialize` handshake wire.

- **Gate homes follow the dependency edge** (`coverage_gate.rs:11-14`): the gate lives in the crate that can
  reach both sides of what it compares.

- **`.gitattributes`** pins `coverage-matrix.md text eol=lf` because that gate byte-compares a `writeln!`
  render; any new committed-artifact byte-comparison inherits the same requirement.

**`v2-21` is already TRUE at HEAD and mechanically checkable.** `requirements.md` declares 32 `v2-NN`
capabilities (`v2-01`…`v2-32`); `verification-matrix.json` holds 32 entries; the id sets are equal, all ids
unique, and zero ids match `^P-\d+$`. So the cap needs an ENUMERATION `/implement` can write — which
satisfies the claim-reachability rule (its decisive artifact is not wrap-authored). Design point the plan
must settle: the matrix path is version-scoped (`conductor-0.2.0/…`), so a gate hard-coding that literal
rots at 0.3.0 — resolve the active version rather than baking it.

**The version stamp is unmandated but observable.** `architecture.md` registers no workspace-package or
`tauri.conf.json` version policy, and its amendment sidecar is explicitly empty on that axis. **No test pins
the live value:** the only two `"service.name":"conductor"` + `"service.version":"0.1.0"` literals are
`baseline_harvest.rs:206` (a synthetic `format!` fixture — "Verbatim shape of Conductor's flat self-obs
line") and `:369` (a deliberately verbatim 2026-08-18 live capture); every other `0.1.0` hit is
`"service.name":"com.andromeda.pulse"`, i.e. the SUT's own lines, which a Conductor bump cannot touch. And
`canary_obs_witness.rs:70` asserts the KEY `"service.version"`, never its value. **A bump therefore breaks
no test** — it changes only what a new run emits, at the two `env!` sites above.

**The SLO pass has a hard, already-ledgered exception.** obs-plan defines the pass as a JSON field
assertion — `latency_ms <= threshold(slo_tier)` against 5000/20000/90000 ms at report-generation time, never
an instrument. The catalog is **36 scenarios** (~9 `<5s`, ~11 `<20s`, ~16 `<90s`). But
`.andromeda/residuals.md` records `constellation-severity-live-wiring`'s `slo_tier = "<20s"` as
**UNATTAINABLE BY CONSTRUCTION** (its own phases sum to 30 s; measured `latency_ms 30212` vs
`deadline_ms 20000`), `open`, target `next`, and explicitly **"neither blocking the release."** So a pass
asserting every scenario's tier CANNOT be green over the whole catalog, and the honest shape records that
residual as a named, ledgered exception rather than descoping the pass or letting it read as a failure.
A graded `latency_ms` also requires a **live Pulse** — without one every row is `Blocked` with null
measurement fields, which asserts nothing.

- `crates/conductor-core/src/obs.rs` — CARRY A: one shared in-code guard covering both tests' take/set/restore
  window. Caller threading: none escapes the file (graph impact above); no signature changes; no `lib.rs`
  re-export needed, which is the point.

- `Cargo.toml` (workspace `version`) **and** `crates/conductor-tauri/tauri.conf.json` (`version`) — only if the
  operator takes the stamp bump; the two must move together or the binary and the bundle disagree.

- A new committed-artifact gate for `v2-21` — home to be set by the dependency edge, `conductor-report`
  being the precedent's crate (`crates/conductor-report/tests/coverage_gate.rs` is the template).

- `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/package.json` + `package-lock.json` — ONLY if the bundle CLI is taken from npm
  rather than `cargo install`; see the open question.

- `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-09-10-release-build-and-bundle/evidence/` — the recorded SLO pass, the
  supply-chain gate output and the bundle manifest, committed durably because `/runs/` is gitignored
  (the precedent this version already uses).

1. **No Tauri CLI exists to produce the bundle** → blocks: **plan-decision**. `cargo-tauri` is not on PATH,
   `Cargo.toml` declares only `tauri-build = "2"` (a build-dependency, not the CLI), and `@tauri-apps/cli`
   appears **0 times** in both `ui/package.json` and `ui/package-lock.json`. `architecture.md:204` states
   plainly that "a bare `cargo build` does NOT run `beforeBuildCommand` — only the Tauri CLI does", and
   `:206` names the bundler as producing "an optional ~3 MB GUI installer". So `v2-27`'s bundle half cannot
   be produced at HEAD without acquiring the CLI. **Lean (decisive, stated in the plan, not asked):**
   `cargo install tauri-cli` at the arch-registered 2.11.3 line — this is the established host-dev-tool
   pattern (cargo-audit / cargo-deny / cargo-llvm-cov / cargo-mutants are all `cargo install`ed FLOORS,
   never lockfile-pinnable), and the security extract already places "a bundler verb" outside spawn rule
   (b)'s six governed forms. The npm alternative would pull the CLI into the frontend lock and the
   `npm audit` arm for no gain.

2. **The SLO pass's leg set** → blocks: **plan-decision**. A graded pass needs a live Pulse, and the choice
   between a bounded in-lane set (last chunk's shape) and the composed `run --live` suite has real
   stability cost — test-plan records the `--live` auto-resolve leg as **not run-stable even under the
   stretched bootstrap posture**. Put to the operator at P4.

3. **CARRY C ownership** → blocks: **plan-decision**. Carried from scope; the route entry itself defers it
   to the operator at promotion. New input from research: **a11y-plan makes the SR leg supplemental, never
   sole**, so no release WCAG claim rests on `S3-04` either way — the fork is about where the work sits, not
   about whether the release can be claimed.

**Working entry (verbatim intent):** _Release build and bundle — release binary plus Tauri 2 bundle with a
final SLO verification pass_

The version's final entry. `conductor-0.2.0` closes here: the two remaining unclaimed capabilities
(`v2-27`, `v2-21`) both resolve inside this chunk, flipping the matrix done-test.

1. **A release binary** — `cargo build --release` over the workspace, produced only behind the standing
   supply-chain gate (`cargo audit` + `cargo deny check` green, `Cargo.lock` committed and un-drifted).
   The `conductor-cli` `agent-run` binary is the release gate; the GUI is convenience.

2. **A Tauri 2 bundle** — the `conductor-tauri` bundle. `tauri.conf.json` already declares
   `bundle.active: true`, `targets: "all"`, and the three icon paths, so this is a build-and-verify job,
   not a bundle-configuration job.

3. **A final SLO verification pass recorded against the shipped artifact** — the pass that makes `v2-27`'s
   acceptance true. Its subject is the artifact this chunk produces, not a debug build.
4. **Two carried defects landed with that pass** (the two open `CARRY` annotations, below).

- **No new capability surface.** No new scenario, no new `CONDUCTOR_*` handle, no new port, no change to the
  5-command harness discipline, no OTLP or MCP contract change.
- **No route mutation.** This chunk does not create, retire or reorder route entries.
- **The version stops here.** Nothing moves to 0.3.0 as part of this chunk.

- **Scope law holds unchanged** — shipped binaries open no inbound listener; the `:4317` port-occupier
  remains the sole deliberate bind.
| Surface | Why it is in scope |
| `Cargo.toml` (workspace) · `crates/*/Cargo.toml` | release profile + the version stamp question below |
| `crates/conductor-tauri/tauri.conf.json` | bundle production; carries its own `version` field |

title: CARRY A — the process-global panic-hook race (OPEN)

data.head: ### CARRY A — the process-global panic-hook race (OPEN)

body:
From `2026-09-03-live-pulse-preconditions-probed`, operator WRAP directive item 1. Folded verbatim in
substance; the entry marks it *"verified first-hand at HEAD"*.

- **Re-verified at HEAD (2026-09-10, this promotion):** the coordinates are **correct**.
  `conductor-core/src/obs.rs` holds `take_hook`/`set_hook` pairs at exactly `:535-540`
  (`panic_hook_emits_one_error_line`, fn at `:528`) and `:582-587`
  (`panic_hook_redacts_host_path_in_payload`, fn at `:575`). A third `set_hook` at `:172`
  (`install_panic_hook`) is the production installer and is **not** part of the race.

- **The mechanism, as the entry states it** `[inferred]` — under `cargo test` (one process, parallel
  threads) one test restoring the previous hook mid-flight leaves the other's deliberate panic handled by
  the DEFAULT hook and its buffer empty. Observed red exactly once; passes since; did not reproduce at HEAD
  in 3 forced-parallel runs. *A race that passes is still a race* — testing.md §Quality gates owns it as a
  shared-state defect to remove at the cause.
- **Pre-existing and UNMASKED, not caused** — both sites are in HEAD's source.

- **Remedy named by the entry:** serialize the two against each other, or give them one shared guard.
  The entry notes relocating them to their own test binary would widen `conductor-core`'s public API for
  tests alone, since both use crate-private helpers — **confirmed at HEAD**: both call `build_subscriber`,
  `fixed_identity` and `log_panic`, all crate-private.
