title: CARRY C — the SR leg's run-to-run announcement variance (OPEN; ownership is an operator call)

data.head: ### CARRY C — the SR leg's run-to-run announcement variance (OPEN; ownership is an operator call)

body: From `2026-09-07-sr-findings-fixed`, wrap light gate. **Real and NOT closed.**

- **Re-verified at HEAD (2026-09-10, this promotion) — the tally is exact.**
  `chunks/2026-09-07-sr-findings-fixed/evidence/nvda-pass.live.run3-lightgate.json` holds 51 rows:
  **33 announced-as-expected / 15 not-run-here / 2 subject-absent / 1 not-announced**. The mover is
  `S3-04` ("Escape resolves NoGo; focus restored"), `outcome: not-announced`, `state: aborted`,
  `arm: agent`.

- **Rate:** 1 row of 51, on the third of three runs — far rarer than the original finding described, which
  is why two runs missed it. The entry's own lesson: *"ONE observation cannot separate variance from
  regression" applies to TWO observations too.*

- **The entry's `hypothesis:` marker text, preserved verbatim** `[inferred]` — *"the `nvda_named_window:
  false` correlation is the thread to pull first — it recurred across sessions and is already recorded as
  the attach signal."*

- **⚠ This promotion's re-verification WEAKENS that hypothesis, and the weakening is a finding, not a
  correction of the CARRY:** the field is **not** a discriminator across the three live runs —
  | run | `nvda_named_window` | S3-04 |
  |---|---|---|
  | `run1` | `true` | announced-as-expected |
  | `run2` | **`false`** | **announced-as-expected** |
  | `run3-lightgate` | `false` | **not-announced** |
  `run2` is the counter-example: the same `false` value with the row announcing normally. So the
  correlation is 1-of-2 on this evidence — necessary-at-best, and not sufficient. Whatever this chunk does
  with CARRY C must not treat that field as the cause on the strength of the CARRY's wording alone.

- **Coordinate correction:** `nvda_named_window` is **not** a top-level field of the evidence JSON. It lives
  at `subjects.{subject}.foreground.nvda_named_window`. A probe reading it at top level gets `None` and
  would mis-read every run as unset.

- **Constraint on any remedy** — test-plan §10's zero-flake bar: the fix is at the cause. **No retry, no
  runner pin, no in-test `sleep(N)`** — that carve-out was proposed and REJECTED at
  `2026-09-06-operator-gated-live-suite`.

- **Disposition — folded in, pending an operator fork raised at P4.** The entry pins it here because *"this
  entry's final SLO verification pass is the plausible owner"* and states: *"if it wants its own entry, that
  is the operator's call at promotion."* It is folded per that stated default so scope is complete; the

title: Discovered in planning, recorded not fixed

body:
**The ledgered P-079 tier defect is one member of a class of eight.** Measured over all 36 scenario TOMLs
(summed `^gap_ms` against the closed tier deadlines), and validated against three independent live
measurements from the previous chunk where summed phases predicted `latency_ms` to within ~200 ms.

tier**, and **6 are mis-declared where a larger tier would hold** — one of those six being the already-
ledgered `constellation-severity-live-wiring`. Scenario calibration is not release work; the finding is
handed to wrap's route-resolve to extend the existing residual, and this chunk's legs deliberately exclude
the known-unattainable scenario.

title: 1. Context — why a new version instead of finishing 0.1.0's tail

data.head: ## 1. Context — why a new version instead of finishing 0.1.0's tail

body:
0.1.0 delivered the harness: **61 chunks, all complete, 0 pending**, CI-green (workspace nextest
420/420, clippy, doctest). The scenario catalog, the seeded deterministic timeline, the emission
journal, the CLI verbs, the 5-command agent-run harness, the Tauri control panel, the coverage-matrix
view, the operator-pause dialog, the CI quality/obs gates — all shipped.
What it did **not** do is the thing the harness exists for. 0.1.0's own definition of done ends with:

> *"End-to-end proof against a real Pulse: at minimum `error-baseline-spike`, `fingerprint-storm`,
> `restart-suppression` (incl. one bypass case), `pii-scrub`, and `connection-lifecycle` produce
> verified expected outcomes (MCP read-back where applicable), and one full `severity-lifecycle` pass
> observes auto-resolve + resolution summary."*

None of that is proven. The last chunk (`2026-06-27-live-pulse-e2e-proof`) shipped **Part A** only — a
canary fingerprint-fidelity bridge — and deferred Part B because Pulse's incident creation was
LLM-in-the-loop non-deterministic. The live `conductor preflight` ran end-to-end correctly
(connect / negotiate `2024-11-05` / 4 tools / emit / poll all ✓) and still returned
`Blocked: incident not found in corpus`.

**That blocker is gone.** Pulse shipped exactly the leading option during its own v0.3.0: a
deterministic env-gated L4 mode (**P-073**, canned `L4Output`, no GPU/3B) plus Tier1 storm coalescing
so a sustained storm yields exactly ONE incident (**P-074**). Both are `verified` in Pulse's matrix. The
0.1.0 route entry *"Pulse LLM-in-the-loop verification posture — OPEN DECISION"* is therefore
**resolved and retired** — it is not a chunk and does not migrate.

**But Pulse moved while Conductor stood still, and that is the first thing 0.2.0 must fix.** Conductor
is a tool that exists to test Pulse; over the 41-day pause Pulse shipped 22 new capabilities
(P-061..P-082) and Conductor cannot so much as *name* them — its P-ID type rejects anything above
P-060 (§4 Theme 1). A 0.2.0 that proved every 0.1.0 scenario and shipped a release would still be a
harness aimed at a version of Pulse that no longer exists. Synchronization with the SUT is therefore
the first epoch, not a housekeeping afterthought.

Eight markerless entries remained in 0.1.0's route, including its own ship-and-close items. They are a
version's worth of coherent work, and they re-decompose better under fresh epoch calibration than they
sit in a tail where one entry (Part B) had swallowed five scenario families, the emit/extract framework
and the live `ready:true` proof. Two structural gains come free with a new version: a
**`verification-matrix.json`** (0.1.0 predates the feature, so Conductor — a verification harness — has
had no capability ledger of its own), and a sizing gate that will not let a Part-B-sized monolith
through again.

**Version story:** 0.1.0 = the harness is built. 0.2.0 = the harness is aimed at the Pulse that
actually exists, proves it, and ships.

> Conductor can drive and read back a real Pulse, but **has never actually proven one** — and it is
> now aimed at a SUT 22 capabilities out of date, its verification legs unbuilt, its four delegated
> timing budgets structurally unassertable, and its own delivery untracked by any ledger.

title: 3. What WORKS today — preserve, build on, do NOT rebuild

data.head: ## 3. What WORKS today — preserve, build on, do NOT rebuild

body: 0.2.0 is re-aiming, completion and proof on top of a working harness, not a rewrite:

- **Deterministic engine** — `current_thread` tokio runtime + seeded RNG; the JSONL emission journal is
  the agent-parseable ground truth and the left side of every SLO check.

- **Scenario catalog + config** — 31 declarative TOML scenarios keyed to P-IDs, garde-validated; the
  "no scenario without a P-ID" scope law holds.

- **Live-Pulse plumbing** — sidecar spawn (`conductor-verify/src/spawn.rs`), the hand-rolled JSON-RPC
  read-back client (`jsonrpc.rs` — rmcp was removed deliberately), the 4 corpus tools (`client.rs`),
  the pinned `contracts/mcp-contract.toml` (`2024-11-05` + required tools).

- **The canary bridge (Part A)** — `conductor-run::emit_canary` → poll `query_incident_list` → assert
  the fingerprint via `retrieve_telemetry_slice.fingerprint_refs`. CI-green. **Part B reuses it; do not
  re-author it.**

- **CLI + GUI surfaces** — run/suite/report verbs, the 5-command agent-run harness, line-oriented
  output, the Tauri control panel (picker, live Channel counters, coverage-matrix view, run-report and
  operator-checklist views, the go/no-go pause dialog).

- **CI** — quality gates, obs conformance gate, artifact uploads, the a11y harness (authored and
  shipped, display-gated).

title: Theme 1 — Synchronization with the SUT (KEYSTONE — everything else is worthless without it)

data.head: ### Theme 1 — Synchronization with the SUT (KEYSTONE — everything else is worthless without it)

body:
- **F1 · The P-ID type hard-rejects Pulse's current capabilities.** OBSERVED:
  `crates/conductor-core/src/scenario.rs:23-33` validates `P-NNN` with `(1..=60).contains(&n)` and
  returns `"expected P-NNN with NNN in 001..=060"`; the unit test at `:195` asserts `"P-061"` MUST be
  rejected. Pulse's ledger now reaches **P-082**. A scenario naming P-074 fails garde validation at
  load — Conductor cannot express, classify or verify anything Pulse built in v0.3.0.
  EXPECT: the accepted capability set tracks the SUT instead of a compile-time constant. Preferred
  shape: source it from a versioned SUT capability artifact under `refs/` (the precedent exists —
  `.andromeda/refs/pulse-v0_2_0-capability-audit-2026-06-12.md`), so a Pulse release is a **data**
  update, not a code change, with a drift check that fails loudly when the SUT advances past what
  Conductor knows. Widening the constant to `001..=082` is the minimum and re-freezes the same defect
  one version later — take it only as an explicit interim, never as the answer.

- **F2 · The coverage universe is frozen at 60.** OBSERVED: `crates/conductor-core/src/coverage.rs`
  enumerates exactly P-001..P-060; the scenario catalog's maximum is P-060; 0.1.0's definition of done
  reads "all **60** P-IDs classified, zero gaps". Nothing in the repo knows P-061..P-082 exist.
  EXPECT: every current Pulse capability is classified — **auto / drive+observe / static-only /
  not-Conductor's** — and the boundary is a recorded decision, not an accident. Conductor's standing
  non-goal ("NO UI automation of Pulse — visual claims are operator-checklist items") means most of
  Pulse's v0.3.0 work is legitimately **Pulse's own** to verify: the UI/visual set
  (P-061..P-066, P-068..P-071, P-080..P-082) via its webview suite and its P-076 tauri-driver e2e, plus
  P-078 (its agent-headful self-verify harness) and P-077 (the demo injector), which are Pulse's own
  tooling. Say so explicitly, so the gap is deliberate. The ones that fall squarely in Conductor's lane
  and MUST be covered:
  - **P-074** — a sustained identical-fingerprint storm yields exactly ONE incident. This is a
    quintessentially Conductor-shaped claim and the natural extension of the `fingerprint-storm`
    family; Pulse verified it with its own integration test only.
  - **P-079** — the incident workspace key is single-sourced. Externally observable via read-back, and
    it is the very defect that currently blocks Conductor's live legs (F10) — verifying it closes the
    loop.
  - **P-073** — the deterministic L4 mode. Conductor depends on it; a run contract that asserts it is
    active (F11) is that verification.
  - **P-072** — Investigate actions produce a real L4-backed result; candidate drive+observe via report
    read-back.
  - **P-067** — live-only service truth; partially observable through the service-registry surface.

- **F3 · Deterministic L4 proves the pipeline and bypasses the product's core value.** OBSERVED: with
  `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC=true` the canned `L4Output` replaces the model, so every live leg
  0.2.0 plans exercises the plumbing and never the interpretation. Pulse's own positioning memo names
  interpretation-correctness — "inject a known root cause, verify the top hypothesis identifies it"
  (the P-033 Conductor path) — as *"the single most important test in all of Pulse"*, because for a
  non-specialist a confident-but-wrong explanation is more dangerous than raw lines.
  EXPECT: a conscious decision, recorded either way. Either 0.2.0 carries one **real-model**
  correctness leg (deterministic mode OFF, known root cause injected, top hypothesis asserted), or the
  gap is explicitly deferred with a named owner and a note that "Conductor green" does not mean
  "interpretation is trustworthy". Do not let determinism silently redefine what the harness proves.

- **F4 · The SUT has a known failure mode that bounds scenario design.** OBSERVED: Pulse records that
  the DuckDB append path stalls after ~10 minutes of sustained 10k/s storm + deterministic L4 — ingest
  keeps receiving while `duckdb.append` stops, so `viz.query.traces` returns 0 rows and no new
  incidents form until restart. Conductor's whole method is sustained shaped load.
  EXPECT: scenario durations and storm profiles stay inside the SUT's proven-good envelope, the
  constraint is recorded where scenario authors will see it, and a run that exceeds it is flagged as
  environment-suspect rather than reported as a Pulse failure.

title: Theme 2 — The live proof (the reason Conductor exists)

data.head: ### Theme 2 — The live proof (the reason Conductor exists)

body:
- **F5 · Coarse emission.** OBSERVED: `conductor-run::coarse_emit` sends one signal per phase; it cannot
  shape the per-family telemetry the scenarios describe. EXPECT: a per-phase dispatcher over the
  `conductor-emit` primitives, faithful to each scenario's declared shape and extensible to the deferred
  families. (0.1.0 chunk plan, Stage 1 step 6.)

- **F6 · Placeholder read-back.** OBSERVED: `execute_scenario` writes the literal token
  `"incidents-listed"` as the observed value, so `evaluate_check` grades a placeholder rather than the
  SUT's actual response. EXPECT: real per-check extraction from `query_incident_list` /
  `retrieve_telemetry_slice`, feeding the existing `evaluate_check` → `classify` path unchanged, with
  `execute_scenario`'s signature preserved. (Stage 1 step 7.)

- **F7 · Never green.** OBSERVED: no run has ever produced live `ready: true`; the headline acceptance
  of the 0.1.0 e2e chunk was never achieved. EXPECT: a live `ready: true` against a real Pulse in
  deterministic-L4 mode, recorded with its journal + `runs.db` evidence.

- **F8 · The five families are unproven.** OBSERVED: only the canary path has touched a live Pulse.
  `fingerprint-storm` (P-017/P-018), `error-baseline-spike` (P-009..P-012), `restart-suppression`
  (P-015/P-016/P-057, incl. one bypass case), `pii-scrub` (P-035/P-047/P-048) and
  `connection-lifecycle` (P-001..P-004 + the `PortOccupier` fault) have never been driven end-to-end.
  EXPECT: each family emits faithfully, reads back through MCP, and yields a verified expected outcome;
  authored tokens and SLO tiers are re-calibrated against live behavior where they prove wrong. The
  `fingerprint-storm` family additionally carries **P-074**'s exactly-one-incident assertion (F2).
  _Sequencing note: fingerprint-storm + error-baseline-spike were the 0.1.0 Stage-2 target; the other
  three were its fast-follow set. Route may split them across chunks — they need not land together._

- **F9 · Severity lifecycle unobserved.** OBSERVED: auto-resolve and the resolution summary have never
  been observed via read-back. EXPECT: one full `severity-lifecycle` pass observes both.

  the CI-side coverage.

title: Theme 3 — The cross-project blocker (a Pulse defect, discovered here) — PREREQ

data.head: ### Theme 3 — The cross-project blocker (a Pulse defect, discovered here) — PREREQ

body:
- **F10 · The workspace filter key diverges between Pulse's app and Pulse's own MCP sidecar.**
  OBSERVED (code read, 2026-08-08 — **verify live before designing around it**): incidents are filtered
  `WHERE workspace = ?1` (`crates/corpus/src/contract.rs:628`). `pulse-app` derives that key via
  `resolve_workspace_for_incidents` (`pulse-app/src/main.rs:688-693` →
  `pulse-app/src/digest_runtime.rs:109-127`) = the **detected project root** whenever
  `workspace_detector::detect(cwd)` succeeds, falling back to `data_dir` only when detection fails. The
  **sidecar** always uses `data_dir` (`crates/mcp-server/src/bin/andromeda-pulse-mcp.rs:74`, whose
  comment still claims parity with `main.rs` — stale since Pulse's P-079 moved the app to the detected
  root). Consequence: if `pulse-app` is launched anywhere the detector recognises,
  `query_incident_list` returns ZERO rows and `conductor preflight` reproduces
  `Blocked: incident not found in corpus` **even with deterministic L4 on**.
  EXPECT: the live legs run against a Pulse whose app and sidecar agree on the workspace key. The real
  fix is **Pulse-side** (align the sidecar with `resolve_workspace_for_incidents`) and is a blocking
  external prerequisite, not Conductor work — but Conductor MUST detect the condition and fail with a
  named precondition rather than an opaque `Blocked`. An interim unblock exists (launch `pulse-app`
  from a directory where detection fails, so both sides fall back to `data_dir`), but it empties the
  digest project context and degrades context-grounding assertions (P-036); use it for a first live
  signal only, never as the standing configuration.
  _First action of this version: run the two-launch check (repo root vs. marker-less temp dir) and
  record the verdict. It decides whether a Pulse chunk gates the live legs._

- **F11 · The run contract is nowhere recorded.** OBSERVED: nothing in this repo states how a
  verifiable Pulse must be launched; `conductor-verify/src/spawn.rs:18` passes only
  `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR`, and there are zero references to Pulse's deterministic mode anywhere in
  the tree. EXPECT: a recorded, reproducible, machine-checked run contract —
  `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC=true` belongs on the **launched `pulse-app`** (the OTLP receiver
  that CREATES incidents), **not** on the MCP sidecar Conductor spawns; both sides must resolve the
  same data dir; in deterministic mode the model prerequisites (`ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MODEL_PATH`,
  `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_LLAMA_CUDA_BIN_PATH`) do not apply. Preflight asserts the contract and names what is
  unmet. This doubles as **P-073**'s verification (F2).

title: Theme 4 — The four delegated timing capabilities

data.head: ### Theme 4 — The four delegated timing capabilities

body:
- **F12 · The budgets are structurally unassertable.** OBSERVED: `SloTier` is a closed three-value set —
  5s / 20s / 90s (`crates/conductor-core/src/scenario.rs:36-61`) — while Pulse delegates **P-025** halo
  hue ≤2s, **P-027** constellation discovery ≤5s, **P-037** report render ≤2s and **P-045** counter
  refresh ≤1s. Only P-027 fits. All four scenarios carry empty `expected` (DriveObserve / ManualCheck),
  and the only latency recorded is the coarse whole-loop `observed_ms - emitted_ms`
  (`conductor-run/src/lib.rs:208`), not per-check.
  EXPECT: the four budgets are assertable at their real values — a sub-5s budget representation (extend
  the tier set, or a per-scenario budget field) plus **per-check** latency measurement, so a run yields
  a real Pass/Fail per capability rather than a ManualCheck.
  _This is what closes Pulse's **P-075**, whose acceptance names all four budgets explicitly. If route
  splits F12 from Theme 2, the plan must say out loud that P-075 stays open until both land._

- **F13 · The harness has no ledger.** OBSERVED: `conductor-0.1.0/` predates the verification-matrix
  feature, so every matrix step in every skill is a noted no-op here; Conductor's own delivery has never
  been coverage-tracked. The 60 Pulse P-IDs live in `coverage.rs` + `scenarios/*.toml` — a **different**

title: 6. Capability id scheme (read this before minting ids)

data.head: ## 6. Capability id scheme (read this before minting ids)

body:
0.1.0's `requirements.md` carries **no** numbered ids, so there is no project scheme to continue; use
the version-scoped form (`v2-NN`).
**Two id spaces coexist in this repo and must not blur:**
- `v2-NN` — **Conductor's own** capabilities. These are what `verification-matrix.json` tracks.

- `P-NNN` — **Pulse's** capabilities, the things Conductor proves. They appear **only inside acceptance
  criteria** ("…proving Pulse P-017/P-018"), in `coverage.rs` and in scenario configs — never as
  Conductor's own ids, and never as matrix entries.
Pulse's own v0.3.0 ledger reaches P-082; nothing here may mint into that space.

Conductor knows the Pulse that actually exists: every current Pulse capability is classified, the ones
in Conductor's lane are covered by scenarios, and the SUT-drift check fails loudly when Pulse advances
again. A real Pulse is launched under a machine-checked run contract; Conductor drives it and —
programmatically, via MCP read-back — proves the five families (including P-074's exactly-one-incident
claim) and one full severity-lifecycle pass, reaching live `ready: true` with journal and `runs.db`
evidence. The four delegated timing budgets (P-025 ≤2s, P-027 ≤5s, P-037 ≤2s, P-045 ≤1s) return real
Pass/Fail at their actual values, closing Pulse's P-075. The interpretation-correctness question (F3)
has a recorded answer. Desktop a11y runs and asserts on Linux+xvfb with its violations gated in CI; CLI
and Tauri produce an identical envelope for the same seed; the coverage matrix is gated zero-gap with
all CI gates green; and a release build plus Tauri bundle ships with a final SLO pass.

_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-09-11-hosted-runner-endpoint-cause-closed · **Version:** conductor-0.3.0 · **Generated:** 2026-09-11T18:25Z

The predecessor chunk probed three candidates on the hosted `windows-2025` runner and closed two of them. It
left `v3-01` deliberately un-claimed because it could not reach the acceptance's second half — that the
readings are *together sufficient to decide* whether the endpoint failure is remediable or permanent. Two
measurements were missing, and this chunk owes exactly those two.

**Arm A — the module-version reading, taken where its subject is alive.** The probe is correct; its POSITION
made the reading unreachable. Section (2) of `scripts/webview2-cause-probe.ps1` enumerates loaded modules of
`msedgewebview2` / `conductor-tauri` / `msedge`, but the step that invokes it runs *after* the
`WebView2 session isolation (diagnostic)` step has already stopped the app it started — 0.645 s later,
measured at run `34586959536`. The only window in the whole job where those processes exist is probe (a) of
that isolation step, between its `Start-Process` and the `Stop-Process` that ends it; the step's own
`tasklist` inside that window shows the app and three webview children alive. The fix is **placement**, not a
longer timeout: a timeout cannot recover a process that no longer exists.

**Arm B — elevation varied, on the side where the control already exists.** The predecessor named elevation as
the one surviving difference (`IsElevatedAdmin: True` on the runner, `False` on the dev host) and recorded it
as *a difference, not a demonstrated cause* — no probe varied it. Varying it on the runner is the expensive
direction: a hosted step is elevated by construction, so de-elevating means a scheduled-task or `runas` token
dance whose own failure modes would then have to be separated from the endpoint's. The inverse is one run:
elevate the **dev host**, where the endpoint works and the non-elevated control is already committed (routine
arm at 12 passing / 2 skipped, banner `[webview2 152.0.4191.66 windows]`, 2026-09-10), and re-run the routine
arm there. This is the discipline the earlier raw-`msedgedriver` probe broke — a probe that has not produced
the KNOWN-GOOD outcome on the known-good host discriminates nothing; here that outcome is already on record,
from this host, under the one variable being changed.

Both outcomes are deliverables: if `DevToolsActivePort` disappears under local elevation, elevation is
established with a control on both sides and no CI round-trip; if it survives, elevation is retired **as
measured on this host** — and only then does a runner-side arm earn its cost. Per architecture.md §Established
Decisions [CI/CD] + a11y-plan §9 Platform + test-plan §6, neither result may be written wider than the host it
was taken on.

**Arm C — driver/runtime major skew, varied (added 2026-09-11 on the operator's ruling, ahead of arm B).**
Arm A landed and changed the picture. At run `34645345201` the hosted image shipped a **coherent 152 triple** —
`msedgedriver: 152.0.4191.66`, `Edge browser: 152.0.4191.66`, WebView2 runtime `152.0.4191.66` before the
install step — and the `Install WebView2 Evergreen runtime 152+ (gate)` step then raised the **runtime alone**
to `153.0.4234.32`. Arm A's live-window reading proves that is what the processes actually load:
`msedgewebview2.exe` / `msedge_elf.dll` / `EmbeddedBrowserWebView.dll` all at `153.0.4234.32`, under a driver
still at 152. The earlier "runtime-major hypothesis falsified" test moved the RUNTIME while the driver stayed
put, so **a driver/runtime major skew has been present in every run this job has ever had** — there exists no
observation of it with the two at the same major. That is a measured candidate, not a proven cause: nothing
has varied it.

The arm that varies it is one conditional inside an existing step, not a deletion. The step's name states a
gate — *152+* — and the image already satisfies it before the step runs, so the step is made to honour its own
contract: install only when the measured `before` is below the floor. On this image it no-ops, driver ==
Edge == runtime == `152.0.4191.66`, everything else identical, and the discriminator is whether
`DevToolsActivePort` appears in the same `a11y` job. The floor assertion still runs on whatever is present, so
the gate's contract is unchanged; only the install ACTION becomes conditional.

1. **Add a section selector to `scripts/webview2-cause-probe.ps1`.** Extend the signature to carry a
   `[ValidateSet(...)]`-constrained section parameter beside the existing `-OutFile` (a closed enum, matching
   the project's validation discipline; an unknown VALUE must be a parameter-binding error, not a silent full
   run). **The param block also takes `[CmdletBinding()]`, and this is not cosmetic** — measured at P5 on the
   untouched tree: `powershell.exe -File scripts/webview2-cause-probe.ps1 -Section modules` exits **0**, prints
   nothing to stderr, and runs all three sections, because a plain `param()` block collects an unknown
   parameter NAME into `$args` instead of rejecting it. Without `[CmdletBinding()]`, a typo'd or stale
   selector silently degrades to a full run — which is precisely the reading arm A cannot afford. Default
   selects all three sections and must leave the default path **byte-identical in behaviour**, including its
   marker.

2. **Make the completion marker report what actually ran.** The all-sections marker stays exactly
   `[probe] complete: 3/3 sections`; a selected run emits a DISTINCT marker naming its selection — neither
   string a substring of the other, so no one grep can be satisfied vacuously by the other invocation. Nothing
   in the tree asserts the existing marker today (research §Scope premise closure item 2: one hit in the whole
   repo, the emit site itself), so this chunk's own gates define the contract.

3. **Invoke the selected section inside the live window.** In `.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s
   `WebView2 session isolation (diagnostic)` step, add the module-section invocation of the SAME repo script
   inside probe (a), after the `tasklist` census and **before** the `Stop-Process` that ends the bare app.
   Literal argv, no shell string, no `Invoke-Expression`. Steps are referred to BY NAME here, never by line
   coordinate (test-plan §9 Matrix builds; a11y-plan §3 Configuration) — research.md's line numbers are that
   document's measurement basis and this edit moves them.

4. **Leave every other step of the `a11y` job untouched — the install step excepted, and only as step 5
   specifies.** The `WebView2 cause probes (diagnostic)` step keeps invoking the full three-section script
   unchanged; its section (2) will still report `no live process`, and that line is now expected rather than a
   defect — `evidence/reading.md` says so explicitly, so a later reader cannot mistake it for the gap this
   chunk closed. The routine arm keeps no `continue-on-error`; the fetch and install steps keep their
   Authenticode check and the ≥ 152 floor; the diagnostic steps keep `if: always()` + `continue-on-error: true`.

5. **Arm C — make the install step honour its own gate.** In the `Install WebView2 Evergreen runtime 152+
   (gate)` step, measure the `before` runtime major and take the fetch + Authenticode + install path ONLY
   when it is below 152; otherwise print an explicit SKIPPED diagnostic naming the version already present.
   **Three invariants survive unchanged and are the point of doing it this way:** the step still carries no
   `continue-on-error`; the `Get-AuthenticodeSignature` gate still runs before the bootstrapper executes on
   every path where a bootstrapper executes at all; and the runtime-major ≥ 152 floor assertion still runs
   unconditionally, on whatever runtime is in effect. The third-party network fetch NARROWS to the case that
   needs it — this is a strictly smaller outbound surface, never a wider one. Reword the post-step reading
   from "after install" to "in effect", which is true on both paths.

6. **OPERATOR STEP — commit, then push `build/conductor-0.3.0`.** Placed here, before any entry that consumes
   a CI run. `ci.yml` triggers on `on: push:` with no branch filter, so the push starts all three jobs. **The
   skill does not commit and this plan does not ask it to** — the predecessor's wrap recorded exactly that
   tension as a deviation, with the attribution that the skill correctly refused.

7. **Read the run.** Capture the log via the `leg = 'operator'` entry carrying `<id>`, which the `gh run list`
   probe above it prints. **Confirm freshness by `headSha`, never by the id alone** — that probe's
   `expect = ['exit 0']` passed against a stale predecessor run once already (measured: it printed
   `34586959536` while the branch sat unpushed). One run carries BOTH readings: arm A's live-window module
   lines and arm C's install-SKIPPED line with the driver/runtime pair.

8. **OPERATOR STEP — arm B, the elevated dev-host run. CONDITIONAL, and deliberately last.** Run it only if
   arm C leaves the endpoint closed; if arm C opens it, skew is the cause and elevation is moot, so this arm
   is never paid for. Elevation cannot be self-granted, so /implement requests it and does not perform it.
   From an **elevated PowerShell**, in one session: the full probe script to
   `runs/webview2-probe/control-devhost-elevated.txt` (this is what makes elevation *machine-proven* rather
   than operator-attested — the capture carries the script's own `IsElevatedAdmin` line), then
   `.\scripts\agent-run.ps1 run --e2e` with `CONDUCTOR_A11Y_STRICT=1` and `CONDUCTOR_MSEDGEDRIVER` set,
   output captured. The shell must be PowerShell running the `.ps1` (in PowerShell `bash` resolves to the WSL
   relay and dies — `verification-harness.md` L57a) and must NOT set
   `$PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference`, which destroys the printed verdict the reading is taken from.
   **Capture through a real handle redirection on a child process:** `agent-run.ps1` reports through
   `[Console]::Error.WriteLine`, which writes the raw console handle that a PowerShell `*>` redirect does not
   capture — a first attempt died three seconds in with its error invisible and no sentinel, because the
   script's `exit` terminated the wrapper. Take a `tasklist` census before and after.

9. **Author `evidence/reading.md`.** The graded record: arm A's module reading from the live window beside its
   dev-host control; arm B's elevated reading beside the committed non-elevated one; the run named by id,
   event, branch and conclusion, and the job and its steps named. A probe that returned nothing is recorded as
   having returned nothing. State the conclusion the pair supports and, explicitly, the scope it does not
   reach: a dev-host result bounds dev-host elevation, not the hosted image. Attribute the run's red to the
   standing WebView2 session-creation failure, not to this chunk.

- `conductor-0.3.0/chunks/2026-09-11-hosted-runner-endpoint-cause-closed/evidence/reading.md` — the graded
  record (step 8).

- `scripts/webview2-cause-probe.ps1` — add the `[ValidateSet]` section parameter; make the marker report the
  selection; preserve the default path's behaviour and its `3/3` marker byte-for-byte. Keep the
  `Emit`-into-`$out`-then-dump structure, the `ModuleName` + `FileVersion`-only rule (never `FileName`), the
  provider-probe/`reg.exe`-report split, and the unconditional `exit 0`.

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — inside the `WebView2 session isolation (diagnostic)` step only: the
  module-section invocation in probe (a)'s live window, above the teardown.

**Caller threading:** none. No symbol is added, removed or re-signatured; the change surface is YAML +
PowerShell + Markdown, outside both indexed planes (research §Graph impact). The script's invocations are
`run:`-step calls with literal argv — no registration table, allowlist or manifest. `Cargo.lock` and
`package-lock.json` are untouched, so no dependency delta and no manifest rides this list.

**The PREREQ runs, and is not re-deferred.** `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci` was deferred at
`2026-09-11-hosted-runner-endpoint-cause-probed` under the source-delta rule, and this chunk again ships zero
`.rs` / `Cargo.*` delta — so the rule alone would defer it a second time. The working-route entry's
`PREREQ: close rust gate deferral` is an explicit instruction to discharge it instead, so the entry carries no
`defer` key and runs. Arm B's `--e2e` leg performs a `cargo build --release` regardless, so the compile is not
an added cost. It runs in its arch-pinned form under the zero-retry `ci` profile: a retry-to-green is not a
pass (architecture.md §Infrastructure Patterns — Build system), and `NextestExitCode` 100/101 is a hard fail.

**No `role = 'smoke'` entry, deliberately.** The modify-set is a workflow file, a PowerShell script and a
Markdown record — no boot-path touchpoint — and `verification-harness.md` §Session Additions records that a
chunk with no producing leg takes the template's *omit* arm rather than minting a vacuous smoke to read.

**No `role = 'self-verify'` entry.** The modify-set contains no frontend path, so this is not a UI/visual
chunk. Arm B *is* the headful a11y arm, but it runs here as an operator-gated measurement, not as the chunk's
standing UI gate.

**No standing external-decay PREREQ is folded.** The advisory-database deferral closed at
`2026-09-05-audit-corrective` and was re-measured green at `2026-09-07-dependency-polish` and
`2026-09-10-live-pulse-in-lane-scenario-round`; this chunk has zero dependency delta, so no audit/deny pin is
owed in-plan.

**Arm B has no separate liveness probe, and does not need one.** Its failure mode is a vacuous skip, and
`CONDUCTOR_A11Y_STRICT=1` is what forecloses it: with the handle set and no driven-session banner in the log,
`Assert-A11yVerdict` writes `error: CONDUCTOR_A11Y_STRICT is set but no driven session attached - the leg
proved nothing.` and exits 1, where an unset handle would instead print a skip line and exit 0
(`scripts/agent-run.ps1:70`–`:77`). The subject is a host-tool handle read by `wdio.conf.ts`, not a live
process, so there is no port or process for a non-priming probe to read.

**Two `leg = 'operator'` classes appear below.** Arm B is operator-run because elevation cannot be
self-granted; the CI capture is operator-run because a public run is not the reader's to re-make. /implement
runs each once with its value substituted and records it in the chunk evidence; the wrap never re-runs either.

**`evidence/reading.md` has no producing gate entry, by design** — it is an authored deliverable (step 8),
written from the captures. The runtime artifacts each carry `artifact` on their producing entry, and all of
them land under gitignored `/runs/`.

  `notes` line, exactly as the predecessor did rather than weakening the clause. A claim discharged by wording
  is the failure mode this version exists to retire.

  local gates → arm B → commit → operator push → CI → capture → author `reading.md`. A later edit to `ci.yml`
  or the probe script invalidates a reading already taken; re-push and re-read instead.

- **Arm B's two parts run in ONE elevated session.** Part 1 (the probe capture) is what proves the session was

   require a CI run of committed code; CI fires only on push; /implement reserves committing for wrap. The
   skill correctly refused to commit and surfaced the tension — the same deviation the predecessor recorded.

3. **Arm C was not in the original plan.** It was minted mid-implement on the operator's ruling after arm A's
   reading exposed the version skew. Justification: arm A's own result created a cheaper discriminator than
   arm B, and running the cheap arm first meant arm B's UAC acceptance was only spent once arm C had failed
   to explain the defect.

4. **Arm B ran before its conditional was satisfied in the strict sense.** The plan made arm B conditional on
   arm C leaving the endpoint closed; arm C did leave it closed, so the condition held — recorded because the
   ordering was decided mid-flight rather than at P4.

5. **A first arm-B attempt produced no reading** and is recorded rather than omitted: it died during the
   release build with its error invisible (`[Console]::Error.WriteLine` writes the raw console handle, which a
   PowerShell `*>` redirect does not capture; the script's `exit` killed the wrapper before any sentinel). A
   capture-correct retry (child process, real handle redirection, sentinel) produced the reading.

- **Fix the output, never the anchor** — applied twice this chunk. The committed-reading hygiene gate
  (`[A-Za-z]:[\/]`) fired on a quoted URL scheme (scheme + colon + slash satisfies it), and then again on the
  prose written to explain that false positive, because the explanation spelled the offending tokens. Both
  fixed in the output; the anchor was never loosened, since loosening it would blind the gate to real leaks.
  This is the same class as the `reg.exe` registry-provider rendering found the day before — **n=2 in two
  days** for one anchor.

- **A gate's GREEN case can be vacuous where its RED baseline could not show it.** The install-SKIPPED counter
  baselined red (count 0) on a log where the conditional did not exist, then measured **2** on its first green
  run: GitHub echoes the step source, so the literal appears in the echoed `Write-Output` template as well as
  in the real output. Fixed with a `grep -av Write-Output` stage. The identical trap had been found and fixed
  on a sibling entry earlier in the same authoring pass and was not carried across.

- **Assert the count beside the distinctness.** The skew probe was first written as `sort -u | wc -l`
  expecting one distinct major; baselined against the pre-arm-C log it returned `1` and read GREEN on a log
  that carries the skew, because the reading it half-depends on is introduced by this chunk. Re-authored to
  print `majors: {n} {d}` — a form that cannot pass on a missing reading.

title: A. Module-version probe placed above the teardown

data.head: ### A. Module-version probe placed above the teardown

body:
The subject is a live process. `scripts/webview2-cause-probe.ps1` section (2) enumerates loaded modules of
`msedgewebview2`, `conductor-tauri` and `msedge`, reporting `ModuleName` + `FileVersion` only (never `FileName`,
which is a host path), and treating an `ACCESS DENIED` throw as a reading in its own right.

The window where those processes exist in the `a11y` job is inside the isolation step's arm (a): from the
`Start-Process` of the app (`ci.yml:411`) to the `Stop-Process` that ends it (`ci.yml:422`) — the same window
whose `tasklist` at `10:13:21.76Z` showed `conductor-tauri.exe` plus three `msedgewebview2.exe` alive. The
section must fire inside that window.

- The probe body stays in `scripts/webview2-cause-probe.ps1`. The predecessor's recorded reason binds here:
  the same code must produce the dev-host control the CI reading is compared against, and an inline CI-only
  body can never do that. So this is a **section-selectable invocation of the existing script**, not an inline
  copy and not a second script. *(P3: verified — `architecture.md` §Infrastructure Patterns registers all four
  properties and a second in-workflow invocation preserves them. Sharpened: the selector does NOT exist today;
  the signature is `param([string]$OutFile)`, so adding it is this chunk's work.)*

- **The selector must be a validated, strictly-bound parameter** *(added at P5; planning surfaced it)*. Measured
  on the untouched tree: `powershell.exe -File scripts/webview2-cause-probe.ps1 -Section modules` exits **0**,
  writes nothing to stderr and runs all three sections — a plain `param()` block without `[CmdletBinding()]`
  collects an unknown parameter NAME into `$args` rather than rejecting it. So a section selector that is not
  strictly bound degrades silently to a full run, and any gate keyed on the exit code or on a section-(2) line
  would pass identically with the selector never implemented.

- `[premise-corrected: the completion marker is asserted by NO committed gate — `grep -rn "3/3 sections"` over
  `*.yml` `*.ps1` `*.sh` `*.ts` `*.rs` returns exactly one hit, the emit site at
  `scripts/webview2-cause-probe.ps1:124`. The only assertion ever written is a `[[gate]]` entry in the
  PREDECESSOR chunk's plan fence, which is per-chunk and is not re-run here.]* There is no standing contract to
  break, so the marker's arity is this chunk's to choose. What stays binding is the class rule: this chunk's own
  gate must be unable to pass vacuously, and two markers must not be substring-satisfiable by one another.

- The three-section step at `ci.yml:513` keeps its `continue-on-error: true` + `if: always()` diagnose-only
  posture, and so does anything added inside the isolation step. No probe may move the job's verdict.

title: B. Elevation varied on the dev host

data.head: ### B. Elevation varied on the dev host

body:
The **inverse** of the expensive direction. A hosted step is elevated by construction, so varying elevation on
the runner means de-elevating inside it — a scheduled-task or `runas` token dance whose own failure modes would
then have to be separated from the endpoint's. Elevating the dev host is one run.

- **The non-elevated control already exists and is not re-derived here:** the routine arm over the shipped
  bundle at **12 passing / 2 skipped**, banner `[webview2 152.0.4191.66 windows]`, recorded 2026-09-10
  (`conductor-0.3.0/intent.md:28`; `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-09-10-release-build-and-bundle/report.md:95`).
  The probe's own dev-host capture records `IsElevatedAdmin: False` beside the runner's `True`.

- **The arm:** re-run the routine arm on this host from an **elevated** shell, and capture the probe's own
  elevated dev-host reading beside it.

- **This run is an OPERATOR step.** Elevation cannot be self-granted. The plan names the step; the operator runs
  it; the reading is recorded beside the existing non-elevated one. It is **not** modelled as a gate the
  fix-loop can drive.

- **`CONDUCTOR_A11Y_STRICT=1` is mandatory on arm B** *(added by P3's closure; scope did not state it)*. Without
  it, a run where elevation kills `DevToolsActivePort` yields no driven-session banner and the harness prints
  `[a11y] leg skipped (no driven session)` and **exits 0** (`scripts/agent-run.ps1:70`–`:77`) — byte-identical to
  an unconfigured host. Arm B's entire discriminating power rests on that handle being set.

- **The invoking shell is elevated PowerShell running `scripts/agent-run.ps1`, never `bash scripts/agent-run.sh`**
  — in PowerShell `bash` resolves to the WSL relay and dies (`verification-harness.md` L57a) — and that shell must
  NOT set `$PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference`, which destroys the printed verdict the reading is taken from
  (`ci.yml`'s routine-arm step records the measurement).

- **Both outcomes are deliverables, and the plan states both in advance.** If `DevToolsActivePort` disappears
  under local elevation, elevation is established as the cause with a control on both sides and no CI
  round-trip. If it survives, elevation is **retired** — and only then does a runner-side arm earn its cost.

- The discipline this satisfies is the one the earlier raw-`msedgedriver` probe broke: a probe that has not
  produced the KNOWN-GOOD outcome on the known-good host discriminates nothing. Here the known-good outcome is
  already on record, from the same host, under the one variable being changed.

- Elevation is the surviving candidate cause of the missing endpoint. Carried with the predecessor's own marker
  text verbatim: *"a difference, not a demonstrated cause — no probe varied it, and nothing here says
  de-elevating opens the endpoint."* This chunk's arm B is what tests it; scope does not assume its outcome.
  *(P3: re-derived true at HEAD — `architecture.md` §Established Decisions [CI/CD] carries the cause OPEN with no
  named replacement candidate, and `v3-01`'s notes state elevation as an unvaried difference. Verified as a
  correctly-stated hypothesis, not as a cause.)*

- That a local elevated run reproduces the runner's failure mode *at all* is itself unproven — elevation on the
  dev host and elevation on a hosted image are not self-evidently the same condition (they differ in principal,
  profile and image). A null result from arm B retires elevation **as measured on this host**; the plan must
  state that reach honestly rather than over-claiming a universal retirement. *(P3: verified, and it is
  mandatory rather than merely prudent — a11y-plan §9 CI Integration → Platform requires distinguishing the
  measured platform SET from the CI arrangement, and test-plan §6 carries the 2026-09-08 precedent bounding a
  reading to its host.)*

- **PREREQ (folded from the working entry):** close the rust gate deferral —

title: Boundaries — what this chunk does NOT do

data.head: ## Boundaries — what this chunk does NOT do

body:
- **Does not de-elevate on the runner.** Explicitly deferred: it earns its cost only if arm B leaves elevation
  standing.

- **Does not attempt to fix the endpoint.** The chunk closes a *measurement*. A remediation, if one is
  indicated, is a later route entry.

- **Does not change the job's verdict or the routine arm's logic.** The `a11y` job's pass/fail stays determined
  by the routine arm's printed verdict; every probe stays diagnose-only.
- **Does not re-derive the non-elevated control.** It is committed evidence and is cited, not re-measured.

- **Does not widen the trust boundary.** No new outbound target, no new bind, no new spawned program: the
  governed harness-spawn form count stays at SIX.
- **Does not touch spec masters.** Any spec↔reality gap surfaces at wrap, not here.

`v3-01` — *Hosted-runner cause measured, not listed* (`manual`, `planned`, currently `chunk: null`). Its
acceptance is unedited and stands as written; the predecessor un-claimed it deliberately rather than refining
the clause. This chunk exists to make the measurement whole so the clause can be met. Whether it is claimable
at this chunk's wrap — and on what concretized acceptance — is settled at P5 against the plan that actually
results, not assumed here.

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — the `a11y` job: the isolation step (`:382`–`:512`) and the cause-probe step
  (`:513`–`:517`).

- `scripts/webview2-cause-probe.ps1` — 141 lines, `param([string]$OutFile)`, three sections, completion marker
  at `:124`.
- `conductor-0.3.0/chunks/2026-09-11-hosted-runner-endpoint-cause-closed/evidence/` — the recorded reading.
- `conductor-0.3.0/verification-matrix.json` — `v3-01`.

- **Marker:** 2026-09-11-hosted-runner-endpoint-cause-probed · **Version:** conductor-0.3.0 · **Generated:** 2026-09-11T07:58Z

Measure why the WebView2 remote-debugging endpoint never appears on the hosted `windows-2025` image, by adding
three named one-line probes to the `a11y` job and recording what each returns on a real CI run. The runtime-major
hypothesis is already FALSIFIED — run `34280136892` installed Evergreen 152.0.4191.66 and `DevToolsActivePort`
still never appeared within 90 s with the app alive and three webview children resident — so `architecture.md`
§Established Decisions [CI/CD] holds the cause OPEN with "a hosted-image policy or session property the leading
unmeasured candidate". This chunk is the successor measurement for exactly that candidate pair, plus the third
unmeasured one: what module the host processes actually loaded, as opposed to what EdgeUpdate reports installed.

The deliverable is **the reading, not a fix**. Every probe is diagnose-only (`continue-on-error: true`, exits 0
whatever it finds) and cannot decide the job's verdict — the posture test-plan §9's E2E row and a11y-plan §11 (CI)
both require, and the shape the job's four existing diagnostics already take. A probe that returns nothing is
recorded as having returned nothing; a reading that contradicts the expected cause is recorded unchanged.

The probes live in a **repo script the workflow calls** (operator-selected at the P4 fork), not inline. The reason
is `v3-01`'s second acceptance half: the readings must be "sufficient to decide whether the endpoint failure is
remediable or permanent", which a CI reading alone cannot do — it needs a dev-host control to compare against. A
script produces both readings from the same code, so the control is measured rather than hand-approximated.
Precedent exists in this workflow: `ci.yml` already calls `.\scripts\agent-run.ps1` at `:80` and `:375`.

1. **Create `scripts/webview2-cause-probe.ps1`** — a read-only PowerShell probe printing three labelled sections
   and nothing else. It takes one optional `-OutFile` parameter (a project-root-relative path); when given it
   writes the same text there as well as to stdout. It **always exits 0**, including on an access error.
   - **(1) policy state** — `Test-Path` + `Get-ItemProperty` over the Edge / EdgeUpdate / EdgeWebView policy keys
     in both the machine and user hives. For each key print either `present … value-names: {N}` or `ABSENT`.
     Print the *names* of any values found, never their contents — a policy value can itself be a path.
   - **(2) loaded module versions** — `Get-Process` + `.Modules` over `msedgewebview2`, reporting each matching
     module's `ModuleName` and `FileVersionInfo.FileVersion`. `.Modules` can throw Access Denied for a process
     owned by another account: catch it and print `ACCESS DENIED` as the reading. Report `no live process` when
     none is running. Print module NAMES and versions only, never `FileName`.
   - **(3) session identity** — `[System.Diagnostics.Process]::GetCurrentProcess().SessionId`,
     `[Environment]::UserInteractive`, and `[Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent()`'s
     `AuthenticationType` / `IsSystem` / `IsAuthenticated`, plus the Administrator role via `WindowsPrincipal`.
     **Read no environment variable** — see Constraints.
   - End with the literal line `[probe] complete: 3/3 sections`, which is the gate's assertion target.

2. **Add one step to the `a11y` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`**, named `WebView2 cause probes (diagnostic)`,
   carrying `if: always()` + `continue-on-error: true` + `shell: pwsh`, whose body is
   `.\scripts\webview2-cause-probe.ps1`. Place it immediately **after** the existing `WebView2 session isolation
   (diagnostic)` step and **before** `Upload session diagnostics`, so its output rides the same diagnostic block.
   Change no existing step's logic, ordering, `if:`, or `continue-on-error` posture.

3. **Produce the dev-host control** by running the probe locally into
   `runs/webview2-probe/control-devhost.txt` (the `role = 'probe'` gate entry below). This is the known-good side of the
   comparison: on this host `DevToolsActivePort` appears in ~1 s.

4. **Commit, then push `build/conductor-0.3.0`.** `ci.yml` triggers on `on: push:` with no branch filter
   (`ci.yml:3-5`), so the push starts all three jobs. **The push is the operator's act** — /implement requests it
   and does not perform it unasked.

5. **Read the run** — capture the run's log to `runs/webview2-probe/a11y-job.log` via the `leg = 'operator'` entry, then
   assert the probe markers are present in it.

6. **Author `evidence/reading.md`** — the recorded reading. For each of the three probes: what the hosted runner
   returned, beside the dev-host control value, and a one-line statement of what the pair does or does not
   establish. Record a probe that returned nothing as having returned nothing. Record a reading that contradicts
   the expected cause unchanged. Identify the job and steps BY NAME (never by `ci.yml` line coordinate) and state
   the run by id / event / branch / conclusion. Attribute the run's red to the standing WebView2
   session-creation failure, not to this chunk. Draw no green, conformance, or platform-capability claim.
- `scripts/webview2-cause-probe.ps1` — the three read-only probes; prints labelled `[diag]` lines, always exit 0.

- `conductor-0.3.0/chunks/2026-09-11-hosted-runner-endpoint-cause-probed/evidence/reading.md` — the recorded
  reading; the `v3-01` `ref`. **Committed.** Authored by step 6 from the two raw captures below.

**Raw captures — gitignored, never committed** (`.gitignore:17` `/runs/`; the SR leg's established split, where
the raw third-party artifact stays under `runs/` and only the graded record is committed):
- `runs/webview2-probe/control-devhost.txt` — the dev-host control capture (produced by a gate entry).

- `runs/webview2-probe/a11y-job.log` — the captured CI run log (produced by the operator entry; ~1.7 MB, which is
  why it is a capture and not an evidence file).

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — ADD one diagnostic step to the `a11y` job (step 2). No existing step changes. No
  caller threading applies: the chunk changes no symbol, no signature, and needs no code-side allowlist or
  registry entry. (The env-registration obligation is a spec-master entry → an Expected amendment, never a
  touchpoint.)

This chunk ships **zero compiled-source delta** — no `.rs` file is touched — so the workspace compile gate is a
`defer` entry per /implement's source-delta rule. There is **no live-Pulse leg**: the chunk drives no external
process of the SUT kind, so no `leg = 'live'` entry and no Pulse liveness probe exists. The CI run is a
`leg = 'operator'` entry — a public CI run is not the reader's to re-run, so /implement runs it once with the
minted run id substituted and the wrap never re-runs it.

**No standing external-decay PREREQ is folded here.** The advisory-database deferral that rode every chunk
through 2026-09-05 is CLOSED (`security.md` §Session Additions, closed at `2026-09-05-audit-corrective`), and
this chunk has zero dependency delta — `Cargo.lock` is untouched — so no audit/deny pin is owed in-plan.

**`evidence/reading.md` has no producing gate entry, by design.** It is an *authored* deliverable (step 6), not
runtime output: /implement writes it from the two raw captures. The two genuine runtime artifacts —
`runs/webview2-probe/control-devhost.txt` and `runs/webview2-probe/a11y-job.log` — each carry `artifact` on the
entry that produces them, and both land under gitignored `runs/` so no raw capture enters the tree.

body:
- (v3-01) A recorded reading exists in `evidence/reading.md` for **each of the three named probes** — policy
  state, loaded module versions, session identity — stating what was found on the hosted runner rather than what
  was suspected; a probe that returned nothing is recorded as having returned nothing rather than omitted, and a
  reading that contradicts the expected cause is recorded unchanged. Each hosted-runner reading is recorded
  **beside its dev-host control value** from `runs/webview2-probe/control-devhost.txt`, so the pair is sufficient to decide
  whether the endpoint failure is remediable or permanent (`verification-matrix.json#v3-01`).

- (arch) Each added step carries `continue-on-error: true`, and no existing step's logic, ordering, `if:`, or
  `continue-on-error` posture changes — the WebView2 install gate in particular keeps no `continue-on-error` and
  no `if:` (per `architecture.md` §Established Decisions [CI/CD]).

- (arch) The job introduces no second non-loopback outbound target and binds no port; §Occupied Resources —
  Ports' CI-scoped egress set stays at exactly one entry (per `architecture.md` §Occupied Resources — Ports).

- (arch) The `a11y` job stays on the explicit `windows-2025` label and the WebView2 runtime stays FLOATED — a
  probe-only chunk does not meet the float's recorded exit condition (per `architecture.md` §Infrastructure
  Patterns — Build system).

- (security) The governed harness-spawn form count remains SIX: no probe constructs a child process (per
  security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Code Patterns rule (b)).

- (security) The WebView2 fetch and `Install WebView2 Evergreen runtime 152+ (gate)` steps still carry no
  `continue-on-error`, still perform the `Get-AuthenticodeSignature` check before the binary runs, and still
  assert the runtime-major ≥ 152 floor (per security-plan §Dependency Security, third dependency class).

- (obs/security/tests/a11y) Zero absolute host paths in the committed reading — proven by the
  `grep -cE "[A-Za-z]:[\\/]|…" … evidence/reading.md` entry reading `0`, not asserted (per obs-plan §9 Log
  conformance check + §11 Logs; security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Logging; test-plan §3; a11y-plan §11 SLO).

- (obs) An absent registry key or unreadable value is recorded as an explicit absent/denied reading rather than
  omitted — the assertion is key presence, not a non-null value (per obs-plan §6 Required fields).

- (obs) The new step mints no span, adds no `tracing` line, and creates no new telemetry-artifact path; the
  `logs/agent-latest.jsonl` and `runs/a11y/<run_id>.jsonl` uploads and the in-job conformance assertion are
  unchanged (per obs-plan §1 instrumentation-scope CI row + §9).

- (a11y/tests) The probes are diagnose-only: the job's pass/fail stays determined by the routine arm's fail-fast
  verdict, and the `CONDUCTOR_A11Y_STRICT` + printed-verdict mechanism is unperturbed (per a11y-plan §11 CI;
  test-plan §9 Pipeline structure). `Assert-A11yVerdict` parses wdio output captured to `$RunsDir/a11y-e2e.log`,
  a different stream from the job log the probes print to.

- (a11y) The reading identifies the job and its steps BY NAME, states the run by id/event/branch/conclusion, and
  attributes the run's red to the standing WebView2 session-creation failure rather than to this chunk — with no
  green, conformance, or platform-capability claim drawn from a probe (per a11y-plan §3 Configuration, §9
  Platform, §11 Strategy).
- (tests) `bash scripts/agent-run.sh status` returns 0 and the workflow still parses to exactly the three jobs.

- Research files inspected: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.andromeda/architecture.md` §Occupied Resources,
  `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/wdio.conf.ts`, `scripts/agent-run.ps1`,
  `crates/conductor-run/tests/journal_conformance.rs`, `.claude/rules/verification-harness.md` (index).

- **Inline probe bodies in `ci.yml`** — rejected at the P4 operator fork: a CI-only form cannot produce the
  dev-host control that `v3-01`'s "sufficient to decide remediable or permanent" half requires.

- **A fourth probe for the `:4444` tauri-driver bind race** — rejected: re-derived at HEAD as a Conductor-side
  code defect (`wdio.conf.ts:405` spawns the driver in `onPrepare` and returns with no readiness wait, while
  `startNvda` at `:199-235` polls a real signal for 30 s). It needs a fix, not a measurement.

- **Fixing that `:4444` race here** — rejected: outside this chunk's diagnose-only boundary. Recorded with its
  mechanism and coordinates for `v3-02` or its own route entry.

- **Any probe that reads an environment variable** — rejected: `ci.yml` already reads `$env:TEMP` and
  `$env:LOCALAPPDATA` without registering them (see Expected amendments); the .NET session APIs answer probe (3)
  with no env read, so this chunk adds nothing to that gap and incurs no new registration obligation.

- **A spawn-based probe** (`query session`, `whoami`, a second driver) — rejected: it would be a seventh governed
  harness-spawn crossing, which security-plan states never becomes routine, and a11y-plan §11 (CI) separately
  bans a second browser-automation stack.

- **Relying on `conductor-core::redact`** for the workflow channel — rejected: a YAML step reaches none of the
  three redaction application sites, so the scrub must be intrinsic to the probe (obs-plan §11 PII Scrubbing).

- **Printing a policy value, a module `FileName`, or a handle value** — rejected: report presence/shape/version
  only, per the `Test-Path`-boolean idiom the job already uses.

- **Ordering is load-bearing.** The reading must cite a run of the code **as committed**, so the sequence is:
  implement → local gates green → commit → operator pushes → CI runs → capture the log → author `reading.md`. A
  later edit to `ci.yml` or the probe script invalidates a reading already taken; re-push and re-read instead.

- **`.Modules` may throw Access Denied** on the runner for a process owned by another account. The probe catches
  it and records `ACCESS DENIED` — which is itself a reading, and a discriminating one (it would say the job runs
  under an account that cannot inspect the webview host).

- **A SIXTH failing run exists that `v3-01`'s `observed_gap` does not name.** That field enumerates
  `34162118841 / 34251573399 / 34256490781 / 34280136892 / 34365300658`; `gh run list --workflow ci.yml --limit 5`
  on 2026-09-11 shows **`34535095643` (failure, `build/conductor-0.2.0`)** newer than all of them. Read it
  alongside the new probe run — it may already carry a changed failure mode, and a reading that assumes the
  enumeration is current would be one run stale.

- **`gh run view <id> --log` exits 0 on a FAILED run** (validated 2026-09-11 against run `34365300658`, 1.66 MB
  captured, exit 0), so the operator entry's default `expect = 'exit 0'` is correct and the run's red conclusion
  does not red the gate.

- **The run will be RED.** The routine arm's pre-existing failure stands; research re-derived its current cause
  (the `:4444` bind race) as structurally real at HEAD. Record that red as pre-existing, never as a regression,

Three **named one-line probes** added to the `a11y` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, run on the hosted
`windows-2025` image, plus a **recorded reading** of what each returned on a real CI run.

> **Amended at P4/P5 (intent-incomplete, operator-ratified):** the probe *bodies* live in a new repo script,
> `scripts/webview2-cause-probe.ps1`, which the job's new step calls — not inline in `ci.yml` as this scope
> originally assumed. The reason is this capability's own acceptance: the readings must be sufficient to decide
> *remediable vs permanent*, which needs a dev-host control produced by the **same code** as the CI reading.
> An inline body can only ever run in CI. `ci.yml` already calls `.\scripts\agent-run.ps1` at `:80` and `:375`,
> so the shape is the workflow's own precedent. The probes answer the
three candidates that `v3-01`'s `observed_gap` names as UNMEASURED — none of which any prior run has probed:

1. **Policy state** — the WebView2 / Edge policy the image carries. A registry read of the Edge and WebView2
   policy keys (machine and user hives), reporting each value found and explicitly reporting the absence of a
   key rather than omitting it. The residual names this "the one-line probe".

2. **Module versions actually loaded** — the module version the *host processes* loaded, as distinct from the
   `EdgeUpdate` client `pv` registry value the existing install gate asserts. The install gate proves what was
   *installed*; it says nothing about what `msedgewebview2.exe` actually mapped. [verified P3] — the two
   sources are genuinely distinct and both readable: `Get-Process msedgewebview2 | .Modules` returned
   `msedgewebview2.exe` / `msedge_elf.dll` at `FileVersion 152.0.4191.66` across 6 live processes on the dev
   host, while the install gate reads EdgeUpdate's `pv` value.

3. **Session identity** — whether the runner's process runs in an interactive session with a window station and
   desktop, or in a service/session-0 context. [verified P3] — the property set is measurable and was measured
   on the dev host: `SessionId 1` · `UserInteractive True` · `AuthenticationType CloudAP` · `IsSystem False` ·
   `IsAuthenticated True` · elevated `False`.

Each probe is **diagnose-only**: `continue-on-error: true`, exits 0 whatever it finds, and can never decide the
gate. This matches the two diagnostics already in the job (`WebView2 driver + runtime versions`, `WebView2
session isolation`) and is the shape the job's own comments state for a diagnostic.

The deliverable is the **reading**, not a fix: a recorded artifact stating what each probe returned on the
hosted runner, including probes that returned nothing, and including any reading that contradicts the expected
cause — recorded unchanged.

title: What this chunk does NOT build

data.head: ## What this chunk does NOT build

body:
- **No fix and no remediation.** Whether the endpoint failure is remediable is what the readings decide; acting
  on that decision is not this chunk.

- **No change to the a11y gate's verdict, assertions, or terminal.** That is `v3-02` (Epoch 3), which this
  chunk feeds. The routine arm stays exactly as it is.
- **No change to the routine arm's spec set, the strict-mode guard, or the conformance gate.**

- **No WebView2 runtime pin disposition.** `v3-02`'s `notes` explicitly folds that into `v3-02`, gated on the
  terminal fork — not here.

- **No console-footer / landmark work.** `v3-02`'s second folded obligation; a surface 0.3.0 deliberately does
  not build.

- **No local-host work.** The subject is the hosted image. A dev-host reading is useful only as the known-good
  control a probe is validated against before it is pushed (see Constraints).
| Surface | Nature of the touch |
| `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — `a11y` job | ADD one diagnostic step only. No existing step's logic, ordering, or `continue-on-error` posture changes. |

| `scripts/webview2-cause-probe.ps1` | NEW (P4 amendment) — the three read-only probe bodies; always exit 0. First script in `scripts/` that is neither harness variant, so `architecture.md`'s directory tree gains an entry at wrap. |
| `conductor-0.3.0/chunks/{marker}/evidence/reading.md` | NEW — the recorded reading, COMMITTED (the `v3-01` `ref`). |
| `runs/webview2-probe/` | NEW, **gitignored** — the raw captures (dev-host control + the ~1.7 MB CI log). The SR leg's split: raw stays under `runs/`, only the graded record is committed. |
| `contracts/`, `crates/`, `scenarios/` | UNTOUCHED. This chunk ships no Rust and no scenario change. |

- **Artifact hygiene.** No absolute host path may reach the job log or the recorded reading. The job's existing
  diagnostics state this rule inline ("Handle NAME + state only, never the path"; "Leaf names only, never a
  path"); new probes follow it, and a policy *value* that is itself a path is reported by presence/shape, not
  verbatim. (CLAUDE.md universal invariant; `security-plan.md` §Error Handling.)

- **Harness-spawn rule (b).** `security.md` governs SIX spawn forms across THREE loci, `ci.yml` among them, and
  states "a seventh crossing escalates again — this class never becomes routine." A probe that reads the
  registry or process state is not a spawn; a probe that launches a program is. [verified P3] — **none of the
  three probes needs a spawn.** All three run on cmdlets and .NET only (`Test-Path` + `Get-ItemProperty`;
  `Get-Process` + `.Modules`; `[System.Diagnostics.Process]::GetCurrentProcess()` +
  `[Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]`), measured end-to-end on the dev host at exit 0. The governed form
  count stays at SIX and no operator escalation is owed.

- **A diagnostic can never gate.** `a11y-plan` §11 bans a gate that passes by skipping; symmetrically the job's
  own comments state a diagnostic "exits 0 whatever it finds, so it can never itself decide the gate."

- **Probe validity before belief.** CLAUDE.md's 2026-09-07 learning: a probe that fails where the real path
  passes is evidence about the probe. Each probe is validated against the dev host (a known-good path) before
  its reading from CI is trusted — the `browserName: "webview2"` omission is the measured precedent.

title: The lifecycle question this chunk must answer at planning time

data.head: ## The lifecycle question this chunk must answer at planning time

body:
`v3-01`'s acceptance requires **a reading from the hosted runner** — which exists only after a push triggers a
CI run. `ci.yml` has `on: push:` with **no branch filter** (`ci.yml:3-5`), so a push of `build/conductor-0.3.0` does
trigger all three jobs; the run is therefore reachable inside this chunk rather than owed to a later one.
[verified P3] — the trigger is measured from the file and the branch carries no exclusion. Two facts shape how:
- The push is an **operator-authorized act**, and the branch currently has **no upstream**.

- The `a11y` job is **already red** for a pre-existing reason (the residual records the routine arm's red having
  moved to tauri-driver never listening on `:4444` — four refused POSTs inside ~1.5 s against a 6.9 s driver
  bind, present in runs 34162118841 / 34251573399 / 34256490781 at runtime 151, predating both the upgrade and
  any driver skew). A red CI run after this chunk's push is that standing red, not a regression this chunk
  introduced, and the plan must say so explicitly so the run is not misread.

title: The `:4444` question — RESOLVED at P3, no fourth probe

data.head: ## The `:4444` question — RESOLVED at P3, no fourth probe

body:
The residual `2026-09-09-workspace-formatting-pass-and-a-fmt-ci-gate` (absorbed as `v3-02`) carries a **fourth**
finding beside the three candidates: the routine arm's red having moved to the `:4444` tauri-driver bind race.
That claim **re-derives structurally TRUE at HEAD** — `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/wdio.conf.ts:405` spawns
tauri-driver in `onPrepare` and returns immediately, with **no readiness wait on the `:4444` bind**; the only
wait in the file's session path is the `before:` hook (`:416`), which runs *after* WebdriverIO has already
POSTed to that port. The asymmetry is visible in the same file: `startNvda` (`:199-235`) polls NVDA's own
"NVDA initialized" log line for 30 s with a comment stating why a sleep is wrong, while the driver spawn has
neither poll nor sleep.

**Resolution: it earns NO probe here.** The race is a Conductor-side code defect in `wdio.conf.ts`, not a
property of the hosted image, and it is already diagnosed by reading the file — it needs a **fix** (a readiness
wait on the driver's bind, in the shape `startNvda` already models), which is outside this chunk's
diagnose-only boundary. It is recorded here with its mechanism and coordinates so `v3-02` or its own entry can
take it up. Adding a fourth probe would measure something no longer in question.

- **Marker:** 2026-09-12-ledger-gate-id-space-generalised · **Version:** conductor-0.3.0 · **Generated:** 2026-09-12T13:02:00Z

`crates/conductor-report/tests/matrix_ledger_gate.rs` asserts, over every version directory carrying both
ledger files, that `requirements.md` and `verification-matrix.json` declare the same id set, that the matrix's
ids are unique, and that no Pulse `P-NNN` sits in an id position. Its module header (`:13-16`) records that the
version directories are resolved BY SCAN rather than named, because "a baked `conductor-0.2.0` would silently
stop covering the ledger at 0.3.0, which is the failure mode this gate exists to prevent." One line then bakes
the **id space** anyway — `:49` filters `requirement_ids` by `starts_with("v2-")` — so at `conductor-0.3.0`'s
eleven `v3-` ids the required set is empty and the gate's own anti-vacuity assertion fires. The failure the
header claims the design prevents arrives one axis over.

This chunk generalises the id-space predicate so coverage tracks every version on the same basis the directory
scan already does, and `conductor-0.4.0` needs no edit here. It owns the RED workspace gate — 906 run / 905
passed / 1 failed — that landed in `b3b51e6` and was dispositioned not-theirs by the two chunks since.

The predicate is a **lexical shape**, not a prefix list, per the project's standing de-hardcoding ruling: when
the accepted P-ID set outgrew its compile-time `(1..=60)` bound, the operator's ruling was to de-hardcode
rather than substitute the newer literal, "precisely so the next transition needs no edit" (per architecture.md
§Established Decisions [Accepted Capability Set]; test-plan §1 Critical Path 6 and §6 forbid the literal-count
form for the same reason, and §6 Selector strategy states the rule directly — name the SET, because "a new
literal re-stales on the next SUT release"). Substituting `v3-` for `v2-` would reproduce the defect on a
three-month timer; enumerating `{v2-, v3-}` reinstates the class the ruling retired.

The filter is load-bearing and must not simply be deleted: `requirements.md` bolds prose titles beside declared
ids (0.3.0 declares 14 such list items for 11 ids, 0.2.0 33 for 32, and 0.1.0 bolds a title in all 31), and
`requirements.md` is immutable, so the whole repair lives in the gate.

1. **Add the version-capability id predicate beside `is_pulse_p_id`.** In
   `crates/conductor-report/tests/matrix_ledger_gate.rs`, immediately adjacent to `is_pulse_p_id` (`:90-95`),
   add a sibling free function taking `&str` and returning `bool`, accepting exactly: the literal `v`, then
   one or more ASCII digits, then `-`, then one or more ASCII digits, and nothing else. Mirror
   `is_pulse_p_id`'s existing structure — `strip_prefix` + a non-empty check + `bytes().all(|b|
   b.is_ascii_digit())` — so the two id-space predicates read as a matched pair and the separation the gate
   asserts is visible in the code itself. No regex, no new dependency (see Constraints).

2. **Replace the baked filter at `:49` with a call to that predicate.** `requirement_ids`'s
   `.filter(|id| id.starts_with("v2-"))` becomes a filter on the new predicate. This is the only filter site:
   research confirmed both the anti-vacuity assertion (`:151-154`) and the set-equality arm consume
   `Ledger.requirement_ids`, populated by the single `requirement_ids(&markdown)` call at `:135`, so one change
   serves both consumers and the "one shared basis" pattern holds (per architecture.md §Occupied Resources).

3. **Re-word the anti-vacuity message at `:153`.** It currently reads "declares no v2-NN capability". Replace
   the `v2-NN` token with a version-agnostic naming of the version-capability id space. Keep the sentence's
   two existing jobs intact: it names the file by `{label}/requirements.md`, and it states that the gate would
   otherwise pass vacuously. Render ids and file names only — no path (per security-plan §Security
   Anti-Patterns → Logging).

4. **Re-word the id-space assertion message at `:208`.** It currently reads "the v2-NN and P-NNN id spaces
   must stay visibly separate, with P-IDs confined to acceptance text". Generalise the version-space half to
   the same version-agnostic naming used in step 3, and **keep the separation contract stated** — that clause
   is the contract this gate exists to hold and the one `refs/`'s capability spec shares (per architecture.md
   §Conventions — Naming patterns).

5. **Extend the module header's de-hardcoding paragraph (`:13-16`).** That paragraph explains why the version
   DIRECTORIES are resolved by scan. Add the id-space axis beside it: the id predicate is a shape, not a
   prefix literal, for the same reason and against the same failure mode. State it as the rule, not as a list
   of the versions that exist today.

6. **Extend `the_gate_discriminates` so it proves the new predicate.** The existing arm is green at HEAD
   *because* its fixtures are `v2-`-shaped, so it currently proves nothing about the repair. Drive
   `requirement_ids` with fixtures covering exactly these four cases, each asserted:
   - a fixture declaring one `v2-NN` and one `v3-NN` id in the bolded list-item form → BOTH extracted, in
     order (this is the cross-version case the whole chunk exists for, and the one a prefix literal fails);
   - a fixture whose bolded first token is a prose title of the shape `requirements.md` actually carries
     (e.g. a back-ticked name followed by prose) → NOT extracted;
   - a fixture whose bolded first token is a Pulse `P-NNN` → NOT extracted, so the two id spaces stay disjoint
     at the requirements side too;
   - the existing prose-mention case at `:221` (an id named in prose, not in the declaring form) → still not
     extracted. Keep this assertion; only its `v2-01` token may stay or change, it tests the declaring form.
   Add direct assertions on the new predicate itself for the same accept/reject set, mirroring the existing
   `is_pulse_p_id` assertions at `:250-252` (accepts `v2-01` and `v3-11`; rejects a bare `v`, a missing
   number on either side, and a `P-NNN`).

7. **Leave the id-space-agnostic fixtures unchanged.** `:228` (`id_positions` JSON), `:250` (the
   `is_pulse_p_id` negative case) and `:256`/`:257`/`:259`/`:260` (`set_difference`) exercise helpers that
   carry no id-space knowledge; their `v2-01`-style strings are arbitrary data. Do not churn them.
   `:2`'s `v2-21` provenance citation is a historical fact and stays.

8. **Do not touch any ledger data.** No `requirements.md` and no `verification-matrix.json` is edited — the
   data is correct and the gate reading it was wrong (per test-plan §7 Test data lifecycle: no test writes or
   normalises the artifacts it reads).
- none.

- `crates/conductor-report/tests/matrix_ledger_gate.rs` — the entire modify-set. Adds one predicate fn;
  changes one filter; re-words two assertion messages; extends the module header and
  `the_gate_discriminates`. Impact is closed: the code-graph impact query returns **25 call edges, every one
  inside this file** (`.andromeda/runs/2026-09-12T10-52-00-phase/tree-query-…-impact.json`, `rows: 25`,
  `db_state: fresh`, plane `rust`), and `requirement_ids @ matrix_ledger_gate.rs:135,147,218,221` is its
  complete caller set. Zero cross-file and zero cross-crate callers; no re-export, no registration site, and
  no other test pins this data.

The gates /implement runs. **Absences, with reasons:** no `smoke` entry — this chunk changes no boot path and
the project's boot smoke is /implement P3, not a gate here. No `self-verify` entry — there is no UI or visual
delta (the extracts for design, layouts and a11y all returned `No domain coverage`). No `e2e`/`leg = 'live'`
entry and therefore no `role = 'probe'` liveness guard — the gate is a static target over committed artifacts
with no live Pulse, no stub and no `runs.db` (per test-plan §4). The supply-chain probes are listed
unconditionally per the project's standing dependency-gate rule even though this chunk expects a zero
dependency delta.
