body:
- (a11y) The a11y job's terminal is closed on ONE of the two arms `verification-matrix.json#v3-02` names,
  decided by the a11y-job conclusion the CI-reading probe entry resolved **for the run id it pinned by
  `headSha`** — never left as a red job carrying a green-looking coverage claim (per a11y-plan §11
  Anti-Patterns → CI). The criterion rests on that run id; `evidence/ci-terminal-reading.md` is the step-7/8
  write-up of it, not a gate-produced artifact.

- (a11y) **Met in mechanism locally; the CI run is the operator's act.** The routine arm's verdict stays
  honest by mechanism: `CONDUCTOR_A11Y_STRICT` remains set on the asserting step (asserted by the probe entry
  below) and `Assert-A11yVerdict`'s three assertions — driven-session banner, `Spec Files:` failed count,
  skip tally against the unchanged expected set of two — remain the basis of any **exit-zero** run.
  **Reach, read at P5 (`agent-run.ps1:269-276`):** `Assert-A11yVerdict` is invoked only after
  `if ($e2eRc -ne 0) { … exit $e2eRc }`, so a non-zero wdio exit short-circuits to the raw exit code and the
  three assertions do NOT run. That is the safe direction — a non-zero exit is already red and cannot become
  a false pass — and the assertions cover exactly the dangerous one, an exit-zero run that asserted nothing.
  The criterion is worded to that reach and claims no more (per a11y-plan §11 Anti-Patterns → CI; test-plan
  §3 `run --e2e` CI stage selectors).

- (arch) The step carrying the a11y verdict has no `continue-on-error` and no `if:`, asserted by the probe
  entry `python … 'A11y routine arm' … last line True` (per arch §Established Decisions [CI/CD]).

- (security) No shell string, `Invoke-Expression` or composed command line appears in any launch path added
  to the `a11y` job; every program is fixed and every supplied value is a separate array-form argv element.
  If the change constitutes a **seventh** governed harness-spawn form it is NAMED as such in the report and
  operator-ratified at wrap, never routine-applied (per security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Code
  Patterns rule (b)).

- (security) The `CONDUCTOR_A11Y_STRICT` strict arm is not disabled and `nativeDriver()` / `nvdaExe()` /
  their `UNSAFE_PATH` checks are byte-unchanged, asserted by the `git diff --quiet` probe entry (per
  security-plan §Input Validation, `CONDUCTOR_A11Y_STRICT` row).

- (security/obs) Every committed `evidence/` record carries 0 absolute host paths — asserted by the
  `test -d … evidence && ! grep -rqE …` probe entry, whose subject exists because step 1 creates it. The
  a11y job's console output and the uploaded session diagnostics carry none either, and each new
  precondition line prints a handle NAME plus a boolean or version, never a resolved path; **that CI-side
  half is not locally greppable and rests on prose, not on a listed entry** (per security-plan §Security
  Anti-Patterns → Logging; obs-plan §9 Log conformance check).

- (security) The WebView2 float is dispositioned in this chunk — pinned if the job gates, retired if the CI
  half is excluded — and the `>= 152` floor assertion stays OUTSIDE any fetch conditional (per security-plan
  §Dependency Security, third dependency class; `verification-matrix.json#v3-02` notes (1)).

- (design/layouts) Whichever arm ships mints no new lamp state, `ReportState`, bracket label, ANSI entry or
  design token; a run-level qualifier, if any, rides outside the lamp column with its ASCII label always
  printed (per design-system §Iconography + §cli Tokens; layout-templates §Surface: cli — Primary content
  block 2).

- (tests) If outcome (B): the exclusion is recorded as a flagged zone naming its measured cause, its source
  and its owner — never an invented driver, never a manual/operator verification step, never a lowered or
  skipped gate (per test-plan §1 Untestable zones; §11 Universal + §11 Quality).

- (obs) The a11y violation record and its in-job `journal_conformance` check are unaffected by the launch
  change: the record still lands under `runs/a11y/` carrying the §9 resource attributes, and a re-parented
  or token-dropped process does not strip them (per obs-plan §9 CI Integration → Telemetry artifact handling).

- Spec anchors: arch §Established Decisions [CI/CD] · §Occupied Resources (Environment variables, Ports,
  On-disk artifacts) · §Cross-cutting Patterns (Scope law, Trust boundary) — security-plan §Input Validation ·
  §Dependency Security · §Security Anti-Patterns (Code Patterns rule (b), Logging, Universal) — test-plan §1
  Untestable zones · §3 `run --e2e` · §9 Pipeline structure · §10 Zero-flakiness · §11 — a11y-plan §3 · §9 ·
  §10 SLO invariants · §11 Anti-Patterns (CI, SLO) + §11 Strategy CARVE-OUT — obs-plan §3 · §6 · §9 · §10 ·
  §11 — design-system §Color Palette (Verdict-vs-ReportState) · §Iconography · §cli Tokens · §Anti-Patterns —
  layout-templates §Surface: cli (Primary screens, Primary content block 2, Footer/error output, IA notes).

- Research files inspected: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` · `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/wdio.conf.ts` ·
  `scripts/agent-run.ps1` · `scripts/agent-run.sh` · `.config/nextest.toml` ·
  `conductor-0.3.0/chunks/2026-09-11-hosted-runner-endpoint-cause-closed/{evidence/reading.md,plan.md}` ·
  `scripts/code-graph-cookbook.md` · `.claude/rules/verification-harness.md` (in full, structural) ·
  CI run 35079315258 log + its `a11y-session-diag` artifact.

- **Dropping the token at the wdio spawn site — rejected.** `wdio.conf.ts:405` is three levels above the app
  in the measured chain (msedgedriver launches it), so a drop there leaves node/wdio elevated and complicates
  attribution for no gain. The step-level drop covers every descendant with one change.

- **A `runas` form that prompts for credentials — rejected.** The headless invariant forbids an interactive
  prompt on the agent-driven path (layout-templates §Surface: cli — IA notes); a credential prompt would
  silently break the release gate. The mechanism must be non-interactive.

- **Reaching outcome (B) by relaxing the gate — rejected, and forbidden by three extracts independently.**
  No `continue-on-error` on the asserting step, no disabling of the strict arm, no touching the handle guards.

- **Concretizing `v3-02`'s acceptance into the token-drop clause — rejected.** The decisive premise (does the
  drop produce the endpoint?) is exactly what this chunk measures, so clauses downstream of it would be
  WEAKER than the outcome they replace. The acceptance is already concrete about the printed verdict and the
  counts, and research confirms `Assert-A11yVerdict` implements precisely that — so it is **premise-checked,
  not re-worded**, and stays outcome-level across the fork.

- **A second browser-automation stack (puppeteer / CDP attach) to obtain a session — banned** (a11y-plan §11
  Anti-Patterns → CI + §3 tool pick; arch §Cross-cutting Patterns Scope law).

- **An inbound listener in a shipped binary to expose the endpoint — banned** (security-plan §Security
  Anti-Patterns → Universal; the `4444`/`4445` carve-out does not extend to `conductor-tauri`).

- **The landmark obligation is MEASURED, not promised.** `v3-02` notes (2) requires measuring whether the
  routine specs pass against the console as it stands before promising a green terminal. They do: the routine
  arm measured **12 passing / 2 skipped** on the non-elevated dev host (2026-09-10, cited at
  `2026-09-11-hosted-runner-endpoint-cause-closed/evidence/reading.md:147` and in `v3-02`'s own
  `observed_gap`), and the console is unchanged since — derivation:
  `git log --oneline --since=2026-09-10 -- crates/conductor-tauri/ui/src crates/conductor-tauri/ui/test`
  returns **0 commits**, and `grep -rn 'contentinfo' crates/conductor-tauri/ui/src` returns **0 hits**. So the
  unshipped footer is not a second cause of red today: the arm passed without a `contentinfo` landmark.

- **A captured `runs/a11y-e2e.log` is UTF-16** (`agent-run.ps1:270` writes it with `*>`), and grep returns
  ZERO on it without decoding — an implausible zero on a non-empty capture is the signal
  (`verification-harness.md:66`). Any new assertion over that capture decodes first.

- **GitHub Actions echoes each step's own source into the job log**, so a literal inside a `Write-Output "…"`
  template appears TWICE; the tell is the unexpanded `$var`, the fix a `| grep -av 'Write-Output'` stage
  (`verification-harness.md:66`). Verified live this pass on run 35079315258. Any gate that COUNTS
  occurrences in a job log needs the filter AND a hand-check of the first green run's hit list — a red
  baseline validates only the failing direction.

- **Prediction to MEASURE, not to restate.** The plan predicts the limited-token launch produces
  `DevToolsActivePort` and the arm reaches its assertions. This is an experiment on a cause established by
  variation but whose mechanism is unestablished — record what the run measures when it disagrees, and take
  the (B) arm rather than re-tuning toward a green.

- **Separate the token dance's own failure modes from the endpoint's** — the risk the prior chunk named when
  it deferred this arm (`…/plan.md:371-375`). A red run that fails at the scheduled-task launch rather than at
  session creation is a THIRD outcome, distinct from both (A) and (B): it is a defect in this chunk's own
  mechanism, to fix, not an exclusion to ratify.

  three sites that together carry the hosted-runner verdict must move together (the 2026-09-11 amendment

- Expected amendments (wrap): `a11y-plan.md` §1 CI integration · §9 Platform/Pipeline integration · §11 CI —

- Expected amendments (wrap): `security-plan.md` §Dependency Security — the WebView2 float's disposition

- Expected amendments (wrap): `architecture.md` §Established Decisions [CI/CD] · §Occupied Resources — the
  a11y job's step set and any new handle; applied as SET-naming per playbook `:127`, never a fresh count.

**Gates** (by `run` text, in order):

- `python … 'A11y routine arm' … continue-on-error/if/strict` — **green** (`last line True`)

body: - **`nativeDriver`** — 1 call site (`wdio.conf.ts:353`); definition `:55`. Local to the config.
- **`exitUnresolvedHandle`** — 2 call sites (`wdio.conf.ts:356`, `:384`); calls `strictMode` (`:75`).
- **`reportSkip`** — 1 call site (`wdio.conf.ts:355`).

- **`census`** — defined in `test/a11y/screen-reader/parse-nvda-log.ts:323`, 4 call sites
  (`wdio.conf.ts:18,239,395,449`, `parse-nvda-log.ts:493`).

- **Meaning for the change:** the handle-guard surface has a blast radius of ONE file. A launch-context
  change placed at the spawn site touches no other module; placed at the CI step it touches no TS at all.

- **The honest-terminal mechanism is already shipped and correct** (`scripts/agent-run.ps1:68-100`).
  `Assert-A11yVerdict` asserts three things in order: the `^\[webview2 [^\]]*windows` driven-session
  banner (absent + strict ⇒ exit 1), the `Spec Files:` failed count, and a skip tally against
  `$A11yExpectedSkips = 2` (`:62`). This answers the a11y and tests extracts' shared research question
  — the strict handle IS declared (`ci.yml:383`, `CONDUCTOR_A11Y_STRICT: '1'`) and the printed verdict
  IS asserted.

- **The asserting step is correctly shaped** (`ci.yml:380-401`): no `continue-on-error`, no `if:`. All
  four `continue-on-error: true` keys in the a11y job sit on diagnostics/uploads (`:361` versions,
  `:412` session isolation, `:548` cause probes, `:554` upload). The arch/tests/security constraint is
  already satisfied — so outcome (B) cannot be reached by relaxing it, and nothing needs repairing here.

- **The step already reads the runner variable in the step SHELL** (`ci.yml:386-394`), not through
  `${{ env.* }}`, with a deliberate comment forbidding `$PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference`
  because it would destroy the diagnostic the verdict is read from.

- **One spawn site, cwd-anchored** (`wdio.conf.ts:405`):
  `spawn(process.execPath, [driverCli, '--native-driver', native], { cwd: repoRoot, env: appEnv })` —
  array-form, no shell. The app is NOT launched here: msedgedriver launches it
  (`msedgedriver.log`: `Launching Microsoft Edge: "…\target\release\conductor-tauri.exe"`), so the
  process chain is `pwsh (elevated) → node/wdio → node/tauri-driver → msedgedriver → conductor-tauri.exe`.

- **`browserName` is translated, not passed through**: the capability block declares `'wry'`
  (`wdio.conf.ts:339`) while the driver's `InitSession` records `"browserName": "webview2"` with
  `ms:edgeOptions.binary` — tauri-driver performs the translation. The real path therefore DOES use the
  host-app launch mode whose omission invalidated an earlier isolation probe (2026-09-07 learning).

- **Assert the token the runner PRINTS, measured** (`verification-harness.md:64`): the `Spec Files:` line
  OMITS the `failed` term when nothing failed; the skip tally is the per-spec `-` markers, never `pending`.
  `Assert-A11yVerdict` already encodes both.

- **A captured `runs/a11y-e2e.log` is UTF-16** (`verification-harness.md:66`, and `agent-run.ps1:270`
  writes it with `*>`): grep returns ZERO on it without decoding. Any new assertion over that capture
  inherits this.

- **GitHub Actions echoes each step's own source into the job log** (`verification-harness.md:66`): a
  literal inside a `Write-Output "…"` template appears TWICE; the tell is the unexpanded `$var`, the fix
  a `| grep -av 'Write-Output'` stage. Verified live this pass — the `[precondition]` sweep over run
  35079315258 returned both the echoes (`ci.yml` source, `:7914-7922`) and the one real output line
  (`:7938`); the real line is the one read.

- **A leg that boots an external process ends with a process census, taken twice, pattern derived from
  what the leg can START** (`verification-harness.md:58`) — and it must include `msedgewebview2.exe`,
  omitted once before, which made attribution impossible.

- **No smoke entry when the chunk has no producing leg** (`verification-harness.md:49`, extended
  2026-09-11 on THIS chunk's direct predecessor): a chunk whose whole surface is a CI workflow step plus
  a script has no boot path, so a listed bare verb satisfies the authoring check while asserting nothing.
  Prefer the stated-absence arm.

- *(provisional — decided by the P4 approach fork)* `scripts/a11y-limited-token-launch.ps1` — if outcome
  (A) is attempted via a de-elevating wrapper. Arch registers CI-only probe scripts under `scripts/`
  (`webview2-cause-probe.ps1` precedent: invoked solely by `ci.yml`, wired into neither harness shell),
  and the prior chunk rejected "an inline probe body in `ci.yml`, or a second script" for its own probe —
  so whether this is a new file or an extension of the existing one is a P4 decision, not settled here.

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — the `a11y` job: the launch context of the asserting step (`:380-401`),
  and, if outcome (B), the exclusion's recorded form. The asserting step's own guard shape is already
  correct and must stay byte-equivalent in that respect.

- `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/wdio.conf.ts` — *only if* the token drop lands at the spawn site (`:405`)
  rather than at the step. Graph says the blast radius is this file alone.

- **Companion sweep** (`grep -rn` over `*.ts,*.rs,*.ps1,*.sh,*.yml,*.toml`, node_modules and `target/`
  excluded): `'A11y routine arm'`: **1 hit** · 1 changed (`ci.yml:380`, the step itself) · 0 no-change.
  `CONDUCTOR_A11Y_STRICT`: **8 hits** · **0 changed** · 8 no-change — `ci.yml:344,383` (comment + the
  set site) and the three READERS `wdio.conf.ts:69,77`, `agent-run.ps1:72,73`, `agent-run.sh:197,199`,
  all of which every extract requires to stay byte-unchanged (security-plan's "ADDED arm, never a
  relaxation"). The reader set is recorded here precisely so the plan cannot drift into it.

- **`[inferred]` the CARRY's causal claim → VERIFIED.** Re-derived at HEAD, not recalled. The cited file
  exists and carries a controlled variation: `reading.md:92` grades elevation **ESTABLISHED** "by direct
  variation with a control on both sides"; `:137-147` tables the pair differing on `IsElevatedAdmin`
  alone (same machine, driver, runtime, tree, session) with the non-elevated known-good at 12 passing /
  2 skipped; `:162-163` scopes it to the dev host with the runner's elevation measured independently.
  Run 35079315258 is a **third, independent** confirmation: `IsElevatedAdmin: True` on the runner with
  every rival cause measured away in the same run.

- **The MECHANISM stays unestablished, and the plan must not assert it.** `reading.md:158` marks it
  `hypothesis:` in the source — WHY WebView2 declines the endpoint under an elevated token is not
  derivable from this repo, and nothing this pass measured establishes it. The CARRY's own marker text
  ("recorded, not established") is therefore accurate at HEAD and is preserved.

- **`[inferred]` the next arm is a limited-token launch → VERIFIED as the sanctioned next step, and its
  cost is now earned.** The prior chunk's `plan.md:371-375` REJECTED de-elevating on the runner for
  itself with an explicit condition — "It earns its cost only if arm B leaves elevation standing" — and
  arm B did leave it standing. The same line names the risk this chunk inherits: a scheduled-task or
  `runas` token dance has "failure modes [that] would then have to be separated from the endpoint's".

- **`[inferred]` no new third-party dependency → VERIFIED.** `schtasks` / `runas` / `Start-Process
  -Credential` are OS built-ins; none enters security-plan's third dependency class (a CI-time-fetched
  binary), so no Authenticode gate is required for this arm.

- **Correction to a supplied count (re-derived, not copied).** The take-up directive states the arm
  failed "after three session attempts over ~63 s". The ~63 s holds (`Spec Files: 0 passed, 1 failed,
  1 total (100% completed) in 00:01:03`). The attempt count does not: the routine-arm step's log carries
  ONE session-creation failure event rendered on four lines at a single instant (09:33:43.564, .565,
  .615 and the reporter echo at 09:33:44.03), with wdio's summary reporting `(1 retries)`. Derivation:
  `grep 'A11y routine arm' <log> | grep -n 'DevToolsActivePort'` → 4 lines, all at one timestamp.

- **The `(1 retries)` does not breach the zero-flakiness bar.** `.config/nextest.toml:7,17` sets
  `retries = 0` in both profiles; `wdio.conf.ts` sets no `specFileRetries` (grep: no match), so the
  count is wdio's own default spec-file behaviour, not a configured retry policy — and the run still
  FAILED, so nothing was masked. This settles the tests extract's research question.

1. Is a non-elevated principal actually reachable inside a hosted `windows-2025` step, and does the app
   survive the token drop — working directory, `RUNNER_TEMP`/`TEMP` on **different volumes** (measured
   `[diag] TEMP and RUNNER_TEMP share a volume: False`), and profile access for `EBWebView`?
   → blocks: **plan-decision** (it decides whether (A) is attemptable at all, and at which level of the
   process chain the drop is placed).

2. Does `--remote-debugging-pipe` offer a route that needs no token drop? The driver's own log recommends
   it over the port file (`msedgedriver.log`: "Use the --remote-debugging-pipe Chrome switch instead of
   the default --remote-debugging-port"), and the driver currently passes `--remote-debugging-port=0` via
   `WEBVIEW2_ADDITIONAL_BROWSER_ARGUMENTS`. Whether tauri-driver/WebView2 honour the pipe transport is
   unverified here. → blocks: **plan-decision** (a second candidate approach for the same outcome).

3. If (B): does the exclusion take design-system's `Blocked` shape (never measured) or `KnownResidual`
   (measured but pre-accepted)? The measured cause points at `KnownResidual`, but the choice changes
   what the a11y capability's matrix acceptance may claim. → blocks: **plan-decision**.

title: Scope — A11y CI gate at an honest terminal

data.head: # Scope — A11y CI gate at an honest terminal

body:
**Marker:** `2026-09-16-a11y-ci-gate-at-an-honest-terminal`
**Version:** conductor-0.3.0 · Epoch 3 — The a11y capability's terminal
**Promoted:** 2026-09-16

> A11y CI gate at an honest terminal — routine arm's asserted verdict green in CI, or a ratified
> exclusion naming its measured cause and owner

Two outcomes are allowed by construction, and the entry does not pre-select one. The chunk's job is to
reach whichever the evidence supports, and to leave the a11y capability's CI terminal **honest** — i.e.
the asserted verdict means what it says, rather than a job that is green because it asserts nothing or
red because nobody has ruled on it.

The a11y routine arm has a registered CI job that **fails**, and the failure is not a defect in the
assertion — it is the runner refusing to give the app a debuggable WebView2 session. This chunk must
close that terminal one of two ways:

- **(A) Green arm** — change the app's launch context in CI so the WebView2 remote-debugging endpoint
  appears, the driver creates a session, and the routine arm's axe + contrast assertions actually run
  and pass. The CARRY names the arm to try (below).

- **(B) Ratified exclusion** — if (A) does not produce the endpoint, record the exclusion with its
  **measured** cause and a named owner, so the a11y capability's coverage claim rests on a stated,
  operator-ratified boundary rather than on a red job nobody has adjudicated.

Which one ships is the operator's call at the P5 review. This scope commits to attempting (A) first
because the CARRY names a live, untried arm; it does not commit to (A) succeeding.

title: The failure is upstream of the driver — three arms, one signature

data.head: ### The failure is upstream of the driver — three arms, one signature

body: The run reproduces the same failure at three independent depths, which localizes it:
1. **In-path** (the real wdio arm): `session not created: DevToolsActivePort file doesn't exist`.

2. **Driver-alone** (`[diag] driver-alone status=500`): body is the *same* `session not created:
   DevToolsActivePort file doesn't exist` — so the failure does not need wdio.

3. **Bare-app, no driver at all**: `[diag] (a) bare-app DevToolsActivePort first seen: never within 90s`
   — while the app is alive and WebView2 is running.

when no driver is involved.** Any fix therefore has to change the app's *launch context*, not the
driver's configuration or the wdio harness. This also satisfies the bypass-probe discipline — the
driver-alone bypass is informative precisely because its in-path twin fails identically, rather than
standing alone.

title: Plan — 2026-09-16-medium-integrity-launch-for-the-a11y-routine-arm: "Medium-integrity launch for the a11y routine arm"

data.head: # Plan — 2026-09-16-medium-integrity-launch-for-the-a11y-routine-arm: "Medium-integrity launch for the a11y routine arm"

body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._

- **Marker:** 2026-09-16-medium-integrity-launch-for-the-a11y-routine-arm · **Version:** conductor-0.3.0 ·
  **Generated:** 2026-09-16T17:45:00Z

The `a11y` CI job's routine arm has never reached its assertions: the hosted runner gives the app no
WebView2 debugging endpoint, and the predecessor chunk established WHY — the mandatory **integrity label**,
not the administrator role, decides whether WebView2 grants one (varied with a control on both sides across
three dev-host legs). It also retired both remedies it built, by mechanism rather than exhaustion:
`RunLevel Limited` cannot lower the label on an account with no filtered token, and `runas /trustlevel`
strips the Administrators group while leaving the label untouched.

This chunk replaces the launch mechanism inside the registered seventh governed spawn form with the one
remedy that can actually move the label — `CreateRestrictedToken` + `SetTokenInformation(TokenIntegrityLevel)`

+ `CreateProcessAsUser` — then **measures on the runner** whether that opens the endpoint, using the ci-probe
the operator authorized for this chunk. The measurement, not an argument, decides which terminal the chunk
closes on: a green routine arm whose printed verdict is asserted (per a11y-plan §11 Anti-Patterns → CI +
test-plan §3 `--e2e`), or the CI half closed as a ratified permanent exclusion resting on the measured cause
and naming its owner. Both arms are legitimate; the plan commits to reaching one, not to which.

Two things research settled that shape the work. **Matrix obligation 2 is dissolved** — the unbuilt console
`contentinfo` footer cannot redden the routine arm, because axe runs only WCAG A/AA-tagged rules and every
landmark-family rule in axe-core 4.12.0 is `best-practice` (68 of 105 rules selected, none of the seven).
The green terminal is therefore not exposed to that second cause. And **the remedy needs no new host**: the
token APIs load from PowerShell 7 through `Add-Type` P/Invoke, so the work stays inside the existing
`scripts/` CI-only script with zero dependency delta (per arch §Infrastructure Patterns — Directory
structure, which bans a new workspace crate for a CI-only mechanism).

1. **Replace the launch mechanism in `scripts/a11y-limited-token-launch.ps1`.** Swap the
   `runas /trustlevel:0x20000` call (`:78-92`) for an `Add-Type` P/Invoke block calling
   `CreateRestrictedToken` (LUA_TOKEN) → `SetTokenInformation(TokenIntegrityLevel = S-1-16-8192)` →
   `CreateProcessAsUser`. Keep the file's parameter surface (`-Program -ArgumentList -WorkingDirectory
   -ForwardEnv -TimeoutSeconds`) byte-identical so the `ci.yml` call site does not move.

2. **Keep the argv guard exactly as it stands** (`:50-62`, the `$unsafe` class + whitespace rejection →
   exit 90). `CreateProcessAsUser` takes `lpCommandLine` as a STRING, so this form remains the composing
   class, not an arraying one — the guard is what keeps it outside rule (b)'s eval class (per security-plan
   §Security Anti-Patterns → Code Patterns rule (b)).

3. **Take the child's exit code from the process handle.** `CreateProcessAsUser` does not detach, so wait on
   the child and read `GetExitCodeProcess` directly. Keep the sentinel read (`runs/a11y-leg-exit.txt`) as a
   FALLBACK only — an absent sentinel must stay a distinct failure rather than a silent pass, so exits 94/95
   remain reachable when the handle path yields nothing usable.

4. **Pass the child environment explicitly.** Build the environment block for `CreateProcessAsUser` from the
   parent's environment plus the `-ForwardEnv` names, and DELETE the User-scope `SetEnvironmentVariable`
   writes and their `finally` restore (`:69-76`, `:115-118`) — a CI step should not mutate persistent user
   environment. Note `CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR` is deliberately NOT forwarded and must stay that way:
   `wdio.conf.ts:373` sets it for the app spawn itself, so the obs sink location is already correct (per
   obs-plan §3 Log file location).

5. **Preserve the per-failure exit-code discipline.** Every failure of the new mechanism prints its own
   `[precondition]` line with a distinct code, so a token-drop failure can never read as a session failure.
   Codes 90/91 keep their meanings; 92/93 are re-pointed from `runas`-absent / `runas`-declined to the
   API-call failures that replace them, each naming the failing API and its `GetLastWin32Error`.

6. **Retire the stale scheduled-task naming.** `.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s asserting step carries two
   comments describing a mechanism that no longer ships ("The scheduler does not capture the task's console",
   "the task never reached its witness"), and `scripts/a11y-token-witness.ps1` prefixes every `[diag]` line
   with `(task)`. The scheduled-task route was replaced by `runas` inside the predecessor chunk and these
   survived it. Re-word to the shipping mechanism.

7. **Drive the ci-probe and record its run id.** Per the operator's 2026-09-16 phase directive, reusing the
   form at `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-09-07-sr-findings-fixed/plan.md:203-216` (verified verbatim at those
   lines). Push the detached probe ref, capture the run id AT INVOCATION into the chunk evidence, read the
   `a11y` job's outcome, delete the ref. **Never author a run id into this plan.** The probe answers two
   questions at once: whether Medium integrity opens the endpoint on the runner (scope premise 1), and
   CARRY 2's window-station axis — `scripts/a11y-token-witness.ps1:88-100` already prints `WindowStation` /
   `UserInteractive` / `SessionName` from inside the leg, so that measurement costs nothing extra.

8. **Fork on what the probe measured — record, do not predict.** If the leg reached its assertions, capture
   the printed verdict and disposition the Evergreen float per its own stated exit condition (pin the
   runtime, Standalone Installer replacing the bootstrapper — security-plan.md:185). If it did not, compose
   the ratified permanent exclusion: the measured cause, the named owner, and the `if-no-files-found: warn`
   disposition for the absent violation record (per obs-plan §9). Which arm lands is a MEASUREMENT to
   record, never an expectation this plan forecasts.

9. **Write the evidence records** under `conductor-0.3.0/chunks/2026-09-16-medium-integrity-launch-for-the-a11y-routine-arm/evidence/` — the probe's run id and job conclusion,
   the witness's token/station readings, and the local mechanism gates' output. Handle NAMES, booleans and
   verdict fields only; no absolute host path, no seam-crate struct name (per security-plan §Error Handling).
   **The repo is public and a probe commit stays fetchable by SHA after the ref is deleted** — keep evidence
   and host paths out of the probed tree, as the predecessor did.

- (none) — the remedy replaces the mechanism inside the existing launcher. A fourth `scripts/` entry point
  would need its own arch directory-tree registration and would double the registered spawn surface for no
  gain.

- `scripts/a11y-limited-token-launch.ps1` — steps 1–5. Preserve the parameter surface, the `[precondition]`
  line style (handle NAME + state, never a path), and the distinct-exit-code discipline.

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (`a11y` job, asserting step) — step 6, comments only if the launcher's
  parameter surface holds. The step must keep carrying no `continue-on-error` and no `if:` (per arch
  §Established Decisions [CI/CD]).

- `scripts/a11y-token-witness.ps1` — step 6 (`(task)` prefix) and the step-3 re-scoping of the sentinel write
  at `:206-208`.

The Rust workspace gates are LISTED AND DEFERRED: this chunk's delta is PowerShell + YAML with zero
`.rs`/`.ts` source change, so `nextest`/`clippy` would re-run over an untouched tree at the cost of a cold
rebuild against a ~78 GB `target/` (per /implement's source-delta rule). **No `smoke` entry**: this chunk
drives no scenario and mints no run id, so there is no `agent-run status <id>` mint-then-read to perform —
the absence is stated here rather than left silent. **No `self-verify` frontend half**: this is not a UI
chunk (zero `ui/src` delta), and the routine `--e2e` leg that would serve as one is deferred for a measured
reason — the dev host floated to WebView2 153, where `accessibility.e2e.ts:384`/`:397` fail (10 passing /
2 failing / 2 skipped), a separate defect with its own owner. Running it here would author a known-red gate.
The arm is measured where it matters, on the runner, by the probe pair below. **No standalone PowerShell parse gate**: one was authored and withdrawn at P5 — the gate tool reads every `$NAME` in a `run` as a required handle, so inline PowerShell referencing `$f`/`$null` is refused as `env f, null unset` and could never fire. The three launcher entries below invoke `a11y-limited-token-launch.ps1` directly, which cannot run unless it parses; `a11y-token-witness.ps1` is exercised by the CI probe.

title: MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL='*' pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts/a11y-limited-token-launch.ps1 -Program C:/Windows/System32/whoami.
body:
[[gate]]
run = '''MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL='*' pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts/a11y-limited-token-launch.ps1 -Program C:/Windows/System32/whoami.exe -ArgumentList /groups -WorkingDirectory .'''
role = 'unit'

  §Error Handling · §Input Validation; architecture.md §Infrastructure Patterns — Directory structure /
  Build system · §Established Decisions [CI/CD] · §Cross-cutting Patterns — Trust boundary · §Occupied
  Resources; a11y-plan §9 CI Integration · §11 Anti-Patterns → CI / Screen Reader · §4 Per-surface landmark

  Primary screens; design-system §Surface: cli — Tokens.

- Research files inspected: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `scripts/a11y-limited-token-launch.ps1`,
  `scripts/a11y-token-witness.ps1`, `scripts/agent-run.ps1`, `scripts/agent-run.sh`,

  `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-09-07-sr-findings-fixed/plan.md`, axe-core 4.12.0 rule metadata,
  `.claude/rules/verification-harness.md` (:58, :62, :64, :66).

- **A fourth `scripts/` launcher wrapping the third — rejected.** It would need its own arch directory-tree
  registration and would double the registered spawn surface; replacing the mechanism inside the existing
  form keeps the registry at SEVEN.

- **A Rust/Win32 crate or an npm package to host the token APIs — rejected.** Measured unnecessary at P3
  (the APIs load from PowerShell 7 via `Add-Type`), and arch bans a new workspace crate for a CI-only
  mechanism. It would also open a dependency class this chunk has no reason to open.

- **Building the console `contentinfo` footer to pre-empt a landmark red — rejected.** Measured
  unnecessary: the routine arm cannot raise a landmark violation (axe-core 4.12.0 tags all seven
  landmark-family rules `best-practice`; `WCAG_TAGS` selects none). The footer remains genuinely unshipped
  and route-owned; this chunk neither builds it nor claims it is unneeded in general.

- **Relaxing the gate to obtain green — banned.** No `continue-on-error` or `if:` on the asserting step, no
  retry-to-green, no soft a11y SLO, and a skipped or unreached leg is never read as a pass (per a11y-plan
  §11 Anti-Patterns → CI / SLO; test-plan §10).

- **Fixing `accessibility.e2e.ts:384`/`:397` here — out of scope.** A separate defect with its own owner

- **Touching `CENSUS_NAMES` / the orphan reap — out of scope.** CARRY 3 surface 2 is SR-leg territory (all

- **A second ci-probe push at the wrap — banned by the directive.** The light gate re-verifies by the
  RECORDED run id.

- **`runs/a11y-e2e.log` is UTF-16 with a `ff fe` BOM** (a PowerShell-redirected capture). `grep` returns a
  silent zero on it, which reads as "the leg never got that far" — decode before concluding
  (`raw[:2] == b'\xff\xfe'` → `.decode('utf-16')`). Basis: `.claude/rules/verification-harness.md:66`,
  measured at `2026-09-11-hosted-runner-endpoint-cause-closed`.

- **GitHub Actions echoes each step's own source into the job log**, so a literal inside a `Write-Output
  "…"` template appears TWICE — once unexpanded in the echo, once for real. Any count over a captured job
  log needs a `| grep -av 'Write-Output'` stage; the tell that a hit is an echo is the unexpanded `$var`.
  Same basis as above.

- **`SE_ASSIGNPRIMARYTOKEN` is not required for this call shape** — `CreateProcessAsUser` needs it only when
  the token is not a restricted version of the caller's own primary token, and `CreateRestrictedToken`
  produces exactly that. `SE_INCREASE_QUOTA` is still needed and is held by the runner's account. Basis:
  the Win32 contract for `CreateProcessAsUser`; the reachability half was measured at P3 (P/Invoke probe:

  measurement for the exclusion arm, not a defect to hide.

- **An integrity level may be lowered, never raised** — so setting Medium on the runner's High token is
  permitted, while the P3 probe (already Medium) could not exercise that direction. Do not report the local
  unit gate as proof of the lowering.

Our image read `windows-2025-vs2026` `20260828.587` — byte-identical. Issue open, no maintainer response. **It mentions no elevation, integrity level or restricted token anywhere.** Microsoft's WebView2 distribution doc read for the second external claim (see Spec claims disproved).

- **Reverted / negative API facts:** `CreateRestrictedToken(LUA_TOKEN)` was written, measured, and REPLACED by `DuplicateTokenEx` within this chunk. It lowers the integrity label AND adds restricting SIDs AND disables the administrator group — moving both axes this chunk exists to separate — and the over-restriction broke child-process creation inside the leg (run 35141676310: label dropped to Medium correctly, then `whoami` failed `ApplicationFailedException` and the leg never reached wdio). The shipped form moves the label alone.

- **Insufficient fixes (written, kept, not the remedy):** **the medium-integrity launcher itself.** It is correct, it works, and it is measured to do exactly what it claims — parent `S-1-16-12288` → child `S-1-16-8192` on the runner, confirmed from inside the leg. It did not resolve the defect it was written for. What it DID resolve: it made the integrity hypothesis decidable, and the answer is negative on this runner. Owner of the remainder: the successor chunk minted at P5.

- **Spec claims disproved by measurement:**
  1. **"the hosted image opens no remote-debugging endpoint"** — stated as an unconditional property. **FALSE as stated.** Run 35192876641: a bare app on windows-2022 at native runtime 131.0.2903.86 publishes `DevToolsActivePort` in **1 s**, and a WebDriver session is created (`status 200`, `debuggerAddress: localhost:60826`, banner `[webview2 131.0.2903.86 windows]`). Stated in: `.andromeda/test-plan.md` · `.andromeda/residuals.md` · `.claude/docs/a11y-summary.md` · `.claude/docs/tests-summary.md`.
  2. **"RED at WebView2 session creation"** — configuration-bound, not unconditional. Stated in: `.andromeda/a11y-plan.md` · `.andromeda/architecture.md` (the CI row).
  3. **"never yet green"** — the arm now runs to completion with 11 of 12 non-skipped specs passing. Stated in: `.claude/docs/a11y-summary.md`.
  4. **security-plan §Dependency Security's `≥ 152` floor, as a POSTURE.** Measured three ways: it DESTROYED the working configuration (run 35185153012 read 131.0.2903.86, fetched Evergreen, put 153.0.4234.32 in effect against a 152 driver); it is NOT NECESSARY (coherent 131/131 works); it is NOT SUFFICIENT (coherent 152/152 fails on windows-2025, run 34654076633). The measured subject is **coherence** — driver major == runtime major — and the floor forbids the only configuration that works.
  5. **security-plan §Dependency Security's stated exit condition for the Evergreen float** — "the versioned Standalone Installer replaces the bootstrapper" — **names a mechanism that does not exist.** Verified at Microsoft's distribution doc: the Standalone Installer installs the EVERGREEN runtime and takes no version argument (`MicrosoftEdgeWebView2RuntimeInstaller{X64/X86/ARM64}.exe /silent /install`). The only versioned route is Fixed Version — "over 250 MB", pointed at by `WEBVIEW2_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE_FOLDER`, no registry key, and only "the most-patched version of the latest and second-latest major releases", so 131 is not obtainable from Microsoft today. The doc's own escape is "Keep an archived copy of any versions you need" — i.e. the project would host the package. **The float's only documented retirement path is not executable as written, independently of this chunk.**

- **Expected amendments (from plan):**
  - `security-plan.md` §Security Anti-Patterns → Code Patterns rule (b) — **carried, and its direction INVERTED.** The plan expected the seventh form's description to move from `runas` to the token-API mechanism. The launcher is now removed from the asserting step, so the registered form no longer describes what ships in CI. Fact in Changes: Harness / gate surface. Sites: `grep -c 'runas /trustlevel' .andromeda/security-plan.md` → 1 (`:363`); `.claude/rules/security.md` → 1 (`:27`). **Escalation 3.**
  - `architecture.md` §Established Decisions [CI/CD] · §Infrastructure Patterns — Build system — **carried.** Fact in Changes: Harness / gate surface + Dev-tool versions. **Escalations 1 and 4.**
  - `a11y-plan.md` §9 Pipeline integration — **carried.** The site names the launcher path; the launcher leaves the asserting step. Fact in Changes: Harness / gate surface.
  - `matrix#v3-02 notes` — **ledger-note — owner P7.3.**

1. **`CreateRestrictedToken(LUA_TOKEN)` → `DuplicateTokenEx`.** The plan named the first. It moves the integrity label AND the admin group — conflating the two axes the chunk exists to separate — and broke child-process creation in the leg. Replaced so only the label moves. Justified by measurement (run 35141676310).

2. **Rust workspace gate deferrals VOIDED and run.** The plan deferred `nextest`/`clippy` for zero compiled-source delta. `crates/conductor-report/tests/matrix_ledger_gate.rs:140` reads `verification-matrix.json` at runtime, and the P5 claim left that file uncommitted — so the plan's own stated reason had fallen. Both ran green (986/986 · exit 0). Basis: `git status --short` names + `grep -rlF` over `crates/**/*.rs` → 4 hits.

3. **Plan step 6 was wider than enumerated.** It named two `ci.yml` comments and the witness's `(task)` prefix; the witness's entire doc block and four body comments were also scheduled-task prose. Extended in place — same file, same defect class, all listed touchpoints.

4. **Unplanned in-scope additions:** the witness's exits 96/97 (a leg that never ran reported exit 0 — the false green a11y-plan §11 bans, caught only by the downstream conformance gate); the leg-console print in `ci.yml`; the driver-log readback; the TEMP write probe.

5. **FOUR PROBE-SCOPED, UNRATIFIED SURFACES now in `ci.yml`, none of which I may ratify:**
   - `runs-on: windows-2025` → `windows-2022` (contradicts this chunk's own acceptance criterion and arch §Established Decisions, though NOT the pin's stated rationale, which is explicit-label-rather-than-`windows-latest` and names no year)
   - the `≥ 152` floor bypassed on `win22` (**Escalation 1**)
   - the driver pin fetching from `msedgedriver.microsoft.com` — a SECOND non-loopback egress where arch registers exactly one (**Escalation 4**)
   - the asserting step's launcher invocation removed — **this chunk's own deliverable**, removed because it is what blocks green on the working configuration (**Escalation 3**)
6. **`:384` NOT fixed** — `accessibility.e2e.ts` is outside this chunk's Files to modify and is named in the plan's `Constraints & rejected approaches`. Recorded, not touched.

- **A token that names one arm of a fork cannot probe the fork.** The attribution sweep keyed on `DevToolsActivePort` — the HIGH-run signature — found 0 from the leg, and I concluded the endpoint question had never been asked at Medium. Every count was right; the inference was wrong. At Medium the leg's error is a DIFFERENT string (`session not created` / `from chrome not reachable`, wrapped across two log lines). Operator-caught.

- **GitHub echoes each step's source into the job log.** Run 35141676310 carried 11 `DevToolsActivePort` hits and **0** outside the command echo. Unfiltered, that reads as "the endpoint stayed closed at Medium" — a false conclusion that would have sent this chunk to the exclusion arm on no basis. The filter is `grep -av $'\033\[36;1m'`.

- **A search summary is a claim ABOUT a source, never the source.** The engine's summary of issue #14738 asserted a mechanism — "WebView2 150+ hardening for elevated hosts, `WEBVIEW2_*` ignored" — that fit this runner's RID 500 account and this chunk's token work so precisely it would have explained everything. The issue says no such thing. Most dangerous exactly when the summary matches the hypothesis already held.

- **`${{ env.X }}` cannot read a runner-PROCESS variable, and in an `if:` it fails SILENTLY.** `if: ${{ env.ImageOS == 'win22' }}` is always false; the step skipped and the job still looked like it ran (run 35190456907). `ci.yml` already documents this trap for `EDGEWEBDRIVER` (run 34148079506) — I read that comment this session and reintroduced the mistake in the quieter form. The guard belongs in the step's shell.

- **Every windows-2022 result was the instrument until proven otherwise** — probe A installed 153 over the native runtime; probe B didn't pin at all. Both would have read as "the coherent pair fails".

- **Verify the instrument, not just the result.** The driver-log readback (`httpAttempts`/`pipeMentions`) changed a cell: pipe-at-Medium showed 49 HTTP attempts, so the switch was NOT honoured and that run re-measured the port path. Recorded UNMEASURED for pipe at Medium, not as "pipe fails at Medium".

- **A generic error string is not a fact about its literal subject.** The High pipe run returned `DevToolsActivePort file doesn't exist` while in pipe mode, where no such file exists — msedgedriver's generic "could not reach the browser" message. Read as a file fact it points the diagnosis somewhere the run does not support.

- **Integrity's SIGN is not invariant.** The predecessor's legs A/B/C were correctly measured; this chunk bounds them rather than retiring them. Medium helped at runtime 153 on the dev host; High is REQUIRED at 131 on windows-2022. It is an interaction with the configuration, not a constant.
- **Sweep hazard:** a bare `$MK` in a count command expanded to empty and matched every line (2238 vs the true 16). An unset variable in a grep is a silent universal match.

**Terminal: NOT reached — and not for lack of a cause.** The chunk's two allowed outcomes were a green routine arm or a ratified permanent exclusion. Neither shipped, and the exclusion arm is now **DEAD on measurement**: the endpoint demonstrably opens on a hosted runner, so a permanent exclusion would have been ratified on a false basis.

**What the arc established.** Run 35192876641 — windows-2022, native runtime 131.0.2903.86, driver pinned 131.0.2903.86, High integrity, launcher removed — opened a WebView2 session on a hosted runner for the first time in this saga (banner `[webview2 131.0.2903.86 windows]`, session id recorded) and the arm RAN: **11 passing / 1 failing / 2 skipped**, the two skips being the expected live-hold set. **SC 2.4.3 (`:397`) PASSES on 131.**

**The single red is `:384` (SC 2.1.1), and it is a COUNTING-BASIS defect in the assertion, not an accessibility defect.** Expected and received bracket lists are identical to the character — same six controls, same order, same one wrap of the focus cycle — and only the prefix differs: expected `"6 reached"`, received `"12 reached"`. The expectation counts DISTINCT controls; the label counts VISITS. **Record it as "12 visits / 6 distinct", never as a bare count.** The reachability property SC 2.1.1 asserts is satisfied, and the proof is inside the failure message.

**NOT established:** why the focus cycle wraps on the runner and did not on the dev host at 152 (the 2026-09-10 green). The assertion is environment-sensitive, and the first successful CI run of this arm is what exposed it. Also not established: the causal pathway by which Medium integrity denies the driver-to-browser channel (the signature and its locus are measured; the mechanism is not).
**Acceptance criteria, re-asserted against the diff:**
- (a11y) `verification-matrix.json#v3-02` — **UNMET.** Neither arm: no green printed verdict, and the exclusion arm is dead on measurement. → P7.3, un-claim.
- (security) registry classification stated — **UNMET as written.** The plan expected a replacement description; the launcher leaves CI entirely. → Escalation 3.

- (security) launch vector carries no shell string, both controls rejected before composition — **MET.** Exit 90 on the whitespace and metacharacter controls, measured green at implement and re-run here.
- (arch) `scripts/`-resident CI-only entry point, no sixth `agent-run` command, no workspace crate — **MET.**

- (arch) asserting step keeps no `continue-on-error`/`if:` on the pinned `windows-2025` label — **UNMET by the diff**: the label is `windows-2022` and the launcher invocation is gone. Both are probe-scoped and unratified. → Escalations 1/4 and the P7.5 hard gate.
- (arch/security) Evergreen float dispositioned — **UNMET, and its stated mechanism disproved.** → Escalations 1 and 2.
- (obs) no host path / struct name / stack trace in any artifact — **MET.** `grep -coE '[A-Za-z]:[\\/]'` over the evidence records → 0.
- (tests) five-command surface, `status` disk read, envelope shapes unchanged — **MET.**
- (a11y) ONE webview-automation stack, no platform-forked assertion path — **MET.**
**Gates** (by `run` text, not ordinal):
- `MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL='*' pwsh … a11y-limited-token-launch.ps1 -Program …whoami.exe -ArgumentList /groups …` — **green** · exit 0 · `contains S-1-16-8192` held (baseline was `red — timeout at 180s`)
- `pwsh … -ArgumentList 'a b' …` — **green** · exit 90 · `contains A11Y_LIMITED_TOKEN_ARGV` held
- `pwsh … -ArgumentList 'a;b' …` — **green** · exit 90 · same atom
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci` — **defer voided — conductor-0.3.0/verification-matrix.json** · ran · green · 986 tests run, 986 passed, 0 skipped
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` — **defer voided — same file** · ran · green · exit 0
- `cargo audit` — **green** · exit 0
- `cargo deny check advisories bans licenses sources` — **green** · exit 0
- `test -n "$CONDUCTOR_MSEDGEDRIVER" && test -f … && echo DRIVER_RESOLVED` — **green** · exit 0 · `last line DRIVER_RESOLVED`
- `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run --e2e` — **`leg = 'live'`, deferred**; the dev host floated to WebView2 153 where `:384`/`:397` both fail. Treatment: driven in CI instead, seven probes.
- `git add -A && … git push origin "$C:refs/heads/ci-probe/…"` — **`leg = 'operator'`**, driven by hand seven times, every ref deleted, HEAD never moved.

- `gh run view <id> --json conclusion,headSha,url,jobs` — **`leg = 'operator'`**, re-verified by recorded run ids; deliberately `expect = ['exit 0']` only, never asserted green, because the terminal is two-armed by construction.

**`red — not this chunk's`:** `:384` SC 2.1.1 fails on a counting-basis defect in the assertion, whose own failure message shows the reachability property holding (identical bracket lists, 6 expected vs 12 received). **Basis:** the file `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/test/a11y/accessibility.e2e.ts` is outside this chunk's Files to modify and carries no edit from it (`git diff --name-only` does not list it); the assertion's counting basis predates this chunk (added by `06db2f9`, 2026-09-07). **Owner:** the successor chunk minted at P5.

**Outcome basis:** this session's own conversation (implement ran in it), plus post-implement artifacts named inline — CI runs 35141676310 · 35143892765 · 35145664132 · 35147042449 · 35150449243 · 35184180963 · 35185153012 · 35186499514 · 35190456907 · 35191569653 · 35192876641, and three operator reading-notes that corrected three of my readings (the echo-filtered `DevToolsActivePort` count, the tauri-driver startup race, and the pipe-transport gap). Each correction is recorded in Decisions & corrections above.

**Process hygiene:** this run started no process that outlived it — launcher/gate/cargo children all exited with their commands. Six `msedgewebview2` processes are on the dev host with `StartTime 18:33:31`, **before this session began (~19:27)**: not this run's, the predecessor's carried survivors (CARRY 3), owner that defect. data.head: ## Graph impact (from the code-graph query; trace at `{run_dir}/tree-query-{marker}.json`)

body:
- **`journal_conformance`** — rust plane, `db_state: fresh`, **rows: 0**. This is NOT an index gap and NOT
  a leaf finding: `grep -rn 'journal_conformance' --include=*.rs crates/` returns **0 lines**, because the
  name is a test-BINARY file (`crates/conductor-run/tests/journal_conformance.rs`, 11,482 B) selected by
  `cargo nextest run -p conductor-run --test journal_conformance`, never a Rust definition. A `symbol`
  query keyed on a file name can never match. Basis: the bare grep, not the exit code.

- **`seedFixtureRuns`** — ts plane, 1 caller: `wdio.conf.ts:365` (graph `line` 364 is 0-indexed; the editor
  line is 365). The routine arm's self-seeding has exactly one call site.

- **Both indexed planes are largely out of this chunk's way.** The modify-set is YAML + PowerShell, neither
  of which is an indexed plane, so the graph bounds the blast radius rather than locating the work:
  no Rust or TS signature changes, hence no caller threading.

- **Distinct exit code per launcher failure mode** (`a11y-limited-token-launch.ps1:56-95`): 90 argv
  rejected · 91 program unresolved · 92 mechanism absent · 93 launch declined · 94 sentinel timeout ·
  95 sentinel unparseable, each with its own `[precondition]` line. This is what keeps a token-drop failure
  from reading as a session failure, and the successor must preserve the property.

- **Printed-verdict assertion, not exit code** (`agent-run.ps1:68-100`): `Assert-A11yVerdict` requires the
  `^[webview2 [^\]]*windows` banner, a last `Spec Files:` line with zero failed, and a skip count `<=
  $A11yExpectedSkips` (2), then prints its own green line.

- **Handle guard mirroring** — the launcher's `$unsafe` class is a deliberate mirror of `wdio.conf.ts`'s
  UNSAFE_PATH guard, cited in its own comment as what keeps the composition outside rule (b)'s eval class.

- **Witness-from-inside** (`a11y-token-witness.ps1`): the launched process reports its OWN token and station
  to a file, because the launch mechanism does not carry the child's console back. Registering a token level
  is not evidence of running at it.

- **CI-only script qualifier**: `scripts/`-resident, invoked solely by `ci.yml`'s `a11y` job, wired into
  neither harness shell, no sixth `agent-run` command (arch §Infrastructure Patterns — Directory structure).

- **Handle NAME + boolean, never a resolved path**, in every `[precondition]` / `[diag]` line — the launcher
  already holds this throughout.

- **Integrity read from the token, not from a role predicate** (`a11y-token-witness.ps1:52-73`; also
  `.claude/rules/host-win32.md` 2026-09-16): `IsInRole` returns False for a deny-only group, and `.NET`
  omits the `S-1-16-*` SID entirely.

title: The two mechanism claims, re-derived at HEAD

data.head: ## The two mechanism claims, re-derived at HEAD

body:
**(1) Inherited premise — "integrity label, not the administrator role, decides the endpoint"**
(marker: `measured, not assumed`; the marker sets spot-check depth). Evidence pointer
`…/evidence/integrity-level-is-the-discriminator.md` is present (3,660 B) and its three legs are restated
verbatim in the route entry. **Still-true at HEAD on its own terms; NOT re-measured on the runner.** All
three legs are dev-host legs at runtime 153. The transfer to the runner is premise 1 below.
**(2) Originated premise — the remedy's API path.** The equality the plan needs is: *`CreateRestrictedToken`

+ `SetTokenInformation(TokenIntegrityLevel)` + `CreateProcessAsUser`, called from PowerShell 7 via
`Add-Type` P/Invoke with no new dependency, yields a child at Medium integrity.* Probed at HEAD
(scratchpad only, nothing added to the tree):

```
[probe] OpenProcessToken: ok
[probe] current token integrity SID: S-1-16-8192
[probe] CreateRestrictedToken(LUA_TOKEN): ok
[probe] SetTokenInformation(TokenIntegrityLevel=Medium): ok
[probe] RESTRICTED token integrity SID: S-1-16-8192
```

**What this shows:** the two token APIs are reachable from PowerShell 7 through `Add-Type`, succeed for this
account, and need no package — so the remedy can live in the existing `scripts/` PowerShell form with zero
dependency delta. **What it does NOT show, and must not be written as if it did:** (a) this shell was
ALREADY Medium (`S-1-16-8192`), so setting Medium was a no-op in effect — the High→Medium LOWERING direction
is unproven here, resting on the documented rule that a label may be lowered but never raised; (b)
`CreateProcessAsUser`, the third API, was not exercised at all, because it requires an actual launch; (c)
nothing about the runner. Two of three APIs, one host, wrong starting integrity.

- (none expected) — the remedy replaces the mechanism INSIDE `scripts/a11y-limited-token-launch.ps1`. A
  fourth `scripts/` entry point would need its own arch directory-tree registration; nesting a second
  launcher inside the first buys nothing and doubles the registered surface.

- `scripts/a11y-limited-token-launch.ps1` — swap the `runas /trustlevel:0x20000` mechanism for the API
  triple. Three consequences the current file's shape makes cheap: `CreateProcessAsUser` does **not**
  detach, so the child handle gives the exit code directly and the sentinel wait (:96-110, exit codes 94/95)
  becomes a fallback rather than the channel; the env block can be passed to the child explicitly instead of
  via User-scope registry writes (:69-76), which removes a global side effect from a CI step; and the
  whitespace/metacharacter guard must STAY, because `CreateProcessAsUser` takes `lpCommandLine` as a string
  and the form therefore remains the composing class, not an arraying one.

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (the `a11y` job's asserting step) — **two stale comments that describe a
  mechanism that no longer ships**: "The scheduler does not capture the task's console" and "the task never
  reached its witness". The scheduled-task route was replaced by `runas` inside the predecessor chunk; these
  sentences survived it. Whether the step's `run:` body itself changes depends on the launcher's parameter
  surface staying fixed (recommended: keep it fixed, so the step is comment-only).

- `scripts/a11y-token-witness.ps1` — the `(task)` prefix on every `[diag]` line is the same stale naming,
  and the sentinel write (:206-208) is re-scoped by the non-detaching launch.

- **Not a touchpoint:** the spec-master text for the Evergreen disposition (CARRY 4 / obligation 1) and the
  spawn-form registry — those are wrap amendments, per the phase contract.

title: Two mechanical hazards this chunk's gates will sit on

data.head: ## Two mechanical hazards this chunk's gates will sit on

body: Both from `verification-harness.md:66`, measured at `2026-09-11-hosted-runner-endpoint-cause-closed`:

- **`runs/a11y-e2e.log` is UTF-16 with a `ff fe` BOM** — a PowerShell-redirected capture. `grep` returns
  **zero** on it, silently, which reads as "the leg never got that far". Decode before concluding
  (`raw[:2] == b'\xff\xfe'` → `.decode('utf-16')`).

- **GitHub Actions echoes each step's own source into the job log**, so a literal inside a `Write-Output
  "…"` template appears TWICE — once unexpanded in the echo, once for real. A counting gate over a captured
  job log needs a `| grep -av 'Write-Output'` stage; the tell that it is an echo is the unexpanded `$var`.

title: Printed-verdict atoms — sources for the `expect` entries

data.head: ## Printed-verdict atoms — sources for the `expect` entries

body:
`verification-harness.md:64` requires a live leg's atoms be read from a recorded output or the tool's own
print site, because a `leg` entry is exempt from P5's baseline run and is checked by nothing at authoring
time. Print sites, read at HEAD:
| atom | source | note |
| `contains [a11y] verdict asserted` | `scripts/agent-run.ps1:99` / `scripts/agent-run.sh:225` | green verdict |
| `lacks [a11y] leg skipped` | `scripts/agent-run.ps1:76` / `scripts/agent-run.sh:202` | the skip-green guard |

**Shell-parity finding — the two shells print DIFFERENT verdict text.** `.ps1:99` uses an ASCII hyphen and
`|` separators (`verdict asserted - 0 failed | … | driven session present`); `.sh:225` uses an EM DASH and
`·` separators (`verdict asserted — 0 failed · … · driven session present`). The same divergence sits on the
skip line (`:76` vs `:202`). The SEMANTICS are identical, which is what test-plan §3's parity contract
binds, so this is not a defect to fix here — but an `expect` atom must stop at the common prefix
(`[a11y] verdict asserted`, `[a11y] leg skipped`) or it will hold in one shell and fail in the other.

- Does a Medium-integrity `CreateProcessAsUser` launch on the RUNNER produce `DevToolsActivePort`?
  → blocks: **implementation-scope**. Only the ci-probe answers it; the plan names the probe, and the
  answer decides which terminal arm (green vs ratified exclusion) the chunk closes on.

- Do `:384`/`:397` hold at the runner's WebView2 152? → blocks: **implementation-scope**. They fail at 153
  on the dev host; their 152 status rests on the 2026-09-10 record, not a fresh run. If the probe opens a
  session, this becomes the next thing the same probe measures — and CARRY 1 says a session is not a green
  arm precisely because of these two.

title: Scope — Medium-integrity launch for the a11y routine arm

data.head: # Scope — Medium-integrity launch for the a11y routine arm

body:
**Marker:** `2026-09-16-medium-integrity-launch-for-the-a11y-routine-arm`
**Version:** conductor-0.3.0 · Epoch 3 — The a11y capability's terminal
**Promoted:** 2026-09-16

> Medium-integrity launch for the a11y routine arm — the a11y job's leg runs at Medium integrity and
> the routine arm's asserted verdict is read from a CI run that reached its assertions, or the CI half
> is closed as a ratified exclusion resting on THIS measured cause

This is the successor to `2026-09-16-a11y-ci-gate-at-an-honest-terminal`, which left the terminal
**UNDECIDED** and shipped a cause instead. The two allowed outcomes are unchanged from the predecessor
(green arm, or ratified exclusion); what is new is that one specific remedy is now named by measurement
rather than by hypothesis, and the two mechanisms already tried are retired **by mechanism**.

**PREMISE (measured, not assumed):** the mandatory INTEGRITY LABEL, not the administrator role, decides
whether WebView2 grants a debugging endpoint. Established 2026-09-16 by variation with a control on both
sides across three dev-host legs at runtime 153 — A admin+High → no session (`DevToolsActivePort`, 2:00) ·
B non-admin+High → no session (2:00) · C non-admin+Medium → session created
(`[webview2 153.0.4234.32 windows]` ×35, 0:06); A→B varies the role with integrity held (no change, role
exonerated), B→C varies integrity with the role held (the session appears).

Evidence re-verified at promotion:
`conductor-0.3.0/chunks/2026-09-16-a11y-ci-gate-at-an-honest-terminal/evidence/integrity-level-is-the-discriminator.md`
(present, 3,660 B).

The marker text `(measured, not assumed)` is preserved verbatim because it sets the re-verification depth
P3 owes this claim. Statedness is not measurement at HEAD: the legs were measured on the **dev host** at
runtime 153, and the subject of this chunk is the **runner**, whose session context differs. P3's scope
premise closure decides whether that gap needs closing before the remedy is built.

**SUBJECT:** an explicit medium-integrity launch — `CreateRestrictedToken` + `SetTokenInformation` setting
the mandatory label to the Medium SID, then `CreateProcessAsUser`.
Both mechanisms the predecessor shipped are retired BY MECHANISM, not by exhaustion:

- `RunLevel Limited` cannot lower the label — the runner's account is the built-in Administrator (RID 500)
  with `FilterAdministratorToken` absent, so no filtered token exists to drop to.

- `runas /trustlevel:0x20000` cannot either — it strips the Administrators group and leaves the label
  (measured on the runner: role False, integrity `S-1-16-12288`).

A **seventh** governed harness-spawn form is already registered for the launcher this entry replaces or
extends; an **eighth crossing escalates again** (security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Code Patterns
rule (b)). Whether this chunk's launcher is a replacement of the seventh form or an eighth crossing is a
scope question P2/P4 must settle explicitly — it is an escalation trigger either way, not a detail.

- **In scope:** the launch mechanism for the a11y job's routine leg, its CI wiring, and reading the
  routine arm's asserted verdict from a run that reached its assertions — or, failing that, composing the
  ratified exclusion on the measured cause with a named owner.

- **Trust boundary:** unchanged. No new inbound listener; the driver ports `4444`/`4445` live and die with
  the harness, as the scope law already admits for the dev-only webview legs.

`v3-02`'s `notes` carry two planning obligations folded at the 2026-09-11 route Phase 4 on operator

Obligation 2 is the sharpest planning input this chunk has and it is invisible from the working entry
alone. P3 owes a measurement, not an argument.

**P3 CLOSURE — obligation 2 measured and dissolved.** The measurement was taken (four independent ways, see
premise 2 below and `research.md`): the routine arm cannot raise a landmark violation, because axe runs only
WCAG A/AA-tagged rules and every landmark-family rule in axe-core 4.12.0 is `best-practice`. The unshipped

chunk may promise is not exposed to it. Obligation 1 (the Evergreen pin disposition) stands unchanged and

1. **Dev-host integrity finding transfers to the runner** — **STILL OPEN, instrument now named.**

3. `[premise-corrected: replacement, not an eighth crossing — the registry counts spawn FORMS and this
   changes one launcher's internal mechanism at one call site]` **The launcher REPLACES the registered

- **Marker:** 2026-09-16-scenario-assertion-audit-gate · **Version:** conductor-0.3.0 · **Generated:** 2026-09-16T07:40Z

Epoch 2 established two corpus properties by hand and recorded them in prose: every committed
`[[expected]]` assertion is satisfiable or retired (`v3-04`), and every scenario's declared `slo_tier`
is accounted for against its own summed phase duration (`v3-05`). Both are TRUE at HEAD and both are
currently re-establishable only by repeating the derivation. This chunk makes them **mechanical and
re-runnable by a reader who did not write them**, which is `verification-matrix.json#v3-06`.

The design is the shipped exact-set ledger gate, not a new invention. `check_load_envelope`
(`load_envelope.rs:367-398`) already grades a committed `Vec<Exemption>` against a measured set in
BOTH directions — failing on `unpinned` (a new member outside the pin), `rotted` (a pinned member that
no longer qualifies) and `lost_subject` (a pin naming a scenario that no longer exists) — and
`testing.md:66` states why that shape is right here: it records work owed at full precision and can
only shrink under compulsion, rather than weakening an assertion. A new `check_scenario_audit` in
`conductor-core` grades a new committed ledger the same way, and a three-armed crate-local test over
the REAL committed corpus registers it as a gate that fails the build (per test-plan §6's
`coverage_gate.rs` precedent; arch §Established Decisions [Accepted Capability Set] for the
named-`CoreError` failure class).

Two research findings shape what the ledger holds. First, the **closed-set property needs no probe**:
`SloTier` (`scenario.rs:50-62`) is a plain derived `Deserialize` with three renamed variants and no
`#[serde(other)]`, so a fourth tier cannot survive `from_toml_str` — the property is enforced by
construction, and the gate's job is to assert that the type stays closed, not to re-scan for
violations. Second, the **two surviving assertions are satisfiable but non-discriminating**: measured
at SUT HEAD `83d4060`, deterministic mode returns a fixed L4 payload regardless of prompt
(`deterministic_inference.rs:126`) whose pinned `"severity": "autonomous"` maps through
`map_l4_incident_severity` (`inference_runtime.rs:697-703`) to `IncidentSeverity::Error`, rendering
`severity_label` `"error"` (`markdown.rs:359-366`) into every report — so both `Contains "error"`
blocks pass on a token their own stimulus never produced. A static check cannot grade discrimination
(test-plan §11 routes SUT-behaviour claims to the live gate), so the gate asserts **satisfiability**
and the ledger **records the weakness with its reason**, exact-set in both directions. The finding is
thereby enforced by something rather than by memory, which is the capability's own standard.

1. **Add the committed ledger `contracts/scenario-audit-ledger.toml`.** Two arrays, each entry
   carrying an identity and a REASON string (a judgment, not a debt — `testing.md:66`), plus the
   SUT version its grounds were measured against so a Pulse change rots them visibly:
   - `[[live_assertion]]` — one per scenario carrying a live `[[expected]]` block: `scenario`,
     `ground` (why the declared token is satisfiable against the SUT), `discriminates` (bool) and,
     when `false`, `weakness` (why the token does not depend on the scenario's own stimulus).
   - `[[over_tier]]` — one per scenario whose summed `gap_ms` exceeds its declared `slo_tier`:
     `scenario`, `reason` (the stated ground for declaring it anyway).
   Seed both from the measured corpus: the two live-assertion rows are `root-span-error-scope` and
   `span-status-error-detection` (derivation: `grep -lE '^\[\[expected\]\]' scenarios/*.toml` → 2 of
   36, re-run at promotion 2026-09-16), each `discriminates = false` with the chain above as its
   `weakness`.

   **Derive the `over_tier` rows by computing the arithmetic directly over the committed corpus —
   `sum(phases.gap_ms) > slo_tier` deadline, per scenario — and record what that computation
   measures.** This is a standalone derivation over `scenarios/*.toml`, available before step 3
   exists and not dependent on it; step 3 later re-computes the same term inside the gate, and the
   POSITIVE arm passing is what proves the two agree. Do NOT copy the row list from
   `verification-matrix.json#v3-05`'s 2026-09-16 `notes` line — that line is the prediction to test,
   not the source. Predicted: 11 rows (9 original ceiling-posture + `ack-cooldown` +
   `severity-tier-autonomous`). If the computation disagrees, the computation wins and the
   disagreement is recorded.

2. **Add the ledger loader in `conductor-core`, following the shipped TWO-PART split exactly.**
   `LoadEnvelope` is the model and the split is explicit in its own doc comment
   (`load_envelope.rs:227-234`): `default_path()` returns a **bare relative `PathBuf`** — a hard-coded
   constant, which is what gives the "no `CONDUCTOR_*` override handle" property — and `load(path)`
   takes an **already-resolved** path, because "the binary edge resolves it before calling `load` —
   never this module". `resolve_under` is applied by the CALLER at the `conductor-cli` edge
   (`paths.rs:34-35`), **not** inside `conductor-core`. Mirror that split; do not call `resolve_under`
   from the new module. Read faults carry `e.kind()` only and never the path
   (`load_envelope.rs:235-238`); absent or malformed is a hard `CoreError`, never a default and never
   a silent widen (security-plan §Input Validation, committed SUT-facing manifests row).

   **The only reader this chunk adds is the gate TEST binary**, which resolves the workspace root from
   `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR/../..` and calls `load(&path)` directly — the `coverage_gate.rs:24-32` shape,
   not the cli edge. No `conductor-cli` `paths.rs` entry is added, because no shipped binary reads the
   ledger. That new reader is RECORDED rather than left implicit (see Expected amendments) — per the
   security extract, an unrecorded reader is the drift, and this repeats the shape
   `2026-09-06-coverage-completeness-gate` escalated and the operator resolved as "record the new
   reader". If a shipped binary ever reads the ledger, it takes the `paths.rs` edge like every other
   committed manifest.

3. **Add `pub fn check_scenario_audit(ledger, catalog) -> crate::Result<()>` in `conductor-core`,**
   modelled arm-for-arm on `check_load_envelope` (`load_envelope.rs:367-398`). It computes two
   measured sets from the loaded catalog and grades each against its ledger array in BOTH directions:
   - **live-assertion set** = scenarios whose `expected` vec is non-empty;
   - **over-tier set** = scenarios where `sum(phases.gap_ms) > slo_tier.deadline_ms()`, consuming
     `SloTier::deadline_ms()` (`scenario.rs:69-73`) rather than re-declaring 5000/20000/90000 (the
     obs-owned single definition, per obs-plan §5 + §10).

   For each, the three failure conditions are `unpinned` / `rotted` / `lost_subject`. The error is a
   named `CoreError` variant carrying scenario names and the ledger's SUT version only — identity-only,
   never a filesystem path or an internal type name (`load_envelope.rs:401-404`'s rule;
   security-plan §Error Handling).

   **Grade every tally, not only the one the verdict keys off (CARRY 1).** The function returns `Err`
   if ANY of the six conditions (three per array) holds, and the message names each non-empty finding
   separately — the failure shape CARRY 1 routes here, and the same discipline `check_load_envelope`
   already applies.

4. **Add the catalog loader sibling `load_catalog(dir, capabilities) -> Result<Vec<Scenario>>` in
   `conductor-core`.** `list_scenarios` returns `ScenarioSummary { name, p_ids, slo_tier }`
   (`scenario_catalog.rs:42-58`) and deliberately carries **no phases**, so it cannot serve the
   over-tier term. This is ADDITIVE — `list_scenarios` keeps its signature and all **six** of its call
   sites are untouched: `drift.rs:362`, `lib.rs:69`, `scenario_catalog.rs:81`, `commands.rs:148`,
   `commands.rs:390`, `main.rs:23` (re-derived by the bare graph query `callee_name =
   'list_scenarios' AND callee_kind = 'fn'`, `rows: 6`). Do not widen `list_scenarios` itself — that
   would make all six boundary members for no gain.

5. **Add the retired-gloss sweep as a `conductor-core` helper + its gate arm.** The REQUIRED form is
   pinned in `verification-matrix.json#v3-05`'s acceptance and is comment-marker-stripped and
   wrap-tolerant: per line, strip the leading `#`; join the lines; collapse whitespace; then test for
   either retired gloss. The plain single-line grep is a **known false negative** and must never be
   substituted. LF is pinned repo-wide (`.gitattributes:2`) and measured 0 of 36 scenarios carry CRLF,
   so the join is host-independent.

6. **Add the three-armed gate test `crates/conductor-core/tests/scenario_audit_gate.rs`.** Crate-local
   `tests/` rather than a `#[cfg(test)]` module, because the subject must be the REAL committed corpus
   (the distinction `coverage_gate.rs:5-9` draws). Resolve the workspace root as
   `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR/../..` — a cargo test binary's CWD is its own package root
   (`coverage_gate.rs:24-32`; `testing.md:84`). Arms:
   - **POSITIVE** — `check_scenario_audit` over the real committed ledger + catalog returns `Ok`.
     Guard vacuity first, as `coverage_gate.rs:37-40` does: assert the catalog is non-empty AND that
     the measured live-assertion set is non-empty, so the gate cannot pass over an empty subject.
   - **NEGATIVE, per row and per direction** — for each ledger row in turn, drop it and assert `Err`
     naming that scenario (`unpinned`); then add a synthetic row naming a scenario that does not
     qualify and assert `Err` naming it (`rotted`); then add a row naming a scenario absent from the
     catalog and assert `Err` naming it (`lost_subject`). Six negative cases, mutating the REAL
     ledger rather than a synthetic fixture.
   - **CLOSED-SET** — assert a minted out-of-set tier (`"<45s"`) fails to deserialize, pinning the
     property `SloTier`'s own definition enforces, so adding a fourth variant breaks this test.
   - **SWEEP CONTROL** — assert the step-5 helper DETECTS a gloss wrapped across two comment lines and
     that the plain single-line form MISSES it, proving the comment-strip-and-join is load-bearing.

7. **Add the synthetic sweep fixture** under `crates/conductor-core/tests/fixtures/` — a committed
   `.toml` whose comment carries a retired gloss wrapped across two lines. Its content lives in a
   COMMITTED file, never inline in the test, and its MEANING is pinned by the step-6 control arm
   asserting both detection and the plain form's miss (`testing.md:75`'s three-part discipline; the
   fixture family test-plan §7 widened at `2026-09-03-conductor-tauri-survivors-dispositioned`). It
   must NOT live under `scenarios/` — that directory is globbed by `scenario_files()` and a fixture
   there would enter the real catalog, and it carries no Pulse P-ID (security-plan §Anti-Patterns).

8. **Register the gate as its own named CI step** in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, modelled on the
   `Coverage-completeness gate` step (`ci.yml:87-93`): assert the ledger file exists (so an absent
   subject fails loudly rather than passing vacuously), then run the specific nextest target. Its own
   named step, no `continue-on-error`, no `if:` (arch §Established Decisions [CI/CD]; the fmt-gate
   shape). A plain `run:` step invoking a fixed toolchain binary with fixed argv is the class of the
   existing `cargo build`/`cargo audit` steps and does **not** move rule (b)'s six governed
   harness-spawn forms (security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Code Patterns; the
   `2026-09-09-workspace-formatting-pass-and-a-fmt-ci-gate` precedent).

9. **Re-export the new public items** from `crates/conductor-core/src/lib.rs` — the export surface is
   not a call, so the P3 caller query does not cover it.
- `contracts/scenario-audit-ledger.toml` — the committed two-array ledger (step 1).

- `crates/conductor-core/src/scenario_audit.rs` — ledger type, loader, `check_scenario_audit`, and the
  gloss-sweep helper (steps 2, 3, 5).
- `crates/conductor-core/tests/scenario_audit_gate.rs` — the three-armed gate test (step 6).
- `crates/conductor-core/tests/fixtures/wrapped-gloss.toml` — the synthetic sweep control (step 7).
- `crates/conductor-core/src/lib.rs` — re-export the new public items; add the module (step 9).

- `crates/conductor-core/src/scenario_catalog.rs` — add `load_catalog` beside `list_scenarios`,
  leaving the latter's signature untouched (step 4).

- `crates/conductor-core/src/error.rs` — one new named `CoreError` variant for the audit gate, joining
  `SutDrift` / `UnbackedCoverage` / `LoadEnvelope` (`error.rs:17-38`).
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — one named gate step after `Coverage-completeness gate` (step 8).

The new gate's own target runs first, then the runner-portability gate test-plan §4 requires, then
the workspace gates. **No smoke entry:** this chunk exercises no boot path — the gate is a static read
over committed files, opens no listener and spawns no sidecar. **No live leg:** the chunk drives no
external process, so no `role = 'probe'` liveness entry and no `stop` form apply. **No `self-verify`
entry:** no UI or visual surface is touched. The supply-chain trio is listed unconditionally so the
wrap can re-pin it (security.md 2026-09-03), with the advisory-db currency probe FIRST.
