- (tests) One check a reader who did not write it can re-run —
  `cargo nextest run -p conductor-core --test scenario_audit_gate --profile ci` — establishes BOTH
  that no committed scenario declares an unsatisfiable assertion and that every scenario's tier is
  accounted for, and it is registered as a CI step that fails the build; per
  `verification-matrix.json#v3-06` (per test-plan §6 Coverage-matrix completeness gate).

- (tests) The gate is demonstrated able to fail as well as to pass by SIX in-suite negative arms —
  `unpinned` / `rotted` / `lost_subject` against each of the two ledger arrays — each mutating the
  REAL committed ledger and asserting the error names the offending scenario (per test-plan §6).

- (tests) No assertion in the gate is keyed on a literal count or a fixed id range; every predicate is
  exact-set equality against the catalog as loaded (per test-plan §6 verification signal + §1 Path 6).

- (tests) The sweep control proves the comment-marker-stripped wrap-tolerant form DETECTS a gloss
  wrapped across two comment lines and the plain single-line form MISSES it (per test-plan §7
  Self-bootstrapping requirement).

- (tests) The new target is green under both `cargo nextest run -p conductor-core --test
  scenario_audit_gate --profile ci` and `cargo test -p conductor-core`, with no retries configured
  (per test-plan §4 Framework + §10 Zero-flakiness budget).

- (arch) The gate lives in the existing `conductor-core` member, adds no workspace crate and no sixth
  `agent-run.{sh,ps1}` command; a red surfaces as a named `CoreError` variant, never a `Verdict` or
  `ReportState` (per architecture.md §Cross-cutting Patterns [Verdict/error wall]).

- (arch) The gate opens no listener, spawns no sidecar and reaches no non-loopback target; it reads
  committed files only (per architecture.md §Cross-cutting Patterns [Trust boundary]).

- (security) The ledger's `default_path()` is a hard-coded relative constant with no `CONDUCTOR_*`
  override handle, and `load()` takes an already-resolved path — the `LoadEnvelope` two-part split
  (`load_envelope.rs:227-234`), with `resolve_under` left to the caller's edge and NOT called from
  `conductor-core`; absent or malformed is a hard `CoreError` naming `e.kind()` only, never the path
  (per security-plan §Input Validation, committed SUT-facing manifests row).

- (security) The one reader this chunk adds — the gate test binary resolving from `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`
  — is explicitly recorded, since an unrecorded reader is the drift (per security-plan §Input
  Validation, env-var path handles row; the `2026-09-06-coverage-completeness-gate` resolution).

- (security) The gate's failure output and every committed artifact this chunk authors contain zero
  absolute host paths and zero internal seam-crate struct names (per security-plan §Security
  Anti-Patterns → Logging).

- (security) The CI step is a fixed-program/fixed-argv `run:` step in the existing
  `.github/workflows/ci.yml` with no shell string, no `Invoke-Expression` and no `continue-on-error`,
  so rule (b)'s six governed harness-spawn forms do not move (per security-plan §Security
  Anti-Patterns → Code Patterns rule (b)).

- (obs) The tier term consumes `SloTier::deadline_ms()` rather than re-declaring 5000/20000/90000, so
  the corpus-side probe and the envelope-side conformance gate assert the same enum (per obs-plan §5
  Per-surface/per-path metrics + §10 Performance budgets).

- (obs) The gate's verdict and per-scenario findings are machine-parseable from the CI job log with no
  dashboard and no human-review step; no absolute host path reaches `logs/agent-latest.jsonl` or any
  `runs/**.jsonl` (per obs-plan §2 Agent-readable invariants + §9 Pipeline integration).

- (a11y) The `a11y` job remains declared in the workflow, not conditioned on or gated behind the new
  step, retaining `CONDUCTOR_A11Y_STRICT` and its printed-verdict assertion (per a11y-plan §11 → CI).

- (design/layouts) The chunk mints no new per-P-ID bracket label, no seventh lamp, no sixth
  `ReportState` and no new ANSI or token entry; it adds no `conductor` verb (per layout-templates
  §cli Component — Primary content block 2).

- Spec anchors: architecture.md §Established Decisions [Accepted Capability Set] / [CI/CD] /
  [Module Boundaries] · §Cross-cutting Patterns [Verdict/error wall] [Trust boundary] · security-plan
  §Input Validation · §Error Handling · §Security Anti-Patterns → Code Patterns rule (b) · test-plan
  §1 Path 6 · §4 · §6 · §7 · §9 · §10 · §11 · obs-plan §5 · §6 · §9 · §10 · a11y-plan §9 · §11 ·
  layout-templates §cli Component — Primary content block 2 · design-system §Surface: cli / Tokens.

- Research files inspected: `crates/conductor-report/tests/coverage_gate.rs`,
  `crates/conductor-core/src/{scenario.rs,scenario_catalog.rs,load_envelope.rs,error.rs,phase_spec.rs}`,
  `crates/conductor-verify/src/{extract.rs,slo.rs}`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.gitattributes`,
  `scripts/mutation-gate.py`, `contracts/pulse-load-envelope.toml`, and six `andromeda-pulse` files at
  HEAD `83d4060`.

- **A `scripts/` Python instrument re-parsing the TOMLs — REJECTED.** Five extracts converge against
  it: security-plan §Input Validation warns a second parse path "grades the corpus but validates
  nothing"; test-plan §4 requires reusing the loader seam; obs-plan §5 requires the tier thresholds
  come from the single obs-owned definition, which a script would have to re-declare as literals. The
  Rust host also inherits CI registration for free through the existing workspace test run.

- **Widening `list_scenarios` to carry phases — REJECTED.** It would make all six call sites boundary
  members for no gain; an additive `load_catalog` sibling leaves them untouched.

- **Re-running the three probes from `2026-09-15-scenario-tier-honesty`'s gate fence verbatim —
  REJECTED.** They are not committed anywhere (`grep -rln 'slo_tier' scripts/ .github/` returns only
  `agent-run.{sh,ps1}`, and that hit is the report-envelope jq projection at `agent-run.sh:293`), they
  re-declare the tier literals, and probe 3's known-positive control names a file that no longer
  carries the gloss.

- **A count probe over the corpus (`grep -c` asserting `last line 2`) — REJECTED.** test-plan §6 bans
  keying a gate on a row count; the exact-set ledger assertion is the sanctioned form.

- **Raising the bar to discrimination-against-own-stimulus — REJECTED for a static gate.** test-plan
  §11 routes a "does this token reach the report BECAUSE of the stimulus" claim to the live/operator
  gate; it is answerable only with deterministic mode off. The finding is recorded in the ledger
  instead, with its reason, so it is enforced rather than remembered.

- **Do not put any fixture under `scenarios/`** — `scenario_files()` globs that directory, so a
  fixture there joins the real catalog and would carry no Pulse P-ID.

- **Order sensitivity:** the step numbers are a reading order, not a build order. `load_catalog`
  (step 4) must exist before `check_scenario_audit`'s over-tier term (step 3) compiles, since the term
  consumes it; build step 4 first. Step 1's ledger seeding is independent of both — it is a direct
  computation over the committed TOMLs, not a call into step 3.

- **The ledger seeds GREEN by design.** Both corpus properties already hold at HEAD, so the gate is
  live and green from its first run; it is a regression guard plus a precision record, not a
  measurement this chunk moves. There is no red→green forecast to measure. What MUST be measured is
  the first green run's arm list, read arm-by-arm — `verification-harness.md:66`: a red baseline
  validates only the failing direction and cannot tell you the green case counts correctly.

- **Re-derive the eleven `over_tier` rows rather than copying them** from `v3-05`'s `notes` line, and
  record what the re-run measures. Predicted: 11 rows (9 original ceiling-posture + `ack-cooldown` +
  `severity-tier-autonomous`) — if the re-derivation disagrees, the measurement wins and the
  disagreement is recorded, not reconciled away.

- **The ledger's grounds are SUT-version-pinned.** They were measured at `andromeda-pulse` HEAD
  `83d4060`; a Pulse change to `severity_label`, `map_l4_incident_severity` or the deterministic
  fixture rots them. Record that version in the ledger header so the rot is visible rather than silent
  (the TIME axis — an alignment verified against an external system is a point-in-time measurement).

- **Expected amendments (wrap):** `architecture.md` §Occupied Resources — register
  `contracts/scenario-audit-ledger.toml` (new on-disk artifact), the new `conductor-core` module, and
  the new `ci.yml` gate step in the CI gate-set enumeration. Per the arch extract, a new CI gate
  restates that enumeration at five arch sites (the `2026-09-09` fmt-gate fan-out).

- **Expected amendments (wrap):** `security-plan.md` §Input Validation — record the gate test binary
  as a new READER of a committed manifest resolving from `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`, joining
  `conductor-report --test coverage_gate` in that row; the duty binds per READER, and an unrecorded
  reader is the drift.

- **Expected amendments (wrap):** `test-plan.md` §6 — record the scenario-audit gate beside the

title: ARMED ORPHAN — for wrap P5 route-resolve (CARRY 1, mutation-gate timeout blindness)

data.head: ### ARMED ORPHAN — for wrap P5 route-resolve (CARRY 1, mutation-gate timeout blindness)

body:
An IN-VERSION follow-up with no plausible owner entry, presented per `route-resolve.md:24` so the
halt arrives armed rather than as prose.

**The fact, re-verified at HEAD 2026-09-16:** `scripts/mutation-gate.py` computes its verdict from
`missed.txt` (`:137`) and `caught.txt` (`:138`) and never reads `timeout.txt` — the file's only
`timeout` token is its module docstring (`grep -c 'timeout' scripts/mutation-gate.py` → 1), so a
caught→timeout regression passes the gate silently. `.github/workflows/` carries no mutation-gate
step. No markerless route entry names the mutation gate. `v3-06`'s acceptance does not reach it.

**Why it is not absorbed here:** the repair is two separable pieces of unequal kind. Reading
`timeout.txt` is a small patch; **rostering the fifteen timeouts** from
`2026-09-14-emit-scrubber-and-percentile-math-under-test` (`evidence/disposition-ledger.md`, tally
`| timeouts | 16 | 15 |`) is a per-item disposition — judgment, not a patch — and folding it here
would mix that chunk's outcome with the audit gate's own measurement, which is the thing this chunk
exists to establish. The CARRY's own text routes the failure SHAPE here, and that shape IS applied
(step 3, and the six negative arms).
**The four dispositions:**

1. **Pin to a named entry** — the nearest plausible is `Full-gate regression over the moved surfaces`
   (`working-route.md:49`, Epoch 5). Weak fit: that entry re-runs gates over surfaces this version
   moved; it does not repair an instrument, and burying a fifteen-item judgment inside a regression
   sweep is the mixing hazard named above.

2. **Mint an entry** (route register kept) — **my lean.** In-version, Epoch 5, ordered BEFORE
   `Full-gate regression over the moved surfaces` so that sweep runs over a repaired gate. It keeps
   the patch and the fifteen dispositions together as one owned unit, which is what they are.

3. **`residuals.md`** — wrong here: the blindness is live now and silently passes regressions in this
   version, so deferring it past 0.3.0 leaves a gate asserting less than it appears to.
4. **Drop** — wrong: the blindness is measured, not hypothesised.

**Chunk:** Scenario-assertion audit gate — one mechanical re-runnable check establishing both epoch-2
outcomes (no committed scenario declares an unsatisfiable assertion · every scenario's tier is
accounted for), registered as a build gate and demonstrated able to fail as well as to pass.
**Date:** 2026-09-16
**Commits:** none since `last_wrap` — the tree carries this chunk uncommitted; HEAD is
`05a7c3f feat(2026-09-15-scenario-tier-honesty)`, the prior wrap's commit, still unpushed (1 ahead of
`origin/build/conductor-0.3.0` at this write; this wrap's commit leaves it 2).

The check is **registered** — either as a CI gate that fails the build or as a named operator
instrument — so the property is enforced by something rather than by memory, and it is **demonstrated
able to fail as well as to pass** (a known-positive control per probe).

- **In scope:** a mechanical check (or check set) plus its registration surface and its failure
  demonstration; the probe forms themselves; whatever enumeration/classification the check needs to
  make the currently-prose-held facts machine-establishable.

- **Not in scope:** changing any scenario's declared assertions or tiers. Both corpus properties are
  already TRUE at HEAD — `v3-04` and `v3-05` are `verified`. This chunk makes them *checkable*, not
  *true*. A probe that goes red here means the probe is wrong, not the corpus.

- **Not in scope:** retiring either of the two surviving `[[expected]]` blocks. They were deliberately
  left standing; the route entry states that retiring live coverage on a false equivalence "would be
  the opposite of solving".
- **Not in scope:** the SUT. No Pulse change, no live leg. This is a static check over committed data.
- **Scope law:** the check opens no listener and spawns no sidecar — it reads committed files only.
- `scenarios/*.toml` — **read-only** (36 files; 2 carry a live `[[expected]]`, 36 carry `slo_tier`).

- `scripts/` — the likely home of the check, beside `scripts/mutation-gate.py` (7119 B) and
  `scripts/agent-run.{sh,ps1}`.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — if the registration is a CI gate.
- `conductor-0.3.0/verification-matrix.json#v3-06` — the capability this chunk claims.

- `crates/conductor-core` — the catalog-gate home if the check ships as Rust. **Verified at P3:** the
  crate already owns `SloTier::deadline_ms()` (a code-native closed enum, `scenario.rs:52-73`), the
  `check_*` gate family (`drift.rs:79/155`, `load_envelope.rs:367`) and a crate-local `tests/` dir
  (2 files). The `coverage_gate.rs` precedent sits in `conductor-report` ONLY because it must reach
  both sides of a dependency edge (`coverage_gate.rs:11-13`) — a constraint that does NOT apply here,
  so `conductor-core` is reachable. The language/host fork itself stays open for P4.

All three annotations standing at an annotation position on the taken-up entry are `CARRY:`. There is
no `PREREQ:` and no `BLOCKED-ON:`. Every named coordinate below was re-verified against the artifact
at promotion; **mechanism claims are preserved verbatim with their original marker text and carry
`[inferred]`** — statedness is not measurement at HEAD, and P3's scope premise closure sets the depth.

title: CARRY 1 — the mutation gate cannot enforce a timeout criterion

data.head: ### CARRY 1 — the mutation gate cannot enforce a timeout criterion

body:

> verdict from `missed.txt` against the roster and never reads `timeout.txt`, so a caught→timeout
> regression passes it silently (measured at
> `2026-09-14-emit-scrubber-and-percentile-math-under-test`: the file's only `timeout` token is in its
> module docstring; that run's FIFTEEN timeouts are held solely by the chunk's own

> this entry authors a mechanical check that must establish BOTH outcomes, and the same failure shape
> applies: grade on every tally the claim rests on, not only the one the verdict keys off.
> Operator-directed at the 2026-09-15 wrap; target chosen at an armed halt, no markerless entry naming
> the mutation gate.

title: CARRY 2 — "satisfiable" is now the whole question

data.head: ### CARRY 2 — "satisfiable" is now the whole question

body:
> "satisfiable" is now the whole question, because the corpus has exactly TWO live `[[expected]]`
> blocks left — `root-span-error-scope` and `span-status-error-detection`, both `Contains "error"`
> (`grep -l '^[[expected]]' scenarios/*.toml` → 2 of 36 at
> `2026-09-15-remaining-structurally-dead-declarations-retired`). Both are satisfiable and both are
> WEAK for the same measured reason: the token they match is the deterministic fixture's pinned
> severity, not their own stimulus — `severity_label` maps every severity to a lowercase literal and
> the fixture pins one severity for every incident (measured at that chunk against `andromeda-pulse`
> HEAD `83d4060`: `crates/interpretation/src/markdown.rs` `severity_label`;
> `pulse-app/src/deterministic_inference.rs:42-43`). A check that asks only "can this token appear?"
> passes both, so this entry's mechanical check has to decide whether satisfiable is the right bar or
> whether discrimination-against-own-stimulus is. They were deliberately left standing rather than
> retired — retiring live coverage on a false equivalence would be the opposite of solving.
**Coordinate re-verification (promotion, 2026-09-16) — all confirmed:**

- Exactly **2 of 36** scenarios carry `[[expected]]`: `root-span-error-scope.toml` and
  `span-status-error-detection.toml`. Confirmed.

- Both are `kind = "Contains"`, `expected = "error"`; classes differ (`CalibrationRegion` vs `Hard`).
  Confirmed — the class difference is NOT stated by the CARRY and matters to any grading design.

- SUT repo present at `D:/dev/projects/andromeda-pulse`, HEAD **`83d4060`** — matches the cited HEAD
  exactly.

- `severity_label` at `crates/interpretation/src/markdown.rs:359` maps
  `Info|Warn|Error|Critical → "info"|"warn"|"error"|"critical"`. Confirmed lowercase.

- `pulse-app/src/deterministic_inference.rs:42` is `"severity": "autonomous"` inside
  `CANNED_L4_OUTPUT_JSON`. Confirmed present at the cited line.

- **[premise-corrected: the CARRY's arithmetic DOES close — `map_l4_incident_severity` is the link it
  never named, and the full chain re-derives TRUE at SUT HEAD `83d4060`.]** At promotion this bullet
  recorded that the CARRY's linking arithmetic failed to close on its own coordinates, because the
  fixture pins `"severity": "autonomous"` while the assertions match `"error"`. That doubt was MY
  error, not the CARRY's: a one-hop mapping the CARRY omitted joins the two. The chain, measured at
  P3 against `andromeda-pulse` HEAD `83d4060`:
  1. `deterministic_inference.rs:126` returns `CANNED_L4_OUTPUT_JSON` **regardless of prompt or
     schema** whenever `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC` is truthy (`:18`);
  2. that fixture pins `"severity": "autonomous"` (`:42`) → `interpretation::schema::Severity`
     (`schema.rs:121-128`, `#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]`) `::Autonomous`;
  3. `map_l4_incident_severity` (`inference_runtime.rs:697-703`) maps
     `L4Severity::Autonomous → IncidentSeverity::Error`;
  4. `inference_runtime.rs:784` binds that to `severity`, and `:847-868` — the SOLE production
     `Incident` construction site — writes it to `incident.severity`;
  5. `assemble_report` (`markdown.rs:257`) renders `severity_label(incident.severity)`, and
     `severity_label` (`markdown.rs:359-366`) maps `Severity::Error → "error"`;
  6. `markdown.rs:134` pushes that label into the report markdown, which Conductor's
     `observe` folds into `Observation.text` (`extract.rs:99-104`) — the exact haystack
     `ComparisonKind::Contains` searches (`slo.rs:51`).

  **So CARRY-2 is correct: in deterministic mode every incident renders `severity_label = "error"`
  irrespective of what the scenario emitted, and both surviving assertions pass on a token their own
  stimulus did not produce.** `v3-04`'s verified acceptance is ALSO correct and not in conflict — it
  claims *satisfiability*, which holds. The two statements sit at different bars, which is precisely
  the distinction this chunk must decide rather than a contradiction to resolve.

- **Verified at P3, and the tests domain supplies the ruling.** The bar choice — *satisfiable* vs
  *discrimination-against-own-stimulus* — is a scope fork the entry leaves open, and `v3-06`'s
  acceptance asks only for "no committed scenario declares an unsatisfiable assertion", i.e. the
  *satisfiable* bar. The tests extract settles which bar a CI check may carry: the satisfiable bar is
  a declarative property of committed files and is gradeable here, whereas a
  discrimination-against-own-stimulus bar asks whether a token reaches the report *because of* the
  scenario's stimulus — a SUT-behaviour claim test-plan §11 routes to the live/operator gate and never
  to a static check. The measured chain above is what makes that ruling bite: the discrimination
  question is answerable only by driving a live Pulse in non-deterministic mode.

title: Plan — 2026-09-17-a11y-routine-arm-terminal-on-the-measured-configuration: "The a11y routine arm's terminal, on the measured configuration"

data.head: # Plan — 2026-09-17-a11y-routine-arm-terminal-on-the-measured-configuration: "The a11y routine arm's terminal, on the measured configuration"

body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-09-17-a11y-routine-arm-terminal-on-the-measured-configuration · **Version:** conductor-0.3.0 · **Generated:** 2026-09-17T09:00Z

Reach the a11y routine arm's terminal by fixing the defect that keeps it red and by moving the `a11y` CI job
onto the configuration on which the arm is measured to run. Two halves, one outcome.

**The assertion half.** `accessibility.e2e.ts:384` (SC 2.1.1) fails because `tabCycleNames()` (`:185`) walks
the Tab order looking for a `BODY` sentinel that does not exist in this webview's focus cycle. It therefore
exhausts both 20-iteration caps, starts collecting from an ARBITRARY position, and reports a truncated visit
tally where the expectation reports a DOM cardinality. The local red baseline (dev host, runtime 153,
`runs/a11y-e2e.log`) printed the walk verbatim: a six-long cycle `DIV_report → Minimize → Close → Filter →
Start → DIV_cov` repeating with no `BODY`, `20 reached` against `6 reached`. The same run shows `:397`
(SC 2.4.3) failing as `Start then DIV` — **the two reds share one root cause**, and `:397`'s pass on runtime
131 was the walk happening to stop one position before `Minimize window`. Repairing the walk fixes both and
makes the pair environment-independent, which a11y-plan §11 → CI requires of every assertion in this harness
and test-plan §10's zero-flakiness budget requires of anything about to be gated.

**The configuration half.** HEAD's `a11y` job is not the configuration that ran the arm. It is
`runs-on: windows-2025` (`ci.yml:250`), it gates on an Evergreen `152+` floor (`:282`), and it launches the
asserting step through `a11y-limited-token-launch.ps1` at Medium integrity (`:431`). The measured-green run
35192876641 was `windows-2022`, a coherent 131/131 driver+runtime pair, High integrity, no launcher. All
three deltas are recorded at HEAD as measured-but-not-acted-on and each states it needs an operator ruling;
**operator ruled 2026-09-17 at this phase's P4: move to the measured configuration, no driver pin.** The
`≥152` floor is retired as a posture because it is falsified on its own terms — not necessary (coherent
131/131 works), not sufficient (coherent 152/152 fails, run 34654076633), and destructive (run 35185153012
fetched 153 over a native 131). Its replacement asserts the subject the evidence actually names:
driver/runtime major COHERENCE.

Provenance in brief: the walk's required property per a11y-plan §5 (Focus order per layout →
run-console-idle) and §11 → CI; the no-literal-count and both-directions shapes per test-plan §6; the
never-skip / never-`continue-on-error` gate posture per test-plan §9 and architecture §Established Decisions
[CI/CD]; the egress and spawn-form constraints per security-plan §Threat Model Summary → Infrastructure and
§Security Anti-Patterns → Code Patterns rule (b).

1. **Replace the `BODY`-sentinel walk with identity-based cycle detection** in
   `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/test/a11y/accessibility.e2e.ts`, at `tabCycleNames()` (`:185-198`). The helper
   must stop depending on ever reaching `BODY`. Per visit it records BOTH the accessible name (via the
   existing `activeName()`, `:165`) and the focused element's **index within the live focusable set** —
   the set being `document.querySelectorAll` over the selector already used at `:381`, re-queried inside the
   page at the same moment as the visit. Walk until an index **repeats**, capped at twice the focusable count
   plus two; the cycle is the run of visits from the first occurrence of the repeated index up to (not
   including) the repeat. A visit that resolves to **no** member of the set (index `-1` — a host-chrome or
   `BODY` stop) is recorded in the returned data for the failure message but is excluded both from the index
   set and from repeat detection. If no index repeats within the cap, return what was collected so the
   assertion fails naming the observed walk rather than hanging or truncating silently.

2. **Re-base SC 2.1.1 (`:373-391`) on set equality over element identity.** The criterion is that the cycle's
   reached index set equals the full focusable index set `{0 … n-1}`, asserted in **both directions** (no
   focusable unreached; nothing reached outside the set). Keep the existing shape of folding observed context
   into the compared value (`frontend.md` 2026-09-02 — `@wdio/globals`' `expect` has no message argument).
   The message records visits and distinct elements separately — never a bare count.
2b. **Repair the SECOND vacuous-by-construction site in the same block** — `:387-390`. The `missing:` half of
   that assertion carries real signal (a set-membership filter over `['Minimize window','Close window']`),
   but the `order:` half interpolates `names.join(' | ')` on BOTH sides of the `.toBe()`, exactly as `:384`
   does, so it is decorative and cannot fail. Re-base the `order:` half on a value the expectation does not
   also supply — the focusable set's own DOM-order names — or drop it and let the `missing:` half stand
   alone. Leaving it is not an option: this chunk closes the vacuity class, and a half-vacuous neighbour two
   lines away would be claimed closed while still asserting nothing.

3. **Re-base SC 2.4.3 (`:393-408`) on rotation-aligned order equality.** Rotate the detected cycle so it
   begins at focusable index `0`; assert the rotated index sequence is exactly `0,1,…,n-1` (the Tab order is
   DOM order), and assert that the first two members' accessible names are `Minimize window` then
   `Close window` (the a11y-plan §5 run-console-idle layout claim, and layout-templates §Component — Header's
   minimize-before-close render order). This is strictly stronger than the current `names[0]`/`names[1]` read
   and no longer depends on where the walk happened to start. Leave the `positiveTabindex` assertion at
   `:401-407` unchanged.

4. **Move the `a11y` job to the measured runner image** — `.github/workflows/ci.yml:250`,
   `runs-on: windows-2025` → `windows-2022`. Update the step's own explanatory comment (`:240-249`) so it
   records the ruling and its basis rather than describing the finding as un-acted-on.

5. **Remove the Evergreen fetch and install entirely** — `.github/workflows/ci.yml:282` and its step body,
   including the fwlink `Invoke-WebRequest` at `:313`. On a `windows-2022` image whose native runtime is 131
   the existing floor-conditional would fire and install a newer runtime over it (the measured destructive
   case, run 35185153012 → runtime 153). This retires the project's only non-loopback egress at HEAD.
5b. **Pin msedgedriver to the runtime major already present on the image** — a new step replacing the one
   removed above, an exact replay of the configuration that measured green at run 35192876641. Read the
   runtime major from the two `EdgeUpdate` client registry keys the removed step already used, fetch the
   msedgedriver build for THAT major, and point `CONDUCTOR_MSEDGEDRIVER` at it. The version is **derived
   from the image, never authored into the workflow**, so the pin cannot drift on its own — which is the
   property the fwlink lacked (it carries no version selector, so every job took whatever was latest). It is
   a GATE: no `continue-on-error`, no `if:`. Print the runtime and driver majors by name so the job log
   carries both readings. Report registry keys in the colon-free `reg.exe` form, never the PowerShell
   provider form, so the host-path hygiene anchor cannot trip on them (`host-win32.md` 2026-09-11).
5c. **Carry the pre-execution Authenticode gate onto the pinned driver, verbatim from the sixth governed
   form** — the shape at `ci.yml:317-326`: `Get-AuthenticodeSignature -LiteralPath`, exit 1 unless
   `Status -eq 'Valid'`, exit 1 unless the signer subject matches `O=Microsoft Corporation`, and a
   precondition line carrying the handle NAME and the state only — never the path. The driver is another
   non-repo-derived binary arriving from the network at job time, so it inherits the third dependency
   class's sole admitting control unchanged (per security-plan §Dependency Security). Neither the fetch nor
   the verification step may carry `continue-on-error`.

6. **Fold the now-redundant version diagnostic into that gate** — the step at `.github/workflows/ci.yml:368`
   (`WebView2 driver + runtime versions (diagnostic)`, `continue-on-error: true`) prints exactly the two
   facts step 5's gate prints. Remove it; the gate is the single source, per architecture's "the gate IS the
   assertion, never a shell re-statement" pattern (§Established Decisions [CI/CD]).

7. **Invoke the routine leg directly in the asserting step** — `.github/workflows/ci.yml:389-448`. Keep the
   `EDGEWEBDRIVER` / `CONDUCTOR_MSEDGEDRIVER` preconditions (`:395-405`) and the `$LASTEXITCODE` handling
   unchanged; replace the `a11y-limited-token-launch.ps1` invocation (`:431-435`) with a direct call of the
   leg entry point, so the step runs at the hosted runner's native High integrity. Remove the token-witness
   readback block (`:438-448`), whose subject only exists inside a launched process. Rewrite the step's
   integrity comment (`:413-430`) to record the ruling and the measurement behind it.
- (none)

- `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/test/a11y/accessibility.e2e.ts` — `tabCycleNames()` (`:185`), SC 2.1.1
  (`:373-391`), SC 2.4.3 (`:393-408`). **Caller threading from the code-graph, not memory:**
  `tabCycleNames` has exactly TWO callers, both in this file — `tabCycleNames @ accessibility.e2e.ts:374`
  and `@ accessibility.e2e.ts:394` (graph lines 373/393, cited +1 per the cookbook's 0-indexed rule). Both
  are boundary members of this chunk because the helper's return shape changes.

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — the `a11y` job: `:250` (label), `:282` (install → coherence gate), `:368`
  (redundant diagnostic removed), `:389-448` (direct invocation, witness readback removed).

- **Not modified:** `scripts/agent-run.{sh,ps1}` — `Assert-A11yVerdict` / `assert_a11y_verdict` grade the
  banner, the `Spec Files:` failed count and skips `> 2`; none is a pass tally, so 10/2/2 → 12/0/2 needs no
  change (`agent-run.ps1:62,68-100` · `agent-run.sh:188,193-226`).

- **Not modified:** `scripts/a11y-limited-token-launch.ps1` and `scripts/a11y-token-witness.ps1` — they
  remain in the tree and remain invoked by the driver-alone diagnostics (`ci.yml:500,529,547`), so the
  seventh governed spawn form keeps its registration and only its call-site set changes.

- **Companion sweep** — `grep -rn 'tabCycleNames' crates/conductor-tauri/ui --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx`:
  **3 hits · 3 in the modify-set · 0 elsewhere**. Sibling sweep on the focusable selector literal
  `grep -rn 'tabindex="-1"' …`: **2 hits · 1 in the modify-set · 1 no-change** (`screen-reader.e2e.ts:207`

body:
- (a11y) The SC 2.1.1 assertion compares the reachability property as set equality over element identity —
  every focusable reached, nothing reached outside the set — and carries no literal count and no name-keyed
  set (per a11y-plan §5 Keyboard Navigation → Focus order per layout → run-console-idle). Claims
  `verification-matrix.json#v3-02`.

- (a11y) Both SC 2.1.1 and SC 2.4.3 are environment-independent: neither's pass/fail varies with where the
  walk starts or how many times the cycle repeats (per a11y-plan §11 A11y Anti-Patterns → CI, "NO assertion
  in this harness is platform-dependent").

- (tests) **No assertion in the Operable block compares a value against itself.** Neither `:384` nor
  `:387-390` interpolates the same expression on both sides of its `.toBe()`; every compared half is
  derivable only from the DOM, not from the expectation. Verified by reading both assertions, not by the
  suite going green — a vacuous assertion passes (per test-plan §6, static-gate Verification signal).

- (tests) `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run --e2e` prints `[a11y] verdict asserted` and lacks
  `[a11y] leg skipped` on the dev host — 12 passing / 0 failing / 2 skipped, against the measured
  2026-09-17 baseline of 10 / 2 / 2 (per test-plan §3, `run` → CI stage selectors, `--e2e`).

- (security) The non-loopback egress count is **one before and one after** — the fwlink is gone (`grep -c`
  for that host over `.github/workflows/ci.yml` returns 0, down from exactly 1 at HEAD, `ci.yml:313`) and
  the pinned msedgedriver host appears exactly once. The count is asserted by two POSITIVE identity probes,
  never by a pattern expressing "everything except loopback" — ERE has no negative lookahead and such a
  guard passes unconditionally (`host-win32.md` 2026-09-08) (per security-plan §Threat Model Summary →
  Infrastructure, Networking).

- (security) The pinned driver carries the pre-execution Authenticode gate verbatim from the sixth governed
  form — `Status -eq 'Valid'` AND an `O=Microsoft Corporation` signer, both exiting non-zero otherwise, with
  neither the fetch nor the verification step carrying `continue-on-error`, and the precondition line
  carrying the handle NAME and state only, never the path (per security-plan §Dependency Security, third
  dependency class).

- (security) The governed harness-spawn registry gains no eighth crossing and the seventh form keeps its
  `-File`-only, pre-composition-guarded shape; only its call-site set changes (per security-plan §Security
  Anti-Patterns → Code Patterns rule (b)).

- (arch) The `a11y` job's asserting step still carries no `continue-on-error` and no `if:`, and the
  coherence gate replacing the install is likewise unguarded, so a silent no-op cannot read as a pass (per
  architecture.md §Established Decisions [CI/CD]).

- (arch) The change lands in the npm subtree and the workflow only — no Cargo workspace member, no
  `[workspace.dependencies]` delta, no `package-lock.json` change (per architecture.md §Occupied Resources —
  Frontend asset subtree).

- (obs) The a11y violation record's key set is unchanged and no absolute host path appears in the arm's
  uploaded artifacts or in any new assertion/diagnostic text (per obs-plan §3 Harness Contract — Log format
  JSON schema; §9 Log conformance check).

- (design) No token, hex, ms literal or palette row is added or changed; the idle console's control
  composition is untouched — the assertion follows the design, never the reverse (per design-system
  §Surface: desktop-webview → Tokens; §Anti-Patterns → Per-Surface Bans).

- **CI-witnessed, spanning two runs by construction:** the `a11y` job's own conclusion is `success` on the
  run whose `headSha` equals the operator's pushed sha, with the coherence gate passing and the routine arm
  printing its green verdict. The acceptance names the run id the final probe entry printed.

- Spec anchors: a11y-plan §3 (Harness Contract), §5 (Keyboard Navigation → Focus order per layout), §9 (CI
  Integration, E2E artifacts row), §10 (SLO Invariants), §11 (Anti-Patterns → CI / Keyboard / SLO) ·
  test-plan §3 (`--e2e` stage selector), §6 (Drivers per surface; static-gate Verification signal), §9
  (E2E-webview stage row), §10 (Zero-flakiness budget) · architecture §Established Decisions [CI/CD],
  §Occupied Resources (Ports · Environment variables · Frontend asset subtree), §Cross-cutting Patterns
  (Trust boundary), §Infrastructure Patterns (Build system) · security-plan §Dependency Security (third
  dependency class), §Security Anti-Patterns → Code Patterns rule (b), §Threat Model Summary →
  Infrastructure (Networking) · layout-templates §Wireframe (Run console, idle), §Component — Header,
  §Component — Hero / signature section, §Surface: cli — Primary screens · design-system §Iconography,
  §Component Patterns 1/5, §Anti-Patterns · obs-plan §3, §9, §11.

- Research files inspected: `accessibility.e2e.ts`, `Titlebar.tsx`, `RunControls.tsx`, `CoverageMatrix.tsx`,
  `RunReport.tsx`, `App.tsx`, `wdio.conf.ts`, `ci.yml`, `agent-run.sh`, `agent-run.ps1`, plus the measured
  red baseline `runs/a11y-e2e.log`.

- **`new Set(names).size` against `focusableCount` — REJECTED, measured wrong.** The idle console has six
  focusable elements but only FIVE distinct accessible names: `CoverageMatrix.tsx:60` and `RunReport.tsx:47`
  are both unnamed `<div tabIndex={0}>` scroll regions and `activeName()` returns `el.tagName` for each, so
  both project to `DIV`. The comparison yields 5 against 6 and leaves the assertion red. Confirmed in the
  baseline log's own bracket list.

- **Giving the two scroll regions `aria-label`s to break the collision — REJECTED.** Both carry a comment
  recording that the name deliberately sits on the inner `<table>`, because a named focusable region made
  NVDA read the whole table in one utterance (SR rows S0-09 / E0-05). The assertion follows the design.

- **Fixing `:384` only and leaving `:397` — REJECTED on measurement.** They share one root cause; `:397`
  passed on runtime 131 by walk-start luck and would ship as a latent flake into the configuration this
  chunk claims green.

- **Adding or removing a control, or a `tabindex`, to reconcile a count — BANNED** (design-system
  §Anti-Patterns → Per-Surface Bans; layout-templates §Wireframe — Run console (idle); a11y-plan §11 →
  Keyboard, never `tabindex > 0`).

- **Pinning msedgedriver (escalation 4) — DECLINED by the operator at this phase's P4.** It would open a
  second non-loopback egress and admit a fourth job-time-fetched binary under the third dependency class.
  The coherence gate is what converts the resulting assumption into a loud, named failure instead.

- **Purging the now-spent `continue-on-error` diagnostics (`ci.yml:488-760`) — DELIBERATELY NOT DONE.** They
  do not gate, and removing them is neither required by the terminal nor covered by the operator's ruling.
  Recorded below as a route candidate.

- **A ci-probe detached ref — NOT AUTHORIZED for this chunk.** The predecessor's was authorized by a named
  2026-09-16 directive; no such directive exists here, so the CI half rides the operator's ordinary push.

- **RETRACTED FORECAST — the image's coherence WAS exercised, and the measurement is negative.** An earlier
  draft of this plan predicted the coherence gate would pass on `windows-2022` "because the image's own
  driver coherence was never exercised". That was false, and `ci.yml:246` named the run ids that disprove it.
  Verified from the runs themselves at this phase's P5:

  | run | title | runtime | msedgedriver | outcome |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 35186499514 | `ci-probe(win2022-native-runtime)` | 131.0.2903.86 | **151**.0.4129.107 | `session not created: This version of Microsoft Edge WebDriver only supports Microsoft Edge version 151 · Current browser version is 131.0.2903.86` |
  | 35185153012 | `ci-probe(win2022)` | 153.0.4234.32 | **152**.0.4191.77 | failure |

  Two consequences, both load-bearing. (1) On an unpinned `windows-2022` the image is **incoherent** — a
  floating msedgedriver over a native 131 runtime — so a coherence GATE there does not carry an unmeasured
  forecast, it carries a measured failure. (2) The driver major is **not stable between runs** (151, then
  152), so the gate would fail *unpredictably* rather than consistently. The coherence of the green run
  35192876641 was PRODUCED BY the driver pin that the "no driver pin" ruling removes.

  Readings taken with the step-source echo filtered out (`verification-harness.md:66a` — GitHub Actions
  echoes each step's own source, so the unexpanded `$before` / `$var` copies are not readings).

- **RULING (operator, 2026-09-17 P5 re-ruling): escalation 4 — the second non-loopback egress — RATIFIED,
  on a measured NET NARROWING.** The original "no driver pin" ruling predated the measurement above and was
  re-taken with it in front of the operator. Steps 5/5b/5c implement it. The basis, recorded because the
  registration owed at wrap rests on it:
  - **The egress count goes one to one, not one to two.** Step 5 removes the fwlink, which at HEAD is the
    project's ONLY non-loopback egress — re-derived independently at this phase: `ci.yml` contains exactly
    two network calls, `:313` (the fwlink) and `:647` (`127.0.0.1:9515`, the driver-alone diagnostic, which
    is loopback and not an egress).
  - **The arriving crossing is strictly NARROWER than the one that leaves.** The fwlink carries no version
    selector, so every job fetched whatever was latest — that float is what put runtime 153 under a 152
    driver (run 35185153012) and what broke `:384`/`:397` on the dev host. The replacement is version-pinned
    and its version is DERIVED from the runtime already on the image, so it cannot drift on its own.
  - **It discharges carried escalation 2 by a route that exists.** security-plan's stated exit condition for
    the Evergreen float — "the versioned Standalone Installer replaces the bootstrapper" — names a mechanism
    that does not exist: the Standalone Installer installs Evergreen and takes no version argument, and the
    only versioned route is Fixed Version (>250 MB, latest and second-latest majors only, so 131 is not
    obtainable). Pinning the DRIVER to the runtime retires the float by a route that does exist. This is the
    float's disposition.

title: The load-bearing mechanism, stated as the equality the fix needs

data.head: ## The load-bearing mechanism, stated as the equality the fix needs

body:
**The idle console's focusable set has SIX members and only FIVE distinct accessible names.** Enumerated
against the spec's own selector
(`a[href],button:not([disabled]),input:not([disabled]),select,textarea,[tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])`):
| # | element | `activeName()` yields |
| 1 | `Titlebar.tsx:51` button | `Minimize window` |
| 2 | `Titlebar.tsx:59` button | `Close window` |
| 3 | picker cmdk `<input>` | its placeholder |
| 4 | `RunControls.tsx:21` `Start` (`aria-disabled`, focusable) | `Start` |
| 5 | `CoverageMatrix.tsx:60` `cov__scroll` | **`DIV`** |
| 6 | `RunReport.tsx:47` `report__scroll` | **`DIV`** |

`Stop` (`RunControls.tsx:34`, native `disabled`) is correctly excluded on both sides. Six matches the
runner's measured `focusableCount = 6` exactly.

**The equality the correction needs, and the one it must NOT use.** `activeName()` (`:165-177`) returns
`el.tagName` for any element that is neither `aria-label`ed nor one of `BUTTON/A/SELECT/TEXTAREA`, so members
5 and 6 both project to the string `DIV`. Therefore:
- `new Set(names).size === focusableCount` yields **5 === 6 → still RED**. The obvious fix is wrong.
- Reconciling those two numbers by NAME would mask a collision rather than measure reachability.

- The sound basis is **element identity**: index each visited element into the live focusable set
  (`Array.from(document.querySelectorAll(SEL)).indexOf(document.activeElement)`) and assert the reached index
  set equals `{0 … n-1}` in both directions. That is invariant under wrap count, survives duplicate names,
  and still fails loudly when a control drops out of the Tab order. Names continue to ride into the message.

**Why the dev host's "5 over 5" baseline is not a contradiction**: it predates the run-report subject whose
`report__scroll` is member 6. The denominator GREW — which is the argument against baking it, not evidence of
a regression.

**ESTABLISHED by a measured local run (2026-09-17, dev host runtime 153, capture `runs/a11y-e2e.log`,
15.2 MB, UTF-8 — encoding probed per `verification-harness.md:66b` before reading).** The red baseline
printed the walk verbatim, and it settles the mechanism:

```
Expected: "6 reached [DIV | Minimize window | Close window | Filter scenarios by name or P-ID… | Start | DIV | DIV | …]"
Received: "20 reached [ …same list… ]"
```

- **`focusableCount` is 6 here too**, and the walk's distinct names are exactly FIVE
  (`DIV`, `Minimize window`, `Close window`, `Filter scenarios by name or P-ID…`, `Start`) — the 6-elements /
  5-names collision is now MEASURED, not inferred.

- **The cycle is six long and contains no `BODY`.** Reading the sequence, positions 1-6 are
  `DIV_report, Minimize, Close, Filter, Start, DIV_cov` and position 7 returns to `DIV_report`. Rotating it
  to the document start gives `Minimize, Close, Filter, Start, cov__scroll, report__scroll` — exactly DOM
  order, which confirms both the enumeration and the render order.

- **`20` is the LOOP CAP (`for i < 20`), not a wrap count.** `tabCycleNames()` phase 1 Tabs up to 20 times
  waiting for a `BODY` stop that never comes, exhausts the cap, and leaves focus at an ARBITRARY point;
  phase 2 then walks 20 more from wherever that was and truncates. The runner's `12` is the same defect
  landing on a different cut.

- **Therefore `:397` (SC 2.4.3) shares the root cause and is NOT wrap-insensitive.** It failed on this run as
  `Start then DIV`. Its pass on runtime 131 was the walk happening to stop one position before
  `Minimize window` — configuration luck, not a property. A fix confined to `:384` would ship a latent flake
  into the very configuration whose green this chunk claims.

**The repair is in the walk, not in either assertion's arithmetic:** stop depending on a `BODY` sentinel.
Detect the cycle by the first REPEATED element identity, then compare against the live focusable set — set
equality for SC 2.1.1, and rotation-aligned order equality for SC 2.4.3. Both become environment-independent
by construction, which is what a11y-plan §11 requires.

- `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/test/a11y/accessibility.e2e.ts` — the SC 2.1.1 assertion at `:384`, and
  whatever `tabCycleNames` (`:185`) must return to supply element identity. **Caller threading (from the
  graph, not memory):** both call sites — `:374` (SC 2.1.1) and `:394` (SC 2.4.3) — are boundary members; if
  the helper's return shape changes, `:397`'s `names[0] / names[1]` reads move with it.

- *(conditional on operator rulings 1 and 3 — see Open questions)* `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — the `a11y`
  job's `runs-on` label (`:250`), the Evergreen floor gate (`:282`), and the launcher in the asserting step
  (`:431`).
- **No change required** to `scripts/agent-run.{sh,ps1}` — see Open question 4's answer.

- **Companion sweep** — `grep -rn 'tabCycleNames' crates/conductor-tauri/ui --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx`:
  **3 hits · 3 in the modify-set · 0 elsewhere** (the definition `:185` + the two call sites). A second sweep
  on the selector literal `grep -rn 'tabindex="-1"' …`: **2 hits · 1 in the modify-set · 1 no-change** —
  `screen-reader.e2e.ts:207` uses a deliberately LOOSER selector (no `:not([disabled])`) for the
  operator-local SR leg, a different arm with a different basis; out of scope, no change.

- Spec count re-derived: `grep -cE "^  it\(" accessibility.e2e.ts` → **14**, consistent with the run's
  11 passing + 1 failing + 2 skipped.

1. **Do operator rulings 1 and 3 land, and which way?** → blocks: **plan-decision**. HEAD's `a11y` job is
   `runs-on: windows-2025` (`ci.yml:250`), gates on the Evergreen `152+` floor (`:282`), and launches the
   asserting step through `a11y-limited-token-launch.ps1` at Medium integrity (`:431`). The configuration
   that produced 11 passing / 1 failing / 2 skipped was `windows-2022` + a coherent 131/131 driver+runtime +
   HIGH integrity + **no launcher**. All three deltas are recorded at HEAD as measured-but-not-acted-on
   (`:243-249`, `:423-430`) and each explicitly says it needs an operator ruling. **So the `:384` correction
   alone cannot produce a green CI verdict** — on HEAD's configuration the arm does not reach its assertions.
   P4 must put this fork to the operator rather than plan around it.

2. **Why does the cycle wrap twice on the runner?** → blocks: nothing (recorded unknown). Wrap-invariant
   under the chosen basis; worth capturing from the next green run's message rather than chasing now.

title: Boundaries — what this chunk is NOT

data.head: ## Boundaries — what this chunk is NOT

body:
- **Not an accessibility fix.** The reachability property SC 2.1.1 asserts is satisfied on the runner;
  the proof is inside the failure message. Nothing in the app's focus behaviour is in scope.
- **Not a re-opening of the exclusion arm.** See the CONTEXT fold below — it is dead on measurement.

- **Not a resolution of the four carried operator escalations.** They are folded below because they ride
  this entry, but none can be actioned without the operator; this chunk surfaces them, it does not decide them.

- ~~**Not a change to the two wrap-insensitive assertions**~~ — **`[premise-corrected: FALSIFIED by a
  measured local run, 2026-09-17. `:397` is NOT wrap-insensitive and shares `:384`'s root cause.]`** The
  dev-host baseline leg (runtime 153, harness capture `runs/a11y-e2e.log`) failed BOTH specs, and `:397`
  failed as `Start then DIV` — because `tabCycleNames()`'s phase 1 Tabs up to 20 times looking for a `BODY`
  stop that **does not exist in this webview's Tab cycle**, exhausts its cap, and leaves focus at an
  ARBITRARY point; phase 2 then starts there. `:397` passing on runtime 131 was configuration LUCK (the walk
  happened to stop one before `Minimize window`), not insensitivity. `:387`'s `missing` check does use set
  membership and is genuinely unaffected.

  **Consequence:** fixing `:384` alone would leave `:397` latently non-deterministic on a configuration whose
  green this chunk is about to claim — which test-plan §10's zero-flakiness budget and a11y-plan §11's
  "NO assertion in this harness is platform-dependent" both forbid. Repairing the shared root cause in
  `tabCycleNames()` is therefore REQUIRED for an honest green, not a scope widening of convenience. Flagged
  for the P5 review as a measured expansion of the touched surface (one helper, both call sites).

data.head: ## Measured this phase (coordinate re-verification, per promotion.md's fold-as-hypotheses rule)

body: Each coordinate the working entry names was re-verified against the artifact before it shaped this scope:

- **`accessibility.e2e.ts:373-384` resolves as stated.** `:373` opens `it('every idle-console control is
  keyboard-reachable by Tab alone (SC 2.1.1)')`; `:384` is the `expect(...)` whose ACTUAL side interpolates
  `names.length` and whose EXPECTED side interpolates `focusableCount` (a `document.querySelectorAll` count
  over `a[href],button:not([disabled]),input:not([disabled]),select,textarea,[tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])`).
  So the entry's reading is correct: the expectation counts DISTINCT DOM-focusable controls, the label counts
  Tab VISITS.
- **`:397` resolves as stated** — the SC 2.4.3 `expect` inside the `it(...)` opened at `:393`.
- **`v3-02`'s acceptance is unchanged and not refined downward**, confirmed by reading the ledger entry.

**One correction to the entry's own reasoning, measured at HEAD rather than assumed:** the entry cites
"expected and received bracket lists are identical to the character" as evidence that the same six controls
were reached. That identity is **true by construction** — both sides of the `.toBe()` interpolate the *same*
`names.join(' | ')` expression, so the bracket lists could not differ whatever the run did. It makes the
failure message legible; it is **not** independent evidence that the reached set equals the focusable set.
The claim that the reachability property holds therefore still needs a basis, and supplying one is part of
this chunk's work rather than something the predecessor already established. *(This does not dispute the
conclusion — it names what has and has not been proven.)*

- **`[premise-corrected: there are six distinct focusable ELEMENTS but only FIVE distinct accessible NAMES —
  two of the six are unnamed `<div tabIndex={0}>` scroll regions that both resolve to the string `DIV`.]`**
  The entry's "6 distinct" is right about elements and wrong about anything name-keyed. Research enumerated
  the seeded idle console's focusable set against
  `a[href],button:not([disabled]),input:not([disabled]),select,textarea,[tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])`:

the statement becomes **mechanically enforced rather than prose-only**. The chunk commits a claim→owner
enumeration beside the suites and a checker that holds it to reality: each named owner's spec must exist and

verdict (per a11y-plan §11 Strategy + §3 Configuration).

`plan-template.md` §Discipline). Operator decision recorded 2026-09-17: the enumeration is /implement's, the
master's prose is wrap's, and CARRY 1's dittography rides the same amendment set rather than a direct edit.

1. **Commit the claim→owner enumeration** at `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/test/a11y/claim-ownership.ts`. One row
   per `a11y-plan.md` §5 keyboard/focus claim, keyed by the bullet's **stable subject identity** (e.g.
   `run-console-HOLD focus trap`), never by a line coordinate — a11y-plan §3 *Configuration* requires naming by
   identity because coordinates move, and CARRY 1 in this chunk's own freight is that rule's worked example.
   Each row carries exactly one of three states:
   - `owned` — the owning suite plus the **exact `it(...)` title** that asserts it;
   - `n/a-by-construction` — with its basis (no repeated nav blocks; no route-change surface);
   - `unasserted` — a measured gap with a one-line reason, recorded as a finding and never as a pass

   `operator-hold.e2e.ts`, screen-reader `screen-reader.e2e.ts` — per `wdio.conf.ts:320-327` and test-plan §6.

   `$A11yExpectedSkips = 2` at `scripts/agent-run.ps1:61` stale against a run that now skips once; and adding
   real assertions would make the routine arm a SECOND owner of claims the driven arm owns, which v3-03's

- `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/test/a11y/check-claim-ownership.ts` — the checker (step 2).

- (a11y) Every `a11y-plan.md` §5 keyboard/focus claim appears in `claim-ownership.ts` in exactly one of the
  three states, and no claim in that section is absent from the enumeration (per a11y-plan §5).

- (a11y) No claim is recorded as owned by a spec that asserts nothing: the checker's anti-vacuity assertion
  fails any `owned` row whose spec body carries no `expect(` (per a11y-plan §11 Strategy — a skip is never
  coverage).

- (a11y) The hold-dependent trap and restoration claims name `operator-hold.e2e.ts` (driven arm,
  `npm run a11y:driven`) as their single owner, and no CI gate is named for them (per a11y-plan §11 Strategy).

- (tests) Every owner named resolves to a suite family test-plan §6 registers — routine
  `accessibility.e2e.ts` · driven `operator-hold.e2e.ts` · `sr*` `screen-reader.e2e.ts` — with no new or
  unregistered suite name (per test-plan §6 *Drivers per surface*).

- (tests) The `a11y` job's spec set is unchanged and the routine arm's verdict still reads 12 passing /
  0 failing / 2 skipped, the expected-skip SET intact (per test-plan §3 CI stage selectors).

- (arch) The `a11y-plan` carve-out text this chunk sends to wrap states the routine arm's CI green with its
  configuration — hosted `windows-2022`, coherent `131.0.2903.86` driver/runtime pair, High integrity, run
  35208593666 — never as a bare verdict, and introduces none of the retired universals (per architecture
  §Established Decisions [CI/CD]).

- (arch) `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/knip.json` and `package.json` are the only registry edits; no new crate,
  port, env var or on-disk artifact, so §Occupied Resources needs no entry (per architecture §Occupied Resources).

- (layouts) The enumeration's layout keys are the shipped run-state names only — `idle` / `live` / `hold`, with
  idle-with-report a sub-state of `idle` — minting no layout name outside that set (per layout-templates
  §Surface: desktop-webview — Primary screens).

- (design) The two N/A-by-construction rows cite the single-station, no-router console as their basis rather
  than standing unsourced (per design-system §Navigation Pattern).

- (security) Zero absolute-host-path tokens and zero internal seam-crate struct names in every file the chunk
  commits; every gate/suite sentence names the handle NAME (`CONDUCTOR_MSEDGEDRIVER` / `CONDUCTOR_A11Y_STRICT`)
  and no resolved value (per security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Logging; §Input Validation).

- (security) Zero dependency delta — `Cargo.lock` and `package-lock.json` un-drifted, `tsx` already present
  (per security-plan §Dependency Security).

- (obs) No claim is attributed to an obs span; the bounded span-name set carries no `focus.*` member and this
  chunk adds none (per obs-plan §11 *Spans / Traces*).
- (tests) `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci` returns 0.
**`v3-03` is NOT claimed by this chunk. It stays pooled, with a `notes` line recording the measured reason.**

This reverses the claimability half of the P4 fork's recommendation, on a measurement taken after that fork was
posed. v3-03's acceptance quantifies over *every* keyboard/focus claim: "exactly one suite is named as its owner
**and the claim is actually asserted in that suite**". Measured this phase, **three §5 claims are asserted by no
suite at all**:
| claim | site | measured state |
| `run-console-live` keyboard-first coverage-matrix row navigation | `:354` | unasserted |
| `idle-with-report` coverage-matrix row navigation, `aria-selected`/`aria-current` | `:356` | unasserted |
| first-class start / stop / proceed / abort shortcuts | `:370` | unasserted |

Derivation: `grep -rnE "ArrowDown|ArrowUp|Arrow|shortcut|aria-current|aria-selected|type-ahead|typeahead"
crates/conductor-tauri/ui/test/a11y/*.ts` returns 18 hits and **every one is in `screen-reader.e2e.ts`**, all on
the picker's `[role="option"]` list — none on the coverage matrix. A full census of keyboard tokens
(`grep -rhoE "browser\.keys\([^)]*\)" … | sort | uniq -c`) returns Tab ×4, Enter ×4, Shift+Tab ×2, Space ×2,
Escape ×2, ArrowUp ×2, ArrowDown ×2 and three single-use tokens — no global shortcut is driven anywhere.

Closing those three gaps means writing new keyboard coverage, which is out of this chunk's scope and is a
different chunk's work. Per `verification-matrix-contract.md` §Acceptance lifecycle, a capability not provable
by THIS chunk **stays pooled** with one `notes` line; concretizing the acceptance to admit a third "recorded
gap" terminal would weaken the outcome, which the never-weaken rule forbids. The enumeration this chunk ships is
what makes the three gaps mechanically visible instead of invisible, so the successor chunk inherits a measured
roster rather than a fresh search.

body:
- **`tabCycle` @ `accessibility.e2e.ts:215`** — 2 call sites, **both inside its own file**: `:409` (the SC 2.1.1
  spec) and `:425` (the SC 2.4.3 spec). No external caller.
- **`focusSnapshot` @ `accessibility.e2e.ts:184`** — 2 call sites, `:216` and `:222`, both inside `tabCycle`.

- **`activeName` / `focusInsideDialog`** — defined TWICE, independently, per suite: `operator-hold.e2e.ts:25`
  / `:37` and `screen-reader.e2e.ts:185` / `:247`. They are **not** a shared helper; each suite carries its own.

- **Consequence for the plan:** every keyboard helper is file-local. Any edit inside a spec file has zero blast
  radius beyond that file, and there is no shared helper whose change would touch two arms at once.

- *(Graph `line`/`def_line` are 0-indexed per `code-graph-cookbook.md`; every number above is the editor line,
  i.e. `line + 1`.)*

- **Independent-halves assertion shape** (`accessibility.e2e.ts:409-422`): the SC 2.1.1 expectation builds its
  ACTUAL side from the Tab walk and its EXPECTED side from a `document.querySelectorAll` roster, so the two can
  actually differ — the predecessor's correction of the `${names}`-on-both-sides defect. The same shape recurs
  at `operator-hold.e2e.ts:147-151` for restoration (`restored=… landed_on=…` vs the invoker name).

- **Identity-keyed cycle detection** (`accessibility.e2e.ts:215-232`): `tabCycle` delimits a lap by the first
  REPEATED element identity and deliberately does not wait for a `BODY` sentinel, with the reason recorded in
  its doc comment. Rotation-compared at `:425-433`, so where the walk enters the ring is not asserted.

- **Skip-guard-then-assert** (`accessibility.e2e.ts:456-467`): the checklist spec guards on the hold marker
  `[role="alertdialog"]` (never on `role="status"`, which is a growing population) and then asserts.

- **Per-arm ownership prose already exists in the DERIVED tier**: `.claude/rules/a11y.md` §Testing already
  names all three families and assigns "the HOLD-dependent half only — trap, Space toggle, Escape→NoGo, focus
  restoration" to the operator-only driven arm. The master `a11y-plan.md` §5 does not.

- **Owners are named by job/suite name, never by workflow line coordinates** — `a11y-plan.md` §3 *Configuration*
  states this in its own words; the registry to name against is `wdio.conf.ts:320-327`: default `specs` =
  `accessibility.e2e.ts` (routine), `suites.driven` = `operator-hold.e2e.ts`, `suites.sr`/`sr-empty`/`sr-error`
  = `screen-reader.e2e.ts`.

- **A CI claim carries its configuration** (`a11y-plan.md:516`) — hosted `windows-2022`, coherent
  `131.0.2903.86` pair, High integrity, run 35208593666 — never a bare verdict.
- **Name the SET, not a fresh literal** (`.claude/rules/a11y.md` 2026-09-17; design/tests/arch extracts agree).
- *(decided at P4 — see Open questions 1; a doc-only outcome creates none.)*

- *(provisional, gated on Open question 1)* `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/test/a11y/accessibility.e2e.ts` — only
  if P4 elects to close the vacuous `:450` spec. Graph-confirmed zero external callers.

- **NOT a touchpoint under any option:** `.andromeda/a11y-plan.md`. `plan-template.md` §Discipline forbids any
  of the seven spec masters in `Files to modify`; its content changes ride
  `Expected amendments (wrap): a11y-plan.md §… — …`.

**F1 — `accessibility.e2e.ts:450` is vacuous by construction.** Its title is
`'operator-pause dialog: alertdialog role, focus trap, Escape resolves NoGo, focus restores'` — four claims —
and its body (`:450-454`) is the `this.skip()` guard **and nothing else**: `sed -n '450,455p' … | grep -c 'expect('`
returns **0**. Even with a hold raised it would assert nothing. This is the same class the predecessor closed at
`:388`, and it sits inside this chunk's claim population. **Naming the routine arm as owner of those four claims
on the strength of this spec's title would attribute four claims to a spec that asserts none.** Its sibling
`:456` is not vacuous (one assertion after the guard).

**F2 — the driven arm genuinely asserts the hold-dependent half.** `operator-hold.e2e.ts:44` asserts trap
containment forward and backward (`focusInsideDialog()` true at `:79` and `:83`), Space toggling a row with the
`role=status` roll-up changing (`:106-117`), Escape dismissing the dialog (`:119-125`), and restoration to the
recorded invoker with `landed_on` empty (`:147-151`). So it is a real owner, not a nominal one.

**F3 — `:366` carries a retired attribution that `:362` contradicts, inside one section.** `:366` reads
"(Radix AlertDialog default, layout excerpt's Focus Management Anchors)", while `:362` states restoration comes
"via the dialog's explicit `onCloseAutoFocus` + `restoreFocusTo` contract, **NOT** a Radix default (… as measured
2026-09-01 Radix restored to `<body>`)". `:131`, `:253` and `.claude/rules/a11y.md` all agree with `:362`. `:366`
is the lone survivor of the retired reading and is one of the bullets this chunk must attribute.

**F4 — §5 omits the checklist rows that §1 and §3 include.** `:355` and `:362` describe the HOLD cycle as
"across Proceed/Abort" only; `:131` and `:253` both put the operator-checklist `checkbox` rows inside the cycle
("across the operator-checklist `checkbox` rows … and then Proceed/Abort"). The layouts extract independently
confirms the rows ARE in the trap population (§Component — Hero / Operator-checklist), and the driven arm
asserts them (`:87`, `:106`). So §5's two bullets are the abbreviated pair, not §1/§3.

**F5 — SC 2.4.7's "visible ring on the active element" is asserted nowhere.** Derivation:
`grep -rnE "2\.4\.7|color-focus|focus-visible|focusRing|outline|boxShadow|box-shadow" crates/conductor-tauri/ui/test/a11y/`
returns **exactly 1 hit** across the whole a11y tree — `accessibility.e2e.ts:33`, a token-pair CONTRAST row
(`{ fg: '--color-focus', bg: '--color-base', need: 3 }`). That proves the ring's 3:1 ratio, not that a ring is
rendered on the focused element. §5 `:372` binds the population to "SC 2.1.1 / SC 2.4.3 / SC 2.1.2 / SC 2.4.7"
and §3 `:253` asks for a "visible `--color-focus` ring on the active element (SC 2.4.7, paired with the contrast
harness for the 3:1 ring)" — the paired half exists, the active-element half does not.

**F6 — the derived tier already says what the master does not.** `.claude/rules/a11y.md` §Testing carries the
per-arm attribution in full. The ownership content is therefore already agreed in this project; what is missing
is the master's own per-claim statement and the carve-out's substitute-gate sentence.

**F7 — the carve-out at `:516` is closer to done than scope assumed.** It already narrows to "the HOLD-DEPENDENT
Operable half only" and already states *why* that half is operator-local ("needs a live Pulse and stays barred
from CI by test-plan §11 and architecture §Established Decisions [CI/CD]"). What it does **not** do is (a) name
the owning SUITE, and (b) say what gates in its place — which is exactly v3-03's second sentence.

Every `[inferred]` bullet in `scope.md` was re-read against these findings; `scope.md` is amended in the same
pass (P4 consumes the corrected copy).

- **VERIFIED** — v3-03 is the targeted capability; the "for every … claim" quantifier is the ledger's, not the
  entry's; `operator-hold.e2e.ts` is the driven suite and CI never runs it (`wdio.conf.ts:321`, test-plan §11,
  architecture §Established Decisions [CI/CD], `.claude/rules/a11y.md`); only the named-owner-plus-carve-out
  terminal is reachable; the `a11y` job's spec set is untouched; no Rust surface and no dependency delta.

- **VERIFIED** — the open channel fork is real and unresolved: `plan-template.md` §Discipline bars spec masters
  from `Files to modify`, so the master's text can only move through `Expected amendments (wrap)`.

- **PREMISE-CORRECTED** — the scope's claim-population table said the `run-console-idle` row was "unnamed
  (asserted in the routine arm)". `:353` in fact **already carries an explicit attribution** ("**Asserted
  UNATTENDED on the routine arm since 2026-09-07**"), so that row is already owned and needs no new statement.
  The genuinely unattributed rows are `:354`, `:355`, `:362`, `:366`, `:370`.

- **PREMISE-CORRECTED** — the scope said "for those two the work is attribution, not relocation", treating the
  routine arm's hold-dependent specs as a non-issue. F1 falsifies the easy reading: `:450` names four claims and
  asserts none, so attribution to the routine arm is not merely unnecessary there, it would be **false**.

1. **Which channel authors the ownership statement, and therefore what /implement builds?** `a11y-plan.md`
   cannot be a touchpoint, so either (a) the chunk is doc-only and everything rides
   `Expected amendments (wrap)` — in which case v3-03's decisive artifact is wrap-authored and the capability is
   **not claimable by this chunk** (`verification-matrix-contract` claim-reachability) — or (b) /implement
   writes an enumeration it CAN author (a committed ownership map beside the suites, and/or closing F1), with
   the master's prose riding wrap. → blocks: **plan-decision** (P4 resolves before synthesis).

2. **Does closing F1 (`:450`) belong to this chunk?** `scope.md` bans "new keyboard or focus-trap assertions",
   and closing a vacuous spec is arguably a fix rather than a new assertion — but it is the only way the routine
   arm's own file stops claiming coverage it does not provide. → blocks: **implementation-scope**.

3. **Do F3/F4/F5 ride this chunk's amendment set, or are they adjacent findings for the route?** All three sit
   inside the claim population, none is an ownership question per se. → blocks: **plan-decision**.

**`[amended at P5 validation-1, 2026-09-17: v3-03 is NOT CLAIMED by this chunk — it stays pooled.]`** Its

navigation and `:370` the first-class shortcuts. Closing those is new keyboard coverage, out of this chunk's

Every keyboard-reachability and focus-order claim the requirement makes gets exactly one named owning
suite, and the claims whose owner is a suite CI never runs get a stated carve-out saying what gates in
their place.

   half that is currently unattributed — **the hold-dependent trap and restoration claims** — but the
   acceptance is quantified over *every* claim, so the unstated-but-already-correct half must be
   attributed too rather than left silently implicit. `[inferred: the "for every … claim" quantifier is

   does not run and by design cannot (it needs a live preflight-ready Pulse). The requirement must state
   what gates in its place rather than leaving those claims unattributed. `[inferred: the suite's identity
   and its never-a-CI-gate status are read from `operator-hold.e2e.ts:1-7` this phase.]`

**`[amended at P5 validation-1, 2026-09-17 — intent-incomplete, justified: the DELIVERABLE grew a mechanical
half the scope did not anticipate.]`** On the operator's P4 ruling the ownership statement is not prose-only:

title: An open question this scope records rather than settles

data.head: ## An open question this scope records rather than settles

body:
**Which channel may write the ownership statement?** The requirement is a spec master
(`.andromeda/a11y-plan.md`), and `/andromeda-phase` and `/andromeda-implement` are both read-only against
spec sources — spec amendments are wrap's flow. v3-03's acceptance turns on the *requirement's* text, so
a naive plan would claim a capability whose decisive artifact only wrap can author, which the matrix
contract's claim-reachability rule forbids (the coverage gate would HALT by construction).

CARRY 1 is an operator-ratified precedent for this chunk editing `a11y-plan.md` directly — but its stated
justification is narrow ("a master-body defect with no report fact behind it and no detector that covers
it"), which does not obviously extend to substantive spec content that the amendment flow does cover.

This is a genuine fork, not a detail: it decides whether v3-03 is claimable by this chunk at all, and if
so through which artifact. **It is carried to P4 for resolution and, if contestable there, to the
operator.** `[inferred — the fork is derived from the skill contract + the ledger's claim-reachability

- **CARRY 1's coordinates hold.** `a11y-plan.md:115` is **3691 characters** (3728 bytes — the char count

  phase added none.

- **`v3-03`'s acceptance and `observed_gap` read as the entry implies**, confirmed from the ledger via the
  matrix tool rather than by loading the JSON.

**The CI fold (promotion.md's second fold source, Setup 5a):** `git log -1 --format=%H` is
`3ddd405c2556003006f3747804173fbf951414b5`; the check-runs API answers **`No commit found for SHA`
(HTTP 422)** — the wrap's commit is **not on the remote yet**, exactly as the handoff states ("this wrap's
commit leaves it 1 ahead. The operator pushes"). This is the documented not-on-the-remote reading, a
**no-op**: there is no completed conclusion to disposition, and nothing folds into this scope from CI.

> `a11y-plan.md:115` carries a verbatim dittography — the clause "the one webview-automation stack running
> on the measured platform SET — " stands twice inside one line, at offsets 2555 and 2627 of a

> line; this wrap's §1 CI-integration amendment moved them, and a stale offset is exactly what this CARRY
