title: Plan — 2026-09-18-real-model-leg-posture-and-grading-rule: "Real-model leg posture and grading rule"

data.head: # Plan — 2026-09-18-real-model-leg-posture-and-grading-rule: "Real-model leg posture and grading rule"

body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-09-18-real-model-leg-posture-and-grading-rule · **Version:** conductor-0.3.0 · **Generated:** 2026-09-18T07:30Z

Ship the committed, dated statement that fixes — **before any real-model leg is driven** — the launch posture,
the grading rule and the per-leg quiet window under which a leg with Pulse's deterministic L4 mode OFF will be
run and judged. This is the posture half of Epoch 4's pair; the drive is the next route entry's work. The
separation is mandated, not stylistic: `verification-matrix.json#v3-09`'s route note states that a chunk which
drives first and decides the grading afterwards "satisfies the letter and defeats the capability".

P3 turned the posture from a formality into a substantive finding. Tracing the hypothesis observable to its
writer in the SUT's own source established that **a single-storm real-model leg has no hypothesis observable at
all**: `retrieve_report` renders its `## Hypotheses` section only when `incident.resolution_summary_text` parses
as an `L4Output`, and neither writer of that field fires on first incident creation — the live writer fires only
on a dedupe re-generation of an already-active incident, the other only after resolution. A leg designed the
obvious way would read back a degraded report, grade nothing, and look like a model failure. The posture's job is
to state the emission profile that makes the observable exist, alongside the launch terms and the grading rule
(per architecture.md §Established Decisions [Probabilistic-Assertion Policy] + test-plan §9/§11 + obs-plan §3/§10).

It also discharges the standing **PREREQ**: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` has deferred
twice consecutively and the third consecutive re-pin trips the age trigger, so this chunk runs it.

1. **Create `contracts/pulse-real-model-leg-posture.md`** as a **reader-less** `contracts/` member, taking the
   `contracts/pulse-p025-measurement-contract.md` regime exactly: no `default_path()`, no `resolve_under`, no
   bounds check, no `CONDUCTOR_*` override handle, and a `provenance` statement saying whether each term is a
   Conductor measurement or a transcribed SUT record (per architecture.md §Occupied Resources — On-disk
   artifacts). Open it with `sut_version` (`andromeda-pulse` HEAD `83d4060`) and `captured_at`.

2. **State the launch posture** as a term list, each term in the run-contract's own three-kind vocabulary
   (`shell-declaration` / `asserted` / `declared-not-observable`; per architecture.md §Occupied Resources —
   `contracts/pulse-run-contract.toml`):
   - `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC` **absent or falsy** — the defining term. Written as a
     **declaration-only observation of Conductor's own environment**, never as a claimed measurement of
     `pulse-app` (per security-plan §Input Validation, declaration-only READ SET row).
   - `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MCP_ENABLED`, `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` equal to the live app's dir, the sidecar built
     and resolvable on `PATH` in POSIX form, and the paired `RUST_LOG=info,conductor_emit=debug` — the
     accumulated firing form from `.claude/rules/verification-harness.md` (entries 2026-08-10, -13, -14, -19,
     2026-09-07), restated here as posture rather than rediscovered at drive time.
   - `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_BASELINE_BOOTSTRAP_SECONDS` — stated as **one boot-time disposition binding the whole
     real-model suite**, with the reason it cannot be per-leg (`Thresholds::from_env` resolves once at the SUT's
     boot), and the instruction to confirm which posture booted by grepping Pulse's log for the target
     `triage.baseline.bootstrap_window.override`, never the emitting function name.
   - The statement that the leg is **operator-invoked and never a CI gate**, written in a11y-plan §11
     *Strategy*'s claim → owner → substitute-gate form: what CI runs in its place, each item stated as *not* a
     substitute for the assertion itself.

3. **State the emission profile the observable requires** — the chunk's decisive content. The posture must
   require that a real-model leg produce **at least two cue-bearing digests on one `(kind, scope, scope_id)`
   identity while the incident is still active**, and must say why: the first incident carries
   `resolution_summary_text: None`, so `retrieve_report` returns `degraded_mode: true` with no `## Hypotheses`
   section at all. Cite the writers by file and line (research.md §The load-bearing mechanism) so the drive
   chunk inherits the derivation rather than repeating it.

4. **State the grading rule**, mapped onto the closed sets and reconciled explicitly with the
   Probabilistic-Assertion Policy rather than silently (per architecture.md §Established Decisions
   [Probabilistic-Assertion Policy]; design-system §Color Palette):
   - The assertion is a `ComparisonKind::Contains` check over the composed observation text, which carries the
     `retrieve_report` markdown (`conductor-verify/src/extract.rs:102`). No new comparison kind, no new verdict
     word, no new envelope key (per obs-plan §3 / §6).
   - **Hit / miss / no-usable-output** each map to a named `Verdict`/`ReportState` pair. A miss is a
     model-interpretive outcome, which is the `CalibrationRegion` class the policy already defines for
     hypothesis quality; the posture states that mapping and its reason, and states that a leg which was never
     measured (precondition unmet, quiet window unmet) is `Blocked` with its named precondition string, never a
     red `Fail` (per design-system §Anti-Patterns → Rejected Defaults).
   - **A failing leg grades as a failure and is never re-driven until it passes** — no retry-once, no soft SLO
     (per test-plan §10 Zero-flakiness budget; a11y-plan §11 *SLO*).
   - **Disposition instead of an SLO tier.** `SloTier` is closed at `<5s`/`<20s`/`<90s` with `deadline_ms()`
     capped at 90 000 (`conductor-core/src/scenario.rs:52-72`), while real-model formation alone measured
     ~110 s — so a real-model leg cannot meet any tier and must not be graded on one. The posture states the
     declare-only landing (`verdict` null, `state` `KnownResidual`) plus a harvest-tier hard assertion over
     verbatim leg captures, which is the shape the system already uses for a claim the envelope cannot carry
     (per obs-plan §4; test-plan §6 Harvest-tier grading).

5. **State the per-leg quiet window and serialization rule** with its arithmetic derived, not restated as a
   literal: Pulse's idle interval plus a resolver tick as the floor, the preflight budget terms from
   `contracts/pulse-run-contract.toml` (`warmup_ms`, `min_canary_poll_seconds`) as the derivation source, and
   the explicit note that the existing suite's 150 s window and `live_leg_budget_sec` arithmetic are calibrated
   to canned-L4 formation (~2 s) and do not transfer to a ~110 s formation path. Legs are **serialized**, each
   riding its own window (per test-plan §11 E2E `sleep(N)` ban scope — a harness-level wait BETWEEN legs, never
   an in-test sleep).

6. **Record the census obligation** — the posture states that a real-model leg ends with a real process census
   taken twice, with the stop form named beside the firing form and `pulse-app` recorded as
   `left running — operator stops it` (per `.claude/rules/verification-harness.md` 2026-09-02).

7. **Discharge the PREREQ** — run the workspace lint gate listed in `## Test Commands`. It runs over a
   zero-`.rs`-delta tree by design; that is the same condition which justified the two prior deferrals, and it
   runs anyway because the pin's third consecutive re-pin trips the age trigger.

- `contracts/pulse-real-model-leg-posture.md` — the committed posture, grading rule and quiet-window statement;
  reader-less regime, no Rust reader, no override handle.

- _(none)_ — the posture is documentation-only this chunk. No `.rs` delta, no harness-shell delta, no
  dependency delta. See §Constraints for why the harness arm is deliberately NOT added here.

No smoke entry and no live-leg entry: this chunk has **no producing leg at all** — it drives nothing and mints

body:
- (arch) `contracts/pulse-real-model-leg-posture.md` exists and declares its regime explicitly as reader-less —
  no `default_path()`, no `resolve_under`, no bounds check, no `CONDUCTOR_*` override handle — and carries
  `sut_version` / `captured_at` / `provenance` stating for each term whether it is a Conductor measurement or a
  transcribed SUT record (per architecture.md §Occupied Resources — On-disk artifacts).

- (arch) Every outcome the grading rule names is drawn from the closed `Verdict` (3) / `ReportState` (5) sets as
  an `Ok` value, never a `Result::Err`, and the miss mapping is reconciled explicitly against the
  `CalibrationRegion → ManualCheck` default rather than silently overriding it (per architecture.md §Established
  Decisions [Probabilistic-Assertion Policy] · [Error Handling]).

- (security) The posture states the `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC` disposition as a declaration-only
  observation of Conductor's own environment, and no posture or grading clause asserts a measurement of
  `pulse-app` (per security-plan §Input Validation, declaration-only READ SET row).

- (security) The committed artifact carries zero absolute host paths, zero `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` values and
  zero internal seam-crate struct names — proven by the `grep -cE "[A-Za-z]:[\\/]|/home/|/Users/|%APPDATA%"`
  entry returning a count of 0 (per security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Logging).

- (tests) The posture names the leg's operator-invoked, never-a-CI-gate footing and names its future invocation
  path as a member of the sanctioned live-leg SET, adding no new member (per test-plan §9 / §11 CI).

- (tests) `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` runs and is green — the PREREQ discharge, not
  deferred (per test-plan §9 Live-Pulse scenarios, Lint stage).

- (tests) The grading rule excludes re-driving a failed leg to obtain a pass, and no reported state it names
  produces a non-zero process exit (per test-plan §3 Status endpoint shape / §10 Zero-flakiness budget).

- (security) `cargo audit` and `cargo deny check advisories bans licenses sources` are both green over a
  committed, un-drifted `Cargo.lock`, with the local advisory-db checkout shown clean by the porcelain probe
  before any red is classified external (per security-plan §Dependency Security; §Security Anti-Patterns →
  Universal).

- (obs) The posture names a **non-tier disposition** for a real-model leg — declare-only row plus harvest-tier
  hard assertion — and states why no `SloTier` value can bound it, citing the closed ladder's 90 000 ms cap
  against the ~110 s formation figure (per obs-plan §10 Performance budgets).

- (obs) The posture introduces no new span name, no non-allowlisted span attribute, no new envelope key and no
  new grade word (per obs-plan §3 Log format JSON schema / §11 Spans/Traces).

- (design) A leg that was never measured grades `Blocked` with its named precondition string, kept lexically
  distinct from a graded miss (per design-system §Color Palette, Verdict-vs-ReportState note).

- (a11y) The existing `driven-a11y` leg keeps its stated owner, posture and results unchanged; the real-model
  posture is additive and re-grades nothing (per a11y-plan §9 E2E artifacts row + §11 Strategy).

- (layouts) No sixth harness command and no new bracket label, ANSI entry or token is minted (per
  layout-templates §Surface: cli — Primary screens and Component — Primary content block 2).

- **Capability:** `verification-matrix.json#v3-09` (*Real-model interpretation leg*) — **partially advanced,
  deliberately NOT claimed.** Its acceptance quantifies over the drive as well as the posture ("A live leg runs
  … and the leg asserts …"), which this chunk does not perform; per the matrix contract's multi-chunk rule the
  cap stays `chunk: null` and is cited here. A `notes` line recording the failed concretization plus P3's
  decisive findings is written at P5 so the drive chunk inherits them.

- **Decisive material leans taken (not operator questions):** (a) leaned documentation-only, no harness arm, per
  v3-09's posture-vs-drive separation and `.claude/rules/verification-harness.md` 2026-09-10, which requires a
  leg's `expect` atoms to be written from a log that has actually been produced — impossible for a chunk that
  drives nothing; (b) leaned declare-only + harvest-tier for the disposition, per obs-plan §4 and test-plan §6,
  the only shape in the system for a claim the envelope cannot carry.

- Spec anchors: architecture.md §Established Decisions [Probabilistic-Assertion Policy] · [Read-Back Dependency
  Posture] · §Occupied Resources · security-plan §Input Validation · §Security Anti-Patterns · test-plan §3 · §9
  · §10 · §11 · obs-plan §3 · §4 · §10 · §11 · design-system §Color Palette · §Surface: cli → Tokens ·
  layout-templates §Surface: cli · a11y-plan §9 · §10 · §11.
- Research files inspected: `research.md` (18 reads, 9 of them in the SUT repo at HEAD `83d4060`), `scope.md`.

- **Adding a `--live-realmodel` arm to `scripts/agent-run.{sh,ps1}` now — REJECTED.** A leg's `expect` atoms are
  the one gate class with no mechanical check, and the standing rule is to run the leg once and read its log
  before writing them; this chunk drives nothing, so any atom authored now would be guesswork that the wrap
  light gate would re-run verbatim. The arm belongs to the drive entry.

- **Flipping the flag on the existing `--live` suite — REJECTED.** `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC` is
  load-bearing for leg B2's dedupe window; real-model formation would fall outside Pulse's idle window and the
  leg would measure the wrong thing. The real-model path needs its own budgets, not the canned ones.

- **Grading a real-model leg on an SLO tier — REJECTED.** The ladder is closed at 90 000 ms and formation alone
  measured ~110 s, so any tier assignment would grade the leg red on timing regardless of the hypothesis.

- **Asserting on `evidence_refs` / `fingerprints` as the identity carrier — REJECTED.** Those fields are
  L4-authored; under the real model they are model output, and the posture's subject is the hypothesis text.

- **Re-deriving the ~110 s figure in this chunk — OUT OF SCOPE.** It is a 2026-09-06 SUT-timing measurement that
  cannot be re-measured without driving. It is carried with its date and witness; the drive chunk confirms it.

- **Expected amendments (wrap): `architecture.md` §Occupied Resources — On-disk artifacts — register
  `contracts/pulse-real-model-leg-posture.md` as a second reader-less `contracts/` member**, following the
  `pulse-p025-measurement-contract.md` precedent. Note that precedent was recorded n=1 with no playbook rule
  minted, so a second member is a judgement the wrap should surface, not a settled pattern.

- **Rule-file curation item (wrap, Tier 2 — NOT an Expected amendment, since the amendment flow owns only the
  seven masters):** `.claude/rules/verification-harness.md`'s 2026-08-16 entry states the deterministic L4
  fixture pins `evidence_refs` to `[]` citing `deterministic_inference.rs:35`. At Pulse HEAD `83d4060` the
  fixture populates it with a `det-*` triple at `:68-72`, and `:35` is now a scrubber-pattern sentence. Basis:
  direct read of the SUT source this chunk performed; the obs extract independently carried the corrected
  version. Same entry's `retrieve_report` framing is stale in the SUT's own docs too (`jsonrpc.rs:189` and
  `markdown.rs:20-27` both say only resolved incidents render hypotheses, which
  `attach_interpretation_summary` exists to defeat) — worth recording, but those are the SUT's artifacts, not
  ours to amend.

- **Code-graph note:** `execute_scenario` is absent from the rust plane's `symbol` view although it is defined at
  `crates/conductor-run/src/execute.rs:44`; `grep -rn 'execute_scenario' --include=*.rs crates/` returns 15
  hits. Any impact claim for that symbol rests on grep. CLAUDE.md's 2026-09-02 learning quotes 7 sites / 5
  callers *from the graph* for this same symbol — do not re-quote that figure without re-measuring.

- **Ordering:** the advisory-db porcelain probe precedes `cargo audit` deliberately; the two document probes
  come last because their subject does not exist until step 1 lands.

**Chunk:** Real-model leg posture and grading rule — the launch posture, the grading rule and the per-leg quiet
window for a non-deterministic L4 live leg fixed and committed BEFORE any drive, operator-gated and never a CI
gate; the posture half of Epoch 4's pair, so `v3-09` is partially advanced and deliberately NOT claimed; folds
the `PREREQ` closing the rust gate deferral at re-pin ordinal 2.
**Date:** 2026-09-18
**Commits:** none since `last_wrap` — this wrap's own commit is the chunk's first.

- **Files:** `contracts/pulse-real-model-leg-posture.md` (**new**, 181 lines). Pipeline artifacts beside it:
  `conductor-0.3.0/chunks/2026-09-18-real-model-leg-posture-and-grading-rule/{scope,research,plan,report}.md`,
  `conductor-0.3.0/verification-matrix.json` (a `notes` write on `v3-09` only),
  `conductor-0.3.0/working-route.md` (the freeze stamp), `.andromeda/master-route.md` (the pending record),
  `.andromeda/friction-log.ndjson`, and the phase/implement/wrap run dirs.

- **Symbols / APIs:** **none.** Zero `.rs` delta. The new file is a **reader-less** `contracts/` member — no
  Rust code reads it, it has no `default_path()`, no resolution through `resolve_under`, no bounds check and
  deliberately no `CONDUCTOR_*` override handle. No new env var, port, socket or export; the document NAMES
  existing registered handles (`ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC`, `_MCP_ENABLED`, `_DATA_DIR`,
  `_BASELINE_BOOTSTRAP_SECONDS`) and mints none.
- **Crates / modules:** none added, removed or changed.

- **Dependencies:** none added or bumped. `Cargo.lock` and `package-lock.json` byte-unchanged; `cargo audit`
  scanned the same 562 crate dependencies as the prior reading.
- **Schema / config:** none. No envelope key, no span name, no span attribute, no violation-schema change.
- **Spec-master edits:** none applied at P1 (P2's fan-out may propose; see Expected amendments below).

- **Counts / qualifiers moved:** **none — verified.** No documented derived value changed: the workspace test
  count held at 986 and the coverage roll-up held at 6/11 verified · 5 unclaimed. (The `cargo audit` advisory
  figure is a host-tool reading and belongs to Dev-tool versions, not here — filing it under both bullets has
  previously drawn two detectors with opposing remedies.)

- **Dev-tool versions:** **none — `cargo audit` re-read at 1247 advisories · 562 crate dependencies · 7 allowed
  warnings (6 `unmaintained` + 1 `unsound`), UNCHANGED.** The baseline is the most recent recorded reading,
  `chunks/2026-09-17-a11y-routine-arm-terminal-on-the-measured-configuration/report.md:292`, which records the
  identical triple (1247 · 562 · 7) one day earlier. The advisory database did not move between the two
  readings. `cargo-audit` and `cargo-deny` themselves were not installed, upgraded or re-versioned this chunk.
  Basis: `grep -rnoE '1(2[0-9]{2}) advisories' conductor-*/chunks/*/report.md` over the whole corpus, bare.

- **Harness / gate surface:** **none — deliberately.** No `agent-run` verb, flag, arm or exit rule changed; the
  5-command surface is untouched and the operator-gated `--live` suite is byte-unchanged. The posture document
  *describes* a future leg's firing form without registering one, which is the chunk's stated boundary.

- **Cross-project / external claims:** several, all read at **`andromeda-pulse` HEAD `83d40601`** (tracked tree
  clean; only that repo's own bookkeeping modified):
  - `crates/mcp-server/src/tools.rs:360-387` — `dispatch_retrieve_report` parses `resolution_summary_text` as
    an `L4Output` and computes `degraded_mode = parsed_l4.is_none()`, returning `{markdown, degraded_mode}`.
  - `crates/interpretation/src/markdown.rs:153` — the literal `## Hypotheses` section header; `:41`
    `HypothesisView`, described at `pulse-app/src/incidents_router.rs:84` as a "Single **ranked** hypothesis".
  - `crates/triage/src/incident/registry.rs:128-160` — the two writers of `resolution_summary_text`:
    `attach_resolution_summary` (Resolved only) and `attach_interpretation_summary` (live incidents).
  - `pulse-app/src/inference_runtime.rs:823` — the live writer fires only inside the **dedupe re-generation**
    branch; `:250` — the resolution writer fires only on a resolution-summary digest.
  - `pulse-app/src/deterministic_inference.rs:68-72` — `evidence_refs` holds a populated `det-*` triple.
  - **CI run `35255156862`** on sha `e75fcb9dc19f9fa3ae97965bc4ec1cef452f43c5` (the tree this chunk started
    from), read at Setup 5a: all three jobs **completed / success** — Rust gate, Frontend gate, and the A11y
    gate (routine arm). No red to disposition. The sha is the record: this wrap's commit adds to that tree.

- **Reverted / negative API facts:** none written-then-removed. One surface was deliberately NOT written and is
  recorded as a plan-level rejection rather than a revert: a `--live`-sibling real-model harness arm, withheld
  because a live leg's `expect` atoms must be authored from a log that exists and this chunk drives nothing.
- **Insufficient fixes (written, kept, not the remedy):** none.

- **Spec claims disproved by measurement:** **one, and it is a rule file rather than a spec master.**
  `.claude/rules/verification-harness.md`'s 2026-08-16 entry states that the deterministic-L4 fixture "pins
  [`evidence_refs`] to `[]` (`deterministic_inference.rs:35`)". Measured false at Pulse HEAD `83d40601`: the
  array sits at `pulse-app/src/deterministic_inference.rs:68-72` and holds a populated triple

  `det-fingerprint-4a7f2b91c6e05d3849b1e7a2c5f08d63`); `:35` is now a doc-comment line about scrubber bounds.
  **It was TRUE when written and went stale the next day**: the triple landed 2026-08-17 in Pulse commit
  `efabe8e` (`feat(2026-08-17-conductor-e2e-verification-closure)`), whose diff changes
  `"evidence_refs": []` to the three values above. **No spec master carries the stale claim** — the only
  master citing that file is `architecture.md:64`, which already states the corrected reading ("freshness stays
  the carrier because the values never vary with what Conductor emitted, *not because the field is empty*").
  Basis: `grep -rnoE '.{130}deterministic_inference\.rs.{60}'` across all seven masters — one hit, current.
  **Owner: P3 curation** (a Tier-2 rule-file correction), not a P2 amendment.
  Two SUT-side descriptions are likewise stale — `crates/mcp-server/src/jsonrpc.rs:189` and
  `crates/interpretation/src/markdown.rs:20-27` both say only resolved incidents render hypotheses, which
  `attach_interpretation_summary` exists to defeat — but those are the SUT's own artifacts and are recorded
  here as a planning hazard, not as anything this repo amends.

- **Expected amendments (from plan):** one entry.
  - `architecture.md` §Occupied Resources — On-disk artifacts — register
    `contracts/pulse-real-model-leg-posture.md` as a second reader-less `contracts/` member. **Carried**: its
    fact is the Files and Symbols/APIs bullets above (a new on-disk artifact under `contracts/`, reader-less
    regime). Site search: `grep -c 'pulse-p025-measurement-contract' .andromeda/architecture.md` → **1 hit**,
    at `architecture.md:181` — the precedent's registry row in §Occupied Resources — so the owning master and
    the insertion point are both named on evidence rather than by assumption. Note for the applier: the P-025 precedent was recorded n=1 with no
    playbook rule minted, so a second reader-less member is a judgement to surface, not a settled pattern.

- **Coverage of new surfaces:**
  - `contracts/pulse-real-model-leg-posture.md` (a committed document, not an external surface) → validation
    `n/a` (nothing parses it) · instrumentation `n/a` (no runtime path) · PII `redacted✓` (asserted by gate 7:
    zero host-path matches, count 0) · tests `unit/integ` (the workspace suite ran green over the tree
    carrying it; two probes assert its presence, structure and host-path freedom) · a11y `n/a` (no UI) ·
    tokens `n/a` (no UI).

**None.** All seven implementation steps executed as written; both touchpoint lists were exactly right; no step
was skipped, reordered or reinterpreted, and no plan-listed rejection was crossed.

- **Operator correction (advisory baseline), applied and then extended by one step.** The implement report
  compared today's 1247 against **1243** (2026-09-10) and framed the delta as "wrong by four". The directive
  corrected the baseline to **1246** (`chunks/2026-09-16-scenario-assertion-audit-gate/report.md:229`, which
  itself records the move 1243 → 1246). Re-deriving the corpus bare rather than accepting either enumeration
  found a **newer** reading still: `chunks/2026-09-17-a11y-routine-arm-terminal-on-the-measured-configuration/report.md:292`
  records 1247 · 562 · 7 — the same triple as today, one day earlier. **The true delta is ZERO.** Both the
  original and the corrected figure were artifacts of reaching past a newer recorded reading; the directive's
  own stated principle applied one step further than the directive itself reached.

- **Operator correction (the 986 attribution), applied.** The implement report attributed the recorded count to
  "the prior chunk". The immediately prior chunk (`2026-09-17-keyboard-and-focus-order-coverage-ownership`,
  = HEAD) records nextest green at exit 0 **without** the count (`report.md:74`). The count is carried by four
  reports — `grep -rln '986 tests' conductor-0.3.0/chunks/*/report.md`, bare — of which the directive's cited
  `2026-09-16-a11y-ci-gate-at-an-honest-terminal/report.md:180` is one and the most recent is
  `2026-09-17-a11y-routine-arm-terminal-on-the-measured-configuration/report.md:288`. The comparison
  986 → 986 across a zero-`.rs`-delta span stands; only the attribution was wrong.

- **Sweep hazard found this chunk (self-inflicted, and the corpus already warned of it).** While checking the
  986 attribution, a sweep run as `grep -rn '986' … | grep -iE 'test|nextest|pass' | tail -8` returned four
  carriers and appeared to show the directive's cited file absent — because `tail -8` had clipped it, the
  alphabetically-earliest hit. Reading the cited line directly is what corrected it. The pattern to distrust is
  any clipped multi-path sweep used to assert an ABSENCE: the honest form is `grep -rln` bare, and the count is
  read from the bare command.

- **Class finding — a cross-repository citation has no re-check mechanism anywhere in either pipeline.** The
  stale entry above cites another repository's `file:line`. Nothing in Conductor's pipeline re-verifies such a
  citation when the other repository moves, and nothing in Pulse's pipeline knows Conductor cites it. This one
  was true when written, went stale the next day in Pulse commit `efabe8e`, and survived a month — surfacing
  only because this chunk happened to read the cited file for an unrelated reason. Note the asymmetry that
  makes it worse than an internal staleness: the wrap cascade sweeps the seven masters and re-derives their
  leaves, so `architecture.md` was corrected; a **rule file** carrying the same kind of citation is swept by
  nothing. Worth stating as a class, not only fixing the instance.

- **Correction to a finding this chunk carried: the code-graph gap was a STALE INDEX, not a missing symbol.**
  P3 recorded `execute_scenario` as absent from the rust plane's `symbol` view (a `symbol`-by-name probe

1. **The deterministic flag is load-bearing for the dedupe WINDOW, not only for reproducibility**

title: The load-bearing mechanism, stated as the equality the design needs — and verified at HEAD

data.head: ## The load-bearing mechanism, stated as the equality the design needs — and verified at HEAD

body:
**Needed:** a real-model leg's incident, read back through the MCP surface, yields a report whose
`## Hypotheses` section carries the model's top-ranked statement, in a form a Conductor check can grade.
**Verified chain (SUT source at `83d4060`, then Conductor source at HEAD):**

2. `serialize_report` emits the literal section header `## Hypotheses` (`markdown.rs:153`) only when the
   parsed L4 is present; `HypothesisView` (`:41`) is described at `incidents_router.rs:84` as a **"Single
   ranked hypothesis"**, so position in the array is the rank.

3. Conductor's `extract.rs:102` pushes that `markdown` into `Observation.text`, and `observed_for()` hands
   the composed text to every substring kind — so **`ComparisonKind::Contains` can grade a hypothesis
   substring**. The assertion is expressible as a scenario `[[expected]]` check; it does not need a new kind.

**The half that decides the design — WHO WRITES `resolution_summary_text`:** two writers, and neither fires
on first incident creation.

- `attach_resolution_summary` — rejects anything not already **Resolved** (`registry.rs:128-143`); fired from
  `inference_runtime.rs:250` only when `digest.kind == DigestKind::ResolutionSummary || parsed.is_resolution_summary`.

- `attach_interpretation_summary` — the **live** sibling (`registry.rs:145-160`), added expressly "so a report
  renders the model's actual content instead of a false-degraded notice"; rejects a Resolved incident. Fired at
  `inference_runtime.rs:823`, and only inside the **dedupe re-generation** branch: an existing active incident
  matching `(kind, scope, scope_id)` whose `observe_reemission` succeeded.

**Therefore:** the FIRST incident a storm forms carries `resolution_summary_text: None`, so `retrieve_report`
returns `degraded_mode: true` and a report with **no `## Hypotheses` section at all** — nothing to grade. The
hypotheses become readable only after a SECOND cue-bearing digest on the same `(kind, scope, scope_id)` identity
while the incident is still active, or after a resolution summary post-resolution. **A single-storm real-model
leg has no hypothesis observable by construction.**

title: Two claims that did NOT survive re-derivation at HEAD

data.head: ## Two claims that did NOT survive re-derivation at HEAD

body:
- **`.claude/rules/verification-harness.md` entry 2026-08-16 is stale on `evidence_refs`.** It states the
  deterministic fixture "pins [`evidence_refs`] to `[]` (`deterministic_inference.rs:35`)". At Pulse HEAD the
  fixture populates it with a `det-*` triple (`deterministic_inference.rs:68-72`) and its doc comment
  (`:26-35`) explains at length why an empty vector would be wrong ("makes every payload-identity assertion …
  compare nothing and pass"); line 35 is now a scrubber-pattern sentence. The obs extract carried the CORRECT
  version ("a constant `det-*` triple"), which is what surfaced the divergence. Owner: a rule-file curation
  item at wrap, not a phase edit.

- **`retrieve_report`'s own tool description (`jsonrpc.rs:189`) is stale**, and so is `markdown.rs`'s header
  contract (`:20-27`). Both say active incidents render a degraded notice and only resolved ones render full
  hypotheses; `attach_interpretation_summary` exists precisely to defeat that, and is the live path. The
  behaviour is decided by `parsed_l4.is_some()`, never by status — which is why the chain above is traced to
  the writers rather than read off either description.
- **5-command surface, sibling stage flag** — no sixth command; `--live` is a `case` branch (`agent-run.sh:270`).
- **Two-shell parity** — every `--live` change lands in both `.sh` and `.ps1` (measured at parity today).

- **Reader-less `contracts/` member** — `contracts/pulse-p025-measurement-contract.md` is the precedent: no
  `default_path()`, no `resolve_under`, no bounds check, no `CONDUCTOR_*` override; carries `provenance`.

- **Host-path freedom** — the committed artifact is grep-verifiable clean of drive-letter/`%APPDATA%`/`/home`
  tokens; note the standing false-positive class (a `letter:slash` run also matches a URL scheme).

- `contracts/pulse-real-model-leg-posture.md` — the committed posture + grading rule + quiet-window statement,
  reader-less regime. (Name/shape is P4's to fix; the regime is settled by the precedent above.)

- `scripts/agent-run.sh` · `scripts/agent-run.ps1` — only if P4 decides the posture needs a registered arm;
  a documentation-only posture may touch neither. Both bind together if either does.

- No `.rs` modify-set is implied by the posture itself. **The PREREQ's `cargo clippy` therefore runs over a
  zero-`.rs`-delta tree by design — which is the same condition that justified deferring it twice. It runs
  anyway: the pin's third consecutive re-pin trips the age trigger, and the discharge is the point.**

- **Does the posture register a harness arm, or is it documentation-only?** → blocks: plan-decision. P4 must
  settle it; layouts/arch both constrain the answer (sibling flag, never a sixth command) but neither requires
  an arm to exist now, and the drive chunk is the natural owner of one.

- **What disposition does a real-model leg carry, given `SloTier` caps at `<90s` and formation alone measured
  ~110s?** → blocks: plan-decision. The declare-only + harvest-tier precedent (Patterns 4) is the only shape
  in the system that fits; P4 states it or states why not.

- **Is the ~110s figure still current at Pulse HEAD?** → blocks: implementation-scope. It is a 2026-09-06
  measurement of SUT timing that cannot be re-measured without a drive, and this chunk does not drive. It is
  recorded with its date and witness; the drive chunk confirms it.
**Epoch 4 — Live proof against a real Pulse** · head entry, `conductor-0.3.0/working-route.md:42`

**Working entry (verbatim intent):** Real-model leg posture and grading rule — deterministic mode off,
operator-gated, never a CI gate, grading and per-leg quiet window fixed beforehand

The **posture half** of Epoch 4's live-proof pair. It fixes — *in advance of any drive* — the launch posture,
the grading rule and the per-leg quiet window under which a real-model (non-deterministic L4) live leg will be
run and judged. The drive itself belongs to the next route entry (`Interpretation proven live`).

The separation is by design, not sequencing convenience. `verification-matrix.json#v3-09` `notes` (route Phase
0/1, 2026-09-11) states it: *"The grading rule is stated in ADVANCE by design: a chunk that drives first and
decides the grading afterwards satisfies the letter and defeats the capability, which is why posture and drive
are separate route entries."* A posture authored after seeing a leg's output is not a posture; it is a
rationalization. This chunk therefore ships a **committed, dated statement** that the drive chunk is bound by.

1. **The launch posture for a real-model leg** — the complete, stated set of SUT-side and harness-side
   conditions under which the leg runs, and the ones that must *not* be set. Anchored on what the registry
   already records: `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC` OFF is the defining term (architecture.md:197 — the flag
   swaps a canned `L4Output` for the Llama-3.2-3B inference; Conductor **reads** it as a run-contract
   `shell-declaration` proxy and never sets it), alongside the already-in-use boot-wide
   `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_BASELINE_BOOTSTRAP_SECONDS` lever whose disposition for *this* leg must be stated rather
   than inherited.

2. **The grading rule** — how a non-deterministic top-hypothesis assertion is graded, written so that it
   decides a verdict without reference to the run that produced it. It must state at minimum: what counts as
   "the top-ranked hypothesis identifies the injected root cause", which `Verdict`/`ReportState` a miss maps
   to, and — explicitly, per v3-09's acceptance — that **a leg that fails grades as a failure rather than
   being re-driven until it passes**.

3. **The per-leg quiet window and serialization rule** — the interval each real-model leg requires before and
   after it, with its arithmetic stated. v3-09 `notes`: *"live legs are serialized rather than merely ordered,
   because the system under test dedupes a new incident against any open one and every run fires its own
   preflight canary, so each leg rides its own quiet window."*

4. **The operator gate** — the leg is operator-invoked and **never a CI gate**, stated as a property of the
   posture rather than left to the invocation path's current shape.
5. **PREREQ discharge** — close the standing rust gate deferral (below).

title: Boundaries — what this chunk does NOT do

data.head: ## Boundaries — what this chunk does NOT do

body:
- **It does not drive a leg.** No live run against a real model, no incident asserted, no hypothesis graded.
  The next entry (`Interpretation proven live`) owns the drive.

- **It does not claim `v3-09`.** v3-09's acceptance quantifies over the drive *and* the posture ("A live leg
  runs … and the leg asserts …"), so this chunk only **partially advances** it: per the matrix contract's
  multi-chunk rule the cap stays `chunk: null` and is cited in this chunk's `plan.md` provenance. Confirmed
  at P5.

- **It does not touch `v3-08`.** That cap is BLOCKED on a Pulse release emitting the P-025 observable —
  externally clearing, not Conductor's to clear, and a different route entry's subject.

- **It does not re-open the deterministic-L4 legs.** The existing `--live` suite (H · B1 · B2 · quiet · A ·
  driven-a11y) keeps its current posture and its verified results; this chunk adds a real-model posture beside
  it, and must not weaken or re-grade what deterministic legs already proved.
- **It opens no inbound listener and adds no network reach** (scope law, unchanged).

- `scripts/agent-run.{sh,ps1}` — the operator-gated `--live` suite and its `preconditions` short-circuit; any
  real-model arm lives here or beside it. `[inferred]` — the entry names neither file.

- `contracts/` — the natural home for a committed, code-unread posture/measurement statement, by the precedent
  of `pulse-p025-measurement-contract.md`. `[inferred]` — form to be settled in P3/P4.

- `.andromeda/residuals.md:9` — the `2026-08-09-interpretation-correctness-posture · absorbed:v3-09` pin, which
  states this exact subject and must stay consistent with what ships.

- `contracts/pulse-run-contract.toml` — `warmup_ms` / `min_canary_poll_seconds`, the terms the harness shells
  already parse for the `boot` budget and the preflight floor a real-model leg's timing must respect.

- The `UNBACKED_AUTO` set in `conductor-core` (P-031 / P-033 / P-034 / P-044) — the diagnostic-quality cluster
  this posture ultimately serves. Read-only here; the cluster is a later entry's subject.

title: Premises — CLOSED at P3 (research.md holds the derivations)

data.head: ## Premises — CLOSED at P3 (research.md holds the derivations)

body:
- **VERIFIED — a real-model leg cannot be the existing suite with the flag flipped.** `agent-run.sh:118-121`
  and `verification-harness.md`'s 2026-09-06 entry (c) both state it: canned-L4 formation ~2s lands leg B2's
  storm inside Pulse's 120s idle window, **real-model formation measured ~110s would fall outside it** — "an
  env missing that flag does not make the leg slow, it makes it measure the wrong thing". Every per-leg budget
  and the 150s quiet window are calibrated to the canned path. The ~110s figure is a 2026-09-06 SUT-timing
  measurement this chunk cannot re-measure without driving; it is carried with its date and witness, and the
  drive chunk confirms it.

- **`[premise-corrected: `Thresholds::from_env` resolves the window ONCE at Pulse's boot, so no per-leg value
  exists to choose]` — the bootstrap-window lever's disposition is SUITE-wide, not leg-specific.**
  `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_BASELINE_BOOTSTRAP_SECONDS` is registered boot-wide and is the one handle Conductor neither
  sets nor reads. The posture must therefore state a single boot-time disposition binding the whole real-model
  suite, and record which posture actually booted by grepping Pulse's log for the target

     - In the `.ps1` twin, `RUST_LOG` is saved, removed and restored in a `finally`: the env is process-wide when the
       script is dot-invoked.
     - Each of (c′) and (e) runs there as
       `Start-Process -PassThru -RedirectStandardOutput <tmp> -RedirectStandardError <tmp>` without `-Wait`, then
       `WaitForExit()` (host-win32.md:135). The temp files hold the child's own bytes, and the two capture files are
       assembled from them with
       `[System.IO.File]::AppendAllText(<path>, <text>, (New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding $false))`, which writes
       BOM-less UTF-8 on both PowerShell editions.
     - Never `>`, `*>`, `Out-File` or `Set-Content`: the harness runs under `powershell.exe` 5.1, whose redirects
       write UTF-16.

     A non-zero exit is a harness error exit, never a graded outcome. The capture is then printed;
   - (f) the reminders: the bootstrap disposition is the default (no override; inert for the storm path, confirmed
     by the capture's Pulse-log witness); the stop form (census-delta rows stopped by PID after a parentage and
     start-time read, the live entry's `stop`); `pulse-app` left running, stopped by the operator; the census taken
     twice.

   A `timeout` exit at (d) ends the arm before its freeze and capture: 124 under `set -euo pipefail`
   (`agent-run.sh:19`), or the `.ps1` twin's `exit 124`. It also leaves `conductor.exe` and the sidecar running,
   because `timeout` and `$p.Kill()` reach only cargo (`agent-run.sh:81`, `agent-run.ps1:137-142`). Census-after and
   the stop form follow, and the attempt is classified per B2 before anything re-fires.

   Also correct the `real-model formation (~110s)` comment (`agent-run.sh:119`, `agent-run.ps1:182`) to its
   deterministic-L4 provenance, and add `--live [real-model]` to the usage strings. The deterministic `--live`
   order, the other stage flags and the five commands are unchanged.

10. **The capture tool** — `crates/conductor-run/tests/real_model_live.rs`, `#![cfg(feature = "live-pulse")]`. The
    feature exists (`Cargo.toml:27`), so no manifest change is needed.
    - The header carries Conductor's firing form and the stop form. It refers to the posture document for the
      operator's `pulse-app` launch and names no unregistered handle.
    - A shared module, `crates/conductor-run/tests/real_model_common/mod.rs`, is declared by this file and by the
      harvest, and both targets use both of its helpers. As a `tests/` subdirectory it is not a target of its own.
      - `rule_section(src)`: the span between the rule's two marker LINES (whole-line match), markers included, with
        line endings normalized to LF.
      - `mask_host_paths(text)`, applied after `redact_value`, which tests only whitespace-separated tokens
        (`conductor-core/src/redact.rs:79-80`). It replaces with `<host-path>` every run that form misses: a
        drive-letter path (`X:\…` or `X:/…`, the `\\?\` prefix included), an MSYS root (`/x/…` after a non-word
        character), and `/home/…`, `/Users/…` or `%APPDATA%…`, each up to the next whitespace, backtick, quote or
        closing bracket.

      The mask's arms live in the harvest (the default suite). The review's five forms are masked: a backticked
      ref, `(D:\…`, `path=D:\…`, `\\?\D:\…` and `/d/…`. A loopback URL and a repo-relative path are left untouched.
    - A second, `#[ignore]`d test, `rule_record`, prints `rule_section(include_str!("real_model_harvest.rs"))` for
      step 9 (c′). The `#[ignore]` keeps it out of B5's exact capture command, where two tests' `--nocapture`
      output would interleave.
    - One `#[tokio::test(flavor = "current_thread")]` that PRINTS and never asserts beyond I/O. B3's `≥ 0` check runs
      last, after every line is printed, so a failing check cannot truncate the one drive's capture. Every printed
      line that carries SUT-derived text passes `redact_value` then `mask_host_paths`:
      - (a) `run_id: {id}`, and the emission instant = the `timestamp_ms` of the leg's `timeline.execute` span-open
        line in `runs/live-suite/rm.jsonl` (workspace-root anchored; `CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR` honoured, as in
        `live_suite.rs:58-64`). If absent, it prints the preflight outcome lines and `emission: none`. It also prints one
        `trace:` summary line from that file: the distinct `span` names on span-open lines, the count of `debug`
        `wire shape:` lines (`conductor-emit/src/client.rs:70`), and whether a `read-back shape: retrieve_report`
        line (`extract.rs:229-233`) is present;
      - (b) the leg's envelope line, with each `fingerprints` element replaced by `<model-text>`. Those elements are
        the union of raw, model-written evidence refs over every active incident, the canary's included
        (`conductor-verify/src/extract.rs:111-117`). They are free text up to 256 chars (Pulse
        `crates/interpretation/src/schema.rs:103`) and never scrubbed. The eleven keys and the closed sets stay
        intact for step 14. Then one count line: `envelope fingerprints: n, det- prefixed: k`;
      - (c) a poll of `query_incident_list` through `ReadbackClient::connect` every 10 s for at most 600 s, for
        items whose `opened_at_unix_nano` is at or after the emission instant. B3 overrides this open-time
        selection: attribution is by the scenario's cue fingerprint, and reading is by id. On the first poll carrying
        exactly one, it prints `attributed: incident_id=… opened_at_unix_nano=… degraded_mode=… pickup_ms=…`, then
        that report's `## Hypotheses` and `## Evidence` sections.
        - `pickup_ms` is `opened_at` − the emission instant, in ms. Pulse stamps `opened_at` at digest PICKUP,
          before inference (B3), so the figure measures pickup, never formation.
        - Two or more → their identity lines and `attribution: ambiguous`. None by the bound →
          `attribution: none within 600s`. A call error → `read-back failed: {redacted reason}`.
        - Items opened earlier print identity only, never text;
      - (d) Pulse-log witnesses from the newest `{ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR}/logs/agent-latest.jsonl.*`: the count
        and structured fields (never `message`) of `interpretation.prompt.assemble` (the tier),
        `interpretation.json.parse` and `interpretation.incident.created` since the leg's first self-obs line, and
        the whole-file count of `triage.baseline.bootstrap_window.override`.
        - Also, from the whole Pulse log (like B1's `interpretation.model.load` witness), the `app.boot.workspace_key`
          line's `workspace_root_basename` (Pulse `pulse-app/src/main.rs:259-266`). It is printed only as
          `workspace basename carries conductor: true|false`, a case-insensitive substring test that is stricter
          than the rule's whole-word one. The basename itself is never printed.
        - Why this matters: `pulse-app`'s cwd reaches the prompt as `PROJECT:`
          (`crates/triage/src/digest/assembler.rs:629`, fed from `main.rs:746-748`). A launch from this repo would
          put `conductor` in front of the model outside the cue.
    - Failure text names a handle or a file name, never a resolved path.

12. **Posture corrections** — `contracts/pulse-real-model-leg-posture.md`. Add dated
    `[corrected 2026-09-22 (2026-09-22-interpretation-proven-live, P3 research, before any drive): …]` notes, each
    citing its evidence:
    - the metadata `provenance` line and the `~110 s` mentions in §Disposition and §The quiet window → a
      deterministic-L4 measurement (P-E);
    - §The emission profile's "Therefore a single-storm leg has no hypothesis observable at all" → false at the
      pinned HEAD. The creation-time attach exists; the multi-digest profile is sufficient, not necessary; and
      `## Hypotheses` always renders (P-B, P-C);
    - §Disposition's "a known-residual state" → the success path lands `ManualCheck` (P-D).

    The items the P5 review adds carry
    `[corrected 2026-09-23 (2026-09-22-interpretation-proven-live, P5 review, before any drive): …]`:
    - §The grading rule's "The assertion is a substring comparison against the composed observation text …"
      (`:103-106`) → false (P-F). No Conductor artifact persists the report text, and the composed text can express
      neither rank nor attribution. The rule is applied to the attributed incident's rank-1 statement, re-read over
      MCP and graded in the harvest. The sentence's "no new comparison kind … span attribute" consequence still
      holds;
    - §Disposition's "a harvest-style test over the leg's verbatim captures" (`:141-143`) → the harvest grades a
      capture that the `live-pulse`-gated tool re-reads after the leg. It never grades the leg's own captures, which
      carry no report text (P-F);
    - the table's "(… or the second generation never landed)" (`:115`) → no second generation is needed, because
      the interpretation attaches at creation (P-B);
    - "the drive chunk confirms rather than inherits" (`:19-20`), and its sibling at `:160-161` ("that figure is
      confirmed at the first drive") → the carried figure is a deterministic-L4 measurement (P-E), so no drive can
      confirm it. This drive measures PICKUP (inference excluded, B3) and records it under that name; real-model
      formation stays unmeasured;
    - D2's stated limit, per the fold.

    All of these are mechanism corrections, never re-decisions: the grading rule, launch posture, window rule and
    census are NOT edited. After the drive, append the measured PICKUP figure (digest pickup, inference excluded,
    never "formation") to the provenance line as a dated measurement record.

14. **Pin and record.** Pin these from the capture into `real_model_harvest.rs` as literals, OUTSIDE the rule's
    markers: the attributed identity line, its `## Hypotheses` and `## Evidence` sections, the envelope, the `trace:`
    line and the witness lines. The header names the capture date, Pulse HEAD, posture, tier and pickup figure. Add
    these tests:
    - `grade(pinned)` equals the outcome the drive measured, whatever it is. The rule graded it; the author did not.
    - The pinned `## Evidence` section carries no `det-` fixture identifier, so the report came from the model and
      not the canned fixture.
    - The envelope test is conditioned on the pinned route (step 11's `route`). Where the capture carries an envelope
      line, its key set equals `ENVELOPE_KEYS_SORTED` (`run_record.rs:15`) through a `serde_json::Value` key-set
      check, and it parses as `RunRecord` (closed verdict/state/tier sets). A typed parse alone cannot prove a
      nullable key present (testing.md 2026-09-06). Where the capture carries none, the route must be
      `PreflightBlocked`, or the test fails.
    - The pinned `trace:` line carries its route's witness set (step 11). For `ReadBack`, that is `scenario.run`,
      `timeline.execute`, `emit.batch` and a `verify.readback*` span, a `wire shape:` count ≥ 1, and the
      `retrieve_report` key-set witness present.
    - `rule_predates_the_drive`: `rule_section` of the committed `evidence/rm-capture.txt` (its pre-leg record, step
      9 (c′)) equals `rule_section` of this file. That shows the rule was not edited after the leg.
    - `pinned_literals_equal_the_committed_capture`: every pinned literal equals its section of the committed
      `evidence/rm-capture.txt`, read workspace-root anchored from `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`.
    - B4's ref test also asserts that the pinned `workspace basename carries conductor:` line reads `false` (step 10
      (d)).

    Record the pickup figure, named as pickup, in the chunk report and in step 12's provenance line. The `v3-09`
    outcome note is wrap's ledger write (see Expected amendments).
15. **Gates** — run the fence.
- `scenarios/real-model-interpretation.toml` — the known cause as declared emission data, declaring the real-model posture.
- `crates/conductor-run/tests/real_model_live.rs` — the `live-pulse`-gated capture tool (step 10).
- `crates/conductor-run/tests/real_model_harvest.rs` — the rule, its synthetic arms and the pinned capture (steps 11, 14).
- `crates/conductor-run/tests/real_model_common/mod.rs` — `rule_section` and `mask_host_paths`, shared by the capture and the harvest (step 10).
- `conductor-0.3.0/chunks/2026-09-22-interpretation-proven-live/evidence/rm-capture.txt` — the drive's bounded capture.

- `crates/conductor-core/src/run_contract.rs` · `crates/conductor-core/src/lib.rs` — `L4Posture`, `ShellAbsence`,
  the posture tag, `evaluate_for` (step 1).
- `crates/conductor-core/src/preconditions.rs` — `evaluate_for` (step 3).
- `crates/conductor-core/src/scenario.rs` — the `l4_posture` field + its tests + the family test (steps 4, 7).

- `crates/conductor-core/src/error.rs` · `crates/conductor-core/src/load_envelope.rs` · `crates/conductor-run/tests/dispatch_wire.rs` ·
  `crates/conductor-timeline/src/convert.rs` — the `Scenario` literals (step 4).
- `contracts/pulse-run-contract.toml` — the tag and the `l4-real-model` term (step 2).
- `crates/conductor-run/src/{preconditions,canary,execute,lib}.rs` — the posture threading + the mismatch Blocked (step 5).
- `crates/conductor-run/tests/composition_root.rs` — the two new public paths (step 5; graph rows `:50`, `:52`) + its `Scenario` literal (step 4).
- `crates/conductor-run/src/testkit.rs` — the `Preflight` and `ContractTerm` literals + the ready-gate builder (steps 1, 5).
- `crates/conductor-run/tests/run_contract_pin.rs` — the doc comments at `:3`, `:70` only; its pins hold through the dedupe (step 1).
- `crates/conductor-cli/src/{cli.rs,main.rs,commands/preconditions.rs,commands/run.rs}` + `crates/conductor-cli/tests/cli_smoke.rs` (step 6).
- `contracts/scenario-audit-ledger.toml` — the `[[over_tier]]` row (step 8).
- `scripts/agent-run.sh` · `scripts/agent-run.ps1` — the `real-model` selector arm + the corrected comment (step 9).
- `contracts/pulse-real-model-leg-posture.md` — the dated corrections + the measured figure (steps 12, 14).

- **Deliberately untouched** (callers of the deterministic entry points, research §Graph impact): `commands/suite.rs:26`,
  `conductor-tauri/src/commands.rs:323`, `conductor-cli/tests/cross_surface_parity.rs:99`, `drive.rs:80`,
  `conductor-verify/tests/preflight.rs` (a constructed contract), `wdio.conf.ts:67` (a comment).

The block runs in the order below. The live leg (`leg = 'live'`) is fired by the agent at step 13 with the operator's
Pulse up, never by the gate tool. It is preceded by its NON-PRIMING probe (`conductor preconditions --for …`, which
fires no canary) and bracketed by a census. The status smoke reads the `run_id` the leg's capture prints
(mint-then-read), so it is an `operator` entry the wrap does not re-run. No `self-verify` entry is listed: this is not
a UI/visual chunk. The deterministic `--live` suite is not driven this chunk. Its gating stays byte-unchanged at the
unit tier (steps 1, 3, 5), and re-launching Pulse deterministic mid-chunk would prime nothing this chunk measures. CI
is read by the next chunk's Setup 5a against this wrap's pushed sha.
Three more notes on the block:

- The live entry is fired BACKGROUNDED and read on its completion notification: at about 24 min, it outlasts one
  foreground call.

- The evidence hygiene entry's subject, `evidence/rm-capture.txt`, is the agent's step-13 copy of the live entry's
  `artifact`. No entry produces it, and it reads red (file absent, exit 2) until the drive.
- The two `run --live bogus` entries exercise each shell's new selector arm without Pulse.

body:
- (arch) Every outcome of the leg is a value from the closed sets. A graded miss is `CalibrationRegion` →
  `ManualCheck` through the posture's table, and never `Fail` or `Err`. A leg that never reached its assertion is
  `Blocked` with its named precondition. The chunk adds no `Verdict`/`ReportState` variant, envelope key or
  `slo_tier` value (per architecture §Established Decisions [Probabilistic-Assertion Policy]).

- (arch) With the scenario committed, `check_scenario_backing`, `check_sut_drift`, `check_load_envelope` (`[[exempt]]`
  still empty), `check_scenario_audit` (with the new `[[over_tier]]` row) and the coverage-completeness byte-compare
  are all green. `UNBACKED_AUTO` and `coverage-matrix.md` are byte-unchanged (per architecture §Established Decisions
  [Accepted Capability Set]).

- (arch) The posture is scenario data. Every pre-existing scenario loads `Deterministic`. `preflight()`,
  `observe_preconditions()` and `RunContract::evaluate` keep their exact results, and a real-model scenario under a
  deterministic gate lands `Blocked`, never executed (per architecture §Standard Contracts — Readiness gate).

- (arch) The pickup figure (`opened_at` − the emission instant: digest pickup, inference excluded) is measured from
  Conductor's own `std::time` emission instant, never test-start wall-clock, and the leg adds no outbound target or listener (per architecture §Design Philosophy — Journal-relative
  ground truth; §Cross-cutting Patterns — Trust boundary).

- (security) The real-model L4 check is declaration-only: the complement of `flag_declared`, over Conductor's own
  environment, naming the handle only. No code writes or unsets any `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_*` handle, and a deterministic run
  with L4 undeclared is still refused by the probe and blocked by preflight (per security-plan §Input Validation, READ
  SET row).

- (security) `l4_posture` is a closed enum: an unknown value is a load-time harness fault. No `#[garde(skip)]` is added
  on a nested struct field (per security-plan §Input Validation, scenario-config row; §Security Anti-Patterns →
  Input).

- (security) A failed read-back, a degraded report, an empty hypothesis body or an unattributable incident grades
  `Blocked`, never `Pass`. Each has its synthetic arm in `real_model_harvest.rs` (per security-plan §Input Validation,
  MCP child stdout row).

- (security) The committed capture and harvest carry zero absolute host paths and no data-dir value. This is proven by
  three hygiene entries each returning 0: the `grep -cE "\b[A-Za-z]:[\\/]|…"` entry over
  `crates/conductor-run/tests/real_model_harvest.rs`, the one over `evidence/rm-capture.txt`, and the
  posture-document entry. The capture elides the envelope's model-written `fingerprints` and masks host paths after
  `redact_value`, with arms for the review's five forms (step 10). `cargo audit` + `cargo deny check advisories bans licenses sources` are green over an unchanged
  `Cargo.lock` (per security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Logging; §Dependency Security).

- (tests) `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci`, `cargo test --workspace --doc`, both clippy entries,
  `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo test -p` for `conductor-core` / `conductor-run` / `conductor-cli` all return 0 (per
  test-plan §3 run; §4 Framework; §10 Coverage thresholds).

- (tests) `real_model_harvest.rs` maps captures onto the posture's four rows, and every negative arm of step 11 holds:
  below-rank-1, degraded, empty, canary mis-attribution, `conductor-canary`, a single facet, justification-only,
  ambiguity and read-back failure. So do the extraction and token-surface arms (13)-(21), each stated limit included,
  and the `mask_host_paths` arms (per test-plan §6 Severity-lifecycle; Fingerprint-storm; Scenario-assertion audit
  leg).

- (tests) The drive is operator-gated and envelope-neutral. It is fired once through `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run
  --live real-model` and exits 0. Its row has a null verdict (`ManualCheck` when the read-back is non-degraded), and
  it writes no `CheckRecord`. No CI step invokes it (per test-plan §3 run; §9 Live-Pulse scenarios; §11 CI).

- (tests) A graded outcome is never re-driven. Only a Conductor-side environment fault named by the probe or the
  gate's non-model preconditions may be repaired and re-fired, and each such attempt is recorded as unmeasured (per
  test-plan §10 Zero-flakiness budget; §11 E2E).

- (obs) The harvest-pinned envelope carries exactly the eleven keys (`ENVELOPE_KEYS_SORTED`) and parses into the
  closed sets. The pinned `trace:` summary names the must-trace chain, the `retrieve_report` key-set witness and at
  least one `debug` wire-shape witness. No new span name, span attribute or envelope key is added (per obs-plan §3;
  §4 Critical Path 1; §6 Boundary-call wrappers; §11 Spans).

- (obs) The pickup figure is recorded as a measurement, named as pickup and never as formation, and never as a
  budget, tier or soft SLO (per obs-plan §5; §10; §11 SLO).

- (design) The leg renders only existing lamps, and its own row renders the lamp its envelope carries:
  - `[MANUAL]` whenever the in-run read-back is non-degraded (`execute.rs:280`). That includes three harvest-`Blocked`
    routes: the empty placeholder, no attributable incident, and ambiguous attribution.
  - `[RESIDUAL]` when the read-back is degraded.
  - `[BLOCKED]` when the gate or the in-run read-back blocked.

  The GRADED outcome is the harvest's, never the leg row's lamp. It is recorded in the chunk report and the v3-09
  notes with its own text label and ASCII prefix from the posture's table (`[PASS]` / `[MANUAL]` / `[BLOCKED]`), so a
  graded Blocked stays lexically distinct from a miss even where the leg row reads `[MANUAL]`. No outcome renders
  `[FAIL]`, and the diff adds no bracket label, ANSI code or token (per design-system §Surface: cli → Tokens;
  §Anti-Patterns → Rejected Defaults).

- (layouts) `agent-run` keeps exactly five commands. `real-model` is a selector of the existing `--live` arm, reached
  by no default stage and no CI job. An unknown `--live` selector is a usage error at exit 2 in both shells (the two
  `run --live bogus` entries). `preconditions --for` takes a scenario name and refuses at exit 1 naming each unmet
  subject (per layout-templates §cli Primary screens).

- (a11y) The driven-a11y leg's owner, posture and results are unchanged, and the real-model arm never runs
  `a11y:driven`. Every verdict/state pair the leg writes resolves to an existing lamp label, and the drive is recorded
  as not-assertable under the `conductor-cli` entity (per a11y-plan §11 Strategy; §6 crosswalk; §1).

- (matrix) `verification-matrix.json#v3-09` — the concretized acceptance written at P5. It is met iff the single
  drive's pinned capture grades `Identified` AND the real-model witnesses hold (the binding fold, D1 · B1 · B4). A
  `NotIdentified` or model-side `Blocked` outcome is recorded, and `v3-09` is un-claimed and deferred at wrap.

- **Operator decisions (P4):** the posture is scenario-declared · the capture is an MCP re-read tool, with a
  §Data Protection amendment raised at wrap for ratification · the cause is identified by `conductor` whole-word AND
  retry, case-insensitive.

- **Decisive leans taken (not asked):**
  - Stimulus P-ID only (`P-018`), per `working-route.md:46` + `verification-matrix.json#v3-10`'s acceptance ("the
    roll-up count and the committed coverage artifact both move in the same change").
  - Kept a multi-burst profile per the posture's emission clause (sufficient under the corrected mechanism).
  - `<90s` + `[[over_tier]]`, per the ledger header's honest-bucket posture.
  - `#[garde(skip)]` on a closed enum, per `phase_spec.rs:60`/`:97`.
  - Grading on the statement only, per `pulse-capability-spec.md:444` ("hypothesis statement in plain language") and
    `markdown.rs:160-168`.
  - ~~The one-sided `Pass` needs no arch-body record~~ — REJECTED at P5 by the operator (D3): it is an Expected
    amendment to [Probabilistic-Assertion Policy].
  - New entry points beside the old, per research §Graph impact.
  - Dated in-place corrections to the posture's mechanism clauses, per the posture's own "the transcribed clauses will
    need re-checking … the drive chunk confirms rather than inherits" (`pulse-real-model-leg-posture.md:19-20`).

- **Spec anchors:** architecture §Standard Contracts · §Established Decisions [Probabilistic-Assertion Policy] ·
  [Accepted Capability Set] · [Read-Back Dependency Posture] · [CI/CD] · §Occupied Resources · security-plan §Input
  Validation · §Security Anti-Patterns · §Dependency Security · test-plan §3 · §6 · §9 · §10 · §11 · obs-plan §3 · §4 ·
  §5 · §6 · §10 · §11 · design-system §Surface: cli → Tokens · §Anti-Patterns · layout-templates §cli Primary screens ·
  a11y-plan §1 · §6 · §11.

- **Research files inspected:** `research.md` (Conductor 29 + Pulse 16 reads at HEAD `83d4060`; one graph query,
  32 rows) · `scope.md` (premise closure applied).

- **Deriving the posture from the environment — REJECTED.** A forgotten `L4_DETERMINISTIC=true` would silently become
  a real-model run and downgrade the deterministic suite's refusal (security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Universal).

- **A per-invocation `--real-model` flag — REJECTED at P4 (operator).** A forgotten flag grades the scenario under
  canned L4 with an indistinguishable envelope.

- **Setting or unsetting any `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_*` handle from the harness or a test — REJECTED** (READ SET: read, never
  written). Removing `RUST_LOG` for the capture invocation touches no READ SET handle.

- **Naming P-033 (or any cluster id) now — REJECTED (lean).** v3-10 moves the cluster's pin and the committed matrix
  together.

- **Grading through an `[[expected]]` `Contains` — REJECTED.** The composed text unions every active incident's report
  and the list fields (`extract.rs:90-103`), so it can express neither rank nor attribution.
- **A production self-obs line carrying hypothesis text, or in-process grading — REJECTED at P4 (operator).**

- **Re-driving after any graded outcome (Pass, miss, or a model-side Blocked) — REJECTED** (posture §The grading
  rule).

- **A long burst train as keep-alive — REJECTED.** Pulse refreshes `updated_at_unix_nano` only on registry writes
  (`crates/triage/src/incident/registry.rs:305-313`; auto-resolve reads it at `:322`), so a dismissed digest keeps
  nothing alive. The capture polls instead.

- **Skipping or softening the preflight canary under the real model — REJECTED** (never downgrade a preflight that
  runs). A dismissed canary is an honest `Blocked`.
- **Firing `boot` (or any preflight) before the leg — REJECTED** (`verification-harness.md:53` (a)).

- **A new `service` field on `EmissionSpec` — REJECTED.** The whole-word rule separates `conductor` from
  `conductor-canary`; a new identity would need arch registration and a model change for no grading gain.

- **Editing the posture's grading rule, launch posture, window rule or census — out of bounds.** Only its falsified
  mechanism clauses carry dated corrections.

- **The attended seam.** Steps 1–12 and the green non-leg gates land first, with the rule fixed before any drive.
  /implement then needs the operator's `pulse-app` under the posture. From Pulse's `AI-Model/RESUME-NOTE.md`, that
  means the model path and CUDA `llama-cli` path handles at launch and a release build made with the tokenizer
  override. The posture itself adds `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MCP_ENABLED=true`, the live data dir, deterministic L4 absent or
  falsy, and no bootstrap override. If the operator is unavailable, /implement ends with the drive PENDING, and the
  chunk holds `pending` until the drive is recorded, never wrapped with it owed (memory: attended-pass chunks hold
  across the seam).

- **Drive accounting.** Exactly one graded drive. Anything the SUT's model decides is the graded outcome: a canary it
  never surfaces within 600 s, a scenario incident it never forms, a degraded or scrub-redacted report, or a hit or a
  miss. A Conductor-side environment fault is not measured, so it is repaired and re-fired as an unmeasured attempt.
  Those faults are an unresolvable sidecar (~0 s `[BLOCKED]`, `verification-harness.md:54`), a refused probe, or a
  protocol/tool/workspace precondition. A re-fire on the same launch waits the quiet window first: 120 s idle plus a
  30 s tick after the last incident (posture §The quiet window).

- **v3-09 reachability.** The `ref` is `crates/conductor-run/tests/real_model_harvest.rs`, which /implement writes on
  green. If the pinned outcome is `Blocked`, the leg never reached its assertion, so the claim cannot flip `verified`.
  The honest exit is to un-claim at wrap with the measurement recorded in `notes`.

  - `architecture.md` §Standard Contracts — the readiness gate is posture-aware: a scenario-declared L4 posture
    selects the run-contract terms and the probe's L4 grading, and a mismatch lands `Blocked` at scenario level. The
    Run-report-envelope passage (`architecture.md:135`):
    - moves its complement "2 of 36" → "2 of 37";
    - records the new scenario as declare-only with a `ManualCheck` success row (`execute.rs:280`; P-D), not as a

    - the `pulse-run-contract.toml` row (`shell-absence`, `posture`, `l4-real-model`);
    - the L4 row (`:198`, "ONE OF TWO shell-declaration proxies …"): the handle is also read for ABSENCE under the

    - the posture row (`:182`): its "the emission profile a hypothesis observable requires" is false (P-B, P-C),

  - `security-plan.md` §Input Validation — the scenario-config row (`l4_posture`); the READ SET row (the L4 handle

callers of `observe_preconditions` · `observe_run_contract` · `preflight` · `readiness` · `canary_gate` ·
`execute_scenario` · `load_run_contract`. Editor lines (graph line + 1):

- **`conductor_run::preflight`** — `conductor-cli commands/run.rs:21`, `commands/suite.rs:26`, `conductor-tauri
  commands.rs:323` (`run_thread`), tests `conductor-cli/tests/cross_surface_parity.rs:99`,
  `conductor-run/tests/composition_root.rs:50` (`public_api_paths_are_stable`). A posture parameter here threads
  through the GUI path too. (The name also collides with `conductor-cli commands::preflight` — the `main.rs:86` row.)

- **`observe_preconditions`** — `conductor-cli commands/preconditions.rs:20`, its own test `preconditions.rs:133`,
  `composition_root.rs:52`.
- **`observe_run_contract`** / **`load_run_contract`** — `canary.rs:179-180` (`canary_gate`) + two unit tests.
- **`canary_gate`** — `canary.rs:55` (`preflight`), `:75` (`readiness`).

- **`execute_scenario`** — `commands/run.rs:23`, `commands/suite.rs:32`, `drive.rs:80` (`drive_run`, the Tauri
  path), three `execute.rs` tests.

**P-A · The posture's launch is unreachable at HEAD, through every path.** The equality the design needs is "a
Conductor environment with `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC` absent/falsy reaches read-back". It does not:
(1) `conductor preconditions` grades the handle by `flag_declared` (core `preconditions.rs:28-31`, `:61-66`), so
`handles-declared` is unmet and `run --live` refuses at exit 1 before any leg (`agent-run.sh:95-98`); (2) independently,
`canary_gate` evaluates term `l4-deterministic` (`shell-declaration`, `pulse-run-contract.toml:32-37`) as unmet and
`run_preflight` sets `ready:false` with the named precondition (`preflight.rs:228-229`) — so even a bare
`conductor run` returns `[BLOCKED]` for every scenario. The posture's own term ("absent or falsy … a
shell-declaration") is an INVERTED declaration the core cannot express: `CheckKind` has no such kind and
`flag_declared` has no complement.

**P-B · A single-storm incident HAS a hypothesis observable — the posture's clause (1) is false at its pinned HEAD.**
`create_incident_from_l4_output` attaches the parsed interpretation AT CREATION: `resolution_summary_text:
scrubbed_l4_json(parsed)` (`pulse-app/src/inference_runtime.rs:884`, comment "The latest cleanly-parsed interpretation
attaches AT CREATION, so the report renders the model's content for a live incident instead of a false-degraded
notice"). `git blame -L 884,884` → commit `b2e4cb3` (2026-08-27, *"a clean parse reaches the report and citing becomes
copying"*) — the SAME commit that added the `:823` dedupe attach the posture did cite, before the pinned `83d4060`
(2026-08-31). The posture traced the two `IncidentRegistry` attach methods and missed the struct-literal write.
Conductor's own record already showed it: leg b1 (2026-09-06, HEAD `83d4060`) read back its single-storm canary
incident as `ManualCheck` — non-degraded, since `state_for` returns `KnownResidual` iff degraded
(`live_suite_harvest.rs:51`, `execute.rs:248-254`). Consequences: the second cue-bearing digest is NOT necessary (it
remains sufficient — the dedupe branch refreshes the attachment with the latest generation); a report is degraded
only when no L4 output was attached OR the attached JSON fails to parse — including Pulse's WHOLE-FIELD scrub, which
replaces the entire JSON with `[redacted: {category}]` if any part trips a scrubber pattern (`:665-671`).

**P-C · `## Hypotheses` always renders; the discriminator is its body.** `serialize_report` pushes the header
unconditionally (`markdown.rs:153`): degraded → `DEGRADED_NOTICE` (`:109`, "_Interpretation pending — …_"); parsed
but empty → "_No ranked hypotheses produced._" (`:158`); otherwise one `- **({confidence})** {statement}` entry per
hypothesis, in L4Output order, with an optional `\n  - {justification}` (`:160-171`). Rank is position (the prompt's
CONVENTIONS: "Hypotheses ranked highest-confidence-first", `prompt.rs:101`). "The report rendered hypotheses" must be
read as "≥1 ranked entry", never "section present".

**P-D · The success-path row lands `ManualCheck`, not `KnownResidual`.** A declare-only scenario whose read-back is
non-degraded takes `state_for(…, ManualCheck)` (`execute.rs:248-254`) — measured by b1. `KnownResidual` arises only
from a degraded report or an emptied active set (`route_read_back`, `:234-240`). The posture's "a null verdict and a
known-residual state" (§Disposition) holds for the failure paths only; the extracts that assumed `[RESIDUAL]` for the
success row (design, layouts) inherited it.

**P-E · The "~110 s real-model formation" figure is not a real-model measurement.** Its only witness is
`crates/conductor-run/tests/lifecycle_live.rs:20` ("INCIDENT FORMATION TOOK ~110s … L3's digest cadence with L4 behind
it"), as first committed at `f1584b1` — a leg whose own firing form sets `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC=true`
(`:14`), recorded "deterministic L4" in `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-08-31-p-075-assert-round/report.md:161`. The
re-attribution is `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-09-06-operator-gated-live-suite/plan.md:102` ("With the real model,
formation took ~110s (`lifecycle_live.rs` header)"), which propagated to `verification-harness.md:60` (c), the
posture, `architecture.md`'s registry row and this entry's CONTEXT. **No real-model formation figure exists in
Conductor's record.** The first drive MEASURES it; "confirm" is not available. The non-tier disposition still stands,
on the ground that survives: real-model timing is unmeasured and non-deterministic, so no tier can be declared
honestly before a drive.

**P-F · The grading as specified needs a capture channel that does not exist.** `extract.rs:102` does push the report
markdown into `Observation.text` (the claim's cited half holds), but `Observation` is in memory only: no envelope field
carries it, the journal holds the envelope, and the only read-back self-obs line logs key NAMES (`extract.rs:99`). A
harvest-tier grade "over the leg's verbatim captures" has nothing verbatim to read. Separately, `Contains` over the
composed text cannot express rank: the text unions list fields and EVERY active incident's report (`:90-103`), so the
comparison must be scoped to the first `- **(` entry of the attributed incident's `## Hypotheses` section.

**P-G · What the model can "identify" is bounded by the digest.** The L4 prompt (`prompt.rs:182-256`) embeds the L3
digest text `render_payload` builds (`assembler.rs:608-690`): `WINDOW`, `PROJECT`, `OVERALL`, `SERVICES` rows
(`{service} {rate}/s | {error}% | {p99}ms`), `ATTENTION CUES` (`[{tier}] {cue_kind} — {cue_kind} scope_id={service}`,
kinds `retry_storm` · `error_rate_spike` · `latency_regression` · `service_went_silent` · `restart_event`,
`:555-564`), corpus matches, plus the citable fingerprint ids. Exception type and message text never reach it (the
digest is contracted to carry no raw attribute payloads, `contract.rs:548-556`). So a "known root cause" is
expressible only as WHICH service and WHAT anomaly kind. Pulse's own P-033 verification line: "verify highest-ranked
hypothesis correctly identifies cause **within reasonable interpretation of model output**"
(`pulse-capability-spec.md:448`); its one committed real-model spike echoed exactly those two facets
("service-a is experiencing latency issues." for a `latency-regression: service-a` digest — `experiments/l4_output.json`).
Hypothesis count depends on the host's tier: `GpuFallback`/`CpuFallback` → the fallback prompt, EXACTLY ONE
hypothesis (`model_router.rs:36`, `prompt.rs:118-136`); primary → up to three.

**P-H · The canary is itself a real-model gate.** Under the posture the preflight canary's incident forms only if the
real model returns `surface` with severity ≠ `none` (`inference_runtime.rs` `create_incident_from_l4_output` returns
early on `Dismiss` / `None`), and within the poll budget. A dismissed canary is `Blocked: no incident opened after
the canary storm` — a model-dependent Blocked BEFORE the scenario emits. The poll floor (90 s) is raisable only
upward, through `CONDUCTOR_PREFLIGHT_TIMEOUT` (`agent-run.sh:38-49`); with formation unmeasured, the first drive's
budget is generous by construction.

- **Capture/grade split** (`live_suite.rs:1-44`, `live_suite_harvest.rs:1-23`): a `live-pulse`-gated target PRINTS what
  the leg produced; a default-suite harvest pins the frozen lines as LITERALS and grades them; no harvest reads a path.

- **Evaluator pure, observation at the caller** (core `preconditions.rs:1-16`, `run_contract.rs:9-18`; run
  `preconditions.rs:27-45`) — both branches testable without env mutation (testing.md 2026-08-10).
- **Freshness carrier** (`canary.rs:204-227`): attribute by an emission stamp taken just before the counted storm.

- **Reading Pulse's own log** (`storm_harvest.rs:9-15`): `{data_dir}/logs/agent-latest.jsonl.<date>`, sliced by pre-leg
  line count (`verification-harness.md:55` (a) — never assume 0).
- **Declare-only state routing** (`execute.rs:234-254`).

- **One truthiness rule**: `flag_declared` is the workspace's single definition (`preconditions.rs:41-53`); any inverse must
  be defined from it, never re-implemented (so the two cannot drift).
- **Exact-set pins, both directions** (`drift.rs:40-63`, `preconditions.rs:435-447`, the audit ledger).
- **Live-leg doc header carries firing + stop form** (`live_suite.rs:13-28`, `lifecycle_live.rs:7-16`).
- **Harvest literals are host-path-free**; drive-letter checks word-anchored (testing.md 2026-09-03).
- **Committed artifacts read from tests via `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`** (testing.md 2026-09-06; `live_suite.rs:58-64`).

- **Expect atoms from printed output**: the CLI verdict line prints lamp prefix + SCENARIO NAME, never the P-ID
  (`verification-harness.md:64`) — success `[MANUAL] <scenario>`, degraded `[RESIDUAL] <scenario>`, gate
  `[BLOCKED] <scenario>`.
