body: - (tests) The PREREQ is closed. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run --unit` both exit 0, run in full with no `defer`, each read from its bare exit, and the nextest summary is recorded (per test-plan §9 Pipeline structure; §3 `run`).

- (a11y) The coverage row's accessible name carries its P-ID and its status. This is asserted by the routine arm's computed-name check in `CONDUCTOR_A11Y_STRICT=1 bash scripts/agent-run.sh run --e2e` (the first row; P-019 → `Blocked`). The roving contract is unchanged: one tab stop, the current row with `tabindex="0"` + `aria-current="true"`, and no `tabindex > 0` (per a11y-plan §4 Coverage matrix row; §5 idle-with-report).

- (a11y) The DOM exposes exactly one `h1` (the phase line), one `main` and one `contentinfo`. The same `--e2e` run asserts this (per a11y-plan §4 landmark inventory and its note, `a11y-plan.md:320`, `:323`, `:548`).

- (design / layouts) The footer strip is one line, `conductor · seed · phase` plus the lamp-labelled roll-up. It uses tokens only (no shadow, no transition, no raw hex/px/ms), is not focusable and is not a live region. The coverage row keeps its four cells, P-ID first, with the `--border-emphasis` current edge (per layout-templates §Component — Footer (status strip), §Component — Primary content block 1; design-system §Component Patterns 3/4/7, §Depth Strategy, §Motion).

- (a11y / tests) `CONDUCTOR_A11Y_STRICT=1 bash scripts/agent-run.sh run --e2e` prints `[a11y] verdict asserted — 0 failed` with the expected-skip set `(expected 2)`, axe is clean under `wcag2a`/`wcag2aa`/`wcag21aa`, and `cd crates/conductor-tauri/ui && npm run a11y:ownership` reads its unchanged summary (per a11y-plan §9, §10, §11 Strategy; test-plan §3 `run`).

- (a11y) The regrade grades all 51 rows: `rows 51 not-run-here 0`, every row carrying its input path, all three subjects recorded after the chunk base on one configuration (runtime × driver × NVDA × Windows build × input path stated in the record), and the operator review transcribed (per a11y-plan §3 Screen reader test pattern; test-plan §1 Untestable zones, §6 desktop-webview row).

- (a11y) The two routed reds close. The focus-row count reads `focus-nonexpected 0` (predicted 2 → 0), and S0-09 / E0-05 grade `announced-as-expected` with `P-001` heard (per a11y-plan §4, §11 Screen Reader).

- (a11y) Every SR row conveys its required content: the probe prints `not-expected none`, with the two subject-absent rows graded by their reasons (per a11y-plan §3; the operator review never accepts a row whose content is absent).

- (a11y) Each of the 18 findings is dispositioned in `nvda-pass-spec.md`'s findings ledger as product fix / re-token / re-action, with a reason citing the rendered DOM (the take-up directive; per a11y-plan §3 Pass spec format).

- (security) No boundary moves. `send-keys.ps1`, `activate-window.ps1` and `wdio.conf.ts` are byte-unchanged against `d7da5d0`. The SR spec keeps exactly two `spawnSync(` sites and no `-Command`. The delta guard prints nothing. No `4444`/`4445` listener or leg process survives (per security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Code Patterns, rule (b) EIGHT forms; §Threat Model Summary → Attack surface; arch §Cross-cutting Patterns → Trust boundary).

- (security / obs) The regraded record passes the closed-set probe (0 violations) and host-path hygiene (0), and every backend sink shows 0 unlogged panics (per security-plan §Input Validation, the speech-log ingest row; §Security Anti-Patterns → Logging; obs-plan §9, §11 PII Scrubbing).
- (obs) The webview delta adds no OTel/OTLP import or egress (per obs-plan §2 desktop-webview row; §11 Universal).

- (ci) The operator's pre-CI commit reads `verdict: green` through `ci.py conclusion --sha HEAD --wait 1200`, and the report names the run id (per test-plan §9; arch §Established Decisions → [CI/CD]).
- No verification-matrix capability is claimed. The pool reads `unclaimed 0 of 11` (`matrix.py show --unclaimed`, P4), and this chunk advances no pooled acceptance.

- Research files inspected: see research.md §Files inspected. Graph: `CoverageMatrix @ App.tsx:366, Gallery.tsx:206`; `Titlebar @ App.tsx:279`; `StatusLamp @ CoverageMatrix.tsx:140, RunReport.tsx:77`; `rowsFor @ screen-reader.e2e.ts:35, parse-nvda-log.ts:382` (ts plane, one `refs` query, 23 rows).

- Leaned per artifact (decisive leans, not questions):
  - **Ship the `contentinfo` strip rather than record a reason for none.** a11y-plan `:548` is a MUST ban. The anatomy is fully buildable from held state (`RunRecord.seed`, `lamp.ts:49`). The playbook's routine pattern covers "a chunk SHIPS the fix that a spec master's own body already names as route-owned-not-shipped".
  - **Drive T-01 as a second run in the same live session** (research.md §Patterns: no new process, port or spawn form, so no escalation).
  - **Name the row with `aria-labelledby` over its own four cells** (a11y-plan §11 ARIA; layouts reading order P-ID first).
  - **The phase line is the `h1`** (a11y-plan `:323` names it).

- Playbook `verdict: escalate` patterns read (`.andromeda/playbook.md:98`, `:110`, `:125`): no option this plan ships matches one. There is no boundary widening, no arch decision reversal, and no cli-row obs attribution.
- A composed `aria-label` on `tr.cov__row` — rejected: `aria-label` is reserved for icon-only controls, and the visible text already names the row (a11y-plan §11 ARIA; `rules/a11y.md`).
- Re-roling the matrix as `grid`/`treegrid` to force row names — rejected: it changes a11y-plan §4's table semantics and the §5 keyboard contract the routine arm owns.
- Recording "no `contentinfo`" with a reason — rejected: a11y-plan `:548` is a MUST ban, and the strip is buildable now.
- A new Tauri command or `Channel` for the seed or the roll-up — rejected: `RunRecord` already carries `seed`, and arch §Conventions → Interface surfaces fixes the command set.

- Widening `send-keys.ps1` (ArrowUp, Escape, NVDA+Space, Shift+h) to reach a row backwards — rejected: that is a NINTH rule (b) crossing needing the founder's live word. The closed five-key set reaches every row from a forward start position (step 7).
- A second NVDA session, second app launch or second driver for T-01 — rejected: a second run inside the same session reaches Done with no new process.
- Adding SR rows (for the h1, the footer or the second run) — rejected: the row set stays at 51, and changed rows are re-tokened in place with their reasons.

- Fixed key counts for the browse reaches — rejected in favour of bounded `browseUntil` loops keyed on the row's own token: NVDA's line granularity is not derivable from the DOM alone, and a cap still turns a miss into a graded finding.
- Grading a row by a physical keyboard, a manual arm or an injected browse key — banned (arm K retired by founder ruling; a11y-plan §3; test-plan §1).
- Editing the prior chunk's evidence — banned: the regrade writes its own record.

- **Slot protocol (take-up directive).** Every NVDA or window run is the operator's quiet-desktop slot. That covers the strict `--e2e` (~12 min with the release build) and the three `sr*` legs (~2 / ~1.5 / ~8 min). STOP and ask before each, stating the length. The live leg also needs the `:4317` grant. title: Per-row DOM confirmation (the take-up directive: product fix vs re-token, reason recorded)

data.head: ## Per-row DOM confirmation (the take-up directive: product fix vs re-token, reason recorded)

body: The mode evidence comes from the record's `heard` fields:

- **The focused coverage row is in focus mode.** E0-09 heard "row current" twice. S0-15's ArrowDown heard "row current". That is the app's roving ArrowDown moving focus (`CoverageMatrix.tsx:64-82`), not a virtual-cursor line.

- **A focused button or the report scroll div is in browse mode.** S3-06's ArrowDown from Start read the Stop line; S3-07 then read the hint line. E0-07/E0-08's ArrowDown from `div.report__scroll` walked into the report table cell by cell.

- [hypothesis] NVDA enters focus mode when focus lands on the focusable `tr`, and browse mode on a button or the scroll div. This is consistent with every heard line in the record; it is not measured directly.
| row | DOM carries the required content? | heard / why silent | disposition |
| E0-05, S0-09 | P-ID in `td.cov__pid`, but the row has NO author name (`CoverageMatrix.tsx:113-123`) | "row current" — an empty name | **product fix**: the row's accessible name carries its P-ID |

| E0-09 | yes (P-019 row, Blocked label) | one ArrowDown moves the roving focus to row index 1 (P-002), never index 18 | **product fix + re-token**: the name fix, plus an action that reaches P-019 (ArrowDown until P-019 is current) |
| S3-07 | yes (P-025 row + its lamp label) | the ArrowDown from Start read the hint line (browse mode) | **re-token**: reach the P-025 row (after the name fix, through the focused row) |

| S0-15 | yes (`span.cov__unrun` "Not yet run", `:142`) | "row current" — focus moved to row index 1 with an empty name | **product fix + re-token**: the row name carries its status, and the row is re-classed as the focus move it is |

| E0-07 | yes (`header.report__summary` "3 scenarios · run lamps-fixture", `RunReport.tsx:41-44`) | the virtual cursor started at the scroll div AFTER the header and moved forward into the table | **re-token**: reach the header by navigation from before it |
| E0-08 | yes ("Blocked" as text, `StatusLamp.tsx:17`) | one ArrowDown reached only "column 2 Scenario"; the Blocked cell is further on | **re-token**: continue until the Blocked cell |
| S3-06 | yes ("Manual" label text) | the ArrowDown from Start read the Stop line | **re-token**: reach the report's status cells |

| S0-13 | the three `h2` are present; NO `h1` (App.tsx, Titlebar.tsx) | `h` sent from the focused coverage row, which is in focus mode, so it goes to the app (`:76-77` ignores it) | **product fix** (an h1 per a11y-plan `:323`) **+ re-token** (send `h` from a browse-mode position, and re-derive the token) |
| S0-14 | banner + main present; NO `contentinfo` | as S0-13 (`d`) | **product fix or recorded reason** (a11y-plan `:548` requires it — a P4 fork) **+ re-token** |

| E0-01, S0-08, S0-10, S0-11, S0-12, S1-02, S2-06 | yes — each row's own DOM assertion passed on the 2026-09-30 leg (`screen-reader.e2e.ts:422`, `:425`, `:486`, `:496`, `:513`, `:539`, `:634`) | no OS key in the row's window (`parse-nvda-log.ts:304-305`) | **re-action**: OS-path browse keys inside each row's window. No product change is planned. [hypothesis] S0-12's `aria-label` sits on a role-less `span` (`Titlebar.tsx:39-47`), which ARIA 1.2 does not name, so browse mode may read the digits. The regrade measures this; any product change waits on it. |

| T-01 | yes (the phase line "Conductor · idle") | never driven: the live subject stops at aborted | **re-action**: a second, un-stopped run in the SAME live session after S3 (Start again, Proceed through both holds, Done). No new process or spawn form (see Patterns). |

- **Row grading spans the whole window** (`parse-nvda-log.ts:299-318`): the tokens are matched anywhere in the window's heard text. So a browse row may send several OS keys in one window, and its record's `input` stays `os`.

- **The leg reads the speech log while it runs** (`screen-reader.e2e.ts:48-54`, `:118-125`). A bounded "send ArrowDown until the row's token appears in the log since the stamp, cap N" loop keys on a signal and uses no sleep (test-plan §11 E2E ban scoped to in-test sync). The cap turns a miss into a graded finding.
- **Browse keys never go through the combobox** (`:402-407`). `h`, `d` and ArrowDown are already in the closed set (`send-keys.ps1:12`), so no key is added.

- **A second run inside one live session:** after S3-05 the app is idle-able and Start is enabled again (S3-02). The app's own sidecar spawn is rule (a), unchanged. No rule (b) form is added: `osKey` and `injectKeys` are the existing forms.

- **Routine and driven arms key on classes:** `cov__row`, `cov__pid` and `titlebar__label` (`accessibility.e2e.ts:61-64`, `:324`; `operator-hold.e2e.ts:79-97`). A row name or a heading tag change moves no selector. The Tab order is unchanged, because a heading and a footer are not focusable.

- **Name from the visible text, never a composed `aria-label`:** `aria-label` is reserved for icon-only controls (a11y-plan §11 ARIA; `rules/a11y.md` Semantic HTML first). `aria-labelledby` pointing at the row's own cells names the row from text that is already rendered.
- **The one lamp truth:** status text comes from `LAMP_META` through `StatusLamp` (`frontend.md` 2026-06-26). The row name references that cell, and never re-spells a label.
- **Tokens by name** on any new visible node (`design-system` §Tokens; `Titlebar.css` binds `var(--text-secondary)`).
- **The `sr*` suites never rebuild** (`verification-harness.md:62`): an app change needs a `--e2e` run before any `sr*` regrade reads it.
- **`nvda-pass.json` is cumulative per subject** (`:63`): the regrade record is complete only when all three subjects ran after the app change, each with its own `recorded_at`.

- **Live `sr` firing form** (`:59`, `:61`): `CONDUCTOR_NVDA`, `CONDUCTOR_MSEDGEDRIVER`, `CONDUCTOR_SCENARIOS_DIR=runs/sr-leg/scenarios`, the three `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_*`, and the Pulse release dir on `PATH`. It needs a quiet desktop (`:59` extended 2026-09-30), and it ends with a census naming who stops each survivor (`:58`).
- **A harness defect gets one re-fire on a new slot; a key-path fix is proven by a short probe first** (`:71`).

- `conductor-0.3.0/chunks/2026-09-30-the-screen-reader-content-findings-fixed/evidence/nvda-pass.json` — the regrade record, copied from `runs/sr-leg/` after the three subjects ran on the changed bundle, with the operator review transcribed
- `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/src/components/Footer.tsx` — only if P4 takes the ship-a-footer branch: the `contentinfo` status strip
- `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/src/components/Footer.css` — only if P4 takes the ship-a-footer branch: its token-bound styles
- `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/src/components/CoverageMatrix.tsx` — the row's accessible name through `aria-labelledby` over its own P-ID and Status cells (per-row cell ids)
- `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/src/components/Titlebar.tsx` — the phase line becomes the single `h1` (a11y-plan `:323`)
- `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/src/components/Titlebar.css` — the `h1` user-agent margin and size reset, so the visible anatomy does not move
- `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/src/App.tsx` — mounts the footer (ship branch only; untouched on the recorded-reason branch)
- `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/test/a11y/screen-reader/rows.ts` — re-tokened rows: E0-07, E0-08, E0-09, S0-13, S0-14, S0-15, S3-06, S3-07, and T-01's `notRun` removed
- `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/test/a11y/screen-reader.e2e.ts` — the OS-path browse actions for the 7 rows, the reaching actions for the re-tokened rows, and T-01's second run
- `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/test/a11y/screen-reader/nvda-pass-spec.md` — the mirror of every changed row, and the findings ledger
- `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/test/a11y/accessibility.e2e.ts` — routine-arm DOM assertions for the row name, the single h1 and the landmark set (the CI-gated baseline beside the supplemental SR pass)

- `contentinfo`: ship a footer strip, or record a reason for none? The master requires it (a11y-plan `:548`). Layouts' footer anatomy names `seed <n>`, and no existing command carries the seed (arch forbids a new command). So the ship branch cannot build the full anatomy, and each branch owes a different master amendment. → blocks: plan-decision (P4)

- Does "the next regrade grades all 51 rows" require T-01 to be HEARD, or does a graded finding satisfy it? Research shows T-01 is drivable with no new crossing, which leans towards heard. → blocks: plan-decision (P4)
- `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/src/srOnly.ts` · in-intent · serves step 9 · self
- `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/test/a11y/operator-hold.e2e.ts` · companion · serves crates/conductor-tauri/ui/src/components/Titlebar.tsx · self

The correction is anchored only on the stimulus pairs (@key vs NVDA Input), never on graded content." — the operator (overseer), 2026-09-30

data.head: ## Operator directives and founder rulings at take-up (2026-09-30)

body: - **Order: the PREREQ comes first.** The Rust gate deferral is closed before any product or harness work (below).
- **Founder ruling: `/andromeda-evolve-diagnose` waits.** The new-session nudge for Epoch 4 stays unacted.

- **Founder ruling: arm K is retired.** It is not run, not planned and not simulated in this chunk. The record reads
  "not run — founder ruling, cause already isolated by C1" (a11y-plan §3).

- **Founder ruling: the U35 upgrade door is not this chunk.** `upgrade.py detect` reads U35 `behind`, awaiting a
  0-pending wrap door. This chunk neither opens nor closes it.

- **Confirm each row against the rendered DOM before planning a change.** For every row below, research reads the
  rendered DOM node the row names. It then records a disposition: **product fix** (the DOM does not carry the content
  the row requires) or **re-token** (the DOM carries it, and the row's token, node or action is what is wrong). The
  reason is recorded either way.

- **Every NVDA or window run is the operator's quiet-desktop slot.** Research and implement alike STOP and ask before
  any NVDA launch or any run that raises a window, and state the run's expected LENGTH. Nothing starts unasked.
- **A live `sr` run also needs the operator's `:4317` grant.** Ask for it alongside the slot, with its length.

- **Any new crossing is a P4 escalation for the founder's live word.** This covers a ninth harness-spawn form, a new
  listener, or any other boundary widening (security-plan; `rules/security.md` rule (b) holds EIGHT forms). A delegate
  cannot ratify it (`rules/security.md` Session Additions 2026-09-29).

- `PREREQ: close rust gate deferral (deferred since 2026-09-30-the-sr-pass-regrades-on-the-os-input-path)`.
  At that chunk's wrap (its `report.md` §Gates), the **clippy** `defer` stood: zero Rust delta, and clippy reads Rust
  source only. The **unit** `defer` was voided at the same wrap: `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run --unit` ran in full
  (exit 0, `1136 tests run: 1136 passed, 0 skipped`).

- Closing it here: run `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run
  --unit` in full against this chunk's tree, and record both verdicts. "Close" means both gates run in full, each as
  its own command (test-plan §9 keeps Lint out of `--unit`; tests extract). The Rust delta is zero: research's
  modify-set is `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/**` plus the chunk's evidence only. So a new deferral must not be
  minted, and the plan lists both gates unconditionally.

Record: `conductor-0.3.0/chunks/2026-09-30-the-sr-pass-regrades-on-the-os-input-path/evidence/nvda-pass.json`. The
operator review is transcribed: 31 accepted as heard, 18 findings, 2 accepted with reason (E0-10, S1-05,
subject-absent). Measured on WebView2 154.0.4258.37 × NVDA 2026.2 × Windows 26200.9457 × the OS input path. The 18
findings split into five groups:

1. **The P-ID is missing from what is heard** (E0-05, S0-09, E0-09, S3-07).
   - E0-05 and S0-09: focus rows, `Tab` on the OS path, node `tr[tabindex=0][aria-current=true]` in

     for E0-05 and S0-09: `tr.cov__row` carries no author name (`CoverageMatrix.tsx:113-123`), and NVDA heard an

     confirmation.]

2. **The report and matrix cells convey their status and fixture values** (E0-07, E0-08, S0-15, S3-06). Each is a
   browse row driven by ArrowDown on the OS path.
   - E0-07: `lamps-fixture` missing; heard "table with 4 rows and 6 columns row 1 column 1 P-ID".
   - E0-08: `Blocked` missing; heard "column 2 Scenario".
   - S0-15: `Not yet run` missing; heard "row current".

   - S0-14: banner, main and two regions; `contentinfo` is absent.
   - [premise-corrected: both halves hold, for different reasons. The product facts are confirmed in the DOM: three

     focused coverage row, and the record shows that row is in focus mode (hypothesis, consistent with every heard
     line), so the keys went to the app, which ignores them (`CoverageMatrix.tsx:76-77`). These rows need the product
     fix AND their keys sent from a browse-mode position, with the tokens re-derived.]

4. **The 7 browse `not-run-here` rows are driven with OS-path browse keys in their windows** (E0-01, S0-08, S0-10,
   S0-11, S0-12, S1-02, S2-06). Each was `arm: operator`, `input: none`: no browse key went through the OS input path
   in the row's window. This is a leg coverage gap, not a product defect: each row's own DOM assertion passed on the
   2026-09-30 leg (research.md). `send-keys.ps1`'s closed `-Key` set admits `h`, `d` and ArrowDown
   (`send-keys.ps1:12`), so driving these rows needs no new key and no new spawn form.

5. **T-01 is a live-class row, not run by design.** The live subject stops at `aborted` (the aborted state needs a
   Stop), so the un-stopped run's "Conductor · idle" on the Done stage is never reached. It needs a second, un-stopped
   live session, not a browse key. That session needs the operator's quiet-desktop slot and `:4317` grant.
   [premise-corrected: T-01 does not need a second SESSION. It needs a second, un-stopped RUN in the same live
   session: after S3 settles, Start is enabled again (S3-02), and a run driven through both holds reaches Done. That
   uses the existing `osKey`/`injectKeys` forms and the app's own rule (a) sidecar spawn, so there is no new process,
   port or spawn form, and no escalation. It lengthens the live leg by one more run, which the slot request states.]

- **Hypothesis, kept as stated:** "these are product a11y defects and the product fix is the remedy, not the tokens;
  the entry's research confirms each row against the rendered DOM before it plans a change, and a row whose token is
  wrong rather than the product is re-tokened with the reason recorded." [premise-corrected: partly true. The
  product defects are the coverage row's missing name (E0-05, S0-09, and through it S0-15 and E0-09), the missing
  `h1` (S0-13) and the missing `contentinfo` (S0-14). E0-07, E0-08, S3-06 and S3-07 carry their content in the DOM
  and are re-tokens of the action. The seven browse rows and T-01 are leg coverage gaps. Per-row table:
  research.md.]

- **Done means the next regrade grades all 51 rows.** Resolved at P4: `rows 51 not-run-here 0`, every row carrying its
  input path, every row except the two subject-absent ones `announced-as-expected`, and the two routed reds
  (focus-row count 2 → bar 0; S0-09/E0-05) closed. T-01 is HEARD, driven by a second un-stopped run in the same live
  session (no crossing — research.md §Patterns), so no accepted-with-reason grade stands in for it (plan.md
  §Acceptance Criteria).

- In: the React webview's accessible structure (row names, status cells, heading and landmark structure), the `sr*`
  legs' row table and key actions (the spec at `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/test/a11y/screen-reader/`), the regrade
  record, and the PREREQ gates.

- Out: arm K (retired), the U35 door, evolve-diagnose, Pulse's own UI, and any change to `send-keys.ps1`'s closed key
  set that adds a spawn form without the founder's word.

- The routine `--e2e` arm, the axe/contrast `a11y` job and every existing test must stay green. [premise-corrected:
  the routine and driven arms key coverage rows and the phase line on CLASSES (`cov__row`, `cov__pid`,
  `titlebar__label` — `accessibility.e2e.ts:61-64,324`; `operator-hold.e2e.ts:79-97`), so a row name or a heading tag
  moves no selector. A heading and a footer are not focusable, so the Tab order is unchanged.]
- No new dependency is expected.

- `d7da5d0`: **verdict not yet available** — run CI#36744501243 (push), `in progress`; checks 3/3; the oldest running
  check was "A11y gate (routine arm · axe · contrast · violation JSON)" at 164 s. Read 2026-09-30 at phase Setup
  (`.andromeda/runs/2026-09-30T16-31-26-phase/`). No red to disposition at take-up. This run reads the previous
  chunk's wrap commit, and implement re-reads it before the pre-CI commit.

title: Plan — 2026-09-30-the-screen-reader-pass-grades-again-on-this-host: "The screen-reader pass grades again on this host"

data.head: # Plan — 2026-09-30-the-screen-reader-pass-grades-again-on-this-host: "The screen-reader pass grades again on this host"

body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-09-30-the-screen-reader-pass-grades-again-on-this-host · **Version:** conductor-0.3.0 · **Generated:** 2026-09-30T12:20Z

- **Chunk base (W182):** `2c9b37d` (`2c9b37d48599ea28d9902deda2e807d76fa4fccf`), HEAD at take-up. Every diff-shaped
  probe names it, because the operator pre-CI commit moves HEAD before the wrap.

- **Matrix:** no capability claimed. The pool reads `unclaimed 0 of 11` (`matrix.py show --unclaimed`); `v3-03` is
  already verified and is not reopened.

Find why NVDA on this host hears Conductor's webview focus only in its first burst and then nothing, and name that
cause from a discriminating measurement, not from a fitting story. Then regrade the silent focus rows on a
configuration the record names. Research ruled the app, the harness path, `tauri`/`wry` and NVDA's own version and
config out by diff over `06db2f9..2c9b37d` (research.md §Variable ledger). What remains is the host:
- the WebView2 runtime/driver pair, 152.0.4191.66 → 154.0.4258.37;
- two Windows cumulative updates;
- the desktop;
- how NVDA's object model meets the new runtime.

Per a11y-plan §3 *Screen reader test pattern*, test-plan §6 (desktop-webview row, third family) and §9 *Matrix builds*,
the cause claim is single-variable against a control, and every verdict is stated with its configuration.
The control, ruled at P4 (overseer, founder-delegated), is **object-model first**:
- an `sr-error` reproduction at NVDA defaults;
- then `sr-empty` with ONE change, `[UIA] allowInChromium = 2` in the leg's own `nvda.ini`.

That value FORCES NVDA onto its UIA path, where the default resolves to the in-process IA2 buffer on both dates
(research.md §Controls, the teardown lines). NVDA's argv, the `CONDUCTOR_NVDA` registration, every spawn form and every
boundary stay unchanged.

**Branch A (heard):** the key becomes the leg's stated AT posture, and all three subjects are regraded under it. The
default-setting silence is recorded as a finding that states the USER consequence. The product-side lever is named and
never built.

**Branch B (silent):** the key is restored byte-identical, and the chunk records the measurement and stops. A runtime
control would need its own ratification, so the chunk reports and never widens.

0. **Operator slots, before everything.** Every NVDA run (`npm run a11y:sr-error`, `a11y:sr-empty`, `a11y:sr`) is a
   quiet-desktop OPERATOR SLOT: /implement STOPS and asks before firing each one, and fires only on the operator's word
   (take-up directive). pulse-builder shares this desktop, and verification-harness.md `:59` (as extended 2026-09-30)
   says its terminal takes the foreground. The live `sr` run also needs the `:4317` slot. Take a `Win32_Process`
   census with parentage before and after every leg (host-win32.md 2026-09-17; the census families are `nvda`,
   `msedgedriver`, `conductor-tauri`, `tauri-driver`, `node`, `msedgewebview2`, `pulse-app`, `andromeda-pulse-mcp`).
   Stop everything this session starts (memory: stop-everything-you-start).

1. **Re-read the configuration** (no slot). Fire the driver/runtime coherence entry. Re-list the machine-wide Evergreen
   runtime directories and read the OS build with the read-only probe form research used (registry `pv`, the
   `CurrentBuild`.`UBR` pair). Write the first rows of the configuration table into `evidence/cause-control.md`:
   runtime, driver, NVDA version (read from the next leg's log), OS build, `allowInChromium` value and bundle commit.
   Name registry keys in the colon-free `reg.exe` form, and describe host paths in words (host-win32.md 2026-09-11).

2. **Fresh bundle** (no slot). Fire `CONDUCTOR_A11Y_STRICT=1 bash scripts/agent-run.sh run --e2e`. It builds the release
   binary and `ui/dist` at the chunk base, which the `sr*` suites never rebuild (verification-harness.md `:62`), and it
   re-proves the routine arm green.

3. **K-reproduce (slot 1): `sr-error` at NVDA defaults.** Check `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/test/a11y/screen-reader/nvda-config/nvda.ini`
   against the base first: `git diff --quiet 2c9b37d -- <that file>` must exit 0. Then fire the `sr-error` entry.
   Snapshot `runs/sr-leg/nvda-pass.json` to `evidence/nvda-pass.defaults.json` (it is cumulative per subject,
   verification-harness.md `:63`, so the snapshot is what keeps this arm). In `cause-control.md` record:
   - R0-02 / R0-03 / R0-04 outcomes (heard on 2026-09-07 at 152.0.4191.66);
   - the silence SHAPE read from `runs/sr-leg/nvda-speech.error.log`: the activation burst heard, then the per-Tab rows
     heard or not, each utterance's time against `actions.error.jsonl`. Quote utterances, never host paths.

4. **K-object-model (slot 2): `sr-empty` with `[UIA] allowInChromium = 2`.** Add a `[UIA]` section to the leg's
   `nvda.ini` holding exactly `allowInChromium = 2`, with a comment in the file's own style giving the measured reason
   (the value set from NVDA's `configSpec.py`, `2` = yes; research.md §Platform issues). Change nothing else: that
   file's diff against `2c9b37d` is that section alone. Fire the `sr-empty` entry. Read the new log for the same
   shape. **Witness that NVDA took the key.** No line in this tree decides whether NVDA applied it; that is the
   dependency's own semantics. So record, with its reading, BOTH:
   - (a) the session's `runs/sr-leg/nvda-speech.empty.log` carries no configuration-error or validation line for
     `[UIA]`;
   - (b) the profile NVDA saved on exit ("Base configuration saved", `runs/sr-leg/nvda-config/nvda.ini`) still holds
     `allowInChromium = 2`.
   A key NVDA rejected or reset makes the arm VOID, not Branch B: stop and report the void arm, and never read it as
   a measurement. Record E0-02..E0-06 outcomes in `cause-control.md` against the three 2026-09-30 silent `sr-empty` runs
   (10:46Z, the 10:52Z base-bundle control and 11:33Z), which are the default arm on the same host configuration.

5. **Decide the branch** only once step 4's witness holds (else the arm is void, as step 4 says). Use one predicate,
   written into `cause-control.md` with its reading: under `= 2`, are E0-02,
   E0-03 and E0-04 all `announced-as-expected`? These are the Minimize / Close / Start rows that 09-07 heard as
   R0-02..04 and 09-30 lost as E0-02..04.
   - **YES → Branch A.** Keep the `nvda.ini` section.
   - **NO or mixed → Branch B.** Restore `nvda.ini` byte-identical to the base (`git diff --quiet 2c9b37d -- <file>`
     exits 0), finish step 8 with the finding, run step 9, and stop. No regrade legs fire. The regrade entries in the
     fence then read red, and the report records why (the forecast in §Implementation notes).
6. **Branch A regrade, `sr-error` (slot 3)** under `= 2`. It refreshes the error subject on the same configuration.

7. **Branch A regrade, live `sr` (slot 4, the `:4317` slot).** The operator has `pulse-app` up under the deterministic
   posture with its data dir equal to `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR`. Fire the non-priming `conductor preconditions`
   entry, then allow a ≥150 s quiet window after any canary (verification-harness.md `:53`, `:60`). Then fire the live
   `sr` entry in its firing form (`CONDUCTOR_SCENARIOS_DIR`, the sidecar `PATH`; `:59`, `:61`). The `sr-empty` subject
   from step 4 is the regrade's empty subject; it is not re-run. Copy `runs/sr-leg/nvda-pass.json` to
   `evidence/nvda-pass.json`: all three subjects on one configuration, all recorded after the chunk base.

9. **Hygiene and teardown.** Fire the evidence gates (host paths, closed sets, the diff guard), then the final census.
   Nothing this session started may be left running. `pulse-app` is the operator's to stop, unless the session
   launched it on the operator's word, in which case the session stops it.

- `conductor-0.3.0/chunks/2026-09-30-the-screen-reader-pass-grades-again-on-this-host/evidence/cause-control.md` — the controls, the configuration table, the verdict, the user-consequence finding, the product lever named, the census tables
- `conductor-0.3.0/chunks/2026-09-30-the-screen-reader-pass-grades-again-on-this-host/evidence/nvda-pass.defaults.json` — the K-reproduce snapshot (the error subject at NVDA defaults)

- `conductor-0.3.0/chunks/2026-09-30-the-screen-reader-pass-grades-again-on-this-host/evidence/nvda-pass.json` — Branch A: the regrade record (all three subjects under `= 2`); Branch B: the record as the `= 2` arm left it

- `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/test/a11y/screen-reader/nvda-config/nvda.ini` — Branch A keeps a `[UIA]` section with `allowInChromium = 2` and its reason comment; Branch B restores it byte-identical to `2c9b37d`

The Rust gates are listed and deferred. The chunk's delta is the leg's `nvda.ini` plus chunk evidence, with zero
Rust source, and no committed file a Rust test reads changes. The frontend-meaningful half is the strict `--e2e` routine
arm, which runs.

There is no smoke entry and no `status` read: no scenario leg mints a `run_id` this chunk reads, so a smoke would be
vacuous (verification-harness.md `:49`, 2026-09-11). There are no CI entries: no acceptance needs a CI run, since
nothing CI executes changes.

The three `sr*` entries are OPERATOR SLOTS (step 0). `sr-error` and `sr-empty` carry `leg = 'operator'` so no reader
re-fires an NVDA run outside a granted slot. /implement fires each once, on the operator's word, and records its result
in `evidence/cause-control.md`. The K-reproduce and K-object-model arms (steps 3–4) are fired from these same two
entries at their step's `nvda.ini` state; the fence's reading is the FINAL state's.
The `sr*` entries produce the cumulative working record `runs/sr-leg/nvda-pass.json` (their `artifact`).
- The committed `evidence/nvda-pass.json` is step 7's copy of it (Branch B: step 5's).
- `evidence/nvda-pass.defaults.json` is step 3's snapshot.

- `evidence/cause-control.md` is authored by step 8, by construction.
So the `jq` and hygiene entries read the committed copies, never the working record.

title: The silence's measured shape (the one datum a control must explain)

data.head: ### The silence's measured shape (the one datum a control must explain)

body:
- **09-07, error subject, heard** (`nvda-speech.error.log`, local clock = UTC+2). Activation, then the load-error alert,
  then "Conductor document" / "banner landmark Minimize window button" / "Start button unavailable" during
  `bringToForeground`'s Tab cycle. Then "Landscape" ×2 (22:05:58–22:06:00Z), then one focus utterance per stamped Tab:
  "banner landmark Minimize window button" 22:06:02Z, "Close window button" 22:06:03Z, "Start … unavailable"
  22:06:04Z.

- **09-30, empty subject, silent** (`nvda-speech.empty.log`, the 11:33Z run). The same opening: "Conductor document",
  "Minimize window button", "Start button unavailable Control+Enter" and "Run report … table" at 11:33:22Z, inside the
  activation cycle. Then "Landscape" ×3 (11:33:23–11:33:24Z), then NOTHING until the app closed at 11:34:03Z. The
  stamped Tabs at 11:33:31/35/39/43/47Z (`actions.empty.jsonl`) fall inside that gap.

- **09-30, live subject, silent** (`nvda-speech.live.log`, the 10:47Z run). NVDA opened on the andromeda-pulse WebView2
  window. Its core then FROZE 20.9 s (`:69-210`); the frozen stack sits in
  `UIAHandler\browseMode._get_isAlive` via `api.setFocusObject → treeInterceptorHandler.cleanup` (`:120-136`), so NVDA
  was handling a WebView2 154 document through its **UIA** browse-mode path. That was the pulse-app window's document;
  Conductor's own is on IA2 (K-object-model below). After recovery it heard "Conductor
  document … Coverage rows table … row current", and afterwards only live regions ("Conductor · live",
  "Scenarios completed: N", "HOLD — operator pause", "aborted"). No row-driven focus was heard.

- **So the equality a cause must satisfy:** on 09-30, NVDA hears Conductor's focus events during the activation burst
  and hears none for the WebDriver-driven Tabs that follow. On 09-07 it heard both. The mechanism exists; what stops
  after the first burst is the open question. A cause that explains "never attaches" is refuted by the burst.
  "Landscape" is present on both sides, so it does not discriminate (it is ×2 vs ×3).

data.head: ### Controls reachable without a network fetch (each is an NVDA run, so an OPERATOR SLOT)

body:
- **K-reproduce:** `sr-error` at today's configuration. Its three focus rows R0-02..04 were heard on 09-07 against
  what is effectively the same app. It needs no Pulse and no port, and it also refreshes the error subject the
  final record must carry on one configuration.

- **K-object-model (single variable), CORRECTED at P4.** Conductor's own webview is on NVDA's in-process **IA2**
  path on BOTH dates, so the UIA freeze stack above belongs to the pulse-app window, not to Conductor. The basis is the
  teardown lines, inside a `msedgewebview2.exe` process as the app closed:
  - 09-30 silent empty run: `runs/sr-leg/nvda-speech.empty.log:309-311` reads
    `ERROR - RPC process 16264 (msedgewebview2.exe) (13:34:03.885)` / `Thread 39208, build\x86_64\vbufBase\backend.cpp,
    VBufBackend_t::terminate, 239:` / `Could not execute renderThread_terminate in UI thread`. That is NVDA's
    in-process virtual-buffer backend, the IA2 path. UIA browse mode builds no in-process buffer.
  - 09-07 heard error run: the same pair at `runs/sr-leg/nvda-speech.error.log:351-355`.
  - The empty run had no other WebView2 app open: `census-before.empty.txt` holds two `node.exe` rows, no
    `pulse-app`, and the teardown lands in the second the app closed.
  - NVDA's own selection rule, from `source/UIAHandler/__init__.py` `_isUIAWindowHelper` on the master branch
    (fetched): for `Chrome_RenderWidgetHostHWND` at the default setting, NVDA stays off UIA whenever
    `canUseOlderInProcessApproach and hasAccessToIA2` holds, and is forced off by `AllowUiaInChromium.NO`.
  So the default resolves to IA2 here, and forcing IA2 (`= 3`) would change nothing. The discriminating arm is
  **`[UIA] allowInChromium = 2` ("yes")**. The control changes only that key in the leg's own `nvda.ini`: NVDA's argv
  is unchanged, the `CONDUCTOR_NVDA` registration and spawn form stay, and the file is committed harness data.
  - HEARD under `= 2`: the IA2 focus-event stream is what stops after the first burst on this runtime/OS pair.
  - SILENT under `= 2`: neither object model hears it, which points past NVDA's API choice to event delivery on the
    host.
  The value set comes from NVDA's master-branch `configSpec.py`; the leg's own behaviour confirms that 2026.2 reads it
  the same way, never an assumption.

- **K-runtime:** the Evergreen runtime **153.0.4234.48 is still on disk** beside 154 (machine-wide
  `EdgeWebView\Application`, dir created 2026-09-20). The WebView2 loader can be pointed at it by the loader's
  executable-folder env variable, set in the invoking shell for one control run. The loader reads it; the harness
  code does not change. But the host holds only a **154** msedgedriver (a bounded search under the user profile and the
  tool roots found one copy), and an incoherent pair is REFUSED (a11y.md 2026-09-17). A 153 control therefore needs a
  153 driver the OPERATOR supplies, which is the operator's host task (test-plan §6), never an agent fetch. The known-good
  152 runtime is absent from the host, and a fixed-version 152 is an operator-supplied artifact under the same rule.
  **Time-sensitive:** Evergreen prunes superseded runtime dirs, so the 153 dir may vanish before implement. Re-list it
  before planning on it.

- **Product-side lever — named, not built (operator condition at P4).** This was measured by source read only; no run
  injected anything into the app.
  - The app sets no WebView2 browser arguments: `grep -rn additionalBrowserArgs|additional_browser_args` over
    `crates/conductor-tauri` (excluding `ui/node_modules`) returns 0 hits.
  - So wry's default applies: `--disable-features=msWebOOUI,msPdfOOUI,msSmartScreenProtection`, at
    `wry-0.55.1/src/webview2/mod.rs:294-297`, handed to `set_additional_browser_arguments` at `:327`.
  - The product surfaces that could carry a lever are Tauri's per-window `additionalBrowserArgs` (tauri.conf.json,
    which REPLACES wry's default, so a lever must re-include those three features) and the WebView2 loader's
    additional-browser-arguments env variable.
  - No specific argument can be named from source. Upstream Chromium's `ui/accessibility/accessibility_features.cc`
    (fetched, `main`) defines only `kUiaDisconnectRootProviders` (disabled), `kUiaEventOptimization` (enabled) and
    `kUiaMathMlSupport` (enabled): no native-UIA-provider switch, and no auto-disable-accessibility feature.
  - Any such lever crosses the app boundary, so it is never built or measured in this chunk. It halts for the founder's
    live word (P4 ruling).

- **Out of reach:** the two Windows cumulative updates. They cannot be rolled back as a control, so if K-object-model
  and K-runtime both fail to discriminate, the OS stays a recorded, unisolated candidate.

- **Configuration-bound verdicts** (`a11y.md` 2026-09-17; test-plan §9, per tests-history `2026-09-11-*`): every

- `2c9b37d` (the last wrap's flip, = HEAD): **verdict not yet available** — CI#36709475243 `in progress`, checks 3/3

- [premise-corrected: the last run that HEARD focus is 2026-09-07T22:09:30Z, not 2026-09-04 — seven committed
  records under `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-09-07-sr-findings-fixed/evidence/nvda-pass.{empty,error,live}.run*.json`,

- **This entry owns the prior chunk's red plan entry 12** (the S0-09 / E0-05 regrade: the `jq` gate over the committed

2. **The cause is removed, or routed around by a stated posture.** The fix goes in whichever layer the cause lives in:

   runtime/driver pin. If the cause turns out to be external and not removable from this repo (a runtime regression

- **Marker:** 2026-09-30-the-sr-cause-isolated-on-this-host · **Version:** conductor-0.3.0 · **Generated:** 2026-09-30T13:25Z

    let it check for itself however it can".
  - Asked «W и 153 — да?» ("W and 153 — yes?"), he answered «Да» ("Yes"). Both widenings are RATIFIED, 2026-09-30,

First close the Rust gate deferral carried from the prior chunk. Then isolate why NVDA hears Conductor's webview focus
only in its first burst on WebView2 154.0.4258.37 / Windows 26200.9457 / NVDA 2026.2. Controls run cheapest-first,
and each comparison changes one variable.
Research found an axis the entry never named: the **input path**.

- Every silent run so far is WebDriver/CDP-injected. Those keys never touch the OS keyboard path and leave no
  `Input:` entry in NVDA's log (0 across all three prior logs, research.md).
- No OS-path key has been measured on 154 in any host.
- The prior chunk's USER consequence therefore rests on an unmeasured equivalence.
The arms, in order:

1. **S — PRIMARY, no human: OS-level synthetic keys** (`SendInput`), sent to Edge 154 (the same Chromium build, a
   non-WebView2 host), to Conductor's release bundle and to Windows Search (the only other WebView2 app, on runtime 153
   today).
   - NVDA handles these like physical keys by default: `keyboardHandler.py` + `configSpec.py`
     `handleInjectedKeys= boolean(default=true)`, and the leg profile has no `[keyboard]` section (research.md §P4
     addendum).
   - NVDA logs each one (`Input: kb(desktop):tab`), so the stimulus is machine-timed.
   - S trips no *Boundary widening* (research.md). It runs on the operator's quiet-desktop slot.

2. **W — RATIFIED: a WebDriver session driving Edge 154**, with the keys CDP-injected as in every prior Conductor run.
   This varies the HOST under the injected path. Its log must show 0 `Input:` entries, the witness that it is on the
   injected path.

3. **153 — RATIFIED, run ONLY if the cause is still undecided (the rule in step 7):** the existing `sr-empty` leg with
   the WebView2 loader pointed at the on-disk 153.0.4234.48 runtime (`WEBVIEW2_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE_FOLDER`) and the
   OPERATOR-SUPPLIED 153 msedgedriver. It varies the runtime/driver pair and holds the OS build and desktop fixed.

4. **K — FALLBACK desk task:** S's three targets at the physical keyboard, runnable ONLY with the founder at the
   machine. He is at work today. It confirms S with a human hand and is never simulated.

The three regrade reds this entry owns are ROUTED, never graded. They are agent-arm rows, and every REMOVAL lever
remains unratified: the product lever, pinning the app to an older runtime, a rollback. The «Да» ratifies 153 as a
control, not as a remedy (scope.md).

This rests on a11y-plan §3 *Screen reader test pattern*, test-plan §6 (the desktop-webview row, third family) and §10,
security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Code Patterns rule (b) and → Logging, and architecture §Cross-cutting Patterns
and §Occupied Resources.

0. **Slots, run lengths, census.**
   - Every NVDA launch is a quiet-desktop OPERATOR SLOT. /implement STOPS and asks before each one, stating its run
     length, because pulse-builder opens windows only on the operator's slot. The lengths are estimates from the prior
     legs' wall-clock (Implementation notes):
     - S ≈ 3–4 min;
     - W ≈ 2 min;
     - 153 ≈ 2 min, after the operator supplies the driver;
     - K ≈ 5 min, founder at the desk.
   - The PREREQ and the strict `--e2e` start no NVDA and need no slot. The `--e2e` release build takes ~10–20 min cold.
   - Take a `Win32_Process` census with parentage before and after every leg (host-win32.md 2026-09-17). The families
     are `nvda`, `msedge`, `msedgedriver`, `conductor-tauri`, `tauri-driver`, `node`, `msedgewebview2`, `SearchHost`,
     `pulse-app` and `andromeda-pulse-mcp`.
   - The user's own Edge and the OS's SearchHost are never this session's.
   - Stop everything this session starts (memory: stop-everything-you-start).

1. **Close the PREREQ (no slot).** Fire the `run --unit` entry, then the clippy entry. Neither carries a `defer` key.
   Record the exits and printed verdicts in `evidence/no-boundary-control.md` §PREREQ, as exit plus verdict only and
   never raw diagnostic lines.

2. **Configuration (no slot).**
   - Fire the 154 coherence entry and the Edge-build entry.
   - Re-read the OS `CurrentBuild.UBR` pair.
   - Read the runtime each SearchHost webview process loaded, by VERSION only (153.0.4234.48 at P3).
   - Start the configuration table: WebView2 runtime · driver · Edge build · SearchHost runtime · NVDA (from the first
     leg's log) · OS build · `allowInChromium` (default; the leg profile has no `[UIA]` section) · bundle commit · input
     path.
   - Name registry keys in the colon-free `reg.exe` form; describe host paths in words (host-win32.md 2026-09-11).

3. **Fresh bundle (no slot).** Fire strict `--e2e`. It rebuilds the release binary at the chunk base, which S and the
   153 leg reuse (verification-harness.md `:62`).

4. **Author the two session scripts** (Write tool, whole-content, ASCII only; host-win32.md 2026-09-30). Both live under the gitignored `runs/sr-control/`, are never committed, and have their full text reproduced in evidence. **Both scripts share these rules:** - Guard `CONDUCTOR_NVDA` (and, for W, `CONDUCTOR_MSEDGEDRIVER`) the wdio way: it exists, is a file and carries no shell metacharacter (`wdio.conf.ts:189-193`). Unset → print a skip line and exit 0. A value is never printed. - Start NVDA with the registered argv (`wdio.conf.ts:213`): `-m --no-sr-flag -c runs/sr-control/nvda-config -l 12 -f runs/sr-control/nvda-speech..log`, detached and array-form. The profile is a copy of the committed leg `nvda.ini`, and the previous log of that mode is removed first. Readiness is the `NVDA initialized` line plus a 1.5 s quiet settle (`wdio.conf.ts:218-241`). - Stamp each stimulus as one UTC JSON line in `runs/sr-control/actions..jsonl`. - Activate a target window ONLY when it is not already foreground (verification-harness.md `:59`, corrected 2026-09-04). - The control page is the typed URL `data:text/html,SR control

SR control

`. It has no file, no listener and no network. - Stop NVDA with `-q`, polled to absence (`wdio.conf.ts:244-250`), then print `walk complete`. **`runs/sr-control/key-walk.ps1 -Mode synthetic|physical`:** - (a) Launch Edge InPrivate on the page, then deliver 5 Tabs, 4 s apart. In synthetic mode `SendInput` sends them; in physical mode the script prints a 25 s window for each target and delivers nothing itself. Close the window it opened. - (b) Launch `target/release/conductor-tauri.exe` by path, with the repo root as its working directory, `CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR=runs/e2e-fixture` and `CONDUCTOR_SCENARIOS_DIR=runs/sr-leg/empty` (the `sr-empty` subject's env, `wdio.conf.ts:103`, `:166`). Deliver 5 Tabs, then stop the pid the launch returned. - (c) Win+S opens the search panel. Deliver 3 Tabs, then Escape. **`runs/sr-control/edge-webdriver-walk.ps1` (W):** - Start the driver from `CONDUCTOR_MSEDGEDRIVER` on `--port=4445`, after checking that no listener holds 4444/4445. That is the registered dev-only native-driver port (arch §Occupied Resources, Ports). - Open a W3C session with `browserName: 'MicrosoftEdge'` and `ms:edgeOptions.args ['--inprivate']`, then navigate to the page. - Deliver 5 Tabs through `POST /session/{id}/actions` (key `U+E004`), 4 s apart. - Delete the session and stop the driver pid.

5. **Arm S — the operator's slot.** Fire the S entry once, on the operator's word.
   - Witness: exactly 13 `Input: kb(desktop):tab` entries. Fewer means the arm is VOID, not silent: stop and report.
   - Decide focus theft from NVDA's own log (verification-harness.md `:59`, extended 2026-09-30).

6. **Arm W — the operator's slot.** Fire the W entry once, on the operator's word. Witness: 0 `Input:` entries (the
   injected path), and a session was created (the script prints `session created`). No session means the arm is VOID.

7. **Decide whether the 153 arm runs.** Apply ONE rule and write it with its reading into the evidence file.
   - **SKIP (decided) only when S-edge is heard AND W-edge is heard AND S-conductor is silent.** Edge 154 then hears
     on both input paths and Conductor alone is silent on the OS path. The cause is Conductor's webview posture on
     154, so the runtime arm cannot separate anything more.
   - **RUN in every other combination.** The prior injected-Conductor silence (152 heard, 154 silent) always stands,
     and only the 153 arm separates the runtime/driver pair from the OS updates and the desktop. That includes the case
     where S and W are heard everywhere.
   - A void S or W arm is not a reading, and the rule is applied only to valid arms. An S or W arm that is void RUNS
     153 and is reported void.
   - A skip is recorded as `| R153-empty | … | not-run |` with the rule's reading.

8. **Arm 153 (only if step 7 says RUN) — the operator's slot.**
   - (a) Fire the runtime-folder re-list entry. `153.0.4234.48` absent → `not-run — folder pruned`. Never fetch.
   - (b) ASK the operator for the 153 msedgedriver and never fetch one. The operator supplies its path as the session
     variable `DRIVER_153`, which no committed file reads.
   - (c) Fire the driver admission entry: Authenticode `Valid` + an `O=Microsoft Corporation` signer + version equal
     to the folder's. A failure means the driver is not used.
   - (d) Fire the 153 leg.
   - (e) Copy `runs/sr-leg/nvda-pass.json` to `evidence/nvda-pass.153.json` (the record is cumulative per subject,
     verification-harness.md `:63`, so the copy is what keeps this arm).
   - (f) The witness reads `webview2_runtime` = `153.0.4234.48`. Anything else means the arm is VOID.
   - (g) Compare E0-02..E0-06 against the prior default-arm `sr-empty` runs on 154.

9. **Arm K — fallback desk task.** Fire the K entry once, and only if the operator confirms the founder is at the
   machine. Before firing, post the timetable in chat. If it is not granted during /implement, record its three rows
   `not-run — desk slot not granted`, with that clearing event.

11. **Hygiene and teardown.** Fire the evidence gates, the delta guard, the port probe and the final census. Nothing
    this session started may be left running.

- `conductor-0.3.0/chunks/2026-09-30-the-sr-cause-isolated-on-this-host/evidence/no-boundary-control.md` — the PREREQ, the configuration, every arm's reading and licensing, the 153 rule, the candidates narrowed, the USER consequence, the three reds routed, the ratifications, both scripts' text, the census
- `conductor-0.3.0/chunks/2026-09-30-the-sr-cause-isolated-on-this-host/evidence/nvda-pass.153.json` — the 153 arm's scrubbed pass record (written only when the arm runs)
- none — the scripts and NVDA logs live under the gitignored `runs/sr-control/`; no harness, `ui/src`, `crates/*/src`, profile, contract, scenario or CI file changes
- **The PREREQ closes:** the unit and clippy entries carry NO `defer` key.

- **No `typecheck:e2e`, smoke, `status` or CI entry:** no TS change, no minted `run_id` read (verification-harness.md
  `:49`), no CI-run acceptance.

- **The S, W, 153 and K entries are operator-slot legs** (`leg = 'operator'`). Their preconditions sit inside each
  script (handle guards, NVDA's readiness line, the port check) or in the probe entries listed before them. The 153
  leg's non-priming probes are the folder re-list and the driver admission.

- **The two evidence files are authored by construction** (steps 8e and 10). Their producers are the 153 leg
  (`artifact` `runs/sr-leg/nvda-pass.json`, copied at step 8e) and the S/W/K legs' logs, which step 10 reads.

- **Branch-dependent witnesses are written to hold in BOTH branches.** The 153 and K witnesses read the artifact when
  the arm ran, else they read the evidence row that records it `not-run`. So a rule-sanctioned skip never reads red.

body:
- **Edge browser** `pv` 154.0.4258.37 (the `EdgeUpdate` client key for the browser). This is the SAME build string as

    and licenses nothing about 154 by itself.

The entry's control (1) reads silent-there ⇒ below Conductor, heard-there ⇒ Conductor's posture. Research found an
axis the entry does not name: the **input path**.

- Every silent run so far is WebDriver-injected: CDP key events that never touch the OS keyboard path and leave no

title: P4 addendum — the no-human variant S (OS-level synthetic keys), researched on the overseer's word

data.head: ### P4 addendum — the no-human variant S (OS-level synthetic keys), researched on the overseer's word

body:
The overseer ruled K the primary control. K is a DESK task, runnable only with the founder at the machine. The
overseer also asked for one no-human variant to be weighed.
- **S = OS-level synthetic keys** (`SendInput` from a script) at Edge and at Conductor, with no WebDriver.

- **Does NVDA treat an OS-injected key like a physical one? Yes, by default.** The fetched sources:
  - NVDA `source/keyboardHandler.py` on `master`: `internal_keyDownEvent(vkCode, scanCode, extended, injected)`
    returns early (passes the key through unprocessed) only
    `if injected and (ignoreInjected or not config.conf["keyboard"]["handleInjectedKeys"])`.
    `ignoreInjected` is NVDA's own flag while it injects keys itself.
  - NVDA `source/config/configSpec.py`: `handleInjectedKeys= boolean(default=true)`.
  - The leg's committed `nvda.ini` carries no `[keyboard]` section (a grep for `handleInjected` returns nothing;
    sections are `[general]`, `[speech]` and `[virtualBuffers]` only), so the default applies.
  - An S key therefore reaches `inputCore.executeGesture`, which logs `Input: kb(desktop):tab` at IO level, the same
    as a physical key.
  - It reaches NVDA's keyboard hook path. That is exactly the path WebDriver/CDP injection bypasses (0 `Input:` entries
    over all three prior logs), so S also reaches browse mode, the class E0-09 waits on. That is a side observation;
    this chunk regrades nothing.
  - To the app, S and a physical key are the same window message; only a low-level hook can see the injected flag.

- **Does S trip *Boundary widening* (playbook `:124`)?** No, as planned.
  - The pattern is "a chunk WIDENS what crosses an already-hardened boundary (… a subprocess/IPC boundary gains a new
    crossing)". S commits no spawn form: the walk script lives under the gitignored `runs/sr-control/`, with its text
    reproduced in evidence for reproducibility.
  - It is invoked from the implement session, outside rule (b)'s three loci (driver stack · `agent-run` · `ci.yml`;
    security.md, the 2026-09-24 `secret_scan_gate` precedent).
  - It binds no listener: Conductor idle opens no port, and the `:4317` occupier arms only in a fault phase. Edge on a
    `data:` URL fetches nothing on the leg's behalf. It adds no handle beyond `CONDUCTOR_NVDA`, which it guards the
    wdio way.
  - The harness already registers OS-level key synthesis (`activate-window.ps1`'s `keybd_event` ALT, a rule (b) form
    in the driver stack), so S introduces no new mechanism class.
  - Residual for review: Edge's own background traffic, such as update and SmartScreen, is the browser's, not the
    leg's. The leg itself requests nothing.

- **Comparability.** S differs from K only in who presses the key, a distinction NVDA itself ignores by default. So an
  S reading is a no-human proxy for K, and K remains the human confirmation. S differs from every prior silent run in
  the input path (OS hook vs CDP), which is the unmeasured axis.

- **Foreground.** SendInput goes to the foreground window. Activate a target only when it is NOT already foreground,
  because a synthetic ALT on an already-foreground app opens its System menu (verification-harness.md `:59`,
  corrected 2026-09-04).

data.head: ### P4 addendum 2 — W and the 153 arm, researched on the founder's ratification («Да», scope.md)

body:
- **W (WebDriver at Edge 154).** Keep it OUT of `wdio.conf.ts`. Research found no way to reach Edge from the config
  without a new capability and program (`wdio.conf.ts:345-349` is fixed to `browserName: 'wry'` + `tauri:options`).
  A committed suite would also be a fourth suite family, restated at five registry sites against arch's ~0 B headroom
  (arch-history items 4, 20). So W is a gitignored session script (`runs/sr-control/edge-webdriver-walk.ps1`), like S's:
  - It starts msedgedriver from `CONDUCTOR_MSEDGEDRIVER` (154.0.4258.37, which drives the Edge 154 browser natively) on
    `--port=4445`, the registered dev-only, harness-lifetime native-driver port (arch §Occupied Resources, Ports), so
    no new listener.
  - It opens a W3C session with `browserName: 'MicrosoftEdge'` and `ms:edgeOptions.args ['--inprivate']`, navigates
    to the same `data:` page, and sends 5 Tabs through `POST /session/{id}/actions`, 4 s apart and stamped.
  - It deletes the session, stops the driver pid and quits NVDA.
  - The keys travel CDP, the same injected path as every prior silent Conductor run. So W's `Input:` count must read
    **0**, the witness that W is on the injected path and S is not.
  - The ratified crossing (scope.md) is exercised from the implement session, outside rule (b)'s three loci. No
    committed spawn form moves, so the wrap records the ratification rather than a new form.

- **The 153 arm.**
  - **The variable.** `WEBVIEW2_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE_FOLDER` REPLACES the app's `browserExecutableFolder` when the
    environment is created. Source: the WebView2 Win32 reference, `CreateCoreWebView2EnvironmentWithOptions`, fetched:
    "If you find an override environment variable, use the `browserExecutableFolder` and `userDataFolder` values as
    replacements…".
  - **The folder is admissible.** The reference refuses only a path containing `\Edge\Application\`, and the Evergreen
    versioned folder is `…\EdgeWebView\Application\153.0.4234.48\`, which holds `msedgewebview2.exe` (re-listed at P4:

body:
- (tests) **C1 is a measurement.** The C1 witness reads exactly 5 `Input: kb(desktop):tab` entries. Every key is
  stamped with its phase, input path, landing and foreground process. The theft check is recorded from NVDA's own
  log. Every phase row carries a closed verdict (the `C1-(I1|O|I2)` entry reads 3) (per test-plan §6 Drivers per
  surface, desktop-webview row; §10 Zero-flakiness).

- (a11y) **The branch follows its rule and states only what it licenses.** Exactly one `**Branch:**` line (the
  branch entry reads 1), derived by step 6 from the phase verdicts. Every reading is bound to runtime × driver × NVDA ×
  OS build × input path × launch posture. The focus-event mechanism stays recorded, not established (per a11y-plan §3
  *Screen reader test pattern*; architecture §Established Decisions → [CI/CD]).

- (security) **Commit only on the founder's word.** The commit-only-on-the-word entry exits 0. On H-R, the founder's
  word is quoted verbatim under `**Founder word:**`. On every other branch, nothing under `crates/conductor-tauri/ui`
  moved from `ff4f571`. The delta guard prints nothing on any branch. The SR spec carries no `-Command` spawn (per
  security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Code Patterns, rule (b); playbook `:124`).

- (security) **H-R only — the send-keys script matches the ratified shape.** It has a closed `-Key` set, and refuses
  (exit 4, nothing sent) when the foreground process is not `conductor-tauri`. It is spawned `-File` only with a
  fixed argv and no operator value. `tab` / `shiftTab` / `browseKey` alone move to it, and a refusal throws rather
  than falling back to injected keys (per security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Code Patterns; design-system
  §Navigation Pattern — no single-letter command or OS shortcut beyond the browse keys `h` / `d`).

- (tests) **H-R only — each changed harness member is loaded by an executed leg.** `typecheck:e2e` is green, AND the
  `sr-empty`, `sr-error` and `sr` legs each print `Spec Files:` then TAB then `1 passed, 1 total`, fired once per
  subject on a granted slot (per test-plan §4 conductor-tauri/ui entry; §3 `--e2e`).

- (a11y) **Every other branch — the reds are ROUTED**, each with the successor owner and C1's measured cause (the
  reds entry reads 3). The prior chunk's committed record stays unedited (`git diff --stat ff4f571 --
  conductor-0.3.0/chunks/2026-09-30-the-screen-reader-pass-grades-again-on-this-host` prints nothing).

- (tests) **The closed sets hold** over any regrade record, `.input` included (the closed-set entry reads 0) (per
  security-plan §Input Validation, the speech-log ingest row).

- (a11y) **Arm K is recorded** — three K rows, `not-run` with the clearing event unless a desk slot was granted.
  Never simulated (the K entry reads 3) (per a11y-plan §3 *Supplemental to automated*).

- (security) **Evidence is host-path-free, and teardown is exact.** Hygiene reads 0, no `4444`/`4445` listener, and
  the post-leg census reads 0. The §Census table names every process started and its final state (per security-plan
  §Security Anti-Patterns → Logging; architecture §Occupied Resources → Ports; obs-plan §11 Logs).

- (tests) **The routine arm is unaffected.** Strict `--e2e` prints `[a11y] verdict asserted — 0 failed` with
  `(expected 2)` (per test-plan §3 `run`, `--e2e`).

- (obs) **Every launched arm's backend log is clean.** C1's and each `sr*` leg's `conductor-tauri.jsonl`, under that
  arm's runs-dir `logs/` (`runs/logs/` for C1 and `sr-empty`, `runs/sr-leg/logs/` for `sr` / `sr-error`), holds zero
  `^thread.*panicked` lines (the panic entry reads 0) (per obs-plan §9 Zero-unlogged-panics gate; §3 Log file
  location).

- Spec anchors:
  - a11y-plan §3 *Screen reader test pattern* / *Pass spec format* / *Supplemental to automated*; §5 *Keyboard
    Navigation*; §11 *SLO*, *CI*.
  - test-plan §1 Untestable zones · Coverage triggers; §3 `run` `--e2e`; §4 conductor-tauri/ui; §6 Drivers per
    surface; §10; §11.
  - security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Code Patterns (rule (b)) · Logging; §Input Validation (speech-log ingest,
    host-tool handles); §Dependency Security (the third class).
  - architecture §Cross-cutting Patterns → Scope law · Trust boundary; §Occupied Resources → Ports · Environment
    variables · On-disk artifacts; §Established Decisions → [CI/CD].
  - obs-plan §3 Log file location; §9; §11 Logs · PII Scrubbing.
  - design-system §Navigation Pattern; layout-templates §Component — Primary content block 1 · Primary navigation.

- Research files inspected: see research.md §Files inspected — `screen-reader.e2e.ts`, `activate-window.ps1`,
  `wdio.conf.ts`, `parse-nvda-log.ts`, `rows.ts`, `nvda-pass-spec.md`, `nvda.ini`, the prior chunk's
  `no-boundary-control.md` / `research.md`, the grades-again chunk's `plan.md` and `nvda-pass.json`,
  `security-plan.md:367` and `playbook.md:124-126`.

- **Escalated at P4 (playbook `:124` *Boundary widening*): committing the OS key path.** The overseer answered «Decide
  after step 1»: "this is the founder live word only, so I am asking him now. Plan both branches; implement halts at
  the branch point UNLESS his quoted word has been relayed by then."

- **Committing any OS key path without the founder's quoted word** — rejected. It is a *Boundary widening*
  (playbook `:124`), ratified only by the founder's live word, never a delegate's (security.md 2026-09-29).

- **Re-running any leg until a row is announced** — rejected (test-plan §10; a11y-plan §11). The only re-fire is a
  VOID: a start failure before any stimulus, or a foreground-guard refusal with no key delivered, recorded with the
  window that took the foreground.

- **Moving picker text, Enter, Space, Escape or the picker's arrows to OS input** — rejected. The ratification
  question named only `tab` / `shiftTab` / `browseKey`, and those rows are not among the routed reds.

- **Sending an OS key into whatever window is foreground** — rejected. Every OS key is gated on the foreground
  process (C1 per key; send-keys.ps1 exit 4). A key into the parallel pulse-builder terminal would type into the
  operator's session.

- **A second automation stack for the OS path** (a standalone input harness) — rejected (a11y-plan §11 *CI*;
  architecture Scope law). The OS keys supplement the one WebdriverIO + tauri-driver session.

- **Editing the prior chunk's committed `nvda-pass.json` or `no-boundary-control.md`** — rejected. A regrade writes
  a new record in this chunk's evidence (a11y-history `2026-09-30-the-screen-reader-pass-grades-again-on-this-host`
  KEPT).

- **Changing `wdio.conf.ts`** — rejected. It holds no key-path code (research.md, scope premise-corrected). The one
  spawn site and its env stay as they are.

- **`boot` before the live leg** — rejected (`verification-harness.md:53`). The app's own preflight canary is the
  gate.
- **Simulating arm K with `SendInput`** — rejected (test-plan §11 Universal; scope.md).

- **Graph impact** (research.md §Graph impact; ts plane, 1 query, 48 rows):
  - `tab @ screen-reader.e2e.ts` — 21 call sites (`:95` … `:665`), including `bringToForeground`'s cycle
    (`:95`, `:101`) and `expectFirstTabLanding` (`:307`);
  - `shiftTab` — 6 sites; `browseKey` — 7 sites;
  - `writeNvdaPass` — callers `wdio.conf.ts:454` and the CLI `:486`; `readStamps` / `grade` — one caller each,
    inside `writeNvdaPass`.

  The spec helpers are file-local; there is no rust-plane or cross-package impact.

- **The theft hazard is live today.** The parallel pulse-builder session moved the Pulse tree's HEAD during this
  phase (`d708ad7`, 2026-09-30T15:41+02:00; research.md). Its terminal can take the foreground mid-slot. The per-key
  foreground gate turns such a theft into a VOID row instead of stray keystrokes, and NVDA's log decides theft
  (`verification-harness.md:59`, as extended).

- **The Tab cycle has six stops** (Minimize · Close · Start · the coverage row · the report region · the host-chrome
  `BODY` stop), per the 153 arm's start-of-document cycle (`no-boundary-control.md` §Arms, R153-empty row). A `BODY`
  landing is excluded from the heard/silent count, never graded silent.

- **Browse mode under OS keys is unmeasured.** Whether NVDA returns to browse mode after the picker combobox's
  automatic focus mode decides S0-13..S0-15. Their measured outcomes are what the regrade records; the plan asserts
  nothing about them.

- **Operator review of the regrade record is owed after the wrap's read** (a11y-plan §3: the operator reviews the
  graded record). The new record carries `operator_review: null` until transcribed. It is recorded as owed and does
  not block.

- **Expected amendments (wrap):**
  - a11y-plan §3 *Screen reader test pattern* — the confound verdict bound to C1's configuration and branch. On H-R,
    also the agent arm's key path (OS for Tab, Shift+Tab and the browse keys) and the browse rows actually driven;
    retire "pending OS-level key injection" ONLY for rows driven and heard on the OS path.
  - test-plan §6 desktop-webview row (the `sr*` firing form gains the OS key path) and §1 Untestable zones (the
    browse-mode zone's remedy discharged for the rows driven) — H-R only.
  - security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Code Patterns, rule (b) — H-R only: the EIGHTH governed form
    (send-keys.ps1, the window-activation shape, foreground-guarded), escalated under playbook `:124` and ratified
    by the founder's quoted word. Who answered is recorded. The count moves seven → eight.
  - architecture §Cross-cutting Patterns → Trust boundary — H-R only: the `sr*` leg's spawned children gain the
    send-keys script beside NVDA and the activation script, with no listener. Amend every site restating it in
    lockstep (arch-history `2026-09-08-webview2-runtime-152-installed-in-job`).
  - No amendment for C1 under rule (b): it is an uncommitted session script outside the three loci, on the
    registered stack and ports, with S-class keys. It adds no form, and the count is unchanged by C1.

**Chunk:** The SR pass regrades on the OS input path. The confound is separated (OS keys into the driver-launched
bundle), then the silent focus rows, S0-09, E0-05 and E0-09 are regraded on the validated path, with the
configuration named.
**Date:** 2026-09-30
**Commits:** none since `last_wrap` (HEAD `ff4f571` = the chunk base; no operator pre-CI commit this chunk)

- **Symbols / APIs:**
  - `send-keys.ps1`:
    - one mandatory `-Key` in a closed `ValidateSet` (`Tab` · `ShiftTab` · `h` · `d` · `ArrowDown`);
    - resolves the foreground window's process and exits **4** (nothing sent) unless it is `conductor-tauri`;
    - sends through `SendInput` one event per call — Shift down, key down, key up, then Shift up 300 ms later;
    - ArrowDown carries `KEYEVENTF_EXTENDEDKEY`;
    - exits **5** if fewer events were inserted than requested, or if `GetAsyncKeyState(VK_SHIFT)` still reads down
      afterwards.
  - `screen-reader.e2e.ts`: new `keyRecord` · `injectKeys` · `osKey` · `type OsKey`.
    - `osKey` spawns `spawnSync('powershell.exe', ['-NoProfile','-ExecutionPolicy','Bypass','-File', <send-keys.ps1>,
      '-Key', <constant>])` with `windowsHide` and a 20 s timeout. A non-zero status THROWS, naming the exit (4 =
      foreground refusal), and never falls back to an injected key.
    - `tab()` (21 call sites), `shiftTab()` (6) and `browseKey()` (7; typed to `'h'|'d'|'ArrowDown'`, combobox guard
      kept) now call `osKey`.
    - `bringToForeground`'s start-of-document reset cycle calls `injectKeys('Tab')` directly and no longer calls
      `tab()`.
    - Every remaining `browser.keys` call goes through `injectKeys`: picker text, Backspace, the picker's arrows,
      Enter, Space, Escape.
    - Every key appends `{ts, id:'@key', key, input}` to the actions timeline.
    - Sole callers are file-local; call-site counts are research.md §Graph impact, ts plane.
  - `parse-nvda-log.ts`:
    - new `export type InputPath = 'os'|'webdriver'|'mixed'|'none'` and `PassRow.input`;
    - `Timeline.keys`, and `readStamps` ingests `@key`;
    - new `inputPathOf`; `grade(row, heard, input)`;
    - `BROWSE_NOT_DELIVERABLE` is replaced by `BROWSE_NOT_DRIVEN`. A silent browse row with an OS key in its window is
      now `not-announced` on the agent arm. Without one it stays `not-run-here` on the operator arm, with the new
      note.
    - `writeNvdaPass`'s signature is unchanged; its callers stay `wdio.conf.ts:454` and the CLI `:486`.
  - Ports: none new. The legs use the registered `4444`/`4445` for their lifetime; pulse-app bound `4317`/`4318` on
    the overseer's grant and released them.
  - Env vars: none new.
  - Processes: the `sr*` leg's spawned children gain one per-key `powershell.exe -File send-keys.ps1`, beside NVDA and
