title: Plan — 2026-09-30-unasserted-keyboard-and-focus-visible-claims-closed: "Unasserted keyboard and focus-visible claims closed"

data.head: # Plan — 2026-09-30-unasserted-keyboard-and-focus-visible-claims-closed: "Unasserted keyboard and focus-visible claims closed"

body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._

- **Marker:** 2026-09-30-unasserted-keyboard-and-focus-visible-claims-closed · **Version:** conductor-0.3.0 ·
  **Generated:** 2026-09-30T09:20:00Z

- **Chunk base (W182):** `7ee2fea` (`7ee2feadac235678e0b2696d4a5202dcb2bb2886`), HEAD at take-up. Every diff-shaped
  probe below names it, because the operator pre-CI commit moves HEAD before the wrap.

- **Forks decided at P4 (overseer, founder-delegated, 2026-09-30):**
  - **Build, then assert** — building what a11y-plan §5 already designs is not new trajectory, and re-stating would be
    a deferral. Keep one tab stop per region.
  - **Key map** — Ctrl+Enter / Ctrl+. / Escape. The design-system k9s single-letter register gets its amendment at
    wrap.
  - **Driven arm, one live leg** — it needs the overseer's slot, because the Pulse builder runs its own live legs on
    `:4317` in the same window. **/implement STOPS and asks the operator before firing it.**

a11y-plan §5 makes four keyboard and focus-visible claims that no suite asserts. Research found three of them UNBUILT,
not merely unasserted:

- the webview has **0** key handlers (`grep -rnE "onKeyDown|keydown|ArrowDown|…" crates/conductor-tauri/ui/src` → 0
  hits);

- the coverage matrix is a plain `<table>` inside one focusable scroll `<div>`, with no row focus, no row selection
  and no virtualization (`CoverageMatrix.tsx:60-108`);
- no start / stop / proceed / abort shortcut exists.

The fourth claim, SC 2.4.7's visible `--color-focus` ring, IS built: seven `:focus-visible` outline rules exist. It is
asserted nowhere except as a 3:1 CONTRAST pair (`accessibility.e2e.ts:33`).

This chunk first closes the PREREQ: workspace nextest and clippy, deferred on zero Rust delta by
`2026-09-30-mutation-gate-grades-every-tally-it-rests-on`, run un-deferred. It then builds the three unbuilt behaviours
in the frontend and gives each of the four claims exactly one owning suite that really asserts it:

- **Coverage-matrix row navigation:** roving focus over the matrix rows, keeping ONE tab stop for the region.
  ArrowUp/ArrowDown/Home/End move it. The current row carries `aria-current="true"` and a `--border-emphasis` left edge,
  distinct from the `--color-focus` ring. This follows the picker precedent (a11y-plan §4 → Coverage matrix; §5
  run-console-live / idle-with-report; design-system §Border Progression; layout-templates §Component — Primary content
  block 1).

- **The first-class shortcuts:** Ctrl+Enter starts from idle and proceeds a hold, Ctrl+. stops a live run, and Escape
  aborts a hold. Escape already exists as Radix's dismiss, which resolves NoGo. Each control carries
  `aria-keyshortcuts`, and a visible hint line makes the map discoverable (a11y-plan §5 Per-surface keyboard shortcuts;
  layout-templates §Component — Primary navigation; design-system §Navigation Pattern). The shortcuts dispatch through
  the SAME `start()` / `stop()` / `resolveHold()` handlers the buttons call, so no command, capability or listener is
  added (architecture §Conventions → Interface surfaces; security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Code Patterns).

- **SC 2.4.7:** a routine-arm assertion that, across one full Tab lap, the focused element renders an outline in the
  resolved `--color-focus` and the element just left renders none (a11y-plan §6 Focus ring tokens; §3 Focus
  management test harness).

The four claims then move from `unasserted` (SC 2.4.7 as a NEW row, since the enumeration never carried one) to
`owned` in `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/test/a11y/claim-ownership.ts`:
- the routine arm (CI) owns SC 2.4.7 and idle-with-report row navigation, over the seeded fixture subject;

- the operator-local DRIVEN arm owns run-console-live row navigation and the shortcuts, in ONE live run that also
  keeps asserting the existing HOLD claims.

Every carve-out row gains a checker-enforced statement of what CI gates in its place. That closes `v3-03`
(`verification-matrix.json#v3-03`).

1. **PREREQ first — close the Rust gate deferral, against the untouched chunk base.** Before any file is edited, fire
   the entries `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run --unit` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` (Test
   Commands, in that order: `run --unit` runs `ensure_frontend` first, `scripts/agent-run.sh:55-57`, `:295`, which
   `clippy` needs for `generate_context!`). Record both exits, read from the bare commands, and the nextest summary line
   in `evidence/prereq-baseline.md`. A red here is a pre-existing defect: STOP and report it, since the chunk does not
   paper over it.

2. **Re-read driver/runtime coherence.** Fire the coherence probe entry and record its printed
   `driver … runtime …` line in `evidence/driver-runtime.md` (take-up measured 154.0.4258.37 on both sides). A
   mismatch blocks both webview legs until the operator refreshes the driver (test-plan §6 desktop-webview row; a11y.md
   2026-09-17 as extended 2026-09-30).

3. **Coverage matrix — roving row focus + current-row marking** (`crates/conductor-tauri/ui/src/components/CoverageMatrix.tsx`).
   - Hold the current row as component-local state, index 0 on mount, so `App.tsx`'s and `Gallery.tsx`'s props are
     unchanged (graph: `CoverageMatrix` is referenced only at `App.tsx` and `Gallery.tsx`).
   - Every `<tr className="cov__row">` gets `tabIndex={i === current ? 0 : -1}` and
     `aria-current={i === current ? 'true' : undefined}`. REMOVE `tabIndex={0}` from the `cov__scroll` `<div>`, so the
     region keeps exactly ONE tab stop (the current row). The table keeps its `aria-label`.
   - A `keydown` handler on the `<tbody>` maps ArrowDown / ArrowUp to current ±1 (clamped, no wrap) and Home / End to
     the first / last row. On a mapped key it calls `preventDefault()`, sets the index and focuses that row's element.
     Any other key is ignored and not prevented.
   - A row receiving focus by any means (Tab, click) becomes current (`onFocus`), so mouse and keyboard agree.
   - Focusing a row scrolls it into view natively. That is how rows off-screen in the scroll region are reached,
     because no virtualization exists and every manifest row renders.

4. **Coverage matrix styling** (`crates/conductor-tauri/ui/src/components/CoverageMatrix.css`).
   - Replace the `.cov__scroll:focus-visible` rule with `.cov__row:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-focus);
     outline-offset: -2px }`.
   - Add the current-row edge on the row's first cell: `.cov__row[aria-current='true'] .cov__pid { border-left: 2px solid
     var(--border-emphasis) }`. Every non-current row's first cell keeps a transparent 2px left border, so the columns
     do not shift.
   - Tokens by name only: no literal colour, spacing or motion value (design-system §Self-Validation Protocol, 4. Token
     Test).

5. **Console shortcuts** (`crates/conductor-tauri/ui/src/App.tsx`).
   - Add ONE `window` `keydown` listener, installed in a `useEffect` and removed on cleanup. It reads the current
     `selection`, `runState` and `holdPrompt` through refs or effect dependencies (implementer's choice), never a stale
     closure.
   - It returns early when: `event.defaultPrevented`; `event.repeat`; `event.altKey`, `event.shiftKey` or
     `event.metaKey` is set; or `holdPrompt !== null` (the dialog owns keys during a hold).
   - Ctrl+Enter (`event.ctrlKey && event.key === 'Enter'`) with `selection !== null && runState !== 'live'` →
     `preventDefault()` then `void start()` — the same guard `RunControls` applies (`RunControls.tsx:24-27`).
   - Ctrl+. (`event.ctrlKey && event.key === '.'`) with `runState === 'live'` → `preventDefault()` then `void stop()` —
     the same guard as Stop's `disabled={!running}`.
   - No other key is bound. Ctrl+W and Alt+F4 are untouched, and single letters stay free for the picker's type-ahead and
     NVDA browse mode.

6. **Run controls declare the map** (`crates/conductor-tauri/ui/src/components/RunControls.tsx` + `RunControls.css`). - Start gets `aria-keyshortcuts="Control+Enter"` and Stop gets `aria-keyshortcuts="Control+."`. Button text stays exactly `Start` / `Stop`, since the specs select `button=Start` and restore focus by that name. - Add a visible hint line as a SIBLING after the two buttons inside the `run-controls` group: a `

` with class `run-controls__hint` and `type-data`, reading exactly `Ctrl+Enter start · proceed Ctrl+. stop Esc abort`. - It is not focusable and carries no live region. It is styled `--text-tertiary` by token.

7. **Dialog shortcuts** (`crates/conductor-tauri/ui/src/components/OperatorPauseDialog.tsx`).
   - `AlertDialog.Content` gets an `onKeyDown` that, on Ctrl+Enter with no Alt/Shift/Meta, calls `preventDefault()` and
     `onProceed()`, so a focused Abort button can never also activate.
   - Proceed gets `aria-keyshortcuts="Control+Enter"` and Abort gets `aria-keyshortcuts="Escape"`.
   - Escape stays Radix's own dismiss → `onOpenChange(false)` → `resolveHold('NoGo')` (`App.tsx:376-378`), unchanged.
     `onCloseAutoFocus` / `restoreFocusTo` are unchanged.

8. **The driven arm's subject** (`crates/conductor-tauri/ui/wdio.conf.ts`).
   - Inside the existing `if (invoked.has('driven'))` block, re-create `runs/driven/scenarios` clean (`rmSync` +
     `mkdirSync`, as the SR block does for its runs dir). Copy exactly `scenarios/halo-breathing-encoding.toml` and
     `scenarios/halo-hue-encoding.toml` into it with `copyFileSync`, then set
     `appEnv.CONDUCTOR_SCENARIOS_DIR = 'runs/driven/scenarios'`. The value is repo-relative, as `resolve_under`
     requires, and is set only by this harness.
   - These are the catalog's only two `[[checklist]]` scenarios (`grep -lE '^\[\[checklist\]\]' scenarios/*.toml` → 2).
     In sorted order `halo-breathing-encoding` holds first (10 s of emission) and `halo-hue-encoding` second (180 s),
     so one run yields two holds behind ONE preflight canary.
   - The `nativeDriver()` / `UNSAFE_PATH` / `exitUnresolvedHandle` guard lines stay byte-unchanged.

9. **Rewrite the driven spec as one live run** (`crates/conductor-tauri/ui/test/a11y/operator-hold.e2e.ts`). Replace
   the single `it` with ONE `it` titled exactly `one live run: Ctrl+Enter starts it, its coverage matrix row-navigates
   while live and the count never takes focus, the HOLD dialog traps focus, Space toggles a row, Escape resolves No-Go
   and restores focus, Ctrl+. stops it and Ctrl+Enter proceeds the next hold`. In order:
   1. **Baseline the log and select the suite.** Record the line count of
      `runs/driven/logs/conductor-tauri.jsonl`, 0 if absent; the path is derived like `VIOLATION_SIDECAR`, repo-root
      relative. Click the `Suite — all scenarios` option. Assert its label names `2 scenarios`: the trimmed catalog
      loaded, so a full-catalog run cannot start by accident.
   2. **Start by shortcut.** Tab (bounded by the focusable count) until `document.activeElement` is a
      `[class~="cov__row"]`. Record its P-ID text, then press `['Control','Enter']`. Wait on the titlebar label
      `Conductor · live`. The focused element is still that row, a non-activating position.
   3. **Navigate rows while live.** Press ArrowDown twice, then ArrowUp. After each, `activeElement` is the row at the
      DOM index expected from the rows list, and it is the only row with `aria-current="true"` and `tabindex="0"`.
      Record the final row's P-ID as the hold invoker.
   4. **Hold 1: trap, Space, Escape, restore.** Keep the existing waits and assertions: trap entry, containment across 8
      Tabs and one Shift+Tab, Space toggling the focused checklist row and the `role=status` roll-up changing, then
      Escape dismissing. Restoration now asserts `activeElement` is the `cov__row` whose P-ID is the recorded invoker,
      compared by P-ID text rather than accessible name, since rows project to `TR`.
   5. **Count never takes focus.** Wait for the titlebar count to read `1` (the first scenario's progress event), then
      assert `activeElement` is still that same row.
   6. **Stop by shortcut.** Press `['Control','.']`. Wait on the titlebar label `Conductor · aborted`.
   7. **Hold 2: proceed by shortcut.** Wait (bounded, 6 min) for the second `[role="alertdialog"]`, then press
      `['Control','Enter']` and wait for the dialog to close.
   8. **Discriminate each decision from the backend's own log.** Read the log lines added since step 1. Assert exactly
      one contains `: No-Go (` and exactly one contains `: Go (`, from the `operator-checklist hold resolved by
      tauri-dialog: {label} (…)` message (`execute.rs:152-158`, `pause.rs:40-44`). Wait until a line containing
      `run aborted by the operator` appears (`drive.rs:96`).

   Every wait is a bounded `browser.waitUntil` with a named `timeoutMsg`, never a sleep (test-plan §11 E2E).

10. **Routine-arm assertions** (`crates/conductor-tauri/ui/test/a11y/accessibility.e2e.ts`). Add three `it` blocks
    after the Operable pair and before the two subject-absence markers, so the expected-skip SET stays at exactly two.
    1. **`the focused control shows a visible --color-focus ring and the control it left shows none (SC 2.4.7)`** —
       walk one full Tab lap by the same first-repeated-identity rule as `tabCycle`. At each stop read, in one
       `browser.execute`, the active element's computed `outlineStyle` / `outlineColor` and the PREVIOUS stop's
       element's `outlineStyle`. Assert every active element reads a style other than `none`, with a colour equal
       (colorjs) to `token('--color-focus')`. Assert every previous-stop element reads `none`. Fold the failures into
       one rendered string (frontend.md 2026-09-02).
    2. **`coverage-matrix rows navigate by Arrow keys and Home/End through one tab stop, the current row marked
       aria-current with a --border-emphasis edge (idle-with-report)`** — Tab until the active element is a `cov__row`,
       then:
       - assert it is DOM row 0 and the only row with `tabindex="0"`;
       - press ArrowDown, ArrowDown, ArrowUp, End, Home; after each, the active row's DOM index is the one expected
         from the live rows list (End = the last row). It is the only `aria-current="true"` row and the only
         `tabindex="0"` row;
       - before End, the last row's bounding rect lies outside the scroll region's; after End it lies inside, so an
         off-screen row is reached;
       - the current row's `.cov__pid` computed `borderLeftColor` equals `token('--border-emphasis')`, a non-current
         row's does not, and the current row's `outlineColor` (the ring) differs from that border colour;
       - finally, `axeFindings()` on the navigated state is empty.
    3. **`the console declares its shortcut map: aria-keyshortcuts on Start and Stop and a visible hint line`** —
       asserts Start `Control+Enter`, Stop `Control+.` and the `run-controls__hint` text. This is the SUBSTITUTE gate
       CI runs in place of the driven shortcut assertion, not an owner.

    Expected halves come from the DOM or literals, never from the value under test (frontend.md 2026-09-17).

11. **Move the enumeration** (`crates/conductor-tauri/ui/test/a11y/claim-ownership.ts`).
    - Add an `inPlace: string` field to the `owned` variant, REQUIRED in practice for a non-CI owner (the checker below
      enforces it).
    - Rows after the move:
      - `run-console-live coverage-matrix row navigation` → `owned` · `driven` · the step-9 title · inPlace names the
        routine arm's row-navigation spec over the SAME `CoverageMatrix` component, which `App.tsx` renders in every
        run state.
      - `idle-with-report coverage-matrix row navigation` → `owned` · `routine` · the step-10.2 title.
      - `per-surface keyboard shortcuts` → `owned` · `driven` · the step-9 title · inPlace names the step-10.3 key-map
        declaration spec.
      - The three HOLD rows (`run-console-HOLD focus order`, `run-console-HOLD focus trap`, `focus restoration to the
        triggering control`) → `assertedBy` becomes the step-9 title. inPlace restates the existing a11y-plan §11
        Strategy gates: the expected-skip SET of two, this enumeration, and its checker.
      - NEW row `visible focus ring on the active element` · `SC 2.4.7` · `owned` · `routine` · the step-10.1 title.
    - `NA_CLAIMS` is unchanged. Result: 11 claims · 9 owned (5 operator-local) · 2 n/a-by-construction · 0 unasserted.

12. **Checker enforces the in-place statement** (`crates/conductor-tauri/ui/test/a11y/check-claim-ownership.ts`).
    - In the `owned` case, an owner NOT in `CI_SUITES` with an empty or absent `inPlace` fails with `carve-out with no
      statement of what CI gates in its place`.
    - The carve-out print line appends `; in its place: {inPlace}`.
    - The summary line format (`:117-119`) and the last line (`:120`) are byte-unchanged.

13. **Re-aim the SR harness at the new tab stop** (P5 condition, overseer: the S0-09 regrade is fired in THIS chunk,
    never left owed). Three SR rows assert the coverage scroll `<div>`, which step 3 removes as a tab stop:
    - S0-09 (`sr`, `screen-reader.e2e.ts:430-433`);
    - E0-05 (`sr-empty`, `:591-594`);
    - E0-09 (`sr-empty`, `:601-605`).

    Changes:
    - In `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/test/a11y/screen-reader.e2e.ts`, add a helper `expectActiveCoverageRow()`, a
      bounded `browser.waitUntil`, never a sleep. It asserts `document.activeElement` is a `[class~="cov__row"]` with
      `tabindex="0"` and `aria-current="true"` inside the table whose `aria-label` is `Coverage rows`. Replace
      `expectActiveScrollRegion('Coverage rows')` with it at those three sites. `expectActiveScrollRegion('Run report
      rows')` (E0-06) is unchanged, since the report keeps its scroll-region stop.
    - In `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/test/a11y/screen-reader/rows.ts`, S0-09 and E0-05 become item `coverage matrix
      current row`, node `tr[tabindex=0][aria-current=true] in table[aria-label="Coverage rows"]`, and expected `the
      focused row alone, its P-ID read, never the table's rows as one utterance`. They take `tokens: ['P-001']` (the P-ID
      of DOM row 0, per manifest order `contracts/pulse-capabilities.toml:14`, which the routine row spec's
      "DOM row 0" read confirms) and `forbidden: ['P-002']` (a second row's P-ID heard = the table read as one
      utterance). E0-05's stale `div[role="group"]` node text goes with it. E0-09's node names the current coverage
      row as its Shift+Tab landing; its expected tokens and its browse class are unchanged.
    - In `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/test/a11y/screen-reader/nvda-pass-spec.md`, rows S0-09, E0-05 and E0-09 restate
      the same node and expectation, so spec and grader agree.

14. **Legs, in order: routine, sr-empty, then (the operator's slot) driven and sr live.**
    1. Fire the routine `--e2e` entry. It rebuilds the release bundle, which every later suite reuses because only
       `--e2e` rebuilds (verification-harness.md 2026-09-07).
    2. Fire `sr-empty`. It needs no Pulse, only `CONDUCTOR_NVDA` (the host's portable copy at
       `/d/dev/tools/nvda/nvda.exe`, passed per invocation, since the handle is not persisted) and
       `CONDUCTOR_MSEDGEDRIVER`.
    3. STOP and ask the operator for the live slot. On their word, and with `pulse-app` running under the
       deterministic posture:
       - take the pre-leg census (`msedgedriver`, `conductor-tauri`, `tauri-driver`/`node`, `nvda`, `msedgewebview2`
         with parentage; verification-harness.md 2026-09-02 as extended 2026-09-08);
       - fire the non-priming probe, then the driven leg, with no `boot` before it and at least a 150 s quiet window
         after any preceding canary (verification-harness.md 2026-08-19 as extended 2026-09-01);
       - wait a further 150 s quiet window, since the SR live subject fires its own preflight canary;
       - fire `sr` (live) with `CONDUCTOR_SCENARIOS_DIR=runs/sr-leg/scenarios` and the sidecar on `PATH`
         (verification-harness.md 2026-09-04, 2026-09-07);
       - take the post-leg census.
    4. Copy `runs/sr-leg/nvda-pass.json` to `evidence/nvda-pass.json`. Read `subjects.live.recorded_at` and
       `subjects.empty.recorded_at` against the two legs' start stamps, so both subjects are THIS session's
       (verification-harness.md 2026-09-07 — the record is cumulative per subject).

    Record the census tables, the legs' verdict lines, the two decision log lines and the SR recorded_at readings in
    `evidence/driven-leg.md`. Stop everything the legs started; NVDA quits through the harness's own `nvda -q`, and
    `pulse-app` is left running only if the operator started it.
    If an SR row grades other than `announced-as-expected`, that is a finding to fix in this chunk (the row's tokens
    or the product). It is never re-owned elsewhere.

- `conductor-0.3.0/chunks/2026-09-30-unasserted-keyboard-and-focus-visible-claims-closed/evidence/` —
  `prereq-baseline.md`, `driver-runtime.md`, `driven-leg.md`, `nvda-pass.json`, `operator-pass.md`.
- `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/src/components/CoverageMatrix.tsx` — roving row focus + `aria-current` (step 3).
- `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/src/components/CoverageMatrix.css` — the row ring and the current-row edge (step 4).
- `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/src/App.tsx` — the window shortcut listener (step 5).
- `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/src/components/RunControls.tsx` — `aria-keyshortcuts` + the hint line (step 6).
- `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/src/components/RunControls.css` — the hint line's token styling (step 6).

- `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/src/components/OperatorPauseDialog.tsx` — Ctrl+Enter Proceed + `aria-keyshortcuts`
  (step 7).
- `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/wdio.conf.ts` — the driven suite's trimmed catalog (step 8).
- `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/test/a11y/operator-hold.e2e.ts` — the one-live-run spec (step 9).
- `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/test/a11y/accessibility.e2e.ts` — three routine `it` blocks (step 10).
- `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/test/a11y/claim-ownership.ts` — rows moved, SC 2.4.7 row, `inPlace` (step 11).
- `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/test/a11y/check-claim-ownership.ts` — the carve-out statement check (step 12).

- `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/test/a11y/screen-reader.e2e.ts` — `expectActiveCoverageRow()` at S0-09, E0-05 and E0-09
  (step 13).

- `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/test/a11y/screen-reader/rows.ts` — S0-09 / E0-05 / E0-09 node, expectation and tokens
  (step 13).
- `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/test/a11y/screen-reader/nvda-pass-spec.md` — the same three rows restated (step 13).

The PREREQ pair runs first, against the untouched base (step 1), and again in the full P2 run over the chunk's delta.
The chunk itself has zero Rust delta, but the PREREQ un-defers workspace nextest and clippy regardless. The UI gate is
the routine `--e2e` self-verify. The driven leg is `leg = 'live'`, preceded by its non-priming probe, and fired only
on the operator's word (the slot). No `status` smoke: the chunk has no boot-path change, and `status` cannot tell this
run from residue (verification-harness.md 2026-08-11). The CI acceptance needs the operator pass (hygiene → pre-CI
commit → push → CI read). The `evidence/` files the criteria name are records /implement WRITES in steps 1, 2 and
14, not artifacts an entry produces; the host-path sweep reads them all. The SR legs (P5 condition) run in the same
session: `sr-empty` needs no Pulse, and `sr` live shares the driven leg's slot.

  capabilities widening is the playbook's `Boundary widening` escalate pattern. A webview `keydown` listener reaches

- Starting a run from the ROUTINE arm to test Start — rejected. `start()` really starts a run against the seeded
  `CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR` (`App.tsx:202-229`, `wdio.conf.ts:373`): a `Blocked` record lands in the fixture, and with a
  sidecar on `PATH` a real preflight canary fires.

- A second driven run for Stop or Proceed — do not. Back-to-back runs dedupe on the open canary incident
  (verification-harness.md 2026-08-16, 2026-08-19); one run with two holds carries all four shortcuts.

- `aria-selected` on the `<tr>` — do not. A plain table row is not a selectable-row composite; `aria-current` is the
  picker's shipped precedent and a11y-plan §5 admits either.

- Keeping the scroll `<div>` focusable beside focusable rows — do not. That makes two tab stops for one region, against
  the overseer's one-stop ruling, and moves the SR leg's Tab rows twice.

- Changing button TEXT to carry the key — do not: `button=Start` selectors and the restoration-by-name checks key on
  it. The hint lives in a sibling line.

- A new `CONDUCTOR_*` handle — do not. `CONDUCTOR_SCENARIOS_DIR` already exists and `wdio.conf.ts` already sets it for
  the `sr-empty` / `sr-error` subjects (`:394`).

- Grading hold decisions by the dialog closing — do not. Proceed and Abort both close it; only the backend's
  `: Go (` / `: No-Go (` lines discriminate them.

- **cmdk Enter interplay.** Inside the picker, cmdk's own Enter handling selects the highlighted item. The window
  listener skips a `defaultPrevented` event, so Ctrl+Enter pressed IN the picker input may only select. The driven spec
  starts from a matrix row, which is the non-activating position a11y-plan §5 means. Do not move the listener to the
  capture phase to "fix" this: that would make Ctrl+Enter change the selection and start in one keystroke.

- **Log path.** The Tauri backend log for the driven suite is `runs/driven/logs/conductor-tauri.jsonl`
  (`runs_dir.parent()/logs`, obs-plan §3 Log file location). The spec reads only the lines added after its own baseline
  count, because the file persists across runs.

- **`No-Go` spelling.** The label is `No-Go` with a hyphen (`pause.rs:43`). `: Go (` does not match `: No-Go (`,
  which is why the atoms include the leading colon and space.

- **Stop does not cancel a scenario in flight.** `drive_run` polls abort between scenarios and after the last
  (`drive.rs:75-93`). So after Ctrl+. the second scenario still runs to its hold, which is what lets Ctrl+Enter proceed
  it. The titlebar reads `aborted` immediately (`App.tsx:241`), and the final `Aborted` stage confirms it.

- **Count update.** The first scenario's progress event (`drive.rs:83-86`) sets the titlebar count to `1` only AFTER
  hold 1 resolves, which is exactly when focus has just been restored to the row. Waiting for `1` and re-reading
  `activeElement` is the no-focus-steal witness.

  (`screen-reader.e2e.ts:430`), E0-05 (`:591`) and E0-09 (`:601`). Their DOM assertion is
  `expectActiveScrollRegion('Coverage rows')` (`:268-280`), which requires a `tabindex="0"` element CONTAINING the

  graded by `parse-nvda-log.ts`, and the operator reviews the record rather than listening. If the host's portable NVDA
  cannot be started, /implement says so in ONE line, and the wrap pins it to an owner entry in THIS version, never
  `residuals.md` (overseer).

  added), with 2 skipped. Record what the leg measures. No prose baked with a count needs changing (test-plan §9, the
  moving-count rule).

  - layout-templates §Component — Primary navigation (the key map and the hint line) and §Component — Primary content
    block 1 (virtual-scroll → shipped; the keyboard-selected row).
  - test-plan §6 desktop-webview row — the driven arm now seeds its own two-scenario catalog under

title: Premises found at take-up — closed at P3

data.head: ## Premises found at take-up — closed at P3

body:
- **"Unasserted" is "unbuilt" for three of the four — VERIFIED at P3.**
  - `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/src` at the chunk base carries **0** key handlers
    (`grep -rnE "onKeyDown|keydown|ArrowDown|ArrowUp|addEventListener\(['\"]key|accessKey|aria-keyshortcuts|useHotkey" src`
    → 0 hits, re-run at P3).
  - The coverage matrix (`CoverageMatrix.tsx:60-108`) and the run report (`RunReport.tsx:47-86`) are plain `<table>`s
    inside a `tabIndex={0}` scroll region. Keyboard SCROLLING exists; row focus and row selection do not. There is no
    virtualization: every manifest row renders (`rows.map`, `:79`), so §5's "off-screen virtual-scrolled rows" has no
    referent.
  - `aria-selected`/`aria-current` + `--border-emphasis` exist only on the picker (`ScenarioPicker.tsx:51,71`,
    `ScenarioPicker.css:59-60`).
  - Start/Stop are native `<button>`s (`RunControls.tsx:21-38`) and Proceed/Abort are Radix `AlertDialog.Action`/`Cancel`
    buttons (`OperatorPauseDialog.tsx:59-71`). Enter/Space activate them only once focused, and Escape resolves NoGo via
    `onOpenChange`. No shortcut exists.
  - **The chunk's real fork is therefore build-then-assert vs re-state the §5 claim to what ships.** It is P4's fork.

- **run-console-live and idle-with-report are the SAME component — VERIFIED at P3.** `App.tsx:344-346` renders one
  `CoverageMatrix` in every run state, with lamps projected from the run report (`App.tsx:172`). The routine arm's seeded
  subject IS the idle-with-report state: the fixture journal has 3 records
  (`grep -c . crates/conductor-run/tests/fixtures/lamps-journal.jsonl` → 3) and the matrix carries every manifest row.
  The `live` state is reachable only through `start_run`, which the routine arm has no Pulse for.

- **SC 2.4.7 is built and unasserted — VERIFIED at P3.**
  - Seven `:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-focus) }` rules exist: `Titlebar.css:90`,
    `RunControls.css:24`, `ScenarioPicker.css:25`, `CoverageMatrix.css:23`, `RunReport.css:49`,
    `OperatorChecklist.css:34`, `OperatorPauseDialog.css:99`.
  - The routine arm's only ring-adjacent row is the token-pair CONTRAST row (`accessibility.e2e.ts:33`), re-derived at P3
    (`PAIRS` holds `--color-focus`/`--color-base` 3:1). It proves the ratio, not that a ring renders.
  - No transition animates `outline` anywhere (`grep -rn "transition" src/components/*.css` → 6 hits, none naming
    outline), so a computed-style read taken right after a key sees the final ring, not a mid-fade value.
  - [premise-corrected: design-system §Depth Strategy states the ring as a `0 0 0 2px` `box-shadow` and §Motion as a
    `--motion-micro` fade-in; the code draws an `outline` with no fade. A ring assertion keys on presence + colour, not on
    the drawing property. Reconciling spec to code is a wrap amendment candidate, not this chunk's code.]

- **The CARRY's "the committed enumeration already names all four" is FALSIFIED at take-up.**
  `claim-ownership.ts` carries THREE `unasserted` rows (`:52-56`, `:65-70`, `:101-106`) and no SC 2.4.7 row; a search of
  the file for `2.4.7` returns 0. So SC 2.4.7 enters the enumeration as a new row. That row is a move of the population,
  not just of the state, so the enumeration's `NA_CLAIMS` set logic and the ownership checker's own population must be
  re-read at P3.

- **Row label mismatch — VERIFIED as a fact, left to P4.** `claim-ownership.ts:53` carries `SC 2.1.1` and `:67`
  carries `SC 2.4.3`. The 2026-09-17 chunk authored both, and the checker (`check-claim-ownership.ts`) never reads `sc`.
  So the label is documentary, and a move re-labels only if the asserting spec proves a different criterion.

- **The ownership checker admits a new row without code change — VERIFIED at P3.** `check-claim-ownership.ts:51-76`
  grades each row by its state. The only SET assertion is `NA_CLAIMS` (`:85-95`), which an `owned` SC 2.4.7 row does not
  touch.
  - An `owned` row needs `assertedBy` to equal an `it('…'` title in its owner spec, whose body carries `expect(`
    (`:43-67`).
  - The title match is a literal `it('${title}'` search, so the title must be single-quoted and byte-equal.

- **Adding tab stops moves other suites.** The routine Operable pair walks the whole focusable set
  (`FOCUSABLE_SELECTOR`, `accessibility.e2e.ts:196-197`). Its roster is live-derived, so it adapts, but the "first two"
  literal (`:492-494`) stays. The operator-local SR leg walks Tab into the coverage region (`screen-reader.e2e.ts:430`,
  S0-09) and the report region (`:591-595`, E0-05/E0-06). Any row-focus design that ADDS tab stops shifts those rows. A
  roving-tabindex design (one stop per region) keeps the stop count.

title: Decided at P4 (validation-1: intent-incomplete, amended here)

data.head: ## Decided at P4 (validation-1: intent-incomplete, amended here)

body: Overseer rulings, founder-delegated, 2026-09-30:

- **Build, then assert.** The three unbuilt claims are BUILT in the frontend (roving matrix row focus with one tab stop
  per region; the Ctrl+Enter / Ctrl+. / Escape key map) and then asserted. Building what a11y-plan §5 already designs is
  not new trajectory, and re-stating would be a deferral (founder: none).

- **Key map:** Ctrl+Enter starts and proceeds, Ctrl+. stops, Escape aborts. The design-system k9s single-letter register
  gets its amendment at wrap.

- **Ownership:** the routine arm (CI) owns SC 2.4.7 and idle-with-report row navigation. The DRIVEN arm owns
  run-console-live row navigation and the shortcuts, in ONE live run over a trimmed two-scenario catalog (two holds, one
  canary). This refines "preferably the routine arm" above for the two claims only a live run can show. Each
  carve-out's in-place CI gate is stated in the enumeration and enforced by its checker.

- **The live leg needs the overseer's slot.** The Pulse builder runs its own `:4317` legs in the same window, so
  /implement stops and asks before the probe and the leg.

- **The SR regrade is IN scope (P5 condition, overseer: founder allows no deferral).** Three SR rows (S0-09 on `sr`;
  E0-05 and E0-09 on `sr-empty`) assert the coverage scroll `<div>` the build removes as a tab stop. They are re-aimed
  at the focused row, and both subjects are fired in this chunk: `sr-empty` needs no Pulse, and `sr` live shares the
  driven leg's slot. The host's portable NVDA exists (the handle is not persisted), so an agent runs it. Only if NVDA
  genuinely cannot start does /implement say so in one line, and the wrap then pins it to an owner entry in this
  version, never residuals.

- **Chunk base (W182):** `1fe46a1` (`1fe46a10948647938168d45da4b21d34bd47de3e`) — every diff-shaped probe names it.
- **SUT:** andromeda-pulse `a2addb3` (`a2addb3755b3029cb79809b96efdd2522749b179`), read at committed state only.

Run a third pre-registered real-model series for `v3-09` against a Pulse that carries its incident-surfacing fix
(`a2addb3`: the L4 schema asks for the decision after the analysis, the storm digest's OVERALL line no longer
reads `nominal`, and a no-incident outcome is logged with its reason). The 2026-09-30 series graded none of its
three drives, because the real model dismissed the canary's storms in d1 and the scenario's own storm digest in
d2 and d3. This series measures whether the fix changes that live. It holds the same discipline: the design and
the rule are fixed in the posture contract before d1, the captures are digest-pinned, and nothing is retried until
it passes (per test-plan §6 Real-model interpretation leg; §9 Live-Pulse scenarios; architecture §Occupied
Resources, the posture-contract entry; §Established Decisions [Probabilistic-Assertion Policy]).

One hermetic change lands first, so a dismissal is recorded with Pulse's OWN stated cause instead of an inferred
one. At `a2addb3` Pulse logs `interpretation.incident.skipped` with closed-enum fields (`skip_reason`, `decision`,
`severity`, `digest_kind`), all four allowlisted. The capture prints that line, and each `canary:` line carries its
paired inference's `skip_reason`. Both changes sit OUTSIDE the grading rule, which stays byte-identical, because
every prior series holds its recorded rule equal to the current one (research.md §Files inspected). Pulse's line
reaches committed evidence through the existing source (2) of the capture ingest row, fields-only, through the
four-stage scrub chain. That is not a widening (security-plan §Input Validation, the real-model capture ingest row).

The rest is gated on two operator slots: building Pulse's binaries in the Pulse tree, and the model runs on `:4317`.
`pulse-app` and the MCP sidecar are both rebuilt from `a2addb3` and each is proven. `pulse-app` is proven by
content: strings the fix introduces are present, and the string it retired is absent. The sidecar has no
source-determinable new string, so it is measured first and falls back to build provenance (scope §What this chunk
builds item 2). The series is three drives on ONE fresh letters-only data dir. Its verdict is stated by a harvest
test over the pinned captures. The `v3-09` ref test is written ONLY if the pass condition holds.

1. **The capture prints Pulse's no-incident outcome.**
   - Where: `crates/conductor-run/tests/real_model_live.rs`, `print_pulse_witnesses`'s target list (`:619-653`).
   - Add the target `interpretation.incident.skipped` with the keys `skip_reason`, `decision`, `severity`,
     `digest_kind`.
   - It prints like every sibling (`pulse-log {name}: {count}`, then one `pulse-log   {name} t=… k=v…` line per hit),
     fields-only, through `emit`. So it passes `mask_workspace_key` → `redact_value` → `mask_host_paths` →
     `elide_fingerprints`.
   - Nothing else in the file changes.

2. **Each `canary:` line carries its inference's skip reason.**
   - Where: `crates/conductor-run/tests/real_model_common/mod.rs`, `canary_attempts` (`:66-142`).
   - Add a const for the target `interpretation.incident.skipped`. It is distinct from the existing `SKIPPED`
     (`interpretation.inference.skipped`, a pipeline skip), and its name must not collide with it.
   - Within the inference segment the function already computes, read the FIRST such line's `skip_reason`. Append it
     as the LAST field of the printed line: ` skip_reason={value}`, or `none` when the segment has none.
   - The token decision (`surfaced` / `dismissed` / `pipeline-fault`) does not change. A surfacing, a pipeline fault
     and a pre-`a2addb3` log simply read `skip_reason=none`.
   - The rule reads only the first token after `canary: ` (`real_model_harvest.rs:433-448`), so this never reaches
     the rule.

3. **Pairing arms for the new field** (harvest, OUTSIDE the rule markers, beside `:1245-1358`). Add two plain
   `#[test]` functions, since `conductor-run` has no `rstest` (testing.md 2026-09-23):
   - **(a)** A parse `ok` followed by an `interpretation.incident.skipped` with `skip_reason = "decision_dismiss"`
     prints a line that starts `canary: dismissed ` and ends ` skip_reason=decision_dismiss`.
   - **(b)** A surfacing (parse `ok`, then `interpretation.incident.created`) ends ` skip_reason=none`, and so does
     the existing pre-fix shape (parse `ok`, no outcome line), which still reads `dismissed`.
   - A one-line source arm asserts that `real_model_live.rs` carries the literal `"interpretation.incident.skipped"`
     (the `include_str!` idiom of `the_capture_prints_every_token_the_rule_reads`, `:1385`).

5. **Hermetic gates green.** Every `role = 'unit'` / `'lint'` entry of `## Test Commands` that needs no Pulse, and
   the base-diff probes, read green before any part of B starts.

title: B — the series (gated on the operator's slots)

data.head: ### B — the series (gated on the operator's slots)

body:
7. **The build slot** — ask the operator for it ("Building Pulse binaries runs in the Pulse tree where
   pulse-builder also builds") and wait. On the grant:
   - build `pulse-app`, then the sidecar, with the two `role = 'build'` entries;
   - run the content and provenance probes;
   - record in `evidence/attempt-ledger.md` the binaries table (name, build time, sha256, new-string count,
     old-string count, which proof arm held for the sidecar).

   Record each build's exit and its `Finished` line only. Cargo's `Compiling …` lines carry host paths and stay out
   of evidence.

8. **The dir.** Record the `%TEMP%/pulse-legs` listing (report-only entry) with `rm-surfacing-series` absent, then
   create the leaf. No recursive delete anywhere (security.md 2026-09-06).

9. **Pre-registration witness.** Before d1, record in `evidence/attempt-ledger.md` the line
   `pre-registration sha256: {hex}` over the new section, LF-normalized, from its heading line up to the next `## `
   heading (the `contract_section` form, `real_model_harvest.rs:1903`). The section is never edited afterwards.

10. **The model-run slot.** Ask the operator for the slot (model runs and `:4317` are the operator's) and whether
    the agent launches `pulse-app` (memory: agent-may-launch-pulse-app). Wait for the answer.
    - On the grant, launch the posture with the agent's or the operator's hands as the word says, by the scripted
      recipe, from a cwd outside this repo.
    - Confirm the booted posture from Pulse's own log, as step 4 states it.
    - Record the grant and the confirmation in the ledger.

11. **The three drives.** For each of `d1`, `d2`, `d3`, in order:
    1. Take a census (PRE).
    2. Run the non-priming preconditions probe.
    3. Fire the drive entry, which copies the capture into `evidence/rm-capture-dN.txt`.
    4. Write one ledger row covering: the slot, run id, route, grade, the three further grades, the `canary:` tokens
       WITH their `skip_reason`s, the scenario digest's outcome and Pulse's stated reason when it was not surfaced,
       the `prompt_version` seen, the key-rendering witness, and the census.
    5. Keep the quiet window before the next drive.

    Only a `pipeline-fault` canary re-fires, once, uncounted (the captured file then takes a `-pipeline-fault`
    suffix). After the last drive, stop every process the agent started (memory: stop-everything-you-start) and take
    the post-census against the pre-series baseline.

    If a drive throws on a HARNESS defect (not a grade), the 2026-09-30 operator rule applies: one fix-loop re-fire on
    a new slot; a second harness defect stops and reports (verification-harness.md 2026-09-30).

- `conductor-0.3.0/chunks/2026-10-01-interpretation-re-proven-after-the-incident-surfacing-fix/evidence/attempt-ledger.md` — steps 6-11: the gate re-check, the binaries table, the dir listing, the pre-registration digest, one row per drive, the series verdict, the operator pass.

- `conductor-0.3.0/chunks/2026-10-01-interpretation-re-proven-after-the-incident-surfacing-fix/evidence/` — `rm-capture-d1.txt`, `-d2.txt`, `-d3.txt` (step 11; plus a `-dN-pipeline-fault.txt` only if a re-fire happens).
- `crates/conductor-run/tests/real_model_live.rs` — step 1.
- `crates/conductor-run/tests/real_model_common/mod.rs` — step 2.
- `crates/conductor-run/tests/real_model_harvest.rs` — steps 3, 12 (never between the rule markers `:61`-`:449`).
- `crates/conductor-run/tests/real_model_series/mod.rs` — step 12.
- `contracts/pulse-real-model-leg-posture.md` — step 4 (add-only).
Graph impact (research.md §Graph impact, rust plane):

- **`canary_attempts`** (common, `real_model_common/mod.rs:65` 0-indexed) — its 7 call sites are all in
  `real_model_harvest.rs` (`:55` import, `:1015`/`:1023`, `paired` `:1241`, `:1611`, `:1826`, `:2033`). Its
  signature does not change. The printed string gains a trailing field, which the rule's own first-token
  `canary_attempts` (`:433`) never reads. The existing pairing arms assert with `starts_with` (`:1262-1265`).

- `print_pulse_witnesses` (`real_model_live.rs:538`) — unindexed (`live-pulse` gate); no caller outside its file
  (grep).

No signature any caller uses changes; no manifest changes (`Cargo.lock` package count 562, `grep -c "^name = "
Cargo.lock` at `1fe46a1`).
Hermetic entries run at /implement P2 and in the wrap light gate.
- **Live entries are `leg = 'operator'`:** fired once, in the operator's slots, and never re-run by the wrap.

- **Liveness probe:** the non-priming probe for every drive is `conductor preconditions --for
  real-model-interpretation`. It fires no canary and spawns nothing.

- **No `boot` before any drive.** It would prime the canary incident the drive dedupes against
  (verification-harness.md 2026-08-19 (a)).
- **Smoke:** `status` is the mint-then-read smoke on d3's `run_id`.

- **Pulse builds:** run in the Pulse tree only on the build-slot grant, inside a subshell `cd`, because cargo reads
  its config from the cwd. Their raw output is never copied into evidence.

- **Host paths:** every Pulse binary probe runs from inside `target/release` with bare file names, so nothing it
  prints names a host path.

title: Plan — 2026-10-01-per-run-span-identity-in-the-real-model-harness: "Per-run span identity in the real-model harness"

data.head: # Plan — 2026-10-01-per-run-span-identity-in-the-real-model-harness: "Per-run span identity in the real-model harness"

body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._

- **Marker:** 2026-10-01-per-run-span-identity-in-the-real-model-harness · **Version:** conductor-0.3.0 ·
  **Generated:** 2026-10-01T21:26Z · **Base:** `2c97d3b` (W182)

Two drives of the same scenario and seed, fired inside one Pulse buffer window, must both land. Today the second
drive's spans are refused. Every span the dispatcher emits draws its `(trace_id, span_id)` from
`emission_seed(scenario.seed, phase, occurrence)` (`dispatch.rs:78` → `exception.rs:185-187`). Pulse keys its span
store on exactly that pair: `spans` `PRIMARY KEY (trace_id, span_id)` at Pulse `a2addb3` `buffer/src/schema.rs:36`.
A replayed identity rejects the whole batch at flush (Pulse's own test `appender.rs:996`), logged as `duckdb.append`
`reject_reason=append_failed`. Pulse holds rows for 600 s plus a 100 s sweep (`retention.rs:41-51`,
`contract.rs:109`). That is the d2 gap of the 2026-10-01 series (scope.md, research.md).

The fix gives each production execution its own span identity and leaves everything else seed-pure. A new
`conductor-emit` primitive re-keys a built trace request. It is a deterministic bijection derived from a `u64` salt
on `ChaCha8Rng`. It XORs every non-empty `trace_id`, `span_id` and `parent_span_id` with salt-derived masks, so
linkage inside a drive is preserved and no content byte moves. Content means fingerprints, events, attributes,
durations, the PII corpus a live harvest re-derives, counts and timing. The dispatcher takes the salt as a required
`connect` parameter. `execute_scenario` passes the `std::time` emission instant it already reads (`emitted_ms`,
`execute.rs:85`), the same per-run base the canary has used since 2026-06-27 (`canary.rs:294`). The dispatcher tier
driven without a salt keeps its identity bytes, so the `dispatch_wire__*` goldens and
`the_same_seed_reproduces_the_same_stream` stay unchanged.

Proof comes in two tiers. In CI, two same-seed drives through the real `Dispatcher` into a loopback stub must share
no `(trace_id, span_id)` pair. That models Pulse's key as verified in Pulse's source, and the test fails when the
re-key is removed. In the operator pass, a live witness runs on the operator's word ("measured over inferred"). It
uses one deterministic-posture `pulse-app` on the `a2addb3` binaries, sha256-verified first. Two
`conductor run exception-event-capture` drives run inside Pulse's retention window, and the witness grades Pulse's
own log: 0 `append_failed`, `append_rejections` 0, spans appended after the second drive. The production wiring
(`execute_scenario` → salt) is only reachable live, because the ready path emits to the fixed `:4317`. So the
witness is the proof of that half.

Provenance: arch §Cross-cutting Patterns → Determinism discipline and §Established Decisions [Determinism RNG] /
[Module Boundaries]; test-plan §4, §7, §8, §10, §6; obs-plan §6 (Boundary-call wrappers), §11; security-plan
§Dependency Security, §Security Anti-Patterns → Data Protection; layout-templates §cli Primary screens (no
surface moves).

1. **The identity primitive** — create `crates/conductor-emit/src/identity.rs` with
   `pub fn rekey_trace_identity(request: &mut ExportTraceServiceRequest, salt: u64)`.
   - Derive one 16-byte trace mask and one 8-byte span mask from `ChaCha8Rng::seed_from_u64(salt)`, drawn in that
     order, reusing `span_tree::gen_id`.
   - For every span in every resource/scope, XOR the mask into `trace_id` (16 B), `span_id` and `parent_span_id`
     (8 B), and into each link's `trace_id` / `span_id`. Skip any id field that is EMPTY: a root's empty
     `parent_span_id` stays empty.
   - Touch no other field.
   - The doc comment states the contract: a bijection per salt, linkage preserved, content untouched, a pure
     function of `(request, salt)`, no clock, no I/O and no self-observation.
   - Unit tests in the same file (`#[cfg(test)]`):
     - (a) on an `error_trace_request(…, ErrorPlacement::DeepChild { depth: 3 }, …)`, every child's
       `parent_span_id` still equals its parent's re-keyed `span_id`, and all spans share one re-keyed `trace_id`;
     - (b) the same request and salt, re-keyed twice, gives byte-equal results;
     - (c) two distinct salts on the same request give `(trace_id, span_id)` sets with an empty intersection;
     - (d) blanking the three id fields (and links) of the original and of the re-keyed request yields byte-equal
       encoded messages, so no content byte moved; use an `exception_trace_request` so the exception event and
       fingerprint attribute are covered;
     - (e) an empty `parent_span_id` stays empty.

2. **Export it** — in `crates/conductor-emit/src/lib.rs`, add `mod identity;` and
   `pub use identity::rekey_trace_identity;` beside the existing re-exports. Add no dependency: `rand_chacha` and
   `opentelemetry-proto` are already this crate's.

3. **The dispatcher carries the salt** — in `crates/conductor-run/src/dispatch.rs`:
   - Change `Dispatcher::connect(scenario, endpoint)` to `connect(scenario, endpoint, identity_salt: Option<u64>)`.
     The field is held on the struct.
   - Route every TRACE export in `dispatch` through one private helper. When the salt is `Some`, it calls
     `rekey_trace_identity` on the request just before `self.traces.export`. The trace-emitting shapes are
     Plain/Traces, Error, Exception, Latency, Pii/Traces, Ramp and Topology.
   - Leave the logs path untouched: Pulse keys logs on a timestamp + `seq` (Pulse `schema.rs:82`), so logs cannot
     replay.
   - The doc comments state the two tiers. `None` means seed-pure identity, the tier the `dispatch_wire__*`
     goldens pin. `Some` means per-execution identity, the production path.
   - Leave `emission_seed` and the per-slot seed fed to builders unchanged, so content stays seed-pure
     (`pii_harvest.rs:104-119` re-derives the PII corpus from it).

4. **Production passes a per-execution salt** — in `crates/conductor-run/src/execute.rs`, `execute_scenario` passes
   `Some(emitted_ms as u64)` to `Dispatcher::connect` (`execute.rs:88`). `emitted_ms` is the existing `now_ms()` read
   at `execute.rs:85`, from `std::time`. Add a one-line comment citing the canary's `now_ms()` base
   (`canary.rs:294`) and the Pulse key. Do not change the signature of `execute_scenario`; its callers are
   `commands/run.rs:23`, `commands/suite.rs:32` and `drive.rs:80`, settled by grep because the async fn has no graph
   symbol.

5. **The CI proof** — in `crates/conductor-run/tests/dispatch_wire.rs`:
   - The `drive_scenario!` macro passes `None`, so every existing test and the three goldens are unchanged.
   - Add a salted twin, `drive_scenario_salted!(scenario, salt)` or an extra macro arm, that passes `Some(salt)`.
   - Add the test `two_same_seed_drives_inside_one_window_share_no_span_identity`. Use one scenario whose phases
     cover an Exception phase (the d2 shape, `occurrences = 5`) and an Error phase with depth ≥ 1, so linkage is
     exercised. Drive it twice with the same seed and two distinct salts. Assert:
     - (i) the union of `(trace_id, span_id)` pairs across both drives has exactly `|A| + |B|` members (Pulse's
       key, `schema.rs:36`), with `|A| = |B| > 0`;
     - (ii) both drives carry the same span count and the same exception fingerprint attribute values in the same
       order (content unchanged);
     - (iii) every child `parent_span_id` in drive B names a `span_id` present in drive B;
     - (iv) the same salt twice reproduces identical identity.
   - Before the final green, /implement shows the test RED with step 3's re-key call removed and records that
     reading in `evidence/revert-red.md`. This is the "fails when the fix is reverted" witness.

6. **The live witness binary** — create `crates/conductor-run/tests/span_landing_live.rs`.
   - Gate it on `#![cfg(feature = "live-pulse")]` and add `mod capture_paths;`. It is auto-discovered like
     `real_model_live.rs`, so it needs no Cargo.toml edit.
   - It drives nothing. It reads:
     - (a) `runs/live-suite/span-a.jsonl` and `span-b.jsonl`, resolved through
       `capture_paths::runs_dir_from(&workspace_root(), CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR)`;
     - (b) every file named `agent-latest.jsonl*` under `capture_paths::pulse_logs_dir_from(ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR)`.
   - From each journal it takes the single `run_id` it carries and the `timestamp_ms` of its ONE `timeline.execute`
     span-`new` line. That is the scenario's emission instant; the canary's `emit.batch` lines precede it.
   - From Pulse's lines (JSON, `target` + `fields` + ISO `timestamp`) it takes:
     - the count of `target == "duckdb.append"` lines carrying `fields.reject_reason`;
     - the LAST `buffer.tick` `fields.append_rejections`;
     - the LAST `buffer.tick` `fields.retention_window_seconds`, which must be present;
     - the count of `duckdb.append` lines with `fields.table_name == "spans"` stamped at or after drive B's
       instant.
   - Parse the ISO stamp to epoch ms by hand (full date + time, so a UTC date change cannot fold), as
     `live_suite.rs:111` does for its own parse.
   - Pass iff: 2 distinct run_ids; `0 < Δ = tB − tA < retention_window_seconds × 1000`; `reject_lines == 0`;
     `append_rejections == 0`; `spans_after_b ≥ 1`.
   - Print exactly one summary line: `span-landing: PASS run_ids=2 delta_ms=N retention_ms=N reject_lines=0
     append_rejections=0 spans_after_b=N` (each N an integer). On failure, panic with the same field set and the word `FAIL`.
   - It prints counts and integers only, never a Pulse line, a path or a fingerprint, so nothing it emits needs the
     capture scrub chain. Every guard rejection keeps `capture_paths`' path-free text.

7. **Operator pass, the slot** — on the operator's word and inside their `:4317` grant. First take the pre-launch
   census (`[[gate]]` census entry). Then verify both binaries' sha256 against the 2026-10-01 ledger
   (`attempt-ledger.md:25-26` there). A mismatch means STOP and ask: nothing rebuilds, since the Pulse tree is
   pulse-builder-busy and a build needs the operator's separate word.

8. **Launch** — the agent may launch `pulse-app` on the operator's word, per the standing recipe (memory
   `agent-may-launch-pulse-app-when-directed`; verification-harness.md:50-53).
   - Use a Write-tool `.ps1` in the scratchpad, ASCII only (host-win32.md 2026-09-30), run by path.
   - It calls `Start-Process` without `-Wait`. The fresh letters-only data dir `%TEMP%/pulse-legs/spanlanding` is
     also the cwd.
   - Set `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC=true` and `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MCP_ENABLED=true`. Remove
     `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_BASELINE_BOOTSTRAP_SECONDS` and `RUST_LOG`.
   - Confirm the posture from Pulse's own log before any drive: `interpretation.model.load` `inference_mode:
     deterministic`, `app.boot.workspace_key` basename `spanlanding`, `app.boot.otlp.grpc.bind` `127.0.0.1:4317`,
     and no bootstrap-override line.
   - Record the PID and UTC CreationDate.

9. **Drive A** — run the non-priming `preconditions` probe, then drive A, then the freeze to
   `runs/live-suite/span-a.jsonl`. Never run `boot` first (verification-harness.md:53).

10. **Quiet window** — at least 180 s after drive A ends: Pulse's 120 s idle plus a 30 s resolver tick plus margin
    (verification-harness.md:50; the posture contract's 150 s). This keeps drive B's preflight canary from deduping
    against A's open incident. It stays well inside the 600 s retention, and the witness asserts that rather than
    assumes it.
11. **Drive B** — the probe, drive B, then the freeze to `span-b.jsonl`.

12. **Witness** — run step 6's binary against the live data dir and record its summary line in
    `evidence/witness-ledger.md`. A witness that FAILs only on `Δ ≥ retention` is a harness-timing fault: the leg ran
    too slowly to be inside the window. It is re-fired once from step 9 on a new slot, never graded as a landing
    result (verification-harness.md 2026-09-30 re-fire rule). Any other FAIL is the result.

13. **Teardown** — stop `pulse-app` by PID AND CreationDate (`CloseMainWindow`, then `Stop-Process -Force`). Take the
    after-census by parentage. Confirm `:4317` has no listener.
14. **Mint-then-read** — `status` on drive B's run_id.
- `crates/conductor-emit/src/identity.rs` — `rekey_trace_identity` + unit tests (step 1).
- `crates/conductor-run/tests/span_landing_live.rs` — the operator-gated live witness (step 6).

- `conductor-0.3.0/chunks/2026-10-01-per-run-span-identity-in-the-real-model-harness/evidence/revert-red.md` — step
  5's red-with-the-re-key-removed reading.

- `conductor-0.3.0/chunks/2026-10-01-per-run-span-identity-in-the-real-model-harness/evidence/witness-ledger.md` —
  steps 7-15's operator-pass record.
- `crates/conductor-emit/src/lib.rs` — the module + re-export (step 2).

- `crates/conductor-run/src/dispatch.rs` — `connect` gains `identity_salt: Option<u64>`; trace exports re-keyed when
  `Some` (step 3). Impact: `Dispatcher::connect` @ `execute.rs:88` (graph) and `dispatch_wire.rs:130` (grep, the
  macro) — the only two call sites.
- `crates/conductor-run/src/execute.rs` — `Some(emitted_ms as u64)` at the connect site (step 4).

- `crates/conductor-run/tests/dispatch_wire.rs` — `None` in the existing macro; the salted twin + the two-drive test
  (step 5).

The gates below run in /implement P2 and the wrap light gate, except those marked `leg = 'operator'`, which the
operator pass fires once, in order (steps 7-15). The live witness has no harness verb (it mints no `agent-run` verb
or selector — arch §Occupied Resources, layout-templates §cli Primary screens), so its leg entries invoke `conductor`
and the witness test binary directly in their firing form. The non-priming liveness probe preceding each drive is
`conductor preconditions`, never `boot`. `pulse-app` is booted for the leg on the operator's word and stopped by the
agent at step 13 (named in each leg's `note`).

One control MUTATES source, so it is not an entry: step 5's red-before-green run. /implement removes the re-key call
from `dispatch.rs` ONCE, records the two-drive test's RED reading, restores the call and records the GREEN reading,
both in `evidence/revert-red.md`. The light gate re-runs the non-mutating `dispatch_wire` entries, which guard the
property thereafter.

body:
- (tests/arch) `rekey_trace_identity` is a per-salt bijection that preserves linkage and moves no content byte.
  Step 1's five unit tests prove it: `cargo nextest run -p conductor-emit --profile ci` and `cargo test -p
  conductor-emit` both green (per test-plan §4; arch §Established Decisions [Determinism RNG]).

- (tests) Two same-seed drives through the real `Dispatcher` with two distinct salts share no `(trace_id, span_id)`
  pair (union = |A| + |B|, Pulse's key `schema.rs:36` at `a2addb3`), with equal span counts and fingerprint
  sequences, intact linkage, and same-salt reproducibility. Held by
  `two_same_seed_drives_inside_one_window_share_no_span_identity` in `cargo nextest run -p conductor-run --test
  dispatch_wire --profile ci`, and shown RED with the re-key removed (`evidence/revert-red.md`) (per test-plan §8
  What to mock → OTLP/gRPC egress).

- (tests/arch) The dispatcher tier stays seed-pure. `the_same_seed_reproduces_the_same_stream` is green and
  unchanged, and every committed golden is byte-unchanged:
  `git diff --numstat 2c97d3b -- crates/conductor-run/tests/snapshots/ crates/conductor-timeline/tests/snapshots/`
  prints nothing (per test-plan §7 Golden artifacts; arch §Cross-cutting Patterns → Determinism discipline).

- (obs) The primitive raises no span, attribute or log line (`grep -c "tracing::" …/identity.rs` → 0), and no product
  identity value reaches a self-obs line (per obs-plan §11 Spans / Traces; §6 Boundary-call wrappers).

- (tests/live) In the operator pass, against one deterministic-posture `pulse-app` on the sha256-verified `a2addb3`
  binaries, two `conductor run exception-event-capture` drives at the same seed both print a verdict line without
  `[BLOCKED]`. The live witness prints `span-landing: PASS run_ids=2 … reject_lines=0 append_rejections=0
  spans_after_b=N` with N ≥ 1, with `delta_ms` below Pulse's own logged `retention_window_seconds × 1000`. That is both drives
  landing inside one buffer window, measured at the SUT, and it proves the production `execute_scenario` → salt
  wiring CI cannot reach (per test-plan §6, §2; verification-harness.md:50-53).

- (tests) `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci` green with zero retries, and doc tests, workspace clippy and
  `cargo fmt --all --check` all green (per test-plan §10).

- (security) The committed evidence carries no host path (the evidence probe reads 0), and `gate.py hygiene` reads
  clean before the pre-CI commit (per security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Logging).

- (ci) After the operator's pre-CI commit and push, `ci.py conclusion --sha HEAD --wait 1500` reads `verdict: green`
  on the pushed HEAD. The acceptance names that run id.

- No verification-matrix capability is claimed: the pool holds 0 unclaimed (`matrix.py show --unclaimed`), and
  `v3-09` stays `deferred` with its next step the founder's.

- History leaned on: arch 2026-08-15-canary-spans-pulse-fingerprints (the per-call identity fix, seed-pure across
  runs); 2026-06-27-live-pulse-e2e-proof (canary unique per run); tests 2026-08-13-dispatcher-determinism-goldens;
  obs 2026-08-14-canary-fingerprint-feed-capture (the witness counts MISSING ids, never repeated ones); security
  2026-09-23 capture-path guards.

- **Shape (b), a measured minimum gap between same-seed drives, is rejected.**
  - A refused row clears only at eviction, 600 s retention plus a 100 s sweep (Pulse `retention.rs:41-51`,
    `contract.rs:109`; d1 evicted 19:48-19:51Z). Every same-seed drive would wait ≥ 700 s, and the gap would ride a
    Pulse launch setting Conductor cannot read.
  - It leaves the deterministic `--live` legs with the same replay.

  `seed = emission_seed(self.scenario.seed, index, point.occurrence)` (:78) and hands that ONE seed to every span

  drives of the same scenario + seed. That is the d2 replay.

  seeds derive from `base = now_ms() as u64` (:294), and the marker is `ConductorCanary_{now_ms()}` (:285). This is why
  d2's canary landed and the scenario did not.

- `crates/conductor-run/tests/lifecycle_live.rs` (37, 78-80) — a second in-tree precedent: the live lifecycle test seeds
  its storm from `canary_storm_seed(now_nanos() as u64, tick)`.

  `run_timeline_with` + `Dispatcher` path (`drive_scenario!`, :124-142). `the_same_seed_reproduces_the_same_stream`
  (:437-472) ASSERTS identical `(trace_id, span_id)` across two same-seed drives. `SpanShape` (:66-90) carries
  `trace_id`/`span_id`/`parent_span_id` hex, so the three `dispatch_wire__*` goldens pin identity bytes.

- `crates/conductor-run/tests/pii_harvest.rs` (20, 104-119) — the live PII harvest RE-COMPUTES each slot's corpus from
  a transcription of `emission_seed` (`leg_emission_seed`). The PII content is a function of the same per-slot seed
  that identity is.

- `crates/conductor-run/tests/canary_wire.rs` (10-14, 105-199) — the in-repo statement of Pulse's span-store key and
  the distinct-identity assertions the canary already carries.

- `crates/conductor-emit/src/client.rs` (48-110) — `TraceEmitter::export` carries the `emit.batch` span and the
  wire-shape witness (`spans_missing_ids`). By construction it counts MISSING ids, never repeated ones.

- `crates/conductor-emit/src/span_tree.rs` (35-90) — `gen_id` (:86-90) is `pub(crate)`. `error_trace_request` links
  children by `parent_span_id` within one trace.
- `crates/conductor-emit/src/lib.rs` (12-36) — module list and re-exports.

- `scripts/agent-run.sh` (82, 157-209) — both live legs run `conductor run <scenario> --agent-mode`, so they go through
  `execute_scenario`. `--live real-model` is one leg per invocation.

- `contracts/pulse-real-model-leg-posture.md` (272, 362, 461) — the quiet window between drives is ≥ 150 s after the
  last incident. Below Pulse's retention, so it cannot separate same-seed drives on its own.

- **Pulse (SUT, read-only) at `a2addb3755b3029cb79809b96efdd2522749b179`** (`git rev-parse HEAD` in the Pulse tree;
  its worktree carries only `.andromeda`/handoff bookkeeping modifications, no source edits):
  - `crates/buffer/src/schema.rs:36` — `spans` `PRIMARY KEY (trace_id, span_id)`. `:52` — `span_events`

  - `crates/buffer/src/consumer.rs:60-91` — a dispatch error → `state.record_append_rejection()` + `tracing::error!`

  - `crates/buffer/src/appender.rs:990-1030` — Pulse's own test
    `append_after_a_constraint_violating_flush_returns_instead_of_hanging`: "a producer restart replays span identities
    already stored, so the composite PK rejects the batch at `flush()`". It asserts "a replayed identity must be
    rejected". The WHOLE batch is rejected, not just the duplicate row.
  - `crates/buffer/src/retention.rs:36-51` + `contract.rs:109` — retention window 600 s by default, sweep cadence

data.head: ## Folded freight (from the entry — hypotheses, re-verified at fold time where a coordinate is named)

body:
- **EVIDENCE (verbatim):** measured at `2026-10-01-interpretation-re-proven-after-the-incident-surfacing-fix` d2 —
  Conductor's exception span identity is a pure function of the scenario seed
  (`crates/conductor-emit/src/exception.rs:177-187`, seed 4317033); d2's scenario emission came ~7 min after d1's
  while Pulse still buffered d1's rows, and all 36 of its appends were refused (`duckdb.append`
  `reject_reason=append_failed`, `buffer.tick` `append_rejections` 36); Pulse evicted d1's rows 19:48-19:51Z and d3
  landed (that chunk's `evidence/attempt-ledger.md`).
  - Coordinates re-verified at fold: `exception_trace_request` sits at `exception.rs:176-187` at `2c97d3b` and seeds
    `ChaCha8Rng::seed_from_u64(seed)` for `trace_id`/`span_id`; `seed = 4317033` is
    `scenarios/real-model-interpretation.toml:42`; the d2 row of `attempt-ledger.md:85` carries the 36 refusals and
    the eviction window.

- **Mechanism claim (measured-marked in the freight, kept verbatim; VERIFIED at P3):** "the scenario's span identity is a
  deterministic function of its seed (`crates/conductor-emit/src/exception.rs` `exception_trace_request`), so d2
  re-sent d1's `(trace_id, span_id)` while Pulse's buffer still held d1's rows (evicted 19:48-19:51Z)". Re-derived:
  Conductor side `dispatch.rs:78` `emission_seed(scenario.seed, phase, occurrence)` → `exception.rs:185-187`;
  Pulse `a2addb3` side `spans` `PRIMARY KEY (trace_id, span_id)` (`buffer/src/schema.rs:36`), a replayed identity
  rejects the whole batch at flush (Pulse's own test `appender.rs:996`), logged as `duckdb.append`
  `reject_reason=append_failed` + `append_rejections` (`consumer.rs:78-84,272`); retention 600 s default with a 100 s
  sweep (`retention.rs:41-51`, `contract.rs:109`) explains the 19:48-19:51Z eviction (research.md).

- **CONTEXT (verbatim):** the fix makes each drive's identity unique, or enforces a measured minimum gap, with a test
  that two same-seed drives inside one buffer window both land (operator relay
  `conductor-wrap-v309third-2026-10-01` §2, entry 1).

- The emission's SHAPE stays a function of scenario + seed (the "determinism is the bar" invariant: same
  scenario+seed ⇒ same stream shape). VERIFIED with its open half resolved: the architecture's prose names timing
  as the seeded shape, but committed tests pin span IDENTITY at the dispatcher tier —
  `dispatch_wire.rs:437-472` asserts identical `(trace_id, span_id)` across two same-seed drives and the three
  `dispatch_wire__*` goldens carry identity hex (`dispatch_wire.rs:66-90`). So a dispatcher driven without a
  run-scoped input must keep its identity bytes; any per-run identity enters only on the production path.

- The d2 canary spans surfaced while the scenario's were refused. VERIFIED: the canary's identity base is the wall
  clock — `base = now_ms()` (`canary.rs:294`), marker `ConductorCanary_{now_ms()}` (`canary.rs:285`); the live
  lifecycle test does the same (`lifecycle_live.rs:80`). That is the in-tree precedent for shape (a).

- [premise-corrected: identity replay is not exception-only, and content shares the seed — `gen_id` 17 sites over 7
  emit modules; `pii_harvest.rs:104-119` re-derives the PII corpus from the same per-slot seed] The replay applies to
  EVERY span the dispatcher emits (`trace_request` · `error_trace_request` · `exception_trace_request` · latency ·
  pii · rate · topology), all drawn from `emission_seed`; and that one seed also draws CONTENT (the PII corpus a
  live harvest re-computes, latency durations, rate counts). So the fix changes span identity only — never the seed
  content is drawn from — and reaches every scenario on the production path (`execute_scenario`, which both live
  legs and the GUI funnel through), deterministic and real-model alike. Logs and metrics are untouched: Pulse keys
  them on a timestamp + `seq` (`schema.rs:66,82`), so they cannot replay this way.
- No Pulse change — Pulse is the SUT. Reading Pulse's source on disk is in scope; building it is not without asking.
- No new real-model series and no `v3-09` re-grade in this chunk — `v3-09`'s next step awaits the founder (handoff).

2026-10-02 («ничего не переносим»: the d3 residual is fixed, not ratified). After this chunk, security-plan's clause

**This plan quotes neither residual value, and no artifact this chunk writes may.** Every value-bearing check
extracts the two values from the two sites at the chunk base `31f9d92` and prints only paths or counts. The
procedure is the same as scope.md §Census's derivation.

1. **Red first: write the new capture arm against the untouched files.**
   - In `crates/conductor-run/tests/real_model_harvest.rs`, add a helper `un_elided_keyed_values(text) -> usize`:
     - it counts the `fingerprint_hex=` occurrences whose value is not the `<fingerprint>` placeholder;

    its anti-vacuity entry's `last line 2`.

    Protection; the P4 subject answer).

- (security) `elide_fingerprints` elides a `fingerprint_hex=` value whatever its character class. It leaves
  `<fingerprint>` and an empty value unchanged, and keeps unkeyed all-digit runs.
  - Proven by the extended `a_fingerprint_is_elided_and_a_stamp_a_seed_and_a_det_prefix_are_not`.
  - The scrub-order arms (`the_later_scrub_stages_leave_the_placeholder_intact`,

- (tests) The inverse control `un_elided_keyed_values_counts_a_planted_value` is green. Its planted value is built at
  test time, never committed (per security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Data Protection, the inverse-control
  precedent; testing.md 2026-09-09 as extended 2026-09-12).

- (tests) The graded 2026-10-01 d3 capture is re-elided on exactly its two keyed-value lines (the numstat entry's
  `last line 2` covers it with the frozen file).
  - Its `SERIES_2026_10_01` pin is moved in the same change.
  - The 2026-10-01 digest, rule-record and graded-outcome tests stay green with the d3 grade unchanged (per test-plan
    §6 Real-model interpretation leg; arch §Established Decisions [Probabilistic-Assertion Policy]).

- (tests) `the_2026_10_01_captures_carry_no_fingerprint_and_no_workspace_key` asserts zero all-digit keyed values for
  every drive. The d3 exception is gone (per test-plan §11 Unit: an observable property, never a re-pinned count).

- (security) The frozen 2026-09-22 capture is elided in place.
  - It is byte-identical to the graded copy (the `cmp` entry) and changed on exactly two lines.
  - `the_frozen_capture_is_elided_in_place_and_equals_the_graded_copy` is green.
  - The exception to "frozen evidence is never edited" is recorded against the founder's 2026-10-02 ruling in
    `evidence/census.md` (per security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Data Protection; the overseer's P4 note).

- (security) The five records quoting the frozen value change by in-place line replacements only (the numstat entry's
  `last line 5`), and both edited gate trails still parse as JSON.

- (tests) `cargo test -p conductor-run`, `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci`, `cargo test --workspace --doc`,
  both clippy entries and `cargo fmt --all --check` are green (per test-plan §4 Framework; §10 Quality Gates).

  --numstat 31f9d92` entry: no output), and `Cargo.lock` holds 562 packages (per arch §Occupied Resources; arch §Stack

  posture; §11).

- (security) `cargo audit` and `cargo deny check advisories bans licenses sources` are green over the unchanged
  lockfile, behind an empty advisory-db porcelain (per security-plan §Dependency Security).

- (ci) The operator pass's `ci.py conclusion --sha HEAD --wait 1200` reads `verdict: green` on the pushed pre-CI
