data.head: # Plan — 2026-10-02-p-075-assert-round-against-pulse: "The P-075 assert round against Pulse"

body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._

- **Marker:** 2026-10-02-p-075-assert-round-against-pulse · **Version:** conductor-0.3.0 · **Generated:**
  2026-10-02T04:55Z

Run ONE deterministic round against Pulse's returned build, S = `03ec94481b0d6c3ba574626e7acb39e33fd40141`. Grade the
six assertions in Pulse's `round-request.md` hard, at their measured values. The six are:
1. read-back content fidelity;
2. runtime-state fidelity;

Each lands as PASS, FAIL or UNGRADED (an absent sample), never re-driven for a pass. The posture is round-request
§Grading posture; arch §Established Decisions [Probabilistic-Assertion Policy] and [Timing-Tolerance Model]; and
obs-plan §4, the Delegated-timing family.
The round re-uses what the 2026-08-31 round and the delegated-timing work shipped:
- `probe_resolve_lifecycle` / `attribute_by_liveness` (`crates/conductor-run/src/lifecycle.rs:72-130`);
- `bounds` / `grade` / `grade_in_window` (`crates/conductor-run/tests/delegated_timing_harvest.rs:63-288`).
It builds only what no shipped code does:
- a live leg that stamps a storm's emission instant;
- reads that incident's `fingerprint_refs` and `degraded_mode`;
- resolves it by liveness.

Conductor-side graders produce STABLE test ids over a COMMITTED, digest-pinned evidence tree, which Pulse's `ref`
cites. Every grade happens at the test/harvest tier: no `Verdict`/`ReportState` variant, envelope key, `classify()`
change, verb or selector is added (arch §Established Decisions [Probabilistic-Assertion Policy]; layout-templates
§cli Primary screens).
The chunk also carries the overseer-ruled span-landing CARRY:
- the witness inputs `span-{a,b}.jsonl` move off the harness-owned `runs/live-suite/` into their own `runs/span-landing/`;
- a named-file, non-recursive clear runs before drive A;
- the witness refuses a pair older than the live Pulse's log, so a stale pair can never be graded.
Per the operator's P4 answers:
- the round drives all four delegated scenarios for per-scenario attribution;
- the CARRY is proven hermetically.

1. **Re-pin the P-025 contract at S, add-only** — `contracts/pulse-p025-measurement-contract.md`.
   - Append a dated clause per moved coordinate, recording each Pulse coordinate re-read at S:
     - the hue emit `crates/ui-bridge/src/telemetry.rs:278-282` → `:316-320`;
     - the allowlist `pulse-app/src/observability.rs:989-992` → `:992-995`;
     - `ServiceListItem` `crates/triage/src/lifecycle/registry.rs:54-69` → `:56-71`, field at `:70`.
   - State that the formula, the one-sample-per-witnessed-change rule and the 60 000 clamp hold at S, and that
     `xtask/src/hue_shift.rs:41` is unchanged (research.md §Pulse at S, Q5).
   - Edit no existing clause, and leave §The grading rule byte-unchanged (arch-history
     2026-09-18-real-model-leg-posture-and-grading-rule: per-clause provenance, add-only re-pins).

2. **New feature-gated live leg** — `crates/conductor-run/tests/p075_round_live.rs`, `#![cfg(feature = "live-pulse")]`,
   one `#[tokio::test(flavor = "current_thread")]` fn `p075_round_live_leg`.
   - Model it on `lifecycle_live.rs`:
     - `ReadbackClient::connect` with `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR`;
     - `TraceEmitter::connect(DEFAULT_OTLP_ENDPOINT)`;
     - an `active_ids` reader accepting `incident_id` then `id`;
     - the 10 s poll with a keep-alive, at most 40 ticks.
   - In order:
     - (a) Read the active set and record its size as `active_at_open`.
     - (b) Take `emitted_unix_nano` from `std::time::SystemTime`. Then build `canary_spec(&marker)` with
       `marker = format!("ConductorP075_{ms}")`, compute `conductor_emit::fingerprint(&spec)`, and
       `emit_canary_storm(…, base = emitted nanos)`.
     - (c) Poll until an active incident's `opened_at_unix_nano` exceeds `emitted_unix_nano`.
     - (d) For that incident, call `retrieve_telemetry_slice({"incident_id": id})` and
       `retrieve_report({"incident_id": id})`.
     - (e) Keep-alive once, stamp an `Instant`, then `probe_resolve_lifecycle(&client, id)` and
       `attribute_by_liveness`.
   - Raw wire values go to STDERR only, never stdout (the raw-dump rule; their titles are corpus text).
   - STDOUT is ONE buffered write: a leading newline, then exactly these lines, in this order. Every value is an
     integer, a boolean, a closed word or `absent`:
     ```text
     p075-round: active_at_open=<n>
     p075-round: incident_id=<i64|none> opened_after_emission=<true|false|absent> opened_minus_emitted_ms=<i64|absent>
     p075-round: fingerprint_refs=<n> det_members=<n> fingerprint_in_refs=<true|false|absent>
     p075-round: degraded_mode=<true|false|absent>
     p075-round: resolve_before=<n> resolved_left_active_set=<true|false|absent> idle_ms=<i64|absent> verdict=<ProvenByLiveness|StillActive|NoControl|Unattributable|absent>
     p075-round: end
     ```
     - `det_members` counts refs beginning `det-`.
     - `Unattributable` is the arm `attribute_by_liveness` returns at or over the 120 s idle threshold
       (`crates/conductor-run/src/lifecycle.rs:82-86`). The variant name is printed without its payload.
     - When no incident forms within the window, the later fields print `none`/`absent` and the leg still exits 0.
       It is a producer, not a grader.
   - It prints NO hex, title, path or workspace key. The 32-hex value is compared in-process and only the boolean
     leaves the process (security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Data Protection; security-history
     2026-10-01-interpretation-re-proven-after-the-incident-surfacing-fix).

3. **Shared digest-pin helper** — `crates/conductor-run/tests/evidence_pin/mod.rs`, a `tests/` subdirectory module
   like `capture_paths` (never its own target).
   - It holds `committed(name)` (workspace-root anchored, LF-normalized), `sha256_hex`, `check_digest` and
     `pinned(name, sha256)`. They are transcribed from `real_model_harvest.rs:1530-1567`, whose copy is left
     untouched.
   - Errors name the repo-relative file and both digests, never the text (2026-09-30 regime).

4. **Assertions 1–2 graders** — `crates/conductor-run/tests/lifecycle_harvest.rs` gains a round section using
   `mod evidence_pin;`.
   - A `ROUND_CAPTURE` path is pinned to `evidence/p075-leg.txt` with its sha256. A pure `round_fields(&str) ->
     HashMap` parses the `p075-round:` lines.
   - The pure grade: `enum RoundGrade { Pass, Fail(String), Ungraded(String) }`.
     - **Assertion 1:**
       - UNGRADED when `active_at_open > 0` (a storm deduping into an open incident never reaches
         `fingerprint_refs`, Pulse `inference_runtime.rs:830-858`), when `incident_id=none`, or when any of its
         three fields is `absent`;
       - otherwise PASS iff `fingerprint_in_refs=true` ∧ `opened_after_emission=true` ∧ `degraded_mode=false`;
       - otherwise FAIL naming the false field(s).
     - **Assertion 2:**
       - PASS iff `verdict=ProvenByLiveness` ∧ `resolved_left_active_set=true`;
       - UNGRADED on `NoControl`/`absent`;
       - otherwise FAIL naming the verdict.
   - Tests:
     - `p075_round_assertion_1_read_back_content_fidelity` and `p075_round_assertion_2_runtime_state_fidelity`
       assert the grade the committed capture MEASURES. Whichever arm it lands in is the one written; nobody
       re-judges.
     - `p075_round_capture_digest_pin_fails_on_a_tampered_byte` mutates one byte in memory and asserts
       `check_digest` errs.
     - Synthetic arms cover each grade branch, including the dedupe-precondition UNGRADED and a `degraded_mode=true`
       FAIL.

5. **Assertions 3–6 graders** — `crates/conductor-run/tests/delegated_timing_harvest.rs` gains a round section using
   `mod evidence_pin;` and the EXISTING `bounds()`/`grade`/`grade_in_window`/`tiered_hue_samples_in_window`/
   `incident_anchor_error_ms`.
   - Committed inputs, each digest-pinned:
     - `evidence/h.jsonl` — leg H's frozen self-obs;
     - `evidence/pulse-h.jsonl`, `pulse-d.jsonl`, `pulse-r.jsonl`, `pulse-f.jsonl` — one target-filtered Pulse
       slice per leg.
   - Tests:
     - `p075_round_assertion_3_p025_hue_update`: `grade_in_window` over `pulse-h.jsonl`. The window is derived
       from `h.jsonl` by the contract's §The grading rule: the one `timeline.execute` `new` + `healthy-baseline`'s
       30 000 ms, through `scenario.run` close. Every in-window non-`none` rise has an anchor error ≤ 1 000 ms.
     - `p075_round_assertion_4_p027_discovery`: `grade` over `pulse-d.jsonl`.
     - `p075_round_assertion_5_p037_report_render`: `grade` over `pulse-r.jsonl`, reading `value`.
     - `p075_round_assertion_6_p045_counter_refresh`: `grade` over `pulse-f.jsonl`.
     - `p075_round_slices_digest_pin_fails_on_a_tampered_byte`.
   - Each grade test asserts what the slice MEASURED: `Ok(worst)`, or the `Err` text carrying the value or the
     UNGRADED reason.

6. **The span-landing CARRY** — `crates/conductor-run/tests/span_landing_live.rs`.
   - `drive()` reads `runs_dir.join("span-landing").join("span-{leg}.jsonl")`. Error text names
     `span-landing/span-{leg}.jsonl`, never a resolved path.
   - Add a pure `fn pair_is_current(a_ms, b_ms, pulse_first_ms, pulse_last_ms) -> Result<(), String>`. It refuses
     unless `pulse_first_ms ≤ a_ms < b_ms ≤ pulse_last_ms`, naming which bound failed, integers only.
   - Call it in `both_same_seed_drives_land_inside_one_retention_window` before grading. A refused pair panics
     `span-landing: FAIL stale pair …` and is never graded.
   - Rewrite the FIRING FORM doc. Before drive A run `rm -f runs/span-landing/span-a.jsonl
     runs/span-landing/span-b.jsonl`: two NAMED files, non-recursive, no handle expansion (security.md 2026-09-06).
     The freezes become `mkdir -p runs/span-landing && cp logs/agent-latest.jsonl runs/span-landing/span-{a,b}.jsonl`.
   - The guard covers a skipped clear and a `CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR` that differs from the literal `runs/`.
   - Add three hermetic `#[test]` arms in the same gated file:
     - `the_span_pair_resolves_under_its_own_subdir` — resolves via `capture_paths::runs_dir_from` with an unset
       handle and asserts the `span-landing` component;
     - `a_pair_older_than_the_live_pulse_log_is_refused`;
     - `a_pair_inside_the_live_pulse_log_is_current`.
   - `scripts/agent-run.{sh,ps1}` are UNCHANGED. The suite's `rm -f "$LIVE_CAPTURE_DIR"/*.jsonl`
     (`agent-run.sh:106`) is a non-recursive glob, so it can no longer reach the moved pair.

7. **The slot ask (to the overseer, before anything live fires).** Say exactly:
   - when the agent will launch `pulse-app` (the moment the slot is granted, `:4317` measured free);
   - that **nobody touches the desktop** from "pulse-app is up" until "round complete". The founder makes NO click.
     The compact widget stays visible, not minimized; that is the boot state (Pulse `main.rs:1134`).
   - **The founder must specifically NOT click a row in Pulse's Findings dropdown.** That dropdown is opened from the
     compact widget's findings-band counter (`CompactWidget.tsx:61,93,107`). A row click (`FindingsWindow.tsx:189-191,
     222`) calls `openReportWindow(id)`, which pins the Report's selection to that incident (`ReportWindow.tsx:23`)
     and suppresses every later `metric.report.render_ms` sample until the Report is closed with its close control
     or Esc (`:26`).
   - With no click, the hidden-at-boot Report webview selects `findings.rows[0]` by itself (`isOpen = effectiveId !==
     null`, `:23,32`). Leg R's own preflight incident then yields its render sample, which is the auto-fire the
     2026-08-21 legs measured (verification-harness.md 2026-08-21).
   - If leg R's slice holds no render sample, P-037 records UNGRADED, said so in the ledger, with no re-drive. The
     agent never automates Pulse's UI.

8. **Launch (agent, on the slot).**
   - Census before.
   - Re-measure both sha256 values; a mismatch STOPS the pass, with no rebuild.
   - Make a fresh data dir `%TEMP%/pulse-legs/assertround`.
   - Launch `target/release/pulse-app.exe` BY PATH via `Start-Process -PassThru` from a cwd outside this repo, with
     `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` = that dir, `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC=true` and
     `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MCP_ENABLED=true`. Record PID + CreationDate.
   - Wait for `:4317` accepting, then report "pulse-app is up — hands off the desktop until 'round complete'".
   - Record the launch posture from Pulse's own log.

10. **Harvest the round into evidence.**
    - Slice Pulse's newest `{data_dir}/logs/agent-latest.jsonl.*` by the recorded pre-leg counts. Leg k's slice is
      `[count_k, count_{k+1})`; F's ends at the post-round count. Note that a UTC date change splits the log
      across two files, both read in order.
    - Write `evidence/pulse-{h,d,r,f}.jsonl` holding ONLY lines whose `target` is one of:
      - the four metric leaves;
      - `interpretation.incident.created`;
      - `triage.incident.auto_resolve.tick` with `resolved_count` ≥ 1.
    - Use a byte-copying filter (binary mode), never a text-mode python write (host-win32.md 2026-09-15).
    - Compute each committed evidence file's LF sha256 and pin it in steps 4–5.
    - Teardown and the census after: stop `pulse-app` by PID + CreationDate, and only the rows the round started
      (host-win32.md 2026-09-17; memory "Stop everything you start").
    - A `Stop-Process -Force` writes no `app.exit` (Pulse `observability.rs:2771-2807`; round-request §The binary
      under test). This is expected, not a finding.

12. **Operator pass** — the status smoke on F's run_id, `gate.py hygiene`, the operator's pre-CI commit
    (`chore(2026-10-02-p-075-assert-round-against-pulse): operator pre-CI commit, for the run this chunk's verdict
    reads`), the guarded push, and the CI read. CI runs the two harvest targets in the default suite over the
    committed evidence.
- `crates/conductor-run/tests/p075_round_live.rs` — step 2's gated live leg.
- `crates/conductor-run/tests/evidence_pin/mod.rs` — step 3's shared digest-pin helper.
- `crates/conductor-run/tests/lifecycle_harvest.rs` — step 4. No existing test's assertion changes.
- `crates/conductor-run/tests/delegated_timing_harvest.rs` — step 5. No existing test's assertion changes.
- `crates/conductor-run/tests/span_landing_live.rs` — step 6.
- `contracts/pulse-p025-measurement-contract.md` — step 1 (add-only).
- **Ordinary gates.** The non-operator gates run in /implement P2 and the wrap light gate.

- **The live block (steps 8–11).** It is the operator's slot, driven by the agent only after the slot is granted and
  the hands-off instruction is relayed (step 7). It is never fired by the gate tool.
  - Its legs are `leg = 'live'`.
  - Its readings (census, hashes, pre-leg counts, freezes, quiet windows, end-line check) are `leg = 'operator'`: one
    point-in-time reading each, recorded in `evidence/round-ledger.md` and never re-run by the wrap. Pulse's binary
    may be rebuilt by another session afterwards.
  - Each leg is preceded by its non-priming `conductor preconditions` probe. There is no `boot` entry anywhere.

- **Launching `pulse-app`** is step 8's agent act on the slot (memory "Agent may launch pulse-app when directed"). It
  is not an entry, and its stop is the agent's at step 10, by PID + CreationDate.

- **Evidence producers.**
  - `evidence/p075-leg.txt` and `evidence/h.jsonl` are produced by entries carrying `artifact`.
  - `pulse-{h,d,r,f}.jsonl` and `round-ledger.md` are hand-authored records written at steps 10–11 from the round's
    outputs. They are slices of the live data dir, which no re-run can reproduce.
  - What re-runs is the two harvest targets, which grade the digest-pinned files.
- **Self-verify:** none. No Conductor UI surface or `ui/dist` input changes.

- **CI:** read by the operator pass. The prior wrap's run took 559 s wall (CI#36946764116, Setup 5a), so
  `--wait 1200` covers it.

- (tests/arch) The round's six grades are produced at the test/harvest tier and are each PASS, FAIL or UNGRADED.
  - Assertions 1–2 are graded in `cargo nextest run -p conductor-run --test lifecycle_harvest --profile ci`
    (`p075_round_assertion_1_read_back_content_fidelity`, `p075_round_assertion_2_runtime_state_fidelity`).
  - Assertions 3–6 are graded in `cargo nextest run -p conductor-run --test delegated_timing_harvest --profile ci`
    (`p075_round_assertion_3_p025_hue_update` … `_6_p045_counter_refresh`).
  - Each test asserts what its committed evidence MEASURED, and green CI on the pushed sha holds them on a clean
    runner.
  - An absent sample is UNGRADED, never PASS (per arch §Established Decisions [Probabilistic-Assertion Policy];
    obs-plan §4 Delegated-timing family).

- (tests) Assertion 1:
  - PASS requires the membership of Conductor's 32-hex `fingerprint(&spec)` in the incident's `fingerprint_refs`,
    plus `opened_after_emission=true` and `degraded_mode=false` read from `retrieve_report`'s result, never passed in.
  - `active_at_open > 0` grades UNGRADED. A dedupe never writes `fingerprint_hashes` (Pulse
    `inference_runtime.rs:830-858`).
  - Synthetic arms cover each branch (per test-plan §6; arch §Established Decisions [Read-Back Dependency Posture]).

- (tests) Assertion 2 grades PASS only on `verdict=ProvenByLiveness` with the resolved id out of the active set, read
  through `probe_resolve_lifecycle` + `attribute_by_liveness` unchanged (per test-plan §5 `mark_incident_resolved`).

- (security/tests) Every committed evidence file is held by an LF sha256 pin and graded only after it matches.
  - A tamper arm per harvest proves the pin can fail.
  - No capture text sits in test source.
  - `grep -cE "[0-9a-f]{16,}" …/evidence/p075-leg.txt` reads 0.
  - The host-path hygiene entry reads 0 over the whole evidence tree.
  - Per security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Data Protection / Logging.

- (tests) The gated lint `cargo clippy -p conductor-run --features live-pulse --all-targets -- -D warnings` exits 0
  (per test-plan §9).

- (security) No dependency is added. `grep -c "^name = " Cargo.lock` reads 562, and `cargo audit` and
  `cargo deny check advisories bans licenses sources` are green after the porcelain probe reads clean (per
  security-plan §Dependency Security).

- (design/layouts) `evidence/round-ledger.md`:
  - renders each graded assertion with a `[PASS]`/`[FAIL]` prefix and each absent sample as the word UNGRADED with
    its reason, with no new label, column, ANSI or emoji;
  - records S, both binary sha256 values, the launch posture, the hands-off instruction,
    both censuses, the teardown, and the graded test ids + evidence path Pulse's `ref` cites (per design-system
    §Anti-Patterns; layout-templates §cli block 2).

- (ops) CI is green on the operator's pushed sha (`ci.py conclusion --sha HEAD --wait 1200` → `verdict: green`, its
  run id named).

- External: Pulse `andromeda-pulse-0.3.0/chunks/2026-10-01-conductor-return/evidence/round-request.md` and
  `round-binary.md` (read-only, cited, never copied); Pulse source at S (research.md §Pulse at S).
- Research files inspected: see research.md §Files inspected.

- A `--live p075` selector or any `scripts/agent-run.{sh,ps1}` edit was rejected. No new verb or selector is needed
  for one round; the 2026-10-01 precedent drives a live witness by direct entries. The `--e2e` shells stay
  byte-identical.

- Committing the 32-hex fingerprint (or the read-back refs) as evidence was rejected. It would open a
  fingerprint-in-evidence question while the founder's ruling on the d3 prefix is PENDING. Membership is computed
  in-process and only the boolean is committed.

- Pinning Pulse lines VERBATIM in test source (the 2026-09-29 shape) was rejected in favour of digest-pinned files
  graded from disk (the 2026-09-30 regime). Pulse's `ref` cites an evidence PATH.

- No automation of Pulse's UI, ever. No human click either: a Findings-row click pins the Report's selection and
  suppresses samples (`ReportWindow.tsx:23`). An empty leg-R slice is UNGRADED and said so.

- REJECTED at P5, the P4 "founder opens the Report window" arm. Its premise (render only while the window is
  visible) misread `useReport(isOpen ? id : null)`, because `isOpen` is `effectiveId !== null`, not visibility. The
  overseer ratified the correction.

- No re-drive for a pass. One re-fire per leg only on a Conductor-side fault or an UNGRADED precondition miss, with
  the first attempt kept.
- No `boot` anywhere. Its canary primes the incident the next leg would dedupe against.
- No Pulse rebuild. A sha256 mismatch stops the pass.

- No change to `lifecycle_live.rs` or to any `crates/*/src`. The prior round's producer and the shipped graders are
  re-used as they stand.

- No live re-witness of span-landing this round (operator P4). Landing was proven live on 2026-10-01, and only the
  input path moves.

- **Basis for "no scenario names P-075":** `grep -ln '"P-075"' scenarios/*.toml` returns no file. P-075 is
  `DriveObserve` at `crates/conductor-core/src/coverage.rs:540-545`.

    empty R slice would be the measurement that it did not, recorded UNGRADED.

data.head: ## Pulse at S (03ec944) — read by an Explore agent, four claims re-verified by hand

body:
Paths are relative to the Pulse repo. The agent's report is condensed below; lines marked **[re-verified]** I read
myself at S.

- **Q1 `fingerprint_refs`:**
  - The source is `incident.evidence_refs.fingerprint_hashes` (`crates/mcp-server/src/tools.rs:439`)
    **[re-verified]**.
  - Its only writer is incident CREATION. `grounded_fingerprint_hashes` (`pulse-app/src/inference_runtime.rs:657-666`)
    **[re-verified]** produces an order-preserving union: the model's refs, then the triggering cue's full-hex
    fingerprint.
  - Under deterministic L4 the refs are the three `det-*` constants (`deterministic_inference.rs:68-72`), so the
    expected shape is `[det-span-…, det-template-0007, det-fingerprint-…, <cue fp>]`.
  - Width: 32 lowercase hex (`triage/src/pattern/storm.rs:323-326`, `contract.rs:165-171`).
  - Derivation: `compute_exception_fingerprint` (`crates/buffer/src/fingerprint.rs:79-96`) **[re-verified]**,
    equal to Conductor's `fingerprint()`. `git log 83d4060..03ec944 -- crates/buffer/src/fingerprint.rs` → 0 commits.
  - **A dedupe re-emission does NOT update `fingerprint_hashes`** (`inference_runtime.rs:830-858`). A storm that
    dedupes into an already-open incident therefore never reaches `fingerprint_refs`.

- **Q2 `degraded_mode`:**
  - `degraded_mode = parsed_l4.is_none()` over `resolution_summary_text` (`tools.rs:377-381`) **[re-verified]**.
    Arity is one `incident_id`.
  - At S, `resolution_summary_text = scrubbed_l4_json(parsed)` (`inference_runtime.rs:906`). Since `9d14166` it
    masks per LEAF (`:675-688`), so the canned L4 output stays parseable, which gives **`degraded_mode: false` under
    deterministic L4**.
  - Before `9d14166`, a whole-string scrub could collapse it, which gave degraded `true`. This is why every
    2026-08-21 render sample reads `degraded_mode: true`.

- **Q3 lifecycle:**
  - Applied response: `{"resolved":true,"incident_id":<id>}` (`tools.rs:477`).
  - Items key: `incident_id`. `query_incident_list` takes no arguments and returns `status != 'resolved'`
    (corpus `contract.rs:692-698`).
  - Auto-resolve: 120 s idle, a 30 s resolver tick that skips its first tick.
  - Dedupe tuple: `(kind, scope, scope_id)`, with the fingerprint excluded.
  - Unchanged since `83d4060`.
  - **New hazard named by source:** the app's in-memory registry learns of an MCP resolve only in the 60 s
    persist-cycle reconcile (`triage/src/incident/persistence.rs:250-283`). An app-side re-emission persist landing
    first can re-write the row `active`.
  - The immediate post-resolve read (what `probe_resolve_lifecycle` does) is unaffected. A LATER re-read could see
    the incident back.

- **Q4 the four leaves:**

  | Leaf | Field | Emit site | Allowlist |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | hue | `duration_ms` | `ui-bridge/src/telemetry.rs:310-324` | `observability.rs:992-995` |
  | discovery | `duration_ms` | `:326-341` | `:996-1002` |
  | counter | `duration_ms` | `:343-356` | `:1003-1006` |
  | report render | `value` | `pulse-app/src/incidents_router.rs:563-569` | `:2430-2435` |

  - **hue:** fires only on a WITNESSED tier change of a dot, mounted in the compact widget, which is shown at boot
    (`main.rs:1134`).
  - **discovery:** fires per batch of newly visible dots. It measures backend first-sighting → first render (since
    `fb93fca`/`87fe658`).
  - **counter:** fires on each `list_active` poll (1000 ms) in the compact widget, Findings and Report webviews.
  - **render:** fires ONLY from the in-app `get_report` resolver, never from MCP `retrieve_report`. The Report
    window is declared `visible: false` at boot (`tauri.conf.json:49-61`), and `Report.tsx:24-26` passes
    `useReport(isOpen ? id : null)`. So **no render sample is produced unless Pulse's Report window is OPEN**.
    **[corrected at P5: `isOpen` is `effectiveId !== null` with
    `effectiveId = clickedId ?? findings.rows[0]?.id` (`pulse-app/ui/src/widget/ReportWindow.tsx:23,32` at S), so the
    hidden Report webview fires on each newly formed incident with no click. A Findings-row click
    (`FindingsWindow.tsx:189-191,222`) pins the selection until the Report is closed (`:26`).]**
  - Whether a hidden WebView2 runs the effect is "not measurable from source".

- **Q5 P-025 coordinates, `226554a` → S:**
  - The formula `duration_ms = max(0, paint − tier_effective_at/1e6)`, the one-sample-per-witnessed-change rule
    and the 60 000 clamp all hold.
  - Moved:
    - the hue emit, `telemetry.rs:278-282` → **`:316-320`**;
    - the allowlist, `observability.rs:989-992` → **`:992-995`**;
    - `ServiceListItem`, `lifecycle/registry.rs:54-69` → **`:56-71`** (field at `:70`).
  - Unchanged: `frame-metrics.ts`, `constellation-types.ts`, `tier_effective.rs`, `ConstellationCanvas.tsx`,
    `xtask/src/hue_shift.rs:41`.

- **Q6 `app.exit`:**
  - New at S (`03ec944`; `observability.rs:2771-2807`).
  - On Windows only the `event_loop` class writes, through tray Quit. `taskkill /F` / `Stop-Process -Force` writes
    none, as the round-request says.

- **Q7 bootstrap override:**
  - `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_BASELINE_BOOTSTRAP_SECONDS` is still present (`triage/src/cue/thresholds.rs:12,17`). The
    default is 3600, accepted values are 0 < v < 86400, and the WARN target is
    `triage.baseline.bootstrap_window.override`.
  - It is inert for this round. Every assertion rides storm-path incidents or UI leaves, never a baseline cue (no
    absence-based arm).

- **`probe_resolve_lifecycle` / `attribute_by_liveness` / `emit_canary_storm` / `canary_spec`** — 33 rows (trace
  `tree-query-2026-10-02-p-075-assert-round-against-pulse.json`).
  - The production callers are `canary.rs:188-189,205` (deterministic/real-model canary). The others are `lib.rs`
    re-exports (`:28-29,36-37`) and test binaries (`canary_wire.rs`, `canary_obs_witness.rs`,
    `lifecycle_harvest.rs`, `lifecycle_live.rs`, `composition_root.rs:21`).
  - `lifecycle_live.rs`'s `probe_resolve_lifecycle(…)` call at `:155` is absent from the rows. It is an async fn,
    the index-gap class the cookbook names. Grep confirms the call site.
  - **This chunk calls these symbols and changes none of their signatures**, so there are no callers to thread and
    no cross-crate blast.

- **The live leg prints and the harvest grades** (`lifecycle_live.rs:31-32`; `delegated_timing_harvest.rs:595-699`).
  The feature-gated leg is the producer, and a default-suite harvest asserts over committed evidence.

- **Absence is UNGRADED, never met** (`delegated_timing_harvest.rs:123-145`, `:451-470`). This matches the
  round-request posture exactly.

- **The windowed P-025 grade with incident anchoring** (`grade_in_window` + `incident_anchor_error_ms` ≤ 1 000 ms,
  `:244-288`). The window comes from the frozen self-obs `timeline.execute` `new` + phase-1 `gap_ms`, through
  `scenario.run` close.

- **A filtered-by-target Pulse slice as committed evidence** (2026-09-29 `evidence/pulse-hue-lines.jsonl`). These
  are closed-field lines: no corpus text, fingerprint or host path.

- **Digest-pinned evidence graded from file** (`real_model_harvest.rs:5-6`, the 2026-09-30 regime): sha256 over LF

- **Raw-wire dump before trusting an extraction** (`lifecycle_live.rs:56-58`; testing.md 2026-09-01).

- **Test-binary readers of `CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR` / `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR`** go through `capture_paths` and fail
  with path-free reasons (`capture_paths/mod.rs:6-9`).

- **The `live-pulse` gated target owes its own clippy line**:
  `cargo clippy -p conductor-run --features live-pulse --all-targets -- -D warnings`.

- **Capture output from a `-q … -- --nocapture` test is buffered and written ONCE**, with a leading newline
  (testing.md 2026-09-23; `span_landing_live.rs:199-201`).
- **Read the live item key `incident_id`, accepting `id` too** (`lifecycle_live.rs:65-67`; `extract.rs:160-174`).

- **Name a scenario by its stem.** Never pass a shared P-ID to `run`/`SCENARIO=`. P-025/027/037/045 are each named
  by more than one scenario (the grep above lists `halo-breathing-encoding` and `constellation-severity-live-wiring`

- **No `boot` before a preflight-firing leg**, and a 150 s quiet window between any two canaries or storms on one

- **Fresh data dir under `%TEMP%/pulse-legs/<letters-only leaf>`**, with `pulse-app` launched BY PATH from a cwd
  outside this repo (verification-harness.md 2026-08-18 [refined 2026-09-30]; 2026-08-10 (2)).

- **The census is taken before and after**, stopping only what the agent started, by PID + parent + CreationDate
  (host-win32.md 2026-09-17; memory "Stop everything you start").

- **The Pulse pre-leg line count is taken after readiness and before the first dispatch** (~2.2 k boot lines;
  verification-harness.md 2026-08-21 (a)).

- `crates/conductor-run/tests/p075_round_live.rs` — the round's P-075 live leg (`#![cfg(feature = "live-pulse")]`).
  - It stamps the `std::time` emission instant, then emits a `canary_spec(marker)` storm through `emit_canary_storm`
    and computes `fingerprint(&spec)`.
  - It polls the active set for an incident opened after that stamp, then calls `retrieve_telemetry_slice` and
    `retrieve_report` for that incident.
  - It does a liveness keep-alive, then runs `probe_resolve_lifecycle`.
  - It prints ONE buffered capture of integers, booleans and ids only (fingerprint membership as a boolean, never
    the hex).

- `crates/conductor-run/tests/delegated_timing_harvest.rs` — the round's P-025 (windowed) and P-027/P-037/P-045

- `crates/conductor-run/tests/lifecycle_harvest.rs` — the round's assertion-1/2 grades over the committed leg
  capture.

- `crates/conductor-run/tests/span_landing_live.rs` — the CARRY: the input subdir moves off `runs/live-suite/`, a
  firing-form clear runs before drive A, and a stale pair is refused.

title: The six graded assertions (round-request.md §The six graded assertions; CONTEXT restates them)

data.head: ## The six graded assertions (round-request.md §The six graded assertions; CONTEXT restates them)

body:
1. **Read-back content fidelity.** The incident read back through MCP `retrieve_telemetry_slice` carries, in
   `fingerprint_refs`, the full 32-hex fingerprint Conductor derives for the storm it emitted. The incident opened
   after the storm's emission instant. `retrieve_report` renders it with `degraded_mode: false`.

2. **Runtime-state fidelity.** `mark_incident_resolved` applies, and the incident leaves `query_incident_list`'s active
   set.

3. **P-025:** the worst `metric.constellation.hue_update_ms.duration_ms` in the leg window is ≤ 2000, graded per
   Conductor's `contracts/pulse-p025-measurement-contract.md` (the constellation dot hue, never the deferred Halo glow).

4. **P-027:** `metric.constellation.discovery_ms.duration_ms` (first-sighting anchored since Pulse
   `2026-09-30-p-027-discovery-bound`) is ≤ 5000.
5. **P-037:** `metric.report.render_ms.value` is ≤ 2000 (the Report window).
6. **P-045:** the worst `metric.findings.counter_refresh_ms.duration_ms` is ≤ 1000 (the Findings counter).
- Each assertion is a hard PASS or FAIL at the MEASURED value. An absent sample is UNGRADED and never counts as met.

- A FAIL is a Pulse finding: **no re-drive for a pass** (Conductor's v3-08 posture). Pulse surfaces it as its own wrap
  escalation.

- Pulse's `ref` cites Conductor's graded test ids and the evidence path at Conductor's commit, and is written only when
  all six read PASS. This chunk therefore produces stable test ids and a committed evidence path that Pulse can cite.

- Since S, a `Stop-Process -Force` teardown of `pulse-app` leaves no `app.exit` record. That is expected, not a finding
  (round-request §The binary under test).

- Give the span-landing witness inputs (`span-{a,b}.jsonl`, today a second, operator-local writer in the harness-owned
  `runs/live-suite/`, uncleared before drive A) their own harness-owned subdir, with a non-recursive clear before drive
  A, so a stale pair can never be graded. Origin: the overseer ruling at the
  `2026-10-01-per-run-span-identity-in-the-real-model-harness` wrap (the D-arch-collision escalation; arch §Occupied
  Resources `runs/live-suite/{leg}.jsonl`).

- Phase-time coordinates (hypotheses for P3): `crates/conductor-run/tests/span_landing_live.rs:38` reads
  `runs.join("live-suite").join("span-{leg}.jsonl")`. The harness capture dir is `scripts/agent-run.sh:69` /
  `scripts/agent-run.ps1:131`. Per security rules 2026-09-06, the clear is non-recursive BY PATTERN inside a known dir.
  (verified at P3 — the rule lives in `.claude/rules/security.md` Session Additions 2026-09-06, not the master)
- No Pulse source, build or ledger is touched. Pulse's evidence is read-only from here and cited, never copied.

- The named gap stays the founder's, not the round's: `incident_events` reaches no MCP tool, so content fidelity is
  scoped to the fingerprint plus runtime state.
- One round. A FAIL is recorded, not re-driven.
- The fixed sidecar NAME and the no-listener boundary are unchanged.

- **Completion axis — VERIFIED, and it narrows the build.**
  - The `2026-08-31-p-075-assert-round` (Pulse `83d4060`) shipped assertion 2's whole mechanism:
    `probe_resolve_lifecycle`, `attribute_by_liveness`, the `live-pulse` feature, and `tests/lifecycle_live.rs` →
    `tests/lifecycle_harvest.rs`. Its verdict was PROVEN-BY-LIVENESS.
  - The four budget graders are shipped in `tests/delegated_timing_harvest.rs` (`bounds`/`grade`/`grade_in_window`).
  - What is NEW is assertion 1:
    - no shipped check compares the emitted fingerprint against `fingerprint_refs`;
    - no shipped live leg calls `retrieve_telemetry_slice`/`retrieve_report` for a named incident or stamps the
      storm's emission instant.
  - The round re-uses the graders against S and builds only that.

- `[premise-corrected: no scenario names P-075; P-037 fires from the Report webview's own fallback selection — corrected again at P5]` **The drivers:**
  - Scenarios:
    - P-025 `halo-hue-encoding`;
    - P-027 `service-constellation-discovery`;
    - P-037 `report-render-surface`;
    - P-045 `findings-counter-refresh`;
    - assertions 1–2 have no scenario (P-075 is `DriveObserve`, `coverage.rs:540-545`) and ride a feature-gated
      live leg, as in the prior round.
  - The P-025, P-027 and P-045 leaves fire with the compact widget, which is shown at boot (Pulse `main.rs:1134`).
  - **[premise-corrected at P5: `isOpen` is `effectiveId !== null` (`ReportWindow.tsx:23,32`), not visibility, so the
    hidden-at-boot Report webview fires on each newly formed incident with NO click, and a Findings-row click PINS the
    selection and suppresses samples. Overseer-ratified: nobody touches the desktop.]** The P3 reading follows, kept
    as the record. **`metric.report.render_ms` fires only from the in-app `get_report`, and only while Pulse's Report window is OPEN**
    (`Report.tsx:24-26`; the window is declared `visible: false`, `tauri.conf.json:49-61`). The MCP `retrieve_report`
    never emits it.
  - Conductor may not automate Pulse's UI, so an unopened Report window makes P-037 UNGRADED by construction. Who
    opens it is a P4 question for the operator.

- **Fingerprint representation and provenance — VERIFIED at S.**
  - `fingerprint_refs` = `incident.evidence_refs.fingerprint_hashes` (`tools.rs:439`), written ONLY at incident
    creation by `grounded_fingerprint_hashes` (`inference_runtime.rs:657-666`). That is the three `det-*` constants
    followed by the triggering cue's full 32-lowercase-hex fingerprint.
  - The derivation, `compute_exception_fingerprint` (`buffer/src/fingerprint.rs:79-96`), is equal to Conductor's
    `fingerprint()`: 0 commits since `83d4060`.
  - **Two conditions bind the assertion.**
    - The storm must CREATE the incident. A dedupe re-emission never updates `fingerprint_hashes`
      (`inference_runtime.rs:830-858`), so the P-075 leg must open on an EMPTY active set.
    - The check is MEMBERSHIP, never equality of the field.

- **`degraded_mode: false` — VERIFIED from source at S.** `degraded_mode = parsed_l4.is_none()` (`tools.rs:377-381`),
  and since `9d14166` the canned L4 output is scrubbed per leaf and stays parseable. The 2026-08-21
  `degraded_mode: true` samples predate that commit.

- **Matrix — VERIFIED.**
  - Conductor's matrix carries `v3-01`..`v3-11` (10 verified, `v3-09` deferred) and no P-075 capability.
  - Pulse's `verification-matrix.json#P-075` is Pulse's ledger.
  - This chunk links no capability.

- **New hazard from source (Q3):** the app learns of an MCP resolve only in its 60 s persist reconcile
  (`persistence.rs:250-283`). An app-side re-emission persist landing first can re-write the row `active`. The
  immediate post-resolve read is unaffected. A later re-read is a witness only, never the grade.

- **CARRY coordinates — VERIFIED, plus one finding.**
  - `span_landing_live.rs:38` reads `runs/live-suite/span-{leg}.jsonl`.
  - The live suite's own clear `rm -f "$LIVE_CAPTURE_DIR"/*.jsonl` (`agent-run.sh:106`, the ps1 twin) ALSO deletes
    the span pair. That is a cross-writer interaction in the shared dir, and the move removes it.
  - Nothing in the witness checks that the pair belongs to the CURRENT Pulse launch.

- **Sidecar on `PATH` — VERIFIED as a firing-form item** (verification-harness.md 2026-08-20, 2026-09-07). It is
  checked by `which andromeda-pulse-mcp`. The sha256 re-measure identifies the FILE, and `PATH` order decides which

Linux build relayed by the overseer (`pulse-app` `23f6ef2b…6ada`, `andromeda-pulse-mcp` `e64f3688…e02e`). The round
grades the SEVEN assertions of S2's `round-request.md`, each a hard PASS / FAIL / UNGRADED at its measured value,
behind stable test ids and a committed evidence path that Pulse's `round-result.md` can cite:
- six carry over from the prior round;

- the seventh is new: the round's incident lifecycle events read back through `retrieve_incident_events` BEFORE and
  AFTER `mark_incident_resolved`, its `resolved` event placed inside the resolve call's `std::time` request→response
  window.

**The round runs on this Linux host**, by the FOUNDER's live word of 2026-10-04 relayed by the overseer (the P4 fork,
recorded in §Provenance). It runs against the relayed binaries: re-measured before launch, never rebuilt. A missing UI
sample grades UNGRADED and is never re-driven.
To read assertion 7 at all, Conductor pins `retrieve_incident_events` as a FIFTH required MCP tool:

- in `READBACK_TOOLS`, `contracts/mcp-contract.toml` and the in-process stub's default list (the CARRY; the
  cancelled P4's Q1);
- with a typed by-id read in the client.

The pin is the founder's LIVE ratification of the playbook's escalate pattern "Boundary widening". A sidecar lacking
the tool blocks on the EXISTING required-tool precondition, and the five named preconditions stay five (per
architecture §Standard Contracts → Readiness gate; security-plan §Input Validation).

The resolve call's window comes from an ADDITIVE timed sibling of `probe_resolve_lifecycle` in `conductor-run`
(the cancelled P4's Q3). The shipped probe delegates to it, and no `LifecycleObservation` literal moves.

1. **Pin the fifth tool in `conductor-verify`.**
   - `src/client.rs`:
     - add `pub const RETRIEVE_INCIDENT_EVENTS: &str = "retrieve_incident_events";` beside the four (`:22-26`), and
       update the doc line above them to say five;
     - add `pub async fn retrieve_incident_events(&self, incident_id: i64) -> Result<Value, VerifyError>`, which
       calls `self.call_tool(RETRIEVE_INCIDENT_EVENTS, Some(json!({ "incident_id": incident_id })))`. That is the
       `resolve_incident` shape (`:186-189`), returning Pulse's RAW result, and its doc names the raw shape
       `{incident_id, events: [{event_kind, occurred_unix_nano}], total, truncated}`. It rides `call_tool`, so it
       inherits the bounded `verify.readback.call_tool` span with `mcp_tool`: no new span and no new attribute.
   - `src/lib.rs`: re-export the const beside the four (`:44`).
   - `src/manifest.rs`: `READBACK_TOOLS` becomes `[&str; 5]`, appending the new const after `MARK_INCIDENT_RESOLVED`,
     and its doc and import line follow.
   - `contracts/mcp-contract.toml`: `required_tools` gains `"retrieve_incident_events"` as its fifth entry. The
     `expected_protocol_version` pin is unchanged.

2. **Teach the in-process stub the new tool** (`crates/conductor-verify/tests/common/mod.rs`).
   - `StubConfig::default().tools` gains `"retrieve_incident_events"` (`:114-121`).
   - Add two fields:
     - `incident_events: Vec<(String, i64)>`, default `vec![("created".into(), 1_700_000_000_050), ("resolved".into(), 1_700_000_000_555)]`;
     - `incident_events_unknown: bool`, default `false`.
   - Add a `tools/call` arm for `retrieve_incident_events` answering with Pulse's RAW S2 keys:
     `{"incident_id": <the requested id>, "events": [{"event_kind", "occurred_unix_nano"}…], "total": <events.len()>, "truncated": false}`.
     The id is echoed from the request, as the resolve arm does (`:272-278`).
   - With `incident_events_unknown` set, the arm answers a JSON-RPC ERROR
     `{code: -32603, message: "tool dispatch failed for `retrieve_incident_events`: incident not found"}`. That is
     Pulse's shape at S2 (`tools.rs:545`; research.md §Pulse at S2), and it follows the `resolve_declines` precedent
     (`:210-219`).

3. **Stub-tier arms for the read** (`crates/conductor-verify/tests/readback.rs`), each awaited through the file's
   existing `bounded(…)` wrapper:
   - (a) a populated read returns the stub's two events, in order, under the S2 keys (`incident_id`,
     `events[].event_kind`, `events[].occurred_unix_nano`, `total`, `truncated`). Assert the KEY NAMES on the raw
     value: item-key fidelity, testing.md 2026-09-01.
   - (b) `incident_events: vec![]` returns `events: []` with `total: 0`.
   - (c) `incident_events_unknown` yields `Err(VerifyError::JsonRpc { code: -32603, .. })` whose message contains

4. **The fifth tool's absence blocks on the EXISTING precondition** (`crates/conductor-verify/tests/preflight.rs`).
   - Add one arm: a `StubConfig` whose `tools` omits `retrieve_incident_events` (the other four kept), run against

     - `required_tools["retrieve_incident_events"]` is `Absent`;

6. **Leave the P-025 contract and the four delegated graders' reading rules untouched.** Pulse moved nothing under

7. **Extend the live leg** (`crates/conductor-run/tests/p075_round_live.rs`). It still grades nothing; it prints.

   - **After the `degraded_mode` line and before the keep-alive** (`:193-197`), call

     `p075-round: before_total=N before_truncated=B before_first=W before_has_resolved=B before_sequence=W,W… before_outside_vocabulary=N`
     - each `event_kind` maps IN-PROCESS to a closed word: `created` / `active` / `acknowledged` / `resolved` /
       `unknown`, else `other`;

      2026-08-10). The env carries `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR=/tmp/pulse-legs/reroundevents`,
      `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MCP_ENABLED=true` and `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC=true`, in one block, echoed back; its
      stdout/stderr go to `/tmp/pulse-legs/reroundevents-app.out`. Record the PID and start time. Confirm deterministic
      L4 from Pulse's own log (`interpretation.model.load` with `inference_mode: deterministic`), and record the count
      of `triage.baseline.bootstrap_window.override` lines.
    - **(c)** Tell the founder: hands-off. No click, the Findings rows untouched, the compact widget left visible (the
      prior round's posture, round-ledger.md §The binary under test and the slot).
    - **(d)** Fire the legs with the same three handles exported:
      - P-075 FIRST on the fresh launch;
      - then H → D → R → F;
      - each preceded by the non-priming `conductor preconditions` probe and the Pulse-log pre-leg line count, with a
        150 s quiet window between legs;
      - freeze leg H's `logs/agent-latest.jsonl` immediately after it;
      - take a post-round line count after F.
      No `boot` anywhere (verification-harness.md 2026-08-19 (a)).
    - **(e)** Stop `pulse-app` by its recorded PID with `kill -TERM`, then `kill -KILL` only if it has not exited
      within 10 s. Take the after-census, and stop only rows absent from the before-census that the round started.
      Whether a SIGTERM teardown writes `app.exit` is RECORDED, not graded (unmeasured on Linux, scope §Host).
- `conductor-0.3.0/chunks/2026-10-03-p-075-re-round-on-incident-events/evidence/` — the round's committed evidence (step 12)
- `contracts/mcp-contract.toml` — `required_tools` gains `retrieve_incident_events` (step 1)
- `crates/conductor-verify/src/client.rs` — the `RETRIEVE_INCIDENT_EVENTS` const and the typed by-id read (step 1)
- `crates/conductor-verify/src/lib.rs` — re-export the const (step 1)
- `crates/conductor-verify/src/manifest.rs` — `READBACK_TOOLS` grows to five (step 1)
- `crates/conductor-verify/tests/common/mod.rs` — the stub's fifth default tool, its events arm and unknown-id knob (step 2)
- `crates/conductor-verify/tests/readback.rs` — three stub-tier arms for the read (step 3)
- `crates/conductor-verify/tests/preflight.rs` — the fifth tool's absence blocks on the existing precondition (step 4)
- `crates/conductor-run/src/lifecycle.rs` — `ResolveWindow`, the timed sibling, the delegating probe, two inline tests (step 5)
- `crates/conductor-run/src/lib.rs` — re-export the two new lifecycle items (step 5)
- `crates/conductor-run/tests/p075_round_live.rs` — the before/after events lines, the timed probe, the host-neutral doc (step 7)
- `crates/conductor-run/tests/lifecycle_harvest.rs` — assertion 7's grader, its synthetic arms, the three re-round ids and pin (step 8)
- `crates/conductor-run/tests/delegated_timing_harvest.rs` — the four re-round ids over this chunk's slices and pins (step 9)
The fence runs in this order:
1. host prerequisites;
2. the `conductor-verify` tier;
3. the leg's lint;
4. the round (the operator slot, step 11);
5. the evidence-graded `conductor-run` tier;
6. the workspace gates;
7. supply chain;
8. evidence hygiene;
9. the operator pass.

The `conductor-run` suites sit AFTER the round because the re-round's graded tests read its evidence (step 8). There is
no self-verify entry, because no UI changes. The smoke is the mint-then-read `status` of leg F's run id. Every live leg
is preceded by the non-priming `preconditions` probe; `pulse-app` itself is launched and stopped by step 11, never by
an entry.

The four Pulse slices `evidence/pulse-{h,d,r,f}.jsonl` that assertions 3–6 grade have NO producing entry, by
construction. Step 12's byte-copying filter makes them once, after the round, from the pre-leg counts the line-count
entry prints and Pulse's post-round log; the source log lives under the operator-supplied data dir and is gone with the
slot, so a re-run could only reproduce a different round. Their contents are held by their digest pins (steps 8–9),
which the `conductor-run` entries run on every re-run.

body:
- (arch/security) The three pin sites agree on the five required tools:
  - `contracts/mcp-contract.toml` `required_tools`, `READBACK_TOOLS` and `StubConfig::default().tools` each name the
    same five tools;
  - a sidecar lacking `retrieve_incident_events` yields `ready: false` on the EXISTING `required tool(s) absent`
    precondition, naming the tool, and no new precondition exists.

  Proven by `cargo nextest run -p conductor-verify --profile ci` (step 4's arm) and `cargo nextest run -p
  conductor-verify --features stub-server --profile ci` (per architecture §Standard Contracts → Readiness gate;
  security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Universal).

- (security/tests) `retrieve_incident_events` read through the stub returns Pulse's RAW S2 keys:
  - `incident_id`, `events[].event_kind`, `events[].occurred_unix_nano`, `total`, `truncated`;
  - an empty `events` reads `total: 0`;
  - an unknown id yields `VerifyError::JsonRpc { code: -32603, .. }` containing `incident not found`, never a panic
    or an `Ok`.

  Proven by `cargo nextest run -p conductor-verify --profile ci` (per security-plan §Input Validation, the
  MCP-child-stdout row; test-plan §5).

- (arch/obs) `probe_resolve_lifecycle_timed`'s window is read from `std::time` around the resolve await:
  - `sent_unix_nanos ≤ received_unix_nanos`, both above the 2020 epoch floor;
  - `probe_resolve_lifecycle` returns the same observation as the timed probe;
  - no `LifecycleObservation` literal changes, and no span name or attribute is added (the incident id stays on
    `message`).

  Proven by `cargo nextest run -p conductor-run --profile ci` (per architecture §Cross-cutting Patterns → Determinism
  discipline; obs-plan §6 Boundary-call wrappers; obs-plan §11 Spans / Traces).

- (tests) `grade_assertion_7` is proven by synthetic arms. The canonical capture grades PASS. Each of the eight failing
  shapes grades FAIL naming its key. An absent field and `after_truncated=true` each grade UNGRADED, never met.
  Proven by `cargo nextest run -p conductor-run --profile ci` (per test-plan §7 Self-bootstrapping requirement).

- (tests) ALL SEVEN assertions are graded hard at their MEASURED value against S2's Linux binaries (verified by
  sha256 before launch):
  - by `lifecycle_harvest::p075_reround_assertion_{1_read_back_content_fidelity,2_runtime_state_fidelity,7_incident_events_read_back}`
    and `delegated_timing_harvest::tests::p075_reround_assertion_{3_p025_hue_update,4_p027_discovery,5_p037_report_render,6_p045_counter_refresh}`;
  - each over its own digest-pinned evidence file in this chunk's `evidence/`;
  - each pin with a tamper arm that fails on a changed byte.

  The criterion is that each is GRADED (PASS / FAIL / UNGRADED recorded and asserted as measured), never that each
  PASSES. A FAIL is a Pulse finding, and nothing is re-driven. Proven by `cargo nextest run -p conductor-run --profile
  ci` and `cargo test -p conductor-run` (per test-plan §2 Agent-runnable invariants; §7; §10 Zero-flakiness budget).

- (security/obs) The P-075 capture carries integers, booleans and closed words only: `grep -cE "[0-9a-f]{16,}"` on
  `p075-leg.txt` reads 0. Every committed evidence file carries zero host paths (the host-path hygiene entry reads 0)
  (per security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Logging; obs-plan §11 Logs).

- (design/layouts) Every verdict in `evidence/round-ledger.md` carries an explicit text label: `[PASS]` / `[FAIL]` /
  UNGRADED with its reason. UNGRADED is an evidence-only label, distinct from FAIL, never a new lamp. The CLI verb set
  and the 6-column results table are unchanged (per design-system §Anti-Patterns → Rejected Defaults; layout-templates
  §Component — Primary content block 2).

- (tests) The workspace stays green:
  - `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci`, `cargo test --workspace --doc`, `cargo clippy --workspace
    --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo clippy -p conductor-run --features live-pulse --all-targets -- -D warnings`
    and `cargo fmt --all --check` all return 0;
  - `cargo test -p conductor-verify` and `cargo test -p conductor-run` return 0 under the shared-process runner;
  - `grep -c "^name = " Cargo.lock` reads 562.

  (per test-plan §4 Framework; §9 Live-Pulse scenarios)

- (security) `cargo audit` and `cargo deny check advisories bans licenses sources` both exit 0, read from the bare
  commands, and the local advisory-db copy reads clean on porcelain (per security-plan §Dependency Security).

- (tests/ci) The pushed sha carrying the evidence and the graded tests reads `verdict: green` in `python -X utf8
  "$HOME"/.claude/skills/andromeda-tools/scripts/ci.py conclusion --sha HEAD --wait 1200`. The acceptance names the run
  id it read (per test-plan §11 CI — the harvest targets run in CI's default suite; the live leg never does).

- **The founder's ruling (P4 fork):** "Where does the live P-075 re-round run?" → **This Linux host**.
  - Founder live word 2026-10-04 via the overseer: "the round runs on this Linux host against the relayed S2 binaries
    (pulse-app 23f6ef2b…6ada, andromeda-pulse-mcp e64f3688…e02e)". A missing UI sample grades UNGRADED and is never
    re-driven.
  - The alternatives offered were a CI runner (would build its own Pulse; contradicts test-plan §11 and arch
    [CI/CD]; a second egress and a ninth rule-(b) crossing) and holding for a Windows host (a new Pulse relay).

- **Carried, not re-asked** (cancel-record.md §The P4 answers that stand for the replan):
  - Q1, the fifth-tool pin, is the founder's LIVE ratification of the playbook escalate pattern **Boundary
    widening** (`.andromeda/playbook.md:124`), per the overseer's 2026-10-03 correction message;
  - Q3, the additive timed sibling.

- **Leaned per artifact:**
  - The Linux data dir is `/tmp/pulse-legs/reroundevents`, leaned per verification-harness.md 2026-08-18 as refined
    2026-09-30: parent `pulse-legs`, a letters-only leaf, under the OS temp dir (`TEMP` is unset here; `/tmp` is not
    a host-path anchor).
  - UNGRADED stays an evidence-only label, leaned per design-history 2026-09-03 (the lamp set is closed at six).
  - `cargo-audit` becomes a host prerequisite, leaned per security-plan §Dependency Security (both gates must be
    green).

- **Research files inspected:** `contracts/mcp-contract.toml`, `crates/conductor-verify/src/{client,lib,manifest,preflight,spawn}.rs`,
  `crates/conductor-verify/src/bin/stub_pulse_mcp.rs`, `crates/conductor-verify/tests/common/mod.rs`,
  `crates/conductor-run/src/{lifecycle,execute}.rs`, `crates/conductor-run/tests/{p075_round_live,lifecycle_harvest,delegated_timing_harvest}.rs`,
  `crates/conductor-run/tests/evidence_pin/mod.rs`, `scripts/agent-run.sh`, the prior round's evidence and plan, and
  Pulse at S2 (`crates/mcp-server/src/tools.rs`, `crates/corpus/src/contract.rs`, `crates/triage/src/contract.rs`,
  `pulse-app/src/inference_runtime.rs`).

- A new field on `LifecycleObservation` — rejected: it threads through four struct literals (`lifecycle.rs:124`,
  `testkit.rs:125`, `lifecycle_harvest.rs:83,94`; grep `\bLifecycleObservation\b` over `crates/`). The additive
  sibling threads none.
- A leg-local re-implementation of the resolve probe — rejected: it moves assertion 2 off the shipped probe.

- A manifest-only pin — rejected: `readback_shape_witness.rs` runs the committed manifest against the in-process
  stub's literal default list, and would block on tool absence.

- A new span name or a dedicated `incident_id` / `event_kind` / window attribute — rejected: the bounded span set and
  `ALLOWLISTED_FIELDS` drop it silently (obs-plan §6; §11). The read rides `verify.readback.call_tool`, and ids stay
  on `message`.

- A new lamp, bracket label or results-table column for UNGRADED or for assertion 7 — rejected: the per-P-ID set is
  closed at six (layout-templates §Component — Primary content block 2).

- Printing raw `occurred_unix_nano` or window stamps — rejected: a 19-digit run matches the 16-hex probe. The leg
  prints window-relative signed nanoseconds.

- Reading or staging Pulse's `corpus.db` / `incident_events` directly to cross-check assertion 7 — banned
  (security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Data Protection).
- Re-driving any leg for a pass, or retrying an UNGRADED UI sample — rejected (the v3-08 posture; the founder's ruling).
- Rebuilding Pulse or tolerating a sha256 mismatch — rejected: a mismatch stops the slot.
- `boot` before any leg — rejected: its canary primes the incident the leg's own canary dedupes against.

- A `/home/…` literal in any `run`, note or evidence line — rejected: it is the host-path anchor on this host. Entries
  realpath `../andromeda-pulse` or expand `$HOME` at fire time.
- A pre-CI commit, push or tag fired by /implement — rejected: those are the operator pass's acts.

- **Order sensitivity:** steps 1–5 and 7 land first, and the `conductor-verify` gates plus the live-pulse clippy go
  green before the slot. The round (step 11) produces the evidence. Only then do steps 8–9's graded tests, their pins
  and the `conductor-run` gates land. The fence is ordered accordingly.

- **The AFTER read follows the resolve immediately:** a deterministic re-emission inside ≤ 60 s before the app's
  reconcile can append `active` after `resolved` (scope §The new tool). No keep-alive and no sleep go between
  `probe_resolve_lifecycle_timed` and the second `retrieve_incident_events`.
- **Host prerequisites are not repo changes:** the frontend bundle (`ui/dist` is gitignored) and `cargo-audit`.

- **Expected amendments (wrap):** architecture §Occupied Resources (Interface routes / surfaces) — the consumed MCP
  tool set grows from four to five (`retrieve_incident_events`), and the live surface's tool count moves 8 → 9.
  Applied within the registry size target (`scripts/arch-registry-check.py`; 38097 B / 38111 B against 38115 B at the
  last wrap).

- **Expected amendments (wrap):** architecture §Established Decisions [Read-Back Dependency Posture] and §Standard
  Contracts → Readiness gate — "`incident_events` reaches no MCP tool" is retired at BOTH sites together, for the
  S2 tool and its graded round. Pattern: **Boundary widening**, answered by the founder's live word (overseer
  correction 2026-10-03).

  MCP-child-stdout row and the corpus-access sites gain the read tool) and §Security Anti-Patterns → Universal (the

  correction 2026-10-03).

- **Expected amendments (wrap):** test-plan §2 (the `p075_round_live` clause's "four registered MCP tools"), §1
  ipc-internal (four raw tool results) and §5 (a `retrieve_incident_events` bullet in the three-tier shape) — sweep for
  what the claim SAYS, not the token.

- **Expected amendments (wrap):** obs-plan §1 (the `conductor-verify` and Pulse MCP rows), §6 Boundary-call wrappers
  (the four-tool enumeration) and §4 Delegated-timing family (a dated S2 re-grade BESIDE the `03ec944` one, never in

body: Paths are relative to the Pulse repo; HEAD = S2 (re-read).

- **The resolve stamp, re-read at S2** (`tools.rs:451-481`; `contract.rs:645-693`):
  - `let now = current_unix_nanos()` (`:459`) = `chrono::Utc::now().timestamp_nanos_opt()` (`:567-568`), the same
    host clock Conductor's `SystemTime` reads;
  - `update_incident_status(id, "resolved", now, Some(now), …)` runs in ONE transaction. It reads the prior status,
    applies a guarded `UPDATE … WHERE updated_unix_nano <= now`, and inserts a `resolved` event at
    `occurred_unix_nano = now` ONLY when the prior status differs.
  - A stale guard → `DeclinedStale` → JSON-RPC error "incident changed concurrently; resolution not applied".
  - **So the `resolved` event's time lies inside Conductor's request-sent → response-received window, inclusive at
    both ends.** An incident already resolved gains no new event.

- **Since the prior round** (`git diff --stat 03ec944 S2 -- crates pulse-app ui` = 9 files): only
  `crates/corpus`, `crates/mcp-server`, `crates/triage/src/contract.rs` (+24, additive) and
  `pulse-app/src/inference_runtime.rs` (+3/−3, the const swap).
  - Nothing under `ui/`, no telemetry leaf, no auto-resolve or observer file moved.
  - The prior round's source readings for assertions 1–6 (fingerprint union, `degraded_mode`, the four delegated
    leaves, auto-resolve 120 s + 30 s tick, post-resolve re-emission ≤ 60 s) therefore carry to S2, and the P-025
    contract's `03ec944` coordinates need no re-pin.

- **Linux launch history:** Pulse's S2 operator pass (`…/evidence/operator-pass.md:54-61`, committed copy at S2)
  records the pass on this Linux host with **"no pulse-app process was launched; 4317/4318 stayed closed"**.

    on this platform.

    the producer → sidecar path, not the UI.

title: The seven graded assertions (round-request.md at S2, §The seven graded assertions)

data.head: ## The seven graded assertions (round-request.md at S2, §The seven graded assertions)

body:
1. **Read-back content fidelity.** The incident read back through MCP `retrieve_telemetry_slice` carries, in
   `fingerprint_refs`, the full 32-hex fingerprint Conductor derives for the storm it emitted. The incident opened after
   the storm's emission instant. `retrieve_report` renders it with `degraded_mode: false`.

2. **Runtime-state fidelity.** `mark_incident_resolved` applies, and the incident leaves `query_incident_list`'s active
   set.

3. **P-025:** the worst `metric.constellation.hue_update_ms.duration_ms` in the leg window ≤ 2000, graded per Conductor's
   `contracts/pulse-p025-measurement-contract.md` (the constellation dot hue, never the deferred Halo glow).
4. **P-027:** `metric.constellation.discovery_ms.duration_ms` (first-sighting anchored) ≤ 5000.
5. **P-037:** `metric.report.render_ms.value` ≤ 2000 (the Report window).
6. **P-045:** the worst `metric.findings.counter_refresh_ms.duration_ms` ≤ 1000 (the Findings counter).

7. **Incident events read-back (NEW).** For the round's incident:
   - read through `retrieve_incident_events` BEFORE `mark_incident_resolved`: the FIRST event is `created`, and the
     response carries NO `resolved` event;
   - read again AFTER it: the FIRST event is still `created`, the LAST event is `resolved`, and its
     `occurred_unix_nano` lies inside the resolve call's wall-clock window (request sent → response received);
   - every `event_kind` in both reads is one of `created` / `active` / `acknowledged` / `resolved`, and no event reads
     `unknown`.

   Between the first and the last event the sequence is not graded.

title: The new tool, as Pulse states it (round-request §What is new at S2 — re-verified at P3 against S2's source)

data.head: ## The new tool, as Pulse states it (round-request §What is new at S2 — re-verified at P3 against S2's source)

body: - `tools/list` carries nine tools: the prior eight plus `retrieve_incident_events`.
- Input `{incident_id: integer}` — required; no other property accepted.

- Response `{"incident_id", "events": [{"event_kind", "occurred_unix_nano"}], "total", "truncated"}`, oldest first, at
  most 256 (`truncated` true when more exist).

- Vocabulary closed: `created` (written when the interpretation path opens the incident) then one row per status VALUE
  change; any other stored value reads `unknown`.
- An unknown id → JSON-RPC error -32603, message containing `incident not found`.

- The resolve stamp, RE-READ at S2 (`tools.rs:451-481,567-568`; `contract.rs:645-693`): the sidecar's
  `mark_incident_resolved` stamps `now` (host clock) INSIDE the call and, in ONE transaction, appends `resolved` at
  `occurred_unix_nano = now` only when the prior status differs; a stale guard declines with a JSON-RPC error. An
  incident already auto-resolved before the call gains no new event. A deterministic re-emission inside ≤ 60 s before
  the app's reconcile can append `active` AFTER `resolved` (an S-time reading; its files did not move S→S2), so the
  AFTER read follows the resolve immediately.

- **Marker:** 2026-10-04-host-portable-tauri-ipc-tests · **Version:** conductor-0.3.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-04T00:55Z

Make `conductor-tauri`'s mock-runtime IPC tests host-portable: the same test source passes on the Linux dev host and
on Windows CI, with no test skipped, `#[ignore]`d, `cfg`-excluded or retried. Today two `#[cfg(test)]` sites build an
`InvokeRequest` with the Windows-only literal `http://tauri.localhost` (`commands.rs:417`, `pause.rs:243`). Tauri
treats a request as local only when its scheme and domain match `tauri_protocol_url`, and that is `http://tauri.localhost`
on Windows/Android but `tauri://localhost` everywhere else (tauri 2.11.3 `manager/mod.rs:339-346`,
`webview/mod.rs:1698-1706`). So on Linux every dispatch resolves as a REMOTE origin and the ACL refuses it with
`"<cmd> not allowed. Plugin not found"` (research.md §The mechanism).

The literal reaches nine tests. Six fail on Linux (named in research.md, measured `20 passed, 6 failed`). Three more
— the `invoke_expecting_error` callers — PASS VACUOUSLY on Linux, because the ACL denial is itself the non-empty error
they assert. The fix therefore has two halves: derive each request's origin from the window it is dispatched to,
which the mock resolves through the same `get_app_url` → `tauri_protocol_url` path `is_local_url` checks against
(research.md §The equality); and make the error-expecting path refuse an ACL denial as its error, so a wrong origin can
never again satisfy a mutation-killing error test. A new host-independent test pins the other direction: a foreign
origin is still refused on every host, so the origin check is made correct and never made irrelevant (per
security-plan §Threat Model Summary → Attack surface, Tauri IPC; test-plan §11 Mocking "NEVER over-stub").

Test code only: no production command, capability file, `tauri.conf.json`, frontend, manifest or lock change (per
architecture §Established Decisions → [Module Boundaries]; security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Code Patterns), and
no new CI job — CI stays Windows-only and the Linux leg is this dev host (per test-plan §9 Matrix builds; architecture
§Infrastructure Patterns → CI/CD approach).

1. **`crates/conductor-tauri/src/commands.rs`, test module — `request()` derives its origin from the window.** Change
   the shared helper `request(cmd, body)` (`:412-422`) to take the dispatching `&MockWindow` and set `url` to that
   window's own URL (`window.url()`, with an `.expect("…")` message naming the mock webview), replacing the
   `"http://tauri.localhost".parse().unwrap()` literal at `:417`. Update its two callers in the same module, `invoke()`
   (`:424-427`) and `invoke_expecting_error()` (`:512-518`), to pass the window they already hold. No test body changes.

2. **Same file — the doc comment states the host-dependent truth.** Rewrite the comment at `:409-411` so it says: the
   request URL is the dispatching window's own URL, which Tauri resolves per host (`tauri://localhost` on Linux/macOS,
   `http://tauri.localhost` on Windows/Android — tauri's `tauri_protocol_url`); any other origin resolves as remote
   and fails with `"<cmd> not allowed. Plugin not found"`. Keep the pointer to `.claude/rules/testing.md`. Comments
   may name both origins; code lines must not (the literal probe in Test Commands skips `//` lines).

3. **Same file — `invoke_expecting_error()` refuses an ACL denial.** After obtaining the `Err`, panic when its rendered
   text contains `"<cmd> not allowed"` (the denial's own prefix, `ipc/authority.rs:409` + the observed failure text in
   research.md), with a message stating that an ACL/origin refusal is not the failure the caller expects. Its three

title: The mechanism (re-derived at HEAD; the freight's causal claim, closed)

data.head: ## The mechanism (re-derived at HEAD; the freight's causal claim, closed)

body:
The dispatch decision is ONE predicate, `Webview::is_local_url(&request.url)` (`webview/mod.rs:1744`), which picks
`Origin::Local` or `Origin::Remote { url }` for the ACL lookup (`:1786-1792`). Its first arm compares the request
URL's scheme + domain against `AppManager::tauri_protocol_url(https)` (`:1702-1706`), and that function is
`cfg!(windows) || cfg!(target_os = "android")` → `http://tauri.localhost`, else `tauri://localhost`
(`manager/mod.rs:339-346`). A non-local origin resolves to a Remote context; no capability admits a remote origin for
an app command, so the dispatch fails with `"{cmd} not allowed. Plugin not found"` (`ipc/authority.rs:409`).

**The equality the fix needs, verified at source for THESE inputs:** for the mock app these tests build
(`mock_context(noop_assets())` — `build: Default::default()`, so no `devUrl` and no `frontendDist` URL,
`test/mod.rs:111-126`) and a window built at `WebviewUrl::default()` (= `App("index.html")`, tauri-utils
`config.rs:122-126`), `prepare_webview` sets the webview URL to `get_app_url(false)` (`manager/webview.rs:443-458`;
`PROXY_DEV_SERVER = cfg!(all(dev, mobile))` is false on desktop, `:43`), and `get_app_url` with no dev/dist URL falls
through to `tauri_protocol_url(false)` (`manager/mod.rs:353-365`). The mock stores that URL verbatim and returns it from
`url()` (`mock_runtime.rs:210`, `:609-611`). So **`window.url()` yields exactly the origin `is_local_url` accepts, on
every host**: `tauri://localhost` on Linux/macOS, `http://tauri.localhost` on Windows. Deriving the request URL from
the window it is dispatched to is host-correct BY CONSTRUCTION, with no per-OS literal in Conductor's tree.
Tauri's own doc example for `assert_ipc_response` uses the other form — a `cfg!(any(windows, target_os = "android"))`
literal pair (`test/mod.rs:216-223`) — which is correct today but restates the framework's rule by hand.

**Measured on this host (Linux, HEAD `f5076ad`):** `cargo nextest run -p conductor-tauri --profile ci` → exit 100,
`26 tests run: 20 passed, 6 failed, 0 skipped`; each failure's text is `"<cmd> not allowed. Plugin not found"`
(log: the session scratchpad's `nextest-tauri-base.log`). The six, by name:
1. `commands::tests::coverage_matrix_command_returns_every_classified_pid`
2. `commands::tests::unbacked_auto_command_returns_the_core_ledger`
3. `commands::tests::run_report_command_returns_a_well_formed_record_list`
4. `commands::tests::run_envelope_command_returns_null_when_no_run_has_an_envelope`
5. `commands::tests::stop_run_command_sets_the_cooperative_abort_flag`
6. `pause::tests::resolve_operator_hold_command_delivers_the_decision`

title: A finding the freight did not name: three tests pass VACUOUSLY on Linux

data.head: ## A finding the freight did not name: three tests pass VACUOUSLY on Linux

body:
`invoke_expecting_error` (`commands.rs:512`) dispatches through the same `request()` and its three callers assert only
`!err.is_empty()`:
- `run_report_errors_on_a_supplied_run_id_with_an_unresolvable_runs_dir` (`:666`)
- `run_envelope_errors_on_a_supplied_run_id_with_an_unresolvable_runs_dir` (`:681`)

- `list_scenarios_errors_when_the_capability_manifest_is_unreachable` (`:694`)
(re-derived: `grep -c 'invoke_expecting_error(&\|invoke_expecting_error($' crates/conductor-tauri/src/commands.rs` → 3.)
On Linux the ACL denial is itself a non-empty error, so all three PASS without the command ever running — they are
among the 20 "passed" above. Their comments name them as mutation killers (`Ok(vec![])` / `Ok(None)` mutants); on a
Linux run they would "kill" every mutant without executing the handler. Fixing the origin alone makes them execute
again, but nothing would stop the same vacuous pass recurring under any future origin drift. This is the same
mechanism and the same helper, so it is in scope: the error-expecting path must reject an ACL denial as its error.
`start_run_errors_before_spawning_a_run_thread` (`:705`) calls `start_run` directly, not over IPC — unaffected.

- **`request()`** (`commands.rs:412`) — derived-without-graph; callers by grep: `invoke()` (`:425`) and
  `invoke_expecting_error()` (`:513`), both in the same test module. Its signature changes (it needs the window to read
  the origin from) — both callers are in this file.
- **`invoke()`** — 6 dispatching tests in `commands.rs` (5 failing ones + `mock_app_registers…` does not dispatch).
- **pause.rs `:237-247`** — the one inline construction; its window (`:230-232`) is in scope at the site.
- No production symbol changes. No caller outside `#[cfg(test)]`.

- **Error-is-the-assertion helper** (`commands.rs:510-518`): `invoke_expecting_error` exists because `invoke` panics on
  an error. The hardening extends that helper, so its three callers inherit the guard without edits.

- **Mock app + window per test** (`commands.rs:385-406`, `pause.rs:225-233`): every test builds its own app and its
  own `"main"` window at `WebviewUrl::default()`, so `window.url()` is available at every dispatch site.
- **Doc comment as the in-tree record of the invariant** (`commands.rs:409-411`), citing `.claude/rules/testing.md`.

- **No `unwrap` without a stated reason in test code**: the test modules use `.expect("…")` with a message
  (`commands.rs:400, 406`; `pause.rs:229, 232`); the existing literal's `.parse().unwrap()` is the exception, not the
  convention.

- **Zero retries** (`.config/nextest.toml:8, :17`); **runner portability**: `cargo test -p conductor-tauri` must
  also be green (test-plan §4, 2026-08-20 entry); **formatter-clean** (`cargo fmt --all --check`, CI `rust` job).
- none

- `crates/conductor-tauri/src/commands.rs` — `request()` derives its URL from the dispatching window; the doc comment
  states the host-dependent truth; `invoke_expecting_error()` rejects an ACL denial as its error; one new negative
  test: a foreign origin is refused on every host.
- `crates/conductor-tauri/src/pause.rs` — the inline `InvokeRequest` takes its URL from its own window.

- none — the form (derive from `window.url()` vs a `cfg!` literal pair) is decided by the artifacts: arch extract

Host-portable Tauri IPC tests — the six `conductor-tauri` mock-runtime tests pass on the Linux dev host as they do on
Windows.

- The `conductor-tauri` mock-runtime IPC tests dispatch through an origin that is correct on the HOST they run on, so
  the same test source passes on the Linux dev host and on Windows (CI `windows-latest`), with no test skipped,
  `#[ignore]`d or `cfg`-excluded on either host to get there.

- The two literal sites that build an `InvokeRequest` with `url: "http://tauri.localhost"` —
  `crates/conductor-tauri/src/commands.rs:417` (the shared `request()` helper) and `crates/conductor-tauri/src/pause.rs:243`
  (an inline construction in the hold-gate dispatch test) — take their origin from one host-correct source rather
  than a Windows-only literal. Re-verified at HEAD `f5076ad`: `grep -rn 'tauri.localhost' crates/ --include=*.rs`
  returns exactly these two sites plus the doc comment at `commands.rs:410`.

- The error-expecting dispatch helper refuses an ACL denial as the error it expects, so a wrong origin can never make
  its callers pass vacuously (added at P3's premise closure — see Folded freight).

- The doc comment at `commands.rs:410` ("The `url` MUST be the mock webview's real origin (`http://tauri.localhost`) —
  any other value fails dispatch") is corrected to state the host-dependent truth, not the Windows value alone.

- No new CI job: CI stays `windows-latest` (this host has no Linux runner obligation); the Linux leg is this dev host.

  origin is made CORRECT per host, never made irrelevant (e.g. by widening a capability to admit any origin).

  exist (the `comm -23 … | wc -l` entry reads 0), and exactly the two step-6 arms are new (the `comm -13` entry reads
  2) (per test-plan §4 Framework; §10 Zero-flakiness).

- (tests/security) The rule section between its markers is byte-identical to the base commit's (the `diff <(git show
  …)` entry prints nothing). `rule_predates_the_drive` and the three `each_*_recorded_the_current_rule_before_it_fired`
  arms pass, and no committed `rm-capture*.txt` or `attempt-ledger.md` moves (the `git diff --quiet … ':(glob)…'`
  entry) (per test-plan §6 Real-model interpretation leg; security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Data Protection).

- (security) `no_committed_capture_text_sits_in_test_source` scans every `tests/real_model_grading/*.rs` beside its
  four prior sources. `the_capture_text_arm_scans_every_grading_module` holds that set equal to the directory's
  runtime listing, and `a_report_line_planted_in_a_grading_module_is_caught` shows the detection fires on a planted line
  and stays silent without it — in memory, with no capture text in source (per security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns →
  Data Protection, the inverse-control form of the 2026-09-30 remedy).

- (arch/obs) The split adds no target, workspace member, package, `Verdict`/`ReportState` variant, envelope key, span
  name or span attribute. The pre-committed-rule `row()` stays test-tier in `real_model_harvest.rs`, so
  architecture.md:71, obs-plan.md:221, security-plan.md:121, test-plan.md:260 and matrix v3-10's `ref` stay true
  as written (per architecture §Established Decisions → Probabilistic-Assertion Policy; obs-plan §4 Real-model posture;
  obs-plan §11 Spans / Traces).

- (security/tests/obs) `cargo nextest run -p conductor-core --test secret_scan_gate --profile ci` reports 7 passed, and
  so does `cargo test -p conductor-core --test secret_scan_gate`:
  - a dir with no `.git` entry is skipped with no spawn;
  - a `git ls-files` failure inside a repository still panics with "the gate has no subject";
  - the vacuity guards and the both-direction allowlist arm are unchanged.
  In a `.git`-less copy of the workspace (the `mktemp -d … --no-capture` entry), the gate exits 0 and prints its one
  path-free skip line (per security-plan §Secret Management → Secret-scan gate shape; test-plan §6 Repository-hygiene
  legs; obs-plan §9 Pipeline integration, Repository-hygiene gates row; obs-plan §10).

- (tests/layouts) Both shells' bundled-default `run` carry both feature-gated clippy lines once each (the `python -X utf8
  -c …` entry reads 4), with no existing harness line removed or rewritten (the `git diff … | grep -c '^-'` entry reads
  0). The harness still exposes exactly `boot`/`run`/`status`/`cleanup`/`logs` (per test-plan §3 5-command
  implementation; test-plan §9 Live-Pulse scenarios; layout-templates §Surface: cli → Primary screens).

  conductor-run --features live-pulse --all-targets -- -D warnings` exit 0, and `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run` exits 0

  strict declaration and driver pin are untouched (per a11y-plan §9 CI Integration; §11 A11y Anti-Patterns → CI).

  privacy admits every descendant, but a parent cannot see a child's private items. So the series capture loaders

A sibling module (`real_model_common`, a new `mod x;`) cannot see them, and adding `pub` changes the pinned bytes. A CHILD module of the file holding the rule CAN see them (`use super::*` / `use crate::*` reach an ancestor's private items). The only way to reach them from another test TARGET is a textual `include!` of a file holding the rule verbatim.

body:
