body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._

- **Marker:** 2026-10-07-a-fifth-pre-registered-real-model-series-for-v3-09 · **Version:** conductor-0.3.0 ·
  **Generated:** 2026-10-07T07:27:08Z
- **Chunk base:** `29adafa` (`29adafa143b58d3c296762af6ed59270ec5e4558`) — every diff-shaped probe names it.

- **Pulse HEAD the series runs against:** `f70be92` (`f70be92c2ca13c951330efeffd725e62a484610c`, inputs#I3). Its
  code commit is `1a2e509`; no product file differs between the two.

Drive the fifth pre-registered real-model series for `v3-09` against a Pulse built at `f70be92`, the sha that ships
"the L4 first hypothesis names the triggering service" (prompt `v2.6`). The design and the grading rule are the
fourth series', byte for byte: three identical drives on one fresh data dir, each through the existing `run --live
real-model` arm, every capture digest-pinned and graded from its file by the unchanged rule (per architecture
§Established Decisions [Read-Back Dependency Posture] and [Probabilistic-Assertion Policy]; test-plan §6 Real-model
interpretation leg; security-plan §Input Validation, real-model capture ingest row).

The series is the only end-to-end reading of the fix. Pulse's own probe read PASS, but its baseline arm also met the
bar and never reproduced the fourth series' d3 miss (inputs#I8), so a pass is not assumed here. A graded
`NotIdentified` or a zero-graded series is recorded NOT MET and never replaced. A met series is three drives and is
read as no more than that (inputs#I1 §2).
The route entry's block reads cleared (inputs#I3), so nothing waits behind it and the chunk carries no gated mode.

The founder opened the GPU for 2026-10-07 (inputs#I2), so the plan reaches the three-drive sitting as early as its
inputs allow. Part A is everything d1 reads. Part B is the series. Part C is the grading and the mark, which wait for
nothing but the captures. Two things differ from the fourth series' order, both on the relay's word (inputs#I1 §3):
the binaries are built BEFORE the contract section is written, so the binary proof is measured on both builds before
it is pre-registered; and the sidecar's proof no longer requires its digest to move.

1. **Gate re-check on Pulse.** Fire the four Pulse git probes (the first four `leg = 'operator'` entries). If Pulse's
   HEAD is no longer `f70be92`, or it is not on the upstream, or a build input is dirty: stop and report to the
   overseer. Never build from another HEAD.

2. **Open the attempt ledger.** Create `evidence/attempt-ledger.md` in the chunk folder with the step-1 readings.
   Every later step of A and B appends to it. The ledger records handle NAMES, the leaf, digests, counts and
   booleans — never a host path (security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Logging).

3. **The old side of the binary control.** Fire the report-only entry that prints both binaries' sha256 and mtime
   and the four candidate strings' counts on each, BEFORE any build. Record it in the ledger.
   - Expected, from research.md §The binaries on this host: `pulse-app` hashes `f69be5bb…` and the sidecar
     `6175fc36…` (the fourth series' builds); on `pulse-app` the two sentence strings read 0 and the two retired
     version literals read 1; the sidecar reads 0 for all four.
   - A reading that differs is recorded as measured, and step 5 decides on what was measured, not on this
     expectation.

4. **Build the binaries** (the two `role = 'build'` entries, with the leg env sourced so the build reads the local
   tokenizer, inputs#I7): `pulse-app`, then the sidecar. Record each exit and `Finished` line. Cargo's raw output
   stays out of evidence.

5. **The new side, and the proof the section will carry.** Fire the asserting entry (at least one sentence string
   present on the rebuilt `pulse-app`), then the report-only entry (the same digests, times and counts as step 3).
   Decide the proof mechanically from the two tables:
   - **present set** — each of the two sentence strings that read 0 before the build and at least 1 after it;
   - **absent set** — each of the two retired version literals that read at least 1 before and 0 after;
   - present set empty → stop and report to the overseer. No section is written and nothing is pre-registered;
   - absent set empty → the proof is the present set alone, and the section says so.

   The sidecar's proof is build provenance: clean build inputs at `f70be92`, its build command at exit 0, and an
   mtime after `1a2e509`'s commit time (2026-10-07 08:16:59 +02:00). Record its four counts and both of its
   digests, and say whether the digest moved. A digest that did not move is not a failure: none of the moved text
   is in that binary (research.md, the eleven-string table).

   Record one binaries table in the ledger: name, command, exit and `Finished` line, built time, sha256 before and
   after, each string's count before and after, the present and absent sets, and the sidecar's arm.

6. **Land the contract section.** In `contracts/pulse-real-model-leg-posture.md`, add `## The 2026-10-07 series`
   between `## The 2026-10-06 series` and `## The quiet window and serialization`. Add-only: no line of any existing
   section changes. The series keeps the name `2026-10-07` (the chunk's marker date) whatever day its drives fire.
   The section opens with the dated `[added …]` note in the prior sections' form and fixes, each as its own bolded
   clause, in the 2026-10-06 section's order:
   - **Provenance.** The founder's ruling it serves: 2026-10-06, `v3-09` is neither relaxed nor deferred — Pulse is
     fixed, then this series runs. The design repeats the 2026-10-06 series' design and was ratified by the overseer
     at this chunk's plan review. It is the second series on the Linux dev host.
   - **Pulse coordinates**, re-pinned to `f70be92` (code commit `1a2e509`) and read with `git show` (research.md
     §Pulse at `f70be92`):
     - the digest's `TRIGGER: ` line, unchanged: the first cue's cause label alone, no scope;
     - the trigger-framing instruction, quoted whole, ending with the new sentence (inputs#I4);
     - the cue line, `{kind label} scope_id={value}` (`cue_summary`, inputs#I6);
     - the grounded incident title, which leaves hypotheses as the model wrote them;
     - what is byte-unchanged from `5f77859`: `crates/triage`, the report render, the skip line, the workspace key,
       the argv and the embedded grammar.
   - **What is graded.** The model file `gemma-4-E4B-it-Q4_K_M.gguf` with its sha256 (unchanged), and the prompt
     versions `v2.6` / `v1.5-fallback` / `v1.5-reflection`. One sentence on Pulse's own reading: its shipped arm
     met its bar and so did its baseline arm, so that reading does not show the sentence fixes the 2026-10-06 `d3`
     miss, and a pass is not assumed.
   - **The rule and the stated limit.** The rank-1 rule is byte-identical to every prior series' recorded rule: the
     statement must name `conductor` as a whole word AND a retry token. Stated limit for this series: both facets
     now reach the model under an instruction. The retry token is on the trigger line and the cue line, with rank 1
     told to use the trigger's words; `conductor` is on the cue line as its `scope_id` value, with rank 1 told to
     name that value exactly as written and not a service whose name merely contains it. So `Identified` means the
     shipped model followed both instructions over a cue line that carries both facets verbatim. It is not
     inference of an unstated cause. A rank 1 that names the service only inside the canary identity
     `conductor-canary` grades `NotIdentified`, as it did on 2026-10-06. A met series is three drives and is not
     read as proof beyond them.
   - **The dir.** ONE fresh data dir, leaf `rm-fifth-series`, under the one-parent convention's `pulse-legs` in the
     user's cache dir, home-rooted for the 2026-10-06 section's reason. The leaf carries no digit, no `@`, no vendor
     prefix, no keyed word and neither word of the grading rule. No prior series' dir is reused.
   - **The binaries.** Both built from a clean `f70be92` tree. `pulse-app` proven by content: the strings of
     step 5's present and absent sets, each written with its count on the `5f77859` build and on the rebuilt one.
     The sidecar by build provenance, as step 5 states it, with both digests and whether they differ.
   - **The drives, the pass condition, the canary, re-fires, no fourth drive, the quiet windows, the launch
     posture, recorded-never-graded, the key rendering** — each in the 2026-10-06 section's words, with `d1`-`d3`,

     and no other. It names NO host rendering lever.
   - **The slots.** The overseer granted the two Pulse builds, the launch and the model runs on `:4317` for this
     chunk (2026-10-07); the founder opened the GPU for 2026-10-07. A GPU drive never runs at night.

   The section names no host path: the dir is described by its leaf and its parent's role.

7. **Pre-registration witness.** Compute the new section's sha256 in the `contract_section` form

8. **Pre-leg env checks** (three `operator` entries; run them in a shell that sourced the leg env script,

9. **The dir.** Fire the listing entry (it also proves the leaf absent), then create the leaf with `mkdir -p`. The

10. **Pre-build Conductor's leg binaries** so no compile falls inside the round: `cargo build -q -p conductor-cli

title: B — the series (GPU; never at night)

data.head: ### B — the series (GPU; never at night)

body:
11. **The go.** Immediately before the launch, ask the overseer for the go (inputs#I2): the round needs about 30
    minutes of GPU time in one sitting (the fourth series took 25 minutes from d1's start to d3's end). No go, or
    less time than that before night: stop here and wait for the word. Never split the three drives across two
    sittings.

12. **Launch and confirm.** Take the pre-series census (the round's census command, by hand) — expect no listener
    and no `pulse-app`. Launch the rebuilt `pulse-app` by path, detached, from the data dir as cwd, with ONE env
    block echoed back by name: the data dir, the leg env's handles as sourced, and
    `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC` and `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_BASELINE_BOOTSTRAP_SECONDS` removed. The block carries
    NO host rendering lever. Record the PID and start time. After 10 s confirm the process is still alive and that
    `:4317` accepts.
    - **If the app died inside those 10 s:** take a census, record the death in the ledger with the first
      launch's last stderr line, then stop and tell the overseer before anything else (inputs#I17). Pulse's CI on
      `f70be92` read red on `boot smoke (ubuntu-22.04)` — the app booted, then exited — and the overseer read it
      as a runner flake; a death on this host says it is not one. The one relaunch, with
      `WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER=1` added to the block, stays the only further posture: it is taken after
      that report, on the overseer's word, recorded as a launch-posture deviation, on the SAME data dir. A second
      death stops the chunk; there is no third posture.
    - Read Pulse's log and record the booted posture: `inference_mode` `real`, the `model_identity` it logged,
      `app.boot.workspace_key`'s `workspace_root_basename` equal to the leaf, 0
      `triage.baseline.bootstrap_window.override` lines, and the render-posture line if one is present. Any term
      off: stop the app, record it, report.

13. **The round.** For each drive in order, fire `gate.py run … --live-legs --entry N` on that drive's `live` entry,
    with `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` and `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MCP_ENABLED=true` set in the invoking command and the L4
    handle absent. The tool fires the round steps since the previous leg (the quiet window, the census, the
    non-priming probe), then the drive, which copies its capture into `evidence/`. Keep each firing's listing as
    `evidence/round-HHMMSSZ.txt`. After each drive:
    1. read the capture copy and Pulse's log for the leg window;
    2. write one ledger row: the grant, timing and run id; the route; the `canary:` tokens with their
       `skip_reason`s; the scenario digest's outcome and Pulse's stated reason when it was not surfaced; the
       `prompt_version` and `model_identity` seen; the envelope's landing state; the key-rendering witness; pickup;
       the census. Grades are left for step 14;
    3. classify the canary from Pulse's own log. Only a `pipeline-fault` canary re-fires, once, uncounted: rename
       that capture copy with a `-pipeline-fault` suffix first, then re-fire the same entry after a quiet window.

    If the round's pre-flight exits 3 on a control of its own (not on a plan defect), drive the same entries by hand
    in block order, each exit read from the bare command, and record that as a deviation. A drive that throws on a
    HARNESS defect, not a grade, may be re-fired once on the overseer's word; a second one stops and reports
    (verification-harness.md 2026-09-30).

    After `d3`: stop `pulse-app` with `kill -TERM` on the recorded PID, wait for it and its WebKit children to exit,
    and take the post-census against the pre-series baseline. Record a table: process, who started it, final state.

14. **Pin and grade the series.**
    - `real_model_series/mod.rs`: add `EVIDENCE_2026_10_07` and `SERIES_2026_10_07` after `SERIES_2026_10_06`
      (`:104-120`) — labels, file names and sha256 digests only (`sha256sum` of each committed capture; the files
      are LF).
    - New child module `real_model_grading/series_2026_10_07.rs`, mirroring `series_2026_10_06.rs` test for test:
      the `Series` value; `SERIES_2026_10_07_RULE_SHA256` with `the_2026_10_07_series_rule_was_fixed_before_d1`;
      captures match their pins; each drive recorded the current rule; no fingerprint and no key
      (`KEY_2026_10_07 = "rm-fifth-series"`); a `measured_2026_10_07` table; each drive grades as the ledger
      records, with the real-model and clear-launch witnesses; the eleven-key envelopes.
    - The `measured_2026_10_07` table is written from what the rule MEASURES, never re-judged: run the grading arm
      first with a placeholder row, read each drive's route, grade, further grades and canary tokens from the arm's
      own failure output, then write them (red before green). Copy the grades into the ledger rows.
    - Register the module at four sites: `real_model_grading/mod.rs` (a `pub(crate) mod` line after `:16`);
      `real_model_harvest.rs` — a `use` line after `:65` and the two constants in the `use real_model_series`
      list (`:66-69`), a `GRADING_MODULES` row after the 2026-10-06 one (`:1283-1286`, the array length moving
      11 → 12 at `:1253`), and a loop in `graded_captures` after the 2026-10-06 one (`:1312-1317`). Nothing
      between the rule markers (`:71`-`:459`) changes.
    - `capture_population.rs`: move `COMMITTED_CAPTURES` (`:9`) by exactly the `rm-capture*.txt` files this chunk
      commits. Predicted 17 → 20 (21 with a pipeline-fault re-fire) — record what the count measures.
    - **The verdict test** states the measured outcome. If at least one drive is graded and every graded drive reads
      `Identified`: `v3_09_is_met_by_the_2026_10_07_series`, plus the separate ref test
      `v3_09_ref_identified_with_the_real_model_witnesses_2026_10_07`. The ref test reads only the committed
      captures: it asserts `v3_09_met` over `GRADING.graded()`, and that `real_model_witnessed` and
      `launch_cwd_clear` hold on every graded drive's capture block. Otherwise
      `v3_09_is_not_met_by_the_2026_10_07_series` and no ref test.
    - A graded drive whose `pulse-report workspace rendering:` reads neither `verbatim` nor `absent` is recorded in
      the ledger beside its grade as contamination.
    - Write the ledger's series verdict by the pre-registered rule, applied mechanically. Beside it, state what the
      three drives measured and nothing wider.

15. **The walker's mark.** In `crates/conductor-tauri/src/commands.rs`, add one comment line directly above the doc
    comment of `fixture_scenarios_dir` (`:530`), in the shipped marks' form (`scenario_catalog.rs:90`): the token
    `andromeda:walks-tree`, an em dash, and one clause saying the catalog loader lists and reads every scenario
    file in the committed fixture dir. A comment only: no assertion, helper or output line changes. The helper is
    the one path through which four tests read that dir (research.md §Graph impact), so one mark covers them.

16. **Evidence hygiene, then the smoke.** Fire the host-path probe and the key probe over the committed evidence,
    then the `status` smoke on `d3`'s `run_id` (mint-then-read).
17. **The standing gates.** Fire the remaining non-leg entries. They may run at any hour; none waits for daytime.

- `conductor-0.3.0/chunks/2026-10-07-a-fifth-pre-registered-real-model-series-for-v3-09/evidence/` —
  `attempt-ledger.md` (steps 2-14), `rm-capture-d1.txt`, `-d2.txt`, `-d3.txt` and the round listings (step 13; a
  `-pipeline-fault` copy only if a re-fire happens).
- `crates/conductor-run/tests/real_model_grading/series_2026_10_07.rs` — step 14.
- `contracts/pulse-real-model-leg-posture.md` — step 6 (add-only).
- `crates/conductor-run/tests/real_model_series/mod.rs` — step 14.
- `crates/conductor-run/tests/real_model_grading/mod.rs` — step 14.
- `crates/conductor-run/tests/real_model_harvest.rs` — step 14 (never between the rule markers).
- `crates/conductor-run/tests/real_model_grading/capture_population.rs` — step 14.
- `crates/conductor-tauri/src/commands.rs` — step 15.
Graph impact (research.md §Graph impact, rust plane, 21 rows):

- `pre_registered @ real_model_grading/mod.rs:152` — three callers (`series_2026_09_30.rs:23`,
  `series_2026_10_01.rs:25`, `series_2026_10_06.rs:25`); the new digest test is a fourth.

- `fixture_scenarios_dir @ crates/conductor-tauri/src/commands.rs:533` — four calling tests (`:560`, `:632`, `:649`,
  `:667`). It gains a comment above its doc comment; no caller changes.
No manifest changes: the dependency basis is the package count, 562 (`grep -c '^name = ' Cargo.lock` at `29adafa`).

- **The live round** is the block's `round` and `live` entries, fired by `gate.py run --live-legs --entry N`, one
  drive at a time (step 13). The wrap never re-runs it; it re-verifies from `evidence/`.

- **Non-priming probe:** `conductor preconditions --for real-model-interpretation` precedes every drive. It fires no
  canary. There is no `boot` before any drive: it would prime the incident the drive's own canary dedupes against
  (verification-harness.md 2026-08-19 (a)).

- **Operator entries before the round** are fired once, by hand, in block order, and their results recorded in the
  ledger: the Pulse git probes, the old-side control, the builds, the new-side control, the env checks, the dir
  listing. `pulse-app` is launched between them and the round (step 12); the agent starts it and stops it, on the
  overseer's grant.

- **The binary control is two report-only entries around the builds and one asserting entry after them.** The
  asserting entry passes when at least one string of the new sentence is in the rebuilt `pulse-app`; on the
  `5f77859` build it prints `sentence-a=0 sentence-b=0` and exits 1 (measured at P4). Which strings the section
  names is decided by step 5's rule over the two report-only tables, so no entry has to be edited if one candidate
  fails a side.
- **Smoke:** `status` is mint-then-read on `d3`'s `run_id`.

- **The attempt ledger has no producing entry:** the agent authors it from the entries' recorded results and from
  Pulse's own log, as every prior series' ledger was. The criteria that read it are held by the harvest
  (`pre_registered` reads its digest line) and by the host-path probe.
- **Night rule:** only the three `live` entries are GPU runs. Every other entry runs at any hour.

- **Pulse builds and binary probes** run in the Pulse tree inside a subshell `cd`: cargo reads its config from the
  cwd, and the session's Bash guard passes a subshell `cd` and blocks a top-level one.

- **Host paths:** every Pulse binary probe runs from inside `target/release` with bare file names; the model digest
  entry prints the digest alone. Nothing an entry prints names a host path beyond what the gate tool respells.

- **Controls owed at implement** (red before green, one-shot): step 14's `measured` table. Its readings go to the
  report.

- **The operator pass** (hygiene, the pre-CI commit, the guarded push, the CI read) is the operator's. The agent
  performs it only on the operator's explicit word, and records it as made on that word.

  inputs#I3), committed 2026-10-07T20:38:39+02:00. Pulse's wrap commit is expected on top of it; the build runs at
  whatever HEAD carries the same product inputs, and both shas are recorded.

Drive the sixth, and last, pre-registered real-model series for `v3-09` against a Pulse built from `9bfefb8`'s
product tree — the sha that ships the measured remedy: under a triggering cue that carries a `scope_id`, the
digest's corpus block keeps that scope's own incidents and drops other scopes' (inputs#I5, inputs#I6). The design
and the grading rule are the fifth series', byte for byte: three identical drives on one fresh data dir, each
through the existing `run --live real-model` arm, every capture digest-pinned and graded from its file by the
unchanged rule (per architecture §Established Decisions [Read-Back Dependency Posture] and [Probabilistic-Assertion
Policy]; test-plan §6 Scenario: Fingerprint-storm — Real-model interpretation leg; security-plan §Input Validation,
real-model capture ingest row).

Two things are new and both are fixed before the launch. The section carries a **stop rule**: this is the one last
series, and if it does not pass there is no seventh (inputs#I1 §2). And the `pulse-app` proof is no longer a string
set: research measured that no string or symbol can tell a `9bfefb8` build from an `f70be92` one, so on the
operator's answer the section carries the moved digest with its build provenance and says plainly that no named
token exists (inputs#I14).

No generation has run on the shipped tree; this series is its first live reading, and a pass is not assumed
(inputs#I8, inputs#I10). Pulse measured the remedy on three replayed prompts of one capture run, on its probe's
arm. A graded `NotIdentified` or a zero-graded series is recorded NOT MET and never replaced. A met series is three
drives and is read as no more than that.

The route entry's block reads cleared (scope.md §Gate), so the chunk carries no gated mode. Two waits stand inside
implement, neither of them a block. Part A's Pulse steps wait for the operator's word that Pulse's wrap is
committed (inputs#I14). Part B, the three-drive sitting, waits for daytime and the operator's go (inputs#I2). Part A
is CPU work and may run at any hour. Part C waits for nothing but the captures.

body:
1. **The word, then the gate re-check on Pulse.** Wait for the operator's word that Pulse's wrap is committed
   (inputs#I14). Record it verbatim as an input (`inputs.py snap --step implement`). Then fire the five Pulse git
   probes (the first five `leg = 'operator'` entries). If `9bfefb8` is not on Pulse's upstream, or something is
   unpushed, or a build input is dirty, or any file under the build inputs differs between `9bfefb8` and HEAD:
   stop and report to the operator. Never build from a tree whose product inputs differ from `9bfefb8`. Steps 2, 8
   and 9 do not read Pulse's tree and may run before the word.

2. **Open the attempt ledger.** Create `evidence/attempt-ledger.md` in the chunk folder. Every later step of A and
   B appends to it. The ledger records handle NAMES, the leaf, digests, counts and booleans — never a host path
   (security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Logging). It records the HEAD the build ran at beside the pin.

3. **The old side of the binary control.** Fire the report-only entry that prints both binaries' sha256 and mtime
   and the four lineage strings' counts on each, BEFORE any build. Record it in the ledger.
   - Expected, from research.md §The binaries on this host: `pulse-app` hashes `df167647…ba4a` and the sidecar
     `6175fc36…d2a9` (the `f70be92` builds); on `pulse-app` the two sentence strings read 1 and the two retired
     version literals read 0; the sidecar reads 0 for all four.
   - A reading that differs is recorded as measured. If `pulse-app` does not hash `df167647…ba4a`, the old side of
     the control is not the recorded `f70be92` build: stop and report before building.

4. **Build the binaries** (the two `role = 'build'` entries, the plain leg env sourced so the build reads the local
   tokenizer, inputs#I7): `pulse-app`, then the sidecar. Record each exit and `Finished` line. Cargo's raw output
   stays out of evidence.

5. **The new side, and the proof the section will carry** (inputs#I14). Fire the asserting entry, then the
   report-only entry (the same digests, times and counts as step 3). The proof of `pulse-app` is four facts, all
   measured before the section is written:
   - the build inputs were clean and equal to `9bfefb8`'s (step 1's probes);
   - its build command exited 0;
   - its mtime follows `9bfefb8`'s commit time;
   - its sha256 differs from the recorded `f70be92` build's `df1676477222776d3e95edae7d219a4d421f2311ea8f17863233630c1ed8ba4a`.

   **If the digest did not move: stop and report to the operator.** No section is written and nothing is
   pre-registered. The linked code changed, so an unmoved digest means the build did not pick the change up.

   The sidecar's proof is build provenance: the same clean inputs, its build command at exit 0, an mtime after
   the commit. Record both of its digests and say whether the digest moved. It links `crates/triage`
   (inputs#I12), so it may move; a digest that did not move is not a failure, as at the fifth series.

   Record one binaries table in the ledger: name, command, exit and `Finished` line, built time, sha256 before and
   after, each lineage string's count before and after, and for each binary whether its digest moved.

6. **Land the contract section.** In `contracts/pulse-real-model-leg-posture.md`, add
   `## The 2026-10-07 sixth series` between `## The 2026-10-07 capture run` and
   `## The quiet window and serialization`. Add-only: no line of any existing section changes. The section opens
   with the dated `[added …]` note in the prior sections' form, saying the series keeps this name whatever day its
   drives fire. It fixes, each as its own bolded clause, in the fifth section's order with one clause added:
   - **Provenance.** The founder's rulings it serves: 2026-10-07 11:49 local, a Pulse chunk reproduces the miss and
     measures a remedy, then this series runs; and 2026-10-07 20:08 local, the rulings the stop rule states. Both
     by dialog, his own picks, relayed by the overseer. The design repeats the 2026-10-07 series' design and was
     ratified at this chunk's plan review. It is the third series on the Linux dev host.
   - **The stop rule** (new; inputs#I1 §2). This is the last series for `v3-09` in 0.3.0. If it meets the pass
     condition, `v3-09` is verified on three drives. If it does not, no seventh series is run: `v3-09` leaves 0.3.0
     for 0.4.0 with a named owner, and Conductor 0.3.0 closes at 10 of 11 capabilities on that measured basis.
     Either way the next route entry is the version close. The clause says it was written before the launch.
   - **Pulse coordinates**, re-pinned to `9bfefb8`, with the HEAD the build ran at when it differs and the empty
     product diff between the two; read with `git show`, never from the working tree:
     - what changed since `f70be92`: `select_corpus_matches` (`crates/triage/src/digest/retrieval.rs`) takes the
       triggering cue's `scope_id`; under one, the scope arm keeps that scope's incidents alone, the fingerprint
       arm keeps a match whatever its scope, the narrowing runs before the five-line cap and only removes; with no
       cue, or a cue with no `scope_id`, every active scope's matches stay (inputs#I5, inputs#I6);
     - for the scenario's storm the cue carries `scope_id=conductor`, so a `conductor-canary` incident reaches
       the corpus block only through the fingerprint arm;
     - the trigger line, the trigger-framing instruction, the cue line and the grounded title: as the 2026-10-07
       series' section states them, unchanged;
     - what is byte-unchanged from `f70be92`: everything under `crates/interpretation`, `pulse-app/src`,
       `crates/workspace-detector`, `crates/security` and `crates/mcp-server`, and both manifests. Two product
       files moved, both in `crates/triage/src/digest`.
   - **What is graded.** The model file `gemma-4-E4B-it-Q4_K_M.gguf` with its sha256 (unchanged), and the prompt
     versions `v2.6` / `v1.5-fallback` / `v1.5-reflection` (unchanged, inputs#I13). Two sentences on Pulse's own
     reading, so the section does not overstate it: replayed through Pulse's probe, the three scenario prompts of
     the 2026-10-07 capture run read 4 service misses of 40, 11 of 20 and 4 of 40 before the remedy, and 0 of 40
     each with it (inputs#I8, inputs#I9); that was measured on the probe's arm, which composes the bytes the
     product selection composes on those prompts (inputs#I10). No generation ran on the shipped tree, so this
     series is its first live reading and a pass is not assumed.
   - **The rule and the stated limit.** The rank-1 rule is byte-identical to every prior series' recorded rule: the
     statement must name `conductor` as a whole word AND a retry token. Stated limit for this series: both facets
     reach the model under an instruction, as in the 2026-10-07 series, and the corpus block no longer lists the
     canary's incidents through the scope arm. So `Identified` means the shipped model followed both instructions
     over a cue line that carries both facets verbatim, on a digest narrowed to the triggering scope. It is not
     inference of an unstated cause. A rank 1 that names the service only inside `conductor-canary` grades
     `NotIdentified`. A rank 1 that names `conductor` as a whole word and also names the canary grades
     `Identified`: the rule reads the words, not where the statement places the storm. That weakness is known,
     left unpatched for 0.3.0 on the overseer's decision, and recorded for 0.4.0 (inputs#I1 §2). A met series is
     three drives and is not read as proof beyond them.
   - **The dir.** ONE fresh data dir, leaf `rm-sixth-series`, under the one-parent convention's `pulse-legs` in the
     user's cache dir, home-rooted. The leaf carries no digit, no `@`, no vendor prefix, no keyed word and neither
     word of the grading rule. No earlier dir is reused.
   - **The binaries.** Both built from a clean tree whose build inputs equal `9bfefb8`'s. The clause states
     plainly that no named content token can prove this build: the change adds no string literal and the release
     profile strips symbols (inputs#I11). `pulse-app` is proven by the four facts of step 5, the digest written
     with both values. The sidecar by build provenance, with both digests and whether they differ.
   - **The drives, the pass condition, the canary, re-fires, no fourth drive, the quiet windows, the launch
     posture, recorded-never-graded, the key rendering** — each in the 2026-10-07 series' words, with `d1`-`d3`,
     the new leaf and the `9bfefb8` build. The launch names the same two model handles the earlier sections name
     and no other, and says the model-binary handle names the runner itself: nothing records prompts in this
     series.
   - **The slots.** The operator's go precedes the launch; the agent builds, launches and stops `pulse-app` inside
     that grant. A GPU drive never runs at night.

   The section names no host path and no capture text: the dir is described by its leaf and its parent's role.

7. **Pre-registration witness.** Compute the new section's sha256 in the `contract_section` form
   (`real_model_grading/mod.rs:145`): the file LF-normalized, from the section's heading line up to and including
   the newline before the next `## ` heading. Use a scratchpad script. Validate it FIRST on two known sections:
   over `## The 2026-10-07 series` it must print
   `57b5e96e60aea77486c3b1a3ace2dc09ffc7e43154d874bd3be3a5d12aec7376`, and over `## The 2026-10-07 capture run`
   `513892694d7d0f16b51bf7d225b8d11986c16281d0647937768889fa763387da` (both measured at P4 with this recipe, each
   equal to its pin in code). Then record in the ledger, at column 0, the line `pre-registration sha256: `
   followed by the 64-hex digest. The section is never edited afterwards.

8. **The dir.** Fire the listing entry (it also proves the leaf absent), then create the leaf with `mkdir -p`. The
   three earlier leaves are listed and not touched. No recursive delete anywhere (security.md 2026-09-06).

9. **Pre-build Conductor's leg binaries** so no compile falls inside the round: `cargo build -q -p conductor-cli
   --bin conductor` and `cargo test -p conductor-run --features live-pulse --test real_model_live --no-run`.

10. **The go.** Part A ends here. Wait for daytime and ask the operator for the go (inputs#I2): the round needs
    about 30 minutes of GPU time in one sitting (the fifth series took 25 minutes from d1's start to d3's end).
    No go, or less time than that before night: wait. Never split the three drives across two sittings. Record
    the go verbatim as an input.

11. **Env checks, launch, confirm.** In the sitting's shell, which sourced the plain leg env (inputs#I7): fire the
    three env entries — both model handles resolve, the model file's sha256 equals the pinned one, the NVIDIA
    kernel-module major equals the userspace major. A mismatch stops before the launch. Re-read `pulse-app`'s
    sha256 against step 5's. Take the pre-series census by hand — expect no listener and no `pulse-app`. Launch
    the rebuilt `pulse-app` by path, detached, from the data dir as cwd, with ONE env block echoed back by name:
    the data dir, the leg env's handles as sourced, and `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC` and
    `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_BASELINE_BOOTSTRAP_SECONDS` removed. The block carries NO host rendering lever and the
    model-binary handle names the runner, never the pass-through. Record the PID and start time. After 10 s
    confirm the process is still alive and that `:4317` accepts.
    - **If the app died inside those 10 s:** take a census, record the death in the ledger with the first
      launch's last stderr line, then stop and tell the operator before anything else. Pulse's CI on `9bfefb8`
      held a boot-smoke death on its first attempt (inputs#I1 §1), as it did on `f70be92`; a death on this host
      says it is not a runner flake. The one relaunch, with `WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER=1` added to the block,
      is taken only after that report, on the operator's word, recorded as a launch-posture deviation, on the
      SAME data dir. A second death stops the chunk.
    - Read Pulse's log and record the booted posture: `inference_mode` `real`, the `model_identity` it logged,
      `app.boot.workspace_key`'s `workspace_root_basename` equal to the leaf, 0
      `triage.baseline.bootstrap_window.override` lines. Any term off: stop the app, record it, report.

12. **The round.** For each drive in order, fire `gate.py run … --live-legs --entry N` on that drive's `live`
    entry, with `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` and `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MCP_ENABLED=true` set in the invoking command and
    the L4 handle absent. The tool fires the round steps since the previous leg (the quiet window, the census, the
    non-priming probe), then the drive, which copies its capture into `evidence/`. Keep each firing's listing as
    `evidence/round-HHMMSSZ.txt`. After each drive:
    1. read the capture copy and Pulse's log for the leg window;
    2. write one ledger row: the grant, timing and run id; the route; the `canary:` tokens with their
       `skip_reason`s; the scenario digest's outcome and Pulse's stated reason when it was not surfaced; the
       creating digest's corpus-row count as the capture prints it; the `prompt_version` and `model_identity`
       seen; the envelope's `state`, `verdict` and key count; the key-rendering witness; pickup; the census.
       Grades are left for step 13;
    3. classify the canary from Pulse's own log. Only a `pipeline-fault` canary re-fires, once, uncounted: rename
       that capture copy with a `-pipeline-fault` suffix first, then re-fire the same entry after a quiet window.

    If the round's pre-flight exits 3 on a control of its own (not on a plan defect), drive the same entries by
    hand in block order, each exit read from the bare command, and record that as a deviation. A drive that throws
    on a HARNESS defect, not a grade, may be re-fired once on the operator's word; a second one stops and reports

    After `d3`: stop `pulse-app` with `kill -TERM` on the recorded PID, wait for it and its WebKit children to

    - The `measured` table is written from what the rule MEASURES, never re-judged: run the grading arm first with

      failure output, then write them (red before green). Copy the grades into the ledger rows.
    - Register the module at four sites: `real_model_grading/mod.rs` (a `pub(crate) mod` line after `:18`);

title: The three questions the relay asks (`inputs#I1` §3)

data.head: ### The three questions the relay asks (`inputs#I1` §3)

body:
1. **What the classifier prints, and how the scenario's digest is told apart.** For a canary storm whose tick
   precedes the instant by milliseconds it prints `canary: surfaced … parse=ok created=false deduped=true
   skip_reason=none`, which is what Pulse's log bears out on d1 and d2. The scenario's own digest is told apart by
   the SIGN of its tick's stamp against the instant, never by distance and never by a digest identity, which
   Pulse's lines do not carry. The instant is the `timeline.execute` span's open, taken before the scenario's first
   emission (`crates/conductor-timeline/src/scheduler.rs:112-116`), and a tier-1 `retry_storm` digest needs the
   Autonomous band, which the scenario's storm reached 5002, 5001 and 5000 ms after the instant on the three
   drives. Its tick is therefore stamped after the instant: it is never selected, and as the next retry-storm tick
   it closes the last canary's segment. In d1 the canary's prompt is 06:32:46.356Z and the scenario's is
   06:32:52.168Z; the canary's own dedupe line carries that same 06:32:52.168Z stamp and sits two lines earlier in
   the file, which is why the pairing reads file order. The rule errs one way only: a canary tick stamped at or
   after the instant (d3, 11 ms after) gets no line, as today.

2. **The failing-first control.** Step 4 runs the new d1- and d2-shaped tests against the pre-fix composition and
   records that each reads `pipeline-fault` with `parse=none`. A standing test keeps that reading reproducible
   after the fix.

3. **Architecture's registries are not grown.** This chunk expects no architecture amendment: no architecture
   text describes the pairing window (research.md §Sweeps; the sixth series' architecture entry says so in its
   Kept line). §Occupied Resources stands at 38114 B and §Established Decisions at 38082 B of 38115 B; if a wrap
   detector proposes an amendment to either, it frees bytes there first.

1. **Read the base.** Confirm the four files of the write set are unmodified against the chunk base, and that
   `cargo nextest run -p conductor-run --test real_model_harvest --profile ci` reads 133 passed (the count at P4:
   `cargo nextest list -p conductor-run --test real_model_harvest --message-format oneline | wc -l` → 133).

2. **Move the composition into the shared module, behaviour unchanged.**
   - `crates/conductor-run/tests/real_model_common/mod.rs`: `canary_attempts` takes a second argument, the
     emission instant in epoch milliseconds, optional. In THIS step it reproduces today's composition exactly:
     given an instant it first drops every line whose stamp is not strictly earlier than the instant (a line whose
     stamp does not parse is dropped), then pairs what is left; given none it pairs every line. The stamp parser
     `iso_ms` moves here from the capture, body unchanged, and becomes `pub`.
   - `crates/conductor-run/tests/real_model_live.rs`: the canary block calls the pairing with the window and
     `emission_ms` and no longer builds its own filtered slice; `iso_ms` is imported from the shared module and its
     local definition is removed. Its two other users in this file keep reading it.
   - `crates/conductor-run/tests/real_model_grading/canary_pairing.rs`: the `paired` helper passes no instant.
   - Check: the harvest target still reads 133 passed, and `cargo clippy -p conductor-run --features live-pulse
     --all-targets -- -D warnings` exits 0 (the capture is compiled only there).

3. **Add six tests** to `canary_pairing.rs`, beside the existing eight, built with the file's own line helpers
   plus a deduped-outcome line and full ISO stamps (the stamps: Implementation notes, the table). Each test's
   failure message prints the paired lines, as the file's existing tests do.
   - `a_canary_tick_just_before_the_instant_reads_the_inference_stamped_after_it_d1` — the d1 shape (third storm
     and the scenario's digest): exactly one `canary:` line, `surfaced`, `t=2026-10-08T06:32:46.351Z`, ending
     `parse=ok created=false deduped=true skip_reason=none`; the closing line reads `canary other cue-bearing
     digests: 0 ()`.
   - `a_canary_tick_just_before_the_instant_reads_the_inference_stamped_after_it_d2` — the d2 shape, which also
     carries a tier-2 cue tick 730 ms after the instant: the same single `surfaced` line at
     `t=2026-10-08T06:42:51.851Z`, and the closing count still `0 ()`.
   - `the_scenario_s_own_storm_digest_never_prints_as_a_canary` — over the d1 and d2 shapes, no printed line
     carries the scenario tick's stamp (`06:32:51.361Z`, `06:42:56.859Z`), although that digest parsed `ok` and
     created an incident.
   - `a_canary_tick_stamped_after_the_instant_gets_no_line_d3` — the d3 shape (two storms before the instant with
     their inferences, one tier-2 cue tick before it, the third storm's tick 11 ms after it): two `canary:` lines,
     `surfaced` created then `surfaced` deduped, no third, and the closing line `canary other cue-bearing digests:
     1 (error_rate_spike)`.
   - `a_tick_the_instant_cannot_place_is_never_selected` — with an instant given, a cue tick whose stamp does not
     parse, and one stamped exactly at the instant, print no `canary:` line; with no instant the same lines print
     one each (the whole window, as when the scenario never emitted).
   - `the_pre_fix_window_read_the_same_shapes_as_a_pipeline_fault` — the standing control: the d1 and d2 shapes,
     with the lines at or after the instant dropped IN THE TEST and paired with no instant, read
     `pipeline-fault … parse=none`. It reproduces what the sixth series' captures printed, from the same lines the
     first two tests read as `surfaced`.
   - The existing source-literal test `the_capture_prints_pulse_s_no_incident_outcome` gains one assertion: the
     capture's source holds the call `canary_attempts(&window, emission_ms)`. No seventh test is added for it.

4. **Measure failing-first, before the fix.** Run `cargo nextest run -p conductor-run --test real_model_harvest
   --profile ci`. Predicted: exit 100, `139 tests run: 137 passed, 2 failed`, the two failures being the d1 and d2
   tests of step 3, each printing a third line `canary: pipeline-fault t=… parse=none created=none deduped=none
   skip_reason=none`. Record what the run measures in `evidence/failing-first.md`: the command, its exit, the
   runner's summary line, each failing test's name and the paired lines its message printed. No compile line and
   no absolute path goes into the file. If any other test is red, or either of the two is green, STOP and report:
   the mechanism this plan rests on is then wrong.

5. **The fix.** In `canary_attempts`, an instant no longer drops lines. It selects cue-bearing ticks: a tick is
   selected when its own stamp parses and is strictly earlier than the instant, and every tick is selected when
   there is no instant. Only a selected tick prints a `canary:` line or is counted among the other kinds. Every
   tick, selected or not, still bounds a segment, and every line stays visible to the pairing of a selected tick.
   The function's doc comment states the selection, what the pairing may read, and the limit (a canary tick stamped
   at or after the instant gets no line). The capture's comment at the call says the same in one sentence.

6. **Re-measure.** The harvest target reads 139 passed, 0 failed (predicted from 133 + 6; record what the run
   counts). Append the green summary line to `evidence/failing-first.md` under its own heading.

7. **The contract note.** In `contracts/pulse-real-model-leg-posture.md`, directly after line 320 (the last line
   of the `[corrected 2026-09-29 …]` note under "The canary classification"), add ONE bracketed block in that
   note's form, indented as it is: `[corrected {the day implement lands it}
   (2026-10-08-capture-canary-pairing-window-corrective, implement): …]`. It states, in this order: what the
   pairing read before (only the lines stamped before the instant); what was measured (d1 and d2 of the
   2026-10-07 sixth series, ticks 4 ms and 2 ms before the instant, prompt assemblies 1 ms and 2 ms after it, the
   third storm printing `pipeline-fault` where Pulse's log reads parsed `ok` and deduped, by the full marker of
   that chunk and its `evidence/attempt-ledger.md`); what holds from this correction (the selection is unchanged,
   the pairing of a selected digest reads its inference wherever it is stamped, up to the next retry-storm tick;
   the scenario's own digest ticks after the instant and never prints as a canary; a canary tick stamped at or
   after the instant still gets no line, as at d3); that those captures keep what they printed; that the proof is
   a default-suite test over lines built from the recorded stamps, with no drive; and that the decision rule
   counts emissions, never these tokens. No existing line of the file is edited or removed, and the block names no
   environment handle.
8. **Run the gates** of `## Test Commands` in order (all but the three `operator` entries).

9. **The operator pass**, on the operator's word only: the hygiene entry, the pre-CI commit
   (`chore(2026-10-08-capture-canary-pairing-window-corrective): operator pre-CI commit, for the run this chunk's
   verdict reads`), the guarded push, the CI read. Each result is recorded in `evidence/operator-pass.md`.
- `conductor-0.3.0/chunks/2026-10-08-capture-canary-pairing-window-corrective/evidence/` — the failing-first record and the operator pass's results
- `crates/conductor-run/tests/real_model_common/mod.rs` — `canary_attempts` takes the instant and selects ticks by their own stamp; `iso_ms` moves here
- `crates/conductor-run/tests/real_model_live.rs` — the canary block hands the pairing the window and the instant; `iso_ms` imported
- `crates/conductor-run/tests/real_model_grading/canary_pairing.rs` — the helper's call, six new tests, one added assertion
- `contracts/pulse-real-model-leg-posture.md` — one add-only dated block after line 320

No smoke entry and no live leg: this chunk has no boot path and drives nothing, so a status read would print a
prior run's envelope and prove nothing (`.claude/rules/verification-harness.md`, the 2026-09-11 extension). Step
4's failing-first run is a one-shot measurement and is not an entry, because it cannot be re-run after step 5; the
entry that reads its record is. Every git-reading entry names the chunk base, since the operator pass moves HEAD.

title: The replay (the control that decides the design)

data.head: ## The replay (the control that decides the design)

body:
The pairing was ported line for line to a read-only script and replayed over the recorded Pulse log, once per
drive, three ways. Derivation: `pairing-probe-script.txt` run from the repository root; output `pairing-probe.txt`.
| Drive | Pre-fix composition (filter by stamp, then pair) | Selection kept, pairing over the whole window | Whole window, no selection |

| d1 | equals the committed capture's four `canary` lines, line for line; third line `pipeline-fault … parse=none` | third line `surfaced … parse=ok created=false deduped=true`; count `0 ()` | 5 lines: the scenario's own digest (tick 06:32:51.361Z) prints as a fourth `canary:` line |

| d2 | equals the committed capture, line for line; third line `pipeline-fault … parse=none` | third line `surfaced … parse=ok created=false deduped=true`; count `0 ()` | 5 lines, and the count reads `3 (error_rate_spike,…)` |
| d3 | equals the committed capture, line for line: two lines, count `4 (…)` | unchanged: two lines, count `4 (…)` | 5 lines, count `6 (…)` |

So the port is faithful (it reproduces all three committed captures), the defect is reproducible from recorded
lines alone, the corrected selection prints what Pulse's log bears out, and dropping the selection would be wrong
in two ways at once.
File order around each instant, from the same output (offsets are from the emission instant):
| Drive | Third canary tick | Its prompt | Scenario's own tick | Canary parse `ok` | Canary outcome line | Next prompt (the scenario's) |
| d1 | -4 ms | +1 ms | +5006 ms | +5779 ms | +5813 ms, `created=false deduped=true` | +5813 ms, two lines later |
| d2 | -2 ms | +2 ms | +5006 ms | +6325 ms | +6358 ms, `created=false deduped=true` | +6358 ms, two lines later |
| d3 | +11 ms | +15 ms | +5004 ms | +6015 ms | +6048 ms, `created=false deduped=true` | +6048 ms, two lines later |

- **Same-stamp order:** the incident outcome line precedes the next prompt assembly in file order on 4 of 4
  same-millisecond pairs in the three windows (the three above and d2's second, at +12290 ms).

- **Stamp order is not file order everywhere:** d1's window holds 1 adjacent stamp inversion in 6200 line pairs
  (d2 and d3 hold none). The selection therefore reads each tick's own stamp, as it does today, never a cut
  position in the file.

- **d2 carries a tier-2 cue tick 730 ms after the instant** (`error_rate_spike`). It is stamped after the
  instant, so it stays out of the closing count.

1. **What the classifier prints after the fix.** For a canary storm whose tick precedes the instant by
   milliseconds: `canary: surfaced t=… cue_kind=retry_storm cue_priority_tier=autonomous parse=ok created=false
   deduped=true skip_reason=none`, the outcome Pulse's own log bears out on d1 and d2. **How the scenario's own
   digest is told apart:** by the SIGN of its tick's stamp against the instant, never by distance and never by an
   identity Pulse's lines do not carry. The instant is taken at `timeline.execute`'s open, before the scenario's
   first emission, and a tier-1 `retry_storm` digest needs the Autonomous band, which the scenario's storm reaches
   about 5 s after the instant (+5002, +5001, +5000 ms on the three drives). So the scenario's tick is always
   stamped after the instant: it is never selected, it gets no `canary:` line, and as the next retry-storm tick it
   closes the last canary's segment. The rule errs one way only: a canary storm whose tick lands after the
   instant (d3, +11 ms) gets no line, exactly as today. It never prints the scenario's digest as a canary.

2. **The failing-first control.** The new d1- and d2-shaped tests, run against the pre-fix composition, read
   `pipeline-fault` with `parse=none`; the replay's first column is that reading, taken from recorded lines.
   Implement reproduces it in Rust before the change and records it.

3. **Architecture's registries are not grown.** No architecture text describes the pairing window: the sweep
   below finds it in obs-plan and test-plan only, and the sixth series' architecture entry says so in its Kept
   line (`arch-history.md`, last item). So this chunk expects no architecture amendment at all. Measured at
   take-up: §Occupied Resources 38114 B, §Established Decisions 38082 B of 38115 B
   (re-derived: `python -X utf8 scripts/arch-registry-check.py measure --file .andromeda/architecture.md`).

title: What the proof does not reach

data.head: ## What the proof does not reach

body:
- The default-suite tests exercise the shared function, selection and pairing together. The gated capture's CALL
  of it is one line; it is proven by compile and lint under `--features live-pulse` and by a source literal, never
  by a run. What the capture binary prints on a next real drive is unmeasured until someone drives it, and no
  drive is planned here.

- The in-test lines are built from recorded stamps and line kinds. They prove the capture's reading of those
  lines, never that Pulse surfaced a digest.

- A canary tick stamped after the instant stays unclassified by the capture (the d3 shape). Recovering it would
  need an identity Pulse's digest lines do not carry, or a read of a different surface; both are outside the pick.

contract attach the input-boundary duties. He ruled by dialog on 2026-10-08 that it does not, and that the
sentence is corrected (`inputs#I4` §1; the founder, 2026-10-08, relayed verbatim by the pc overseer). So the
contract gains one dated add-only block, the close record carries his words, and the masters are the wrap's,
quoting him. Nothing was written on a reading (`inputs#I2`).

1. **Read the ledger.** Fire the coverage read and one `show --id` per capability, `v3-01` through `v3-11`
   (the tool lists no whole ledger). Every row of the close record's table comes from these reads: `id`, `title`,
   `method`, `status`, `chunk`, and the first clause of `ref` up to its first dash. Nothing is typed from memory or
   from this plan.

2. **Re-point the first comment.** In `scripts/agent-run.ps1`, on the comment line that reads "waits on the child
   alone (host-win32.md)", replace the parenthetical with `(.claude/rules/verification-harness.md, 2026-09-16)`.
   - Change that one line and no other. Do not re-wrap the comment block. ASCII only.

3. **Re-point the second comment.** In `scripts/a11y-token-witness.ps1`, on the comment line that ends "does not
   (host-win32.md).", replace the parenthetical with
   `(.claude/docs/session-learnings.md, the 2026-09-11 host-leaf entry)`.
   - Change that one line and no other. ASCII only.

4. **Write `evidence/next-version-direction.md`.** Three sections, in this order:
   - `## The founder's direction, in his words` — one line saying when and how it was given (by dialog,
     2026-10-07, relayed by the pc overseer, `inputs#I1` §5), then the quote, whole, inside one pair of `«` `»`
     marks, copied from this chunk's `inputs/` copy of the relay. The relay wraps the quote over three block-quote
     lines; join them with single spaces and drop the `>` marks. Add nothing inside the marks. Use no other `«` in
     the file.
   - `## Proposals that are not the founder's` — one line saying the pc overseer's relay lists them and that the
     relay does not say who first proposed each; none is his and none is decided. Then the four, as the relay
     names them: a sanctioned capture path; expected answers per event; structured fields in the model's answer
     or a semantic grader; the unmeasured live print of the corrected classifier.
   - `## Where a next version meets this` — the wrap appends one open line to `.andromeda/residuals.md` that
     carries the quote and points here; no `conductor-0.4.0` directory exists and none is created.
   - Then compare the file's quote with the relay copy's quote, whitespace folded, and keep the reading (both
     character counts and whether they are equal) for step 5. Research measured the relay's quote at 344
     characters by this fold; record what this comparison measures.

5. **Write `evidence/version-close.md`.** Sections, in this order:
   - `## Where 0.3.0 stands` — the coverage line as the tool printed it, the date, the tool's stamp.
   - `## The 11 capabilities` — one table row per capability: the id in backticks as the row's first cell, then
     title, method, owning chunk, measured basis. The basis is the ledger's `ref`, shortened to its first clause,
     with the owning chunk's folder as the pointer. For `v3-02` and `v3-03` keep the configuration and the owner
     arm the `ref` names (per a11y-plan §11 A11y Anti-Patterns § Strategy). For `v3-08` and `v3-09` name the
     harvest-tier test as the basis and offer no envelope state as proof (per obs-plan §4 Critical Path 1,
     Real-model posture).
   - `## Three statements` — the three sentences of `scope.md` item 2, each followed by where it is recorded: the
     ledger's notes on `v3-09` for the first and third, obs-plan §4 and test-plan §6 for the second. The first
     names its holding tests, `v3_09_is_met_by_the_2026_10_07_sixth_series` and the ref test the ledger gives. The
     third states the exception by location only.
   - `## Limits known and not closed` — named as limits, not as debts of this version:
     - the grading rule grades `Identified` a rank 1 that names `conductor` as a whole word and also names the
       canary; unchanged for 0.3.0; no hypothesis of the sixth series named the canary;
     - what the capture binary prints on a next real drive is unmeasured until someone drives it;
     - the third position's live record on this host: 2 misses of 4 runs, a rate and not a cause;
     - limits the plans already state, each cited and not re-argued: the PowerShell red path is read from the
       script and not measured (test-plan §3 `run`); SC 2.3.3 is asserted from the compiled rule (a11y-plan §6
       Visual Design Verification, Motion tokens); the Linux `xvfb` job is an unrun target (test-plan §9 Matrix
       builds); the control-panel-launched half of critical path 7 is owed (test-plan §1 Critical paths).
   - `## The founder's ruling on the contract's readers` — copied from this chunk's `inputs/` copy of the ruling
     relay (`inputs#I4` §1), each part marked for whose words it is:
     - the question as the pc overseer put it to him, verbatim, in its own language;
     - his pick, verbatim, marked as his: the one line the relay gives between `«` `»` after "His pick";
     - the text of the option he picked, verbatim, marked as the option's text as he saw it;
     - when and how: by dialog, 2026-10-08, relayed by the pc overseer.
     Then, in this record's own words and marked so: what it settles (a test-tier digest read is not the runtime
     read the contract's notice names; the duties do not attach; the notice stands for a real runtime read), and
     the three places it lands — the contract's dated block (step 6), the registry row and its key line, and
     security-plan's fixed-path-manifests row or a dated note beside it, the last two written by the wrap.
     Add no translation inside any quoted part.
   - `## Open, with no owner` — the three items of `scope.md` §Noticed at take-up, in their widened form.
   - `## The four carried items` — what was done with each: comments re-pointed here; the exception stated here;
     the registry freed and the sites corrected by the wrap, in that order and with both ordinals kept; the
     contract's own sentence corrected here by a dated block, on the founder's ruling.
   - `## What this close did not do` — no merge into `main`, no tag, no release, no publishing version bump, no
     branch deletion; no GPU run, no live drive; no new development entry, no route for a next version, no
     next-version directory. Say that each waits for the founder's word.
   - `## The next version's direction` — one line pointing at `next-version-direction.md`.
   - `## Checks` — step 4's comparison reading; the count of table rows.
   - Write no model text anywhere in the file. Do not open the frozen capture-run chunk's `report.md`, and copy
     from no capture. Name data dirs by leaf. Give the file no name that starts `rm-capture`.

6. **Add the dated block to the contract.** In `contracts/pulse-real-model-leg-posture.md`, directly after line
   49, the last line of the `## Regime` section, and before the next heading: a blank line, then one block in the
   file's own form for a dated note, opening
   `[corrected 2026-10-08 (2026-10-08-version-close-on-measured-evidence,` and naming the founder's ruling by
   dialog, relayed by the pc overseer. In English, like the rest of the file, it says four things:
   - the sentence "No Rust code reads it" is false as written since the 2026-09-30 series;
   - no shipped code reads the file; a test helper in `conductor-run`'s real-model harvest holds each dated
     section by sha256 and parses nothing from it;
   - that digest hold is not the runtime read this section's notice names, so the committed-manifest
     input-boundary duties do not attach;
   - the notice stands as written for a real runtime read: were shipped code to read or parse the file, the
     duties attach in full.
   Edit and remove no existing line of the file. Touch no other section. Do not touch the helper or any code
   (`inputs#I4` §2).
7. **Run the gates** of `## Test Commands`, in block order.

8. **Operator pass** (the operator's acts, never /implement's): the hygiene entry, the pre-CI commit, the push
   entry, the CI read. Record each result in `evidence/operator-pass.md`.
- `conductor-0.3.0/chunks/2026-10-08-version-close-on-measured-evidence/evidence/version-close.md` — the close record
- `conductor-0.3.0/chunks/2026-10-08-version-close-on-measured-evidence/evidence/next-version-direction.md` — the founder's words, and under their own heading the proposals that are not his
- `scripts/agent-run.ps1` — one comment line re-pointed; no executed line moves
- `scripts/a11y-token-witness.ps1` — one comment line re-pointed; no executed line moves
- `contracts/pulse-real-model-leg-posture.md` — one dated add-only block at the end of its Regime section, on the founder's ruling; no existing line moves

No smoke entry and no live leg: this chunk has no boot path and drives nothing; its one edit to a harness
shell is a comment line, and the test plan declares no boot-smoke trigger list. Four entries hold step 6's
block: the contract loses no line, has one hunk, has it only at the end of its Regime section, and that hunk
opens with this chunk's dated note. No mutation run: the instrument
belongs to the epoch-boundary code audit (test-plan §9 Scoped mutation audit). The two `.ps1` files cannot be
executed on this host, which carries no `pwsh`; their only executing proof is the CI run the operator pass
reads. Every git-reading entry names the chunk base, since the operator pass moves HEAD.

title: The byte arithmetic of CARRY 3 and CARRY 4

data.head: ### The byte arithmetic of CARRY 3 and CARRY 4

body:
- Headroom in §Occupied Resources: 1 B (38114 of 38115 B, `scripts/arch-registry-check.py measure --file
  .andromeda/architecture.md`, 2026-10-08).

- The posture row's false sentence is 106 B: "It is the **SECOND** `contracts/` member with **NO Rust reader**,
  taking the P-025 regime above unchanged."

- `[superseded at the P5 review, 2026-10-08 (inputs#I4 §3; inputs#I5)]` The first arithmetic paid for the
  correction by dropping "FIRST" from the P-025 row (−34 B) and rewriting the posture sentence without its
  ordinal (+32 B). The operator overruled it: the playbook's rule note says a historical ordinal "is not a
  uniqueness claim and stays as written" (`.andromeda/playbook.md:243`, confirmed with the user on 2026-09-18).
  Both ordinals stay as written.

- With both ordinals kept, three drafts of the posture sentence, measured by script over the row at HEAD
  (`fb48cee`), each keeping "the **SECOND** `contracts/` member with **NO Rust reader**" and the regime clause:
  - "… **NO Rust reader** but a test-tier digest hold (its `## Regime`), taking …" — 152 B, +46 B, 45 B to free;
  - "… **NO Rust reader** at runtime (a test-tier digest hold: its `## Regime`), taking …" — 160 B, +54 B, 53 B to
    free;
  - "… **NO runtime Rust reader**, taking …" — 114 B, +8 B, 7 B to free. This one names no reader and points
    nowhere; it changes the bolded phrase itself.
  The kind and tier of the reader live in the contract's dated block and in security-plan; the row points at the
  first (`inputs#I4` §3).

- One freeing candidate that is neither an ordinal nor a phrase a rule pins: the posture row repeats the P-025
  row's face-field sentence one row below it. "Carries `sut_version` · `captured_at` · `pinned_at` · `provenance`
  on its own face." becomes "Carries the same four face fields.", −52 B. It is the by-reference form the
  registry already uses. The phrase stands in no playbook rule and no gate reads it
  (`git grep -c -E 'on its own face|sut_version' -- .andromeda/playbook.md scripts/arch-registry-check.py
  crates/conductor-core/tests crates/conductor-report/tests .claude/rules` prints no file).

- Predicted with the first draft: 38114 − 52 + 46 = 38108 B. Free first, then correct. The second draft with the
  same freeing lands at 38116 B, 1 B over, so it needs more. These are arithmetic, not final wording; the wording
  is the wrap's, measured by the same instrument and proven lossless by it.

- If the wrap finds the by-reference form is not lossless, or that no true sentence fits without breaking the
  ordinal rule or the threshold, it stops and shows the operator the arithmetic (`inputs#I4` §3).
- §Established Decisions (38082 B) is not grown by this chunk: nothing the close states needs a word there.

- The key file's line and the two leaves are outside both measured sections. "no Rust code reads" becomes
  "no shipped code reads" (+3 B per site), true of both members.

title: The rider — does security-plan's fixed-path-manifests row owe the test-binary reader a row

data.head: ### The rider — does security-plan's fixed-path-manifests row owe the test-binary reader a row

body:
What the code does: one test helper opens the contract by a hard-coded repo-relative name, rooted at
`CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`; reads no handle and no operator value; cuts one section; compares a digest. No value from
the file reaches any decision except "equal to the pin or not". A read fault carries the name and the error
kind. A missing section or a mismatch is a hard failure.
What the record says:

- The row's own criterion: "a committed artifact parsed at runtime earns its row whether or not a shipped binary
  is the one parsing it" (`.andromeda/security-plan.md:113`). Its four members are TOML manifests parsed into
  typed values that steer a run.

- For a row: the 2026-09-06 escalation resolved "record the reader" for the first test-binary reader of a
  `contracts/` file ("an unrecorded reader is the drift"); the 2026-09-13 P-025 amendment left this row unmoved
  because the member was reader-less, which a measured reader re-opens.

- Against a row in THIS place: digest-held committed files already have a home, the real-model capture ingest
  row (2026-09-30), not the manifests row; and 2026-10-02 holds a reasoned no-row decision for a test that reads
  no value.
- The contract's own `## Regime` notice: the duties "attach in full" if the file becomes runtime-read.

The reading: the helper does not parse the contract, it holds it. So it is outside the manifests row's class by
that row's own word "parsed". But the per-reader principle says a reader is recorded, never assumed, and the
honest record is one of two writes: a clause that names this reader (in the manifests row or beside the digest
pins in the ingest row), or a dated note that it sits outside the row and why. Choosing between them — and
deciding whether a test-time digest read is the "runtime-read" the contract's notice names — fixes where the
clause's edge is. That is a reading of what a boundary clause covers. It is brought to the review and written
nowhere by this chunk.

The ruling (`inputs#I4` §1): the operator put the question to the founder by dialog on 2026-10-08. His pick,
verbatim: «Нет, исправить фразу (Recommended)». A test-tier digest read is not the runtime read the `## Regime`
notice names, and the duties do not attach. The notice stands for a real runtime read. Where it lands
(`inputs#I4` §2): one dated add-only block at the end of the contract's `## Regime` section; the close record,
in his relayed words; the masters, written by the wrap and quoting him. No code changes and the helper is not
touched. Checked at this re-plan: the six headings a digest pins are the dated ones
(`git grep -h -A3 -F 'pre_registered(' -- crates/conductor-run/tests/real_model_grading`), so a block inside
`## Regime` moves no pin; and no live file cites the contract by line number (every hit of
`git grep -n -E 'pulse-real-model-leg-posture\.md`?:[0-9]'` sits in a frozen chunk folder). The date the block
states was re-derived: the first test read of the contract landed in commit `b8e7bca`, 2026-09-30
(`git log --reverse -S'committed("contracts/pulse-real-model-leg-posture.md")' -- crates/conductor-run/tests`);
the helper took its present name on 2026-10-04 (`91f0f04`).

title: What an evolve diagnosis and a code audit cost and answer

data.head: ### What an evolve diagnosis and a code audit cost and answer

body: - Both run only when the operator invokes them (`disable-model-invocation: true` in each skill).

- **Evolve diagnosis** of Epoch 5b. Question it answers: which pipeline frictions recurred across this epoch's
  eight chunks, by type and cost, as proposals for the founder. Its input is 220 friction records carrying this
  epoch's label (`grep -o '"epoch": ?"Epoch 5b[^"]*"' .andromeda/friction-log.ndjson`, one spelling). It changes
  nothing. The two diagnoses of 2026-10-04 each took about 9 to 10 minutes from first to last file in their run
  dir and wrote 131 KB and 169 KB. Their token cost is not recorded anywhere this chunk reads.

- **Code audit** at the Epoch 5b boundary. Questions it answers, as test-plan names them: whether
  `conductor-core`'s mutation tier holds without `--copy-vcs true`; roster rows for `member-1` to `member-3`,
  which need their crates' tiers re-run; the timeout rows that seed `conductor-emit`'s gate, which fails closed
  until then. It also appends one metrics snapshot and diffs it against the last. The 2026-10-04 audit's run dir
  spans about 21 minutes of file times and holds nine per-crate mutation result files; that span does not prove
  the mutation runs' own wall-clock, which the run dir does not state in one place. Since that audit no file
  under any crate's `src/` has moved (`git log --since='2026-10-04T12:00:00+02:00' --name-only -- 'crates/*/src'`
  lists none); what moved is test code, the two harness scripts and the posture contract. A mutation tier
  re-run would therefore measure the same shipped code as the last one, against a changed test suite.
- `conductor-0.3.0/chunks/2026-10-08-version-close-on-measured-evidence/evidence/version-close.md` — the close record
- `conductor-0.3.0/chunks/2026-10-08-version-close-on-measured-evidence/evidence/next-version-direction.md` — the founder's words and, under their own heading, the proposals that are not his
- `scripts/agent-run.ps1` — one comment line re-pointed
- `scripts/a11y-token-witness.ps1` — one comment line re-pointed
- `contracts/pulse-real-model-leg-posture.md` — one dated add-only block at the end of its Regime section, on the founder's ruling

- What is written in the contract's own `## Regime` section → blocks: plan-decision. Resolved: first by the
  operator at P4 (`inputs#I3`, the chunk does not touch the contract while the founder is asked), then by the
  founder's ruling (`inputs#I4` §1, `inputs#I5`): the contract gains one dated add-only block.

- Where the founder's direction is recorded, and in what form → blocks: plan-decision. Resolved at P4 by the
  operator (`inputs#I3`): a document in this chunk's evidence tree plus one `open` residual line; no
  `conductor-0.4.0` directory.

**Working entry (`working-route.md:102`):** Version close on measured evidence — every capability verified or
deferred on a measured basis with a named owner.

**Matrix target:** none. The ledger reads 11 of 11 verified, 0 deferred, 0 unclaimed, done-test YES
(`matrix.py coverage`, read at take-up 2026-10-08). This chunk claims no capability; it states what the ledger
already holds and re-grades nothing.

**Why it exists:** it is the last entry of 0.3.0. After it this line stops: no new development entry starts
without the founder's word (`inputs#I1` §4; the handoff's Position says the same).

1. **The version's close record**, a committed document a reader of 0.3.0 opens. It lists each of the 11
   capabilities with its measured basis and the chunk that owns it, read from the ledger and never re-derived.
   It carries the three sentences below, the limits known and not closed, what was done with each CARRY, and what
   the close did not do.
   - Its home is the chunk's own `evidence/` tree, with the wrap's `report.md` carrying the three sentences in its
     Outcome. Verified at P3: the version dir holds no close document and no tool reads one there; the prior
     version closed on a release chunk with none; the master record's link leads a reader to the chunk folder. The
     lean is named at the P5 review for the operator to overrule.

2. **Three sentences, carried as the relay states them** (`inputs#I1` §2). Each was read at P3 against the
   ledger's notes on `v3-09` (`matrix.py show --id v3-09`) and the two plans' dated notes:
   - `v3-09` is verified on the sixth pre-registered series, three drives, and no wider. The pass is not
     attributed to the Pulse-side remedy: no prompt was recorded in that series, and the capture run on the
     pre-remedy build also read three `Identified`. The third position's live record on this host stays as
     stated: 2 misses of 4 live runs. Verified at P3: the ledger's sixth-series note says each of these in so many
     words ("met on THREE DRIVES and read no wider", "NOT attributed", "2 misses of 4 — a rate, not a cause").
   - The capture's pairing-window fix is proven on lines built from the sixth series' recorded stamps, with a
     failing-first reading. What the capture binary prints on a next real drive is unmeasured until someone drives
     it. A canary tick stamped at or after the emission instant still gets no line. Verified at P3: obs-plan §4
     and test-plan §6 each carry the 2026-10-08 note that states this limit; the ledger holds no note of its own on
     it, since the corrective claimed no capability.
   - One known exception to "model text lives only in `evidence/`": one rank-1 model statement stands in the
     frozen capture-run chunk's `report.md`. The founder ruled it stays ("Оставить как есть", dialog, 2026-10-08).
     The exception is stated without quoting the statement. Verified at P3: the ledger's last note on `v3-09`
     records the ruling and that the version close states the exception.

3. **One limit named as a limit, not as a debt of this version** (`inputs#I1` §2): the grading rule grades
   `Identified` a rank 1 that names `conductor` as a whole word and also names the canary. Left unchanged for
   0.3.0; the sixth series did not lean on it. Verified at P3: the ledger says the rule "is left unchanged for
   0.3.0 on the overseer's decision, the weakness recorded for 0.4.0", and that no ranked hypothesis of any sixth
   series drive names the canary identity.
4. **Two comment-only re-points in product scripts** (CARRY 1; `inputs#I1` §3, the operator's decision).

5. **The sites that say no Rust code reads the posture contract are corrected to what is true** (CARRY 4), after
   bytes are freed in architecture §Occupied Resources (CARRY 3).

6. **The founder's ruling on the contract's readers, recorded where it lands** (CARRY 4's rider; `inputs#I1`
   §3; `inputs#I2`; `inputs#I4`). Research's reading went to the plan review and was written nowhere. The
   operator took the question to the founder, who ruled by dialog on 2026-10-08: a test-tier digest read does not
   attach the input-boundary duties, and the sentence is corrected. So the contract gains one dated add-only
   block, the close record carries his words, and the masters are the wrap's, quoting him.

7. **The founder's direction for the next version, held in his words** where the pipeline keeps a next version's
   direction (`inputs#I1` §5).
8. **The stops stated**: what the close does not do without the founder's word (`inputs#I1` §4).

  amendment with its freeing step. Verified at P3: each master's header bars edits during a phase-loop run, and
  the wrap's apply is the one writer of a key file.

- `[premise-corrected: the claim stands at more than four sites — swept with
  `git grep -i -E 'no rust (code )?read|reader-less'` over the masters, the registries, the playbook, the leaves,
  `contracts/`, `crates/` and `scripts/`]` The four named sites stand as named. Three more carry the claim or lean
  on it:

    member", "No Rust code reads it", and a notice that "were a future chunk to make it runtime-read, those duties

    among them).

  (`crates/conductor-core/tests/secret_scan_gate.rs:213`). It reads the tree, not a member by name, and the
  corrected wording says "by name" where that matters.

- **The rider question:** does security-plan's fixed-path-manifests row owe the test-binary reader a row. P3
  researched it (`research.md` §The rider). The reading went to the plan review. If the honest answer changes
  what a boundary clause permits, nothing is written on this reading or the operator's: the operator takes it to
  the founder (`inputs#I1` §3; `inputs#I2`). He ruled (`inputs#I4` §1): the duties do not attach. The per-reader
