title: F1 — The routine a11y arm is not gated in CI, and the keyboard half its requirement names lives in a different suite

data.head: ## F1 — The routine a11y arm is not gated in CI, and the keyboard half its requirement names lives in a different suite

body: **OBSERVED — two independent gaps behind one deferred capability (`v2-24`, "A11y CI gate and violation JSON").**

Its acceptance reads: the routine a11y specs — axe under `wcag2a`/`wcag2aa`/`wcag21aa`, the colorjs.io token-pair
contrast ratios, and the hold-free Operable pair (SC 2.1.1 keyboard reachability of the idle console's controls,
SC 2.4.3 focus order per a11y-plan §5 `run-console-idle`) — run in the `a11y` CI job on the measured Windows
WebView2 runner.

1. **The endpoint never appears on the hosted image, and the cause is unmeasured.** Locally the driven arm passes
   over the shipped bundle: 12 passing / 2 skipped (the expected skip set), banner `[webview2 152.0.4191.66
   windows]`, measured 2026-09-10 during the release chunk (implement, re-run verbatim at its light gate). On the runner the app boots — `EBWebView`
   present, three `msedgewebview2` children, the staged `conductor-tauri.jsonl` shows the UI calling
   `list_scenarios` / `coverage_matrix` / `run_report` / `run_envelope` within one second — yet
   `DevToolsActivePort` is never seen within 90 s. The reading is identical across CI runs `34162118841`,
   `34251573399`, `34256490781`, `34280136892` and `34365300658`, and identical under runtime 151 and 152, which
   falsifies the runtime-major hypothesis. `tauri-driver`'s bind on `:4444` is intermittent (four `ECONNREFUSED`
   in 1.56 s on one run, two on the next) and is therefore not the stable obstacle. What remains UNMEASURED: the
   WebView2/Edge policy state on the image (a registry read is a one-line probe), the module version the host
   processes actually loaded (image names only were captured), and any session / service-account property of the
   runner. The current record names these as candidates; none has been probed on the runner.

2. **The stated keyboard half is not in the routine arm at all.** Measured at the 2026-09-07 chunk's P3: the
   routine arm carries ZERO `browser.keys` calls — every keyboard, focus-trap and restoration assertion lives in
   `operator-hold.e2e.ts`, the driven suite. The capability's concretization failed on exactly this at that
   chunk's P5 and the cap was left pooled. So even with the endpoint problem solved, the requirement as written
   would still not be satisfiable by the routine arm.

**EXPECT.** The runner cause is measured rather than listed — one probing pass with named one-line probes, whose
reading is recorded whatever it says — and the capability then reaches one of two honest terminals: the routine
arm runs green in the `a11y` CI job, or the CI half is closed as a ratified permanent exclusion whose basis is a
MEASURED cause and whose owner is named. Independently, the requirement and the suites agree about where keyboard
and focus-order coverage lives: either the routine arm carries it, or the requirement names the driven suite as
its owner and says what CI gates instead.

title: F2 — Committed scenarios carry checks that cannot pass by construction, and tiers below their own phase duration

data.head: ## F2 — Committed scenarios carry checks that cannot pass by construction, and tiers below their own phase duration

body: **OBSERVED — one class, three shapes, all measured live during 0.2.0's last two chunks.**

1. **The `CountAtLeast` family is structurally unsatisfiable.** Conductor sums `evidence_count` from `span_refs`
   (`crates/conductor-verify/src/extract.rs:116`) and grades every `CountAtLeast` against that count whatever the
   scenario declares (`extract.rs:55`); Pulse writes `EvidenceRefs.span_ids: Vec::new()` at its only production
   incident-construction site (`andromeda-pulse pulse-app/src/inference_runtime.rs:871`) and
   `incidents_router.rs:67` derives `evidence_count` from that same empty vector. A `CountAtLeast >= 1` therefore
   evaluates `0 >= 1` forever. Three committed scenarios carry a live `kind = "CountAtLeast"` key:
   `scenarios/constellation-severity-live-wiring.toml:53`, `findings-counter-refresh.toml:49`,
   `pulse-run-contract.toml:58`. The row is non-blocked only because an unmet sample floor routes to
   `ClaimClass::CalibrationRegion` (`conductor-verify/src/slo.rs:97-100`) — the verdict is honest, the assertion
   is empty.

2. **A Hard `Contains` on an inferred token measured dead on its first live drive.**
   `scenarios/cross-incident-recurrence.toml:42-45` declares `Contains` / `Hard` / `"Previously seen"`; the
   scenario's own header concedes the token is inferred. Driven live on 2026-09-10 it returned `[FAIL]`, exit 1,
   state `Fail`, with read-back succeeding — the corpus was read and the token is not in it.

3. **Tier declarations below their own phase duration.** Of 36 committed scenarios, 17 declare an SLO tier
   shorter than the sum of their own phase `gap_ms`: 9 are the operator-ratified `<90s`-as-honest-bucket posture,
   2 exceed every tier in the closed set (`ack-cooldown` 370 s at `<20s`, `severity-tier-autonomous` 120 s at
   `<5s`), and 6 could hold a larger tier. `constellation-severity-live-wiring` carries this defect on top of
   shape 1 — measured 30 212 ms against its own `<20s` deadline.

Retiring any of these is not a TOML-only edit: the declarations are pinned by tests, and at least one
(`crates/conductor-core/src/scenario.rs:1188-1202`) is an inline `#[cfg(test)]` module inside `src/`, which the
project's prescribed companion sweep (`grep -rln "<scenario-name>" crates/**/tests`) structurally cannot see. The
precedent for the class is recorded at `.andromeda/architecture-amendments.md:403` (2026-08-21), the ground on
which five severity-lifecycle scenarios were retired to declare-only.

**EXPECT.** Every committed scenario's declared checks are satisfiable by construction against a live Pulse, or
are retired to declare-only **as a class in one pass** with their pinning tests updated in the same change; and
every scenario's tier either fits its own phase duration or carries a stated reason why it does not. The outcome
is auditable by a mechanical check that a fresh reader can re-run.

title: F3 — The hue budget is graded through an instrument that cannot resolve it (cross-project; blocked on Pulse)

data.head: ## F3 — The hue budget is graded through an instrument that cannot resolve it (cross-project; blocked on Pulse)

body:
**OBSERVED.** Pulse delegated four timing budgets to Conductor. Three are graded hard at real measured values and
are verified under `v2-20`: P-027 constellation discovery 702.4 ms against ≤5000, P-037 report render 1 ms and
0 ms against ≤2000, P-045 counter refresh worst 7.0 ms of 269 in-window samples against ≤1000. The fourth, P-025
(hue shift ≤2 s), measured 35 581 ms and 36 705 ms on 2026-08-21, and `v2-20`'s acceptance was narrowed to three
budgets by operator ratification with P-025 routed forward. The 2026-09-06 re-drive concluded the bound is
UNMEASURABLE through `metric.constellation.hue_update_ms`. Measured at Pulse HEAD `83d4060`: that metric is a
Tauri command (`record_constellation_hue_latency`) whose `duration_ms` is computed in the FRONTEND canvas
(`pulse-app/ui/src/canvas/frame-metrics.ts`) and merely logged by the backend
(`crates/ui-bridge/src/telemetry.rs:279`); its start point is tied to a tick-refreshed `last_seen`, so its
resolution is the lifecycle tick, not the flip. The 35 s figure is therefore the reading of an instrument that
cannot see the quantity, not a proven pipeline latency — the true hue-shift latency is at present measured by
nothing.

**EXPECT.** Conductor states the measurement contract P-025 needs — which observable, at what resolution, over
what window, and what would constitute a hard grade — in a form Pulse can implement; and once Pulse emits it,
Conductor re-drives `halo-hue-encoding` and grades P-025 hard at its real value, restoring the fourth budget.

**SEQUENCING.** The instrument is Pulse's to ship. The re-drive entry is therefore `BLOCKED-ON` that Pulse-side
emission and must not be placed as if Conductor could satisfy it alone; the contract half (what Conductor needs)
is unblocked and can land first.

title: F4 — Every live leg runs under canned L4, so Conductor proves plumbing and never interpretation

data.head: ## F4 — Every live leg runs under canned L4, so Conductor proves plumbing and never interpretation

body:
**OBSERVED.** Every live leg in 0.2.0 ran with `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC=true`, where a canned
`L4Output` replaces the inference. That is what makes the legs reproducible — the in-lane
scenario round's light gate re-measured its three legs within 34 ms of the implement round (18 169 → 18 145 ·
35 120 → 35 111 · 30 212 → 30 246 ms), and the release chunk's legs reproduced within milliseconds too — and it
is also what bounds what they prove:
"Conductor green" today means Pulse's plumbing carried a known payload, never that Pulse's interpretation is
trustworthy. The diagnostic-quality cluster P-031 / P-033 / P-034 / P-044 is pinned meanwhile in
`conductor_core::UNBACKED_AUTO` (`crates/conductor-core/src/drift.rs:61`, asserted by `check_scenario_backing`)
rather than exercised. Pulse's own memo calls the real-model path the single most important test in all of Pulse.
The prerequisite Conductor owed for it is already met: `v2-09` (real per-check read-back extraction) is
`verified` in 0.2.0. Recorded as a residual on 2026-08-09 with `target: 0.3.0`.

**EXPECT.** A live leg exists that runs with deterministic mode OFF, injects a known root cause, and asserts that
the top hypothesis identifies it — with the non-determinism handled as a property of the leg (operator-gated,
never a CI gate, its grading stated in advance) rather than by retrying until it passes. The diagnostic-quality
cluster is then backed by an exercised path instead of a drift pin.

title: Who this is for, and why now

data.head: ## Who this is for, and why now

body:
Conductor's single operator, immediately before attention moves to Pulse. The version's whole reason for
existing is that a harness left in this state would keep reporting green over claims it never measured, and
the cost of that is paid later and by someone reading the ledger rather than the evidence. The intent states
the bar directly: switching attention to Pulse must leave **nothing here that is true only by wording**.

- **The a11y CI gate reaches an honest terminal** (`v2-24`, the one deferred capability). The hosted-runner
  cause is *measured* rather than listed as candidates — and the capability then either runs green in CI or
  is closed as a ratified permanent exclusion resting on that measured cause. Separately, the requirement
  and the suites are made to agree about where keyboard and focus-order coverage actually lives.

- **Committed scenarios stop carrying checks that cannot pass.** The structurally-dead assertion class is
  retired *as a class in one pass*, pinning tests updated in the same change; every scenario's SLO tier
  either fits its own phase duration or states why it does not; and the result is auditable by a mechanical
  check a fresh reader can re-run.

- **The fourth delegated budget gets an instrument.** Conductor states the measurement contract P-025 needs
  in a form Pulse can implement, and re-drives the grade once Pulse emits it.

- **One live leg proves interpretation, not plumbing.** Deterministic L4 off, a known root cause injected,
  the top hypothesis asserted to identify it — with the non-determinism handled as a stated property of the
  leg, never by retrying until it passes.

Named in the intent so the intake does not mint work for them: **`incident_events`-through-MCP** (a
PULSE-side capability gap — no MCP tool surfaces that table at any width, already routed to Pulse's 0.4.0
incubator; it stays a residual here), **Pulse's own `P-075` bookkeeping** (a decision in Pulse's ledger, not
Conductor work), and **release/bundle work** (done in 0.2.0; owed only if a 0.3.0 change moves it).

Every capability below is `verified` or explicitly `deferred` with a named owner and a measured basis — and
for this version specifically, **no capability closes on a narrowing that a later reader would have to
re-derive.** Where a bound genuinely cannot be measured, the record says what would measure it and who owns
that; where an assertion cannot pass, it is retired rather than left standing as decoration. The blocked
half of the hue-budget work is expected to remain blocked on Pulse and is routed as such — a version that
ends with that entry still `BLOCKED-ON` its named clearing event is a version that closed honestly.

`status` verb is untouched, and the `--live` arm is edited but never fired, because ports 4317/4318 are shared
with Pulse's builder (`inputs#I1` §6). Every entry below binds only `:0` ports. The one reach to

(research.md §Files inspected). The PowerShell twin is measured by a parse here and run whole by CI's dogfood
step on its Windows runner. There is no headful self-verify: the chunk removes the only UI. The removed
`--e2e` token's refusal is proven by the census (`--e2e` appears nowhere in either shell, so only the existing
unknown-token `usage:` branch can take it), never by firing it: on the untouched tree the same call would build
the release bundle and start the e2e leg. `evidence/lock-delta.md` and `evidence/supply-chain.md` are written
by step 11 from the outputs of the lock, audit and deny entries below, so no entry carries `artifact` for them.

- (arch) The workspace's members are the eight remaining `conductor-*` crates. `cargo build --workspace --locked`
  exits 0, and the standalone sweep (`for p in conductor-core … --lib --locked …`) exits 0 for each library crate
  and for `conductor-cli --bins` (per architecture §Established Decisions [Module Boundaries]).

- (arch / security) The committed `Cargo.lock` holds no window-toolkit package (the `grep -c -E '^name =
  "(tauri|…)"$' Cargo.lock` entry reads 0). It is the base lock pruned: the `comm -13` entry reads 0 added or moved
  pairs, and `evidence/lock-delta.md` lists every removed pair with its count (per security-plan §Dependency
  Security).

- (security) With the advisory-db copy porcelain-clean before and after, `cargo audit` exits 0, and `cargo deny
  check advisories bans licenses sources` exits 0 printing neither `advisory-not-detected` nor
  `license-not-encountered`. Every `deny.toml` entry left names a package in the new lock, and none was added (per
  security-plan §Dependency Security).

- (tests) `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run` exits 0 with no frontend step in it, `cargo test --workspace --lib
  --bins --tests` exits 0, and `cargo llvm-cov report --fail-under-lines 60 …` passes over the smaller workspace
  (per test-plan §3 `run`, §4 Framework, §10 Coverage thresholds).

- (tests / a11y) `.github/workflows/ci.yml` holds the one job `rust`. Its ten gate steps and the
  `agent-latest.jsonl` upload are each present by name. The file holds no `continue-on-error`, and its only `if:`
  lines are the three upload steps'. No window reference stays in the workflow, the manifests, `.gitignore` or
  either harness shell (the `git grep … --e2e|a11y:driven` entry prints nothing) (per test-plan §9, a11y-plan §9
  CI Integration and §11 CI).

- (obs / tests) CI on the push carrying the operator pass's pre-CI commit reads `verdict: green`, its check list
  naming neither the `A11y gate` nor the `Frontend gate`. That run includes the obs conformance +
  zero-unlogged-panics gate and the `agent-latest.jsonl` upload, both present by name above. The report names the
  run id (per obs-plan §9 Log conformance check; `inputs#I1` §5).

- (layouts) The verb set is unchanged: `crates/conductor-cli/src/cli.rs`, which declares `Commands`, is
  byte-identical to the base `321dc8f` (the `git diff --quiet 321dc8f… -- crates/conductor-cli/src/cli.rs` entry)
  (per layout-templates §cli Component — Primary navigation (verb structure)).

- Spec anchors: architecture §Established Decisions [Module Boundaries] · [CI/CD] · §Infrastructure Patterns →
  Build system · CI/CD approach · §Occupied Resources (Ports · Environment variables) · §Cross-cutting Patterns
  (Trust boundary); security-plan §Dependency Security · §Security Anti-Patterns → Code Patterns (rule (b)) ·
  §Secret Management; test-plan §3 `run` · §4 Framework · §9 · §10; obs-plan §9 · §11; a11y-plan §9 · §11;
  design-system §Surface: cli; layout-templates §cli Primary screens (commands).

- Research files inspected: `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` (via `cargo metadata`), `deny.toml`,
  `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `scripts/agent-run.{sh,ps1}`, `.gitignore`, `scripts/mutation-roster.toml`,
  `crates/conductor-tauri/{Cargo.toml,src/main.rs,src/commands.rs}`, `crates/conductor-cli/src/{cli,main,pause,
  render}.rs`, `crates/conductor-cli/src/commands/report.rs`, the `conductor-run` fixture and harvest tests.
- External inputs: `inputs#I1` (the phase directive), `inputs#I2` (the operator's invocation and the founder's word).

- Graph: two rust-plane queries, trace `.andromeda/runs/2026-10-11T01-52-22-phase/tree-query-2026-10-11-conductors-window-retired.json`.
  No surviving crate-private item loses its last use. `drive_run` @ `crates/conductor-run/src/drive.rs:53`,
  `read_envelope` @ `crates/conductor-run/src/envelope.rs:47` and `validate_selection` @
  `crates/conductor-core/src/scenario_catalog.rs:79` keep test callers and `pub use` re-exports only.

- Running `cargo update` / `cargo generate-lockfile` to refresh the lock — rejected. Either can move versions the
  removal has no reason to touch, and the prune-only entry would then read a delta that is not the removal's.

- Gating the a11y job off (`if: false`, `continue-on-error`) or leaving the strict-verdict plumbing with nothing to
  skip — rejected. The gate leaves whole (a11y-plan §11 CI).

- Adding a `deny.toml` ignore or allow to turn the gate green — rejected. The justified-exception mechanism is for
  a non-actionable item a new dependency pulls, and this chunk adds none (security-plan §Dependency Security).

- Giving the four functions that lose their only entry point their commands in this chunk — rejected. "The
  command line reaches every function" is `Panel-shaped types retired`'s stated subject (`working-route.md:13`),
  and the catalogue listing needs a new command word, which halts for the operator's word (`inputs#I1` §6).
  Leaned per working-route.md:13 and v4-01's requirement line.

- Touching the panel-shaped types, the two webview fixtures, `cross_surface_parity.rs` or the Tauri-naming doc
  comments in surviving code — rejected here. They are `:13`'s, and the comments the rest go to `No-survivor
  sweep` (`:136`). Leaving them breaks no gate: they compile without `tauri`, and `dead_code` does not fire on a
  reachable pub item (research.md §Graph impact).
- Firing `run --live`, or any run binding 4317/4318 — not in this chunk (`inputs#I1` §6).
- Removing the Windows runner or the PowerShell twin — rejected. Both are `Linux-only base CI`'s (`:15`).

- **Function reach — the B4 answer** (research.md §Function reach; `inputs#I1` §3). When the window goes, four
  functions lose their only entry point. All four are given their command by the next entry, `Panel-shaped types
  retired` (`:13`), whose text is "command line reaches every function":
  1. **The catalogue listing** (the picker): there is no listing verb. A command word is new, so `:13` asks the
     operator for it.
  2. **A graceful mid-run stop**: Ctrl-C ends the process; `drive_run`'s abort flag has no CLI caller.
  3. **A past run's load-envelope standing**: `report` prints the results table only.
  4. **A hold's `[[checklist]]` items**: the CLI hold prints scenario · P-ID · step · prompt.

  `Window grading retired` (`:77`) later removes the hold and checklist themselves. Until `:13` wraps, the four are
  reachable by no command; nothing else is lost. Everything else the window did has a command today: start,
  follow, read, coverage, go/no-go and cleanup.

- **Route carry (wrap route-resolve):** a `CARRY:` on `working-route.md:13` naming the four functions above, with
  research.md §Function reach as their source, so `:13`'s take-up folds them as acceptance.

- **Basis of the stated numbers:**
  - 59 / 47 files: `git ls-files crates/conductor-tauri | wc -l` and `… /ui | wc -l` at `321dc8f`.
  - 562 / 270 / 292 packages: `cargo metadata --format-version 1 --locked --offline`, walked from the eight
    members over every dep kind and platform, at `321dc8f`.

title: Function reach — the window's eight handlers against the command line (B4, `inputs#I1` §3)

data.head: ## Function reach — the window's eight handlers against the command line (B4, `inputs#I1` §3)

body: | window handler | its function | command-line entry today |
| `start_run` | pick + start a scenario or the suite | `conductor run <name\|P-ID>` · `conductor suite [--filter]` |
| `coverage_matrix` · `unbacked_auto` | the capability coverage view + its `(N unbacked)` caption | `conductor coverage [--write]` (`render::coverage_summary`, `UNBACKED_AUTO` read in core) |
| `run_report` | read a past run's results | `conductor report [run_id]` |
| `resolve_operator_hold` | go/no-go at a hold | the `inquire` confirm (`crates/conductor-cli/src/pause.rs:46-62`) |
| `list_scenarios` | list the catalogue (name, P-IDs) before choosing | **none** — no listing verb; the hint at `main.rs:66` points at `scenarios/` |
| `stop_run` | stop a run between scenarios, keeping what finished | **none graceful** — Ctrl-C ends the process; `drive_run`'s abort flag has no CLI caller |

| `run_envelope` | a past run's load-envelope standing | **none** — `report` prints the results table only (`commands/report.rs:17-20`); the caption prints at run time only (`commands/run.rs:33`, `commands/suite.rs:40`) |

| (hold dialog content) | the hold's `[[checklist]]` items (induced + observation) | **none** — `hold_line` + `confirm` print scenario · P-ID · step · prompt, never `hold.checklist` (`render.rs:201-206`, `pause.rs:46-62`) |

- **Removal as one act, both shells** (`scripts/agent-run.sh:294-350` ↔ `scripts/agent-run.ps1:343-410`): every run
  arm has a twin. The closed selector refuses an unknown token with `usage:` and exit 2, so a removed `--e2e` falls
  to the existing refusal (`agent-run.sh:350`).

- **A `deny.toml` entry retires with its subject** (`deny.toml:9-12`, the 2026-09-07 `number_prefix` precedent): the
  comment says which path left. The same act at scale here.

- **Static gates are presence-guarded `rust`-job steps** (`ci.yml:76-80`, `:102-108`, `:123-139`): editing the
  workflow must leave each step's shape intact.

- **The lock moves by pruning, never by bumping**: the new `Cargo.lock` must equal the old one minus the 292 packages,
  every remaining package at its old version and source (security-plan §Dependency Security; the 2026-09-02
  basis-by-package-count learning).

- **Supply-chain readings take the porcelain first and last** (`.claude/rules/security.md` Session Additions
  2026-09-05 / 2026-10-07 / 2026-10-08): `git -C $CARGO_HOME/advisory-db status --porcelain` empty before and after
  `cargo audit`.
- **Harness shells delete by pattern, never recursively** (2026-09-06 addition): removing arms adds no `rm -r`.

_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-10-12-panel-shaped-types-retired · **Version:** conductor-0.4.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-12T06:59Z

Retire what intent R1 lists, outside the removed crate, as "types shaped for the panel" (`intent.md:88-90`). The
run-event channel payload (`RunEvent` / `RunStage`), the desktop framing of the envelope read, the picker-only
selection guard (`SUITE_SELECTION` / `validate_selection`), the dialog-row justification of the checklist bound,
the Tauri log-sink text and the two webview fixtures all leave. A type that still serves a function is re-framed
for the command line, never kept for a panel (per architecture §Design Philosophy "Headless-drivable core, thin
shell").

Then give the four functions that lost their only entry point when the window left (the CARRY,
`2026-10-11-conductors-window-retired/research.md` §Function reach) a command-line entry. Each is a thin
`conductor-cli` surface over an existing library function, so nothing is left unreachable (`inputs#I2` §2):

- **The catalogue listing.** A new verb, `conductor scenarios`, named by the operator (`inputs#I3`). It runs over
  `conductor_core::list_scenarios` and the manifest-checked load `run` / `suite` already use (per architecture
  §Established Decisions [Accepted Capability Set]).

- **A graceful mid-run stop.** The first Ctrl-C during `conductor suite` lets the running scenario finish and keeps
  every finished record. A second Ctrl-C ends at once. A stopped suite exits 130 (`inputs#I3`). `suite` now drives
  through `conductor_run::drive_run`, whose abort flag had no CLI caller.

- **A past run's load-envelope standing.** `conductor report` prints the stored `[ENVIRONMENT-SUSPECT]` caption above
  its table, read through `conductor_run::read_envelope` (per layout-templates §Output structure).

- **A hold's `[[checklist]]` items.** These print as indented lines under the CLI `HOLD` line (per layout-templates
  §Component — Primary content block 2, the indented-detail-line precedent).

Nothing Conductor reads of Pulse moves (`inputs#I2` §4). The read-back, preflight and emission paths are outside the
write set (research.md §Files to modify). No listener, handle, place on disk or credential is added (per
security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Universal; architecture §Occupied Resources).

1. **The picker guard leaves; the catalogue read is re-framed** (`crates/conductor-core/src/scenario_catalog.rs`,
   `crates/conductor-core/src/lib.rs`).
   - Delete `SUITE_SELECTION`, `validate_selection` and their two tests (`validate_selection_accepts_suite_name_and_pid`,
     `validate_selection_rejects_unknown`). The graph puts their only references inside the module plus the
     `lib.rs:75-76` re-export (research.md §Graph impact).
   - Rewrite the module doc and the `ScenarioSummary` / `list_scenarios` docs so they name the CLI catalogue listing
     (`conductor scenarios`), never a picker, the Tauri `start_run` or a desktop surface.
   - Keep `ScenarioSummary`, `list_scenarios`, `load_catalog` and `scenario_files` as they are. `list_scenarios` stays
     in [Accepted Capability Set]'s loader set.
   - Drop the two names from the `lib.rs` re-export.

2. **The checklist bound loses its dialog-row reason, keeps its value, and gains its tests**
   (`crates/conductor-core/src/scenario.rs`).
   - `MAX_CHECKLIST_TEXT` stays `200`. Leaned 200 per security-plan §Input Validation (the bound is a trust-boundary
     rule) and arch §Conventions: no artifact asks for a new number, and `Window grading retired` (`:77`) removes the
     checklist later.
   - Rewrite the `ChecklistItem` and `MAX_CHECKLIST_TEXT` docs. The reason is a bound on untrusted scenario text that
     the CLI hold prints as one terminal line each. They no longer cite design-system §Surface: desktop-webview, an
     a11y-plan critical path or a dialog row.
   - Keep `#[garde(length(min = 1, max = MAX_CHECKLIST_TEXT))]` on both halves, the `dive` on `Scenario.checklist` and
     `check_checklist` on the load path.
   - Add inline tests (the bound has none today; research.md §Graph impact lists only its two attribute references):
     - a half of exactly `MAX_CHECKLIST_TEXT` chars loads;
     - a half of `MAX_CHECKLIST_TEXT + 1` is rejected at `Scenario::from_toml_str` as `CoreError::Validation`, for
       `induced` and for `observation` alike;
     - an empty half is rejected the same way;
     - a `[[checklist]]` beside a non-empty `expected` is still `CoreError::Config`.

3. **Core doc text loses the window** (`crates/conductor-core/src/obs.rs:58-61`, `crates/conductor-core/src/pause.rs`).
   - `ObsSink`'s doc names the cli's `--agent-mode` file sink alone. The `ObsSink` enum and its two variants are
     unchanged.
   - `pause.rs`'s module doc (`:13`) and resolver doc (`:99`) drop the Tauri dialog.
   - The test prompt `"Observe the desktop toast"` (`:244`) becomes a surface-neutral prompt. It is a test value only.

4. **`drive_run` becomes the suite's driver; the channel payload leaves** (`crates/conductor-run/src/drive.rs`,
   `crates/conductor-run/src/lib.rs`, `crates/conductor-run/tests/composition_root.rs`).
   - Delete `RunEvent` and `RunStage`.
   - `drive_run` takes a progress callback `FnMut(usize)` (scenarios completed so far) in place of `emit`. It returns
     a `DriveOutcome { records: Vec<RunRecord>, stopped: bool }`.
   - The abort poll at the loop head and after the last scenario (`drive.rs:75-93`) and the single `persist`
     (`drive.rs:94`) are unchanged, so a stop keeps and persists every finished record.
   - Re-export `DriveOutcome` and drop the two deleted names (`lib.rs:33`).
   - Rewrite the module, type and function docs and the `lib.rs:1-16` crate doc. The crate is the run composition
     root `conductor-cli` drives. No "both shells", GUI, Tauri `Channel` or `TauriResolver`.
   - Re-shape the three unit tests (`drive.rs:119-213`):
     - the Blocked spine ticks progress to 1 and returns `stopped = false`;
     - an abort before the first scenario returns no records and `stopped = true`;
     - an abort raised during the last scenario keeps its 1 record, writes the journal and returns `stopped = true`.
   - `composition_root.rs:43-44` pins `DriveOutcome` where it pinned `RunEvent` / `RunStage`. Its `:4` and `:64` docs
     drop "both bins" / "the a11y fixtures and both shells".

5. **The envelope read names its CLI caller** (`crates/conductor-run/src/envelope.rs`).
   - `read_envelope`'s doc (`:41-46`) names `conductor report` as its reader and drops the `conductor-tauri` edge
     argument. `persist`'s doc (`:12-15`) drops "both shells" / "the GUI".
   - Signature, boundary `info!` line and behaviour are unchanged (per obs-plan §6 Boundary-call wrappers).

6. **`conductor suite` drives through `drive_run` and stops on the first Ctrl-C** (`crates/conductor-cli/src/commands/suite.rs`,
   `crates/conductor-cli/Cargo.toml`, `crates/conductor-cli/src/render.rs`).
   - `conductor-cli`'s `tokio` gains the `signal` feature. No new package: `signal-hook-registry` is already in the
     graph (research.md §Mechanisms re-derived).
   - `suite` installs a stop handler on the current-thread runtime (`tokio::signal::ctrl_c`) before driving. The
     first press sets a shared stop flag and prints one stderr line saying the running scenario will finish and a
     second Ctrl-C ends now. The second press calls `std::process::exit(130)`.
   - `suite` calls `conductor_run::drive_run` with the spinner's `set_position` as progress and the flag as
     `should_abort`, in place of its own loop (`suite.rs:29-39`).
   - On `stopped`:
     - the spinner stops in place (`abandon`, never `finish_and_clear` and never driven to its length — per
       design-system §Brand Identity, Signature element);
     - the envelope caption and the results table print over the kept records;
     - one stderr line states how many of the scenarios were kept;
     - the exit is `ExitCode::from(130)`.
   - On a completed suite the exit stays `exit_code(&records)`.
   - Put the exit decision in a pure function `suite_exit(records, stopped)` with an inline test: stopped → 130
     whatever the records; not stopped → the existing hard-Fail rule.
   - Put the handler install in a function returning the flag. Add one `#[cfg(unix)]` inline test that installs the
     handler, then sends SIGINT to its own process through the test binary's own fixed-argv spawn:
     `std::process::Command::new("kill").args(["-INT", &std::process::id().to_string()])`. That is a fixed program,
     no operator value and no shell — a cargo test binary's own spawn, outside harness-spawn rule (b), the
     `secret_scan_gate` precedent of 2026-09-24. The test awaits the flag under a bounded `tokio::time::timeout`,
     never a sleep, and asserts the flag is set and the process lives. No dependency is added, so the lock stays 268
     (`inputs#I4` (1)). The second-press exit arm is not testable in-process and stays unwitnessed by the operator's
     word (`inputs#I4` (3)).

7. **The catalogue listing verb `conductor scenarios`** (`crates/conductor-cli/src/cli.rs`,
   `crates/conductor-cli/src/main.rs`, `crates/conductor-cli/src/commands/mod.rs`,
   `crates/conductor-cli/src/commands/catalog.rs`, `crates/conductor-cli/src/paths.rs`,
   `crates/conductor-cli/src/render.rs`).
   - `Commands` gains `Scenarios` with no arguments and the doc "List the scenario catalogue (name, P-IDs, SLO
     tier)".
   - `Paths` gains a catalogue read that calls `conductor_core::list_scenarios(&self.scenarios_dir, &capabilities)`
     through its existing `capabilities()` load (`paths.rs:40-41`), so an absent or malformed capability manifest or
     scenario is a harness fault with a named reason.
   - The handler in `commands/catalog.rs` prints `render::scenarios_table(&summaries)` on stdout:
     - a `comfy-table` sized from the terminal width;
     - columns Scenario · P-IDs · SLO;
     - P-IDs in the ID-cyan mapping and SLO as its `<5s>`/`<20s>`/`<90s>` label, the colour behind the existing
       `stdout_color()` gate;
     - no verdict/state column;
     - followed by one plain roll-up line `{N} scenarios`, the count derived from the summaries;
     - exit 0.
   - An empty catalogue prints the plain line `No scenarios found.` and exits 0.
   - `main.rs`: dispatch the verb. The `no scenario matches` hint (`:66`) becomes "list them with `conductor
     scenarios`, or pass a P-ID like P-009".

8. **`conductor report` prints a past run's stored standing** (`crates/conductor-cli/src/commands/report.rs`).
   - After the `Run report <id>` line and before the table, read `conductor_run::read_envelope(&paths.runs_dir,
     &run_id)?`.
   - When it is `Some(status)` and `render::envelope_caption(&status)` is `Some`, print the caption once.
   - In-envelope, exempt or no row prints nothing new. The six-column table is unchanged (per layout-templates §IA
     notes: no column without `--format`). No flag.

9. **The CLI hold prints its checklist items** (`crates/conductor-cli/src/render.rs`, `crates/conductor-cli/src/pause.rs`).
   - `render::hold_checklist_lines(&HoldPoint) -> Vec<String>` yields two indented plain lines per item,
     `  induced: {induced}` and `  observe: {observation}`. There is no new bracket label, lamp, ANSI code or token.
   - `PromptResolver::resolve` (`crates/conductor-cli/src/pause.rs:34-37`) is the resolver that prints `hold_line`
     and calls `confirm`. It prints the checklist lines on stderr after `hold_line` and before `confirm`, inside the
     same spinner-suspended closure (`pause.rs:35-42`).
   - `CliResolver::resolve` (`:114-119`) only dispatches and stays unchanged (`inputs#I4` (4)).
   - The headless path is unchanged and never blocks.
   - `hold_line`'s doc (`render.rs:94`) drops "the desktop titlebar hold signature".
   - Inline test: a hold with two items renders four lines in order, and a hold with none renders none.

10. **The webview fixtures leave.**
    - Delete `crates/conductor-run/tests/envelope_fixture.rs`, `crates/conductor-run/tests/lamps_fixture.rs`,
      `crates/conductor-run/tests/fixtures/over-envelope.toml` and `crates/conductor-run/tests/fixtures/lamps-journal.jsonl`.
    - Delete `journal_conformance.rs`'s `the_committed_fixture_journal_conforms` (`:156-164`), the fixture's third
      consumer. The target's production-writer test (`:169-…`) stays, so CI's `--test journal_conformance` step
      (`ci.yml:219`) keeps its subject.
    - `CONDUCTOR_E2E_SEED_DIR` loses its only reader.

11. **The parity test's in-process arm is the suite's composition** (`crates/conductor-cli/tests/cross_surface_parity.rs`).
    - Rename the "Tauri arm" to the in-process arm throughout: comments `:15-16`, `:58`, `:93`; run id
      `run-path7-tauri` → `run-path7-inproc`; the variable and the divergence-message label.
    - Call the re-shaped `drive_run` (`|_| {}` progress, `|| false` stop). It reads `.records`.
    - Rewrite the module doc (`:1-16`) to say why the test lives in `conductor-cli`. It no longer narrates the removed
      crate.
    - The comparison, the shared non-default runs dir and the excluded identity/wall-clock fields are unchanged (per
      test-plan §5 Cross-surface parity).

12. **Binary tests for the new entries** (`crates/conductor-cli/tests/cli_smoke.rs`).
    - `help_lists_the_verbs` also asserts `scenarios`.
    - `scenarios_lists_the_catalogue`: a sandbox with two scenarios and the capability manifest. It asserts exit 0,
      both stems, each one's P-ID, the roll-up line `2 scenarios`, zero ANSI escape bytes on the piped stdout, and no
      sandbox absolute path in stdout+stderr. It sets no `CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR` (per test-plan §3 Test data bootstrap,
      a write-nothing verb).
    - `scenarios_with_an_absent_capability_manifest_is_a_harness_fault`: exit 1, `error:` and `hint:` on stderr, no
      absolute path.
    - `report_prints_the_stored_envelope_caption_for_a_suspect_run`:
      - stages a load envelope whose `max_sustained_storm_ms` (`contracts/pulse-load-envelope.toml:28`) is below the
        copied scenario's longest emitting phase;
      - runs `conductor run` into a `CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR` sandbox, then `conductor report`;
      - asserts `[ENVIRONMENT-SUSPECT]` exactly once on report's stdout and the table's header unchanged.
    - `report_renders_the_latest_run` (`:391`) also asserts report's stdout lacks `[ENVIRONMENT-SUSPECT]` for the
      in-envelope run.
- `crates/conductor-cli/src/commands/catalog.rs` — the `conductor scenarios` handler

body:
- (v4-09, not claimed) v4-09 stays pooled. `working-route.md` lists it on `:47`, `:49`, `:107` and `:113`, whose legs
  this chunk does not build: the live progress following of `:113` and the closed text-label set of `:47`. At P5
  step 4, one dated note on v4-09 records what this chunk adds toward it — the catalogue listing, the suite stop, a
  past run's standing on `report`, and the hold's checklist lines — and that the claim stays with those entries
  (the card's decision, approved at `inputs#I4` (2)).

- (arch) The standalone per-seam sweep exits 0 after the removals (per architecture §Established Decisions [Module
  Boundaries]).

- (arch) `conductor scenarios` loads through `list_scenarios` with the capability manifest. An absent manifest is a
  harness fault, exit 1, with `error:` + `hint:` and no absolute path (per architecture §Established Decisions
  [Accepted Capability Set]; per security-plan §Error Handling).

- (security) A `[[checklist]]` half of `MAX_CHECKLIST_TEXT + 1` chars, or an empty half, is rejected at load as
  `CoreError::Validation`, and one of exactly `MAX_CHECKLIST_TEXT` loads. A checklist beside `expected` is
  `CoreError::Config`. The halves keep `length(...)` and the field keeps `dive` (per security-plan §Input Validation).

- (security) `cargo audit` and `cargo deny check advisories bans licenses sources` exit 0 over the lock, the
  advisory-db porcelain empty before and after (per security-plan §Dependency Security).

- (design) The piped `conductor scenarios` output carries zero ANSI escape bytes. `report`'s stored standing prints
  as the `[ENVIRONMENT-SUSPECT]` caption once, with no new lamp, label or column (per design-system §Surface: cli →
  Component Patterns, pattern 4).

- (design) A stopped suite's spinner stops in place, never driven to its length or cleared. A stopped suite exits
  130, and a completed one exits on the hard-Fail rule alone (`suite_exit`'s test; `inputs#I3`) (per design-system
  §Brand Identity, Signature element).

- (layouts) The hold's checklist items render as indented plain lines under the `HOLD` line with no new bracket
  label, and the headless path is unchanged (per layout-templates §Component — Hero / signature output).

- (tests) `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci` (inside `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run`) and
  `cargo test --workspace --lib --bins --tests` both exit 0. `cross_surface_parity.rs` still asserts equal
  `verdict` / `state` / `seed` between its in-process arm and `conductor run` (per test-plan §5 Cross-surface
  parity; test-plan §10).

- (tests) `cargo llvm-cov report --fail-under-lines 60` passes, the threshold unchanged (per test-plan §11
  Quality).

- (obs) `conductor report`'s envelope read logs its one boundary `info!` line through `read_envelope` and mints no
  `db.*` span, `read_envelope` unchanged. The `--agent-mode` sink still writes `logs/agent-latest.jsonl`
  (`agent_mode_routes_self_obs_to_the_log_file_not_stderr` green) (per obs-plan §6 Boundary-call wrappers; obs-plan
  §3 Log file location).
- Operator forks (`inputs#I3`): the verb word `scenarios`; a stopped suite exits 130.

- Playbook: the three `verdict: escalate` patterns (`.andromeda/playbook.md:97`, `:109`, `:124`) were read; no option
  here matches one. No listener, subprocess crossing or new input class: `scenarios` takes no argument.

- A `conductor stop` verb or a stop file — rejected: it needs a second process to reach the running one, either a
  socket, pipe or listener (security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Universal) or a new place on disk (`inputs#I2`
  §3).

- A `--envelope` flag on `report` — rejected: the run-level caption already prints by default on `run` / `suite`.
  A flag would fork one qualifier into two forms (layout-templates §Component — Primary content block 2: "adapted
  per surface, never forked").

- Deleting `drive_run` and keeping `suite`'s own loop — rejected: the loop has no abort poll, and test-plan §5's
  in-process parity arm needs a library composition. Re-using `drive_run` gives the stop and the arm one home.
- Deleting `read_envelope` — rejected: it is the reader CARRY item 3 needs.

- Dropping the checklist bound or switching `checklist` to `#[garde(skip)]` — banned (security-plan §Security
  Anti-Patterns → Input).

- A `db.*` read span or a new log attribute for the listing or the report read — banned (obs-plan §11 Spans; the
  `message` field precedent).

- A seventh lamp, a new bracket label or a new ANSI code for any new output — banned (layout-templates §Component —
  Primary content block 2).
- Touching `conductor-verify`, `conductor-emit`, `canary.rs` or `execute.rs` — out of bounds (`inputs#I2` §4).

- `libc::kill` through a `libc` dev-dependency for the SIGINT test — not taken: the call is an `unsafe` FFI call,
  and the security rules say never to add `unsafe` across an FFI boundary without review. The fixed-argv `kill`
  spawn needs neither the dependency nor the `unsafe` (`inputs#I4` (1) offered both).

- **Size:** 26 files (research.md §Files to modify, `gate.py scope --lists-only` parsed 26), most of them doc or
  small edits. It fits one chunk, so no cut is proposed (`inputs#I2` §6).

- **Second Ctrl-C:** the exit-130 arm runs `std::process::exit` and cannot be asserted in-process. It is the
  pre-chunk behaviour (an immediate end) carried by one call. It stays unwitnessed by the operator's word, 2026-10-12
  (`inputs#I4` (3)), with no owner.

- **Windows:** `tokio::signal::ctrl_c` compiles there, and CI (`windows-latest`) builds and runs the suite. The
  `#[cfg(unix)]` SIGINT test runs on the Linux dev host only until `Linux-only base CI` (`working-route.md:15`).

- **`drift.rs`** keeps its `list_scenarios` call (`:361`) and its `"ScenarioSummary"` leak token (`:463`). The type
  stays.

- **Expected amendments (wrap):**
  - architecture §Occupied Resources — `logs/conductor-tauri.jsonl` row retired (no sink, no writer), and the
    `CONDUCTOR_E2E_SEED_DIR` row retired (its reader gone); the `conductor-run` crate row restates `drive_run` as
    the suite's driver with a stop flag.
  - architecture §Conventions (config) — the `MAX_CHECKLIST_TEXT` reason restated as a terminal-line bound on
    untrusted text.
  - security-plan §Input Validation — the `CONDUCTOR_E2E_SEED_DIR` row and its mentions (Threat Model, Secret
    Management, Bootstrap, Anti-Patterns → Input) retire; the checklist row's reason restated; the CLI-arguments row
    gains `conductor scenarios` (no argument) and `suite`'s Ctrl-C stop.
  - test-plan §1 Coverage triggers Vector 1 — the seed-dir reader class retires; §3 Log format key — the Tauri sink
    row retires (lockstep with obs-plan §3); §5 Cross-surface parity — the arm is the in-process suite composition;
    §7 — the committed-fixture tree set and its round-trip enumeration lose the two webview fixtures (both sites).
  - obs-plan §3 Logging stack / Log file location and §6 Sink configuration — the Tauri backend sink retires; §4
    In-process ↔ headless parity — the arm's naming.
  - layout-templates §Primary screens (commands) — a `conductor scenarios` entry (third table shape: Scenario ·
    P-IDs · SLO, roll-up line, `No scenarios found.`); `report` prints the stored caption; `suite`'s stop line and
    exit 130; the hold's indented checklist lines.
  - design-system §Surface: cli → Component Patterns 3 — the catalogue listing as a static table beside
    `coverage`.

**Chunk:** Panel-shaped types retired — the panel types, limit, sink and fixtures leave; four functions get a command-line entry

title: Mechanisms re-derived (the equalities the plan rests on)

data.head: ## Mechanisms re-derived (the equalities the plan rests on)

body:
- **A graceful suite stop keeps what finished** — `drive_run(.., should_abort)` with `should_abort` returning true
  after scenario k yields k records persisted and a stopped outcome; measured by `drive.rs:173-213`
  (`drive_run_reports_an_abort_raised_during_the_last_scenario`, 1 record kept, journal written). The frame that
  produces it is `drive.rs:91-94` (re-poll after the loop, then `persist`).

- **No new package for a Ctrl-C handler** — `cargo tree --locked --offline -e normal -i signal-hook-registry`:
  `signal-hook-registry v1.4.8` is already in the graph through `tokio` (its `process` feature, enabled by
  `conductor-verify`) and through `crossterm` (`comfy-table`, `inquire`); `cargo tree -p conductor-cli -e features
  -i tokio` lists `signal-hook-registry` active and `signal` NOT active. So adding tokio's `signal` feature to
  `conductor-cli` turns on a feature over packages already locked; the package count (268) is the basis to
  re-measure at implement, never lockfile byte-identity.

- **A past run's standing is readable from the CLI** — `conductor-cli` already declares `conductor-report` and
  `conductor-run` (`crates/conductor-cli/Cargo.toml`), so `read_envelope`'s stated reason (the window crate had no
  `conductor-report` edge, `envelope.rs:44`) no longer holds; the CLI `report` path can call it directly.

- **A hold's checklist is on the value the CLI already receives** — `HoldPoint.checklist: Vec<ChecklistItem>`
  (`crates/conductor-core/src/pause.rs:71-76`, filled from the scenario at `crates/conductor-run/src/execute.rs:151`)
  reaches `PromptResolver::resolve(&HoldPoint)` through `CliResolver::resolve`'s interactive arm
  (`crates/conductor-cli/src/pause.rs:114-119` → `:34`); no plumbing is missing, only the print.
- `crates/conductor-cli/src/commands/catalog.rs` — the listing handler (the file name is fixed whatever word the verb takes)
- `crates/conductor-cli/src/cli.rs` — the listing verb's `Commands` arm

- `crates/conductor-cli/src/commands/suite.rs` — drive the catalogue through `conductor_run::drive_run` with a stop flag
- `crates/conductor-cli/src/commands/report.rs` — print the stored load-envelope caption above the table
